summary: Romulus founded the city of Rome and established the Roman Kingdom as its first king.
text: The city of Rome and the Roman Kingdom were thought to be founded, according to Roman tradition, and is ruled by Rome's first king, Romulus. Beginning of the Roman 'Ab urbe condita' calendar. Rome adopts the Etruscan alphabet, which the Etruscans themselves had adopted from the Greeks. Set by Varro, this was the most common date used.

summary: Romulus celebrated Rome's first triumphs over the Caeninenses and the Antemnates.
text: Romulus, first king of Rome, celebrates the first Roman triumph after his victory over the Caeninenses, following the Rape of the Sabine Women. He celebrates a further triumph later in the year over the Antemnates.

summary: The Roman Kingdom established its first colonies.
text: Rome's first colonies were established.

summary: Greeks established colonies throughout southern Italy and Sicily.
text: Greeks establish colonies in Italy and Sicily.

text: Founding of Rome according to Livy's ab urbe condita

summary: Akragas was founded in Sicily.
text: Akragas is founded on Sicily.

text: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus was killed in a riot instigated by the sons of Ancus Marcius.

text: Phocaean Greek colonists clash with Carthaginian and Etruscan ships in the Battle of Alalia (near Corsica).

text: Servius Tullius was murdered by his daughter Tullia Minor and her husband Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, who declared himself King of Rome on the steps of the Curia Hostilia.

text: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus becomes the seventh king of Rome, after murdering his predecessor Servius Tullius.

text: Pythagoras arrives in the Greek colony of Croton (modern-day Crotone) in Magna Graecia and founds the philosophical school of Pythagoreanism .

summary: The Greeks of Cumae defeated an allied army of Umbrians, Daunians, and Etruscans at the Battle of Cumae.
text: Battle of Cumae - An army of Umbrians, Daunians, Etruscans, and others is defeated by the Greeks of Cumae, present-day Italy.

text: Sarcophagus, from Cerveteri is made. It is now at National Etruscan Museum, Rome .

text: The reign of Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, last king of the traditional seven Kings of Rome, concludes. The Kingdom of Rome falls and is replaced by the Roman Republic. (or 509 BC)

summary: The Roman Kingdom fell and the Roman Republic was established.
text: Fall of the Roman Kingdom and establishment of the Roman Republic.

summary: The Greek city of Sybaris was defeated and destroyed by Croton.
text: Defeat and destruction of Sybaris.

summary: The Roman Republic elected its first pair of consuls.
text: The first pair of Roman consuls are elected.

summary: The Tarquinian conspiracy to restore the deposed Roman monarchy was uncovered, and its participants were executed.
text: The Tarquinian conspiracy is formed yet discovered, and the conspirators are executed.

text: Forces of Veii and Tarquinii, led by the deposed king Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, are defeated in the Battle of Silva Arsia by the Roman army. Consul Publius Valerius Publicola celebrates the first republican triumph on March 1.

summary: The Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on Rome's Capitoline Hill was dedicated.
text: The Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on Rome's Capitoline Hill is dedicated on the ides of September.

summary: Carthage signed a treaty with Rome establishing their respective spheres of influence.
text: Carthage signs a treaty with Rome, delineating their respective spheres.

summary: Lucius Junius Brutus, founder of the Roman Republic and consul, died at the Battle of Silva Arsia.
text: Lucius Junius Brutus, Roman consul and founder of the Roman Republic (traditional date)

text: Titus Junius Brutus and Tiberius Junius Brutus, brothers (and sons of the consul Lucius Junius Brutus) together with their two uncles the Vitellii and three brothers Aquillii, all executed following the discovery of the Tarquinian conspiracy

text: The patrician Lucretia was raped by Lucius Tarquinius Superbus' son Sextus Tarquinius.

summary: Lucius Junius Brutus and the Curiate Assembly overthrew King Lucius Tarquinius Superbus and founded the Roman Republic led by two consuls.
text: Overthrow of the Roman monarchy: Following Lucretia's suicide, Lucius Junius Brutus called the Curiate Assembly, one of the legislative assemblies of the Roman Kingdom. The latter agreed to the overthrow and expulsion of Lucius Tarquinius Superbus and to a provisional constitution under which two consuls acted as a joint executive and a Curiate Assembly held legislative power, and swore never again to let a King rule Rome. It further elected Lucius Junius Brutus and Lucius Tarquinius Collatinus, Lucretia's husband, Died.

states.value: Lucius Junius Brutus and Lucius Tarquinius Collatinus

summary: Consul Publius Valerius Publicola enacted reforms opening the consulship to all citizens and placing the treasury under quaestors.
text: The consul Publius Valerius Publicola enacted a number of liberal reforms, including opening the office of consul to all Roman citizens and placing the treasury under the administration of appointed quaestors.

summary: Clusium waged war against the Latin town of Aricia.
text: Clusium fights a war with Aricia.

summary: The Roman Republic created the priesthood of rex sacrorum to assume the religious responsibilities previously held by the Roman kings.
text: The office of rex sacrorum is created in Rome to carry out the religious duties formerly held by the kings.

summary: An army from Clusium failed to capture Rome during the Roman-Etruscan Wars.
text: Roman–Etruscan Wars: A Clusian army failed to conquer Rome.

summary: A war broke out between the Roman Republic and the Sabines.
text: A war between Rome and the Sabines begins, concluding in 504 BC.

summary: Consul Publius Valerius Publicola defeated the Sabines in battle.
text: Roman–Sabine wars: Roman victory over the sabines in the battle of 504 BC by consul Publicus.

text: The Latin towns of Pometia and Cora, with the assistance of the Aurunci, revolt against Rome.

text: Publius Valerius Publicola (or Poplicola, his agnomen meaning "friend of the people"), one of four Roman aristocrats who led the overthrow of the monarchy.

summary: The Roman Republic suppressed the revolt of Pometia.
text: Rome suppresses the Pometian revolt.

summary: Renowned Greek wrestler Milo of Croton died.
text: Milo of Croton, ancient Greek wrestler

summary: Carthage captured Gadir.
text: Gadir (present-day Cádiz) is captured by Carthage.

summary: The Roman Senate authorized the consuls to appoint a dictator, leading to the selection of Titus Larcius.
text: In the face of a potential Sabine invasion, the Senate passed a senatus consultum authorizing the consuls to appoint a dictator, a magistrate who held absolute power during a national emergency. The dictator would in turn appoint the Magister equitum, the commander of the cavalry. The consuls Titus Larcius and Postumus Cominius Auruncus selected the former as dictator.

summary: Vulca made the terracotta Apollo of Veii for the Portonaccio Temple.
text: Vulca makes Apollo of Veii, from Portonaccio Temple, now kept at Museo Nazionale di Villa Giulia, Rome.
names: National Etruscan Museum of Villa Giulia

summary: Hanno the Navigator explored the western coast of Africa, possibly reaching as far south as Gabon.
text: Hanno the Navigator's naval exploration of the western coast of Africa could have reached as far south as Gabon.

summary: The bronze Capitoline Wolf statue was crafted.
text: The She-wolf, with late 15th century or early 16th century additions (twins), is made. It is now kept at the Museo Capitolino in Rome .

summary: Hippocrates succeeded his assassinated brother Cleander as tyrant of Gela and conquered several Sicilian cities.
text: After the assassination of Cleander, tyrant of Gela, power is transferred to his brother, Hippocrates, who subdues the Sicels and conquers the Chalcidian cities of Callipoli, Leontini, Naxos and Zancle (now known as Messina). He also captures the Syracusan city of Camarina, but is prevented from capturing Syracuse itself when Corinth and Corcyra interferes in the war.

summary: Cleander, tyrant of Gela, was assassinated.
text: Cleander, tyrant of Gela, assassinated

summary: The Temple of Saturn in the Roman Forum was consecrated and the Saturnalia festival was first celebrated.
text: Consecration of the newly constructed Temple of Saturn in the Roman Forum, and Saturnalia festival first celebrated.

summary: Tisicrates of Kroton won the stadion race at the 71st Olympic Games.
text: Tisicrates of Kroton wins the stadion race at the 71st Olympic Games.

summary: The Roman army defeated Tarquinius Superbus, Octavius Mamilius, and the Latin League at the Battle of Lake Regillus.
text: The former Etruscan King of Rome, Tarquinius Superbus, who had been exiled by the Romans in 509 BC, and his ally Octavius Mamilius, of Tusculum, together with the Latins are defeated by the Roman Republic army in the Battle of Lake Regillus, near Frascati. The outcome of this battle establishes Roman supremacy over the Latins.

summary: Former Roman consuls Marcus Valerius Volusus and Titus Herminius Aquilinus died in combat at the Battle of Lake Regillus.
text: Marcus Valerius Volusus and Titus Herminius Aquilinus, both former Roman consuls died at the Battle of Lake Regillus

summary: Octavius Mamilius, ruler of Tusculum, died fighting against Rome at the Battle of Lake Regillus.
text: Octavius Mamilius, ruler of Tusculum also died at the Battle of Lake Regillus

summary: A temple dedicated to Mercury was built and consecrated on the Circus Maximus in Rome.
text: A temple is built on the Circus Maximus, between the Aventine and Palatine hills, in Rome, in honour of the god Mercury and was dedicated on 15 May.

summary: The Roman Republic increased the number of voting tribes to twenty-one.
text: The number of Roman tribes is increased to 21.

summary: The Roman Republic dispatched additional colonists to reinforce the Latin colony at Signia.
text: Additional colonists were sent to the colony at Signia.

text: The Volsci launch an invasion against Rome, but are defeated, and in retaliation Rome plunders Suessa Pometia.

summary: Roman forces defeated an invading army of Sabines.
text: Roman troops defeat an invading force of Sabines.

summary: Roman forces defeated an army of the Aurunci near Aricia.
text: Roman troops defeat an army of the Aurunci near the town of Aricia.

text: The beginning of discord between the plebs and patricians leading to the first secession of the plebs.

summary: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, the deposed final king of Rome, died in exile at Cumae.
text: Tarquinius Superbus, former king of Rome died in exile in Cumae

summary: The Roman Senate appointed Manius Valerius Maximus as dictator to confront military enemies and popular unrest.
text: The Senate appoints Manius Valerius Maximus to the office of dictator to deal with a series of military threats, and a popular uprising.

summary: Dictator Manius Valerius Maximus defeated the Sabines and celebrated a triumph in the Circus Maximus.
text: The dictator Valerius defeats the Sabines, and is awarded a triumph plus the honour of a curule chair in the Circus Maximus.

summary: Consul Aulus Verginius Tricostus Caeliomontanus defeated the Volsci, and a Roman colony was planted at Velitrae.
text: The Roman consul Aulus Verginius Tricostus Caeliomontanus defeats the Volsci, and a Roman colony is planted at Velitrae.

summary: Consul Titus Veturius Geminus Cicurinus defeated the Aequi to protect Rome's Latin allies.
text: The Roman consul Titus Veturius Geminus Cicurinus defeats the Aequi at the request of Rome's Latin allies.

summary: The plebeians retired to Mons Sacer during the first secession of the plebs, securing the establishment of the office of the tribunate.
text: At the end of the military campaigns, the plebs retire to the Sacred Mountain outside Rome in the Secession of the Plebs. To end the secession, the plebeians gain acceptance from the patricians that they may choose two leaders to whom they give the title of Tribunes. The office of the tribunate is thereby established.

summary: The magistracy of the plebeian aediles was created in Rome to oversee the temple and cult of Ceres.
text: The aediles, magistrates of ancient Rome who are in charge of the temple and cult of Ceres, are first established. They are two officials of the plebeians, created at the same time as the tribunes, whose sanctity they share.

summary: The first secession of the plebs ended after political compromises were enacted in Rome.
text: The secession of the plebs concludes.

summary: Postumus Cominius Auruncus defeated the Volsci and captured Corioli, where Gaius Marcius earned his cognomen Coriolanus.
text: The Roman army, led by Postumus Cominius Auruncus defeats the Volsci and the Romans capture the towns of Longula, Pollusca and Corioli. Gaius Marcius distinguishes himself in the battle for Corioli, and earns the cognomen Coriolanus.

summary: Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus ratified the Foedus Cassianum treaty with the Latin League.
text: During his second consulate, the Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus concludes a treaty with the Latin League, the Foedus Cassianum, confirming Roman primacy in Latium.

summary: Former Roman consul Agrippa Menenius Lanatus died.
text: Agrippa Menenius Lanatus, former Roman consul.

summary: Hippocrates of Gela defeated Syracuse at the Heloros River and secured possession of Camarina following Corinthian mediation.
text: When Camarina, a Syracusan colony, rebels, Hippocrates, the tyrant of Gela, intervenes to wage war against Syracuse. After defeating the Syracusan army at the Heloros River, he besieges the city. However, he is persuaded by the intervention of forces from the Greek mainland city of Corinth to retreat in exchange for the possession of Camarina.

summary: Roman consuls averted a famine following the secession of the plebs by obtaining grain from Etruria.
text: Following the conclusion of the secession of the plebs, a famine strikes Rome. The consuls avert the crisis by obtaining grain from Etruria.

summary: Rome reinforced its colony at Velitrae and founded a new colony at Norba while a pestilence incapacitated the Volsci.
text: War with the Volsci is averted because a pestilence affects the Volsci. Rome sends additional colonists to Velitrae and establishes a new colony in Norba.

summary: Gelon succeeded Hippocrates as tyrant of Gela after Hippocrates was killed in battle against the Sicels.
text: Hippocrates, tyrant of Gela, loses his life in a battle against the Siculi, the native Sicilian people. He is succeeded as Tyrant of Gela by Gelo, who had been his commander of cavalry.

summary: Tribunes exiled Gnaeus Marcius Coriolanus from Rome after he proposed withholding grain unless the tribunate was abolished, prompting him to join the Volsci.
text: During this year there was a famine in Rome. General Gais Marcius Coriolanus suggested that people should not receive grains unless they agree to abolish the Office of Tribune. Because of this, the Tribunes had him exiled. In response, Coriolanus takes refuge with the leader of the Volsci, eventually leading the Volscian army in a war against Rome. It was only due to entreaties from his mother and wife that he abandoned his war against Rome.

summary: The Temple of Fortuna Muliebris was completed outside Rome along the Via Latina.
text: On the Via Latina, a main road leading out of Rome, the Temple of Fortuna Muliebras was finished.

summary: Hippocrates, tyrant of Gela, was killed in battle against the Sicels.
text: Hippocrates, tyrant of Gela

summary: The Carthaginian navigator Himilco explored the northwestern coast of Europe.
text: Carthaginian navigator Himilco is the first known explorer from the Mediterranean Sea to reach the northwestern shores of Europe .

summary: The Greek philosopher Empedocles was born in Agrigento.
text: Empedocles, Greek philosopher (d. c. 430 BC)

summary: The philosopher Zeno of Elea was born in Elea.
text: Zeno of Elea, Greek philosopher (d. c. 430 BC)

summary: Appius Claudius Sabinus Regillensis, founder of the Roman gens Claudia, died.
text: Appius Claudius Sabinus Regillensis, legendary founder of the gens Claudia

summary: Theron became tyrant of Acragas in Sicily.
text: Theron becomes tyrant of Acragas in Sicily.

summary: Gaius Marcius Coriolanus and Attius Tullius led a Volscian army to besiege Rome before Coriolanus was persuaded to withdraw.
text: Gaius Marcius Coriolanus and Attius Tullius, leading an army of the Volsci, besiege Rome. Coriolanus' mother and wife convince him to break off the siege. In recognition of the service of these women, a temple is erected in Rome dedicated to Fortuna. Subsequently, the Volsci and their allies the Aequi have a falling out, and their armies fight as a result, significantly diminishing the strength of each of them.

summary: Astylos of Croton won the stadion race at the seventy-third Olympic Games.
text: Astylos of Croton wins the stadion race at the 73rd Olympic Games.

summary: Rome defeated both the Volsci and the Hernici in separate conflicts.
text: Wars are fought between Rome and each of the Volsci and the Hernici. Rome prevails in both disputes.

summary: Greek philosopher Gorgias was born.
text: Gorgias, Greek philosopher (d. c. 376 BC)

summary: Rome concluded a new treaty with the Hernici.
text: Rome enters into a new treaty with the Hernici.

summary: Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus proposed an agrarian law to aid needy plebeians, prompting patrician opposition.
text: During his third consulate, the Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus proposes an agrarian law to assist needy plebeians. The proposal is vehemently opposed by the patricians including the other consul Proculus Verginius Tricostus Rutilus, and the plebs turn against the patricians. In the following year Cassius is condemned and executed for high treason.

summary: Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus was executed.
text: Spurius Cassius Vecellinus, Roman consul (executed)

summary: Gelon took control of Syracuse and left his brother Hieron in charge of Gela.
text: Gelo, the tyrant of Gela, takes advantage of an appeal by the descendants of the first colonist of Syracuse, the Gamoroi, who had held power until they were expelled by the Killichiroi, the lower class of the city. He makes himself master of that city, leaving his brother Hieron to control Gela.

summary: Former Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus was tried, condemned, and executed for high treason.
text: Three times Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus is tried, condemned and executed for high treason.

summary: Roman consul Quintus Fabius Vibulanus defeated the Volsci and Aequi in battle and placed the spoils in the public treasury.
text: The consul Quintus Fabius Vibulanus defeated the Volsci and Aequi in battle, but incurred the anger of the plebs by lodging the spoils of victory with the publicum.

summary: Three-time Roman consul Spurius Cassius Vecellinus died.
text: Spurius Cassius Vecellinus, three times Roman consul.

summary: Astylos of Croton won the stadion race for the second time at the seventy-fourth Olympic Games.
text: Astylos of Croton wins the stadion race for a second time at the 74th Olympic Games.

summary: The Romans defeated the Volsci and Aequi in battle.
text: The Romans defeat the Volsci and Aequi in battle.

summary: The Temple of Castor and Pollux was dedicated in Rome.
text: Dedication of the Temple of Castor and Pollux

summary: Gelon, tyrant of Syracuse, conquered Megara Hyblaea and Euboea, enslaving their commoners and relocating their oligarchs to Syracuse.
text: Gelo, the tyrant of Syracuse conquers the nearby Sicilian cities of Euboea and Megara Hyblaea, selling their common people into slavery and bringing their oligarchs to Syracuse.

summary: The Fabian war commenced between Rome and Veii.
text: Commencement of the Fabian war with Veii.

summary: Hostilities continued between Rome and the Volsci.
text: Ongoing hostilities with the Volsci.

summary: The Vestal Virgin Oppia was punished in Rome for an alleged breach of chastity.
text: Punishment of the vestal virgin Oppia for a breach of chastity.

summary: Hostilities continued between Rome and the Aequi.
text: Continuation of hostilities with the Aequi.

summary: The Veientine army invaded Roman territory and ravaged the countryside.
text: Continuation of hostilities with Veii. The Veientine army enters Roman territory and ravages the countryside.

summary: The Romans defeated the Aequi after the Aequi laid siege to Ortona.
text: The Aequi lay siege to Ortona but are defeated by the Romans. Tensions between the Roman classes flare during the battle.

summary: The army of Veii threatened to besiege Rome as hostilities continued.
text: Continuation of hostilities with Veii. The Veientine army threatens to besiege Rome but nothing notable occurs.

summary: Tribune Spurius Licinius unsuccessfully advocated for an agrarian law in Rome.
text: The tribune Spurius Licinius unsuccessfully advocates an agrarian law.

summary: Rome defeated Veii in a closely contested battle in which Quintus Fabius and consul Gnaeus Manlius Cincinnatus were killed.
text: The Romans achieve a significant victory against Veii after a close-fought battle. Tensions between the Roman classes flare during the battle. Quintus Fabius and the consul Manlius perish in the fighting.

summary: Tribune Titus Pontificius unsuccessfully advocated for an agrarian law in Rome.
text: The tribune Titus Pontificius unsuccessfully advocates an agrarian law.

summary: Carthage dispatched a large army under Hamilcar to attack Greek settlements in Sicily.
text: Xerxes encourages the Carthaginians to attack the Greeks in Sicily. Under the Carthaginian military leader, Hamilcar, Carthage sends across a large army.

summary: Gelon of Syracuse and Theron of Akragas defeated the Carthaginian army at the Battle of Himera, after which Hamilcar committed suicide.
text: The Greek city of Himera in Sicily, in its quarrel with Akragas, enlists Carthaginian support. With the help of Gelo, the tyrant of Syracusae, and Theron of Akragas, the Carthaginians are defeated in the Battle of Himera. After the defeat, Hamilcar kills himself.

summary: Painting of the Musicians and Dancers began inside the Tomb of the Lionesses in Tarquinia.
text: Work begins on the detail Musicians and Dancers on a wall painting in the Tomb of the Lionesses in Tarquinia. It is finished some ten years later.

summary: The Greek philosopher Xenophanes died.
text: Xenophanes, Greek philosopher (b. 570 BC)

summary: The Carthaginian general Hamilcar committed suicide following his defeat at the Battle of Himera.
text: Hamilcar, Carthaginian general (suicide after his defeat in the Battle of Himera)

summary: Quintus Fabius Vibulanus, former consul of Rome, died in battle against Veii.
text: Quintus Fabius Vibulanus, a former consul (twice) of Rome, dies in battle against Veii.

summary: Roman consul Gnaeus Manlius Cincinnatus died in battle against Veii.
text: Gnaeus Manlius Cincinnatus, Roman consul, dies in battle against Veii.

summary: Caeso Fabius Vibulanus proposed distributing captured land to the plebs, but the Roman Senate rejected the bill.
text: The Roman consul Caeso Fabius proposed an agrarian law to distribute land won in recent wars amongst the plebs, but this was rejected by the senate.

summary: Hostilities continued between Rome and the Aequi without a major battle.
text: Ongoing hostilities between Rome and the Aequi. No major battle is fought.

summary: The Fabii took sole responsibility for the war against Veii and built a fortified camp on the Cremera River.
text: Ongoing hostilities between Rome and Veii. The family of the Fabii requests and is granted sole responsibility for the war, and the Fabii march from Rome, establishing a fortified camp at the Cremera.

summary: Hiero I became the tyrant of Syracuse following the death of his brother Gelon.
text: Hiero I (Hieron) becomes the Tyrant of Syracuse following the death of his brother Gelo.

summary: Gelon, tyrant of Gela and Syracuse, died.
text: Gelo, tyrant of the cities of Gela and Syracuse in Sicily

summary: The Greek philosopher Xenophanes died.
text: Xenophanes, Greek poet and philosopher (approximate year)

summary: Veientine forces defeated the Roman army in the Battle of the Cremera.
text: Roman forces in a stronghold on the Cremera River are defeated by an army of Veientes from the Etruscan city of Veii in the Battle of the Cremera.

summary: The Greek poet Pindar visited Sicily and was welcomed at the courts of Theron of Acragas and Hiero I of Syracuse.
text: The Greek poet Pindar visits Sicily and is made welcome at the courts of Theron of Acragas and Hieron I of Syracuse. They commission some of his greatest poetry. It is through these connections that Pindar's reputation spreads all over the Greek world.

summary: Mount Etna experienced its first recorded volcanic eruption.
text: The first recorded eruption of Mount Etna occurs.

summary: The Greek philosopher Philolaus was born.
text: Philolaus, Greek philosopher (approximate year)

summary: Hiero I of Syracuse and allied southern Italian Greek navies defeated the Etruscan fleet at the Battle of Cumae.
text: Hiero I, tyrant of Syracuse, allied with naval forces from the maritime Greek cities of southern Italy defeats the Etruscan navy in the Battle of Cumae as the Etruscans try to capture the Greek city of Cumae. This victory marks the end of the Etruscan aggression against the Greeks in southern Italy and saves the Greeks of Campania from Etruscan domination.

summary: The Messapians, Peucetians, and Lucanians defeated the allied armies of Taras and Rhegion near Kailia.
text: Taras signs an alliance with Rhegion, to counter the Messapians, Peucetians, and Lucanians, but the joint armies of the Tarentines and Rhegines are defeated near Kailia.

summary: Hiero I of Syracuse constructed a fortress on the island of Ischia.
text: Hiero builds Castello Aragonese on the island of Ischia.

summary: Lucius Furius Medullinus and Gnaeus Manlius Vulso served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Lucius Lucius Furius Medullinus and Gnaeus Manlius Vulso

summary: The Roman Republic executed the Vestal Virgin Orbinia by live burial.
text: Orbinia, a Vestal virgin, is executed via live burial.

summary: The Greek colony of Pixunte was founded in Magna Graecia.
text: The colony of Pixunte (Pixous) is founded in Magna Graecia.

summary: The Roman Plebeian Council was reorganized by tribes rather than curiae.
text: After a law allowing organization of the plebs tribe, the Plebeian Council was reorganized by tribes rather than curiae.

summary: Roman forces captured the Volscian city of Antium.
text: Antium is captured by Roman forces.

summary: Quintus Fabius Vibulanus took office as consul of the Roman Republic for the first time.
text: Quintus Fabius Vibulanus becomes consul of the Roman Republic for the first of three times.

summary: Thrasybulus became tyrant of Syracuse following the death of his brother Hiero I.
text: After the death of his brother Hiero I, Thrasybulus becomes Tyrant of Syracuse.

summary: Aeschylus staged his tragedy The Persians in Sicily.
text: Aeschylus' play, The Persians is produced in Sicily.

summary: Hiero I, tyrant of Syracuse, died.
text: Hiero I, Tyrant of Syracuse

summary: The citizens of Syracuse expelled the tyrant Thrasybulus and established a democracy.
text: The Tyrant, Thrasybulus, is driven out by the citizens of Syracuse, Sicily. The city moves to a democratic system of government.

summary: The native inhabitants of Apulia defeated Taras, leading to the overthrow of its monarchy and the establishment of a democracy.
text: The Greek colony of Taras, in Magna Graecia, is defeated by the native population of Apulia. As a result, the Tarentine monarchy falls, with the installation of a democracy.

summary: The Roman Senate and people appointed Gaius Aemilius Mamercus as interrex.
text: The Senate and People of Rome appoint Gaius Aemilius Mamercus interrex.

summary: A Tusculan relief force led by Lucius Mamilius helped Romans recover the Capitoline Hill and suppress a slave revolt during which consul Publius Valerius Publicola died.
text: Conflicts arise between the Roman patricians and plebeians. There is also a revolt by Rome's slaves. During the revolt, the Campidoglio is held by the slaves for a lengthy period, along with the most important temples of Rome. It is during this revolt that consul Publius Valerius Publicola dies. The revolt only ends with the arrival of an army from Tusculum, led by Tusculan dictator Lucius Mamilius. Meanwhile, Lucius Quinctius Cincinnatus is appointed as consul to replace Publicola.

summary: Ducetius, leader of the Sicels, expelled the colonists of tyrant Hieron from Catana and restored it to its indigenous inhabitants.
text: Ducetius, a Hellenised leader of the Siculi, an ancient people of Sicily, takes advantage of the confusion that follows the collapse of the tyranny in Syracuse and other Sicilian states. With the support of the Syracusan democracy, he drives out the colonists of the former tyrant Hieron from Catana and restores it to its original inhabitants.

summary: The comic poet Epicharmus died in Syracuse.
text: Epicharmus, Greek poet (b. 550 BC)

summary: Roman consul Publius Valerius Publicola died during the slave revolt that seized the Capitoline Hill.
text: Publius Valerius Publicola, Roman consul

summary: The Tusculans, aided by Roman consular armies, recaptured their city from the occupying Aequi.
text: The Aequi occupied Tusculum. In response to the threat, the Roman Senate decided to send an army to help the allied city, under the command of consul Lucius Cornelius Maluginensis. In addition, the consul Fabius Vibulanus, who was at that point besieging Antium, moved his forces to attack Tusculum. The Tusculans were able to recapture their city. A truce was then arranged with the Aequi.

summary: Ducetius, the leader of the Sicels, captured and destroyed the Sicilian town of Morgantina.
text: The Sicilian town of Morgantina was destroyed by Ducetius, Hellenised leader of the Siculi (according to Diodorus Siculus).

summary: Under popular pressure, the Roman Senate expanded the number of tribunes of the plebs from two to ten.
text: Under popular pressure, the Senate increased the tribunes of the plebs from two to ten.

summary: Lucius Quinctius Cincinnatus was appointed Roman dictator, relieved the besieged consul by routing the Aequi at Mount Algidus, and resigned sixteen days later.
text: The Roman general Lucius Quinctius Cincinnatus is summoned by the Roman Senate to defend the city from attack by the approaching Aequi. He is named dictator of Rome for six months. He goes on to defeat the enemy in a single day at the Battle of Mount Algidus and celebrates a triumph in Rome. Sixteen days after the battle, he resigns his dictatorship and returns to his farm.

summary: The Greek playwright Aeschylus died at Gela in Sicily.
text: Aeschylus, Greek playwright (b. 525 BC)

summary: The Roman plebeians compelled the patricians to begin codifying the laws, dispatching a three-man commission to Athens to study Greek legal systems.
text: The Roman Plebs, suffering from a number of economic and financial ills, force the city’s patricians to begin the reform and codification of the law. As a first act, a three-man commission is sent to Athens to study that city's laws.

summary: Segesta and Selinunte entered into conflict over access to the Tyrrhenian Sea.
text: Hostilities between Segesta and Selinunte, two Greek cities on Sicily, take place over access to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

summary: The Sicel leader Ducetius founded the city of Palice in Sicily.
text: Ducetius founds the town of Palice

summary: Spurius Furius Medullinus Fusus died.
text: Spurius Furius Medullinus Fusus

summary: Publius Curiatius Fistus Trigeminus died.
text: Publius Curiatius Fistus Trigeminus

summary: Roman consul Sextus Quinctilius died.
text: Sextus Quinctilius

summary: An epidemic of plague spread throughout Italy.
text: An outbreak of plague spreads throughout Italy.

summary: Roman consul Sextus Quinctilius died of the plague.
text: Sextus Quinctilius, consul of the Roman Republic, 453–452 BC, plague.

summary: Rome established the first Decemvirate under Appius Claudius Crassus and Titus Genucius Augurinus, drafting the first ten tables of Roman law.
text: Following the report of a three-man commission into the design of Roman law, the patricians set up in Rome a Board of Ten, the Decemviri. The first Decemviri, composed entirely of patricians is led by consuls Appius Claudius Crassus and Titus Genucius Augurinus. The first ten codes of the Roman Law of the Twelve Tables are completed by the first Decemvirate.

summary: A second Decemvirate including plebeian members completed the Law of the Twelve Tables before descending into tyrannical rule.
text: The success of the first Decemvirate prompts the appointment of a second Decemvirate which also includes plebeians amongst its members. This second decemviri adds two more headings to their predecessor's ten, completing the Law of the Twelve Tables (Lex Duodecim Tabularum), which will form the centrepiece of Roman law for the next several centuries. Nevertheless, this Decemvirate's rule becomes increasingly violent and tyrannical.

summary: The allied forces of Syracuse and Acragas defeated the Sicel leader Ducetius, forcing him into exile in Corinth.
text: After minor preliminary successes (including the capture of Inessa from its Greek colonists), Ducetius, a Hellenised leader of the Siculi, an ancient people of Sicily, is decisively defeated by the combined forces of Syracuse and Acragas. Ducetius flees to exile in Corinth.

summary: The Decemviri formally promulgated the Law of the Twelve Tables and displayed them on ivory tablets in the Roman Forum.
text: The Law of the Twelve Tables (developed by the Decemvirates) is formally promulgated in 450 B.C. The Twelve Tables are literally drawn up on twelve ivory tablets which are posted in the Forum Romanum so that all Romans can read and know them.

summary: The Decemviri were forced to resign following a popular uprising triggered by Appius Claudius Crassus's actions against Verginia, restoring the ordinary magistrates.
text: When the Decemvirate's term of office expires, the decemviri refuse to leave office or permit successors to take office. Appius Claudius Crassus is said to have made an unjust decision which would have forced a young woman named Verginia into prostitution, prompting her father to kill her. This leads to an uprising against the Decemvirate forcing the decemviri to resign their offices. The ordinary magistrates (magistratus ordinarii) are re-instituted. Appius Claudius is said to have committed suicide as a result of these events.

summary: Former decemvir Appius Claudius Crassus died by suicide in prison.
text: Appius Claudius Crassus, former decemvir (suicide)

summary: Resolutions of the Plebeian Council were granted the full force of law, subject to Senate veto.
text: Resolutions of the Plebeian Council were given the full force of law subject to Senate veto.

summary: Tribune Lucius Trebonius Asper introduced the Lex Trebonia, barring tribunes from co-opting colleagues into office.
text: Following the co-optation of two patricians to the office of Tribune of the Plebs, the tribune Lucius Trebonius Asper introduces the Lex Trebonia, a law forbidding tribunes from co-opting their colleagues in the future.

summary: The Tribal Assembly was established in Rome and granted the authority to elect quaestors.
text: The Tribal Assembly was established, and granted the right to elect quaestors.

summary: Sicel leader Ducetius returned from exile in Corinth to Sicily and colonised Cale Acte with Greek and Sicel settlers.
text: Ducetius, the Hellenised leader of the Siculi, an ancient people of Sicily, returns from exile in Corinth to Sicily and colonises Cale Acte on the north coast with Greek and Siculi settlers.

summary: Syracuse defeated Acragas at the Battle of the Himera River after Acragas declared war over the return of Ducetius.
text: Acragas declares war on Syracuse because of the return of Ducetius and is defeated by Syracuse in the Battle of the Himera River.
names: Battle of the Himera River (446 BC)

summary: Titus Quinctius Capitolinus Barbatus led Roman forces to victory over the Aequi and Volsci at the Battle of Corbione.
text: In the Battle of Corbione, Titus Quinctius Capitolinus Barbatus leads Roman troops to a victory over the Aequi of north-east Latium and the Volsci of southern Latium.

summary: Roman soldier and statesman Marcus Furius Camillus was born.
text: Marcus Furius Camillus, Roman soldier and statesman (traditional date) (d. 365 BC)

summary: Rome enacted the Lex Canuleia, removing the ban on intermarriage between patricians and plebeians.
text: A new law, the Lex Canuleia removes the ban on inter-marriage of the Roman classes, i.e. plebeian with patrician.

summary: The Roman Senate refused plebeian demands for the consulship and instead compromised by establishing the office of Consular Tribune.
text: The Plebeians demand the right to stand for election as consul but the Roman senate refused to grant them this right. Ultimately, a compromise is reached, and consular command authority is granted to Consular Tribunes ("Military Tribunes with Consular powers" or tribuni militares consulari potestate).

summary: Roman patricians instituted the office of censor to prevent plebeian military tribunes from conducting the Roman census.
text: No consuls are elected in Rome, but rather military tribunes with consular power are appointed in their stead. While only patricians could be consuls, some military tribunes were plebeians. These positions had responsibility for the census, a vital function in the financial administration of Rome. So to stop the plebeians from possibly gaining control of the census, the patricians remove from the consuls and tribunes the right to take the census, and rather entrust it to two magistrates, called censores who were to be chosen exclusively from the patricians in Rome.

summary: Pericles founded the Athenian colony of Thurii near the former site of Sybaris in southern Italy.
text: Pericles founds the colony of Thurii near the site of the former city of Sybaris, in southern Italy. Its colonists include Herodotus and Lysias.

summary: The Roman state established the collegium of consular tribunes to hold consular power subject to the Senate.
text: The offices of the Tribuni militum consulari potestate were established. A collegium of three patrician or plebeian tribunes, one each from specific Roman tribes (the Titienses, the Ramnenses, and the Luceres), would hold the power of the consuls from year to year, subject to the Senate.

summary: A famine struck the Roman Republic.
text: A famine strikes in Rome.

summary: Ducetius, leader of the Sicels and founder of a united Sicilian state, died.
text: Ducetius, a Hellenized leader of the Sicels and founder of a united Sicilian state

summary: Spurius Maelius distributed cheap grain to the plebeians during a Roman famine, prompting accusations of aspiring to kingship.
text: Spurius Maelius, a wealthy Roman plebeian, tries to buy popular support with the aim of making himself king. During the severe famine affecting Rome, he buys up a large store of grain and sells it at a low price to the people of Rome – the first time this had been done in Rome. This leads Lucius Minucius, the patrician praefectus annonae ("president of the market"), to accuse Maelius of seeking to take over the government.

summary: Gaius Servilius Ahala killed Spurius Maelius after Spurius Maelius refused a summons before Cincinnatus, and Maelius's house was destroyed.
text: Maelius is summoned before Cincinnatus but refuses to appear. Shortly thereafter, Maelius is killed by Gaius Servilius Ahala and his house is burnt to the ground.

summary: Spurius Maelius was slain in Rome after being accused of plotting to seize royal power.
text: Spurius Maelius - was the youngest man to ever attempt taking over Rome

summary: Cincinnatus accepted a second dictatorship to suppress the alleged conspiracy of Spurius Maelius before resigning after twenty-one days.
text: Cincinnatus was called upon to accept a second dictatorship by the patricians to prevent Spurius Maelius from seizing power; the patricians suspected Spurius of using wheat to purchase the support of the plebeians, to set himself up as a king. Gaius Servilius Ahala was appointed magister equitum in order to stop Maelius; following an attack by Maelius, Ahala slew him. Cincinnatus again resigned his dictatorship and returned to his farm after 21 days.

summary: The Samnites captured the city of Capua.
text: The city of Capua falls to the Samnites.

summary: Roman statesman Lucius Quinctius Cincinnatus died.
text: Cincinnatus, Roman politician, consul and dictator (b. 519 BC)

summary: Roman forces under dictator Quintus Servilius Priscus captured the nearby city of Fidenae by tunneling through the hill beneath it.
text: Forces of the Roman Republic, led by dictator Quintus Servilius Priscus, captured the nearby city of Fidenae by tunneling in through the hill the town was built upon. He was awarded the cognomen 'Fidenas' as a reward for his success.

summary: Pericles renewed Athenian alliances with Rhegium in southern Italy and Leontini in Sicily, threatening Sparta's western grain route.
text: Pericles renews alliances with the Rhegium on the southwest corner of Italy and Leontini in southeast Sicily, threatening Sparta's food supply route from Sicily.

summary: Colonists from Tarentum and Thurii founded the Greek colony of Heraclea in southern Italy.
text: The Greek colony of Heraclea in Southern Italy is founded by colonists from Tarentum and Thurii.

summary: Dionysius I, future tyrant of Syracuse, was born.
text: Dionysius, tyrant of Syracuse (d. 367 BC) (approximate birth date)

summary: The Romans defeated the combined forces of the Aequi and Volsci at the Battle of Mount Algidus.
text: The Romans defeat the Aequi and the Volsci at the Battle of Mount Algidus.

summary: Empedocles proposed that all matter is composed of four classical elements driven by Love and Strife.
text: The Greek philosopher Empedocles distinguishes the four elements - earth, fire, water, and air - that he claims all substances are made of. He explains the development of the universe by the forces of attraction and repulsion known as Love and Strife.

summary: The Greek philosopher Empedocles died in Sicily.
text: Empedocles, Greek philosopher (b. c. 490 BC)

summary: The Greek philosopher Zeno of Elea died.
text: Zeno of Elea, Greek philosopher (b. c. 490 BC)

summary: The Samnites captured the Greek colony of Cumae and took control of the Campanian plain.
text: The Greek colony of Cumae in Italy falls to the Samnites, who begin to take control of the Campanian plain.

summary: The Greek philosopher, mathematician, and statesman Archytas was born in Tarentum.
text: Archytas, Greek philosopher, mathematician, astronomer, statesman, and strategist (d. 347 BC)

summary: Athens sent a naval expedition under Laches to assist Leontini against Syracuse, but achieved little success.
text: In an effort to blockade Sparta from access to Sicilian corn, Athens responds to a plea for help from a delegation from the city of Leontini led by Gorgias, the sophist and rhetorician. Leontini is being threatened by Syracuse which is allied to Sparta. However, the Athenian mission led by the Athenian general Laches is unable to offer much help. Laches is later prosecuted by Cleon for his unsuccessful mission to support Athenian interests in Sicily.

summary: The Roman Republic opened the quaestorship to the plebeians.
text: The Quaestorship is opened to the Plebs.

summary: Herodotus of Halicarnassus, Greek historian, died.
text: Herodotus of Halicarnassos, Dorian Greek historian (b. 484 BC)

summary: Hermocrates persuaded the Sicilian cities to make peace at the Congress of Gela, forcing Athenian forces to withdraw from Sicily.
text: At the Congress of Gela, the statesman Hermocrates of Syracuse persuades the cities of Sicily to agree to make peace and urges the exclusion of foreign powers. As a result, the three-year war between his city and Sicily's pro-Athenian town ends and the Athenian forces, which had been sent to Sicily to support Greek settlements, are forced to withdraw.

summary: Gaius Sempronius Atratinus and Quintus Fabius Vibulanus were elected consuls of Rome.
text: Gaius Sempronius Atratinus and Quintus Fabius Vibulanus are elected as consuls

states.value: Gaius Sempronius Atratinus and Quintus Fabius Vibulanus

summary: The Roman plebeians elected Sextus Tempanius, Aulus Sellius, Sextus Antistius, and Spurius Icilius as tribunes.
text: Sextus Tempanius, Aulus Sellius, Sextus Antistius, and Spurius Icilius are chosen by the commons as tribunes

summary: The Samnites captured the Greek colony of Cumae in southern Italy.
text: The city of Cumae, the most northerly of the Greek colonies in Italy, falls to the Samnites.

summary: The Sicilian city of Segesta appealed to Athens for military assistance against Selinunte and Syracuse.
text: In Sicily, the Ionian city of Segesta asks for Athenian help from the Dorian city of Selinus (which is supported by the powerful Sicilian city of Syracuse). The people of Syracuse are ethnically Dorian (as are the Spartans), while the Athenians, and their allies in Sicily, are Ionian. The Athenians feel obliged to assist their ally and therefore prepare an armada to attack Sicily.

summary: The Athenian expedition sailed for Sicily under Nicias, Lamachus, and Alcibiades, who was shortly recalled to face trial.
text: The Athenian expedition to Sicily sets sail under Nicias, Lamachus and Alcibiades. After his departure with the armada, Alcibiades is accused of profanity and is recalled to Athens to stand trial.

summary: Alcibiades defected to Sparta after being condemned in absentia, while Athenian forces under Nicias landed near Syracuse.
text: After learning that he has been condemned to death in absentia, Alcibiades defects to Sparta and Nicias is placed in charge of the Sicilian expedition. The Athenian forces land at Dascon near Syracuse but with little result. Hermocrates heads the Syracusan defence.

summary: Athens sent seventy-three ships commanded by Demosthenes to reinforce Nicias at the siege of Syracuse.
text: Athens responds to appeals from its general, Nicias, by sending out 73 vessels to Sicily under the command of Demosthenes to assist Nicias and his forces with the siege of Syracuse.

summary: Spartan commander Gylippus routed Athenian forces during a night battle at Syracuse, killing the Athenian general Lamachus.
text: The Athenian army moves to capture Syracuse while the larger fleet of Athenian ships blocks the approach to the city from the sea. After some initial success, the Athenian troops become disorganised in the chaotic night operation and are thoroughly routed by Gylippus, the Spartan commander. The Athenian commander Lamachus is killed. Nicias, although ill, is left in sole charge of the siege of Syracuse.

summary: Athenian general Lamachus died in combat during the siege of Syracuse.
text: Lamachus, Athenian general

summary: Syracusan and Spartan forces destroyed the Athenian expedition in the harbour of Syracuse, capturing and executing Nicias and Demosthenes.
text: After suffering a defeat in which the Athenian commander Lamachus is killed, Demosthenes suggests that they immediately give up the siege of Syracuse and return to Athens, where they are needed to defend against a Spartan invasion of Attica. Nicias refuses, but the Syracusans and Spartans under Hermocrates are able to trap the Athenians in the harbour and the Athenians sustain heavy losses in the Battle of Syracuse. Demosthenes is ambushed by the Syracusans and is forced to surrender. Nicias is soon captured as well, and both are executed, with most of the surviving Athenian soldiers sent to work in the Sicilian quarries. Ten proboulos (including Sophocles) are elected to help run Athens.

summary: Athenian general Demosthenes was executed after surrendering to Syracusan forces.
text: Demosthenes, Athenian general

summary: Athenian general and statesman Nicias was executed in Sicily following the failure of the Sicilian expedition.
text: Nicias, Athenian soldier and statesman (b. 470 BC)

summary: The epidemic reached Rome and caused a severe food shortage.
text: The epidemic hits the Roman Republic and causes a food shortage.

summary: Hannibal Mago led a Carthaginian invasion of Sicily, capturing and destroying Selinus and Himera.
text: Taking advantage of the quarrels between the Greek cities in Sicily and of the mutual exhaustion of Athens and Syracuse, Carthage seeks to reimpose its influence over the island. Hannibal Mago, grandson of Hamilcar, invades Sicily with a strong force. He defeats the Sicilian Greeks and avenges his grandfather through the torture and killing of 3,000 Greek prisoners. In the Battle of Selinus and Battle of Himera he captures and destroys both cities before returning triumphantly to Carthage with the spoils of war.

summary: Dion, later tyrant of Syracuse, was born.
text: Dion, tyrant of Syracuse (d. c. 354 BC)

summary: Consular tribunes exercised supreme magistracy in Rome.
text: The Tribuni militum consulari potestate held office.

summary: Hermocrates, exiled former political leader of Syracuse, was killed trying to force his return to the city.
text: The exiled former leader of the moderate democrats of Syracuse, Hermocrates, is killed while attempting to force his way back into Syracuse.

summary: Hermocrates, leader of the moderate democrats of Syracuse, died.
text: Hermocrates, leader of the moderate democrats of Syracuse

summary: Roman forces began a ten-year siege of the Etruscan city of Veii.
text: The Roman forces begin a decade-long siege against Veii.

summary: Carthaginian forces under Himilco captured Agrigentum, Gela, and Camarina after Hannibal Mago died of plague.
text: The Carthaginians again invade Sicily and attack Agrigentum (Acragas). Plague breaks out in their camp and Hannibal Mago dies. Himilco assumes command and captures Agrigentum (Acragas), Gela and Camarina. Gela is destroyed and its treasures sacked. The survivors take refuge in Syracuse. The plague is carried back to Carthage by its soldiers.

summary: Carthaginian general Hannibal Mago died of plague during the siege of Agrigentum.
text: Hannibal Mago, Carthaginian general

summary: Dionysius the Elder rose to power as tyrant of Syracuse and concluded a peace treaty with Himilco of Carthage.
text: Dionysius the Elder rises to power as the tyrant of Syracuse. He makes peace with the Carthaginian general, Himilco (whose army has been weakened by the plague), and fortifies Syracuse. This treaty leaves Carthage in control of most of Sicily.

summary: Dionysius the Elder fortified Syracuse and Epipolae and expelled the Greek populations of Naxos, Catana, and Leontini.
text: Dionysius the Elder ruthlessly consolidates and expands his power. He builds a wall around Syracuse and fortifies Epipolae. The Greek citizens of Naxos, Catana, and Leontini are removed from their cities; many of them are enslaved and their homes are given to Sicilian and Italian mercenaries. Dionysius prepares his army to fight against Carthage, which now occupies western and southern Sicily.

summary: The Pythagorean mathematician and philosopher Philolaus died.
text: Philolaus, Greek mathematician and philosopher (b. c. 480 BC)

summary: Rome elected eight military tribunes with consular power for the year.
text: Rome elects eight military tribunes with consular power; Manlius Aemilius Mamercus, Lucius Valerius Potitus, Appius Claudius Crassus, Marcus Quinctilius Varus, Lucius Julius Julus, Marcus Postumius, Marcus Furius Camillus, and Marcus Postumius

summary: Greek engineers invented the mechanical catapult.
text: The catapult is invented by Greek engineers.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse reminted coinage at twice its nominal value, causing rapid inflation.
text: Dionysius I, Greek tyrant of Syracuse, confiscates gold and silver coins and re-mints them, keeping the weight the same but changing the denomination from one to two drachmae — the first known official devaluation at the expense of the general population. A virulent inflation ensues .

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse broke his peace treaty with Carthage, attacked plague-weakened Carthaginian cities in Sicily, and captured Motya.
text: Dionysius, tyrant of Syracuse, breaks his peace treaty with Carthage and strikes at Carthaginian cities in the western corner of Sicily which have been weakened by the plague. There is a massacre of Carthaginians in many of these cities. Motya, with its fine harbour, is attacked and captured.

summary: Syracuse defeated the Carthaginian army under Himilco after the Carthaginians were stricken by plague during the siege.
text: Siege of Syracuse: A Carthaginian expeditionary army (some 50,000 men) under Himilco crosses to Sicily. They conquer the north coast and put Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse, on the defensive and besiege Syracuse. However, the Carthaginian army suffers from the plague. The Syracuse counterattacked and completely defeat Himilco's army. Himilco has to escape back to Carthage.

summary: Carthage established the town of Lilybaeum in Sicily to replace Motya.
text: The Carthaginians establish the town of Lilybaeum in Sicily to replace Motya.

summary: Dionysius II, son of Dionysius I and future tyrant of Syracuse, was born.
text: Dionysius II, son of Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse (d. 343 BC)

summary: Carthage abandoned the siege of Syracuse due to plague, ending the war in victory for Dionysius I, and Himilco committed suicide.
text: The Carthaginians are forced to abandon their siege of Syracuse (begun in 398 BC) due to a plague, but destroy Messina. Dionysius' first war with Carthage ends with a notable victory for Dionysius, who confines his enemy's power to an area of northwest Sicily. On his return home, the Carthaginian general, Himilco, commits suicide.

summary: Roman dictator Marcus Furius Camillus captured and destroyed the Etruscan city of Veii, doubling the territory of Rome.
text: Marcus Furius Camillus is made dictator by the Romans. Camillus finally destroys the Etruscan city of Veii in southern Etruria as the town falls to Roman forces after what is said to be a 10 year siege. The capture of Veii and its surrounding territories marks the first major expansion of Rome which doubles its territory after this victory.

summary: The Carthaginian general Himilco died by suicide in Carthage.
text: Himilco, Carthaginian general.

summary: Roman soldiers first began receiving regular pay.
text: Roman soldiers first earned a salary ("salary" from Latin for "salt").

summary: Consuls took office in the Roman Republic.
text: The consuls held office.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse allied with the Sicels and defeated the Carthaginian army under Mago II.
text: Dionysius I of Syracuse, having increased his power over the native Sicilians (Sicels), is now attacked by a second Carthaginian expedition. He is forced to ally himself with the Sicels. The Carthaginian army, under Mago II, is defeated, makes peace, and returns to Carthage. The treaty with Carthage is advantageous to Dionysius.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse unsuccessfully besieged Rhegium in an effort to extend his control over southern Italy.
text: Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse, begins an attempt to extend his rule to the Greek cities of southern Italy. He unsuccessfully besieges Rhegium.

summary: Marcus Furius Camillus went into voluntary exile after being accused of misallocating spoils from Veii.
text: The Roman dictator Marcus Furius Camillus is accused of making an unfair distribution of the spoils of his victory at Veii. He goes into voluntary exile.

summary: Brennus and the Senones besieged Clusium and advanced toward Rome after a Roman embassy killed one of their leaders.
text: Quintus Fabius Ambustus and two other Fabii are sent as ambassadors by Rome to a wandering tribe of Celts (whom the Romans call Gauls), under Brennus, who are advancing down the Tiber while the Celtic army is besieging Clusium. After Quintus Fabius' group becomes involved in a skirmish with the Gauls and kill one of the Gauls' leaders, the offended Gauls demand that Rome surrender the Fabii members to them. The Romans refuse, so the Gauls advance on Rome.

summary: Consular tribunes held office in the Roman Republic.
text: The Tribuni militum consulari potestate held office.

summary: Brennus and the Senones defeated the Romans at the Allia and sacked Rome, extorting one thousand pounds of gold.
text: Battle of the Allia: Brennus, a chieftain of the Senones of the Adriatic coast of Italy, leads an army of Cisalpine Gauls in their attack on Rome. They capture the entire city of Rome except for the Capitoline Hill, which is successfully held against them. However, seeing their city devastated, the Romans attempt to buy their salvation from Brennus. The Romans agree to pay one thousand pounds weight of gold.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse won the Battle of the Elleporus and captured Croton.
text: Battle of the Elleporus and the capture of Kroton by Dionysius I of Syracuse

summary: Artaxerxes II of Persia and Agesilaus II of Sparta formed an alliance against Athenian expansion, joined by Dionysius I of Syracuse.
text: Concerned about the revival of Athenian imperialist ambitions, the Persian King Artaxerxes II and King Agesilaus II of Sparta enter into an alliance. Sparta also seeks and gains the support of Dionysius I of Syracuse.

summary: Plato traveled to Syracuse at the invitation of Dion.
text: Plato, having left Athens on Socrates' death to visit Megara and possibly Egypt, travels to Syracuse at the invitation of Dionysius I's brother-in-law Dion.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse captured Rhegium with Lucanian aid and established colonies at Ancona and Adria.
text: With the aid of the Lucanians, Dionysius I of Syracuse devastates the territories of Thurii, Crotone, and Locri in mainland Italy. When Rhegium falls, Dionysius becomes the chief power in Greek Southern Italy. He then turns his attention to the Adriatic and founds the colonies of Ancona (Ankon) and Adria (Adrìa).

summary: Dionysius I expelled Plato from Syracuse, after which Plato returned to Athens.
text: Plato is forced by Dionysius to leave Syracuse after having exercised the right of free speech too broadly. Plato returns to Athens, outside which he founds a school.

summary: Rome began to rebuild after the Gallic sack led by Brennus.
text: Rome begins to rebuild after being invaded by the Gauls under Brennus.

summary: Marcus Furius Camillus instituted the Capitoline Games in Rome to celebrate the survival of the Capitoline Hill.
text: Marcus Furius Camillus introduces the Capitoline Games (Ludi Capitolini) in honour of Jupiter Capitolinus, and in commemoration of Rome's Capitol not being captured by the Gauls.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse expanded Adriatic influence by founding colonies at Adria, Ancona, and Issa.
text: Dionysius I of Syracuse extends the influence and trade of Syracuse to the Adriatic, establishing colonies at Adria, Ancona and Issa.

summary: Dionysius I of Syracuse attempted to restore Alcetas I of Epirus to his throne.
text: Dionysius I of Syracuse attempts to restore Alcetas I of Epirus to the throne.

summary: Lysias delivered a speech at Olympia rebuking Greeks for submitting to Dionysius I of Syracuse and the Persians.
text: Lysias, the Athenian orator, on the occasion of the Olympiad, rebukes the Greeks for allowing themselves to be dominated by the Syracusan tyrant Dionysius I and by the barbarian Persians.

summary: Rome pacified a revolt in Tusculum, annexed the city, and granted it status as the first municipium cum suffragio.
text: The district of Tusculum is pacified after a revolt against Rome, and then conquered. After an expression of complete submission to Rome, Tusculum becomes the first "municipium cum suffragio", and thenceforth the city continues to hold the rank of a municipium.

summary: The Volsci defeated a Roman army under Publius and Gaius Manlius following Rome's dispatch of colonists to Setia.
text: Rome sends colonists to Setia, the inhabitants complain that their numbers are too small. Publius and Gaius Manlius are assigned to the Volsicans for campaign. A defeat follows for the Romans after having been attacked in their camp and foraging parties being killed. The Roman soldiers do not waver even when they have no leader. A dictator is soon afterwards requested but the Volsicans do not know how to follow up a victory. At the end of the year the Parenestines inspire the Latin peoples to revolt.

summary: Carthage defeated Dionysius I of Syracuse at Cronium, compelling Syracuse to pay an indemnity and cede western Sicily up to the Halycus River.
text: Dionysius I's third war with Carthage proves disastrous. He suffers a crushing defeat at Cronium and is forced to pay an indemnity of 1,000 talents and cede the territory west of the Halycus River to the Carthaginians.

summary: The Romans constructed the Servian Wall around Rome to protect against sack and invasion.
text: The Servian Wall is constructed around Rome to prevent the city from being captured or sacked (see 390 BC). This is the first fortification that the Romans build around their home city.

summary: Athenian general Timotheus captured Corcyra and defeated the Spartan fleet off Alyzia.
text: Sparta attacks Corcyra, enlisting Syracusan help. Athens comes to the island's aid. The Athenian general, Timotheus, captures Corcyra and defeats the Spartans at sea off Alyzia (Acarnania).

summary: Roman general and consul Marcus Valerius Corvus was born.
text: Marcus Valerius Corvus, Roman hero (d. c. 270 BC)

summary: Dionysius II succeeded his father Dionysius I as tyrant of Syracuse under the guidance of Dion and Plato.
text: Dionysius I of Syracuse dies and is succeeded as tyrant of the city by his son Dionysius II. As the younger Dionysius is weak and inexperienced, Dion, brother-in-law of the elder Dionysius, assumes control and persuades Plato, whose friendship he has acquired, to train the new tyrant in the practical application of his philosophical principles.

summary: Dionysius II concluded a peace treaty with Carthage on existing terms.
text: Dionysius II makes peace with Carthage on the same terms established after his father's defeat by Carthage in the previous decade.

summary: Gaius Licinius Stolo secured the passage of the Lex Licinia Sextia, restoring the consulship and opening one seat to plebeians.
text: During the ten-year period that Gaius Licinius (Calvus) Stolo is tribune in Rome (376 BC to 367 BC) he does much to reduce the enmity between patricians and plebs by reforming a number of laws. During his term, he proposes the Lex Licinia Sextia, which restores the consulship to the plebs, requires a plebeian consul seat, limits the amount of public land that one person can hold, and regulates debts. The patricians oppose these laws, though they are now finally passed and take effect from 366 BC.

summary: Marcus Furius Camillus constructed the Temple of Concordia on the Roman Forum.
text: The temple to Concordia on the Forum Romanum in Rome is built by Marcus Furius Camillus.

summary: Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse, died.
text: Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse (b. 430 BC)

summary: Dionysius II of Syracuse banished both Dion and Plato after their philosophical instruction failed.
text: The experiment by Dion (brother-in-law of Dionysius I) and Plato to educate the new ruler of Syracuse, Dionysius II, in the practical application of Plato's philosophical principles fails and Dion and Plato are banished from Syracuse.

summary: The Roman Republic restored the consulship, abolished consular tribunes, and created the office of praetor.
text: The use of military tribunes with consular power is abandoned permanently and the dual consulship is restored. A new magistracy is established, which is called the praetorship. Its holder, the praetor, is elected annually by the Assembly and takes charge of civil matters, thus relieving the consuls of this responsibility. The praetor is regarded as a junior colleague of the consuls. Nevertheless, the praetor can command an army, convene a Senate or an assembly, as well as exercise the consular functions.

summary: The Roman Republic created two curule aediles, alternating annually between patricians and plebeians.
text: Two additional aediles, called curule ("higher") aediles, are created in the Roman hierarchy. These are at first patricians; but those of the next year are plebeians and so on year by year alternately. They are elected in the assembly of the tribes, with the consul presiding.

summary: Lucius Sextius Lateranus was elected as the first plebeian consul of Rome.
text: Lucius Sextius was elected the first plebeian consul.

summary: Etruscan actors staged the first theatrical performances in Rome.
text: Etruscan actors stage the first theatrical performances in Rome.

summary: Roman soldier and statesman Marcus Furius Camillus died.
text: Marcus Furius Camillus, Roman soldier and statesman. (b. c. 446 BC)

summary: Plato failed to reconcile Dionysius II with Dion and was forced to flee Syracuse.
text: Plato returns once more to Syracuse to teach the young Syracusan tyrant Dionysius II. He fails to reconcile the tyrant to Dion, who Dionysius II banished in 366 BC. Because of this, Plato is forced to flee Syracuse to save his life.

summary: Agathocles, future tyrant of Syracuse, was born.
text: Agathocles, tyrant of Syracuse (d. 289 BC)

summary: Roman forces beat back the Gauls who had once again advanced to the gates of Rome.
text: The Gauls again reach the gates of Rome, but are beaten back.

summary: The Romans defeated the Volsci, annexed most of their territory, and renewed their alliance with the Latin League.
text: The Romans defeat the Volsci, annex most of their territory, and settle it with Roman colonists. The Romans also force the Latin League to renew its close alliance with Rome, an alliance which was weakened by Rome’s defeat at the hands of the Gauls in 390 BC.

summary: Dion sailed from Zakynthos to Sicily with mercenaries and ousted Dionysius II from Syracuse.
text: The brother-in-law of Dionysius I, Dion, exiled from Syracuse in 366 BC by Dionysius II, assembles a force of 1,500 mercenaries at Zacynthus and sails to Sicily. Dion wrests power from the weak Dionysius II, who is exiled and flees to Locri.

summary: Gaius Marcius Rutilus was elected consul of Rome.
text: Gaius Marcius Rutilus elected Consul

summary: Gaius Marcius Rutilus became the first plebeian appointed dictator of Rome.
text: Gaius Marcius Rutilus is the first plebeian to be chosen as a dictator in Rome.

summary: The Sicilian Greek historian Philistus died.
text: Philistus.

summary: Callippus assassinated Dion of Syracuse amid growing popular discontent with Dion's rule.
text: Reflecting the growing level of discontent with his tyrannical conduct, Dion is assassinated by Callippus, an Athenian who has accompanied him on his expedition to take over as tyrant of Syracuse. Dionysius II remains in exile in Italy.

summary: The Roman Republic concluded a mutual defense pact and alliance with the Samnites.
text: Rome allies itself with the Samnites and they agree on a mutual defence pact.

summary: Rome defeated the Etruscans of Caere.
text: Rome defeats the Etruscans of the city of Caere.

summary: Dion of Syracuse, tyrant of Syracuse, was assassinated.
text: Dion, Greek tyrant of Syracuse (assassinated) (b. c. 408 BC)

summary: Publius Valerius Publicola and Gaius Marcius Rutilus served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Publio Valerio Publicola & Gaius Marcius Rutilus

summary: Gaius Julius Iulus was appointed dictator of Rome.
text: Dictator: Gaius Julius Iulus

summary: The Romans decisively defeated the Etruscans, forcing them to sue for peace.
text: The Etruscans are badly defeated by the Romans and abandon their attacks on the city and sue for peace.

summary: Roman soldiers made the first recorded use of the pilum in battle against the Gauls.
text: First use of the heavy throwing spear, the pilum, (according to Livy) in battle against the Gauls.

summary: Gaius Marcius Rutilus became the first plebeian to be elected Roman censor.
text: Gaius Marcius Rutilus becomes the first Roman plebeian to be elected to the office of censor.

summary: The first plebeian dictator was elected in Rome.
text: The first plebeian dictator was elected.

summary: Alexander I became king of Epirus after Philip II of Macedon helped him depose Arybbas.
text: Alexander I becomes king of Epirus after his brother-in-law, Philip II of Macedon, aids him in ousting the previous king, Arymbas.

summary: A Roman army and its allies decisively defeated a force of Gauls threatening Rome.
text: The Gauls, once more threatening Rome, are decisively beaten by an army comprising Rome and its allies.

summary: Dicaearchus was born in Messana.
text: Dicaearchus, Greek philosopher, cartographer, geographer, mathematician and polymath (d. c. 285 BC)

summary: Archytas died near Tarentum.
text: Archytas, Greek philosopher, mathematician and statesman (or 347 BC) (b. 428 BC)

summary: The Roman Republic and Carthage concluded a trade treaty safeguarding Rome's Latin allies.
text: Rome and Carthage make a trade agreement under which Carthage will not attack those Latin states which are faithful to Rome. This agreement demonstrates that Rome is now the dominant power in the Latin League.

summary: Coinage was introduced into Rome for the first time.
text: Coinage is introduced into Rome for the first time.

summary: Archytas died.
text: Archytas, Greek philosopher, mathematician and statesman (or 350 BC) (b. 428 BC)

summary: Dionysius II was restored to power in Syracuse.
text: Dionysius II is restored to power in Syracuse.

summary: Carthaginians ravaged and blockaded Entella in Sicily.
text: Carthaginians ravage and blockade Entella.

summary: Timoleon landed in Sicily, defeated Dionysius II and Hicetas, and occupied Syracuse.
text: The aristocracy of Syracuse appeal to their mother city of Corinth against their tyrant Dionysius II. The Corinthian general Timoleon is chosen to lead a liberation force to Sicily. Landing at Tauromenium (Taormina) on March 21st, Timoleon faces two armies, one under Dionysius and the other under Hicetas (tyrant of nearby Leontini), who has also called in Carthaginian forces. By shrewd tactics Timoleon defeats his enemies and occupies Syracuse.

summary: Dionysius II went into exile following the invasion of Syracuse by Timoleon.
text: Dionysius II goes into exile once more after the successful invasion by Timoleon of Corinth.

summary: King Archidamus III of Sparta sailed to Italy with mercenaries to aid Tarentum and other Greek colonies against the Lucanians and Bruttians.
text: The native Italian tribes, the Lucanians and Bruttians, press down upon the Greek colonies of Magna Graecia, including Tarentum. Responding to calls for help from these former Greek colonies, King Archidamus III of Sparta sets sail with a band of mercenaries for Italy.

summary: Timoleon took control of Syracuse, allowed the deposed tyrant Dionysius II to retire into exile at Corinth, and reformed the Syracusan constitution.
text: After his surrender to the Corinthian general Timoleon, who takes over as ruler of Syracuse, the former tyrant, Dionysius II, is allowed to retire to Corinth to live in exile, although he dies within the year. The Syracusan constitution is changed by Timoleon with the new constitution designed to have safeguards against tyranny. Timoleon invites new settlers from Greece to come to Sicily.

summary: The First Samnite War began between Rome and the Samnites over disputed territory in the Middle Liris Valley.
text: First Samnite War began when Rome fought the confederated Samnites over disputed territory in the Middle Liris Valley.

summary: Dionysius II, former tyrant of Syracuse, died in exile.
text: Dionysius II, tyrant of Syracuse (b. c. 397 BC)

summary: A Roman army routed a Samnite force near Mount Barbaro in the Battle of Mount Gaurus.
text: Battle of Mount Gaurus: A Samnite force was routed by a Roman army near Mount Barbaro.

summary: Timoleon expanded his control across Sicily, removing several tyrants and preparing defenses against a threatened Carthaginian invasion.
text: The Corinthian general Timoleon spreads his rule over Sicily, removing a number of other tyrants and preparing Sicily for another threatened Carthaginian invasion.

summary: Roman forces led by Marcus Valerius Corvus defeated the Samnites at the Battle of Mount Gaurus near Cumae.
text: The Battle of Mount Gaurus is fought between the Romans and the Samnites. The battle is a success for the Romans, who, it is said, are led by Marcus Valerius Corvus. Fought at the foot of Mount Gaurus, near Cumae, it is the most notable engagement of the First Samnite War.

summary: The Roman Republic enacted the Leges Genuciae, barring simultaneous holding of offices, setting a ten-year hiatus between terms, and banning interest on loans.
text: The Leges Genuciae were passed, banning a person from holding two offices at the same time, or during any ten-year period; charging interest on loans was also banned.

summary: The Roman Senate agreed to peace with the Samnites after they appealed to an earlier treaty of friendship.
text: Samnite Wars: The Senate agreed a peace, following an appeal by the Samnite to a previous treaty of friendship.

summary: Timoleon defeated a Carthaginian army at the Battle of the Crimissus, confining Carthaginian control to western Sicily.
text: Hicetas, the tyrant of Leontini, again persuades Carthage to send a large army to Sicily, which lands at Lilybaeum. Timoleon of Syracuse meets this large Carthaginian army in the Battle of the Crimissus in the west of Sicily and achieves a brilliant victory against superior odds. Despite this victory, the Carthaginians continue to occupy the western half of Sicily, with a treaty being concluded that confines the Carthaginians to the area west of the Halycus (Platani) River.

summary: The Roman Senate rejected an embassy demanding political equality for the Latins, precipitating the Latin War.
text: An embassy is sent by the Latin peoples to the Roman Senate asking for the formation of a single republic between Rome and Latium, in which both parties would be considered to be equal. As Rome considers that it is the leader of the Latin League, it refuses to treat the Latin people as being equal politically, or to have Latin people in the Roman Senate. With Rome's refusal of the proposal, the Latin War begins. The Latins fight with the Campanians, while Rome joins the Samnites to attack the Latins. Only the Laurentes in Latium and the equites of Campania remain with the Romans, who, for their part, find support among the Paeligni.

summary: A Roman-Samnite army under consuls Publius Decius Mus and Titus Manlius Torquatus defeated the Latins and Campanians at the Battle of Vesuvius.
text: The Roman-Samnite army under consuls Publius Decius Mus and Titus Manlius Torquatus attack and defeat the Latins and Campanians near Mount Vesuvius in the Battle of Vesuvius.

summary: The Romans detached Campania from the Latins, granting Roman citizenship to Capua and Cumae and expanding their territory to the Bay of Naples.
text: The Romans succeed in detaching the Campanians from their alliance with the Latins (through their fear of the Samnites) and induce them to make a separate peace. Three Campanian cities, including Capua and Cumae, are granted Roman citizenship and thus become part of the Roman state. The Roman state now extends to the Bay of Naples.

summary: The Roman politician and future consul Appius Claudius Caecus was born.
text: Appius Claudius Caecus, Roman politician and consul

summary: The Latin League invaded Samnium at the outbreak of the Latin War.
text: Latin War: The Latin League invaded Samnium.

summary: Roman consul Titus Manlius Imperiosus Torquatus defeated the Latins in the Battle of Trifanum.
text: The Roman consul Titus Manlius Imperiosus Torquatus defeats the Latins in the Battle of Trifanum.

summary: The Roman Republic passed a law requiring the election of at least one plebeian censor every five years.
text: A law was passed which required the election of at least one plebeian censor every five years.

summary: Lucanians defeated and killed King Archidamus III of Sparta and his troops at Manduria.
text: King Archidamus III of Sparta, after five years of campaigning in southern Italy, fails to achieve any decisive results and while leading a mercenary army to help Tarentum against the Lucanians, is killed with most of his troops at Manduria in Calabria.

summary: Timoleon defeated Hicetas of Leontini and concluded a peace treaty with Carthage bounding Carthaginian territory west of the Halycus River.
text: Carthage makes another effort to conquer all of Sicily. The Carthaginians dispatch some mercenaries to extend the conflict between Timoleon and the Sicilian tyrants. But this effort ends in the defeat of Hicetas, the tyrant of Leontini, who is taken prisoner and put to death. By a treaty between Syracuse and Carthage, the dominion of Carthage in Sicily is confined to the lands west of the Halycus (Platani) River.

summary: Timoleon deposed two tyrants in Sicily before retiring to private life.
text: With peace finally achieved with Carthage, Timoleon of Syracuse is able to depose two more tyrants in Sicily and then retires into private life.

summary: Rome ended the Latin War, dissolving the Latin League and incorporating many Latin cities into the Roman state.
text: The Latin War ends with the Latin League being dissolved and the individual Latin cities having to accept Rome's terms. Many of the cities are incorporated into the Roman state. In making peace with the cities of the defeated Latin League, Rome offers liberal terms. The men of many of these cities are granted citizenship and, as a result, Rome gains friends rather than enemies.

summary: Rome captured Antium, ending Volscian resistance and bringing the Volsci into alliance with Rome.
text: With the fall of their chief city, Antium, to the Romans, the Volsci finally abandon their resistance against the Romans and accept an alliance with Rome.

summary: Archidamus III, King of Sparta, was killed in battle at Manduria.
text: Archidamus III, king of Sparta (killed in battle)

summary: A plebeian was elected praetor of Rome for the first time.
text: A plebeian is chosen to be praetor of Rome for the first time.

summary: Minucia, a Vestal Virgin, was convicted of unchastity at Rome.
text: Minucia, a Vestal Virgin, is convicted of unchastity.

summary: Greek statesman and general Timoleon died in Syracuse.
text: Approximate date – Timoleon, Greek statesman and general (b. c. 411 BC)

summary: Marcus Valerius Corvus was elected consul of the Roman Republic for the fourth time.
text: Marcus Valerius Corvus is elected consul of the Roman Republic for the fourth time.
