As a result, the Dalmatians are compelled to pay tribute to Rome, which puts an end to the first Dalmatian war. In recognition of his victory, Corculum is granted a triumph in Rome.

summary: The Lusitanians raided Roman provinces in Hispania while the Celtiberians of Numantia revolted against Roman occupation.
text: The Lusitanians harry the inhabitants of the Roman provinces in Hispania. At the same time, the Celtiberians of Numantia on the Douro revolt against their Roman occupation.

summary: Attalus II Philadelphus of Pergamon defeated King Prusias II of Bithynia with assistance from Cappadocia and Rome.
text: After a two-year struggle, Attalus II Philadelphus of Pergamum is finally able to defeat Prusias II, the aggressive king of Bithynia in northern Anatolia. He is assisted in his battle against Prusias II by Ariarathes V of Cappadocia (who has sent his son Demetrius to command his forces) and by the Romans.

summary: Prusias II sent his son Nicomedes to Rome to appeal for Roman assistance in reducing war reparations demanded by Attalus II.
text: After his victory, Attalus II insists on heavy reparations from Prusias II. In response, Prusias II sends his son Nicomedes to Rome to ask the Romans' help in reducing the amount of these reparations.

summary: Ptolemy VI Philometor defeated his brother Ptolemy VIII Physcon on Cyprus but restored him to rule Cyrenaica.
text: The Egyptian king Ptolemy VI Philometor defeats his brother, Ptolemy VIII Euergetes, after he attempts to seize Cyprus by force. Nevertheless Philometor restores his brother to Cyrenaica, marries one of his daughters to him, and grants him a grain subsidy.

summary: Roman politician and reformer Gaius Gracchus was born.
text: Gaius Gracchus, Roman politician, younger brother of Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, who, like him, will pursue a popular political agenda that ultimately ends in his death (d. 121 BC)

summary: Roman philologist Lucius Aelius Stilo Praeconinus was born.
text: Lucius Aelius Stilo Praeconinus, Roman philologist (d. 74 BC)

summary: The Roman Republic moved the start of the consular year to January 1 to deal with military crises in Hispania.
text: The uprisings in Rome's Hispanic provinces oblige the year's consuls to take office earlier than the traditional date of 15 March, a change that becomes permanent. Some suggest that, as a consequence, January 1 becomes the first day of the Roman year.

summary: Attalus II of Pergamon and Ptolemy VI of Egypt backed the pretender Alexander Balas against Seleucid king Demetrius I Soter.
text: The Seleucid king Demetrius I Soter's relations with Attalus II Philadelphus of Pergamum and Ptolemy VI Philometor of Egypt deteriorate to the point where they support a rival claimant to the Syrian throne, Alexander Balas, who claims to be the son of the former Seleucid king Antiochus IV Epiphanes and, therefore, a first cousin of Demetrius. He has been "discovered" by Heracleides, a former minister of Antiochus IV and brother of Timarchus, who has been executed by Demetrius I Soter in 160 BC after leading a revolt against him in Media.

summary: Demetrius I Soter granted extensive concessions to Jonathan Apphus to secure Judea, permitting him to fortify Jerusalem as High Priest.
text: As a result of the rise of the pretender, Alexander Balas, Demetrius I Soter is forced to recall most of his garrisons in Judea. To retain control of Judea, he makes a bid to gain the loyalty of Jonathan Maccabeus, whom he permits to recruit an army and to take back the hostages that the Syrians are holding in the city of Acre. Jonathan gladly accepts these terms, takes up residence in Jerusalem and begins to fortify the city, becoming High Priest of Jerusalem until 143 BC.
names: List of high priests of Israel

summary: A powerful earthquake destroyed large sections of the Greek city of Sicyon.
text: Substantial parts of the city of Sikyon are destroyed by an earthquake.

summary: Alexander Balas appointed Jonathan Apphus as High Priest in Jerusalem to secure his allegiance against Demetrius I Soter.
text: The pretender to the Seleucid throne, Alexander Balas, makes contact with Jonathan Maccabeus offering him terms even more favorable than those offered by the king Demetrius I Soter. In particular, Alexander offers him the official appointment as High Priest in Jerusalem. In response, Jonathan withdraws his support from Demetrius and declares his allegiance to Alexander. Thus Jonathan becomes the first member of his family to achieve appointment as High Priest.

summary: Former consul, censor, and Pontifex Maximus Marcus Aemilius Lepidus died.
text: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, Roman statesman, consul, Pontifex Maximus and censor; as a praetor, he has been governor of Sicily in 191 BC.

summary: Roman jurist Marcus Porcius Cato Licinianus, son of Cato the Elder, died.
text: Marcus Porcius Cato Licinianus, Roman jurist, son of Cato the Elder by his first wife, Licinia.

summary: Carthage completed the repayment of its war indemnity to Rome and declared the Second Punic War treaty expired.
text: The Carthaginian debt to Rome is fully repaid, meaning that, according to Carthage, the treaty with Rome, which was put in place at the end of the Second Punic War, is no longer in force. The Romans do not agree with this interpretation. Instead they view the treaty as a permanent declaration of Carthaginian subordination to Rome.

summary: Numidia launched a border raid and besieged a town on Carthaginian soil, prompting Carthage to dispatch an army of 25,000 soldiers.
text: Numidia launches another border raid on Carthaginian soil, besieging a town. In response Carthage launches a large military expedition (25,000 soldiers) to repel the Numidian invaders.

summary: Scipio Aemilianus secured the support of Cato the Elder to release the remaining Achaean hostages held in Rome.
text: At Polybius' request, Scipio Aemilianus manages to gain the support of the Roman statesman Cato the Elder (whose son has married Scipio's sister Aemilia) for a proposal to release (and return to Greece) the 300 Achaean internees who are still being held without trial after being deported to Rome in 167 BC.

summary: Roman forces assisted the allied Greek port of Massilia against raids by Celts from Cisalpine Gaul.
text: Roman forces help the thriving Greek commercial port of Massilia combat raids from the Celts from Cisalpine Gaul.

summary: Roman forces led by Lucius Licinius Lucullus and Servius Sulpicius Galba arrived in Hispania Ulterior and halted the Celtiberian revolt at Numantia.
text: Roman armies under the leadership of praetor Servius Sulpicius Galba and the proconsul Lucius Licinius Lucullus arrive in Hispania Ulterior and begin the process of subduing the local population. The revolt of the Celtiberians of Numantia is stopped.

summary: Lucius Licinius Lucullus sent Scipio Aemilianus to Numidia to obtain war elephants from King Masinissa.
text: Scipio Aemilianus is sent by the Roman general, Lucius Licinius Lucullus, to Numidia to obtain some elephants from the Numidian king Masinissa, the friend of his grandfather Scipio Africanus. While there, he witnesses a great but indecisive battle between the Numidians and the Carthaginians. The latter then ask Scipio Aemilianus to arrange a settlement, but the negotiations break down.

summary: The Roman Senate demanded satisfaction from Carthage for waging war without consent and began assembling an army.
text: The Roman Senate shows displeasure with Carthage's decision to wage war against its neighbour without Roman consent, and tells Carthage that in order to avoid a war it has to "satisfy the Roman People". The Roman censor, Cato the Elder, urges the destruction of Carthage and the Roman Senate orders the gathering of an army.

summary: Alexander Balas defeated and killed Demetrius I Soter in battle to become ruler of the Seleucid Empire with Roman support.
text: The pretender to the Seleucid throne, Alexander Balas, who claims to be the son of the late Antiochus IV, defeats the Seleucid king, Demetrius I Soter, in battle and kills him. The Roman Senate, along with Attalus II Philadelphus of Pergamum and Ptolemy VI Philometor of Egypt, support Alexander Balas and he becomes the ruler of the Seleucid Empire. Demetrius I Soter's son, Demetrius, goes into exile in Crete.

summary: Seleucid king Alexander Balas married Cleopatra Thea, daughter of King Ptolemy VI Philometor of Egypt.
text: The new king of the Seleucid Empire, Alexander Balas, marries Cleopatra Thea, a daughter of Ptolemy VI Philometor of Egypt.

summary: Nicomedes rebelled against his father King Prusias II of Bithynia after uncovering a plot by the king to assassinate him in Rome.
text: Nicomedes, the son of king Prusias II of Bithynia, who has been sent to Rome to argue for smaller reparations arising from his father's unsuccessful war against Pergamum, gains the support of the Roman Senate to the point where Prusias sends an emissary with secret orders to assassinate Nicomedes. However, the emissary reveals the plot to Nicomedes and persuades him to rebel against his father.

summary: Mithridates V Euergetes succeeded his uncle Mithridates IV as king of Pontus and reaffirmed an alliance with Rome.
text: Mithridates V Euergetes succeeds his uncle Mithridates IV Philopator Philadelphus as king of Pontus. He continues the strategy of maintaining an alliance with the Romans which was started by his predecessor.

summary: Roman praetor Servius Sulpicius Galba defeated the Lusitanians in Hispania, treacherously massacred 9,000 during peace talks, and enslaved 20,000.
text: The Romans, led by praetor Servius Sulpicius Galba, defeat the Lusitanians in a major battle in Hispania. summary: The Cimbri and Teutones defeated a Roman consular army under Gnaeus Papirius Carbo at the Battle of Noreia.
text: Battle of Noreia: The Cimbri and Teutones cross the Danube and enter the lands of the Celtic tribe, the Taurisci (centered in what is now Austria and north-eastern Italy). The latter sent emissaries to Rome, seeking help in dealing with the migration. The Senate sends consul Gnaeus Papirius Carbo across the Julian Alps, to deal with the migration at the head of an army (some 30,000 men). He offers guides to escort them out of the territory of the Taurisci. The guides are instructed to lead the tribes to the town of Noreia, where Carbo sets an ambush. The Cimbri manage to discover Carbo's plan, they turn the tables and defeat the Romans during an ambush. Carbo manages to escape with the remnants of his consular army (some 6,000 men) during a heavy thunderstorm. Later, he is indicted by the Senate for losing the battle, but escapes conviction by committing suicide.

summary: Consul Gaius Marius defeated Saturninus and Glaucia under the senatus consultum ultimum, and renegade senators stoned them to death in the Curia Hostilia.
text: Late summer–autumn: Saturninus stands for tribune again for the following year, and is elected. His associate, the praetor Gaius Servilius Glaucia, attempts to stand for the consulship (illegally, as praetors cannot immediately become consul). A rival candidate, Gaius Memmius, is found murdered by agents of Saturninus and Glaucia, who are declared public enemies by the Senate. The Senate issues the senatus consultum ultimum, and Marius, as consul, defeats his former ally in battle in the Forum. Saturninus and his followers surrender on condition that their lives are spared, but they are stoned to death with roof tiles in the Curia Hostilia by renegade senators.

text: Lex Pompeia grants Latin rights to cities in Cisalpine Gaul.

summary: The Roman Republic annexed the city of Pompeii.
text: Pompeii is annexed by the Roman Republic.

summary: Cicero ended his military service in the Roman army.
text: Cicero ends his service in the Roman army.

summary: Mithridates VI of Pontus invaded Bithynia and Cappadocia, initiating the First Mithridatic War.
text: Mithridates VI of Pontus invades Bithynia and Cappadocia, thus beginning the First Mithridatic War.

summary: Roman politician and general Marcus Aemilius Lepidus was born.
text: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, Roman politician and general (d. 12 BC)

summary: Roman praetor Aulus Sempronius Asellio was murdered in Rome by creditors.
text: Aulus Sempronius Asellio, Roman praetor (murdered by creditors)

summary: Roman consul and general Lucius Porcius Cato was killed at the Battle of Fucine Lake.
text: Lucius Porcius Cato, Roman politician and general

summary: Prominent Roman politician Marcus Aemilius Scaurus died.
text: Marcus Aemilius Scaurus, Roman politician (b. c. 163 BC)

summary: Roman general Titus Didius was killed in battle during the Social War.
text: Titus Didius, killed in battle during the Social War

summary: The Social War ended with the defeat of the Italian allies by the Roman Republic.
text: The Social War ends with the defeat of the Italian allies by the Romans.

summary: Sulla became the first Roman commander to march on Rome and take the city by force.
text: August: The consul Lucius Cornelius Sulla becomes the first Roman commander to march on Rome with his army and to capture the city by force. This extraordinary act is prompted by his desire to maintain his proconsular command for the First Mithridatic War in Asia Minor. Sulla then murdered his enemy P. Sulpicius Rufus and forced Gaius Marius to flee to Africa.

summary: The Dardani, Scordisci, and Maedi attacked the Roman province of Macedonia.
text: The Dardani, Scordisci, and the Maedi attack the Roman province of Macedonia.

summary: Mithridates VI of Pontus invaded Greece and Asia Minor, dismantled the Roman province of Asia, and ordered the massacre of resident Italians.
text: May – King Mithridates VI of Pontus invades Greece. Defeating the Roman forces four times in succession, he conquers Bithynia, Phrygia, Mysia, Lycia, Pamphylia, Ionia and Cappadocia. The Roman province of Asia is dismantled. On the king's orders, the local authorities in every city of the province round up and put to death all resident Italians in a single day (App.Mith.§§85–91). Plutarch (Sulla 24.4) says that 150,000 are killed, other sources calculate a figure of 80,000 people.

summary: Former Roman consul Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus died.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, Roman consul

summary: Former Roman consul Manius Aquillius was captured and executed by Mithridates VI of Pontus.
text: Manius Aquillius, Roman consul and general

summary: Ptolemy X Alexander I, king of Egypt, died during a naval battle near Cyprus.
text: Ptolemy X Alexander I, king (pharaoh) of Egypt

summary: Roman tribune Publius Sulpicius Rufus was murdered by order of Sulla.
text: Publius Sulpicius Rufus, Roman tribune of the plebs, murdered by Sulla

summary: Roman consul and jurist Quintus Mucius Scaevola Augur died.
text: Quintus Mucius Scaevola Augur, Roman consul

summary: Marsi commander Quintus Poppaedius Silo was killed in battle during the Social War.
text: Quintus Poppaedius Silo, Italian tribe leader

summary: Lucius Cornelius Cinna and Gaius Marius marched on Rome, seized the city, and restored Cinna's consulship.
text: Gnaeus Octavius and Lucius Cornelius Cinna are inaugurated as consuls. With Cinna seeking to enrol the Italians into all the tribes, he is expelled from the city by Octavius and replaced as consul by Lucius Merula. Mobilising against the regime at Rome, Cinna marches on the city, occupies it with the support of Gaius Marius, and regains his consulship. In the aftermath Octavius is killed, Merula is forced to suicide.

summary: Sulla arrived in Greece and began the siege of Athens while Lucullus gathered a fleet.
text: First Mithridatic War: Siege of Athens (87–86 BC) – Sulla arrives in Greece and from Autumn besieges Athens. He orders Lucius Licinius Lucullus to raise a fleet from Rome's allies around the eastern Mediterranean.
names: Siege of Athens and Piraeus (87–86 BC)

summary: The Antikythera mechanism was manufactured.
text: Antikythera mechanism manufactured.

summary: Roman consul Lucius Munatius Plancus was born.
text: Lucius Munatius Plancus, Roman consul

summary: Former Roman consul Gaius Atilius Serranus was killed during the Marian-Cinnan purge.
text: Gaius Atilius Serranus, Roman consul and senator

summary: Roman politician Gaius Julius Caesar Strabo was murdered in Rome.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Strabo, Roman politician

summary: Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo, Roman general and politician, died during the siege of Rome.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo, Roman general and politician

summary: Lucius Cornelius Merula committed suicide in Rome during the Marian purges.
text: Lucius Cornelius Merula, Roman politician and priest

summary: Lucius Julius Caesar was killed in Rome by partisans of Gaius Marius.
text: Lucius Julius Caesar, Roman consul (killed by partisans of Gaius Marius)

summary: Marcus Antonius was executed in Rome on the orders of Gaius Marius and Lucius Cornelius Cinna.
text: Marcus Antonius, Roman consul (executed by order of Marius and Cinna)

summary: Publius Licinius Crassus was killed in Rome by invading Marian forces.
text: Publius Licinius Crassus, Roman consul and censor (killed by Marians invading Rome)

summary: Quintus Ancharius was executed in Rome by order of Gaius Marius.
text: Quintus Ancharius, Roman politician (executed by order of Marius and Cinna)

summary: Roman forces landed in Epirus during the First Mithridatic War.
text: First Mithridatic War: Roman forces landed at Epirus.

summary: Lucius Cornelius Sulla captured Athens from the Pontic army and removed the tyrant Aristion.
text: First Mithridatic War: March 1 – Siege of Athens (87–86 BC) ends when Sulla captures Athens from the Pontic army, removing the tyrant Aristion.
names: Siege of Athens and Piraeus (87–86 BC)

summary: Lucius Licinius Lucullus decisively defeated the Pontic fleet at the Battle of Tenedos.
text: First Mithridatic War: Lucius Licinius Lucullus decisively defeats the Mithridatic fleet in the Battle of Tenedos.

summary: Lucius Cornelius Sulla defeated the Pontic army under Archelaus at the Battle of Chaeronea.
text: First Mithridatic War: The Roman forces of Lucius Cornelius Sulla defeat the Pontic forces of Archelaus in the Battle of Chaeronea.

summary: Lucius Cornelius Sulla defeated the Dardani after they allied with the Kingdom of Pontus.
text: First Mithridatic War: The Dardani ally with Pontus and are defeated by Sulla soon after.

summary: Roman historian Sallust was born in Amiternum.
text: Sallust, Roman historian (d. 34 BC)

summary: Fausta Cornelia, daughter of Lucius Cornelius Sulla, was born.
text: Fausta Cornelia, twin sister of Faustus Cornelius Sulla, wife of Gaius Memmius and later of Titus Annius Milo

summary: Faustus Cornelius Sulla, son of Lucius Cornelius Sulla, was born.
text: Faustus Cornelius Sulla, Roman senator, son of the dictator Lucius Cornelius Sulla (d. 46 BC)

summary: Gaius Marius died in Rome during his seventh consulship.
text: Gaius Marius, Roman general and politician (b. c. 157 BC)

summary: Aristion, tyrant of Athens, was executed following the Roman capture of the city.
text: Aristion, Greek philosopher and tyrant

summary: Lucius Cornelius Sulla defeated the Pontic forces under Archelaus at the Battle of Orchomenus.
text: First Mithridatic War: Lucius Cornelius Sulla again defeats Archelaus in the decisive Battle of Orchomenus.

summary: Atia, niece of Julius Caesar and mother of Augustus, was born.
text: Atia, niece of Julius Caesar and mother of Augustus (d. 43 BC)

summary: Marcus Junius Brutus, Roman politician and assassin of Julius Caesar, was born.
text: Marcus Junius Brutus, conspirator and assassin in the murder of Julius Caesar

actor: Tiberius Claudius Nero (father of Tiberius Caesar)
summary: Tiberius Claudius Nero, Roman politician and father of the emperor Tiberius, was born.
text: Tiberius Claudius Nero, Roman politician and father of Tiberius (d. 33 BC)
cast: Tiberius Claudius Nero (father of Tiberius Caesar)
names: Tiberius Claudius Nero (father of Tiberius Caesar)

summary: Gaius Julius Caesar, Roman praetor and father of Julius Caesar, died in Rome.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar, Roman politician (b. c. 140 BC)

summary: Stoic philosopher Mnesarchus of Athens died.
text: Mnesarchus of Athens, Stoic philosopher (b. c. 160 BC)

summary: Rome and the Kingdom of Pontus agreed to a peace treaty restoring pre-war borders.
text: First Mithridatic War: A peace was agreed between Rome and Pontus under which the latter returned to its pre-war borders.

summary: The First Mithridatic War between the Roman Republic and the Kingdom of Pontus concluded.
text: The First Mithridatic War comes to an end.

summary: Julius Caesar married Cornelia, the daughter of Lucius Cornelius Cinna.
text: Julius Caesar marries Cornelia

summary: Roman poet Catullus was born in Verona.
text: Catullus, Roman poet (d. c. 54 BC)

summary: Roman politician Publius Servilius Casca was born.
text: Servilius Casca, Roman politician (d. c. 42 BC)

summary: Greek book collector Apellicon of Teos died.
text: Apellicon of Teos, Greek book collector

summary: Roman general Gaius Flavius Fimbria committed suicide after his legions defected to Sulla.
text: Gaius Flavius Fimbria, Roman politician and general (suicide)

summary: Roman consul Lucius Cornelius Cinna was killed in a mutiny of his troops at Ancona.
text: Lucius Cornelius Cinna, Roman consul (killed by mutinying troops)

summary: Lucius Cornelius Sulla landed at Brundisium and defeated Gaius Norbanus at the Battle of Mount Tifata.
text: Spring – Lucius Cornelius Sulla returns to Italy from his campaigns in Greece and lands with his legions unopposed at Brundisium. He defeats the popular forces of Gaius Norbanus in the Battle of Mount Tifata.

summary: Pompey raised a private army of three legions in Picenum to support Sulla.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius, age 22, raises, on his own initiative, a private army of three legions from his father's veterans and ' in Picenum.

summary: Lucius Licinius Murena attacked the forces of Mithridates VI, starting the Second Mithridatic War.
text: Lucius Licinius Murena, the Roman governor of Asia, clashes with the Pontic forces of Mithridates VI, starting the Second Mithridatic War.

summary: A fire destroyed the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the Sibylline Books in Rome.
text: A fire breaks out which burns down the Temple of Jupiter (Jupiter Capitolinus) and destroys the collection of Sibylline Books.

summary: The Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the Tabularium were completed on the Capitoline Hill in Rome.
text: Two new buildings were completed on the Capitoline Hill in Rome: the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the Tabularium.

summary: Tigranes the Great entered Syria and ended Seleucid rule over the region.
text: Tigranes the Great, King of Armenia was invited by a faction in the Seleucid civil wars, entered Syria and effectively ended Seleucid rule. Though a weakened Seleucid monarchy was briefly restored after Roman victories, ongoing instability led Pompey to abolish the dynasty and annex Syria as a Roman province in 63 BC.

summary: Fulvia, later a prominent Roman matron and wife of Mark Antony, was born.
text: Fulvia, Roman matron and wife of Mark Antony

summary: Julia, daughter of Julius Caesar and Cornelia, was born in Rome.
text: Julia, daughter of Julius Caesar and Cornelia

summary: Roman politician and general Mark Antony was born in Rome.
text: Mark Antony, Roman politician and General (who later married Cleopatra) (d. 30 BC)

summary: Seleucid king Philip I Philadelphus died in Syria.
text: Philip I Philadelphus, Seleucid king

summary: Sulla defeated Gaius Marius the Younger at the Battle of Sacriportus and captured Rome.
text: April: Sulla defeats the consul Gaius Marius the Younger at the Battle of Sacriportus, and takes control of Rome.

summary: Sulla defeated an allied army of Samnites and Lucanians at the Battle of the Colline Gate.
text: November 1: Sulla defeats an army of Samnites and Lucanians alliance in the Battle of the Colline Gate.

summary: Sulla slaughtered Samnite prisoners at the Villa Publica after the Roman Senate rejected his proscription plan.
text: November 2: Sulla slaughters the Samnite prisoners in the Villa publica; the senate rejects his proscription plan.

summary: Sulla passed his proscriptions through a popular assembly and published a death list of senators and equites.
text: November 3: Sulla passes his proscription through a popular assembly; he publishes a list of 520 senators and equites to be murdered on sight.

summary: Gaius Marius the Younger committed suicide after being besieged at Praeneste.
text: Gaius Marius the Younger is besieged at the fortress city of Praeneste in Latium. After a fierce resistance, Marius commits suicide.

summary: Pompey was dispatched by Sulla to eliminate Marian rebels in Sicily and Africa.
text: Pompey is ordered by Sulla to stamp out Marian rebels in Sicily and Africa, after his campaigns in he gets the insulting nickname of adulescentulus carnifex, the "teenage butcher".

summary: Lucius Licinius Murena launched a raid against Pontus at the Battle of the Halys, starting the Second Mithridatic War.
text: Lucius Licinius Murena launches a raid against Pontus in the Battle of Halys, starting the Second Mithridatic War.

summary: Burebista unified the Dacian tribes and established the Dacian Kingdom.
text: Burebista unifies the Dacian population forming the first (and biggest) unified Dacian Kingdom, on the territory of modern Romania and surroundings. 82 BC is also the starting year of his reign.

summary: Roman orator and poet Gaius Licinius Macer Calvus was born.
text: Licinius Macer Calvus, Roman orator and poet (d. c. 47 BC)

summary: Roman orator and politician Marcus Caelius Rufus was born.
text: Marcus Caelius Rufus, Roman orator and politician (d. c. 48 BC)

summary: Roman poet Varro Atacinus was born in Gallia Narbonensis.
text: Varro Atacinus, Roman poet and writer (d. c. 35 BC)

summary: Gallic chieftain and leader Vercingetorix was born in the territory of the Arverni.
text: Vercingetorix, Gaul warrior and leader (d. 46 BC)

summary: Roman politician and general Gaius Carrinas was executed by order of Sulla.
text: Gaius Carrinas, Roman politician and general (executed by order of Sulla)

summary: Roman politician and governor Gaius Fabius Hadrianus died after being burned alive in Utica.
text: Gaius Fabius Hadrianus, Roman politician and governor

summary: Marian general Gaius Marcius Censorinus was executed on the orders of Sulla.
text: Gaius Marcius Censorinus, Roman politician and general (executed by order of Sulla)

summary: Roman consul Gaius Marius the Younger committed suicide while besieged at Praeneste.
text: Gaius Marius the Younger, Roman politician (commits suicide)

summary: Roman politician Gaius Norbanus committed suicide on Rhodes to avoid capture by Sulla.
text: Gaius Norbanus, Roman consul and governor (commits suicide)

summary: Former consul Gnaeus Papirius Carbo was executed in Sicily by order of Pompey and Sulla.
text: Gnaeus Papirius Carbo, Roman consul (executed by order of Sulla)

summary: Roman praetor Marcus Marius Gratidianus was brutally executed by Sulla's partisans in Rome.
text: Marcus Marius Gratidianus, Roman praetor and politician (executed by order of Sulla)

summary: Pontifex Maximus Quintus Mucius Scaevola was murdered in Rome on the orders of Gaius Marius the Younger.
text: Quintus Mucius Scaevola Pontifex, Roman consul (murdered by order of Marius the Younger)

summary: Roman politician and poet Quintus Valerius Soranus was executed by order of Sulla.
text: Quintus Valerius Soranus, Roman politician and Latin poet (executed by order of Sulla)

summary: Sulla was appointed dictator of the Roman Republic.
text: Sulla's civil war: Sulla was declared dictator.

summary: Sulla governed as dictator, executed opponents through proscriptions, and enacted constitutional reforms.
text: Sulla is appointed dictator, executes his political enemies in a series of proscriptions, and implements aristocratic reforms to the Roman government.

summary: Cicero won his first major legal case while defending Publius Quinctius in Rome.
text: Cicero wins his first case.

summary: Marian general Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus was defeated and killed in Africa by Pompey.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, Roman politician

summary: Ptolemy IX Lathyros, ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, died.
text: Ptolemy IX Lathyros, king of Ptolemaic Egypt

summary: Lucius Licinius Murena withdrew his Roman forces from Pontus on Sulla's orders, ending the Second Mithridatic War.
text: Second Mithridatic War: Murena withdrew from Pontus.

summary: Sulla resigned his position as dictator after implementing his constitutional reforms.
text: Sulla resigns dictatorship after enacting numerous reforms in the same year.

summary: Sulla served his final consulship and retired from Rome at the end of the term.
text: rowspan="2" | | | Final consulship of Sulla, he leaves Rome once the year is over.

summary: Quintus Sertorius landed on the Iberian Peninsula to support a rebellion among the Lusitanians.
text: Sertorian War: Quintus Sertorius landed on the Iberian Peninsula in support of a Lusitanian rebellion.

summary: Quintus Sertorius returned to the Iberian Peninsula and initiated a campaign against Sullan forces.
text: Quintus Sertorius re-enters Iberia with a tiny army (2,600 men) and opens a successful campaign against the Sullan forces.

summary: Quintus Sertorius defeated the Roman army under Lucius Fulfidias at the Battle of the Baetis River in Hispania.
text: Battle of the Baetis River: A force of Populares exiles under Sertorius defeat the legal Roman army of Lucius Fulfidias in Hispania, starting the Sertorian War; Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius takes command on behalf of Sulla.

summary: Sulla occupied Pompeii and established it as a Roman colony for veteran soldiers.
text: Pompeii becomes the Roman colony Colonia Cornelia Veneria Pompei when Sulla occupies the city with at least 4,000 soldier-colonizers.

summary: Ptolemy XII Auletes succeeded Ptolemy XI Alexander II to the throne of Egypt.
text: Ptolemy XII Auletes succeeds Ptolemy XI Alexander II to the throne of Egypt.

summary: Ptolemy XI Alexander II married Berenice III and then murdered her.
text: Ptolemy XI marries Berenice III, but murders his bride for unknown reasons.

summary: Alexandria came under Roman jurisdiction.
text: Alexandria comes under Roman jurisdiction.

summary: Roman artists began visually extending room spaces using painted landscapes, cityscapes, and stage scenes.
text: Roman artists begin to extend the space of a room visually with painted scenes of figures on a shallow stage or with a landscape or cityscape.

summary: Scribonia, later the second wife of Augustus, was born.
text: Scribonia, wife to the Roman Emperor Augustus (d. AD 16)

summary: Berenice III, queen regnant of Egypt, was murdered.
text: Berenice III, queen regnant of Egypt (b. 120 BC)

summary: Caecilia Metella Dalmatica, wife of Sulla, died.
text: Caecilia Metella Dalmatica, daughter of Lucius Caecilius Metellus Dalmaticus

summary: Lucius Cornelius Chrysogonus, a Greek freedman of Sulla, died.
text: Lucius Cornelius Chrysogonus, Greek freedman

summary: Ptolemy XI Alexander II, king of Egypt, was lynched in Alexandria.
text: Ptolemy XI Alexander II, king (pharaoh) of Egypt

summary: Sulla resigned from his dictatorship over the Roman Republic.
text: Sulla renounces his dictatorship.

summary: Cicero traveled to Athens and Rhodes to continue his studies in philosophy and oratory.
text: Cicero travels to Athens and then to Rhodes to continue his studies of philosophy and oratory.

summary: Sulla died in Campania.
text: Sulla dies in Campania

summary: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus became consul in Rome, opposed the Sullan constitution, and rebelled after being sent to Transalpine Gaul.
text: In Rome, Marcus Aemilius Lepidus becomes consul. He attempts to undermine the Sullan reforms, quarrels with his consular colleague, is sent to govern Transalpine Gaul, and initiates a rebellion against the Senate with his army there.

summary: Publius Servilius Vatia conducted a successful campaign against pirates in southern Anatolia.
text: The Senate sends Publius Servilius Vatia to Cilicia as governor, where he fights a successful campaign against the Piracy in southern Anatolia (Lycia, Pamphylia and Isauria), he is thereafter known by the agnomen Isauricus.

summary: The Tabularium was built in the Roman Forum.
text: The Tabularium is built in the Forum.

summary: The Third Dalmatian War began between Rome and the Dalmatae.
text: The Third Dalmatian war begins.

summary: Julius Caesar returned to Rome after serving in the Roman army for two years.
text: Julius Caesar returns to Rome after about two years of service in the army

summary: Lucius Cornelius Sulla, Roman general and statesman, died.
text: Lucius Cornelius Sulla, Roman general and statesman (b. 138 BC)

summary: Quintus Lutatius Catulus defeated Marcus Aemilius Lepidus at the Milvian Bridge outside Rome.
text: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, Roman proconsul of Transalpine Gaul and leader of the Populares faction in the senate, is defeated by Quintus Lutatius Catulus at the Milvian bridge outside Rome. The remnants of the rebels are wiped out by Pompey in Etruria.

summary: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus escaped to Sardinia with his troops and died shortly afterward.
text: Lepidus, with some 21,000 troops, manages to escape to Sardinia. Soon afterwards he becomes ill and dies, his battered army, now under command by Marcus Perperna Vento, sails on to the Iberian Peninsula.

summary: Pompey marched through Gallia Narbonensis into Spain to assist Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius against Quintus Sertorius.
text: Pompeius marches along the Via Domitia through Gallia Narbonensis crossing the Pyrenees to Spain. He joins with Quintus Metellus Pius to suppress the revolt of Quintus Sertorius, but is at first unsuccessful.

summary: Tigranes the Great founded the city of Tigranakert in Artsakh.
text: The city of Tigranakert of Artsakh is built.

summary: Berenice IV Epiphaneia, future queen of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, was born.
text: Berenice IV Epiphaneia, Greek princess and queen of the Ptolemaic Kingdom (d. 55 BC)

summary: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, Roman statesman and former consul, died.
text: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, Roman statesman and consul (b. 120 BC)

summary: Titus Quinctius Atta, Roman comedic poet and playwright, died.
text: Titus Quinctius Atta, Roman comedy writer

summary: Salome Alexandra succeeded her late husband Alexander Jannaeus as queen of Judea.
text: Salome Alexandra becomes queen of Judea, after the death of her husband, Alexander Jannaeus, until 67 BC.

summary: Hyrcanus II became High Priest of Jerusalem following the death of his father Alexander Jannaeus.
text: Hyrcanus II becomes high priest of Jerusalem for the first time, on the death of his father, Alexander Jannaeus, until 66 BC.

summary: Gaius Cosconius captured Salona, successfully concluding the Third Dalmatian War for Rome.
text: The Third Dalmatian war ends with the capture of Salona by proconsul Gaius Cosconius and the victory of Rome.

summary: Quintus Sertorius defeated Pompey at the Battle of Lauron in Hispania Citerior.
text: On the Iberian Peninsula, in the Roman province of Hispania Citerior, the rebel forces of Quintus Sertorius defeat the republican army of Pompey the Great at the Battle of Lauron.

summary: Alexander Jannaeus, king and high priest of Judea, died.
text: Alexander Jannaeus, king and high priest of Judea

summary: Tribune Quintus Opimius spoke out against Sullan restrictions on the tribunate in Rome.
text: In Rome, the tribune Quintus Opimius speaks out against Sullan restrictions on the tribunate, in orations noted for sarcasm against conservatives.

summary: Cicero served as quaestor in western Sicily.
text: Cicero is quaestor in Western Sicily.

summary: Nicomedes IV of Bithynia bequeathed his kingdom to Rome upon his death, prompting Mithridates VI of Pontus to invade.
text: Nicomedes IV of Bithynia bequeaths his kingdom to Rome on his death (75/4 BC). Angered by the arrangement, Mithridates VI of Pontus declares war on Rome and invades Bithynia, Cappadocia and Paphlagonia, thus starting the Third Mithridatic War.

summary: Mithridates VI of Pontus defeated Marcus Aurelius Cotta at the Battle of Chalcedon.
text: Third Mithridatic War: Marcus Aurelius Cotta is defeated by Mithridates in the Battle of Chalcedon.

summary: Pompey defeated an army of Sertorian rebels at the Battle of Valentia.
text: In the Roman province of Hispania Citerior a republican army under Pompey the Great defeats an army of Sertorian rebels at the Battle of Valentia.

summary: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius defeated Sertorian rebels at the Battle of Italica.
text: In the Roman province of Hispania Ulterior a republican army under Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius defeats an army of Sertorian rebels at the Battle of Italica.

summary: Quintus Sertorius defeated a Roman republican army under Pompey at the Battle of Sucro.
text: In the Roman province of Hispania Citerior an army of Sertorian rebels under Quintus Sertorius himself defeats a republican army under Pompey the Great at the Battle of Sucro.

summary: Pompey and Metellus fought Quintus Sertorius to a draw at the Battle of Saguntum, forcing Sertorius to withdraw.
text: At the Battle of Saguntum the republican forces on the Iberian Peninsula and the Sertorian rebels fight each other to a draw. Quintus Sertorius is forced to withdraw leaving the battlefield to Pompey and Metellus (the republican commanders).

summary: After being captured and ransomed by Cilician pirates, Julius Caesar raised a fleet and crucified the pirates at Pergamon.
text: Julius Caesar travels to Rhodes to study under Apollonius Molon. On his way across the Aegean Sea, he is kidnapped by Cilician pirates and held prisoner in the Dodecanese islet of Pharmacusa. The young Caesar is held for a ransom of twenty talents, but he insists they ask for fifty. After his release Caesar raises a fleet at Miletus, pursues and crucifies the pirates in Pergamon.

summary: The Golden Age of Latin Literature began.
text: Start of Golden Age of Latin Literature.

summary: Calpurnia, Roman noblewoman and later wife of Julius Caesar, was born.
text: Calpurnia, Roman noblewoman and wife of Julius Caesar

summary: Roman politician and poet Gaius Asinius Pollio was born.
text: Gaius Asinius Pollio, Roman politician and poet (d. AD 4)

summary: Gaius Herennius, legate to Quintus Sertorius, was killed at the Battle of Valentia.
text: Gaius Herennius, tribune of the plebs in 80 BC and legate to Quintus Sertorius during the Sertorian War, killed at the Battle of Valentia.

summary: Lucius Hirtuleius, commander under Quintus Sertorius, was killed at the Battle of Saguntum.
text: Lucius Hirtuleius, right-hand-man of Quintus Sertorius during the Sertorian War, killed at the Battle of Saguntum.

summary: Gaius Memmius died at the Battle of Saguntum.
text: Gaius Memmius, brother-in-law of Pompey the Great, died at the Battle of Saguntum.

summary: Nicomedes IV bequeathed his kingdom to the Roman Senate upon his death.
text: Nicomedes IV, last king of Bithynia bequeaths his kingdom to the Roman Senate upon his death (75/4 BC)

summary: Roman forces under Lucius Lucullus defeated the forces of Mithridates VI of Pontus at Cyzicus.
text: Third Mithridatic War: Battle of Cyzicus: Roman forces under Lucius Lucullus defeat the forces of Mithridates VI of Pontus.

summary: Praetor Marcus Antonius received wide-ranging powers to fight pirates throughout the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Marcus Antonius (father of Mark Antony), a praetor, receives wide-ranging powers and considerable resources to fight the pirates in the Mediterranean Sea.

summary: Publius Servilius Vatia celebrated a triumph in Rome against pirates in Anatolia and received the agnomen Isauricus.
text: Publius Servilius Vatia returns to Rome, where he has triumphed against the pirates in Anatolia, and is given the agnomen Isauricus.

summary: Cyrene became a Roman province.
text: Cyrene becomes a Roman province.

summary: Pompey founded the city of Pamplona.
text: Pamplona is founded.

summary: Roman philologist Lucius Aelius Stilo Praeconinus died.
text: Lucius Aelius Stilo Praeconinus, Roman philologist

They defeat a small Roman force and equip themselves with captured military equipment as well with gladiatorial weapons. Spartacus and his band of gladiators plunder the region surrounding Capua and retire to a defensible position on Mount Vesuvius.

text: Third Servile War: Spartacus moves with his followers northward to the Po Valley. Roman forces under Lucius Gellius Publicola defeat a group of slaves (30,000 men) led by Crixus near Mount Gargano. He kills two-thirds of the rebels, including Crixus himself.

summary: Spartacus defeated the Roman legions under Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Clodianus and Lucius Gellius.
text: Summer – Spartacus and his followers defeat the Roman forces under Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Clodianus and Gellius, forcing the Roman legions to retreat in disarray. Both consuls are recalled to Rome in disgrace and relieved of their duties.

summary: Spartacus defeated Roman forces under Gaius Cassius Longinus outside Mutina.
text: Spartacus moves north again, to cross the Alps into Gaul and then to Thracia. Outside Mutina on the plain of the River Po he defeats the Roman forces under Gaius Cassius Longinus, governor of Gallia Cisalpina.

summary: Spartacus and his followers withdrew south to the Bruttium peninsula while the Roman Senate dispatched Marcus Licinius Crassus to confront them.
text: Autumn – Spartacus and his followers withdraw to the Bruttium peninsula. At one juncture he contemplates attacking Rome – but moves south. The Senate sends Marcus Licinius Crassus against Spartacus.

summary: Marcus Licinius Crassus attempted to trap Spartacus in southern Italy by constructing a fortified trench and rampart near Thurii.
text: Winter – Spartacus decides to camp near Thurii. Marcus Licinius Crassus with ten Roman legions tries to trap the rebels in the toe of Italy. He builds a trench and a low earth rampart (with a fortified palisade).

summary: Lucius Lucullus defeated Mithridates VI at the Battle of Cabira and overran Pontus, forcing Mithridates to flee to Armenia.

text: Cyprus becomes a Roman province.

summary: Julius Caesar began military campaigns that opened the Gallic Wars.
text: First year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

summary: Julius Caesar became proconsul and invaded Gaul with six Roman legions and various auxiliary troops.
text: Julius Caesar becomes a provincial governor (proconsul) and leads a Roman army (6 Roman legions; Legio VII, Legio VIII, Legio IX, Legio X, and newly levied Legio XI and Legio XII) into Gaul. He deploys auxiliaries as part of this army, including Balearic slingers, Numidian and Cretan archers, and Celtic/Gallic cavalry (such as the allied Aedui).

summary: Julius Caesar built a nineteen-mile earthwork with fortifications and watchtowers between Lake Geneva and the Jura Mountains.
text: Caesar builds a 19-mile earthwork, complete with fortifications and watchtowers, between Lake Geneva and the Jura Mountains.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated the migrating Helvetii at the Battle of the Arar.
text: June – Caesar defeats the migrating Helvetii in the Battle of the Arar (Saône).

summary: Julius Caesar decisively defeated the Helvetii at the Battle of Bibracte.
text: July – Caesar decisively defeats the Helvetii in the Battle of Bibracte.

summary: Julius Caesar decisively defeated the Suebi under King Ariovistus at the Battle of Vosges.
text: September – Caesar decisively defeats the Suebi led by King Ariovistus in the Battle of Vosges.

summary: Julius Caesar stationed his legions in winter quarters among the Sequani in Burgundy and returned to Cisalpine Gaul.
text: Winter – Caesar leaves his legions in winter quarters among the Sequani (located in modern-day Burgundy) far to the north of the formal boundary of Gallia Transalpina. He returns to Gallia Cisalpina, carrying out judicial and administrative activities.

summary: Berenice IV became queen of Egypt after temporarily dethroning her father Ptolemy XII Auletes.
text: Berenice IV becomes queen of Egypt after temporarily dethroning her father, King Ptolemy XII Auletes.

summary: Attica, future wife of Roman general Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, was born.
text: Attica, first wife of the Roman general Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa

summary: Ptolemy of Cyprus, the last Hellenistic king of Cyprus, died.
text: Ptolemy of Cyprus, last Hellenistic king of Cyprus

summary: Publius Cornelius Lentulus Spinther and Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Publius Cornelius Lentulus Spinther and Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos.

summary: Julius Caesar entered the second year of the Gallic Wars.
text: Second year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

summary: Julius Caesar raised two new legions, bringing his army in Gaul to eight legions.
text: Spring – Julius Caesar raises a further two legions (Legio XIII and Legio XIV), bringing his army in Gaul to eight legions (at which strength it remains until 54 BC).

summary: Servius Sulpicius Galba led the Twelfth Legion into Alpine territory and occupied Octodurus.
text: Caesar sends Servius Sulpicius Galba with Legio XII into the territory of the Nantuates, Seduni and the Veragri. He occupies Octodurus (modern-day Martigny) in Switzerland.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated a Belgic army near Bibrax and advanced north against the Nervii and Aduatuci.
text: Caesar defeats a Belgic army near Bibrax (modern-day Laon) in the territory of the Remi. He moves northwards against the Belgic tribes, the Nervii and the Aduatuci.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated the Belgic forces led by King Galba at the Battle of the Axona.
text: May – Battle of the Axona: Caesar defeats the forces of the Belgae under King Galba of the Suessiones.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated the Nervii at the Battle of the Sabis after surviving an ambush.
text: July – Battle of the Sabis: Caesar defeats the Nervii, Roman forces are almost annihilated in an ambush.

summary: Julius Caesar besieged and captured Aduatuca.
text: September – The siege and capture of Aduatuca (modern-day Tongeren) by Caesar.

summary: Mithridates IV became king of Parthia.
text: Mithridates IV becomes king of Parthia.

summary: Boduognatus, leader of the Nervii, died in battle against the Romans.
text: Boduognatus, leader of the Nervii

summary: Cleopatra VI, queen of Egypt, died.
text: Cleopatra VI, queen of Egypt

summary: Phraates III, king of Parthia, died.
text: Phraates III, king of Parthia

summary: Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Marcellinus and Lucius Marcius Philippus served as Roman consuls.
text: Roman Consuls are Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Marcellinus and Lucius Marcius Philippus.

summary: Marcus Caelius Rufus was acquitted of poisoning charges brought by Clodia following Cicero's Pro Caelio defense.
text: Clodia accuses her former lover Marcus Caelius Rufus of trying to poison her. The trial ends with the defendant acquitted thanks to the Pro Caelio speech of Cicero. There is no more reference to the formerly well-known Clodia.

summary: Julius Caesar continued his campaign during the third year of the Gallic Wars.
text: Third year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

summary: Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus defeated the Veneti fleet at Quiberon Bay during the Battle of Morbihan.
text: Battle of Morbihan: Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus, one of Caesar's subordinates, defeats the Veneti of Brittany. The Gauls lose most of their warships to the Romans in a sea battle at modern-day Quiberon Bay. The strongholds on the coast are stormed, and the population is slaughtered or sold into slavery.

summary: Julius Caesar, Pompey, and Marcus Licinius Crassus renewed their alliance at the Luca Conference.
text: The three Roman politician-generals of the First Triumvirate — Caesar, Pompey and Crassus — meet at the Luca Conference at the town of Luca (modern Lucca, in Tuscany), near Pisa, where they renewed their fraying political alliance, and further cemented the three men's increasing consolidation of power in the Roman Republic.

summary: Julius Caesar attacked the Morini and Menapii before retreating into Gallia Belgica due to adverse weather.
text: Autumn – Julius Caesar leads an attack on the Morini and the Menapii tribes of the Belgae on the North Sea. They withdraw into their forests, creating difficulties for Caesar's supply lines. The onset of bad weather forces him to pull back into Gallia Belgica.

summary: Cassivellaunus overthrew and killed King Imanuentius of the Trinovantes, causing Mandubracius to flee to Gaul.
text: This year, or possibly the following year, the king of the Trinovantes called Imanuentius, is overthrown and killed by his rival Cassivellaunus. His son Mandubracius flees to Gaul and appeals to Julius Caesar for help.

summary: Roman politician and general Lucius Licinius Lucullus died.
text: Lucius Licinius Lucullus, Roman politician (b. 118 BC)

summary: Philip II Philoromaeus, the former ruler of the Seleucid Empire, died.
text: Philip II Philoromaeus, king of the Seleucid Empire

summary: King Imanuentius of the Trinovantes died in Britain.
text: Imanuentius, the king of the Trinovantes (a kingdom in Pre-Roman Britain)

summary: Marcus Licinius Crassus and Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Marcus Licinius Crassus and Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus.

summary: Consuls Marcus Licinius Crassus and Pompey enacted the Lex Trebonia.
text: Consuls Marcus Licinius Crassus and Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus pass the Lex Trebonia.

summary: Pompey built Rome's first permanent stone theater on the Campus Martius.
text: Pompey's Theater, the first permanent (non-wooden) theatre in Rome is built. Built of stone on the Field of Mars, it included a temple to Venus Victorious, a public courtyard, and a meeting hall or curia in the far end near the "Sacred Area".

summary: Julius Caesar continued his military operations in the fourth year of the Gallic Wars.
text: Fourth year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

object: List of ancient tribes in Illyria
summary: Julius Caesar campaigned in Illyricum against the Pirustae for raiding Roman territory.
text: Spring – Julius Caesar starts the season campaigning in Illyricum (in the Balkan region) against the Pirustae, who have been raiding Roman territory.
names: List of ancient tribes in Illyria

summary: Julius Caesar defeated the Germanic Usipetes and Tencteri tribes after they crossed the Rhine River.
text: Summer – Julius Caesar defeats the Usipetes and the Tencteri, two Germanic tribes who have been driven across the Rhine River by the Suebi. He spreads Roman law and order, and makes the whole country as far as the Channel accessible to trade.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated a Germanic army and massacred camp followers near modern-day Kessel.
text: May – Julius Caesar defeats a Germanic army and massacres the women and children near the Meuse and Rhine Rivers (now known as the city of Kessel in the Netherlands).

summary: Julius Caesar constructed a wooden bridge and crossed the Rhine River between Andernach and Neuwied.
text: June – Julius Caesar crosses the Rhine River near modern-day Koblenz. He constructs a wooden bridge between Andernach and Neuwied (Germany).

summary: Julius Caesar commanded the first Roman invasion of Britain before withdrawing back to Gaul.
text: August 22 or August 26 – Julius Caesar commands his first invasions of Britain, likely a reconnaissance-in-force expedition, in response to the Britons giving military aid to his Gallic enemies. Caesar retreats back to Gaul when the majority of his force is prevented from landing by storms.

summary: Surena defeated the Roman-backed claimant Mithridates IV of Parthia in the Battle of Seleucia.
text: Mithridates IV, claimant to the throne of Parthia, supported by Aulus Gabinius, Roman governor of Syria, is defeated by Surena, general under Orodes, in the Battle of Seleucia.

summary: The Roman Latin poet Tibullus was born.
text: Tibullus, Roman Latin poet

summary: Archelaus, high priest of Comana in Cappadocia, died.
text: Archelaus, high priest of Comana (Cappadocia)

summary: Berenice IV Epiphaneia, queen of Egypt, died.
text: Berenice IV Epiphaneia, queen of Egypt (b. 77 BC)

summary: The Roman philosopher and poet Lucretius died.
text: Lucretius, Roman philosopher (b. c. 99 BC)

summary: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos Iunior, former Roman consul, died.
text: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos Iunior, Roman consul

summary: Tigranes the Great, ruler of Armenia, died.
text: Tigranes the Great, Armenian Emperor (b. c. 140 BC)

summary: Appius Claudius Pulcher and Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Appius Claudius Pulcher and Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus.{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Cadoux |first1=Theodore John |last2=Seager |first2=Robin J. |author2-link=Robin Seager |date=2012 |title=Claudius (RE 297) Pulcher (3), Appius |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-1640?rskey=Og8k2L&result=4 |encyclopedia=
