summary: Julius Caesar waged the fifth year of his Gallic Wars campaign.
text: Fifth year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

summary: Julius Caesar received submission from Cassivellaunus and installed Mandubracius as an allied king during his second invasion of Britain.
text: July – Second of Caesar's Invasions of Britain: Julius Caesar receives nominal submission from the tribal chief Cassivellaunus and installs Mandubracius as a friendly king.

summary: Ambiorix initiated a revolt against Roman forces in Gaul.
text: Winter – Ambiorix revolts in Gaul.{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Scullard |first1=Howard Hayes |author1-link=Howard Hayes Scullard |last2=Drinkwater |first2=John Frederick |author2-link=John F. Drinkwater |date=2012 |title=Ambiorix |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-345?rskey=Dqx9ZG&result=1 |encyclopedia=

summary: Pompey built the first permanent stone theatre in Rome.
text: Pompey builds the first permanent theatre in Rome.

summary: Marcus Licinius Crassus arrived in Syria as proconsul and invaded the Parthian Empire, initiating the Roman-Persian Wars.
text: Crassus arrives in Syria as proconsul and invades the Parthian Empire, initiating the Roman–Persian Wars, which were to last nearly seven centuries.

summary: Gaius Claudius Marcellus married Octavia the Younger.
text: Octavia the Younger and Gaius Claudius Marcellus marry.

summary: Future Roman consul Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Augur was born.
text: Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus, Roman consul (d. AD 25)

summary: The Roman rhetorician and writer Seneca the Elder was born.
text: Seneca the Elder, Roman rhetorician and writer

summary: The Roman poet Tibullus was born.
text: Tibullus, Roman poet and writer (d. 19 BC)

summary: Aurelia Cotta, the mother of Julius Caesar, died.
text: Aurelia Cotta, mother of Julius Caesar (b. 120 BC)

summary: Ariovistus, chieftain of the Suebi, died.
text: Ariovistus, leader of the Suebi (approximated date)

summary: The Roman poet Gaius Valerius Catullus died.
text: Gaius Valerius Catullus, Roman poet and writer (b. 84 BC)

summary: Julia, daughter of Julius Caesar and wife of Pompey, died in childbirth.
text: Julia, daughter of Julius Caesar (dies in childbirth)

summary: Lucius Aurunculeius Cotta, a Roman legate serving Julius Caesar, was killed in Gaul.
text: Lucius Aurunculeius Cotta, Roman legate of Julius Caesar

summary: Lucius Gellius Publicola, Roman politician and former consul, died.
text: Lucius Gellius Publicola, Roman politician

summary: Lucius Valerius Flaccus, Roman tribune and praetor, died.
text: Lucius Valerius Flaccus, Roman tribune and praetor

summary: Orodes II executed his rival brother Mithridates IV of Parthia.
text: Mithridates IV, king of Parthia (executed by Orodes II)

summary: Quintus Laberius Durus, a Roman tribune serving Julius Caesar, died in Britain.
text: Quintus Laberius Durus, Roman tribune of Julius Caesar

summary: Quintus Titurius Sabinus, a Roman legate serving Julius Caesar, was killed during the revolt in Gaul.
text: Quintus Titurius Sabinus, Roman legate of Julius Caesar

summary: General Surena defeated and killed Marcus Licinius Crassus at the Battle of Carrhae, securing victory for the Parthian Empire.
text: The Parthian Empire achieved a decisive victory against Rome at the Battle of Carrhae, where General Surena defeated and killed Roman triumvir Marcus Licinius Crassus. According to some historical interpretations, the Mahestan (Parthian noble council) supported preparations for the defense of the empire and advised the king during the military mobilization.

summary: Marcus Valerius Messalla Rufus and Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Marcus Valerius Messalla and Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus.

states.value: Marcus Valerius Messalla Rufus and Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus

summary: Marcus Licinius Crassus sacked the temple at Hierapolis and the Temple in Jerusalem before marching against Parthia.
text: Parthian War: Crassus sacks the Temple of Hierapolis and the Temple in Jerusalem on his way to engage the Parthians.

summary: Julius Caesar suppressed a revolt led by Ambiorix near the Sambre river in Northern Gaul.
text: Gallic War: Julius Caesar suppresses a revolt led by Ambiorix near Sabis (Northern Gaul).

summary: The Carnutes massacred Roman merchants at Cenabum.
text: Gallic War: At Cenabum (modern Orléans) Roman merchants are massacred by the Carnutes.

summary: The Arverni chieftain Vercingetorix launched a major revolt against Julius Caesar across Central Gaul.
text: Gallic War: Vercingetorix, an Arverni chieftain, leads a revolt against Caesar in Central Gaul.

summary: Julius Caesar enrolled non-citizen soldiers in Gallia Transalpina to form Legio V Alaudae, expanding his army to ten legions.
text: Gallic War: Winter – Caesar enrolls non-citizen soldiers in Gallia Transalpina, genesis of Legio V Alaudae. He increases his army to ten legions.

summary: Artavasdes II became king of Armenia.
text: Artavasdes II becomes king of Armenia.

summary: Aristobulus III, future high priest of Jerusalem, was born.
text: Aristobulus III, high priest of Jerusalem (d. 36 BC)

summary: Roman captives were executed following the Battle of Carrhae.
text: May 6 (executed after the Battle of Carrhae)

summary: Roman politician and general Marcus Licinius Crassus was killed following the Battle of Carrhae.
text: Marcus Licinius Crassus, Roman politician and general

summary: Publius Licinius Crassus died at the Battle of Carrhae.
text: Publius Licinius Crassus, son of Marcus Licinius Crassus

summary: Abgar II, king of Edessa, died.
text: Abgar II, Arab king of Edessa (modern Turkey)

summary: Roman statesman and orator Gaius Scribonius Curio died.
text: Gaius Scribonius Curio, Roman statesman and orator

summary: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius Scipio and Pompey served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius Scipio Nasica and Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus.

summary: Pompey married Cornelia Metella.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius marries Cornelia Metella.

summary: Titus Annius Milo was convicted of the murder of Publius Clodius Pulcher and exiled to Massilia despite Cicero's defence.
text: Milo is tried for the murder of Clodius. Despite Cicero's legal defence (Pro Milone) he is found guilty and exiled in Massilia (modern Marseille).

summary: Julius Caesar conducted military operations during the Gallic Wars.
text: Gallic Wars (Julius Caesar):

summary: Julius Caesar besieged and captured the Gallic oppidum of Avaricum.
text: March – Siege and capture of Avaricum (Bourges).

summary: Julius Caesar was repulsed by the Gauls at the siege of Gergovia.
text: April–May – Siege and repulse from Gergovia.

summary: Julius Caesar and his German auxiliaries defeated the Gallic cavalry of Vercingetorix at the Battle of the Vingeanne.
text: July – Battle of the Vingeanne: Julius Caesar rebuffs, with his German auxiliaries, a Gallic cavalry attack of Vercingetorix.

summary: Julius Caesar besieged the Gallic stronghold of Alesia, constructing lines of circumvallation and contravallation.
text: Summer – Siege of Alesia: Julius Caesar spreads out his legions around the Oppidum and builds a string of fortifications surrounding the stronghold of Alesia.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated the Gallic relief army at the Battle of Alesia, leading to Vercingetorix's surrender.
text: September – Battle of Alesia: Julius Caesar defeats the Gallic allies coming to aid Vercingetorix, led by his cousin Vercassivellanus. Vercingetorix surrenders on October 3, signalling the Roman conquest of Gaul. The final pacification of Gaul is completed the following year.

summary: Julius Caesar led his army through snow-covered passes across the Cévennes to surprise the Arverni.
text: Winter – Julius Caesar crosses Mons Cevenna (central Gaul) and sends his army through the passes covered with snowdrifts to take the rebellious Arverni by surprise.

summary: Roman historian Fenestella was born.
text: Fenestella, Roman historian

summary: Juba II, future king of Numidia and Mauretania, was born.
text: Juba II, king of Numidia (d. AD 23)

summary: Publius Clodius Pulcher was murdered on the Appian Way by Titus Annius Milo.
text: Publius Clodius Pulcher, murdered on the Appian Way by Titus Annius Milo (b. 93 BC)

summary: Roman architect Cyrus died.
text: Cyrus, Roman architect (builder for Cicero)

summary: Gaulish chieftain Sedullos died at the Battle of Alesia.
text: Sedullos, Gaulish chieftain (b.87 BC)

summary: Parthian general Surena was executed.
text: Surena, Parthian general (b. 84 BC)

summary: Marcus Claudius Marcellus and Servius Sulpicius Rufus assumed the consulship of the Roman Republic.
text: Consuls: Marcus Claudius Marcellus and Servius Sulpicius Rufus.

summary: Pompey demanded that Julius Caesar relinquish his command before standing for consul.
text: Pompey demands that Julius Caesar lay down his command before he can stand for consul.

summary: Following the death of Ptolemy XII Auletes, Cleopatra and Ptolemy XIII became co-rulers of the Ptolemaic Kingdom.
text: by March 22 – Pharaoh Ptolemy XII Auletes dies and is succeeded by his eldest surviving daughter Cleopatra VII and her younger brother Ptolemy XIII as co-rulers of the Ptolemaic Kingdom. By August 29, official documents start listing Cleopatra as sole ruler.

summary: Roman aristocrat and future governor Publius Sulpicius Quirinius was born.
text: Publius Sulpicius Quirinius, Roman aristocrat (d. 21 AD)

summary: Ariobarzanes II, king of Cappadocia, died.
text: Ariobarzanes II (Philopator), king of Cappadocia

summary: Julia Minor, sister of Julius Caesar and grandmother of Augustus, died.
text: Julia Minor, sister of Julius Caesar (b. 100 BC)

summary: Roman praetor and governor Marcus Atius Balbus died.
text: Marcus Atius Balbus, Roman praetor and governor (b. 105 BC)

summary: Greek philosopher, astronomer, and geographer Posidonius died.
text: Posidonius, Greek philosopher, astronomer and geographer

summary: Ptolemy XII Auletes, king of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, died.
text: Ptolemy XII (Auletes), king (pharaoh) of the Ptolemaic Kingdom

summary: Lucius Aemilius Paullus and Gaius Claudius Marcellus became consuls of Rome.
text: Consuls: Lucius Aemilius Paullus and Gaius Claudius Marcellus.

summary: The Roman Senate rescinded Julius Caesar's military authority and ordered him to return, prompting him to break his alliance with Pompey.
text: The Senate recalls Julius Caesar and rescinds his authority. Caesar breaks alliance with Pompey.

summary: The Roman military artillery piece known as the scorpio was invented.
text: The Roman artillery piece called Scorpio is invented.

summary: The wall painting depicting the initiation rites of the cult of Bacchus was created at the Villa of the Mysteries in Pompeii.
text: Initiation Rites of the Cult of Bacchus, detail of a wall painting in the Villa of the Mysteries, Pompeii, is made .

summary: The Roman Republic took control of Judea.
text: The Roman Republic takes control of Judea .

summary: Antonia, daughter of Mark Antony, was born.
text: Antonia, daughter of Mark Antony

summary: Gaius Antistius Vetus, future Roman consul, was born.
text: Gaius Antistius Vetus, Roman consul (d. 1 AD)

summary: Shammai, Jewish scholar and rabbi, was born.
text: Shammai, Jewish scholar and rabbi (d. 30 AD)

summary: Aristobulus II, former king of Judea, died.
text: Aristobulus II, king of Judea

summary: Quintus Hortensius, Roman orator and advocate, died.
text: Quintus Hortensius, Roman orator and advocate (b. 114 BC)

summary: The Roman Republic defeated the last Gaulish rebels, concluding the Gallic Wars.
text: Gallic Wars: The last Gaulish rebels were defeated.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Lucius Cornelius Lentulus Crus and Gaius Claudius Marcellus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Lucius Cornelius Lentulus Crus, Gaius Claudius Marcellus.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Caesar's Civil War commenced.
text: Caesar's Civil War commences:

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: The Roman Senate rejected Julius Caesar's proposal that he and Pompey lay down their commands simultaneously, demanding Caesar surrender his immediately.
text: The Roman Senate receives a proposal from Julius Caesar that he and Pompey should lay down their commands simultaneously. The Senate responds that Caesar must immediately surrender his command.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon into Italy, initiating a civil war.
text: January – Caesar leads his army across the Rubicon, which separates his jurisdiction in Cisalpine Gaul from that of the Senate in Rome, and thus initiates a civil war.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Pompey and most of the Roman Senate fled Italy for Epirus.
text: February – Pompey's flight to Epirus (in Western Greece) with most of the Senate.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Julius Caesar advanced against Pompeian forces stationed in Spain.
text: Caesar advances against Pompeian forces in Spain.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Julius Caesar commenced the siege of Massilia against the Pompeian commander Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus.
text: Siege of Massilia: Caesar commences a siege at Massilia against the Pompeian Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus. He leaves the newly raised legions XVII, XVIII and XIX to conduct the siege. Decimus Brutus – victor over the Veneti (see 56 BC) – is in charge of the fleet to blockade the harbor.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Julius Caesar arrived in Spain and seized the passes of the Pyrenees from Pompeian commanders Lucius Afranius and Marcus Petreius.
text: June – Caesar arrives in Spain; seizes the Pyrenees passes against the Pompeians L. Afranius and Marcus Petreius.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Cicero slipped out of Italy and traveled to Thessaloniki.
text: Cicero slips out of Italy and goes to Thessaloniki.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Julius Caesar surrounded the army of Lucius Afranius and Marcus Petreius at Ilerda.
text: Caesar surrounds Afranius and Petreius's army in Ilerda.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: The Pompeian forces at Ilerda surrendered to Julius Caesar and were granted pardon.
text: Pompeians in Ilerda surrender to Caesar and are granted pardon.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Publius Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia defeated Gaius Scribonius Curio at the Battle of the Bagradas.
text: Caesar's general Gaius Scribonius Curio is defeated in North Africa by the Pompeians under Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia (whom he defeated earlier in the Battle of Utica) in the Battle of the Bagradas, after which he commits suicide.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus defeated combined Pompeian and Massilian naval forces at the siege of Massilia.
text: September – Brutus defeats the combined Pompeian-Massilian naval forces of the siege of Massilia, while the Caesarian fleet in the Adriatic Sea is defeated near Curicta (Krk).

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Massilia surrendered to Julius Caesar upon his return from Spain.
text: Massilia surrenders to Caesar, as he is coming back from Spain.

region: By place and Date / Roman Republic
summary: Julius Caesar was appointed dictator in Rome.
text: October – Caesar is appointed Dictator in Rome.

summary: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, future Roman consul, was born.
text: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, Roman consul (d. 25 AD)

summary: Aristobulus II, former king and high priest of Judea, died.
text: Aristobulus II, king and high priest of Judea

summary: Gaius Memmius, Roman orator and poet, died.
text: Gaius Memmius, Roman orator and poet (presumed).

summary: Gaius Scribonius Curio, Roman politician and general, died by suicide.
text: Gaius Scribonius Curio, Roman politician

summary: Marcus Perperna, Roman politician and censor, died.
text: Marcus Perperna, Roman politician

summary: Julius Caesar and Publius Servilius Isauricus took office as Roman consuls, with Caesar appointed for a five-year term.
text: Consuls: Gaius Julius Caesar and Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus. Caesar is named consul for a period of five years.

summary: Mark Antony arrived in Greece and joined Julius Caesar's forces.
text: Caesar's Civil War: March – Mark Antony joins Julius Caesar.

summary: Julius Caesar built fortified entrenchments and besieged Pompey at Dyrrhachium.
text: Caesar's Civil War: April – Siege of Dyrrhachium: Julius Caesar builds a fortified line of entrenchments and besieges Pompey the Great.

summary: The temple of Bellona on the Capitoline outside Rome was burnt to the ground.
text: Caesar's Civil War: The Roman temple to Bellona on the Capitolinus outside Rome is burnt to the ground.

summary: Publius Servilius Isauricus destroyed the magistrate's chair of Marcus Caelius Rufus on his tribunal.
text: Caesar's Civil War: May – Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus, co-consul with Julius Caesar, destroys Caelius's magistrate's chair on his tribunal.

summary: Pompey defeated Julius Caesar at the Battle of Dyrrhachium, forcing Caesar to retreat to Thessaly.
text: Caesar's Civil War: July 10 – Battle of Dyrrhachium: Julius Caesar barely avoids a catastrophic defeat to Pompey in Macedonia; he retreats to Thessaly.

summary: Julius Caesar decisively defeated Pompey at the Battle of Pharsalus, causing Pompey to flee to Egypt.
text: Caesar's Civil War: August – Battle of Pharsalus: Julius Caesar decisively defeats Pompey at Pharsalus, who flees to Egypt. Pompey's army by and large is pardoned.

summary: Julius Caesar captured Oricum after Lucius Manlius Torquatus surrendered the garrison.
text: Caesar's Civil War: Winter – Siege of Oricum: Julius Caesar captures the strategic city port of Oricum in Epirus (modern Albania). The garrison opens the town's gate and Lucius Manlius Torquatus surrenders to Caesar.

summary: King Pharnaces II of Pontus defeated Roman forces commanded by Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus at the Battle of Nicopolis.
text: Caesar's Civil War: December – Battle of Nicopolis: King Pharnaces II of Pontus defeats the Roman forces under Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus, a loyal partisan of Julius Caesar.

summary: King Ptolemy XIII ordered the assassination of Pompey upon his arrival in Egypt.
text: Pompey the Great is assassinated on the orders of King Ptolemy XIII, after landing in Egypt (may have occurred September 29, records unclear).

summary: Julius Caesar arrived in Alexandria, where an Egyptian delegation presented him with Pompey's severed head and signet ring.
text: October – Julius Caesar reaches Alexandria, a city founded by Alexander the Great. He is met by an Egyptian delegation from Ptolemy XIII. The Egyptians offer him gifts: the ring of Pompey and his head.

summary: Cleopatra was smuggled into the palace to meet Julius Caesar and became his mistress.
text: Queen Cleopatra VII returns to the palace rolled into a Persian carpet and has it presented to Caesar by her servant. The Egyptian princess, only twenty-one years old, becomes his mistress.

summary: Julius Caesar and Cleopatra defeated Ptolemy XIII and Arsinoe IV in Alexandria, during which part of the Library of Alexandria caught fire.
text: December – Battle in Alexandria: Forces of Caesar and his ally Cleopatra VII and those of rival King Ptolemy XIII and Queen Arsinoe IV. The latter two are defeated and flee the city, but during the battle part of the Library of Alexandria catches fire.

summary: Roman statesman Lucius Calpurnius Piso was born.
text: Lucius Calpurnius Piso, Roman consul (d. AD 32)

summary: Roman politician Publius Cornelius Scipio was born.
text: Publius Cornelius Scipio, Roman consul and governor

summary: Roman general and statesman Pompey the Great was assassinated in Egypt.
text: Pompey (the Great), Roman politician (b. 106 BC)

summary: Roman legal orator Gaia Afrania died.
text: Afriana Carfania, Roman orator

summary: Cotys I, client king of the Odrysian kingdom in Thrace, died.
text: Cotys I, Thracian client king of the Odrysian Kingdom

summary: Roman consul and orator Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Marcellinus died.
text: Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Marcellinus, Roman statesman

summary: Roman consul Lucius Cornelius Lentulus Crus was executed in Egypt.
text: Lucius Cornelius Lentulus Crus, Roman politician

summary: Roman politician Marcus Calpurnius Bibulus died near Corcyra.
text: Marcus Calpurnius Bibulus, Roman politician

summary: Roman political agitator Titus Annius Milo was killed during a rebellion in southern Italy.
text: Titus Annius Milo, Roman politician

summary: Roman orator and politician Marcus Caelius Rufus was killed at Thurii.
text: Marcus Caelius Rufus, Roman orator and politician

summary: Julius Caesar landed at Durrës in pursuit of Pompey and the Optimates.
text: Caesar's Civil War: Caesar landed at Durrës in pursuit of Pompey and his partisans the optimates.

summary: Quintus Fufius Calenus and Publius Vatinius took office as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Quintus Fufius Calenus, Publius Vatinius.

summary: Julius Caesar returned to Rome and was appointed dictator for one year.
text: Julius Caesar returns to Rome and is dictator for a year.

summary: Julius Caesar quelled a mutiny among his veteran soldiers in Rome.
text: Civil War: August – Julius Caesar quells a mutiny of his veterans in Rome.

summary: Julius Caesar invaded Africa to confront Metellus Scipio and Titus Labienus.
text: Civil War: October – Caesar's invasion of Africa, against Metellus Scipio and Labienus, Caesar's former lieutenant in Gaul.

summary: Queen Cleopatra VII promoted her younger brother Ptolemy XIV to co-ruler of Egypt.
text: Queen Cleopatra VII promotes her younger brother Ptolemy XIV of Egypt to co-ruler.

summary: Julius Caesar and Cleopatra defeated Arsinoe IV at the Battle of the Nile, leading to Ptolemy XIII's death and the relief of Alexandria.
text: February – Caesar and his ally Cleopatra VII of Egypt defeat the forces of the rival Egyptian Queen Arsinoe IV in the Battle of the Nile. Ptolemy is killed; Caesar, with the aid of Mithridates I of the Bosporus, then relieves his besieged forces in Alexandria.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated Pharnaces II of Pontus at the Battle of Zela, summarising the campaign as veni, vidi, vici.
text: Caesar defeats Pharnaces II of Pontus, king of the Bosphorus, in the Battle of Zela (the war Caesar tersely describes as veni, vidi, vici).

summary: Roman forces commanded by Aulus Gabinius defeated Alexander of Judaea at Mount Tabor.
text: Battle at Mount Tabor in Judea: Roman troops, commanded by Gabinius, defeat the forces of Alexander, son of Aristobulus II of Judea, who is attempting to re-establish Judean independence. Some 10,000 Jews die at the hands of the Romans.

summary: Caesarion, son of Julius Caesar and Cleopatra, was born.
text: Caesarion, prince of Egypt, later Ptolemy XV (d. 30 BC)

summary: Marcus Antonius Antyllus, eldest son of Mark Antony and Fulvia, was born.
text: Marcus Antonius Antyllus, son of Mark Antony and Fulvia (d. 30 BC)

summary: Pharnaces II, King of Pontus and the Bosporan Kingdom, was killed after his defeat by the Romans.
text: Pharnaces II of Pontus, king of the Bosporan Kingdom (b. c. 97 BC)

summary: King Ptolemy XIII of Egypt drowned in the Nile after his defeat in the Battle of the Nile.
text: Ptolemy XIII Theos Philopator, king of Egypt (drowned in the Nile)

summary: Hasmonean prince Alexander of Judaea was executed.
text: Alexander, Hasmonean prince (executed)

summary: Julius Caesar and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Gaius Julius Caesar, Marcus Aemilius Lepidus.

summary: Julius Caesar founded the colony of Julia Paterna Arelate at Arles for veterans of the Sixth Legion.
text: Julius Caesar establishes Julia Paterna Arelate as a colony in Gaul for veterans of the Sixth Legion, at the present day site of Arles.

summary: Titus Labienus clashed with Julius Caesar in the Battle of Ruspina.
text: Civil War: January 4 – Titus Labienus fights Julius Caesar in the Battle of Ruspina.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated Pompeian loyalists at the Battle of Thapsus.
text: Civil War: April – Caesar defeats Pompey loyalists at Thapsus.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated Metellus Scipio and Juba I at Thapsus, granting Legio V Alaudae the right to bear the elephant symbol on its shields and standards.
text: Civil War: April 6 – Caesar defeats the combined army of Pompeian followers and Numidians under Metellus Scipio and Juba I of Numidia at Thapsus. After the battle Caesar grants Legio V Alaudae the right to bear the elephant symbol on its shields and standards, for bravery against a charge of elephants.

summary: Cicero wrote to Marcus Terentius Varro urging that they serve their country through philosophical and legal writings.
text: Civil War: April 20 – Cicero, in Rome, writes to Varro "If our voices are no longer heard in the Senate and in the Forum, let us follow the example of the ancient sages and serve our country through our writings, concentrating on questions of ethics and constitutional law."

summary: Queen Cleopatra VII of Egypt and Caesarion took up residence at Julius Caesar's estate on the Tiber.
text: Civil War: Caesar's erstwhile mistress, Queen Cleopatra VII of Egypt, and his son by her, Caesarion, take up residence in one of the dictator's estates on the Tiber.

summary: Julius Caesar dedicated a temple to Venus Genetrix in Rome in fulfillment of a vow made at the Battle of Pharsalus.
text: Civil War: September 26 – Julius Caesar dedicates a temple to his mythical ancestor Venus Genetrix in fulfillment of a vow he made at the battle of Pharsalus.

summary: Julius Caesar reformed the Roman calendar to create the solar Julian calendar.
text: Civil War: Caesar reforms the Roman calendar to create the Julian calendar. The transitional year is extended to 445 days to synchronize the new calendar and the seasonal cycle. The Julian Calendar would remain the standard in the western world for over 1600 years, until superseded by the Gregorian Calendar in 1582.

summary: Julius Caesar appointed his great-nephew Octavian as his primary heir.
text: Civil War: Caesar appoints his nephew Octavian his heir.

summary: Julius Caesar subdued a mutiny among soldiers of his Tenth Legion.
text: Civil War: Caesar subdues a mutiny of his Tenth Legion.

summary: Julius Caesar celebrated his Gallic triumph in Rome, during which Vercingetorix was executed.
text: Civil War: Caesar celebrates his Gallic Triumph, after which Vercingetorix is executed. The celebrations run for forty days in Rome, and include public banquets, plays and gladiatorial games.

summary: Imhotep-Pedubast, future High Priest of Ptah, was born in Egypt.
text: Imhotep-Pedubast, High priest of Ptah (d. 30 BC)

summary: Antipater, the eldest son of Herod the Great, was born in Judea.
text: Antipater, son of Herod the Great (d. 4 BC)

summary: Lucius Seius Strabo, future praetorian prefect of Rome, was born.
text: Lucius Seius Strabo, Roman prefect of the Praetorian Guard (d. 16 AD)

summary: Roman general and politician Publius Quinctilius Varus was born.
text: Publius Quinctilius Varus, Roman politician and general (d. 9 AD)

summary: Cato the Younger committed suicide in Utica after the Pompeian defeat at Thapsus.
text: Marcus Porcius Cato (the Younger), Roman politician (b. 95 BC) (commits suicide)

summary: Roman politician Faustus Cornelius Sulla was captured and killed in North Africa.
text: Faustus Cornelius Sulla, Roman politician and quaestor

summary: King Juba I of Numidia died following the Battle of Thapsus.
text: Juba I, king of Numidia (killed after the Battle of Thapsus)

summary: Publius Sittius defeated and killed the Numidian general Saburra in battle.
text: Saburra, General of Juba I (killed in battle by Publius Sittius)

summary: Former Roman consul Lucius Afranius was captured and killed after the Battle of Thapsus.
text: Lucius Afranius, Roman consul and governor (b. 112 BC)

summary: Roman general Lucius Manlius Torquatus died after fleeing the Battle of Thapsus.
text: Lucius Manlius Torquatus, Roman politician and general

summary: Pompeian general Marcus Petreius committed suicide in Africa after the Battle of Thapsus.
text: Marcus Petreius, Roman politician and general (b. 110 BC) (commits suicide)

summary: Roman commander Metellus Scipio committed suicide at sea near Hippo Regius after his fleet was intercepted.
text: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Scipio, Roman consul and general (commits suicide)

summary: Gaulish chieftain Vercingetorix was executed in Rome following Julius Caesar's triumph.
text: Vercingetorix, Gaulish king and chieftain of the Arverni tribe (executed at the end of a triumph)

summary: Julius Caesar left Africa for Hispania in pursuit of Gnaeus and Sextus Pompey.
text: Caesar left Africa for Iberia in pursuit of Pompey's sons Gnaeus Pompeius and Sextus Pompey.

summary: Julius Caesar assumed his fourth consulship without a colleague.
text: Fourth consulship of Gaius Julius Caesar (without colleague).

summary: The Julian calendar took effect as the official civil calendar of the Roman world.
text: The Julian calendar takes effect as the civil calendar of the Roman Empire, establishing a solar calendar that is based on the Egyptian calendar of the day.

summary: Julius Caesar defeated Pompeian forces led by Titus Labienus and Gnaeus Pompeius at the Battle of Munda.
text: Civil War: In his last victory, Julius Caesar defeats the Pompeian forces of Titus Labienus and Pompey the younger in the Battle of Munda. Labienus dies in battle, Pompey the younger is executed, but Sextus Pompey escapes to take command of the remnants of the Pompeian fleet.

summary: Julius Caesar demobilized veterans of the Tenth and Thirteenth legions, settling them in Narbo and Italy.
text: The veterans of Julius Caesar's Legions Legio XIII Gemina and Legio X Equestris demobilize. The veterans of the 10th legion are settled in Narbo, while those of the 13th are given somewhat better lands in Italia itself.

summary: The Roman civil war between Julius Caesar and the Pompeian faction came to an end.
text: End of the Roman Civil War.

summary: The Roman Senate appointed Julius Caesar dictator for life.
text: Caesar is named dictator for life.

summary: Julius Caesar likely authored his Commentaries during this year.
text: Caesar probably writes his Commentaries in this year.

summary: Iullus Antonius, son of Mark Antony and Fulvia, was born in Rome.
text: Iullus Antonius, son of Mark Antony and Fulvia; consul 10 BC (d. 2 BC)

summary: Tullia, the beloved daughter of Cicero, died following childbirth.
text: February – Tullia, daughter of Cicero (b. 79 BC or 78 BC)

summary: Roman general Titus Labienus was killed fighting at the Battle of Munda.
text: March 17: Titus Labienus, Roman general (killed in the Battle of Munda) (b. c. 100 BC)

summary: Pompeian governor Publius Attius Varus was killed in combat at the Battle of Munda.
text: March 17: Publius Attius Varus, Roman governor (killed in the Battle of Munda)

summary: Gnaeus Pompeius, the elder son of Pompey the Great, was executed after fleeing the Battle of Munda.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius, son of Pompey the Great (executed after the Battle of Munda)

summary: Roman suffect consul Quintus Fabius Maximus died on the last day of his consulship.
text: Quintus Fabius Maximus, Roman general and politician

summary: Roman scholar and praetor Nigidius Figulus died while in exile.
text: Nigidius Figulus, Roman scholar (b. 98 BC)

summary: Roman politician Publius Cornelius Sulla died.
text: Publius Cornelius Sulla, Roman politician

summary: Julius Caesar and Mark Antony assumed office as consuls of the Roman Republic.
text: Consuls: Gaius Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.

summary: Julius Caesar refused a royal diadem presented by Mark Antony during the Lupercalia festival in Rome.
text: February – Rome celebrates the festival of the Lupercal. Mark Antony twice presents Caesar with a royal diadem, urging him to take it and declare himself king. He refuses this offer and orders the crown to be placed in the Temple of Jupiter.

summary: Mount Etna erupted in Sicily shortly before the assassination of Julius Caesar.
text: Shortly before March 15 – According to the Roman historian Livy, Mount Etna in Sicily erupts.{{cite journal|last=Forsyth|first=P.Y.|title=In the Wake of Etna, 44 B.C.|journal=Classical Antiquity|volume=7|issue=1|pages=49-57|year=1988|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25010878|access-date=15 October 2026

summary: Julius Caesar was assassinated in Rome by a conspiracy of senators led by Marcus Junius Brutus and Cassius.
text: March 15 (the Ides of March) – Julius Caesar, dictator of Rome, is assassinated by a group of senators, amongst them Gaius Cassius Longinus, Marcus Junius Brutus, and Caesar's Massilian naval commander, Decimus Brutus.

summary: Mark Antony delivered a funeral eulogy for Julius Caesar, inciting the Roman crowd against Caesar's assassins.
text: Caesar's funeral is held. Marcus Antony gives a eulogy and in his speech he makes accusations of murder and ensures a permanent breach with the conspirators against Caesar. He snatches Caesar's bloody tunic and purple toga to show the crowd the stab wounds; the citizens tear apart the forum and cremate their Caesar on a makeshift pyre. Antony becomes the highest ranking politician in Rome.

summary: Octavian returned from Apollonia to Rome to claim his inheritance as the adopted son of Julius Caesar.
text: April – Octavian returns from Apollonia in Dalmatia to Rome to take up Caesar's inheritance, against advice from Atia (his mother and Caesar's niece) and consul Antony.

summary: Octavian sought to win the political backing of Cicero against Mark Antony.
text: April 21 – Octavian engages in a charm offensive with consular Cicero who is fulminating against Mark Antony.

summary: Mark Antony secured a five-year governorship over Transalpine and Cisalpine Gaul.
text: June – Antony is granted a five-year governorship of northern and central Transalpine Gaul (France) and Cisalpine Gaul (Northern Italy).

summary: Cleopatra VII declared her young son Caesarion co-ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom.
text: September 2: Pharaoh Cleopatra VII of Egypt declares her son co-ruler as Ptolemy XV Caesarion.

summary: Cicero delivered and published the first of his fourteen Philippic speeches attacking Mark Antony.
text: September 2: The first of Cicero's Philippicae (oratorical attacks) on Antony is published. He will make 14 of them over the next several months.

summary: Mark Antony besieged Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus at Mutina.
text: December – Antony besieges Brutus Albinus in Mutina (Modena), with Octavian, an ally of Decimus, who is one of his uncle's assassins, close by.

summary: Roman statesman and consul Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso was born.
text: Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso, Roman statesman, consul and governor (d. 20 AD)

summary: Julius Caesar was assassinated in the Theatre of Pompey by Roman senators.
text: Julius Caesar, Roman politician and general (assassinated in the Theatre of Pompey) (b. 100 BC)

summary: Ptolemy XIV of Egypt died, presumed murdered by his sister and co-ruler Cleopatra.
text: c. August – Ptolemy XIV, king (pharaoh) of Egypt (presumed murdered) (b. c. 59 BC)

summary: Roman politician Lucius Caninius Gallus died.
text: Lucius Caninius Gallus, Roman politician, tribune

summary: Former Roman consul Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus died.
text: Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus, Roman consul

summary: Roman mercenary commander Publius Sittius was killed in Numidia.
text: Publius Sittius, Roman mercenary commander

summary: The Roman Senate appointed consuls Gaius Vibius Pansa and Aulus Hirtius and confirmed Octavian as propraetor against Mark Antony.
text: Consuls: Gaius Vibius Pansa Caetronianus and Aulus Hirtius. The Roman Senate confirms Octavian as propraetor with joint responsibility for the campaign against Antony. Hirtius and Octavian mobilize troops for the march to Mutina, while Pansa continues the levy. Embassy dispatched to treat with Antony.

states.value: Gaius Vibius Pansa Caetronianus and Aulus Hirtius

summary: The Roman Senate conferred imperium on Octavian, initiating his public political career.
text: Octavian is given imperium, marking the start of his public career.

summary: Gaius Cassius Longinus defeated the forces of Publius Cornelius Dolabella at Laodicea.
text: Marcus Junius Brutus proceeds to secure his position in Thrace and Macedonia. Gaius Cassius Longinus campaigns in Syria and defeats the army of Publius Cornelius Dolabella at Laodicea.

summary: Consul Vibius Pansa marched from Rome with four newly recruited legions to relieve Mutina.
text: March – Vibius Pansa set out to link up with Hirtius and Octavian, bringing four legions of recruits, having left one, the legio urbana, to defend Rome.

summary: At the Battle of Forum Gallorum, Mark Antony defeated consul Pansa but was routed by consul Aulus Hirtius.
text: Battle of Forum Gallorum: Mark Antony, besieging Caesar's assassin Decimus Brutus Albinus in Mutina, defeats the forces of the consul Pansa, but is then immediately defeated by the army of the other consul, Hirtius. Both consuls are killed (Hirtius does not die until after the Battle of Mutina).

summary: Octavian was proclaimed imperator by his soldiers for the first time.
text: Octavian is first proclaimed imperator by his troops.

summary: Cicero delivered his fourteenth and final Philippic against Mark Antony.
text: April 21: Cicero's 14th and last Philippic.

summary: Octavian, Decimus Brutus, and the consuls defeated Mark Antony at the Battle of Mutina.
text: April 21: Antony is again defeated in the Battle of Mutina by a coalition of Octavian, Decimus Brutus, and the two consuls of the year.

summary: Mark Antony crossed the Ligurian Alps to Vada Sabatia and united his forces with Lepidus.
text: Antony marches to Parma (which is sacked) and Placentia. He then crosses the Ligurian Alps to Vada Sabatia, south-west of Genoa, and joins with Aemilius Lepidus, soon after Decimus Brutus is killed by brigands. The Senate declares Antony a hostis, an enemy of the state. Sextus Pompey becomes supreme commander of the Roman navy and Gaius Cassius proconsul of Syria.

states.value: supreme commander of the Roman navy

summary: Gaius Cassius Longinus defeated the Rhodian fleet, captured the island of Rhodes, and plundered the city.
text: Summer – Gaius Cassius captures Rhodes after they refuse to pay tribute. Their fleet is defeated by Roman galleys in the Aegean Sea. He lands a military force on the island and plunders the city. Cassius puts to death 50 of the leading citizens and seizes all the gold he can lay hands on.

summary: Octavian entered Rome with his legions unopposed, demonstrating the collapse of Cicero's senatorial coalition.
text: July–August – Antony is again at the head of a large army; Octavian enters Rome in force without opposition. It is clear that Cicero's plan to divide them against each other has failed.

summary: Octavian assumed office as consul and enacted the lex Pedia, outlawing the assassins of Julius Caesar.
text: Octavian takes office as consul. He's prevailed to pass the lex Pedia, a law establishing the murder of Caesar as a capital crime.

summary: Octavian, Mark Antony, and Lepidus met near Bononia and formed the Second Triumvirate.
text: Octavian meets Antony and Lepidus in Bononia and the three enter into an official five-year autocratic pact, the Second Triumvirate (see lex Titia). To cement their reconciliation Octavian agrees to marry Claudia, a daughter of Antony's wife Fulvia by her former husband Publius Clodius Pulcher.

summary: The Second Triumvirate introduced proscriptions condemning hundreds of senators and equites as outlaws.
text: November – The triumvirs introduce proscriptions in which allegedly 130 senators and 2,000 equites are branded as outlaws and deprived of their property.

summary: Cicero was murdered near Formiae by triumviral soldiers, and his severed head and hands were displayed on the Rostra in Rome.
text: The orator Cicero is killed in Formiae in a litter going to the seaside, by a party led by Herennius (a centurion) and Popilius (a military tribune). His head and hands are displayed on the Rostra in the Forum Romanum.

summary: Lucius Munatius Plancus founded the Roman colony of Lugdunum.
text: Lugdunum (modern-day Lyon) is founded.

summary: The settlement of Cularo was recorded for the first time in Roman historical correspondence.
text: First reference to Cularo (Grenoble).

summary: Roman poet Ovid was born in Sulmo.
text: Ovid, Roman poet (d. AD 17/18)

summary: Princess Iotapa of Media Atropatene was born.
text: Iotapa, princess of Media Atropatene (daughter of Artavasdes I)

summary: Roman consul Iullus Antonius, son of Mark Antony, was born.
text: Iullus Antonius, Roman consul (son of Mark Antony) (suicide 2 BC)

summary: Roman consul Gaius Vibius Pansa died from wounds suffered at the Battle of Forum Gallorum.
text: Gaius Vibius Pansa, Roman consul and general (killed in battle)

summary: Roman orator and statesman Cicero was murdered under the proscriptions of the Second Triumvirate.
text: Cicero, Roman statesman and orator (murdered) (b. 106 BC)

summary: Antipater the Idumaean, procurator of Judaea and father of Herod the Great, was poisoned and died.
text: Antipater the Idumaean, Jewish founder of the Herodian dynasty (murdered)

summary: Atia, the mother of Octavian and niece of Julius Caesar, died.
text: Atia, niece of Julius Caesar and mother of Augustus (b. 85 BC)

summary: Aulus Hirtius, Roman consul and historian, was killed in battle outside Mutina.
text: Aulus Hirtius, Roman consul and historian (killed in battle)

summary: Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus, Roman statesman and assassin of Julius Caesar, was murdered while attempting to flee to Macedonia.
text: Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus, Roman statesman (murdered) (b. c. 81 BC)

summary: Decimus Laberius, a Roman knight and writer of Latin mimes, died.
text: Decimus Laberius, Roman nobleman and Latin writer (b. c. 105 BC)

summary: Gaius Trebonius, a Roman politician and assassin of Julius Caesar, was captured and killed by Publius Cornelius Dolabella at Smyrna.
text: Gaius Trebonius, Roman politician (assassin of Julius Caesar)

summary: Gaius Verres, the former Roman governor of Sicily, was proscribed and executed in exile.
text: Gaius Verres, Roman politician and governor (b. c. 120 BC)

summary: Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus, Roman consul and father-in-law of Julius Caesar, died.
text: Lucius Calpurnius Piso, Roman consul and governor (b. c. 100 BC)

summary: Lucius Minucius Basilus, Roman politician and assassin of Julius Caesar, was murdered by his own enslaved servants.
text: Lucius Minucius Basilus, Roman politician (assassin of Julius Caesar, murdered by his own slaves)

summary: Lucius Roscius Fabatus, Roman politician, was killed in the Battle of Forum Gallorum.
text: Lucius Roscius Fabatus, Roman politician (killed in battle)

summary: Pontius Aquila, Roman tribune and assassin of Julius Caesar, was killed at the Battle of Mutina.
text: Pontius Aquila, Roman politician (assassin of Julius Caesar)

summary: Publius Cornelius Dolabella, Roman suffect consul, committed suicide after being besieged in Laodicea by Gaius Cassius Longinus.
text: Publius Cornelius Dolabella, suffect consul after the assassination of Julius Caesar (b. 70 BC)

summary: Publilius Syrus, a Syrian-born Latin comic dramatist and writer of mimes, died.
text: Publilius Syrus, Syrian comic dramatist and Latin writer

summary: Quintus Pedius, Roman suffect consul who authored the law punishing Caesar's assassins, died suddenly in office.
text: Quintus Pedius, suffect consul after the assassination of Julius Caesar

summary: Quintus Tullius Cicero, Roman general and brother of Marcus Tullius Cicero, was killed during the proscriptions.
text: Quintus Tullius Cicero, Roman statesman and general (b. 102 BC)

summary: Servius Sulpicius Rufus, Roman politician and jurist, died while serving on an embassy to Mark Antony near Mutina.
text: Servius Sulpicius Rufus, Roman politician and jurist (b. c. 106 BC)

summary: Publius Vatinius surrendered his army of three legions at Dyrrachium to Marcus Junius Brutus.
text: January – Publius Vatinius, governor of Illyricum, seizes Dyrrachium and is forced to surrender his army (three legions) to Marcus Junius Brutus.

summary: Marcus Junius Brutus besieged and captured the Lycian city of Xanthus after hard fighting.
text: Marcus Brutus begins to plunder the cities of Asia Minor, in order to obtain money and soldiers. The inhabitants of Lycia refuse to submit to Rome, and Brutus besieges Xanthus. After destroying their suburbs, the Xanthians withdraw into the heavily fortified city. The Roman legionaries (2,000 men) force the gate and fight their way into the forum. The citizens make a last stand by the temple of Sarpedon and, as night falls, the Roman army conquers the city.

summary: Gaius Cassius Longinus occupied Rhodes and levied ten years of tribute on the cities of Asia.
text: The confederation of Lycia sends ambassadors to Brutus, promising to form a military league and contribute money for building ships. Gaius Cassius Longinus occupies Rhodes, and orders all the other cities of Asia to pay a tribute for 10 years.

summary: Mark Antony landed an army in Illyria and marched to Amphipolis while Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus blockaded the Adriatic Sea.
text: July – Mark Antony lands with an army (28 legions) in Illyria, leaving Octavian ill at Dyrrachium, and marches to Amphipolis. Admiral Ahenobarbus, with the Republican fleet (130 warships), blockades the Adriatic Sea.

summary: Mark Antony appointed Lucius Decidius Saxa and Gaius Norbanus Flaccus to lead an advance force of eight legions into Macedonia and Thrace.
text: August – Lucius Decidius Saxa and Gaius Norbanus Flaccus are appointed by Mark Antony, to lead an advanced force of eight legions to Macedonia along the Via Egnatia into Thrace.

summary: Lucius Decidius Saxa blocked the advance of Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus at the Corpili Pass after they crossed the Hellespont.
text: September – Brutus and Cassius cross the Hellespont. They march to Doriscus but further progress is blocked by Saxa's occupation of the Corpili Pass.

summary: The Republican forces outflanked Lucius Decidius Saxa and Gaius Norbanus Flaccus through northern mountain routes.
text: Saxa retreats to link up with Norbanus at the Sapaei Pass. The Republicans outflank the enemy, forging an alternate route through the mountains in the north.

summary: Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus fortified positions at Philippi as Mark Antony and Octavian advanced to meet them.
text: Brutus and Cassius advance to Philippi and build fortifications. Antony links up with Norbanus and Saxa at Amphipolis, Octavian arrives on a litter 10 days later.

summary: Sextus Pompeius led naval operations from Sicily and blockaded grain shipments from Spain and Africa to Italy.
text: In Sicily, Sextus Pompeius leads the naval operations in the Mediterranean Sea against the triumvirs. He blockades the grain routes from Spain and Africa.

summary: Mark Antony and Octavian fought Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus in the indecisive First Battle of Philippi, prompting Cassius to commit suicide.
text: First Battle of Philippi: The Triumvirs Mark Antony and Octavian fight an indecisive battle with Caesar's assassins Marcus Brutus and Cassius. The Roman forces including 2,000 Spartans, who have just arrived, are routed. Octavian takes refuge in the marsh. Cassius' camp is captured by Antony's men and, wrongly fearing that Brutus is dead, Cassius commits suicide. He orders his freedman Pindarus to kill him. Brutus, fearing the impact on morale, secretly buries his beheaded body on Thasos. The Republican navy, in the Adriatic, intercept and destroy the supply ships with two legions of the Triumvirs.

summary: Mark Antony and Octavian decisively defeated Marcus Junius Brutus at the Second Battle of Philippi, ending the Republican cause.
text: Second Battle of Philippi: Brutus' army is defeated by Antony and Octavian. The Triumvirs smash through the weakened Republican centre and take Brutus's right wing in their flank. After the battle, 14,000 legionaries lay down their arms. Brutus flees to the heights of Philippi, where he commits suicide the following day. After the victory, Brutus' body is brought to Antonius' camp, where he casts his purple paludamentum over his dead body and orders an honourable funeral for his erstwhile comrade. The Republican cause is crushed, and Rome rests in the hands of the Second Triumvirate.

summary: Octavian returned to Rome and arranged settlements for approximately forty thousand military veterans across Italy.
text: Octavian returns to Rome and arranges for ± 40,000 veterans' settlements in Campania, Etruria, Picenum, Samnium, Umbria, and in northern Italy.

summary: Tiberius, the future Roman emperor, was born in Rome.
text: Tiberius, Roman emperor (d. 37 AD)

summary: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, nephew and son-in-law of Octavian, was born.
text: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, nephew of Augustus (d. 23 BC)

text: Gaius Antonius, Roman general and brother of Mark Antony (murdered)

summary: Lucius Antonius and Publius Servilius Isauricus served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Lucius Antonius and Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus.

summary: Quintus Salvidienus Rufus captured and destroyed the Umbrian city of Sentinum during the Perusine War.
text: Perusine War: An armed resistance breaks out across Italy; the Umbrian city of Sentinum is captured and destroyed by Quintus Salvidienus Rufus.

summary: Octavian defeated Lucius Antonius and Fulvia in the Battle of Perugia.
text: Lucius Antonius occupies Perusia. He accepts the appeal of the local population. Lucius and Fulvia are defeated by Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian in the Battle of Perugia.

summary: Mark Antony met Cleopatra in Tarsus, formed an alliance, and ordered the execution of Arsinoe IV.
text: Mark Antony meets Cleopatra VII in Tarsus (Cilicia) and forms an alliance. He returns to Alexandria with her and they become lovers in the winter of 41–40 BC. To safeguard herself and Caesarion, she has Antony order the execution of her (half) sister Arsinoe IV, who is living at the temple of Artemis in Ephesus.

summary: Gaius Asinius Gallus Saloninus, future Roman consul, was born.
text: Gaius Asinius Gallus Saloninus, Roman consul under Caesar Augustus (d. AD 33)

summary: Arsinoe IV, Egyptian princess and sister of Cleopatra, was executed at Ephesus.
text: Arsinoe IV, Egyptian princess and (half) sister of Cleopatra VII (b. 68 or 67 BC)

summary: Serapion, an Egyptian general and governor, died.
text: Serapion, Egyptian general (strategos) and governor

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus and Gaius Asinius Pollio entered office as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus and Gaius Asinius Pollio.

summary: Lucius Antonius surrendered to Octavian at Perusia, ending the siege.
text: Siege of Perusia: trying a last attempt to break the siege, which fails; Lucius Antonius surrenders to Octavian. His life is spared, but the citizens are executed or sold into slavery. Fulvia flees with her children and is exiled to Sicyon, where she dies of a sudden illness.

summary: Octavian divorced Claudia and married Scribonia.
text: Spring – Quintus Salvidienus Rufus marches to Transalpine Gaul to take command of the eleven legions, after the death of Quintus Fufius Calenus. Octavian divorces Claudia and marries Scribonia, a sister of Lucius Scribonius Libo and a follower of Sextus.

summary: Former consul Gaius Claudius Marcellus died, leaving Octavia the Younger widowed.
text: May – Gaius Claudius Marcellus, a distinguished member of the Claudii, dies. He leaves Octavia the Younger (the elder sister of Octavian) widowed. She will later marry Mark Antony.

summary: Sextus Pompey dispatched Menas to capture Sardinia and Corsica, and besieged Cosenza and Thurii.
text: Sextus Pompey dispatches Menas with four legions and captures Sardinia, driving out Octavian's governor Marcus Lurius. He seizes the capital, Caralis and occupies Corsica. Sextus besieges Cosenza in Bruttium and Thurii in Lucania, ravaging the territory with his cavalry.

summary: Sextus Pompey's fleet raided Puteoli and Ostia, sparking a riot in the Roman Forum where Octavian narrowly escaped.
text: Sextus' fleet raids the ports of Puteoli and Ostia. The populace hold the Triumvirs responsible for prolonging the war, provoking a riot on the Forum. Octavian, with the Praetorian Guard, goes to intercept the riot, and only escapes with his life because Antony summons troops to rescue his junior colleague.

summary: The Triumvirs concluded the Treaty of Brundisium, dividing the Roman Republic into spheres of influence.
text: Treaty of Brundisium: The Triumvirs agrees to divide the Roman Republic into spheres of influence. Gaius Octavian styles himself "Imperator Caesar" and takes control of the Western provinces. Mark Antony is given the Eastern provinces; the River Drin, the boundary between the provinces Illyricum and Macedonia, is to serve as their frontier. Marcus Aemilius Lepidus controls Hispania and Africa. The treaty is cemented by the marriage of Antony and Octavia the Younger.

summary: Quintus Labienus occupied Cilicia and invaded Anatolia with Parthian forces, proclaiming himself emperor.
text: Quintus Labienus occupies Cilicia and marches, with an army, into Anatolia. Most cities surrender without resistance, except for Alabanda and Mylasa. The Parthians restore their territory to nearly the limits of the old Achaemenid Empire. Labienus proclaims himself "Parthian Emperor" of Asia Minor.

summary: Mark Antony left Alexandria for Italy and met envoys of Sextus Pompey in Athens.
text: Mark Antony leaves Alexandria. After receiving news of the outcome at Perusia while en route to Phoenicia, he sets sail for Italy meeting the ambassadors of Sextus Pompey in Athens.

summary: The philosopher Athenodorus encountered a ghost in Athens.
text: Athenodorus, a philosopher, encounters a ghost in Athens. This popular story is one of the first poltergeist stories in history.

summary: Pacorus crossed the Euphrates with Quintus Labienus and invaded Syria, capturing Antioch, Phoenicia, and Judea.
text: Pacorus crosses, with the help of Quintus Labienus, the Euphrates and invades Syria. The capital Antioch surrenders, and the Parthians take Phoenicia and Judea. However, they cannot besiege the fortified city of Tyre, because they have no fleet.

summary: Parthian forces captured Jerusalem and installed Antigonus as king, while Herod fled to Rome.
text: Parthians conquer Jerusalem. Hyrcanus II is removed from power, while Antigonus the Hasmonean becomes king of Judea under Parthian rule. Herod the Great flees Jerusalem to Rome. There he is titled king of Judea by Mark Antony.

summary: Ariobarzanes II, future Roman client king of Media Atropatene and Armenia, was born.
text: Ariobarzanes II, Roman client king of Armenia (d. 4 AD)

summary: Cleopatra Selene and Alexander Helios, twin children of Cleopatra and Mark Antony, were born.
text: Cleopatra Selene (d. AD 6) and Alexander Helios (d. between 29 and 25 BC), twins of Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony

summary: Fulvia, wife of Mark Antony, died of an illness in exile at Sicyon.
text: Fulvia, wife of Publius Clodius Pulcher and Mark Antony (b. 77 BC)

summary: Gaius Claudius Marcellus, former Roman consul, died.
text: Gaius Claudius Marcellus, Roman consul (b. 88 BC)

summary: Lucius Decidius Saxa, Roman governor of Syria, died during the Parthian invasion.
text: Lucius Decidius Saxa, Roman general and governor

summary: Phasael, prince of Judea and brother of Herod the Great, died.
text: Phasael, prince of the Herodian dynasty of Judea

summary: Quintus Fufius Calenus, Roman general and consul, died in Gaul.
text: Quintus Fufius Calenus, Roman general and consul

summary: Quintus Salvidienus Rufus, Roman general and advisor to Octavian, died.
text: Quintus Salvidienus Rufus, Roman general and advisor

summary: Simeon ben Shetach, Pharisee scholar and leader of the Sanhedrin, died.
text: Simeon ben Shetach, Pharisee scholar and prince (Nasi)

summary: Tigellius, Sardinian lyric poet and friend of Julius Caesar, died.
text: Tigellius, Sardinian lyric poet (close friend of Julius Caesar)

summary: Publius Ventidius Bassus drove Quintus Labienus out of Asia Minor and defeated him at the Taurus Mountains.
text: Marcus Antonius dispatches Publius Ventidius Bassus with 11 legions to the East and drives Quintus Labienus out of Asia Minor. Labienus retreats into Syria, where he receives Parthian reinforcements. Ventidius finally defeats him in the battle at the Taurus Mountains.

summary: Publius Ventidius defeated Pharnastanes at the Amanus Gates, reclaimed Syria, Phoenicia, and Judea, and had Quintus Labienus executed.
text: Publius Ventidius defeats Pharnastanes with his cataphracts at the Amanus Gates, and goes on to reclaim Syria, Phoenicia and Judea. Labienus flees to Cilicia, where he is captured and executed.

summary: The Triumvirate recognized Sextus Pompey's control of Sicily, Sardinia, and Corsica in the Pact of Misenum.
text: Sextus Pompey, controls Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica and the Peloponnesus, and is recognized by the Triumvirate in the Pact of Misenum. The pact helps to assure Rome's grain supply, and the blockade on Roman Italy is lifted.

summary: Antonia the Elder, daughter of Mark Antony and Octavia the Younger, was born.
text: Antonia the Elder, daughter of Mark Antony, grandmother of Nero and Messalina (d. bef. AD 25)

summary: Julia the Elder, daughter of Caesar Augustus, was born.
text: Julia the Elder, daughter of Caesar Augustus (d. AD 14)

summary: Quintus Labienus was captured and executed in Cilicia.
text: Quintus Labienus, Roman general (murdered)

summary: Augustus married Livia Drusilla, making Tiberius his stepson.
text: Augustus marries Livia Drusilla, biological mother of Tiberius making Tiberius the step-son of Augustus.

summary: The Hispanic era calendar system began in Roman Hispania.
text: Beginning of the Hispanic era.

summary: Octavian married the pregnant Livia with permission from the College of Pontiffs.
text: Octavian marries Livia while she is still pregnant from a recently broken marriage. Octavian gained permission from the College of Pontiffs to wed her while she is still pregnant from another husband. Three months after the wedding she gives birth to a second son, Nero Claudius Drusus, while he and his elder brother, the four-year-old Tiberius, are living in Octavian's household.

summary: Octavian appointed Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa governor of Transalpine Gaul, where Agrippa put down an Aquitanian rebellion and crossed the Rhine.
text: Octavian appoints Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa governor of Transalpine Gaul, where he puts down an uprising of the Aquitanians. He also fights successfully against the Germanic tribes, and becomes the next Roman general to cross the Rhine after Julius Caesar.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus, Roman politician and military commander, was born.
text: Nero Claudius Drusus, Roman politician and military commander, future stepson of Augustus Caesar (d. 9 BC)

summary: Lucius Volusius Saturninus, future Roman suffect consul, was born.
text: Lucius Volusius Saturninus, Roman suffect consul (or 37 BC)

summary: Antiochus I, king of Commagene, died.
text: Antiochus I, king of Commagene (b. c. 86 BC)

summary: Pacorus I, crown prince of Parthia, was killed in battle against Roman forces.
text: Pacorus I, crown prince of Parthia (b. c. 63 BC)

object: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Titus Statilius Taurus
summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Titus Statilius Taurus served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Titus Statilius Taurus.
names: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Titus Statilius Taurus

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa constructed the naval harbour Portus Julius near Puteoli and equipped a new fleet with the harpax.
text: Agrippa creates the harbour "Portus Julius" in the today-submersed town of Puteoli (the modern Pozzuoli, close to Naples). The port is used to train the warships for naval battles, and a new fleet is built, with 20,000 oarsmen gathered by freeing slaves. He also incorporates, on quinqueremes, a technical innovation, called the harpax ("snatcher"): a combination ballista and grappling hook, based on the corvus.

summary: Octavian concluded the Second Pact of Tarentum with Mark Antony, renewing the Second Triumvirate for five years.
text: Caesar Augustus (Octavian) engineers the "Second Pact of Tarentum" which renews the Triumvirate for an additional five years. Mark Antony exchanges 120 ships, for service against Sextus Pompeius. Octavian Caesar donates 1,000 troops from the Praetorian Guard and 20,000 legionaries for the Parthian campaign in Syria.

summary: Mark Antony reorganized Roman client kingdoms across Asia Minor, installing Polemon I over Pontus and confirming Amyntas and Archelaus.
text: Antony reorganizes Asia Minor under strongmen loyal to him. He raises troops from his allies: Amyntas and Archelaus, kings of Galatia and Cappadocia. The old kingdom of Pontus is restored, from Armenia to the River Halys under Polemon I.

summary: Roman forces captured Jerusalem from Antigonus II Mattathias and installed Herod the Great as king of Judea.
text: Romans conquer Jerusalem from the Parthians. Herod the Great becomes king of Judea and Ananelus is installed as High Priest; both positions are seized from Antigonus II Mattathias after a five-month siege. Thousands of Jews are slaughtered by Roman troops supporting Herod.
names: List of high priests of Israel

summary: Antigonus II Mattathias was executed on the orders of Mark Antony.
text: Antigonus II Mattathias (Antigonus the Hasmonean) (executed by order of Mark Antony)

summary: Aristobulus II, former king and high priest of Judea, died.
text: Aristobulus II, king and high priest of Judea (66–63 BC; assassinated)

summary: Orodes II, king of the Parthian Empire, died after being assassinated by Phraates IV.
text: Orodes II, king of the Parthian Empire (b. 95 BC)

object: Lucius Gellius Poplicola and Marcus Cocceius Nerva
summary: Lucius Gellius Poplicola and Marcus Cocceius Nerva served as Roman consuls.
text: Consuls: Lucius Gellius Poplicola and Marcus Cocceius Nerva.
names: Lucius Gellius Poplicola and Marcus Cocceius Nerva

summary: Publius Canidius Crassus invaded Armenia and Iberia, compelling King Pharnavaz II into an alliance against Caucasian Albania.
text: Publius Canidius Crassus invades Armenia and Iberia (Georgia); he forces Parnavaz II into an alliance against Zober, king of Albania.

summary: Mark Antony launched a major offensive against the Parthian Empire, marching his legions to Carana in Anatolia.
text: June – Mark Antony launches a major offensive against the Parthians, in which he marches with 10 legions and 10,000 cavalry to Carana in Anatolia.

summary: Octavian attempted to invade Sicily with his fleet from Puteoli, but was turned back by a storm off Vibo.
text: July – Octavian's fleet (102 warships) embarks from Puteoli and tries to invade Sicily, but it is caught in a storm at Vibo and forced to return.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa secured the Lipari Islands and raided the Sicilian coast while Octavian landed legions at Tauromenium.
text: August – Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, an admiral of Octavian Caesar, secures the Lipari Islands and harasses the coast from Mylae to Tyndaris. Octavian transports his legions, via Leucopetra, to Tauromenium (modern Taormina).

summary: Mark Antony crossed into Media Atropatene and began the siege of Phraaspa.
text: Antony crosses the frontier into Media Atropatene and commences the siege of Phraaspa. He establishes a line of circumvallation and builds siege engines.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa defeated Sextus Pompey at the Battle of Naulochus, forcing him to flee to Asia Minor.
text: Battle of Naulochus: Agrippa defeats Sextus Pompeius, a son of Pompeius, in a naval engagement off Naulochus. Sextus escapes with 17 ships to Messana and then to Asia Minor.

summary: Octavian absorbed the mutinous legions of Lepidus at Lilybaeum and placed him in permanent confinement in Rome.
text: Marcus Lepidus lands 12 legions from Africa and lays siege to Lilybaeum. He loses his army to Octavian when his men mutiny. Lepidus is kept in luxurious captivity in Rome until his death.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa was awarded the Naval Crown for his decisive naval victory over Sextus Pompey.
text: Agrippa receives the unprecedented honor of a Naval Crown (corona navalis), wrought of gold and decorated with the prows of ships.

summary: Mark Antony abandoned the siege of Phraaspa, retreated with heavy losses to Egypt, and married Cleopatra.
text: October – Antony abandons the siege of Phraaspa (near Maragheh, Iran). He retreats, loses many men to disease and starvation in the subsequent retreat to Egypt, and marries Cleopatra VII while still married to Octavia.

summary: Aristobulus III of Judea replaced Ananelus as High Priest in Jerusalem.
text: Judea: Aristobulus III, the last of the Hasmoneans, becomes High Priest in Jerusalem, replacing Ananelus, who has only held the position for one year.
cast: List of high priests of Israel
names: List of high priests of Israel

states.entity: List of high priests of Israel

summary: Antonia Minor, daughter of Mark Antony and Octavia the Younger, was born.
text: Antonia Minor, daughter of Mark Antony and Octavia Minor, mother of the emperor Claudius

summary: Ptolemy Philadelphus, son of Cleopatra and Mark Antony, was born.
text: Ptolemy Philadelphus, son of Cleopatra VII of Egypt and Mark Antony (d. 29 BC)

summary: Vipsania Agrippina, daughter of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Pomponia Caecilia Attica, was born.
text: Vipsania Agrippina, daughter of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Pomponia Caecilia Attica (d. AD 20)

summary: Ariarathes X, king of Cappadocia, died after being deposed by Mark Antony.
text: Ariarathes X (or Eusebes Philadelphos), king of Cappadocia

summary: Aristobulus III, high priest of Jerusalem, drowned on the orders of Herod the Great.
text: Aristobulus III, high priest of Jerusalem (Hasmonean dynasty)

summary: Phraates IV ascended the Parthian throne after eliminating Orodes II and consolidating power against the Mahestan.
text: Phraates IV ascended the Parthian throne after eliminating his father Orodes II and several royal rivals. The Mahestan (the noble council of the Parthian Empire) initially opposed his rise due to concerns about his violent methods. However, Phraates IV consolidated power by executing or exiling many council members, significantly weakening the influence of the Mahestan.

summary: Octavian organized Illyria as a Roman province and coordinated with Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa to clear the Dalmatian coast of pirates.
text: Illyria becomes a Roman province. Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian conducts a rendezvous with the Roman fleet under Agrippa, which is engaged in clearing the Dalmatian coast of piracy.{{cite journal

summary: Octavian attacked Pannonia and captured the stronghold of Siscia after a thirty-day siege.
text: Pannonia is attacked by Octavian Caesar, who conquers and sacks the stronghold Siscia (Sisak) of the Segestani, which is taken after a 30-day siege. The country is not definitely subdued, however, until 9 BC.

summary: Sextus Pompey defeated Gaius Furnius and captured Nicaea and Nicomedia in Asia Minor.
text: Sextus Pompeius defeats the governor of Asia, Gaius Furnius, with three legions and seizes Nicaea and Nicomedia (modern Izmit).

summary: Marcus Titius captured Sextus Pompey in Miletus and executed him without trial.
text: Marcus Titius arrives in Syria with a large army and marches to Asia Minor. Sextus is caught in Miletus and executed without trial.

summary: Aristobulus III, high priest of Judea, died by drowning.
text: Aristobulus III, high priest of Judea (drowned) (b. 53 BC)

summary: Roman general Sextus Pompey was executed in Asia Minor.
text: Sextus Pompeius, Roman general (executed) (b. 67 BC)

summary: Octavian pacified Dalmatia and Pannonia, creating the province of Illyricum, and forced the surrender of Promona.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian pacifies Dalmatia and Pannonia forming the province of Illyricum, while Antony regains Armenia from Parthia. Octavian reduces the outposts defending the Liburnian town of Promona, sets up siege works and forces its surrender.

summary: Mark Antony became Roman consul for the second time alongside Lucius Scribonius Libo.
text: Mark Antony becomes Roman Consul for the second time. His partner is Lucius Scribonius Libo. The latter is replaced with Aemilius Lepidus Paullus during the year.

summary: Mark Antony advanced into Armenia, marched to Artaxata, and arrested King Artavasdes II.
text: Antony advances into Armenia with an expeditionary force (16 legions) and marches to the capital Artaxata. He arrests king Artavasdes II and takes him to Alexandria.

summary: Mark Antony distributed eastern kingdoms to Cleopatra's children and named Cleopatra Queen of Kings in the Donations of Alexandria.
text: Autumn – The Donations of Alexandria: Antony distributes the eastern kingdoms as a gift to the children of Cleopatra; he declares Caesarion, Caesar's illegitimate son, as co-ruler of Egypt and Cyprus. Alexander Helios receives Armenia and Media; to Cleopatra Selene II he gives the kingdoms of Cyrenaica and Libya. His youngest son Ptolemy Philadelphus receives the Egyptian possessions in Phoenicia, Syria and Cilicia. Antony establishes Cleopatra as a Hellenistic monarch at Alexandria and gives her the title of "Queen of Kings".

summary: Octavian became consul for the second time and attacked the Donations of Alexandria in the Roman Senate.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian becomes consul for the second time. His partner is Lucius Volcatius Tullus. Octavian delivers a speech; de summa Republica in the Roman Senate, in which he subjects the Donations.

summary: The second five-year term of the Second Triumvirate expired.
text: The second term of the Second Triumvirate expires.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa served as aedile, built the Aqua Julia aqueduct, and cleaned the Cloaca Maxima.
text: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa is self demoted to Aedile, and builds the Aqua Julia, one of the aqueducts on which Rome's water supply depends, as well as cleaning the Cloaca Maxima sewerage system.

summary: Mark Antony annexed Media and arranged the marriage of Alexander Helios to Princess Iotapa.
text: Mark Antony annexes the kingdom of Media and arranges the marriage of his son Alexander Helios with princess Iotapa, the daughter of king Artavasdes I.

actor: List of ancient tribes in Illyria
summary: The Kinambroi surrendered to Octavian in Illyria.
text: The Kinambroi surrender to Octavian.
cast: List of ancient tribes in Illyria
names: List of ancient tribes in Illyria

actor: Tiberius Claudius Nero (father of Tiberius Caesar)
summary: Roman politician Tiberius Claudius Nero, father of the future emperor Tiberius, died.
text: Tiberius Claudius Nero, Roman politician and father of Tiberius (b. 85 BC)
cast: Tiberius Claudius Nero (father of Tiberius Caesar)
names: Tiberius Claudius Nero (father of Tiberius Caesar)

summary: Mark Antony's campaign against the Parthian Empire concluded in failure.
text: Antony's Parthian War: A campaign led by Antony against the Parthian Empire ended in failure.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus and Gaius Sosius became consuls of Rome.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus and Gaius Sosius become consuls of Rome.

summary: Mark Antony transferred his military headquarters from Samos to Athens and assembled a large fleet and army.
text: Spring – Final War of the Roman Republic: Mark Antony transfers his headquarters from Samos to Athens, where he assembles a fleet of 500 combat vessels and 300 transport ships, crewed by 150,000 men.

summary: Sparta declared support for Octavian while Lappa and Kydonia revolted against Cleopatra.
text: Sparta under Caius Iulius Eurycles, whose father Antony had been ordered to be executed for piracy, declares his support for Octavian. Lappa (modern Argyroupoli) in Attica and Kydonia in Crete revolt against Cleopatra.

summary: The Roman Senate declared war upon Mark Antony and Cleopatra VII after Octavian disclosed Antony's will.
text: July – The Roman Senate declares war upon Mark Antony and Cleopatra VII. Octavian Caesar is proclaimed dux and the West - Gallic and Spanish provinces, Africa, Sicily and Sardinia - swear an oath (sacramentum) of loyalty to him. In order to assure this oath, Octavian forces the high priest of the Vestal Virgins in Rome to hand over Antony's will, which contains information about the Roman-conquered territories as kingdoms and plans to build a tomb in Alexandria for him and Cleopatra.

summary: Mark Antony established his headquarters at Patrae and stationed his fleet at Actium.
text: Winter – Antony distributes garrisons along the west coast of Greece, stations the fleet at Actium and establishes his headquarters at Patrae.

summary: Gaius Sosius held Zacynthus and Bogud of Mauretania held Methone for the Antonian faction.
text: Zacynthus is held by Gaius Sosius, and Methone (Messenia) by Bogud of the royal house of Mauretania, driven into exile by his brother Bocchus II.

summary: Roman politician Marcus Valerius Messalla was born.
text: Marcus Valerius Messalla, Roman politician

summary: Roman equestrian and man of letters Titus Pomponius Atticus died.
text: Titus Pomponius Atticus, Roman nobleman

summary: Octavian became Roman consul for the third time with Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus after Antony was deposed.
text: Augustus, then known as Imperator Caesar, becomes Roman Consul for the third time. Antony was designated as his colleague but is deposed from office, an action that Antony does not recognise. Elected in Antony's place is Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus; Antony's consulship is not recorded in some sources, as Valerius is marked instead as consul ordinarius.

summary: Octavian landed an army in Epirus and advanced to Toryne on the Gulf of Ambracia.
text: Octavian crosses the Strait of Otranto and lands with an army (15 legions) at Panormus in Dalmatia. He marches to Toryne in the south, and establishes a bridgehead at the Gulf of Ambracia.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa sailed to the western Peloponnese and occupied positions around the Gulf of Corinth.
text: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa sails with 300 war galleys to the western Peloponnese, and occupies strategic positions around the Gulf of Corinth to cut off Antony's line of communication.

summary: Mark Antony established camp at Actium to confront the advancing forces of Octavian.
text: Antony, alerted by Octavian's presence, sets up camp on the southern shore, at the promontory of Actium. He dispatches a force to isolate the camp of Octavian in the valley of Louros.

summary: Agrippa stormed Leucas, seized the garrison at Patrae, and captured Antony's headquarters.
text: Agrippa storms Leucas, giving Octavian an anchorage and a second depot for his land supplies. He seizes the garrison at Patrae, and takes Antony's headquarters.

summary: King Amyntas of Galatia defected to Octavian with two thousand cavalry.
text: Amyntas, king of Galatia, deserts with 2,000 cavalry to Octavian. One-third of Antony's oarsmen are lost to malnutrition, disease and desertion.

summary: Octavian defeated the combined naval forces of Mark Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium.
text: Roman Civil War: Battle of Actium: Off the western coast of Greece, Octavian Caesar defeats naval forces under Mark Antony and Cleopatra VII.
names: List of Roman civil wars and revolts

summary: Cleopatra and the Egyptian fleet broke through the Roman blockade and retreated toward Taenarus.
text: The Egyptian fleet (60 warships), including Cleopatra's treasure ship, retreats to Taenarus. Antony transfers his flag to a smaller vessel and breaks through Octavian's line.

summary: Octavian wintered at Samos and founded the victory city of Nicopolis near the site of Actium.
text: Winter – Octavian (32 years old) takes court at Samos. After his decisive victory at Actium he builds Nicopolis; the city is populated by Greeks from settlements further inland.

summary: Herod the Great completed the fortification of Masada in the Judean Desert.
text: In the Judean Desert on an isolated rock plateau, fortress Masada is completed. Herod the Great builds an armory, barracks, storehouses and a palace.

summary: A major earthquake struck the Herodian Kingdom of Judea.
text: 31 BC Judea earthquake, earthquake mentioned in catalogues of historical earthquakes. It affected the Herodian Kingdom of Judea in the Holy Land.

summary: The Hellenistic period came to an end following the Battle of Actium.
text: The Hellenistic period ends (or AD 14 by some scholars).

summary: Aristobulus IV, prince of Judea and son of Herod the Great, was born.
text: Aristobulus IV, Jewish prince of Judea (d. 7 BC)

summary: Roman general and politician Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus died.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, Roman general and politician

summary: Tarcondimotus I, Roman client king of Cilicia, was killed during fighting before Actium.
text: Tarcondimotus I, Roman client king of Cilicia

summary: Octavian became Roman consul for the fourth time, serving alongside Marcus Licinius Crassus the Younger.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus becomes consul for the fourth time. His partner is Marcus Licinius Crassus the Younger.

summary: Octavian crossed the Dardanelles into Asia Minor and marched into Syria, where Herod the Great pledged loyalty and provided military support.
text: Spring – Octavian leads his army to the Dardanelles, ships them across to Asia Minor and marches into Syria where Herod the Great sends him vows of loyalty and thousands of his own troops in support.

summary: Cornelius Gallus landed in Cyrenaica and occupied Paraetonium, resisting a counter-attack by Mark Antony.
text: Summer – Cornelius Gallus lands in Cyrene and occupies Paraetonium. Mark Antony storms the city walls and blockades the harbour, then retreats with his army (7 legions) to Egypt and receives the news that Pelusium has opened its gates to Octavian without resistance.

summary: Mark Antony achieved a minor victory against Octavian's forces outside Alexandria before the mass desertion of his army led to his suicide.
text: Battle of Alexandria: Mark Antony achieves a minor victory over Octavian's forces, but most of his army subsequently deserts, leading to his suicide.

summary: Octavian captured Alexandria and annexed Egypt to the Roman Republic while the Nabataean king destroyed Cleopatra's fleet on the Red Sea.
text: Octavian Caesar captures Alexandria. This marks the official annexation of Ancient Egypt to the Roman Republic. Cleopatra evacuates her court and treasury to Berenice on the west coast of the Red Sea, but king Malchus of Nabatea attacks from the desert and burns the Egyptian ships.
