summary: Cleopatra died by suicide in Alexandria and her son Caesarion was murdered, ending the Ptolemaic dynasty.
text: August 10 or 12 – With the death of Cleopatra, probably by suicide, in Alexandria and the probable murder soon afterwards of her son and nominal co-ruler Caesarion, the Ptolemaic dynasty, the last of Ancient Egypt, comes to an end. The first year of Octavian's reign in Egypt.

summary: Octavian spared the surviving children of Cleopatra and brought them to Rome to be raised in the household of Octavia Minor.
text: The remaining children of Cleopatra are spared by Octavian and taken back in triumph; Octavia Minor raises Alexander Helios, Cleopatra Selene and Ptolemy Philadelphus in her household in Rome.

summary: Octavian claimed Cleopatra's treasury at Taposiris Magna to pay his legionaries and purchase land in Italy for his veterans.
text: Octavian claims Cleopatra's treasure in the mausoleum at the Taposiris Magna (Temple of Isis); he pays the salaries of his veteran legionaries and gives them land in Italy.

summary: The Revolt of Thebes broke out in Upper Egypt following the establishment of Roman rule.
text: The Revolt of Thebes (c. 30–29 BC) outbreaks in Egypt immediately after Octavian's victory. Followed by a series of Egyptian resistances, military conflicts and revolts, the following centuries.

summary: Imhotep-Pedubast, the high priest of Ptah in Memphis, died.
text: July 31 or August 1 – Imhotep-Pedubast, high priest of Ptah in Memphis (b.46 BC)

summary: Roman general and statesman Mark Antony died by suicide in Alexandria.
text: Mark Antony, Roman consul and general (suicide) (b. 83 BC)

summary: Cleopatra VII, the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, died by suicide in Alexandria.
text: c. August 12 – Cleopatra VII, queen of Ptolemaic Egypt (likely suicide) (b. 69 BC)

summary: Marcus Antonius Antyllus, the eldest son of Mark Antony and Fulvia, was executed by order of Octavian.
text: Marcus Antonius Antyllus, son of Mark Antony and Fulvia (executed) (b. 47 BC)

summary: Ptolemy XV Caesarion, co-ruler of Egypt and son of Julius Caesar, was assassinated by order of Octavian.
text: c. August 29 – Ptolemy Caesar, son of Julius Caesar and Cleopatra of Egypt, co-ruler of Egypt (likely assassinated) (b. 47 BC)

summary: Hyrcanus II, former king and high priest of Judea, died.
text: Hyrcanus II, king and high priest of Judea (until 40 BC)

summary: Roman politician Marcus Aemilius Lepidus the Younger was executed for conspiring against Octavian.
text: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus Minor, Roman politician

summary: Roman general Publius Canidius Crassus was executed on Octavian's orders after the fall of Alexandria.
text: Publius Canidius Crassus, Roman general and politician (executed)

summary: Octavian organized Egypt as a Roman province and assumed the traditional royal title of pharaoh.
text: The province of Egypt was organized. Augustus took the title pharaoh.

summary: Octavian became consul for the fifth time alongside Sextus Appuleius, received the title of imperator, and closed the doors of the Temple of Janus.
text: Octavian Caesar becomes Roman Consul for the fifth time. His partner is Sextus Appuleius. He is granted the title of imperator, and for the third time in Roman history the doors of the Temple of Janus are closed, signalling peace.

summary: Octavian celebrated three triumphs over consecutive days in Rome to commemorate his victories in Illyricum, Actium, and Egypt.
text: Octavian celebrates, in Rome, three triumphs on consecutive days (August 13, August 14, and August 15) to commemorate his victories in Illyricum, Actium and Egypt.

summary: Marcus Licinius Crassus campaigned in the Balkans and killed the king of the Bastarnae, but Octavian refused him the honor of dedicating the spolia opima.
text: Marcus Licinius Crassus campaigns successfully in the Balkans, killing the king of the Bastarnae by his own hand, but is denied the right to dedicate the spolia opima by Octavian.

summary: The Romans conquered Serdica, modern-day Sofia, incorporating it into the Roman Republic.
text: Sofia, modern day capital of Bulgaria, is conquered by the Romans and becomes known as Ulpia Serdica.

summary: Octavian completed and dedicated the Temple of Caesar, the Curia Julia, and the Chalcidicum in the Roman Forum.
text: Though started under the triumvirate with Mark Anthony and Marcus Lepidus, Octavian completes three projects in the Forum Romanum: Temple of the Deified Julius, the Curia, and the Chalcidicum.

summary: Roman forces suppressed the native Egyptian rebellion known as the Revolt of Thebes.
text: Revolt of Thebes suppressed in Egypt.

summary: Horace wrote the ode Occidit Daci Cotisonis agmen celebrating Roman frontier peace.
text: Horace writes the ode Occidit Daci Cotisonis agmen.

summary: Virgil finished composing the Georgics and began writing the Aeneid.
text: Virgil probably completes the Georgics and begins composition of the Aeneid.

summary: Antiochus II, prince of Commagene, was executed in Rome on Octavian's orders.
text: Antiochus II, Armenian prince of Commagene (executed)

summary: Mariamne I, Hasmonean princess and second wife of Herod the Great, was executed.
text: Mariamne I, wife of Herod the Great (executed) (or 28 BC)

summary: Ptolemy Philadelphus, the youngest son of Cleopatra and Mark Antony, died in Rome.
text: Ptolemy Philadelphus, Ptolemaic prince of Egypt (b. 36 BC)

summary: Moesia was annexed by the Roman Republic following the successful campaigns of Marcus Licinius Crassus.
text: Moesia was annexed to Rome.

summary: Rome deployed eighty thousand troops against the Cantabri in northern Hispania, escalating the Cantabrian Wars.
text: Cantabrian Wars: Rome deployed some eighty thousand soldiers against the Cantabri in Iberia.

summary: Octavian became Roman consul for the sixth time, with Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa serving as his consular colleague.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian becomes Roman Consul for the sixth time. His partner Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa becomes Consul for the second time.

summary: The Roman Senate granted Octavian supreme imperium maius over the legions of the Roman armed forces.
text: The Roman Senate grants Octavian Caesar imperium maius (supreme command) of the Roman armed forces (Around 28 legions).

summary: Augustus initiated a census across the Roman Republic, the first since 69 BC.
text: Augustus initiates a census of the Roman Republic for the first time since 69 BC.

summary: The Roman–Dardanian wars came to an end in the central Balkans.
text: Roman–Dardanian wars end

summary: Alexandra the Maccabee, daughter of Hyrcanus II, was executed on the orders of Herod the Great.
text: Alexandra the Maccabee, Hasmonean princess

summary: Mariamne I, Hasmonean princess and wife of Herod the Great, died.
text: Mariamne I, Hasmonean princess and wife Herod the Great (or 29 BC)

summary: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian became Roman consul for the seventh time alongside Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa.
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian becomes Roman Consul for the seventh time. His partner Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa becomes Consul for the third time.

summary: The Roman Senate bestowed the titles Princeps and Augustus on Octavian, making him the first Roman emperor.
text: Octavian formally returns full power to the Senate; they give him the titles of Princeps and Augustus. He accepts this honor, having declined the alternative title of Romulus, thus becoming first Roman emperor.

summary: Caesar Augustus initiated military reforms, reducing the legions to twenty-six and creating the Praetorian Guard.
text: Caesar Augustus starts a new military reform. He reduces the number of legions to 26 and creates the Praetorian Guard (1,000 men).

summary: Augustus formed the Classis Misenensis fleet, based at Portus Julius in Misenum.
text: Augustus forms the Classis Misenensis, based in the harbor of Portus Julius at Misenum.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa divided Hispania Ulterior into Baetica and Lusitania, and enlarged Hispania Citerior.
text: Agrippa divides Hispania Ulterior into Baetica and Lusitania, and enlarges Hispania Citerior.

summary: An earthquake in Egypt shattered the northern statue of the Colossi of Memnon.
text: Northern statue of the Colossi of Memnon is shattered by an earthquake in Egypt (according to Strabo).

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa began construction of the original Pantheon in Rome.
text: Marcus Agrippa begins the construction of the old Pantheon, Rome.

summary: Augustus conducted his first census of the Roman Empire, recording 4,063,000 citizens.
text: Augustus' first census of the Roman Empire (formerly the Roman Republic) reports a total of 4,063,000 citizens.

summary: Roman scholar and writer Marcus Terentius Varro died.
text: Marcus Terentius Varro, Roman scholar and writer (b. 116 BC)

summary: Augustus became Roman consul for the eighth time alongside Titus Statilius Taurus, who refounded Ilici.
text: Imperator Caesar Augustus becomes Roman Consul for the eighth time. His partner Titus Statilius Taurus becomes Consul for the second time and refounds the old Contestanian Iberian capital of Ilici (Elche), known since then as "Colonia Iulia Ilici Augusta".

summary: Cleopatra Selene married Juba II of Numidia, and Augustus made her queen of Mauretania.
text: Cleopatra Selene marries Juba II of Numidia, and as a wedding present Augustus makes her the queen of Mauretania in her own right.

summary: Aelius Gallus led a disastrous Roman military campaign into the Arabian Peninsula.
text: Disastrous campaign of Aelius Gallus in the Arabian Peninsula, then known as "Arabia Felix".

summary: Tiridates II invaded Parthia and issued coins in his name.
text: Tiridates II invades Parthia and issues coins dated from March and May, 26 BC.

summary: Caesar Augustus listened to the orator Gavius Silo.
text: Gavius Silo, orator, is heard by Caesar Augustus - mentioned by Seneca.

summary: Augustus launched a military campaign against the Cantabrians in northern Hispania with eight legions.
text: Augustus starts a campaign against the Cantabrians in northern Hispania. He leads an army (8 legions) and consolidates the north-eastern region.

summary: Dioteimus Alaieus served as Archon of Athens.
text: Dioteimus Alaieus is one of the Archons of Athens.

summary: Abgar IV Sumaqa succeeded Abgar III as king of Osroene.
text: Abgar III of Osroene is succeeded by Abgar IV Sumaqa.

summary: Roman politician and poet Gaius Cornelius Gallus died.
text: Gaius Cornelius Gallus, Roman politician and poet (b. 70 BC)

summary: Roman politician Marcus Valerius Messalla Rufus died.
text: Marcus Valerius Messalla Rufus, Roman politician

summary: Augustus became Roman consul for the ninth time alongside Marcus Junius Silanus.
text: Imperator Caesar Augustus becomes Consul for the ninth time. His partner is Marcus Junius Silanus.

summary: A temple to Neptune was constructed at the Circus Flaminius in Rome.
text: The temple to Neptune on the Circus Flaminius is built.

summary: Rome surpassed Chang'an to become the largest city in the world by population.
text: Estimation: Rome, capital of the Roman Empire, becomes the largest city in the world, taking the lead from Chang'an, capital of China.

summary: Galatia became a Roman province following the death of its king, and Roman troops stationed there were transferred to Egypt.
text: Galatia becomes a Roman province after the death of its king. The Roman troops stationed there are relocated to Egypt.

summary: The Roman colony of Emerita Augusta was founded in Hispania.
text: The Roman colony of Emerita Augusta is founded (present-day Mérida).

summary: Roman encyclopedist and medical writer Aulus Cornelius Celsus was born.
text: Aulus Cornelius Celsus, author of De Medicina (d. c. AD 50)

summary: King Amyntas of Galatia died.
text: Amyntas of Galatia, King of Galatia

summary: Augustus signaled his nephew Marcus Claudius Marcellus as his successor by marrying him to Julia the Elder.
text: Augustus indicated his nephew Marcus Claudius Marcellus (Julio-Claudian dynasty) as his chosen successor by marrying him to his only daughter Julia the Elder.

summary: Augustus became Roman consul for the tenth time alongside Gaius Norbanus Flaccus.
text: Caesar Augustus becomes Roman Consul for the tenth time. His partner is Gaius Norbanus Flaccus.

summary: Augustus founded the city of Nicopolis in Egypt to commemorate his victory over Mark Antony.
text: Augustus founds the city of Nicopolis in Egypt to commemorate his final victory over Mark Antony.

summary: Herod the Great married his third wife, Mariamne II.
text: Herod the Great marries for a third time, to Mariamne II, after a 4-year hiatus from family life (after putting to death his 2nd wife Mariamne I).

summary: Roman general and politician Aulus Terentius Varro Murena died.
text: Aulus Terentius Varro Murena, Roman general and politician

summary: Augustus concluded his active campaign against the Cantabrians in Hispania Tarraconensis.
text: Augustus' campaigns against the Cantabrians in Hispania Tarraconensis, the Cantabrian Wars, ended.

summary: Caesar Augustus served as Roman consul for the eleventh time alongside Aulus Terentius Varro Murena.
text: Caesar Augustus becomes Roman consul for the eleventh time. His co-consul is Aulus Terentius Varro Murena.

summary: Augustus relinquished the consulship, retained tribunician power, and consolidated his role as Princeps.
text: Augustus relinquishes the position of consul, retains that of tribune of Rome, and assumes that of Princeps, or "First Citizen." (see Roman Empire).

summary: During a severe illness, Augustus gave his signet ring to Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and granted him proconsular imperium.
text: Augustus gets seriously ill: he gives Agrippa his signet ring and grants him the title imperium pro consule.

summary: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, nephew of Augustus, died of a fever at the age of nineteen while serving as aedile.
text: Marcus Claudius Marcellus (nephew of Augustus) falls ill from a fever shortly after his uncle recovers and dies at the age of nineteen while serving as an aedile.

summary: Nubians led by Queen Amanirenas attacked the Roman province of Egypt and advanced toward Elephantine.
text: The Nubians, led by queen Kandake Amanirenas, take the initiative against the Roman Empire, and attack the Roman province of Egypt moving towards Elephantine.

summary: Roman legions marched south in response to incursions into Upper Egypt and razed Napata.
text: In response to Meroë's incursions into Upper Egypt, the Roman legions move south and raze Napata. (History of Sudan).

summary: Herod the Great built a palace in Jerusalem, constructed the fortress Herodium in Judea, and married Mariamne.
text: Herod the Great builds a palace in Jerusalem and the fortress Herodium in Judaea. He also marries his third wife, named Mariamne, the daughter of high priest Simon.

summary: The Roman Empire reformed its coinage, striking the as in pure copper and introducing the sestertius and dupondius in bronze.
text: Following coinage reform, the as is struck in reddish pure copper, instead of bronze. The denominations of sestertius and dupondius are introduced as large bronze coins.

summary: Marcus Vitruvius Pollio finished writing his treatise De Architectura.
text: The Roman writer, architect and engineer Marcus Vitruvius Pollio finishes writing De Architectura (known today as The Ten Books of Architecture), a treatise in Latin on architecture, and perhaps the first work about this discipline.

summary: Horace published the first three books of the Odes.
text: The Roman poet Horace publishes the first three books of Odes.

summary: Herod Archelaus, future ethnarch of Samaria and Judea, was born.
text: Herod Archelaus, ethnarch of Samaria (Judea) (d. AD 18)

summary: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, son of Octavia and nephew of Augustus, died at the age of nineteen.
text: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, son of Octavia and nephew of Augustus (b. 42 BC)

summary: Paullus Aemilius Lepidus and Lucius Munatius Plancus served together as censors.
text: Aemilius Lepidus Paullus and Lucius Munatius Plancus are Censors.
names: List of censors of the Roman Republic

states.value: Paullus Aemilius Lepidus and Lucius Munatius Plancus

summary: Roman governor Gaius Petronius marched up the Nile and destroyed the Nubian capital of Napata.
text: The Roman governor of Egypt, Gaius Petronius, marches up the Nile with legions XXII Deiotariana and III Cyrenaica, and destroys the Nubian capital of Napata.

summary: Artaxias II returned to Armenia with Parthian support and reclaimed the throne, forcing Artavasdes I to flee to Rome.
text: King Artaxias II returns, with the support of the Parthians, to Armenia and claims the throne. Artavasdes I escapes to Rome, where Caesar Augustus receives him.

summary: Roman politician Lucius Licinius Varro Murena was executed.
text: Lucius Licinius Varro Murena, Roman politician, executed

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa divorced Claudia Marcella Major and married Julia the Elder, daughter of Augustus.
text: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa divorces Claudia Marcella Major, and marries Julia the Elder, daughter of Caesar Augustus.

summary: Naevius Sutorius Macro, future Praetorian prefect, was born in Alba Fucens.
text: Naevius Sutorius Macro, Roman prefect and politician (d. AD 38)

summary: Augustus negotiated peace with Parthia, making Armenia a buffer zone and recovering the lost Roman legionary standards.
text: Emperor Augustus Caesar negotiates a peace with Parthia, making Armenia a buffer zone between the two major powers. The captured eagles of Marcus Licinius Crassus and Mark Antony are returned.

summary: Lucius Aelius Sejanus, future Praetorian prefect and confidant of Tiberius, was born in Volsinii.
text: Lucius Aelius Sejanus, advisor of Tiberius (d. AD 31)

summary: Gaius Caesar, grandson and adopted heir of Augustus, was born.
text: Gaius Caesar, grandson of Augustus Caesar (d. AD 4)

summary: Lucius Antonius, grandson of Mark Antony, was born.
text: Lucius Antonius, grandson of Mark Antony d. AD 25)

summary: Hellenistic Jewish philosopher Philo was born in Alexandria.
text: Philo of Alexandria, Jewish philosopher (d. AD 50)

summary: Artavasdes I, former king of Media Atropatene, died in exile in Rome.
text: Artavasdes I, king of Media Atropatene

summary: King Artaxias II of Armenia was assassinated by his subjects.
text: Artaxias II, king of Armenia (Artaxiad dynasty)

summary: King Mirian II of Iberia died.
text: Mirian II (or Mirvan), king of Iberia (Georgia)

summary: King Mithridates II of Commagene died.
text: Mithridates II, king of Commagene (Armenia)

summary: The Aeneid, Virgil's epic poem describing the founding of Rome, was published posthumously.
text: The Aeneid by the Roman poet Virgil is published after his death. The Aeneid is an epic poem in 12 books that tells the story of the foundation of Rome from the ashes of Troy.

summary: Lucius Cornelius Balbus celebrated a Roman triumph in the Roman Forum for his victories against the Garamantes.
text: In Rome, Lucius Cornelius Balbus receives the honor of a triumph on the Forum Romanum, for his victories over the Garamantes in Africa.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa completed construction of the Aqua Virgo aqueduct supplying Rome.
text: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa completes the Aqua Virgo; the aqueduct is in length and supplies the city of Rome with about 100,000,000 liters of water every day.

summary: The Roman Empire brought the Cantabrians of northern Spain under Roman rule.
text: The Cantabrians, living on the northernmost coast of Spain, are brought under Roman control. The region is completely subdued until 16 BC.

summary: Herod the Great began the extensive renovation and expansion of the Temple in Jerusalem.
text: King Herod the Great begins renovation of the Temple in Jerusalem.

summary: Augustus introduced the Julian Laws to reform Roman social and moral behavior.
text: Caesar Augustus introduces the Lex Julia (Julian Laws):

summary: The Lex Iulia de Ambitu penalized bribery in the acquisition of political offices.
text: Lex Iulia de Ambitu penalised bribery when acquiring political offices.

summary: The Lex Iulia de maritandis ordinibus established incentives for marriage and prohibited senators from marrying prostitutes or freedmen.
text: Lex Iulia de maritandis ordinibus introduced penalties and incentives to promote marriage, and forbade marriage of senators, as well as of their children, to prostitutes and to freedmen.

summary: Augustus adopted his grandsons Gaius Caesar and Lucius Caesar as his own sons and heirs.
text: Augustus adopted the sons of Agrippa and Julia, his grandsons Gaius Caesar and Lucius Caesar, as his own sons.

summary: Augustus celebrated the Secular Games in Rome, commissioning Horace's hymn Carmen Saeculare for the occasion.
text: Emperor Augustus celebrates the secular games in Rome, for which Horace's hymn the "Carmen Saeculare" is commissioned.

summary: The Roman Empire conquered and annexed Raetia and Noricum.
text: Raetia and Noricum were conquered and annexed to Rome.

summary: Publius Silius Nerva defeated the invading Noricans and Pannonians in Istria.
text: The Noricans having joined with the Pannonians in invading Histria, are defeated by Publius Silius Nerva, proconsul of Illyricum.

summary: The Roman city of Bracara Augusta was founded at modern Braga.
text: Braga, Portugal is founded.

summary: Augustus reorganized the German provinces and established Trier as their capital.
text: Caesar Augustus reorganizes the German provinces, making Trier their capital.

summary: Germanic tribes defeated the Roman consul Marcus Lollius in the Clades Lolliana.
text: Clades Lolliana: Roman consul Marcus Lollius is defeated by a Germanic horde.

summary: Construction began on the Roman temple of the Maison Carrée at Nîmes.
text: Construction of the Roman temple of Maison Carrée at Nîmes in Gallia Narbonensis .

summary: Tiberius and Nero Claudius Drusus subjugated the Raeti tribes and established the province of Raetia.
text: The Raeti tribes of the Alps are subjugated by Tiberius and Nero Claudius Drusus and the new Roman province of Raetia is established with Chur (in modern-day Switzerland) as its capital. During the campaign, Roman triremes destroy the fleet of the Vindelici in the Battle of Lake Constance. Augsburg is founded as Augusta Vindelicorum; and Legio XXI Rapax is stationed at Regensburg in the new province.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus began construction of the Via Claudia Augusta across the Alps.
text: Drusus decides to improve the passage through the Alps for military control of Noricum and Raetia and builds the Via Claudia Augusta through Italy.

summary: Marcus Livius Drusus Libo and Lucius Calpurnius Piso took office as Roman consuls.
text: Marcus Livius Drusus Libo and Lucius Calpurnius Piso are Roman Consuls.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus fortified Augusta Vangionum at modern Worms.
text: The Roman general Nero Claudius Drusus fortifies Augusta Vangionum, the modern city of Worms, Germany.

summary: Augustus granted Beeroth the status of a Roman colonia as Colonia Julia Augusta Felix Berytus.
text: Caesar Augustus makes Beeroth (modern Beirut) a colonia, named Colonia Julia Augusta Felix Berytus.

summary: Legio X Fretensis was stationed in Syria and its veterans were settled at Beirut.
text: Winter – The Roman Legio X Fretensis is stationed in Syria, and the legionaries are settled at the ancient city of Beirut.

summary: Tiberius Claudius Nero and Publius Quinctilius Varus served as Roman consuls.
text: Tiberius Claudius Nero and Publius Quinctilius Varus are Roman Consuls.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus built the Roman castrum Moguntiacum at modern Mainz.
text: The Roman general Nero Claudius Drusus builds the stronghold of castrum Moguntiacum in the location of the modern-day city of Mainz, Germany.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus became governor of Gaul and launched a campaign driving the Germanic tribes across the Rhine.
text: Drusus is granted governor of Gaul and mobilises a Roman army to beat the Germans back across the Rhine. He travels to the North Sea and pays tribute to the Frisii.

summary: The Roman Senate commissioned the Ara Pacis Augustae to honor Augustus' return from Hispania and Gaul.
text: The Ara Pacis Augustae ("Altar of Augustan Peace") is commissioned by the Roman Senate to honor the triumphal return of Emperor Augustus from Hispania and Gaul.

summary: Vologases led a revolt against Roman rule in Thrace.
text: Revolt in Thrace against Roman rule led by Vologases.

summary: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa died of fever in Campania.
text: Agrippa died of fever.

summary: Marcus Valerius Messalla Appianus and Publius Sulpicius Quirinius served as Roman consuls.
text: Marcus Valerius Messalla Appianus and Publius Sulpicius Quirinius are Roman consuls.

summary: The Dalmatae launched a major revolt in Pannonia, requiring the intervention of Tiberius Claudius Nero.
text: Tiberius Claudius Nero summoned to Pannonia due to severe revolt by the Delmatae.

summary: Roman armies based along the Rhine launched military campaigns beyond the river.
text: Roman armies based at Xanten, Cologne and Mainz campaign beyond the Rhine.

summary: The city of Argentoratum, modern Strasbourg, received its first official mention.
text: First official mention of Argentoratum, the city known in modern times as Strasbourg.

summary: Augustus was appointed Pontifex Maximus.
text: Emperor Augustus is given the title Pontifex Maximus.

summary: The Pyramid of Cestius was erected in Rome as a tomb for Gaius Cestius.
text: Approximate date – Pyramid of Cestius erected in Rome.

summary: Augustus married his daughter Julia the Elder to his stepson Tiberius.
text: Augustus married Julia to his general and stepson Tiberius.

summary: Quintus Aelius Tubero and Paullus Fabius Maximus served as Roman consuls.
text: Quintus Aelius Tubero and Paullus Fabius Maximus are Roman Consuls.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus defeated Germanic forces at the Battle of the Lupia River.
text: Battle of the Lupia River: Roman forces under Augustus's stepson Nero Claudius Drusus win a victory in Germania.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus repulsed a Germanic ambush at the Battle of Arbalo.
text: Battle of Arbalo: Roman forces under Augustus's stepson Nero Claudius Drusus beat off a German ambush.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus secured the Rhine frontier and established Roman fortresses along the river.
text: May – Drusus secures the Rhine frontier and builds Roman fortresses near Bonn, Dorsten, Haltern, and Oberaden.

summary: Augustus brought the Obelisk of Montecitorio from Egypt to Rome to serve as the gnomon of the Solarium Augusti.
text: The Obelisk of Montecitorio is brought from Egypt to Rome by Emperor Augustus to be erected as a sundial gnomon of the Solarium Augusti. It is now in the Piazza Montecitorio.

summary: The Romans constructed a bridge across the Rhine near Bonn.
text: The Romans build a bridge across the Rhine near Bonn .

summary: A Roman military camp was established at Speyer.
text: A Roman military camp is established at Speyer (Germany).

summary: The Ara Pacis Augustae was dedicated in Rome.
text: The ("Altar of Augustan Peace"), which was voted for by the Senate four years earlier, is dedicated.

summary: Pannonia was incorporated into the Roman Empire as part of Illyricum.
text: Pannonia is incorporated into the Roman Empire as a part of Illyria.

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus died from a fall from his horse while campaigning against the Marcomanni.
text: Nero Claudius Drusus, Emperor Augustus' stepson, begins a campaign against the Marcomanni, but dies soon after, due to a fall from his horse.

summary: Aretas IV Philopatris ascended the throne of the Nabataean Kingdom.
text: Aretas IV Philopatris ascended to become the King of the Nabataeans (modern Jordan).

summary: The Roman historian Quintus Asconius Pedianus was born.
text: Quintus Asconius Pedianus, Roman historian (d. AD 76)

summary: Nero Claudius Drusus, son of Livia and stepson of Augustus, died in Germania.
text: Nero Claudius Drusus, son of Livia and stepson of Augustus (b. 38 BC)

summary: King Maroboduus became ruler of the Marcomanni and resisted Roman expansion in Bohemia.
text: King Maroboduus becomes ruler of the Marcomanni and fights against the Roman Empire's expansion in Bohemia.

summary: Arminius was taken as a hostage to Rome, where he received a military education.
text: Arminius, son of a Cheruscan chieftain, is taken as a hostage to Rome, where he receives a military education.

summary: Emperor Augustus initiated his second census of the Roman Empire.
text: After 20 years, Emperor Augustus initiates his second census of the Roman Empire.

summary: The Roman Senate decreed that the month of Sextilis be renamed Augustus in honor of the emperor.
text: Sextilis, the eighth month of the early Julian calendar, is renamed Augustus (August) by a decree of the Roman Senate in honor of Augustus.

summary: Roman lyric poet Horace died.
text: Horace, Roman lyric poet and writer (b. 65 BC)

summary: Roman politician and patron Gaius Maecenas died.
text: Gaius Maecenas, Roman politician and advisor (b. 70 BC)

summary: Polemon I, Roman client king of the Bosporan Kingdom, died.
text: Polemon I, Roman client king of the Bosporan Kingdom

summary: Augustus' second census reported 4,233,000 Roman citizens.
text: Augustus' second census of the Roman Empire reports a total of 4,233,000 citizens. However, the specific criteria of the census are still not clear.

summary: The city of Rome was divided into 14 administrative regions.
text: The city of Rome is divided into 14 administrative regions.

summary: Aristobulus IV, Jewish prince of Judea, died.
text: Aristobulus IV, Jewish prince of Judea (b. 31 BC)

summary: Tiberius refused Augustus' offer of tribunician power and imperium over the East, retiring to Rhodes instead.
text: Augustus offered Tiberius tribunician power and imperium over the eastern half of the Empire. Tiberius refused, announcing his retirement to Rhodes.

summary: Roman noblewoman Aemilia Lepida was born.
text: Aemilia Lepida, Roman noblewoman and fiancée of Claudius (d. AD 43)

summary: Roman noblewoman Domitia Lepida was born.
text: Domitia Lepida, daughter of Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus and Antonia Major (d. AD 54)

summary: Roman consul and governor Lucius Vitellius the Elder was born.
text: Lucius Vitellius the Elder, Roman consul and governor of Syria (d. AD 51)

summary: John the Baptist was born.
text: John the Baptist (d. c.AD 30)

summary: Acme, an enslaved maid in the service of Empress Livia, died.
text: Acme (enslaved woman), Jewish slave and personal maid in the service of the Empress Livia Drusilla, wife of Augustus

summary: Roman noblewoman Curia died.
text: Curia, Roman noblewoman and wife of Quintus Lucretius Vespillo

summary: Following Herod the Great's death, unrest broke out in Judea and Syrian governor Varus marched to Jerusalem to suppress it.
text: Herod the Great dies, which causes unrest in his client kingdom of Judea. His son, Herod Archelaus, becomes the new ruler. Herod Antipas becomes tetrarch of Galilee and Perea,and the governor of Syria, Publius Quinctilius Varus, marches down to Jerusalem from Antioch to restore order; around 3000 Jews are crucified.

summary: Roman Stoic philosopher and statesman Seneca the Younger was born in Corduba.
text: Approximate date – Seneca the Younger, Córdoban-born Roman Stoic philosopher, statesman and dramatist (d. AD 65)

summary: Herod the Great, Roman client king of Judea, died.
text: March or April – Herod the Great, king of Judea (b. 73 BC); some authors date his death to 1 BC (see Date of Herod's death).
names: Date of the birth of Jesus

summary: Antipater, heir and son of Herod the Great, was executed.
text: Antipater, Jewish heir and son of Herod the Great

summary: Malthace, wife of Herod the Great, died.
text: Malthace, Jewish woman and wife of Herod the Great

summary: Roman rhetorician Marcus Porcius Latro died.
text: Marcus Porcius Latro, Roman rhetorician

summary: Roman writer and freedman Marcus Tullius Tiro died on his estate near Puteoli.
text: Marcus Tullius Tiro, Roman writer, freedman of Cicero

summary: The Pont Julien was constructed in southern Gaul.
text: The Pont Julien was constructed in modern southern France.

summary: Future Roman emperor Servius Sulpicius Galba was born near Terracina.
text: Servius Sulpicius Galba, Roman emperor in AD 69.

summary: Augustus convicted Julia the Elder of adultery and treason and exiled her to Ventotene.
text: Augustus convicted Julia of adultery and treason, annulled her marriage to Tiberius, and exiled her with her mother Scribonia to Ventotene.

summary: The Roman Senate proclaimed Augustus pater patriae.
text: Augustus is proclaimed pater patriae ("father of the country") by the Roman Senate. This bestowed title is the logical consequence and final proof of Augustus' supreme position as princeps, the first in charge over the Roman state.

summary: Augustus dedicated the Forum of Augustus in Rome.
text: The Forum Augustum is dedicated.

summary: Phraates V and his mother Musa became rulers of the Parthian Empire after the murder of Phraates IV.
text: Phraates V and his mother Musa become rulers of the Parthian Empire following the murder of Phraates IV.

summary: Tigranes IV and Erato deposed Artavasdes III and were restored to the throne of Armenia.
text: Tigranes IV and Erato are restored to the throne after deposing Artavasdes III.

states.value: Tigranes IV and Erato of Armenia

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, father of Emperor Nero, was born.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, father of Nero

summary: Roman consul Iullus Antonius died by suicide after being accused of adultery with Julia the Elder.
text: Iullus Antonius, Roman consul and son of Mark Antony (b. 43 BC)

summary: Phraates IV, king of the Parthian Empire, was murdered.
text: Phraates IV, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Gaius Caesar married Livilla to enhance his political standing.
text: Gaius Caesar marries Livilla, (daughter of Antonia Minor and Nero Claudius Drusus) in an effort to gain prestige.

summary: Construction of the Roman theatre in Cartagena was completed.
text: The Roman theatre in Cartagena, which was built by Gaius and Lucius Caesar, finishes construction.

summary: Augustus appointed Aulus Caecina Severus consul.
text: Aulus Caecina Severus was appointed consul by Emperor Augustus, succeeding Cossus Cornelius Lentulus Gaetulicus and Lucius Calpurnius Piso.

summary: Tiberius quelled revolts in Germania under the orders of Emperor Augustus.
text: Tiberius, under order of Emperor Augustus, quells revolts in Germania (AD 1–5).

summary: Gaius Caesar met King Phraates V on the Euphrates and concluded peace, with Parthia recognizing Roman claims to Armenia.
text: Gaius Caesar meets with Phraates V, the king of Parthia, on the Euphrates. Rather than invading the Parthians, Gaius Caesar concludes peace with them; Parthia recognizes Roman claims to Armenia.

summary: Jesus was born, as traditionally assigned by Dionysius Exiguus in the Anno Domini era.
text: Birth of Jesus, as assigned by Dionysius Exiguus in his anno Domini era according to at least one scholar.{{cite book

summary: Future Roman praetorian prefect Sextus Afranius Burrus was born in Vasio.
text: Sextus Afranius Burrus, Roman praetorian prefect (d. AD 62)

summary: Roman Stoic philosopher Seneca the Younger was born in Cordoba.
text: Seneca the Younger, Roman stoic philosopher born in Cordoba (d. AD 65)

summary: Queen Amanishakheto of Kush died.
text: Amanishakheto, queen of Kush (Nubia)

summary: Juba II of Mauretania joined Gaius Caesar in Armenia as a military advisor and became enamoured with Glaphyra.
text: Juba II of Mauretania joins Gaius Caesar in Armenia as a military advisor. It is during this period that he meets Glaphyra, a Cappadocian princess and the former wife of Alexandros of Judea, a brother of Herod Archelaus, ethnarch of Judea, and becomes enamoured with her.

summary: Augustus permitted Tiberius to return to Rome as a private citizen after six years on Rhodes.
text: Following the death of Lucius Caesar, Augustus allows his stepson Tiberius back into Rome as a private citizen, after six years of enforced retirement on Rhodes.

summary: The Maison Carrée was built in Nîmes.
text: Maison Carrée, Nîmes, France, is built.

summary: Lucius Caesar, grandson and adopted heir of Augustus, died in Massalia.
text: Lucius Caesar, son of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Julia the Elder (b. 17 BC)

summary: Roman consul Gaius Marcius Censorinus died in the East while serving with Gaius Caesar.
text: Gaius Marcius Censorinus, Roman consul

summary: The imperial rule of Augustus was renewed for a ten-year term.
text: The rule of Emperor Augustus is renewed for a ten-year period.

summary: Roman politician and astrologer Tiberius Claudius Balbilus was born.
text: Tiberius Claudius Balbilus, Roman politician and astrologer (d. AD 79)

summary: Gaius Caesar died in Lycia from wounds sustained in battle.
text: Gaius Caesar died in Lycia from wounds suffered in battle.

summary: King Phraataces and Queen Musa were overthrown and killed, and the crown of Parthia was offered to Orodes III.
text: King Phraataces and Queen Musa of Parthia are overthrown and killed, the crown being offered to Orodes III of Parthia—the beginning of the interregnum.

summary: Augustus summoned Tiberius to Rome and adopted him alongside Agrippa Postumus as his designated heirs.
text: Emperor Augustus summons Tiberius to Rome, and names him his heir and future emperor. At the same time, Agrippa Postumus, the last son of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, is also adopted and named as Augustus' heir.

summary: Tiberius adopted Germanicus as his own heir.
text: Tiberius also adopts Germanicus as his own heir.

summary: The Roman state enacted the Lex Aelia Sentia to regulate the manumission of slaves.
text: The Lex Aelia Sentia regulates the manumission of slaves.

summary: The Roman Empire signed a treaty of friendship with the Cherusci, bringing Arminius and Flavus into the Roman army as auxiliary leaders.
text: A pact of non-aggression and friendship is signed between the Roman Empire, represented by Tiberius, and the German tribe the Cherusci, represented by their King Segimer. Arminius and Flavus, sons of Segimer, are brought into the Roman army as leaders of the auxiliary troops.

summary: Julia the Elder was permitted to leave Pandateria and relocated to Rhegium in disgrace.
text: Julia the Elder returns from exile to live in Rhegium in disgrace.

summary: Livilla married Drusus Julius Caesar, the son of Tiberius.
text: Livilla marries Drusus Julius Caesar, son of Tiberius.

summary: Nicolaus of Damascus wrote his fifteen-volume History of the World.
text: Nicolaus of Damascus writes the 15-volume History of the World.

summary: Roman agricultural writer Columella was born.
text: Columella, Roman Latin writer (d. AD 70)

summary: Roman nobleman Publius Quinctilius Varus the Younger was born.
text: Publius Quinctilius Varus the Younger, Roman nobleman (d. AD 27)

summary: Jesus of Nazareth was born according to this traditional chronology.
text: Jesus, Jewish preacher and religious leader (executed c. AD 30/33)

summary: Ariobarzanes II, Roman client king of Armenia and Media Atropatene, died.
text: Ariobarzanes II, Roman client king of Armenia (b. 40 BC)

summary: Roman orator, poet, and historian Gaius Asinius Pollio died.
text: Gaius Asinius Pollio, Roman orator, poet and historian (b. 65 BC)

summary: Roman consul Lucius Cornelius Lentulus died.
text: Lucius Cornelius Lentulus, Roman consul

summary: Rome acknowledged Cunobelinus, king of the Catuvellauni, as king of Britain.
text: Rome acknowledges Cunobelinus, king of the Catuvellauni, as king of Britain.

summary: The Germanic Cimbri and Charydes sent diplomatic envoys to Rome.
text: The Germanic tribes of Cimbri and Charydes send ambassadors to Rome.

summary: Tiberius completed the conquest of Germania Inferior.
text: Tiberius conquers Germania Inferior.

summary: Agrippina the Elder married her second cousin Germanicus.
text: Agrippina the Elder marries Germanicus, her second cousin.

summary: Syrian disciple and martyr Habib the Carpenter was born.
text: Habib the Carpenter, Syrian disciple, martyr

summary: Paul the Apostle, early leader of the Christian church, was born.
text: Paul the Apostle, Jewish leader of the Christians

summary: Augustus deposed Herod Archelaus and annexed Samaria, Judea, and Idumea as the Roman province of Judea.
text: Augustus deposed Herod Archelaus, ethnarch in Samaria, Judea and Idumea, and organized the province of Judea on his territories.

summary: The Daesitiates rose in revolt against Roman authority in Illyricum, beginning the Bellum Batonianum.
text: Bellum Batonianum: The Daesitiates, an Illyrian people, rose up against Roman authority in Illyricum.

summary: Augustus created the Vigiles to ensure rapid firefighting in Rome following a catastrophic fire.
text: Due to a catastrophic fire in Rome, the barracks system - the vigiles, initially manned only by freedmen - is created by the Princeps Augustus to allow quicker response to outbreaks of fire in the city.

summary: Augustus doubled grain rations, sent away his slave retinue, and placed the Senate in indefinite recess to manage a severe food shortage in Rome.
text: Due to a food shortage in Rome, Augustus doubles the grain rations distributed to the people, sends away his slave retinue, and places the senate in recess indefinitely.

summary: Augustus set up the aerarium militare with 170 million sestertii to pay bonuses to retiring legion veterans, financed by a 5% tax on inheritances.
text: The Princeps Augustus sets up a treasury, the aerarium militare (170 million sestertii), with the specific purpose of paying bonuses to retiring legion veterans. This is financed by a 5% tax on inheritances, a system said to have been suggested in Julius Caesar's memoirs.

summary: Tiberius rededicated the Temple of Castor and Pollux in Rome after its destruction by fire.
text: The Temple of Castor and Pollux is rededicated in Rome by Tiberius after being destroyed by fire in 14 BC.

summary: Augustus quashed a pamphleteering campaign in Rome, and Publius Plautius Rufus was accused but acquitted.
text: A pamphletting campaign in Rome is quashed by the Princeps Augustus. Publius Plautius Rufus is accused but found innocent of the crime.

summary: Augustus banished his adopted son Agrippa Postumus to the island of Planasia.
text: Princeps Augustus banishes Agrippa Postumus, one of his adopted sons, to the island of Planasia.

summary: Tiberius established Carnuntum as his operational base and campaigned with Legio XX Valeria Victrix against Maroboduus and the Marcomanni.
text: Tiberius makes Carnuntum his base of operations against Maroboduus; The Roman legion XX Valeria Victrix fight with Tiberius against the Marcomanni.

summary: The construction of a Roman fort established the origins of Wiesbaden.
text: The building of a Roman fort signifies the origin of the city of Wiesbaden.

summary: Freedmen and newly emancipated slaves were levied in Rome to reinforce Illyricum.
text: Troops are levied in Rome to send to Illyricum from freedmen and slaves freed specifically for the purpose.

summary: Tiberius marched from the northern frontier to Illyricum to begin operations against the Illyrians.
text: Tiberius marches back from the northern border to Illyricum to commence operations against the Illyrians.

summary: Aulus Caecina Severus was appointed governor of Moesia and took part in the opening battles of the Great Illyrian Revolt.
text: Gaius Caecina Severus is made governor of Moesia, and is heavily involved in the first battles of the or Great Illyrian Revolt.

summary: Marcus Plautius Silvanus became governor of Galatia and Pamphylia and suppressed an uprising of the Isaurians.
text: Marcus Plautius Silvanus is made governor of Galatia and Pamphylia and suppresses an uprising of the Isaurians in Pamphylia.

summary: Judaea and Moesia were organized as Roman provinces.
text: Iudaea and Moesia become Roman provinces.

summary: Quirinius conducted a census in Judea, sparking a suppressed revolt led by Judas of Galilee and the rise of the Zealots.
text: Quirinius conducts a census in Judea (according to Josephus), which results in a revolt in the province, led by Judas of Galilee, and supported by the Pharisee Zadok. The revolt is repressed, and the rebels are crucified, but it results in the birth of the Zealot movement, the members of which regard the God of Judaism as their only master.

summary: Gaius Manlius Valens, later a Roman senator and consul, was born.
text: Gaius Manlius Valens, Roman senator and consul (d. AD 96)

summary: John the Apostle, Jewish Christian mystic, was born.
text: John the Apostle, Jewish Christian mystic (d. AD 100)

summary: Roman politician Marcus Aemilius Lepidus was born.
text: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, Roman politician (d. AD 39)

summary: Milonia Caesonia, future Roman empress, was born.
text: Milonia Caesonia, Roman empress (d. AD 41)

summary: Nero Julius Caesar, son of Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder, was born.
text: Nero Julius Caesar, son of Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder (d. AD 30)

summary: Cleopatra Selene II, ruler of Cyrenaica and Libya, died.
text: Cleopatra Selene II, Egyptian ruler of Cyrenaica and Libya (b. 40 BC)

summary: Terentia, wife of Cicero, died.
text: Terentia, wife of Marcus Tullius Cicero (b. 98 BC)

summary: Illyrian tribes in Pannonia and Dalmatia continued the Great Illyrian Revolt against Roman rule.
text: Illyrian tribes in Pannonia and Dalmatia continue the Great Illyrian Revolt against Roman rule.
names: List of Illyrian peoples and tribes

summary: Publius Quinctilius Varus was appointed governor of Germania to organize the territory between the Rhine and Elbe rivers.
text: Publius Quinctilius Varus is appointed governor of Germania, charged with organizing Germania between the Rhine and Elbe rivers. He carries out a census, devises tributes and recruits soldiers, all of which creates dissension among the Germanic tribes.

summary: Construction began on the Temple of Concord in Rome.
text: Construction of the Temple of Concord begins.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo, Roman general, was born.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo, Roman general (d. AD 67)

summary: Julia Livia, daughter of Drusus Julius Caesar and Livilla, was born.
text: Julia Livia, daughter of Drusus Julius Caesar and Livilla (d. AD 43)

summary: Stoic philosopher Athenodorus Cananites died.
text: Athenodoros Cananites, Stoic philosopher (b. 74 BC)

summary: Roman consul Aulus Licinius Nerva Silianus died.
text: Aulus Licinius Nerva Silianus, Roman consul

summary: Glaphyra, daughter of King Archelaus of Cappadocia, died.
text: Glaphyra, daughter of Archelaus of Cappadocia

summary: Roman politician Lucius Sempronius Atratinus died.
text: Lucius Sempronius Atratinus, Roman politician

summary: Tincomarus was deposed as king of the Atrebates and fled to Rome, being succeeded by Eppillus.
text: Tincomarus, deposed king of the Atrebates, flees Britain for Rome; Eppillus becomes king.

summary: Vonones I became king of the Parthian Empire.
text: Vonones I becomes king (shah) of the Parthian Empire.

summary: Tiberius defeated the Illyrians on the River Bathinus in Dalmatia.
text: Roman general Tiberius defeats the Illyrians in Dalmatia on the River Bathinus, but the Great Illyrian Revolt continues.

summary: Augustus exiled Julia the Younger, disgraced Lucius Aemilius Paullus, and broke off the betrothal of Claudius to Aemilia Lepida.
text: Vipsania Julia is exiled. Lucius Aemilius Paullus and his family are disgraced. Augustus breaks off the engagement of Claudius to Paullus' daughter Aemilia Lepida. An effort is made to betroth Claudius to Livia Medullina Camilla.

summary: Ovid began writing the Fasti after completing the Metamorphoses.
text: After completing Metamorphoses, Ovid begins the Fasti (Festivals), 6 books that detail the first 6 months of the year and provide valuable insights into the Roman calendar.

summary: Augustus banished the poet Ovid from Rome to Tomis on the Black Sea.
text: Roman poet Ovid is banished from Rome and exiled to the Black Sea near Tomis (modern-day Constanța).

summary: Drusus Caesar, member of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, was born.
text: Drusus Caesar, member of the Julio-Claudian dynasty (d. AD 33)

summary: Future Roman consul Titus Flavius Sabinus was born.
text: Titus Flavius Sabinus, Roman consul and brother of Vespasian (d. AD 69)

summary: Roman general Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus died.
text: Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus, Roman general (b. 64 BC)

summary: Bato the Daesitiate surrendered to Roman forces, ending the Bellum Batonianum.
text: Bellum Batonianum: The Daesitiate chieftain Bato (Daesitiate chieftain) surrendered to Roman forces.

summary: Arminius and his Germanic allies destroyed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
text: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest: Legio XVII, XVIII and XIX are lured by Arminius into an ambush and defeated by his tribe, the Cherusci, and their Germanic allies. The Roman aquilae are lost and the Roman general and governor Publius Quinctilius Varus dies by suicide. Legio II Augusta, XX Valeria Victrix, and XIII Gemina move to Germany to replace the lost legions.

summary: The Roman province of Illyricum was divided into Pannonia and Dalmatia.
text: First record of the subdivision of the province of Illyricum into lower (Pannonia) and upper (Dalmatia) regions.

summary: The Lex Papia Poppaea was adopted in Italy to encourage marriage and childbearing by penalizing celibacy.
text: In order to increase the number of marriages, and ultimately the population, the Lex Papia Poppaea is adopted in Italy. This law prohibits celibacy and childless relationships.

summary: The Roman government instituted inheritance and sales taxes to relieve financial strain caused by military campaigns.
text: Roman finances become strained following the Danubian insurrection and the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, resulting in the levying of two new taxes: five percent on inheritances, and one percent on sales.

summary: Cunobeline was first recorded as king of the Catuvellauni at Camulodunum.
text: Cunobeline is first recorded to be king of the Catuvellauni at Camulodunum (modern-day Colchester) in Britain.

summary: Ovid completed the curse poem Ibis while exiled at Tomis.
text: Ovid completes the curse poem Ibis.

summary: Future Roman emperor Vespasian was born near Reate.
text: Vespasian, Roman emperor (d. AD 79)

summary: Roman general Publius Quinctilius Varus died by suicide following defeat at the Teutoburg Forest.
text: Publius Quinctilius Varus, Roman general (b. 46 BC)

summary: Roman centurion Marcus Caelius was killed at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
text: Marcus Caelius, Roman centurion (b. c. 45 BC)

summary: Tiberius assumed command of Roman forces in Germania.
text: Tiberius assumed command of Roman forces in Germania.

summary: The Roman province of Illyricum was divided into Pannonia and Dalmatia.
text: Illyricum was divided into the provinces of Pannonia and Dalmatia.

summary: Localized Germanic tribes of the Irminones became distinct.
text: Differentiation of localized Teutonic tribes of the Irminones.

summary: The Roman Senate adopted the Senatus consultum Silanianum regarding slaves in a murdered master's household.
text: Senatus consultum Silanianum is adopted.

summary: Ovid completed the third book of the Tristia describing the grief of banishment.
text: Ovid completes Tristia III (the "Sorrows") describing the sadness of banishment.

summary: Greek engineer Hero of Alexandria was born.
text: Hero of Alexandria, Greek engineer (d. c. AD 70)

summary: Future pope Linus was born.
text: Pope Linus, Pope in Catholic church (d. AD 76)

summary: Roman consul Lucius Vipstanus Poplicola was born.
text: Lucius Vipstanus Poplicola, Roman consul (d. after AD 59)

summary: Future Praetorian prefect Tigellinus was born in Agrigentum.
text: Tigellinus, Roman Praetorian prefect (d. AD 69)

summary: Greek scholar Didymus Chalcenterus died in Alexandria.
text: Didymus Chalcenterus, Greek scholar and grammarian (b. c. 63 BC)

summary: Jewish scholar and leader Hillel the Elder died in Jerusalem.
text: Hillel the Elder, Babylonian sage, scholar, and Jewish leader (b. c. 110 BC)

summary: Germanicus secured Germania Inferior and the Rhine frontier.
text: Germania Inferior and the Rhine are secured by Germanicus.

summary: Augustus abandoned plans to establish an imperial border at the Elbe, reinforcing defenses along the Rhine and Danube.
text: Emperor Augustus abandons his plan to create a defensive border at the Elbe, in order to reinforce the Roman defenses along the Rhine and the Danube.

summary: An imperial edict prohibited divinatory practices across the Roman Empire and forbade consultations regarding anyone's death.
text: An edict is issued effecting an empire-wide ban on divinatory practices, especially astrology. The edict requires any consultation between a customer and a practitioner to be conducted with at least one third party witness present, and bans inquiry into anyone's death.

summary: Artabanus II became ruler of Parthia.
text: Artabanus II becomes ruler of Parthia.

summary: Prominent Roman jurist Marcus Antistius Labeo died.
text: Marcus Antistius Labeo, prominent Roman jurist

summary: Augustus ordered a major Roman invasion of Germany beyond the Rhine.
text: Augustus orders a major invasion of Germany beyond the Rhine.

summary: Quirinius returned from Judea to Rome to become a counselor to Tiberius.
text: Quirinius returns from Judea to become a counselor to Tiberius.

summary: The Roman Empire overthrew the Armenian Artaxiad dynasty.
text: The Armenian Artaxiad dynasty is overthrown by the Romans.

summary: Ovid ceased work on his Fasti while in exile after completing six books.
text: Ovid stops writing Fasti, because of the lack of resources (being far from the libraries of Rome). He completes 6 books that detail festivals found in the Roman calendar.

summary: Annius Rufus was appointed Prefect of Judea.
text: Annius Rufus is appointed Prefect of Judea.

summary: Christian evangelist Mark the Evangelist was born.
text: Mark the Evangelist, Christian evangelist, martyr, known for The Gospel of Mark (d. 68 AD)

summary: Future Roman emperor Caligula was born at Antium.
text: Caligula, Roman emperor (d. 41 AD)

summary: King Rhoemetalces I of the Odrysian kingdom of Thrace died.
text: Rhoemetalces I – king of the Odrysian kingdom of Thrace from 12 BC to 12 AD

summary: Augustus granted Tiberius powers equal to his own as co-princeps.
text: Tiberius was granted power equal to Augustus as co-princeps.

summary: Emperor Augustus initiated his third census of the Roman Empire.
text: Emperor Augustus initiates his third census of the Roman Empire after 20 years.

summary: Abgar V of Edessa was reinstalled as king of Osroene.
text: Abgarus of Edessa is reinstalled as king of Osroene.

summary: The Roman Senate passed a decree restricting the Vigintisexviri magistracies to the equestrian order.
text: The Senate passes a senatus consultum restricting the reduced Vigintisexviri to the Ordo Equester.

summary: Ovid published the first three books of his Epistulae ex Ponto while in exile.
text: Ovid publishes books 1-3 of his Epistulae ex Ponto.

summary: Strabo published his treatise on the shape of the Earth.
text: Strabo publishes his book on the shape of the Earth.

summary: Future Roman praetorian prefect Casperius Aelianus was born.
text: Casperius Aelianus, Roman praetorian prefect (d. AD 98)

summary: Roman politician Gaius Silius was born.
text: Gaius Silius, Roman politician (d. AD 48)

summary: Deaf Roman painter Quintus Pedius died.
text: Quintus Pedius, Roman (deaf) painter

summary: Tiberius sent Germanicus to Germania and his son Drusus Julius Caesar to Pannonia to suppress mutinies.
text: Germanicus and Tiberius's natural son Drusus Julius Caesar were sent to suppress mutinies in Germania and Pannonia, respectively.

summary: Augustus concluded his third Roman census, recording nearly five million citizens.
text: Augustus' third (and final) 20-year census of the Roman Empire reports a total of 4,973,000 citizens.

summary: Augustus died at Nola and was deified by the Roman Senate.
text: Augustus, the first Roman emperor, dies and is declared to be a god.

summary: Tiberius succeeded his stepfather Augustus as Roman emperor.
text: Tiberius succeeds his stepfather Augustus as Roman emperor.

summary: Germanicus restored discipline among the mutinous Roman legions stationed along the Rhine.
text: Legions on the Rhine mutiny after the death of Augustus; Germanicus restores discipline amongst the legions.

summary: Germanicus was appointed commander of the Roman legions in Germania.
text: Germanicus is appointed commander of the forces in Germany, beginning a campaign that will end in 16.

summary: Germanicus led a brutal punitive raid against the Marsi along the upper Ruhr river.
text: Germanicus leads a brutal raid against the Marsi, a German tribe on the upper Ruhr river, who are massacred.

summary: A mutinous Roman legion sacked and plundered the town and port of Nauportus.
text: The town and port of Nauportus are plundered by a mutinous Roman legion that was sent there to build roads and bridges.

summary: Sextus Appuleius and Sextus Pompeius served as Roman consuls.
text: Sextus Appuleius and Sextus Pompeius serve as Roman consuls.

summary: Roman banker Lucius Caecilius Iucundus was born at Pompeii.
text: Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, Roman banker (d. AD 62)

summary: Future Roman consul Marcus Junius Silanus was born.
text: Marcus Junius Silanus, Roman consul (d. AD 54)

summary: First Roman emperor Augustus died at Nola.
text: Augustus, Roman emperor (b. 63 BC)

summary: Agrippa Postumus, grandson of Augustus, was executed while in exile on Planasia.
text: Agrippa Postumus, grandson of Augustus and former heir to the Empire (b. 12 BC)

summary: Roman consul Gnaeus Pompeius died.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius (Rufus), Roman consul

summary: Julia the Elder, daughter of Augustus, died in exile at Rhegium.
text: Julia the Elder, daughter of Augustus (b. 39 BC)

summary: Roman consul Lucius Aemilius Paullus died.
text: Lucius Aemilius Paullus, Roman consul

summary: Greek grammarian and poet Parthenius of Nicaea died.
text: Parthenius of Nicaea, Greek grammarian

summary: Roman consul Paullus Fabius Maximus died.
text: Paullus Fabius Maximus, Roman consul

summary: Roman nobleman Sempronius Gracchus was executed on the island of Cercina.
text: Sempronius Gracchus, Roman nobleman

summary: Lucius Seius Strabo was appointed governor of Egypt, leaving his son Sejanus as sole prefect of the Praetorian Guard.
text: Lucius Seius Strabo was appointed governor of Egypt. His son Sejanus remained as the sole prefect of the Praetorian Guard.

summary: Legio XV Apollinaris founded the colony of Emona on the site of modern Ljubljana.
text: Early (approx.) – Emona (on the site of modern-day Ljubljana) is founded by Legio XV Apollinaris.

summary: Germanicus captured Thusnelda, wife of Arminius, during his campaign against the Germanic tribes.
text: May – As part of his campaign against the Germanic peoples, Germanicus captures Thusnelda, wife of Arminius.

summary: Germanicus launched an offensive into Germania, recaptured the eagle of Legio XIX, and buried the remains of Varus' army at the Teutoburg Forest.
text: Summer – Germanicus launches a two-pronged attack from Vetera and Moguntiacum. On his return journey, he recaptures the aquila of Legio XIX and visits the battlefield of the Teutoburg Forest. Germanicus arranges the burial for the remains of Varus' army.

summary: Odessus on the Bulgarian Black Sea coast was annexed to the Roman province of Moesia.
text: Varna (Odessus), on the Bulgarian Black Sea Coast, is annexed to the Roman province of Moesia.

summary: The election of magistrates in Rome was transferred from the popular assemblies to the Emperor and the Senate.
text: In Rome, the election of magistrates passes from the people to the Emperor and the Senate.

summary: The river Tiber flooded parts of Rome.
text: The river Tiber floods parts of Rome.

summary: Nicolaus of Damascus wrote a biography of the emperor Augustus.
text: Nicolaus of Damascus writes a biography of the Emperor Augustus (Bios Kaisaros).

summary: The future Roman emperor Vitellius was born.
text: Vitellius, Roman emperor (d. AD 69)

summary: Agrippina the Younger, future Roman empress, was born.
text: Agrippina the Younger, Roman empress (d. AD 59)

summary: The Greek philosopher Apollonius of Tyana was born.
text: Apollonius of Tyana, Greek philosopher (d. c. AD 97)

summary: The Roman noblewoman Ennia Thrasylla was born.
text: Ennia Thrasylla, Roman noblewoman (d. AD 38)

summary: The future Roman empress Lollia Paulina was born.
text: Lollia Paulina, Roman empress (d. AD 49)

summary: The Roman consul and commander Lucius Verginius Rufus was born.
text: Lucius Verginius Rufus, Roman consul (d. AD 97)

summary: The Roman praetorian prefect Lucius Seius Strabo died.
text: Lucius Seius Strabo, Roman praetorian prefect (b. 46 BC)

summary: Germanicus led a Roman army of fifty thousand men to defeat the Germanic war chief Arminius at Idistaviso, recovering lost legionary eagles.
text: A Roman army of 50,000 men commanded by Germanicus gains a great victory at Idistaviso, defeating the German war chief Arminius, and recovering the lost eagles of Varus' legions.

summary: Germanicus embarked an army aboard a North Sea fleet and defeated Germanic forces along the Ems and Weser rivers before the fleet was hit by storms.
text: Germanicus employs the North Sea fleet to avoid dangerous rivers, embarking an army in the Rhine Delta, aboard circa 1,000 ships. He defeats the Germans at the Amisius river estuary and the Weser, but during its return, the Roman fleet is partially destroyed by storms.

summary: Roman governor Creticus Silanus summoned Vonones, the king of Armenia, to Syria.
text: Vonones, the beleaguered king of Armenia, is summoned to Syria, by Roman governor Creticus Silanus.

summary: Ovid published his poetry collection Epistulae ex Ponto while exiled in Tomis.
text: Ovid's "Epistulae ex Ponto" appears.

summary: Julia Drusilla, daughter of Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder, was born.
text: Julia Drusilla, daughter of Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder (d. AD 38)

summary: Claudius Drusus, son of Claudius and Plautia Urgulanilla, was born.
text: Claudius Drusus, son of Claudius and Plautia Urgulanilla

summary: Decimus Junius Silanus Torquatus, future Roman consul, was born.
text: Decimus Junius Silanus Torquatus, Roman consul (d. AD 64)

summary: The Roman senator Marcus Scribonius Libo committed suicide after being accused of conspiracy.
text: Marcus Scribonius Libo, Roman senator (forced to commit suicide)

summary: Tiberius executed Clemens, a Roman slave who impersonated Agrippa Postumus.
text: Clemens, Roman slave and impostor (executed by Tiberius)

summary: Scribonia, former wife of Caesar Augustus and mother of Julia the Elder, died.
text: Scribonia, second wife of Caesar Augustus

summary: Following the death of Archelaus, Tiberius annexed Cappadocia and organized it into a Roman province.
text: Archelaus of Cappadocia, king in Cappadocia and a Roman client, died. Tiberius annexed his territory, organizing it as the province of Cappadocia.

summary: Following the death of Antiochus III, Tiberius annexed Commagene and incorporated it into the province of Syria.
text: Antiochus III of Commagene, king of Commagene and a Roman client, died. Tiberius annexed his territory to the province of Syria.

summary: Germanicus returned to Rome and celebrated a triumph for his victories over the Germanic tribes west of the Elbe.
text: Germanicus returns to Rome as a conquering hero; he celebrates a triumph for his victories over the Cherusci, Chatti and other Germanic tribes west of the Elbe.

summary: Tiberius sent Germanicus to the East to lead a military campaign against Parthia.
text: Emperor Tiberius sends Germanicus to the east, in order to lead a military campaign against Parthia.

summary: Lucius Aelius Sejanus became praetorian prefect.
text: Lucius Aelius Sejanus becomes Praetorian prefect.

summary: Tacfarinas, leading the Musulamii and allied Berbers, began a guerrilla war against Rome and attacked the Limes Tripolitanus.
text: Tacfarinas, Numidian deserter from the Roman army, begins a guerrilla war against the Romans. He leads his own Musulamii tribe and a coalition of Berbers, attacking the Limes Tripolitanus, a fortified zone (limes) of the Roman Empire in Africa.

summary: Herod Antipas built the city of Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee in honor of Tiberius.
text: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, builds the city Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, in honor of Tiberius.

summary: A major earthquake in Anatolia destroyed Sardis and damaged several other cities.
text: An earthquake in Anatolia destroys the city of Sardis and damages several other cities.

summary: Archelaus, the last king of Cappadocia, died in Rome.
text: Archelaus, king of Cappadocia

summary: The Roman Latin writer Gaius Julius Hyginus died.
text: Gaius Julius Hyginus, Roman Latin writer

summary: The Roman historian Livy died in Patavium.
text: Livy, Roman historian

summary: The Roman senator and praetor Lucius Vipstanus Gallus died.
text: Lucius Vipstanus Gallus, Roman senator

summary: The Roman poet Ovid died in exile at Tomis.
text: Ovid, Roman poet (or AD 18)

summary: Tiberius granted Germanicus imperium over the eastern provinces of the Roman Empire.
text: Tiberius granted Germanicus imperium over the eastern half of the Empire.

summary: A detachment of Legio III Augusta was destroyed in an ambush by insurgent forces in Africa.
text: A vexillatio (sub-unit or detachment) of Legio III Augusta is destroyed by an ambush in Africa.

summary: Germanicus arrived in Syria as commander-in-chief for the Roman East.
text: Winter – Germanicus Caesar arrives in Syria, as new commander-in-chief for the Roman East.

summary: Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso ignored an order from Germanicus to send legions to Armenia.
text: Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso, governor of Syria, ignores the order of Germanicus to send Syrian-based legions, including Legio VI Ferrata and Legio X Fretensis, to Armenia to back him in his planned coronation of Artaxias III.

summary: Germanicus concluded a peace treaty with Artabanus II of Parthia recognizing him as king and friend of Rome.
text: Germanicus concludes a peace treaty with Artabanus II of Parthia, in which he is recognized as king and friend of Rome.

summary: Julia Livilla, daughter of Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder, was born.
text: Julia Livilla, daughter of Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder (d. AD 41)

summary: Greek epigrammatist Crinagoras died.
text: Crinagoras, Greek epigrammatist (b. 70 BC)

summary: Former ethnarch Herod Archelaus died in exile.
text: Herod Archelaus, Jewish ruler (ethnarch) (b. 23 BC)

summary: Roman poet Ovid died in exile at Tomis.
text: Publius Ovidius Naso, Roman poet (or AD 17)

summary: Catualda deposed Maroboduus as king of the Marcomanni, leading Rome to grant Maroboduus protection.
text: Maroboduus, king of the Marcomanni, is deposed by Catualda. This ends the threat to the Romans from Germanic tribes until the reign of Marcus Aurelius. Rome places them under its protection.

summary: Germanicus died near Antioch, accusing Syrian governor Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso of poisoning him.
text: Germanicus Julius Caesar, commander in chief of the Roman legions in the East and beloved by the legionaries, falls ill and dies. On his deathbed he accuses Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso, the governor of Syria, of poisoning him.

summary: Emperor Tiberius expelled practitioners of Egyptian rites from Rome and deported thousands of Jews from Sicily.
text: Emperor Tiberius expels the Egyptians from Rome, and deports 4,000 Jews from Sicily.

summary: Agrippina the Elder accused Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso of murdering her husband Germanicus.
text: Agrippina the Elder accuses Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso of having assassinated her husband Germanicus Julius Caesar in Antioch. However, there is no credible evidence and the charge is never proven. (In ancient times, when medical science was not advanced, poison was usually suspected whenever a young, healthy person died suddenly. There was no way to pinpoint and trace the substance after death; therefore, it was considered a quick, easy and non-traceable form of homicide.)

summary: A triumphal arch dedicated to Germanicus was erected in Saintes.
text: A triumphal arch is built for Germanicus Julius Caesar in Saintes.

summary: Deposed king Vonones I escaped custody in Cilicia and was killed by a Roman veteran.
text: King Vonones I is removed to Cilicia and kept under house arrest. He escapes, but is caught and killed by a retired Roman legion veteran.

summary: Tiberius Gemellus, grandson of Tiberius, was born.
text: Tiberius Gemellus, grandson of Tiberius (d. c. 38 AD)

summary: Roman general Germanicus died.
text: Germanicus, Roman general (b. 15 BC)

summary: Roman client king Cotys III of Thrace died.
text: Cotys III (or Cotys VIII), Roman client king of Thrace

summary: Former Parthian king Vonones I died in Cilicia.
text: Vonones I, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Galba served as praetor in Rome.
text: Galba, the future emperor, is a Roman praetor.

summary: Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso committed suicide in Rome ahead of his trial for the death of Germanicus.
text: Emperor Tiberius is forced to order an investigation and a public trial in the Roman Senate, for the murder of Germanicus. Fearing he will be found guilty, Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso commits suicide.

summary: Roman statesman and former governor of Syria Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso died.
text: Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso, Roman statesman and governor of Syria (b. 44 BC)

summary: Vipsania Agrippina died.
text: Vipsania Agrippina, wife of Gaius Asinius Gallus and former wife of Tiberius (b. 36 BC)

summary: Queen Amanitore of the Kingdom of Kush died.
text: Amanitore, Nubian Queen Regnant of the Kushitic Kingdom of Meroë

summary: Gaius Silius suppressed a revolt of the Aedui led by Julius Sacrovir.
text: The Aedui revolt under Julius Florus and Julius Sacrovir; the revolt is suppressed by Gaius Silius.

summary: Tiberius took office as Roman consul for the fourth time.
text: Emperor Tiberius is a Roman Consul for the fourth time.

summary: The Romans established a buffer state in the territory of the Quadi in modern Slovakia.
text: The Romans create a buffer state in the territory of the Quadi, in southern Slovakia.

summary: Barracks for the Praetorian Guard were constructed on the Quirinal Hill in Rome.
text: Barracks are constructed for the Praetorian Guard, on the Quirinal (located on the Seven Hills of Rome).

summary: The manufacture of pens and metal writing tools began in Rome.
text: The manufacture of pens and metal writing tools begins in Rome .

summary: Germanic chieftain Arminius was assassinated.
text: Arminius, Germanic military leader (b. 18/17 BC)

summary: Roman poet Clutorius Priscus was executed.
text: Clutorius Priscus, Roman poet (b. c. 20 BC)

summary: Roman consul Marcus Valerius Messalla Barbatus died.
text: Marcus Valerius Messalla Barbatus, Roman consul (b. 11 BC)

summary: Roman governor Publius Sulpicius Quirinius died.
text: Publius Sulpicius Quirinius, Roman governor (b. c. 51 BC)

summary: Tiberius granted Drusus Julius Caesar tribunician power, marking Drusus Julius Caesar as his chosen successor.
text: Tiberius granted Drusus Julius Caesar tribunician power, marking him as his choice as successor.

summary: Valeria Messalina, future wife of Emperor Claudius, was born.
text: Valeria Messalina, third wife of Emperor Claudius (d. 48 AD)

summary: Roman jurist Gaius Ateius Capito died.
text: Gaius Ateius Capito, Roman jurist and suffect consul (b. c. 30 BC)

summary: Junia Tertia, widow of Gaius Cassius Longinus, died.
text: Junia Tertia, wife of Gaius Cassius Longinus (b. c. 75 BC)

summary: Drusus Julius Caesar died, possibly poisoned by Sejanus or Livilla.
text: Drusus Julius Caesar died, possibly after being poisoned by Sejanus or his wife Livilla.

summary: Strabo published Geographica, describing the world known to the Greeks and Romans.
text: Greek geographer Strabo publishes Geographica, a work covering the world known to the Romans and Greeks at the time of Emperor Augustus – it is the only such book to survive from the ancient world.

summary: Sejanus began to dominate the Roman Senate and Tiberius following the death of Drusus Julius Caesar.
text: Lucius Aelius Sejanus begins to dominate the Roman Senate and Tiberius, after the death of Drusus.

summary: Roman writer and naturalist Pliny the Elder was born.
text: Pliny the Elder, Roman scientist and writer (d. 79 AD)

summary: Drusus Julius Caesar, son of Emperor Tiberius, died.
text: Drusus Julius Caesar, son of Emperor Tiberius (b. 14 BC)

summary: King Juba II of Mauretania died.
text: Juba II, king of Mauretania (b. c. 50 BC)

summary: Roman statesman Servius Cornelius Lentulus Maluginensis died.
text: Servius Cornelius Lentulus Maluginensis, Roman statesman

summary: The consular terms of Servius Cornelius Cethegus and Lucius Visellius Varro expired after passing the Lex Visellia laws on slavery.
text: The terms of Servius Cornelius Cethegus and Lucius Visellius Varro as Roman consuls expire. During their terms, two laws pertaining to slavery had been passed, the lex Visellia de iure Quiritium Latinorum qui inter vigiles militaverant granting freed slaves Roman citizenship after six years service, and the Lex Visellia de poenis libertinorum qui ingenuorum honores usurpabant which penalized non-citizens who falsely claimed to be ingenui or freeborn Romans.

summary: Gaius Calpurnius Aviola and Publius Cornelius Lentulus Scipio took office as suffect consuls.
text: Midway through the Roman year 777 A.U.C., Gaius Calpurnius Aviola and Publius Lentulus Scipio begin the new consular year as the new suffect consuls.

states.value: Gaius Calpurnius Aviola and Publius Cornelius Lentulus Scipio

summary: The Roman Empire ended its war against Numidia and Mauretania and annexed the kingdoms.
text: The Roman war against Numidia and Mauretania ends with the annexation of the two African kingdoms.

summary: Roman forces suppressed the revolt of Tacfarinas in North Africa.
text: The revolt of Tacfarinas revolt in Africa is repressed.

summary: The Roman Senate expelled actors from the city of Rome.
text: The Senate expels actors from Rome.

summary: The Masinissa line of rulers in North Africa came to an end.
text: The Masinissa line of the rulers of Carthage ends.

summary: Roman general and consul Gaius Silius died.
text: Gaius Silius, Roman general and consul

summary: Roman consul Lucius Calpurnius Piso died.
text: Lucius Calpurnius Piso, Roman consul

summary: Greek geographer Strabo died.
text: Strabo, Greek geographer and historian

summary: Numidian rebel leader Tacfarinas died.
text: Tacfarinas, Numidian military leader

summary: Emperor Tiberius settled a dispute over the Ager Dentheliales on Mount Taygetus by awarding the land to Messenia instead of Sparta.
text: Emperor Tiberius settles a dispute between Messenia and Sparta over the Ager Dentheliales on Mount Taygetus, awarding the land to Messenia.

summary: Sejanus unsuccessfully sought permission to marry Livilla.
text: Lucius Aelius Sejanus unsuccessfully attempts to marry Livilla.

summary: Gaius Julius Civilis was born.
text: Gaius Julius Civilis, Batavian military leader

summary: Quintus Volusius Saturninus, later Roman consul, was born.
text: Quintus Volusius Saturninus, Roman consul

summary: Roman historian and writer Aulus Cremutius Cordus died.
text: Aulus Cremutius Cordus, Roman historian and writer

summary: Roman consul Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Augur died.
text: Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus, Roman consul (b. 54 BC)

summary: Lucius Antonius, grandson of Mark Antony, died.
text: Lucius Antonius, grandson of Mark Antony (b. 20 BC)

summary: Roman consul Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus died.
text: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, Roman consul (b. 49 BC)

summary: Emperor Tiberius retired to Capri, leaving Sejanus in effective control of Rome.
text: Emperor Tiberius retires to Capri, leaving the Praetorian Guard under Lucius Aelius Sejanus in charge of the Roman Empire and the city of Rome.

summary: Romans crushed an uprising of Thracian tribesmen.
text: Romans crush an uprising of Thracian tribesmen.

summary: Pontius Pilate was appointed prefect of the Roman province of Judea.
text: Pontius Pilate is appointed as prefect of the Roman imperial province of Judea.

summary: Jesus was baptized in the Jordan River by John the Baptist.
text: Jesus is baptized in the Jordan River by John the Baptist and begins his public ministry, according to some scholars.

summary: Claudia Pulchra, friend of Agrippina the Elder, died.
text: Claudia Pulchra, cousin and close friend to Agrippina the Elder (b. 14 BC)

summary: Roman consul Marcus Asinius Agrippa died.
text: Marcus Asinius Agrippa, Roman consul

summary: Roman politician Quintus Haterius died.
text: Quintus Haterius, Roman politician

summary: A fire broke out in Rome.
text: A fire breaks out in Rome.

summary: A poorly built amphitheatre in Fidenae collapsed, killing 20,000 spectators.
text: A poorly built amphitheatre in Fidenae collapses, killing 20,000 of the 50,000 spectators.

summary: An Arch of Triumph was erected in Rimini in honor of Augustus.
text: An Arc of Triumph is erected in Rimini, in honor of the former Emperor Augustus.

summary: John the Baptist began preaching and, according to some interpretations, baptized Jesus.
text: Using the dates and ranges listed in the Gospel of Luke, this year can be established as when John the Baptist begins preaching. It is also argued that Jesus was baptised by John in the final months of this year before his temptation and the first of three Passovers listed in the Gospel of John (another possibility is AD 29).

summary: Herod Agrippa II, future king of Judea, was born.
text: Herod Agrippa II, king of Judea

summary: Roman writer and suffect consul Petronius was born.
text: Petronius, Roman writer and suffect consul (d. AD 66)

summary: Roman nobleman Publius Quinctilius Varus the Younger died.
text: Publius Quinctilius Varus the Younger, Roman nobleman (b. AD 4)

summary: Roman legions were transported by fleet to the fortress of Flevum on the Rhine to oppose the rebellious Frisians.
text: Roman legions in Germania are transported by fleet to the fortress of Flevum on the Rhine, to operate against the rebellious Frisians.

summary: The Frisians negotiated a treaty with the Roman Empire at the River Rhine.
text: The Frisians negotiate a treaty with the Roman Empire at the River Rhine.

summary: Frisians revolted against Roman authorities, hanging tax collectors and besieging a local fort.
text: Frisians revolt against Roman authorities, hanging tax collectors and besieging a local fort. Frisians achieve victory and gain considerable prestige among other local tribes.
