summary: Jewish client queen Julia Berenice was born.
text: Julia Berenice, Jewish client queen of the Roman imperial province of Judea

summary: Roman consul and epic poet Silius Italicus was born.
text: Silius Italicus, Roman consul and epic poet

summary: Agrippina the Elder was exiled to Pandataria and her sons were imprisoned by Sejanus.
text: Agrippina the Elder is exiled to the island of Pandataria, and her sons (except Caligula) are imprisoned by Lucius Aelius Sejanus.

summary: Aulus Plautius became suffect consul alongside Lucius Nonius Asprenas.
text: Aulus Plautius, later military leader of the invasion of Britain under Emperor Claudius, becomes suffect consul alongside Lucius Nonius Asprenas.

summary: The ministries of John the Baptist and Jesus are thought to have started in this year according to the Gospel of Luke.
text: According to the Gospel of Luke (Luke 3:1-2), the ministries of John the Baptist and Jesus is thought to have started this year.

summary: Jesus was executed by crucifixion according to Roman Catholic tradition and Tertullian.
text: Jesus is executed by crucifixion, according to Roman Catholic tradition and Tertullian's chronology.

summary: Roman consul Gaius Fufius Geminus died.
text: Gaius Fufius Geminus, Roman plebeian tribune and consul

summary: Julia the Younger, granddaughter of Augustus, died in exile.
text: Julia the Younger, granddaughter of Augustus (b. 19 BC)

summary: Livia, wife of Augustus and mother of Tiberius, died.
text: Livia, wife of Augustus and mother of Tiberius (b. 58 BC)

summary: Jesus died in Jerusalem according to some chronological traditions.
text: Jesus (debatable) (b. 5 BC)

summary: Sejanus ordered the arrest and exile of Agrippina the Elder and her sons Nero Julius Caesar and Drusus Caesar.
text: Agrippina the Elder (the wife of Germanicus) and two of her sons, Nero Julius Caesar and Drusus Caesar, are arrested and exiled on orders of Lucius Aelius Sejanus (the prefect of the Praetorian Guard), and later starved to death in suspicious circumstances. In Sejanus's purge of Agrippina the Elder and her family, her son Caligula, and her three daughters, Agrippina the Younger, Julia Drusilla and Julia Livilla are the only survivors.

summary: Phaedrus translated Aesop's fables into Latin verse and composed new fables of his own.
text: Phaedrus translates Aesop's fables, and composes some of his own.

summary: Velleius Paterculus wrote a general compendium of Roman and world history.
text: Velleius Paterculus writes the general history of the countries known in Antiquity.

summary: Jesus was crucified in Jerusalem.
text: Jesus is crucified in Jerusalem (possible date)

summary: Future Roman emperor Nerva was born in Narni.
text: Nerva, Roman emperor (d. AD 98)

summary: Poppaea Sabina, future wife of Emperor Nero, was born in Pompeii.
text: Poppaea Sabina, second wife of Nero (d. AD 65)

summary: Roman general Quintus Petillius Cerialis was born.
text: Quintus Petillius Cerialis, Roman general

summary: Tiberius invited Caligula to join him on Capri.
text: Tiberius invited Germanicus's son Caligula to join him on Capri.

summary: Tiberius discovered the treachery of his co-consul Sejanus and had him arrested and executed.
text: Lucius Aelius Sejanus is named co-Consul to Emperor Tiberius. However, Tiberius becomes aware of Sejanus' treachery and has him arrested and executed.

summary: Naevius Sutorius Macro became prefect of the Praetorian Guard after the execution of Sejanus.
text: Naevius Sutorius Macro becomes the leader of the Praetorian Guard after Sejanus is executed.

summary: Roman consul Gnaeus Arrius Antoninus was born.
text: Gnaeus Arrius Antoninus, Roman consul

summary: Roman Stoic philosopher Gaius Musonius Rufus was born in Volsinii.
text: Musonius Rufus, Roman Stoic philosopher (d. 101)

summary: Jesus was crucified in Jerusalem according to some scholarly chronologies.
text: Jesus of Nazareth (possible date of the crucifixion) (born circa 4 BC) The other possible dates also supported by scholarly consensus among a survey of 100 published scholarly biblical statements are April 7, AD 30 and April 3, AD 33, and April 27, AD 31 (according to a Chodesh calculating system).

summary: Praetorian prefect Sejanus was executed in Rome.
text: Lucius Aelius Sejanus, Roman prefect and advisor (b. 20 BC)

summary: Livilla died in Rome following the downfall of Sejanus.
text: Claudia Livia Julia, niece and daughter-in-law of Tiberius (b. 13 BC)

summary: Roman historian Marcus Velleius Paterculus died.
text: Marcus Velleius Paterculus, Roman historian and writer (b. c. 19 BC)

summary: Nero Julius Caesar died in exile on the island of Ponza.
text: Nero Julius Caesar Germanicus, grandson and heir of Tiberius (b. AD 6)

summary: Philo wrote an allegorical interpretation of the Hebrew Scriptures in Alexandria.
text: Philo writes his symbolic interpretation of the Old Testament (Allegory).

summary: Future Roman emperor Otho was born in Ferento.
text: 28 April – Marcus Salvius Otho, Roman emperor (d. AD 69)

summary: Roman rhetorician and satirist Cassius Severus died in exile on Serifos.
text: Cassius Severus, Roman rhetor and writer

summary: Roman consul Decimus Haterius Agrippa died.
text: Decimus Haterius Agrippa, Roman consul

These actions lead to a lack of money, a crisis of confidence, and much land speculation. The primary victims are senators, knights and the wealthy. Many aristocratic families are ruined.

According to Josephus, Herod's defeat was popularly believed to be divine punishment for his execution of John the Baptist. Emperor Tiberius orders his governor of Syria, Vitellius, to capture or kill Aretas, but he is reluctant to support Herod and abandons his campaign upon Tiberius' death in AD 37.

summary: Caligula fell severely ill and, upon recovering, began executing those close to him whom he perceived as threats.
text: October – Caligula becomes seriously ill, or perhaps is poisoned. He recovers from his illness, but Caligula turns toward the diabolical: he starts to kill off those who are close to him, whom he sees as a serious threat.

text: Caligula orders that a statue of himself be placed in the Temple in Jerusalem. The governor of Syria, Publius Petronius, who is responsible for having an erecting the statue, faces mass demonstrations by Jews of the region and manages to delay construction of the statue until the death of Caligula in AD 41.

summary: Aulus Plautius landed four Roman legions in Kent and defeated the Britons led by Caratacus and Togodumnus at the Battle of the Medway.
text: Roman conquest of Britain: May – Aulus Plautius, crossing (probably) from Boulogne (Bononia) in the Classis Britannica, lands with four Roman legions (20,000 men) and a similar number of auxiliaries at Rutupiae (probably modern Richborough) on the east coast of Kent. General (future emperor) Vespasian plays a major role in the defeat of the Britons led by the brothers Caratacus and Togodumnus (leaders of the Catuvellauni) in the 2-day Battle of the Medway (probably at the river near Rochester) and the Romans drive them back to and across the River Thames; Togodumnus dies soon after. Plautius halts at the Thames and sends for the Emperor.

summary: Emperor Claudius led the march on Camulodunum, received the submission of eleven British kings, and made Aulus Plautius governor.
text: Roman conquest of Britain: September – Emperor Claudius, who arrives with reinforcements including war elephants, leads the march on Camulodunum (modern Colchester). Eleven British kings, probably including those of the Iceni and Brigantes, submit without a fight. Plautius becomes the first Governor of Roman Britain.
names: List of governors of Roman Britain

summary: Vespasian began campaigns to subdue southwest Britain for the Roman Empire.

text: Roman conquest of Britain: The Romans capture a Brythonic settlement at Kent and rename it Durovernum Cantiacorum (modern Canterbury); and establish a Roman fort to guard the crossing of the Kentish River Stour.

summary: The Romans established Londinium on the River Thames.

text: The Senate holds consultations regarding real estate speculation in Rome.

summary: Paul the Apostle began his missionary travels from Antioch.
text: Paul of Tarsus begins his missionary travels, according to one traditional dating scheme.

summary: Roman noblewoman Domitilla the Younger was born.
text: Domitilla the Younger, Roman noblewoman (d. AD 66)

summary: Roman politician Lucius Julius Ursus Servianus was born.
text: Lucius Julius Ursus Servianus, Roman politician (d. 136)

summary: Roman orator Lucius Vipstanus Messalla was born.
text: Lucius Vipstanus Messalla, Roman orator

summary: Greek biographer and historian Plutarch was born in Chaeronea.
text: Plutarch, Greek historian and biographer

summary: Roman poet Statius was born in Naples.
text: Publius Papinius Statius, Roman poet

summary: Roman politician Tiberius Julius Celsus Polemaeanus was born.
text: Tiberius Julius Celsus Polemaeanus, Roman politician

summary: Roman geographer Pomponius Mela died.
text: Pomponius Mela, Roman geographer

summary: Vardanes I, king of the Parthian Empire, was assassinated.
text: Vardanes I, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Rhoemetalces III, the Roman client king of the Odrysian kingdom, was killed by anti-Roman insurgents.
text: The Odrysian king Rhoemetalces III, a Roman client, was killed by anti-Roman insurgents.

summary: The settlement of Celje received municipal rights and was named municipium Claudia Celeia.
text: The settlement at Celje gets municipal rights, and is named municipium Claudia Celeia.

summary: Dobruja was annexed into the Roman province of Moesia.
text: Dobruja is annexed into Roman Moesia.

summary: A census revealed that there were over six million Roman citizens.
text: A census shows that there are more than 6,000,000 Roman citizens.

summary: Following the death of its king, Thracia was organized into a Roman province.
text: After the death of its king, Thracia becomes a Roman province.

summary: The Via Claudia Augusta reconnected Rome with the Danube frontier.
text: Rome and its northeast border are reunited by the Danube Road.

summary: A major famine caused by poor harvests struck the province of Syria.
text: A large famine occurred across Syria, recorded by Orosius, Suetonius, Tacitus and Josephus, due to bad harvests.

summary: Greek biographer and historian Plutarch was born in Chaeronea.
text: Plutarch, Greek historian and biographer

summary: Roman consul and provincial governor Marcus Vinicius died.
text: Marcus Vinicius, Roman consul and governor (b. c. 5 BC)

summary: Roman politician Servius Asinius Celer was executed.
text: Servius Asinius Celer, Roman politician (executed)

summary: Claudius revived the censorship and Secular Games and organised the order of the Haruspices in Rome.
text: Claudius revives the censorship and ludi saeculares, and organises the order of the Haruspices, with 60 members.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo took command of the Roman army in Germania Inferior, conquered the Chauci, and fought the Cherusci and Frisians.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo is made commander of the Roman army in Germania Inferior. He conquers the Chauci and fights against the Cherusci and Frisians.

summary: Gannascus led Chauci pirates to ravage the Gallic coast until Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo deployed the Rhine fleet against them.
text: Cauci pirates led by the Roman deserter Gannascus ravage the Gallic coast; Corbulo uses the Rhine fleet against them. The Frisian revolt is suppressed.

summary: Publius Ostorius Scapula replaced Aulus Plautius as governor of Roman Britain and suppressed incursions against the province.
text: Publius Ostorius Scapula replaces Aulus Plautius as governor of Britain. The south-east of the island is now a Roman province, while certain states on the south coast are ruled as a nominally independent client kingdom by Tiberius Claudius Cogidubnus, whose seat is probably at Fishbourne near Chichester. Ostorius immediately faces incursions from unconquered areas, which he puts down.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo ordered the construction of the Fossa Corbulonis canal connecting the Rhine and Meuse rivers.
text: Corbulo orders the construction of the canal Fossa Corbulonis, between the Rhine and Meuse in the Netherlands, which connects the city Forum Hadriani (Voorburg).

summary: Romans built the fortification of Traiectum near the mouth of the Rhine.
text: Romans build the Traiectum fortification near the mouth of the Rhine, which will later grow to be the city of Utrecht.

summary: Claudius founded the city Forum Claudii Vallensium at modern Martigny in the Alps.
text: Claudius founds the city Forum Claudii Vallensium (modern Martigny) in the Alpes Poeninae (Switzerland).

summary: Ananias son of Nedebeus became the high priest in Judea.
text: Ananias becomes high priest in Judaea.

summary: Paul the Apostle began his first missionary journey accompanied by Barnabas and Mark.
text: Paul starts his evangelistic work (first missionary journey), accompanied by Barnabas and Mark (possible date).

summary: Decimus Valerius Asiaticus, Roman politician and former consul, died.
text: Decimus Valerius Asiaticus, Roman politician and consul

summary: Gaius Sallustius Passienus Crispus, Roman consul, died.
text: Gaius Sallustius Crispus Passienus, Roman consul

actor: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (husband of Claudia Antonia)
summary: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, Roman nobleman and son-in-law of Claudius, died.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, Roman nobleman
cast: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (husband of Claudia Antonia)
names: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (husband of Claudia Antonia)

summary: Quintus Sanquinius Maximus, Roman politician and governor, died.
text: Quintus Sanquinius Maximus, Roman politician

summary: Vardanes I, king of the Parthian Empire, died.
text: Vardanes I, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Empress Messalina was executed in Rome for conspiring against Emperor Claudius.
text: Claudius's wife Messalina was executed for conspiracy.

summary: Emperor Claudius invested Herod Agrippa II with the superintendence of the Temple in Jerusalem.
text: Emperor Claudius invests Agrippa II with the office of superintendent of the Temple in Jerusalem.

summary: Claudius obtained senatorial approval to marry his niece Agrippina the Younger following Messalina's execution.
text: After the execution of his wife Messalina, Claudius gets senatorial approval to marry his niece, Agrippina the Younger.

summary: Publius Ostorius Scapula defeated a revolt of the Iceni and campaigned against the Deceangli and Brigantes in Britain.
text: Publius Ostorius Scapula, governor of Britain, announces his intention to disarm all Britons south and east of the Trent and Severn. The Iceni, an independent, allied kingdom within that area, revolt but are defeated. Ostorius then moves against the Deceangli in north Wales, but is forced to abandon the campaign to deal with a revolt among the allied Brigantes.

summary: Claudius granted Roman citizenship to the Aedui and admitted Gallic nobles into the Roman Senate.
text: Gallic nobles are admitted to the Roman Senate. Claudius grants the rights of citizenship to the Aedui.

summary: Paul the Apostle traveled to Cyprus and Asia Minor during his first missionary journey.
text: Paul of Tarsus through his first mission goes to Cyprus and Asia Minor.

summary: According to Christian tradition, Martha traveled to Avignon.
text: According to Christian tradition, Martha travels to Avignon.

summary: Ulpia Marciana, sister of the future emperor Trajan, was born.
text: Ulpia Marciana, sister of Trajan (d. 112)

summary: Roman politician Gaius Silius was executed for conspiring with Empress Messalina.
text: Gaius Silius, Roman politician (b. AD 13)

summary: Roman pantomime actor Mnester was executed following the fall of Messalina.
text: Mnester, Roman pantomime actor

summary: Emperor Claudius married his niece Agrippina the Younger, who gained significant influence in Rome.
text: Emperor Claudius marries his niece Agrippina the Younger , and most of the real power falls to Agrippina.

summary: Seneca the Younger became tutor to the future emperor Nero.
text: Seneca the Younger becomes Nero's tutor.

summary: Melankomas won the boxing championship at the 207th Olympic Games.
text: Melankomas is the boxing champion, at the 207th Olympic Games.

summary: Emperor Claudius expelled the Jewish community from the city of Rome.
text: Likely date for the expulsion of the Jews from Rome.

summary: Nero became engaged to Claudia Octavia, the daughter of Emperor Claudius.
text: Nero becomes engaged to Claudia Octavia, daughter of Claudius.

summary: Lucius Junius Silanus Torquatus was accused of incest by Agrippina the Younger and sentenced to death by the Senate.
text: Agrippina the Younger charges Octavia's first fiancé, Lucius Junius Silanus Torquatus, with incest. He is brought before the Senate, and sentenced to death.

summary: Publius Ostorius Scapula founded a veteran colony at Camulodunum and prepared a legion to invade the Silures.
text: In Britain, governor Publius Ostorius Scapula founds a colonia for Roman veterans at Camulodunum (Colchester). Verulamium (St Albans) is probably established as a municipium the same year. A legion is stationed on the borders of the Silures of South Wales in preparation for invasion.

summary: The first apostolic council of the early Christian church convened in Jerusalem.
text: First apostolic council in Jerusalem .

summary: Paul the Apostle departed with Silas on his second missionary journey while Barnabas and Mark sailed to Cyprus.
text: The Apostle Paul begins his second missionary journey with Silas while Barnabas goes to Cyprus with Mark.

summary: Paul the Apostle composed his Epistle to the Galatians.
text: The New Testament book Paul's Epistle to the Galatians is probably written.

summary: Christianity spread into Europe, gaining communities in Philippi and Rome.
text: Christianity spreads into Europe, especially at Rome and at Philippi (probable date according to chronology derived from the Acts of the Apostles).

summary: Former Roman empress Lollia Paulina died.
text: Lollia Paulina, Roman noblewoman and empress (b. AD 15)

summary: Emperor Claudius adopted Nero as his son.
text: Claudius adopted Agrippina's son Nero as his own son.

summary: Cologne was elevated to the status of a Roman colony and city.
text: Cologne is raised to the status of a city.

summary: The Romans founded Utrecht and built a castellum on the Rhine frontier.
text: Utrecht is founded, and a Roman fortification (castellum) is constructed at the Rhine border in the present-day Netherlands.

summary: Emperor Claudius appointed Herod Agrippa II as ruler of Chalcis.
text: Roman emperor Claudius appoints Agrippa II governor of Chalcis.

summary: Procurator Ventidius Cumanus had a Roman soldier beheaded for burning a Torah scroll in Judaea.
text: In Judaea, a Roman soldier seizes and burns a Torah scroll. Procurator Cumanus has the culprit beheaded, calming down local Jews and delaying for almost two decades the outbreak of their revolt.

summary: The Apostles convened the Council of Jerusalem.
text: The Apostles hold the Council of Jerusalem .

summary: Paul travelled to Philippi, Thessaloniki, Beroea, and Athens on his second missionary journey.
text: Paul travels to Philippi, Thessaloniki, Beroea, and Athens (second missionary journey).

summary: Paul the Apostle wrote the Epistle to the Romans.
text: The Epistle to the Romans is written .

summary: Hero of Alexandria invented an early steam turbine.
text: Hero of Alexandria invents a steam turbine (possible date).

summary: Pamphilus of Alexandria wrote a poetic lexicon.
text: Pamphilus of Alexandria writes a poetic lexicon.

summary: Pedanius Dioscorides documented the medicinal properties of plants in De Materia Medica.
text: Pedanius Dioscorides describes the medical applications of plants in De Materia Medica.

summary: Publius Ostorius Scapula campaigned against the Silures in Wales as Londinium and other Roman settlements were established.
text: In Britain, governor Publius Ostorius Scapula begins his campaign against the recalcitrant Silures of south Wales, who are led by the former Catuvellaunian prince Caratacus. London (Londinium), Exeter (Isca Dumnoniorum), Tripontium (near modern Rugby) and the fort of Manduessedum (near modern Atherstone) are founded .

summary: The Romans built a wooden bridge across the Thames at Londinium.
text: Romans build a wooden bridge across the Thames in the London area.

summary: Abgar V, Roman client king of Osroene, died.
text: Abgar V, Roman client king of Osroene

summary: Roman medical encyclopedist Aulus Cornelius Celsus died.
text: Aulus Cornelius Celsus, Roman author of De Medicina (b. c. 25 BC)

summary: Gamaliel the Elder, Jewish Nasi, died.
text: Gamaliel the Elder, Jewish ruler (Nasi) in Babylonia

summary: Roman fabulist Gaius Julius Phaedrus died.
text: Gaius Julius Phaedrus, Roman fabulist (b. c. 15 BC)

summary: Hellenistic Jewish philosopher Philo of Alexandria died.
text: Philo of Alexandria, Jewish philosopher (b. c. 20 BC)

summary: Roman physician Scribonius Largus died.
text: Scribonius Largus, Roman court physician (b. c. AD 1)

summary: Emperor Claudius and Vespasian assumed office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Claudius and future emperor Titus Flavius Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.

summary: Praetorian prefect Burrus tasked Seneca the Younger with educating Nero.
text: Burrus, praetorian prefect (51–62 AD), charges Seneca with the education of Nero.

summary: Publius Ostorius Scapula defeated Caratacus in Wales, after which Cartimandua handed him over to Rome.
text: In Britain, governor Publius Ostorius Scapula defeats Caratacus and the Silures in the territory of the Ordovices in central Wales. Caratacus seeks sanctuary with Cartimandua, queen of the Brigantes in northern England, but she is a Roman ally and hands him over to Ostorius. Despite the defeat, the Silures continue to fight.

summary: Caratacus was displayed in Claudius's triumph at Rome, but the emperor spared his life.
text: The captured Caratacus is exhibited in chains in Claudius' triumph in Rome, but his dignified demeanour persuades the emperor to spare his life and allow his family to live free in the capital for a short period of time.

summary: Vonones II died shortly after ascending the throne, and his son Vologases I became king of Parthia.
text: Vonones II dies a few months after he had ascended to the throne. His son Vologases I becomes the new Parthian king.

summary: Gotarzes II, king of the Parthian Empire, died.
text: Gotarzes II, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Roman consul and censor Lucius Vitellius the Elder died.
text: Lucius Vitellius the Elder, Roman consul (b. 5 BC)

summary: Mithridates of Armenia, a Roman client king, was killed.
text: Mithridates of Armenia, Roman client king

summary: Vonones II, king of the Parthian Empire, died.
text: Vonones II, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Emperor Claudius began an effort to drain the Fucine Lake by digging a tunnel through Monte Salviano.
text: Emperor Claudius attempts to control the Fucine Lake by digging a 5.6 km tunnel through Monte Salviano, requiring 30,000 workers and eleven years.

summary: Emperor Claudius completed the Aqua Claudia and Anio Novus aqueducts started by Caligula.
text: Claudius completes the Aqua Claudia and Anio Novus, two aqueduct projects started by Caligula.

summary: A Roman law was enacted prohibiting the execution of elderly and disabled enslaved persons.
text: In Rome, a law prohibits the execution of old and crippled slaves.

summary: Barea Soranus served as suffect consul in Rome.
text: Barea Soranus is consul suffectus in Rome.

summary: Pliny the Elder wrote an account of the German wars.
text: Pliny the Elder writes his account of the German wars.

summary: Ananias son of Nedebeus, the high priest in Jerusalem, was sent to Rome after being accused of violence.
text: Ananias, a high priest in Jerusalem, is sent to Rome after being accused of violence.

summary: Following the death of Publius Ostorius Scapula, the Silures heavily defeated the Roman Second Legion in Britain before Aulus Didius Gallus quelled the uprising.
text: In Britain, governor Publius Ostorius Scapula dies while campaigning against the Silures of south Wales. Following his death, the Roman Second Legion are heavily defeated by the Silures. His replacement is Aulus Didius Gallus, who quells the rebellion and consolidates the gains the Romans have so far made, but does not seek new ones.

summary: Jewish leader Gamaliel died.
text: Gamaliel, Jewish leader (nasi)

summary: Queen Julia Iotapa of Commagene died.
text: Julia Iotapa, queen of Commagene

summary: Roman governor and general Publius Ostorius Scapula died while campaigning in Britain.
text: Publius Ostorius Scapula, Roman statesman and general

summary: Emperor Claudius removed Herod Agrippa II from the tetrarchy of Chalcis.
text: Emperor Claudius removes Herod Agrippa II from the tetrarchy of Chalcis in Greece.

summary: Decimus Junius Silanus Torquatus and Quintus Haterius Antoninus assumed the consulship in Rome.
text: Decimus Junius Silanus Torquatus and Quintus Haterius Antoninus become Roman consuls.

summary: Emperor Claudius secured a senatorial decree granting judicial power in financial cases to imperial procurators.
text: Claudius secures a senatorial decree that gives jurisdiction in financial cases to imperial procurators. This marks a significant strengthening of imperial powers at the expense of the Senate.

summary: Claudius adopted Nero as his son and arranged his marriage to Claudia Octavia.
text: Nero is adopted by Claudius as his son and marries his 14-year-old daughter Claudia Octavia.

summary: Claudius recognized Nero as his successor ahead of his biological son Britannicus.
text: Claudius accepts Nero as his successor, to the detriment of Britannicus, his son by his first wife, Valeria Messalina.

summary: Seneca the Younger wrote the tragedy Agamemnon in Rome.
text: Seneca writes the tragedy Agamemnon, which he intends to be read as the last chapter of a trilogy including two of his other tragedies, Medea and Edipus.

summary: Paul the Apostle wrote his Epistle to the Galatians from Ephesus.
text: Paul the Apostle writes his epistle to the Galatians from Ephesus .

summary: Evodius succeeded Saint Peter as Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Evodius succeeds Saint Peter as Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Aulus Didius Gallus established a Roman fort at Cardiff.
text: Cardiff is founded by Aulus Didius Gallus.

summary: Tiridates I, brother of Parthian King Vologases I, took the throne of Armenia in opposition to Rome.
text: Tiridates I, brother of Vologases I, comes to power in Armenia as an adversary of the Romans.

summary: Future Roman emperor Trajan was born.
text: (approximate year) Marcus Ulpius Traianus, Roman emperor (d. 117)

summary: Future Roman empress Domitia Longina was born.
text: Domitia Longina, Roman empress

summary: Emperor Claudius died, suspected of being poisoned, and was succeeded by Nero.
text: Emperor Claudius dies (possibly after being poisoned by Agrippina, his wife and niece), and is succeeded by Nero.

summary: Nero attempted to prohibit gladiatorial games in Rome.
text: Nero attempts to prohibit the gladiatorial games.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo arrived in the East to govern Asia with secret orders to restore Roman control over Armenia.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo arrives in the East and takes up an assignment as governor of Asia, with a secret brief from Nero and his chief ministers, Seneca and Burrus, to return Armenia to the Roman Empire.

summary: Domitius Corbulo marched Roman legions into Cappadocia and put the troops through rigorous mountain training.
text: Winter – Domitius Corbulo marches his legions (Legio VI Ferrata and Legio X) into the mountains of Cappadocia and makes camp. He gives the men a harsh training, twenty-five-mile marches and weapons drills.

summary: Onesimus succeeded Stachys as Bishop of Byzantium.
text: Patriarch Onesimus succeeds Stachys the Apostle as Patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Apollos was converted to Christianity at Ephesus.
text: Apollos, a later assistant of Paul, is converted to Christianity in Ephesus.

summary: Corbulo inspected Legio X Fretensis at Cyrrhus in Syria and found the soldiers demoralized by long peace.
text: Corbulo inspects a base of Legio X Fretensis in Syria, at Cyrrhus; the Roman legionaries are demoralized by a "long peace". Many soldiers sell their helmets and shields.

summary: Corbulo recruited Syrian auxiliary units and stationed them along the frontier under orders to avoid provoking Parthia.
text: Corbulo recruits Syrian auxiliary units in the region and stations them in border forts, with orders from Nero not to provoke the Parthians.

summary: Marcus Julius Agrippa gradually received territories in Palestine between 48 and 54.
text: Palestine is returned piecemeal to Herod Agrippa's son Marcus Julius Agrippa between 48 and 54.

summary: Roman procurator Antonius Felix attacked Jewish rioters in Caesarea during violent clashes over civic status.
text: Violence erupts in Caesarea regarding a local ordinance restricting the civil rights of Jews, creating clashes between Jews and pagans. The Roman garrison, made up of Syrians, takes the side of the pagans. The Jews, armed with clubs and swords, meet in the marketplace. The governor of Judea, Antonius Felix, orders his troops to charge. The violence continues and Felix asks Nero to arbitrate. Nero sides with the pagans, and relegates the Jews to second-class citizens.

summary: Rome annexed the port of Aden under Nero to secure maritime trade routes.
text: Under Nero, Rome annexes Aden to protect the maritime route between Alexandria and Asia.

summary: Caesius Nasica led a Roman legion in defeating the rebel Venutius in support of Queen Cartimandua.
text: In Britain, Venutius leads a revolt against his ex-wife Cartimandua, queen of the Brigantes and a Roman ally. Governor Aulus Didius Gallus sends her military aid, and after some indecisive fighting a legion commanded by Caesius Nasica defeats the rebels (approximate date – some time between 52 and 57).

summary: Two Roman centurions explored south of Egypt toward the source of the Nile and reported the region unworthy of conquest.
text: Two centurions are sent to the south of Egypt to find the source of the Nile, and possible new provinces. They report that while there are many cities in the desert, the area seems too poor to be worthy of conquest.

summary: Roman emperor Claudius died in Rome, allegedly poisoned by Agrippina.
text: Claudius, Roman emperor, possibly poisoned by his wife Agrippina (b. 10 BC)

summary: Domitia Lepida the Younger, mother of Empress Valeria Messalina, died in Rome.
text: Domitia Lepida the Younger, widow of Marcus Valerius Messalla Barbatus, mother of Valeria Messalina and former mother-in-law of Claudius (b. 10 BC)

summary: Gaius Stertinius Xenophon, court physician to Emperor Claudius, died.
text: Gaius Stertinius Xenophon, Greek physician, possibly poisoned Claudius

summary: Marcus Junius Silanus, proconsul of Asia, died after being poisoned on the orders of Agrippina the Younger.
text: Marcus Junius Silanus, Roman consul (b. AD 14)

summary: Stachys the Apostle, bishop of Byzantium, died.
text: Stachys the Apostle, Byzantine bishop and saint

summary: Emperor Nero assumed the office of Roman consul.
text: Emperor Nero becomes a Roman Consul.

summary: The Roman jurist Masurius Sabinus wrote three treatises on the rights of Roman citizens.
text: The Roman jurist Sabinus writes three books on the rights of citizens.

summary: Paul the Apostle wrote his First Epistle to the Corinthians while residing in Ephesus.
text: The apostle Paul writes his First Epistle to the Corinthians.

summary: The Stoic philosopher Epictetus was born into slavery at Hierapolis.
text: Epictetus, Greek-Roman philosopher (d. 135)

summary: Britannicus, the son of the late emperor Claudius, died after being poisoned.
text: Britannicus, son of Claudius (b. AD 41)

summary: Antonia Tryphaena, queen of Thrace and client ruler of Rome, died.
text: Antonia Tryphaena, Roman client queen (b. 10 BC)

summary: King Izates II of Adiabene died.
text: Izates bar Monobaz, Parthian client king (b. c. AD 1)

summary: War broke out between Rome and Parthia after King Vologases I invaded Armenia and installed his brother Tiridates I on the throne.
text: War between Rome and Parthia breaks out due to the invasion of Armenia by King Vologases I, who has replaced the Roman-supported ruler with his brother Tiridates I of Armenia.

summary: Publius Clodius Thrasea Paetus became a suffect consul in Rome.
text: Publius Clodius Thrasea Paetus becomes a consul in Rome.

summary: Paul the Apostle wrote his Second Epistle to the Corinthians from Philippi.
text: The apostle Paul writes his second Epistle to the Corinthians, probably from Philippi.

summary: Paul the Apostle composed his Epistle to the Romans while staying in Corinth.
text: The apostle Paul writes his Epistle to the Romans, from Corinth .

summary: The Roman historian Tacitus was born.
text: Gaius Cornelius Tacitus, Roman historian.

summary: Roman politician and urban prefect Lucius Volusius Saturninus died.
text: Lucius Volusius Saturninus, Roman politician and governor

summary: Envoys from Cilicia arrived in Rome and successfully accused their former governor Cossutianus Capito of extortion before the Senate.
text: Envoys from Cilicia come to Rome to accuse their late governor, Cossutianus Capito, of extortion; the Roman Senate is supported in the case by Publius Clodius Thrasea Paetus.

summary: Emperor Nero entered his second consulship at Rome.
text: Emperor Nero becomes a Roman consul again.

object: Second Epistle to the Corinthians and Epistle to the Romans
summary: Paul the Apostle probably composed his Second Epistle to the Corinthians and his Epistle to the Romans.
text: Paul of Tarsus writes his Second Epistle to the Corinthians and his Epistle to the Romans (probable date).
names: Second Epistle to the Corinthians and Epistle to the Romans

summary: Quintus Veranius replaced Aulus Didius Gallus as governor of Britain and began a military campaign against the Silures in south Wales.
text: Quintus Veranius Nepos becomes governor in place of Aulus Didius Gallus. He begins a campaign against the Silures of south Wales.

summary: Roman general and governor of Britain Quintus Veranius died while on campaign.
text: Quintus Veranius, Roman consul and general

summary: Emperor Nero and Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus entered office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Nero and Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus become Roman consuls.

summary: Nero sent Otho to govern Lusitania after the two fell out over Poppaea Sabina.
text: The friendship between Nero and Marcus Salvius Otho ends when they both fall in love with Poppea Sabina, and Otho is sent to Lusitania as governor.

summary: Nero expelled his mother Agrippina the Younger from the imperial palace and banished her to a villa in Misenum.
text: Agrippina the Younger is expelled from the imperial palace by her son Nero, who installs her in Villa Antonia in Misenum, and leaving more of the effective and real power of Empire in the hands of Nero.

summary: The sacred fig tree Ficus Ruminalis in the Roman Forum began to wither and die.
text: The Ficus Ruminalis begins to die (see Rumina).

summary: Agrippina the Younger conspired with Roman senators to overthrow Emperor Nero.
text: Agrippina the Younger, conspired with the senators in late 58 to overthrow Nero.

summary: Paul the Apostle was arrested in Jerusalem, imprisoned at Caesarea, and appealed to Caesar to be tried in Rome.
text: The apostle Paul returns to Jerusalem with the money he has collected to give the Christian community there. However, he is accused of defiling the temple, and is arrested and imprisoned in Caesarea. He then invokes his Roman citizenship and is sent to Rome to be judged.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo launched an invasion of Armenia and captured the fortress of Volandum.
text: Roman-Parthian War: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo, commander in the East, launches his Armenian offensive against Parthia. He leads a Roman army (four legions) through the mountainous country of Armenia, against the fortress at Volandum, to the southwest of Artaxata. After a siege of eight hours Corbulo takes the city; the legionnaires massacre the defenders and plunder Volandum to their hearts' content.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo captured the Armenian capital of Artaxata and burned it to the ground.
text: Corbulo marches to Artaxata crossing the Aras River; along the valley he is shadowed by tens of thousands of mounted Parthian archers led by king Tiridates I. The city opens its gates to Corbulo, just as it had to Germanicus four decades before. When he takes the 250-year-old Armenian capital, Corbulo gives the residents a few hours to collect their valuables and burns the city to the ground.

summary: Gnaeus Julius Agricola served as a military tribune in Britain attached to Legio II Augusta.
text: Gnaeus Julius Agricola, 18 years old, is serving as a military tribune in Britain under Gaius Suetonius Paulinus and is attached to Legio II Augusta.

summary: Romans adopted the manufacture and use of soap from the Gauls.
text: Romans learn the use of soap from the Gauls .

summary: The Roman poet Juvenal was born.
text: Juvenal, Roman poet and writer

summary: Pharasmanes I, king of Iberia, died.
text: Pharasmanes I, Roman client king of Iberia

summary: Rhadamistus, former king of Armenia, was executed.
text: Rhadamistus, Roman client king of Armenia

summary: Emperor Nero had his mother Agrippina the Younger murdered at Baiae after a planned shipwreck failed.
text: Emperor Nero orders the murder of his mother Agrippina the Younger. He tries to kill her through a planned shipwreck, but when she survives, he has her executed and frames it as a suicide.

summary: Publius Clodius Thrasea Paetus retired from the Roman Senate in protest over the murder of Agrippina.
text: Publius Clodius Thrasea Paetus retires from the Roman Senate. He openly shows his disgust at the behaviour of Nero regarding the murder of Agrippina.

summary: Violent rioting broke out between the residents of Pompeii and Nuceria during a gladiatorial show in Pompeii.
text: Rioting breaks out between the people of Pompeii and the people of Nuceria during a gladiator fight in Pompeii. Thousands are killed.

summary: Petronius satirized Roman immorality in his work Satyricon.
text: In the Satyricon, Petronius pokes fun at Roman immorality.

summary: Paul the Apostle defended his faith and testified before King Agrippa II at Caesarea.
text: Paul the Apostle pleads his case and testifies to his Christianity before King Agrippa II of the Herodians, who reportedly responds "You almost persuade me to be a Christian."

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo captured Tigranocerta and installed Tigranes VI as client king of Armenia.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo, Roman commander in the east, captures Tigranocerta in Mesopotamia. He installs Tigranes VI, a Cappadocian prince, as ruler of Armenia. For the next four years, a cohort from Legio VI Ferrata and Legio X Fretensis is stationed in the capital as bodyguard to the king, supported by fifteen hundred auxiliaries.

text: An eclipse on 30 April over North Africa is recorded by Pliny the Elder in his Natural History.

names: List of solar eclipses in antiquity

text: Agrippina the Younger, mother of Nero (b. AD 15)

text: Domitia Lepida the Elder, granddaughter of Mark Antony

text: Gnaeus Domitius Afer, Roman politician and orator

text: Servilius Nonianus, Roman consul and historian

summary: Roman forces defeated the Roxolani along the Danube.
text: The Roxolani are defeated on the Danube by the Romans.

summary: Emperor Nero sent a Roman expedition up the Nile that reached Meroë.
text: Nero's exploration of the Nile: Emperor Nero sends an expedition which reaches the historical city Meroë (Sudan).

text: Vitellius is (possibly) proconsul of the province of Africa.

summary: Herod Agrippa II ruled northeastern Judea.
text: Agrippa II of the Herodians rules the northeast of Judea.

summary: An earthquake destroyed the city of Laodicea on the Lycus.
text: The city of Laodicea on the Lycus is destroyed by an earthquake

summary: Major events and revolts unfolded in Roman Britain around this time.
text: The following events in Roman Britain (Britannia) take place in AD 60 or 61:

summary: Roman governor Gaius Suetonius Paulinus captured the island of Mona, destroying the Druid stronghold.
text: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus, Roman governor of Britain, captures the island of Mona (Anglesey), the last stronghold of the Druids.

summary: Following the death of King Prasutagus, the Roman army annexed the Iceni kingdom and mistreated his family.
text: Prasutagus, king of the Iceni (modern East Anglia), dies leaving a will which passes his kingdom to his two daughters and the Roman Empire. The Roman army, however, annexes the kingdom as if conquered, depriving the nobles of their hereditary lands and plundering the land. The king's widow, Boudica, is flogged and forced to watch their daughters publicly raped. Roman financiers, including Seneca the Younger, call in their loans.

summary: Boudica led an anti-Roman revolt, sacking Camulodunum, Londinium, and Verulamium.
text: Boudica leads a rebellion of the Iceni against Roman rule in alliance with the Trinovantes, Cornovii, Durotriges and Celtic Britons. The Iceni and Trinovantes first destroy the Roman capital Camulodunum (Colchester), wipe out the infantry of the Legio IX Hispana (commanded by Quintus Petillius Cerialis) and go on to burn Londinium (London) (probably destroying London Bridge) and Verulamium (St Albans), in all cases massacring the inhabitants by the thousands.

summary: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus defeated Boudica's rebel army at the Battle of Watling Street.
text: Battle of Watling Street: Paulinus defeats the rebels, using a flying wedge formation, imposes wide-ranging punishments on native Britons, and the Romanization of Britain continues. Boudica either poisons herself, or falls sick and dies.

summary: The First Epistle of Peter was written.
text: The First Epistle of Peter, if by Peter, is probably written between this year and c. AD 64.

summary: Paul the Apostle was shipwrecked on Malta on his journey to Rome and converted Publius.
text: Paul of Tarsus journeys to Rome, but is shipwrecked on Malta. He stays for three months and converts Publius, the first bishop of Malta.

summary: Paul the Apostle wrote the Epistle to the Philippians from Rome.
text: Paul's Epistle to the Philippians is written from Rome.

summary: Hero of Alexandria wrote several treatises on mathematics and mechanics.
text: Hero of Alexandria writes Metrica, Mechanics, and Pneumatics.

summary: The House of the Vettii in Pompeii began to be rebuilt.
text: AD 60–79 – House of the Vettii, Pompeii, is rebuilt.

text: Marcus Vitorius Marcellus, Roman politician

summary: Greek mathematician Nicomachus was born.
text: Nicomachus, Greek mathematician

summary: Abdagases I, ruler in the Parthian realm, died.
text: Abdagases I, king of the Parthian Empire

text: Boudica, British queen of the Iceni tribe

summary: Peter of Rates, bishop of Braga, died.
text: Peter of Rates, first bishop of Braga

summary: Publius Petronius Turpilianus and Lucius Caesennius Paetus became Roman consuls.
text: Publius Petronius Turpilianus and Lucius Caesennius Paetus become Roman consuls.

summary: Galba became the governor of Hispania Tarraconensis.
text: Galba becomes governor of Hispania Tarraconensis.

summary: Roman Britain experienced several major events around this time.
text: The following events in Roman Britain (Britannia) take place in AD 60 or 61:

summary: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus captured the island of Mona, destroying the stronghold of the Druids.
text: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus, Roman governor of Britain, captures the island of Mona (Anglesey), the last stronghold of the Druids.

summary: Following the death of King Prasutagus, the Roman army annexed the kingdom of the Iceni and mistreated his family.
text: Prasutagus, king of the Iceni (modern East Anglia), dies leaving a will which passes his kingdom to his two daughters and the Roman Empire. The Roman army however annexes the kingdom as if conquered, depriving the nobles of their hereditary lands and plundering the land. The king's widow, Boudica, is flogged and forced to watch their daughters publicly raped. Roman financiers, including Seneca the Younger, call in their loans.

summary: Boudica led an anti-Roman rebellion of Britons, sacking Camulodunum, Londinium, and Verulamium.
text: Boudica leads a rebellion of the Iceni against Roman rule in alliance with the Trinovantes, Cornovii, Durotriges and Celtic Britons. The Iceni and Trinovantes first destroy the Roman capital Camulodunum (Colchester), wipe out the infantry of the Legio IX Hispana (commanded by Quintus Petillius Cerialis) and go on to burn Londinium (London) (probably destroying London Bridge) and Verulamium (St Albans), in all cases massacring the inhabitants in their thousands.

summary: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus defeated the British rebel forces at the Battle of Watling Street.
text: Battle of Watling Street: Paulinus defeats the rebels, using a flying wedge formation, and imposes wide-ranging punishments on native Britons, but is removed from office after an enquiry instituted by Gaius Julius Alpinus Classicianus (appointed procurator 61) and the Romanisation of Britain continues. Boudica either poisons herself or falls sick and dies.

summary: Roman author and statesman Pliny the Younger was born.
text: Pliny the Younger, Roman author and statesman (d. c. 113)

summary: Cypriot Jew and early Christian missionary Barnabas died.
text: Barnabas, Cypriot Jew and bishop of Milan

summary: Queen of the Iceni Boudica died.
text: Boudica, British queen of the Iceni tribe

summary: Roman politician and prefect Lucius Pedanius Secundus died.
text: Lucius Pedanius Secundus, Roman politician and prefect

summary: Roman politician Publius Memmius Regulus died.
text: Publius Memmius Regulus, Roman politician

summary: Roman Emperor Nero married Poppaea Sabina.
text: Emperor Nero marries for the second time, to Poppaea Sabina, ex-wife of Marcus Salvius Otho.

summary: Ofonius Tigellinus became Nero's counselor following the death of Burrus and Seneca's withdrawal.
text: After the death of Burrus and the disgrace of Seneca, Nero is free from their influence and becomes a megalomaniacal artist fascinated by Hellenism and the Orient. Tigellinus becomes Nero's counselor. His rule is highly abusive.

summary: Nero completed the construction of the Baths of Nero in Rome.
text: Nero completes the Baths of Nero in Rome.

summary: A major earthquake struck Campania, causing severe destruction in Pompeii.
text: A great earthquake damages cities in Campania, including Pompeii (February 5).

summary: Vologases I of Parthia invaded Armenia and unsuccessfully besieged Tigranocerta before preparing to move against Syria.
text: The Parthians invade Armenia and lay siege to Tigranocerta. The city is well-fortified and garrisoned by the Romans. The assault fails and king Vologases I retreats. Instead, he makes preparations to invade Syria.

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo reinforced the Euphrates frontier with fortifications, a flotilla, and a bridge.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo strengthens the fortifications on the Euphrates frontier. He builds a strong flotilla of ships equipped with catapults and a wooden bridge across the river, which allows him to establish a foothold on the Parthian shore.

summary: Lucius Caesennius Paetus marched toward Tigranocerta and made winter camp at Rhandeia.
text: Lucius Caesennius Paetus advances towards Tigranocerta, but due to lack of supplies he makes camp for the winter in the fortress at Rhandeia in northwestern Armenia.

summary: Vologases I attacked the Euphrates frontier, where Roman legions repulsed his assault.
text: Vologases I leads the Parthian army in a full-scale assault on the Euphrates. Legio X Fretensis and men of the other two legions (Legio III Gallica and Legio VI Ferrata) defend the eastern bank of the river, fighting off a desperate attack.

summary: Parthian forces under Tiridates I defeated a Roman army at the Battle of Rhandeia, forcing Paetus to surrender.
text: Battle of Rhandeia: The Roman army (two legions) is defeated by the Parthians under king Tiridates I. Paetus surrenders and withdraws his disheveled army to Syria.

summary: A violent storm destroyed two hundred Roman ships anchored at Portus.
text: A violent storm destroys 200 ships anchored at Portus.

summary: Lucan began writing an epic poem about the civil war between Julius Caesar and Pompey.
text: Lucan writes a history of the conflict between Julius Caesar and Pompey.

summary: The creation of a still life wall painting began in Herculaneum.
text: The making of Still Life, a detail of a wall painting from Herculaneum, begins (finished in AD 79). It is now kept at Museo Nazionale in Naples.

summary: Paul the Apostle was released from imprisonment in Rome.
text: Paul of Tarsus is released from imprisonment in Rome .

summary: Claudia Octavia, the former wife of Emperor Nero, was executed.
text: Claudia Octavia, wife of Nero (possibly executed) (b. AD 40)

summary: Roman satirist and poet Persius died.
text: Aulus Persius Flaccus, Roman poet (b. AD 34)

summary: Roman politician and former consul Faustus Cornelius Sulla Felix was murdered.
text: Faustus Cornelius Sulla Felix, Roman consul (murdered) (b. AD 22)

summary: Nero's cousin Rubellius Plautus was executed.
text: Gaius Rubellius Plautus, cousin of Nero (executed) (b. AD 33)

summary: James the Just, leader of the Jerusalem church, was martyred.
text: James the Just, brother of Jesus (martyred)

summary: Roman banker Lucius Caecilius Iucundus died in Pompeii.
text: Lucius Caecilius Iucundus, Roman banker from Pompeii (b. c. AD 14)

summary: Sextus Afranius Burrus, praetorian prefect and advisor to Nero, died.
text: Sextus Afranius Burrus, Roman prefect and friend of Seneca (b. AD 1)

summary: Vespasian was appointed proconsular governor of Africa.
text: Vespasian becomes governor of Africa (estimated year).

summary: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo invaded Armenia and forced Tiridates I to accept Roman suzerainty, ending the war with Parthia.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo is restored to command after the Roman debacle at the Battle of Rhandeia. He invades Armenia and defeats Tiridates I, who accepts Roman sovereignty. Parthia withdraws from the war.

summary: Pompeii began building a new monumental forum after the earthquake damage.
text: Pompeii, the city at the foot of Mount Vesuvius, builds a new monumental forum, after the town is heavily damaged by a strong earthquake.

summary: According to legend, Joseph of Arimathea traveled to Glastonbury on a Christian mission.
text: According to legend, Joseph of Arimathea goes to Glastonbury on the first Christian mission to Britain.

summary: Paul the Apostle may have visited Spain.
text: Apostle Paul possibly visits Spain.

summary: Aulus Cornelius Celsus compiled an encyclopedic work on the arts and sciences.
text: Aulus Cornelius Celsus writes a dictionary (encyclopedia) on the arts and sciences.

summary: Claudia Augusta, the infant daughter of Emperor Nero, died.
text: Claudia Augusta, daughter of Nero

summary: The Great Fire of Rome broke out, destroying three regions of the city and causing severe damage to several others.
text: 27 – Great Fire of Rome: A fire begins which destroyed three of fourteen of the administrative regions of Rome, more commonly known as the Palatine Hill, the Circus Maximus, and the Oppian hill. Also suffering severe damage were the Campus Martius and the Via Lata.

summary: Emperor Nero initiated the persecution of Christians in Rome following the Great Fire.
text: Persecution of Christians in Rome begins under Nero. Peter the Apostle is possibly among those crucified.
names: Persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire

summary: Nero proposed a new urban planning program featuring wide streets, porticos, and open spaces to rebuild Rome.
text: Nero proposes a new urban planning program based on the creation of buildings decorated with ornate porticos, the widening of the streets and the use of open spaces. This plan will not be applied until after his death in AD 68.

summary: Lyon sent money to Rome for post-fire reconstruction, and Nero later sent aid when Lyon itself suffered a catastrophic fire.
text: Lyon sends a large sum of money to Rome to aid in the reconstruction. However, during the winter of AD 64–65, Lyon suffers a catastrophic fire itself, and Nero reciprocates by sending money to Lyon.

summary: Seneca proclaimed the equality of all men, including enslaved people.
text: Seneca proclaims the equality of all men, including slaves.

summary: Julia Flavia, daughter of Titus, was born.
text: Julia Flavia, daughter of Titus and lover of his brother Domitian (d. AD 96)

summary: Julia Agricola, daughter of Gnaeus Julius Agricola, was born.
text: Julia Agricola, daughter of Gnaeus Julius Agricola

summary: Phoenician historian Philo of Byblos was born.
text: Philo of Byblos, Phoenician historian and writer (d. 141)

summary: Saint Peter was crucified in Rome during Nero's persecution.
text: Peter the Apostle (Margherita Guarducci, who led the research leading to the rediscovery of Peter's reputed tomb in 1963, concluded that Peter died on that date, shortly after the Great Fire of Rome and during the festivities to mark "dies imperii" of Emperor Nero, and that Peter and other Christians were crucified in honor of the decennial of Nero's October 13, AD 54 ascension to the imperial throne.) (b. 1 BC)

summary: Roman consul Decimus Junius Silanus Torquatus died.
text: Decimus Junius Silanus Torquatus, Roman consul (b. AD 16)

summary: Paul the Apostle died in Rome under Nero according to the earliest dating.
text: Paul the Apostle (earliest date) (b. AD 5)

summary: Nero began construction of his extravagant palace complex, the Domus Aurea, in Rome.
text: Nero began construction of his large and extravagant villa the Domus Aurea.

summary: The freedman Milichus betrayed the Pisonian conspiracy against Nero, leading to the arrest of Gaius Calpurnius Piso and the other conspirators.
text: The freedman Milichus betrays the Pisonian conspiracy led by Gaius Calpurnius Piso to kill Emperor Nero and all the conspirators are arrested.

summary: An epidemic afflicted the city of Rome.
text: An epidemic afflicts Rome.

summary: Nero launched reprisals against senators and critics after facing disapproval for his stage performances.
text: After a stage performance in which he appears and shocks the senatorial class considerably, Nero engages in a series of reprisals against Seneca the Younger and Tigellinus, pro-republican senators, and anyone else he distrusts.

summary: Nero's pregnant wife Poppaea Sabina died after being kicked by Nero or from pregnancy complications.
text: Nero's pregnant wife, Poppea Sabina, dies from Nero kicking her stomach or while having a miscarriage.

summary: Paul ordained Timothy as bishop of Ephesus.
text: Paul of Tarsus ordains Timothy as bishop of Ephesus (traditional date).

summary: Paul wrote his first epistle to Timothy from Corinth before traveling to Nicopolis for the winter.
text: Paul writes his first epistle to Timothy in Corinth; afterwards, he goes to Nikopoli to spend the winter.

summary: Mark the Evangelist founded the first Christian community in Africa at Alexandria.
text: The first Christian community in Africa is founded by Mark, a disciple of Peter.

summary: Philopappos, a prince of the Kingdom of Commagene, was born.
text: Philopappos, Greek prince of Commagene (d. AD 116)

summary: Greek aristocrat Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes was born.
text: Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes, Greek aristocrat

summary: Roman poet Lucan died by suicide after being implicated in the Pisonian conspiracy.
text: Lucan, Roman poet and philosopher (b. AD 39)

summary: Praetorian prefect Faenius Rufus was executed for his role in the Pisonian conspiracy.
text: Faenius Rufus, Roman praetorian prefect (executed)

summary: Gaius Calpurnius Piso died by suicide after his conspiracy against Nero was discovered.
text: Gaius Calpurnius Piso, Roman consul

text: Gaius Julius Alpinus Classicianus, Roman procurator

text: Lucius Antistius Vetus, Roman consul and governor

summary: Roman politician Lucius Junius Gallio Annaeanus was forced to commit suicide following the Pisonian conspiracy.
text: Lucius Junius Gallio Annaeanus, Roman politician

summary: Roman consul Marcus Julius Vestinus Atticus was forced to commit suicide by Nero.
text: Marcus Julius Vestinus Atticus, Roman politician

summary: Roman politician Marcus Ostorius Scapula committed suicide after being falsely accused of treason.
text: Marcus Ostorius Scapula, Roman politician

summary: Roman politician Plautius Lateranus was executed for participating in the Pisonian conspiracy.
text: Plautius Lateranus, Roman politician (executed)

summary: Roman Empress Poppaea Sabina died.
text: Poppea Sabina, second wife of Nero (b. AD 30)

summary: Roman statesman and philosopher Seneca the Younger was forced to commit suicide by Nero.
text: Seneca, Roman statesman and tutor of Nero (b. AD 1)

summary: Simon the Zealot died as a Christian martyr.
text: Simon the Zealot, Christian martyr

summary: Emperor Nero raised Legio I Italica and appointed Vespasian commander and governor of Judea.
text: Emperor Nero creates the Legio I Italica. He appoints Titus Flavius Vespasian as General of the army of Judea, and Governor of Judea which gives him command of three legions — V Macedonica, X Fretensis and XV Apollinaris.

summary: Jewish rebels launched the First Jewish-Roman War, besieged Jerusalem, and seized Masada.
text: October – The Jewish Revolt commences against the Roman Empire. The Zealots lay siege to Jerusalem and annihilate the Roman garrison (a cohort of Legio III Cyrenaica). The Sicarii capture the fortress of Masada overlooking the Dead Sea.

summary: Gaius Cestius Gallus marched an army of 30,000 men into Judea to suppress the Jewish revolt.
text: Mid–late October – Cestius Gallus, legate of Syria, marches into Judea and leads a Roman army of 30,000 men to put down the Jewish rebellion. At its core is Legio XII Fulminata, plus 2,000 selected men from the other three Syrian legions, six more cohorts of infantry and four alae of cavalry, plus over 14,000 auxiliaries furnished by Rome's eastern allies, including Herod Agrippa II and two other client kings, Antiochus IV of Commagene and Sohaemus of Emesa, who lead their forces (largely archers and cavalry) in person.

summary: Gaius Cestius Gallus advanced down the Judean coast and captured the Bezetha suburb of Jerusalem.
text: Gallus leads his main force down the coast from Caesarea via Antipatris to Lydda, detaching other units, by land and sea, to neutralize the rebel strongholds at Joppa, Narbata and the Tower of Aphek. With Galilee and the entire Judean coast in his hands, Gallus assumes his campaign before the winter rains render the roads impassable. He turns inland and marches on Jerusalem, taking the road via the plain at Emmaus. Gallus succeeds in conquering Beit She'arim (the "New City") on the Bezetha Hill.

summary: Judean rebels ambushed and routed Gaius Cestius Gallus's Roman army at the Battle of Beth-Horon.
text: November – Battle of Beth-Horon: Gallus abandons the siege of Jerusalem and chooses, for uncertain reasons, to withdraw west to winter quarters, where he is ambushed and defeated by Judean rebels. Some 5,300 Roman troops are killed, as well as all their pack animals, their artillery (which is to serve the Jews of Jerusalem during Titus's siege operations four years later), and the greatest disgrace of all, the eagle standard of Legio XII Fulminata. Gallus abandons his troops in disarray, fleeing to Syria.

summary: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus became a Roman consul.
text: Suetonius Paullinus, governor of Britannia, becomes a Roman Consul.

summary: Legio II Augusta was stationed at Gloucester.
text: The Roman Legio II Augusta is stationed at Gloucester.

summary: Dioscorides completed De Materia Medica, a comprehensive pharmacopoeia on medicinal treatments.
text: Dioscorides writes his De Materia Medica, a treatise on the methodical treatment of disease by use of medicine .

summary: The First and Second Epistles to Timothy were traditionally composed.
text: The first and second Epistles to Timothy are written (speculative date, if actually written by St. Paul).

summary: Paul visited Asia Minor and Greece before undergoing his second imprisonment in Rome.
text: Paul in Asia Minor for second time after his release from Rome. Then probably goes to Greece. Second imprisonment in Rome.

summary: Claudia Antonia, daughter of Emperor Claudius, was executed on Nero's orders.
text: Claudia Antonia, daughter of Claudius (b. AD 30)

summary: Roman suffect consul Gaius Anicius Cerialis died.
text: Gaius Anicius Cerialis, Roman suffect consul

summary: Roman courtier and author Petronius died by suicide.
text: Gaius Petronius Arbiter, Roman politician (b. AD 27)

summary: Roman senator Lucius Annius Vinicianus died by suicide after being condemned by Nero.
text: Lucius Annius Vinicianus, Roman politician (b. AD 36)

summary: Roman noblewoman Marcia Servilia Sorana was executed.
text: Marcia Servilia Sorana, Roman noblewoman

summary: Former praetorian prefect Rufrius Crispinus committed suicide in exile.
text: Rufrius Crispinus, Roman praetorian prefect

summary: Gaius Julius Vindex launched a revolt against Nero in Gaul.
text: Gaius Julius Vindex revolts, first in a series of revolts that lead to Nero's downfall.

summary: Gaius Licinius Mucianus succeeded Gaius Cestius Gallus as governor of Syria.
text: Gaius Licinius Mucianus replaces Gaius Cestius Gallus as governor of Syria.

summary: Vespasian arrived at Ptolemais with two legions to quell the Jewish revolt.
text: First Jewish–Roman War: Vespasian arrives in Ptolemais in Phoenicia along with the Legio X Fretensis and Legio V Macedonica, to put down the revolt.

summary: Titus brought Legio XV Apollinaris from Alexandria to reinforce Vespasian in Judea.
text: Vespasian is joined by his son Titus, who brings Legio XV Apollinaris from Alexandria. By late spring the Roman army numbers more than 60,000 soldiers, including auxilia and troops of King Herod Agrippa II.

summary: Factions in Jerusalem fought a brutal civil war as Zealots and Sicarii executed fleeing citizens.
text: Jewish leaders at Jerusalem are divided through a power struggle, and a brutal civil war erupts. The Zealots and the Sicarii execute anyone who tries to leave the city.

summary: Roman troops led by Vespasian captured Yodfat, massacring thousands and capturing Josephus.
text: Siege of Yodfat: Its 40,000 Jewish inhabitants are massacred. The historian Josephus, leader of the rebels in Galilee, is captured by the Romans. Vespasian is wounded in the foot by an arrow fired from the city wall.

summary: Roman forces captured the fortress of Gamla and massacred its defenders and inhabitants.
text: The Jewish fortress of Gamla in the Golan falls to the Romans, and its inhabitants are massacred.

summary: Nero toured Greece to compete in the Olympic Games and other Panhellenic festivals.
text: Nero travels to Greece, where he participates in the Olympic Games and other festivals.

summary: Nero ordered general Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo to commit suicide.
text: Nero, jealous of the success of Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo in Armenia, orders that he be put to death. Corbulo literally "falls on his sword".

summary: The Apostles Peter and Paul were traditionally martyred in Rome.
text: Apostles Peter and Paul are martyred in Rome (possible date).

summary: Linus succeeded Peter as Bishop of Rome.
text: Linus succeeds Peter, as the second Bishop of Rome.

summary: Roman jurist and consul Publius Juventius Celsus was born.
text: Publius Juventius Celsus, Roman consul (d. 130)

summary: Roman senator Publius Anteius Rufus committed suicide after being accused of conspiracy.
text: Publius Anteius Rufus, Roman politician

summary: Gaius Cestius Gallus, former governor of Syria, died.
text: Cestius Gallus, Roman politician and governor

summary: Roman general Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo committed suicide on Nero's orders.
text: Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo, Roman general (b. c. AD 7)

summary: Roman actor Lucius Domitius Paris was executed on Nero's orders.
text: Lucius Domitius Paris, Roman freedman and actor

summary: Paul the Apostle was martyred in Rome.
text: Paul the Apostle, Christian martyr (b. c. AD 5)

summary: Christian martyr Paulinus of Antioch died.
text: Paulinus of Antioch, Roman bishop and martyr

summary: Roman senator Publius Sulpicius Scribonius Proculus committed suicide on Nero's orders.
text: Publius Sulpicius Scribonius, Roman politician

summary: Tacitus's narrative in the Annals ended with the events of this year.
text: Final year that Tacitus records Annals, a written history of the Roman Empire.

summary: Lucius Clodius Macer revolted against the reign of Emperor Nero.
text: Lucius Clodius Macer revolts against the reign of Nero.

summary: The Roman Senate declared Nero persona non grata and an enemy of the state.
text: The Senate declares Nero as persona non grata.

summary: The Roman Senate accepted Servius Sulpicius Galba as Roman emperor.
text: The Roman Senate accepts Servius Sulpicius Galba, as Roman Emperor.

object: Legio I Macriana liberatrix and Legio I Adiutrix
summary: Legio I Macriana liberatrix and Legio I Adiutrix were created.
text: Legio I Macriana liberatrix and Legio I Adiutrix are created.
names: Legio I Macriana liberatrix and Legio I Adiutrix

summary: Marcus Ulpius Trajanus, father of Trajan, became consul.
text: Marcus Ulpius Trajanus, father of Trajan, becomes consul.

summary: Trajan crossed the Jordan River with Legio X Fretensis, besieged Jericho, and destroyed the monastery at Qumran.
text: Trajan moves to Scythopolis and crosses the Jordan River with Legio X Fretensis. He lays siege to Jericho and destroys the monastery of Qumran, where the Dead Sea Scrolls are originated.

summary: Titus set up camp at Jericho and cut off escape routes toward Jerusalem.
text: Winter – Titus sets up camp at Jericho and the Romans cut off escape routes toward Jerusalem.

summary: Venutius deposed his wife Cartimandua and became the ruler of the Brigantes.
text: Venutius successfully deposes his wife Cartimandua and becomes the ruler of the Brigantes.

summary: Apostles Peter and Paul were martyred in Rome.
text: Apostles Peter and Paul are martyred in Rome (latest possible date).

summary: Ignatius of Antioch became the third bishop of Antioch.
text: Ignatius of Antioch becomes the third bishop of Antioch.

summary: The Essenes placed the Dead Sea Scrolls in the caves at Qumran.
text: The Essenes place the Dead Sea Scrolls in the caves at Qumran.

summary: Salonia Matidia, niece of future emperor Trajan, was born.
text: Salonia Matidia, niece of Trajan (d. AD 119)
