summary: Nero ordered his secretary Epaphroditus to assist in his suicide after being condemned by the Senate.
text: Nero, then in hiding in the villa of the freedman Phaon, was notified that the Senate had declared him an enemy of the state and ordered him brought to the Forum to be publicly beaten to death. He ordered his secretary Epaphroditus to kill him.

summary: Forces of Ananus ben Ananus besieged the Zealots in the Second Temple.
text: Zealot Temple Siege: The forces of Ananus ben Ananus, the Jewish former High Priest of Israel, laid siege to the Zealots in the Second Temple.

summary: The Year of the Four Emperors saw Galba, Otho, Vitellius, and Vespasian succeed each other as Roman emperor.
text: The Year of the Four Emperors: After Nero's death, Galba, Otho, Vitellius and Vespasian succeed each other as emperor during the year. The year is marked by numerous instances of a breakdown in discipline and mutinous conduct amongst the Roman legions and the praetorian guard.

summary: The legions of Germania Superior refused loyalty to Galba and proclaimed Vitellius emperor.
text: The Roman legions in Germania Superior refuse to swear loyalty to Galba. They rebel and proclaim Vitellius as emperor.

summary: Galba adopted Lucius Calpurnius Piso Licinianus and appointed him deputy emperor.
text: Lucius Calpurnius Piso Licinianus is adopted by Galba and appointed to deputy Roman Emperor.

object: Galba and Lucius Calpurnius Piso Frugi Licinianus
summary: The Praetorian Guard murdered Galba and his adopted son Piso in the Roman Forum.
text: Galba and his adopted son Piso are murdered by the Praetorian Guard on the Roman Forum.
names: Galba and Lucius Calpurnius Piso Frugi Licinianus

summary: Otho seized power in Rome and proclaimed himself emperor before committing suicide three months later.
text: Otho seizes power in Rome, proclaims himself emperor, and reigns for three months before committing suicide.

summary: Legio XX Valeria Victrix mutinied at Chester, forcing Governor Marcus Trebellius Maximus to flee to Gaul.
text: Marcus Trebellius Maximus, governor of Britannia, is forced to flee to Gaul after a mutiny of Legio XX Valeria Victrix at Deva Victrix (Chester).

summary: Following the First Battle of Bedriacum, Vitellius became Roman emperor.
text: After the First Battle of Bedriacum, Vitellius becomes emperor.

summary: Marcus Vettius Bolanus became governor of Britain and faced an insurrection by Venutius of the Brigantes.
text: Marcus Vettius Bolanus becomes the new governor of Britain and faces a second insurrection of Venutius, king of the Brigantes.

summary: Legions in Egypt, Syria, and Judea declared Vespasian emperor.
text: two legions in Egypt, a legion in Syria, and a legion in Judea declare Vespasian emperor

summary: Tiberius Julius Alexander ordered his legions in Alexandria to swear allegiance to Vespasian as emperor.
text: Tiberius Julius Alexander orders his legions in Alexandria to swear allegiance to Vespasian as emperor.

summary: The Roman army in Judea swore allegiance to Vespasian as emperor.
text: The army of Judea swears allegiance to Vespasian as emperor.

summary: The Batavians in Germania Inferior revolted against Roman rule under the leadership of Gaius Julius Civilis.
text: Batavian rebellion: The Batavians in Germania Inferior (Netherlands) revolt under the leadership of Gaius Julius Civilis.

summary: German warbands crossed the Rhine to join the revolt and attacked the Roman fortress at Mainz.
text: German warbands cross over to join the revolt and attack the fortress at Mainz.

summary: The Batavians attacked Roman forts along the Rhine frontier, destroying Fectio and Traiectum.
text: The Batavians attack Roman forts on the Rhine frontier; Fectio and Traiectum (modern Utrecht) are destroyed.

summary: The second Tungrian auxiliary cohort revolted against Roman authority in Gallia Belgica.
text: In Gallia Belgica, cohors II Tungrorum, raised from the inhabitants of Atuatuca Tungrorum in the north-west of the Ardennes Forest, revolt against the Romans.

summary: The Danubian legions stationed in Raetia and Moesia proclaimed Vespasian as Roman emperor.
text: The Danubian legions of Raetia and Moesia proclaim Vespasian as emperor.

summary: Flavian forces under Marcus Antonius Primus defeated the Vitellian army at the Second Battle of Bedriacum.
text: Second Battle of Bedriacum: Flavians under Antonius Primus defeat the Vitellians.

summary: Vitellius was captured and killed at the Gemonian stairs in Rome, allowing Vespasian to become emperor.
text: Vitellius is captured and murdered by the Gemonian stairs. Vespasian becomes emperor.

summary: Vespasian laid siege to Jerusalem during the First Jewish-Roman War.
text: Judea: The Jewish Revolt – Vespasian lays siege to Jerusalem; the city is captured the following year by his son Titus.

summary: The Jewish rebel leader Josephus was brought before Vespasian, prophesied his rise to power, and became his historian.
text: Josephus, Jewish rebel leader, is dragged before Vespasian and becomes his historian (he "prophesied" him his elevation to the purple).

summary: The Roman legion Legio I Macriana liberatrix was disbanded.
text: Legio I Macriana liberatrix is disbanded.

summary: The Flavian dynasty began its rule over the Roman Empire with the accession of Vespasian.
text: The Flavian dynasty starts.

summary: The Roman historian Gaius Suetonius Tranquillus was born.
text: Gaius Suetonius Tranquillus, Roman historian

summary: Polycarp, the future bishop and Christian martyr of Smyrna, was born.
text: Polycarpus, bishop and martyr of Smyrna (d. AD 155)

summary: Praetorian prefect Cornelius Laco was murdered in Rome.
text: January 15: Cornelius Laco, Roman praetorian prefect (murdered)

summary: Sempronius Densus, centurion and imperial bodyguard, was killed defending the deputy emperor.
text: January 15: Sempronius Densus, Roman bodyguard (killed)

summary: Deputy emperor Lucius Calpurnius Piso Licinianus was murdered in Rome.
text: January 15: Lucius Calpurnius Piso Licinianus, Roman deputy emperor (b. AD 38)

summary: Roman emperor Galba was murdered in the Roman Forum by mutinous praetorians.
text: January 15: Servius Sulpicius Galba, Roman emperor (b. 3 BC)

summary: Roman emperor Otho died by suicide following defeat in the civil war.
text: Marcus Salvius Otho, Roman emperor (b. AD 32)

summary: Roman consul Titus Flavius Sabinus was murdered in Rome.
text: Titus Flavius Sabinus, Roman consul (murdered)

summary: Roman emperor Vitellius died after being lynched by Flavian supporters in Rome.
text: Aulus Vitellius Germanicus, Roman emperor (b. AD 15)

summary: Cartimandua, queen of the Brigantes, died.
text: Cartimandua, Queen of the Brigantes

summary: Former praetorian prefect Gaius Ofonius Tigellinus committed suicide after receiving an order to die.
text: Gaius Ofonius Tigellinus, Roman praetorian prefect (suicide)

summary: The Roman authorities executed Locusta, the poison expert employed under Nero.
text: Locusta, Roman female poison expert to Nero (executed)

summary: The politician Lucius Vitellius the Younger was executed following the defeat of his brother Vitellius.
text: Lucius Vitellius (the Younger), Roman politician (executed)

summary: Roman general Marcus Hordeonius Flaccus was murdered by his own troops during the Batavian revolt.
text: Marcus Hordeonius Flaccus, Roman politician (murdered)

summary: Sextilia, mother of the emperor Vitellius, died by suicide.
text: Sextilia, mother of Aulus Vitellius and Lucius Vitellius (suicide)

summary: Sporus, the freedman and companion of Nero, committed suicide.
text: Sporus, Roman freedman and male lover of Nero (suicide)

summary: Roman general and consul Titus Vinius was killed in Rome during the overthrow of Galba.
text: Titus Vinius, Roman general and consul (b. AD 12)

summary: Otho committed suicide near Calvatone to prevent further civil war following his defeat by Vitellius.
text: Following his defeat by Vitellius, the commander of the Roman army on the lower Rhine, near modern Calvatone, and to prevent further civil war, Otho committed suicide.

summary: The Roman Senate recognized Vespasian as the ruler of the Roman Empire.
text: The Senate recognized Vespasian, the commander of Roman forces in Egypt and Judea, as ruler of Rome.

summary: Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus assumed office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Vespasian and his son Caesar Vespasian (the future Emperor Titus) become Roman consuls.

summary: Panic broke out in Rome as adverse winds delayed grain shipments from Africa and Egypt, causing a severe bread shortage.
text: Panic strikes Rome as adverse winds delay grain shipments from Africa and Egypt, producing a bread shortage. Ships laden with wheat from North Africa sail 300 miles to Rome's port of Ostia in 3 days, and the 1,000 mile voyage from Alexandria averages 13 days. The vessels often carry 1,000 tons each to provide the city with the 8,000 tons per week it normally consumes.

summary: Frontinus served as praetor of Rome while Legio II Adiutrix was formed from marines of the Ravenna fleet.
text: Sextus Julius Frontinus is praetor of Rome. Legio II Adiutrix is created from marines of Classis Ravennatis.

summary: Pliny the Elder served as imperial procurator in Gallia Narbonensis.
text: Pliny the Elder serves as procurator in Gallia Narbonensis.

summary: Titus surrounded Jerusalem with four Roman legions and cut off escape for Passover pilgrims.
text: 14th of Xanthikos (14th of Nisan, about April 14) – Siege of Jerusalem: Titus surrounds the Jewish capital, with three legions (V Macedonica, XII Fulminata and XV Apollinaris) on the western side and a fourth (X Fretensis) on the Mount of Olives to the east. He puts pressure on the food and water supplies of the inhabitants by allowing pilgrims to enter the city to celebrate Passover and then refusing them egress.

summary: Titus launched a full-scale assault on the Third Wall of Jerusalem using siege engines and battering rams.
text: About April 21 – Titus opens a full-scale assault on Jerusalem, concentrating his attack on the city's Third Wall (HaHoma HaShlishit) to the northwest. The Roman army begins trying to breach the wall using testudos, mantlets, siege towers, and battering rams.

summary: The Third Wall of Jerusalem collapsed under Roman assault, forcing Jewish defenders to withdraw from Bezetha to the Second Wall.
text: 7th of Artemisios (7th of Iyar, about May 6) – The Third Wall of Jerusalem collapses and the Jews withdraw from Bezetha to the Second Wall, where the defences are unorganized.

summary: Titus breached the Second Wall of Jerusalem and began encircling the city with a circumvallation wall.
text: 12th of Artemisios (12th of Iyar, about May 11) – Titus and his Roman legions breach the Second Wall of Jerusalem. The Jewish defenders retreat to the First Wall. The Romans start building a circumvallation; all trees within 90 stadia (ca. fifteen kilometres) of the city are cut down.

summary: Chariots and troops were reportedly witnessed running across the clouds in an omen seen around Jerusalem.
text: 21st of Artemisios (about May 20 or 21) – A "certain prodigious and incredible phenomenon", "chariots and troops" seen running in the clouds around Jerusalem

summary: Priests in the Temple in Jerusalem felt a quaking and heard a mysterious sound during Pentecost.
text: Pentecost (Shavuot, 6th of Sivan, about June 4) – Priests in the Temple in Jerusalem feel a quaking and hear "a sound as of a great multitude saying, Let us remove hence".

summary: Daily sacrifices ceased in the Temple in Jerusalem during the Roman siege.
text: 17th of Panemos (17th of Tammuz), about July 14) – Sacrifices cease in the temple.

summary: Roman forces set fire to a cloister after capturing the Antonia Fortress and engaged in street fighting with the Zealots.
text: 24th of Panemos (about July 20) – Romans set fire to a cloister after the capture of the Fortress of Antonia, north of the Temple Mount. The Romans are drawn into street fighting with the Zealots.

summary: Titus destroyed the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem, and Roman troops abolished the Jewish high priesthood and Sanhedrin.
text: 10th of Loios (9th or 10th of Av, about August 4) – Titus destroys the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem. Roman troops are stationed in Jerusalem and abolish the Jewish high priesthood and Sanhedrin. This becomes known as the Fall of Jerusalem, a conclusive event in the First Jewish–Roman War (the Jewish Revolt), which began in 66 AD. Following this event, the Jewish religious leadership moves from Jerusalem to Jamnia (present-day Yavne), and this date is mourned annually as the Jewish fast of Tisha B'Av.

summary: Titus captured the city of Jerusalem.
text: August – Titus captures Jerusalem.

summary: Roman forces gained full control of Jerusalem, burning the city and killing or enslaving its remaining residents.
text: 8th of Gorpiaios (8th of Elul, about September 2) – Romans gain control of all of Jerusalem and proceed to burn it and kill its remaining residents, except for some who are taken captive to be killed later or enslaved.

summary: The Roman Empire founded the city of Neapolis in Judaea Province.
text: Neapolis (present-day Nablus) is founded in Iudaea Province.

summary: Batavian rebels captured a Roman flagship during clashes on the Rhine and imprisoned its crew at Augusta Treverorum.
text: Naval clashes on the Rhine during the Batavian Revolt; the crew of a captured Roman flagship is imprisoned at Augusta Treverorum (modern Trier).

summary: Batavian rebels destroyed two Roman legions before Quintus Petillius Cerialis suppressed the rebellion of Gaius Julius Civilis.
text: Roman legions V Alaudae and XV Primigenia are destroyed by the Batavi. Later, Quintus Petillius Cerialis puts down the Batavian rebellion of Gaius Julius Civilis.

summary: Vespasian disbanded four Rhine legions disgraced for surrendering or losing their eagles during the revolt of Gaius Julius Civilis.
text: Vespasian disbands four Rhine legions (I Germanica, IV Macedonica, XV Primigenia and XVI Gallica), disgraced for having surrendered or lost their eagles during the revolt of Julius Civilis.

summary: Domitian married Domitia Longina.
text: Later Roman emperor Domitian marries Domitia Longina.

summary: Roman forces launched a punitive expedition against the Garamantes, forcing them into an official relationship with the Roman Empire.
text: Romans make a punitive expedition against the Garamantes – they are forced to have an official relationship with the Roman Empire.

summary: The Roman Empire under Vespasian annexed the island of Samothrace.
text: Annexation of the island of Samothrace by the Roman Empire under Vespasian.

summary: Roman commander Septimius Flaccus led an expedition to southern Egypt and probably reached Sudan.
text: Expedition by the Roman Septimius Flaccus to southern Egypt. He probably reaches Sudan.

summary: Following the destruction of Jerusalem, the Sanhedrin relocated to Jamnia.
text: Following the destruction of Jerusalem, the Sanhedrin moved to Jamnia.

summary: Greek Cynic philosopher Demonax was born in Cyprus.
text: Demonax, Greek Cynic philosopher

summary: Roman politician and general Gaius Julius Quadratus Bassus was born.
text: Gaius Julius Quadratus Bassus, Roman politician (d. AD 117)

summary: Greek geographer and cartographer Marinus of Tyre was born.
text: Marinus of Tyre, Greek geographer and writer (d. AD 130)

summary: Greek mathematician and astronomer Menelaus of Alexandria was born.
text: Menelaus of Alexandria, Greek mathematician (d. AD 140)

summary: Eleazar ben Simon, Jewish leader of the Zealots, died during the siege of Jerusalem.
text: Eleazar ben Simon, Jewish leader of the Zealots

summary: Roman general Gaius Dillius Vocula was murdered during the Batavian rebellion.
text: Gaius Dillius Vocula, Roman general (murdered)

summary: Greek mathematician and engineer Hero of Alexandria died.
text: Hero of Alexandria, Greek mathematician and engineer

summary: Roman consul and governor Lucius Calpurnius Piso was assassinated.
text: Lucius Calpurnius Piso, Roman consul and governor

summary: Roman writer on agriculture Lucius Junius Moderatus Columella died.
text: Lucius Junius Moderatus Columella, Roman writer

summary: Malichus II, Roman client king of Nabatea, died.
text: Malichus II, Roman client king of Nabatea

summary: Phannias ben Samuel, the last High Priest of Israel, died during the fall of Jerusalem.
text: Phannias ben Samuel, high priest of Israel

summary: Simeon ben Gamliel, Jewish leader and nasi of the Sanhedrin, died.
text: Simeon ben Gamliel, Jewish leader (nasi)

summary: Simon bar Giora, Jewish military leader during the revolt against Rome, was executed.
text: Simon bar Giora, Jewish leader (executed)

summary: The Roman army established a fortress at Eboracum as a base for northern forces including Legio IX Hispana.
text: The Romans establish a fortress at York (Eboracum), as a base for their northern forces. Initially established solely for Legio IX Hispana, it expands later to include public housing, baths and temples.

summary: Roman governor Quintus Petillius Cerialis suppressed a revolt by the Brigantes at the Battle of Stanwick.
text: Battle of Stanwick: Quintus Petillius Cerialis, governor of Britain, puts down a revolt by the Brigantes.

summary: Emperor Vespasian and Marcus Cocceius Nerva served as Roman consuls.
text: Emperors Vespasian and Marcus Cocceius Nerva are Roman Consuls.

summary: Quintus Petillius Cerialis defeated Claudius Civilis at the Battle of Trier, quelling the Batavian rebellion.
text: Battle of Treves: Cerialis defeats Claudius Civilis, thus quelling the Batavian rebellion.

summary: Titus celebrated a Roman triumph in Rome accompanied by Vespasian and Domitian, displaying Jewish captives and temple treasures while executing Simon bar Giora.
text: Titus is awarded with a triumph, accompanied by Vespasian and his brother Titus Flavius Domitian. In the parade are Jewish prisoners and treasures of the Temple of Jerusalem, including the Menorah and the Pentateuch. The leader of the Zealots, Simon Bar Giora, is lashed and strangled in the Forum.

summary: Vespasian appointed Titus praetorian prefect of the Praetorian Guard and granted him proconsular imperium and tribunician power.
text: Titus is made praetorian prefect of the Praetorian Guard and receives pro-consular command and also tribunician power, all of which indicates that Vespasian will follow the hereditary tradition of succession.

summary: Legio X Fretensis captured and destroyed the Jewish fortress of Herodium on their march to Masada.
text: Herodium, a Jewish fortress south of Jerusalem, is conquered and destroyed by Legio X Fretensis on their way to Masada.

summary: Roman settlers founded Doncaster under the name Danum.
text: Doncaster is founded by Roman settlers. The area was originally known as Danum.

summary: King Rabbel II Soter made Bosra the second capital of the Nabataean Kingdom.
text: Reign of Rabel II, king of Nabataea. He makes Bostra, Syria, his second capital.

summary: Mithraism began to spread throughout the Roman Empire.
text: Mithraism begins to spread throughout the Roman Empire.

summary: Roman forces entered Scotland during the Roman conquest of Britain.
text: Roman conquest of Britain: Roman forces entered modern Scotland.

summary: Emperor Vespasian deposed King Antiochus IV of Commagene and annexed his kingdom.
text: Antiochus IV of Syria is deposed by Emperor Vespasian.

summary: Vespasian and Titus served as Roman consuls.
text: Vespasian and Titus are Roman Consuls.

summary: Sextus Lucilius Bassus led Legio X Fretensis to besiege and capture the fortress of Machaerus.
text: First Jewish–Roman War: The Roman army (Legio X Fretensis) under Sextus Lucilius Bassus lays siege to the Jewish garrison of Machaerus at the Dead Sea. After they capitulate, the Zealots are allowed to leave the fortress before it is destroyed.

summary: The Romans laid siege to Masada, a desert fortress held by the Sicarii.
text: The Romans lay siege to Masada, a desert fortress held by the Sicarii.

summary: The Romans founded the city of Flavia Neapolis.
text: Flavia Neapolis (Nablus) is founded.

summary: Vespasian began construction of the Colosseum in Rome.
text: Vespasian starts the building of the Colosseum; the amphitheatre is used for gladiatorial games and public spectacles, such as sea battles, re-enactments of famous battles, and dramas of Classical mythology.

summary: Julia Balbilla, princess of Commagene, was born.
text: Julia Balbilla, princess of Commagene

summary: Vespasian and Titus took office as Roman censors.
text: Vespasian and Titus are appointed to be Roman censors.

summary: Lucius Flavius Silva breached Masada after the defending Sicarii committed mass suicide.
text: Spring – The Roman governor Lucius Flavius Silva lays siege to Masada, the last outpost of the Jewish rebels following the end, in AD 70, of the First Jewish-Roman War (Jewish Revolt). The Roman army (Legio X Fretensis) surrounds the mountain fortress with a 7-mile long siege wall (circumvallation) and builds a rampart of stones and beaten earth against the western approach. After the citadel is conquered, 960 Zealots under the leadership of Eleazar ben Ya'ir commit mass suicide when defeat becomes imminent.

summary: Pliny the Elder served as procurator in Hispania Tarraconensis.
text: Pliny the Elder serves as procurator in Hispania Tarraconensis.

summary: Domitian became a Roman consul.
text: Titus Flavius Domitianus becomes Roman Consul.

summary: Emperor Vespasian began conquests east of the Rhine and reorganized Roman defenses along the Danube.
text: Emperor Vespasian begins conquest of territory east of the upper Rhine and south of the Main. In addition, he reorganizes the defenses of the upper and lower Danube.

summary: Martial wrote a satire on military cowardice.
text: Martial writes a satire on "military cowardice".

summary: Titus Flavius Hyrcanus, son of Josephus, was born.
text: Titus Flavius Hyrcanus, Roman aristocrat

summary: Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus became Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.

summary: The Black Forest region was reattached to the Roman Empire.
text: The Black Forest region is reattached to the Roman Empire.

summary: Emperor Vespasian granted privileges to doctors and teachers throughout the Roman Empire.
text: Vespasian grants generous privileges to doctors and teachers.

summary: Hyginus, the future bishop of Rome, was born.
text: Hyginus, bishop of Rome

summary: Caenis, former secretary to Antonia Minor and mistress of Emperor Vespasian, died.
text: Caenis, Roman slave and secretary of Antonia Minor (mother of Emperor Claudius) and mistress of Emperor Vespasian

summary: Polemon II, former king of Pontus, Cilicia, and the Bosporan Kingdom, died.
text: Polemon II, prince of the Bosporan Kingdom, Pontus, Cilicia and Cappadocia

summary: Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus served as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.

summary: The Temple of Peace was constructed in Rome to celebrate the conquest of Jerusalem.
text: The Temple of Peace, also known as the Forum of Vespasian, is built in Rome. The temple celebrates the conquest of Jerusalem (in AD 70) and houses the Menorah from Herod's Temple.

summary: Emperor Vespasian fortified Armazi for King Mithridates I of Iberia while Alans raided Roman Armenia.
text: Vespasian fortifies Armazi (Georgia) for the Iberian king Mithridates I. The Alans raid the Roman frontier in Armenia.

summary: Sextus Julius Frontinus became governor of Britannia and established headquarters at Isca Augusta.
text: Sextus Julius Frontinus becomes governor of Britannia and makes his headquarters in Isca Augusta (Wales).

summary: Frontinus began the Roman conquest of Wales, stationing Legio II Augusta along the River Usk.
text: Frontinus begins his conquest of Wales; Legio II Augusta is moved to the border of the River Usk.

summary: The Roman historian Suetonius was born.
text: Suetonius, Roman historian (d. c. 122)

summary: Cilician prince Gaius Julius Alexander Berenicianus was born.
text: Gaius Julius Alexander Berenicianus, Cilician prince (d. 150)

summary: Vespasian and Titus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperors Vespasianus Augustus and Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.

summary: Sextus Julius Frontinus subdued the Silures in Wales and established the legionary fortress of Isca Augusta at Caerleon.
text: Governor Sextus Julius Frontinus subdues the Silures and other hostile tribes of Wales, establishing a fortress at Caerleon or Isca Augusta for Legio II Augusta, and makes a network of smaller forts for his auxiliary forces.

summary: Pope Anacletus succeeded Pope Linus as the head of the Catholic Church.
text: Pope Anacletus I succeeds Pope Linus as the third pope of the Catholic Church (according to the official Vatican list).

summary: The future Roman emperor Hadrian was born.
text: Hadrian, Roman emperor (d. 138)

summary: Pope Linus died.
text: Linus, pope of the Catholic Church

summary: Roman politician and former governor Marcus Vettius Bolanus died.
text: Marcus Vettius Bolanus, Roman politician and governor (b. 33 AD)

summary: Greek Christian missionary Nicanor the Deacon was martyred.
text: Nicanor the Deacon, Greek missionary and martyr

summary: Roman historian Quintus Asconius Pedianus died.
text: Quintus Asconius Pedianus, Roman historian (b. 9 BC)

summary: Gnaeus Julius Agricola was appointed governor of Roman Britain and pushed Roman control toward the River Clyde.
text: Gnaeus Julius Agricola is named governor of Britannia, a post he occupies until AD 84. He extends the Roman influence to the mouth of the River Clyde (Scotland), and builds fortifications.
names: List of governors of Roman Britain

summary: Gnaeus Julius Agricola subdued the Ordovices in Wales and pursued them onto Anglesey.
text: Agricola subdues the Ordovices in Wales, and pursues the remnants of the tribe to Anglesey, the holy island of the Druids.

summary: Caledonian tribes in Scotland established a confederacy led by Calgacus.
text: The Caledonian tribes in Scotland form a confederacy of 30,000 warriors, under the leadership of Calgacus.

summary: Gnaeus Julius Agricola conquered Anglesey and withdrew his troops to winter quarters.
text: Winter – Agricola conquers Anglesey, and disperses his army to their winter quarters.

summary: Pliny the Elder published the first ten volumes of his Natural History.
text: Pliny the Elder publishes the first ten books of Naturalis Historia.

summary: The Romans developed an early technique for distillation.
text: The Romans develop a simple method of distillation.

summary: The Romans completed the conquest of the Ordovices and the Silures in Wales.
text: The Romans conquer the Ordovices, located in present-day northern Wales, as well as the Silures.

summary: Gnaeus Julius Agricola succeeded Sextus Julius Frontinus as governor of Roman Britain.
text: Gnaeus Julius Agricola replaces Sextus Julius Frontinus as governor of Roman Britain, which leads to the conquering of portions of Wales and northern England.

summary: Emperor Kadphises of the Kushan Empire sent an embassy to Rome to seek an alliance against Parthia.
text: Emperor Kadphises of the Kushan Empire sends a delegation to Rome, to seek support against the Parthians.

summary: Pacorus II ascended the throne of the Parthian Empire.
text: Pacorus II becomes king of the Parthian Empire (r. 78–115).

summary: Roman senator Gaius Salonius Matidius Patruinus died.
text: Gaius Salonius Matidius Patruinus, Roman politician

summary: King Vologases I of the Parthian Empire died.
text: Vologases I, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Vespasian and Titus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Vespasianus Augustus and Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.

summary: Emperor Vespasian died, Titus succeeded him as emperor, and Titus dismissed Berenice from Rome.
text: Emperor Vespasian dies of fever from diarrhea; his last words on his deathbed are: "I think I'm turning into a god." Titus succeeds his father as Roman emperor. Titus' Jewish mistress, Berenice, comes to join him in Rome, but he exiles her to please the Senate.

summary: Mount Vesuvius erupted, obliterating Pompeii, Herculaneum, Stabiae, and Oplontis, and causing the death of Pliny the Elder.
text: August 24 or c. October 24 – Eruption of Mount Vesuvius: Mount Vesuvius erupts, destroying Pompeii, Herculaneum, Stabiae and Oplontis. The Roman navy (based at Misenum), commanded by Pliny the Elder, evacuates refugees. Pliny dies after inhaling volcanic fumes.
names: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

summary: Nerva died at the Gardens of Sallust and was succeeded as Roman emperor by his adopted son Trajan.
text: Nerva dies of a fever at his villa in the Gardens of Sallust and is succeeded by his adopted son Trajan. Trajan is the first Roman Emperor born in Italica, near Seville. A brilliant soldier and administrator, he enters Rome without ceremony and wins over the public. Continuing the policies of Augustus, Vespasian and Nerva, he restores the Senate to its full status in the government and begins a form of state welfare aimed at assuring that poor children are fed and taken care of. He has a specific vision of the Empire, which reaches its maximum extent under his rule, and keeps a close watch on finances. Taxes, without any increase, are sufficient during his reign to pay the considerable costs of the budget. The informers used by Domitian to support his tyranny are expelled from Rome. In order to maintain the Port of Alexandria, Trajan reopens the canal between the Nile and the Red Sea.

text: Silius Italicus, Roman politician and author of the Punica (annals of Hannibal during the Second Punic War) (b. c. AD 28)

summary: Lucius Julius Ursus Servianus and Lucius Licinius Sura assumed office as Roman consuls.
text: Lucius Julius Ursus Servianus and Lucius Licinius Sura become Roman consuls.

summary: Emperor Trajan returned to Rome after a successful campaign in Dacia, re-establishing Roman authority over King Decebalus.
text: Emperor Trajan returns to Rome after a successful campaign against Dacia, through which he reestablishes clear Roman sovereignty over King Decebalus.

summary: Emperor Trajan divided the province of Pannonia into Pannonia Superior and Pannonia Inferior.
text: Trajan divides Pannonia into two provinces, sometime between this year and 107.

summary: The Roman port facility at Portus was enlarged.
text: The port of Portus is enlarged.

summary: Planning and surveying commenced for the expansion of harbor facilities at Ostia.
text: Planning and surveying for the port of Ostia is undertaken.

summary: Bishop of Rome Clement I died according to Roman Catholic tradition.
text: Clement I, bishop of Rome (approximate date according to Roman Catholic tradition)

summary: Trajan and Manius Laberius Maximus became Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Trajan and Manius Laberius Maximus become Roman consuls.

summary: Pliny the Younger became a member of the college of augurs.
text: Pliny the Younger becomes a member of the college of Augurs (103–104).

summary: Legio X Gemina moved its base to Vindobona.
text: Legio X Gemina moves to Vienna, where it remains until the 5th century.

summary: A Temple of the Sun was erected to the god Baal in Palmyra.
text: In Palmyra, Syria, a Temple of the Sun is erected to the god Baal.

summary: Roman author and general Sextus Julius Frontinus died.
text: Sextus Julius Frontinus, Roman author (b. c. AD 40)

summary: Roman poet and satirist Martial died.
text: Martial, poet and satirist

summary: Roman politician and epic poet Silius Italicus died.
text: Silius Italicus, Roman politician and author (b. c. AD 28)

summary: Pliny the Younger continued serving as a member of the College of Augurs.
text: Pliny the Younger continues as a member of the College of Augurs (103–104).

summary: Nijmegen was renamed Ulpia Noviomagus Batavorum.
text: Nijmegen is renamed Ulpia Noviomagus Batavorum.

summary: A fire broke out in Rome.
text: A fire breaks out in Rome.

summary: Trajan ordered the construction of the Alcántara Bridge over the Tagus River.
text: Trajan gives the order to have the Alcántara Bridge, constructed by the architect Lacer, built over the Tagus River at Alcántara (Hispania).

summary: Apollodorus of Damascus built a monumental stone bridge over the Danube connecting Serbia with Dacia.
text: Apollodorus of Damascus builds a stone bridge over the Danube more than long, almost high and wide. The bridge connects what is now Serbia with Romania (at the time known as Dacia).

summary: Roman charioteer Gaius Appuleius Diocles was born.
text: Gaius Appuleius Diocles, Roman charioteer

summary: Trajan departed Brundusium with the Roman fleet to launch his second expedition against Dacia.
text: Emperor Trajan starts the second expedition against Dacia; he leaves with the Imperial Roman fleet from Brundusium.

summary: Legio II Adiutrix established a permanent castrum at Aquincum in Pannonia.
text: Permanent castrum of Legio II Adiutrix at Aquincum (modern Budapest) in Pannonia.

summary: Trajan created Legio XXX Ulpia Victrix and Legio II Traiana Fortis.
text: Legio XXX Ulpia Victrix and II Traiana Fortis are created by Trajan.

summary: The Romans captured Kerak from the Nabataeans.
text: The Romans conquer Kerak from the Nabateans.

summary: Vologases III succeeded Pacorus II as ruler of the Parthian Empire.
text: Pacorus II of Parthia dies after a 27-year reign, in which he has reclaimed all of his empire. His successor Vologases III reigns until 147 AD, suppressing brief rebellions, as he battles against the Kushan and Alani.

summary: Trajan's Bridge over the Danube was completed.
text: The Trajan Bridge is finished. For more than a thousand years, it is the longest arch bridge in the world to have been built, in terms of both total and span length.

summary: Pope Alexander I succeeded Pope Evaristus as Bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Alexander I succeeds Pope Evaristus as the sixth pope according to Roman Catholic tradition .

summary: Sedecion succeeded Plutarch as Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Change of Patriarch of Constantinople from Patriarch Plutarch to Patriarch Sedecion.

summary: Greek mystic and oracle Alexander of Abonoteichus was born.
text: Alexander of Abonoteichus, Greek mystic and oracle (d. 170)

summary: Roman politician and general Marcus Sedatius Severianus was born.
text: Marcus Sedatius Severianus, Roman politician (d. 161)

summary: Roman politician Gnaeus Afranius Dexter died.
text: Gnaeus Afranius Dexter, Roman politician

summary: Roman general Gnaeus Pompeius Longinus died while held captive in Dacia.
text: Gnaeus Pompeius Longinus, Roman politician

summary: Roman grammarian Marcus Valerius Probus died.
text: Marcus Valerius Probus, Roman grammarian

summary: Pacorus II, King of the Parthian Empire, died.
text: Pacorus II, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Plutarch, Bishop of Byzantium, died.
text: Plutarch, bishop of Byzantium

summary: Ignatius of Antioch wrote a letter to the Christians in Smyrna using the term Catholic Church for the first time in surviving literature.
text: Ignatius writes a letter to Christians in Smyrna, using the term Catholic Church . This is the earliest surviving witness to the use of the term "Catholic Church".

object: Dacian Fortresses of the Orăștie Mountains
summary: Emperor Trajan conquered the Dacian Fortresses of the Orăştie Mountains and surrounded the Dacian capital of Sarmizegetusa.
text: Emperor Trajan conquers the Dacian Fortresses of the Orăştie Mountains, and surrounds the capital, Sarmizegetusa.
names: Dacian Fortresses of the Orăștie Mountains

summary: Roman forces defeated the Dacians at the Battle of Sarmizegetusa, leading King Decebalus to flee and commit suicide.
text: Battle of Sarmizegetusa: The Dacians are defeated with 50,000 captured. King Decebalus flees and commits suicide.

summary: The southeastern part of Dacia was organized into the Roman province of Roman Dacia and settled with legionary veterans.
text: The south-eastern part of Dacia (modern Romania) becomes a Roman province: Roman Dacia. The veterans of the legions are given land in the new province for their service in the Roman army.

summary: Emperor Trajan annexed the Nabataean Kingdom, organizing it into the Roman province of Arabia Petraea.
text: Trajan annexes the Nabataean Kingdom (with its capital Petra) as the Roman province of Arabia Petraea. The epoch of the calendar of the province of Arabia begins on March 22.

summary: The Romans constructed a road connecting Eilat and Damascus.
text: Romans construct a road between Eilat and Damascus.

summary: Aelianus Tacticus wrote his military treatise Taktike Theoria.
text: Aelianus Tacticus (or Aelian) writes his Taktike Theoria .

summary: King Decebalus of Dacia committed suicide while being pursued by Roman forces.
text: Decebalus, king of Dacia (suicide, being pursued by the Romans) (b. AD 87)

summary: Rabbel II Soter, ruler of the Nabataean Kingdom, died.
text: Rabbel II Soter, ruler of the Nabataean Kingdom

summary: Lucius Licinius Sura and Quintus Sosius Senecio became Roman consuls.
text: Lucius Licinius Sura and Quintus Sosius Senecio become consuls of Rome.

summary: Emperor Trajan received an Indian ambassador.
text: An Indian ambassador is received by Emperor Trajan.

summary: Roman politician and governor Titus Avidius Quietus died.
text: Titus Avidius Quietus, Roman politician and governor

summary: Ignatius of Antioch died.
text: Ignatius of Antioch (possible date)

summary: Appius Annius Trebonius Gallus and Marcus Atilius Bradua became Roman consuls.
text: Appius Annius Trebonius Gallus and Marcus Atilius Bradua become Roman Consuls.

summary: Tacitus wrote his Histories, chronicling Roman history from the Year of the Four Emperors through the Flavian dynasty.
text: Tacitus writes Histories, which covers the period from AD 69 to AD 96.

summary: The Hypogeum of Yarhai underground tomb was built in Palmyra for the family of Yarhai.
text: The Hypogeum of Yarhai, an underground tomb from the Syrian city of Palmyra dedicated to the family of Yarhai, is built.

summary: Christian martyr Hyacinth of Caesarea died.
text: Hyacinth of Caesarea, Christian martyr

summary: Emperor Trajan inaugurated the Aqua Traiana aqueduct channeling water into Rome from Lake Bracciano.
text: The Aqua Traiana is inaugurated by Emperor Trajan; the aqueduct channels water from Lake Bracciano, northwest of Rome.

summary: Emperor Trajan constructed the Via Traiana linking Benevento to Brindisi at his personal expense.
text: The Via Traiana is constructed at the Emperor Trajan's personal expense; the road connects Benevento with Brundisium (Brindisi).

summary: The Baths of Trajan, designed by Apollodorus of Damascus over the Domus Aurea in Rome, were dedicated.
text: The Baths of Trajan, built by the architect Apollodorus of Damascus, are dedicated during the Calends. The thermae are constructed on the platform of the Palace of Nero (Domus Aurea) in Rome.

summary: Pliny the Younger served as imperial legate to the province of Bithynia.
text: Pliny the Younger is legate to Bithynia.

summary: Osroes I succeeded his brother Pacorus II as ruler over the western Parthian Empire.
text: Osroes I of Parthia succeeds his brother Pacorus II, and rules over the western Parthian Empire.

summary: The Christian Church proclaimed its universal character across the Mediterranean world.
text: The Christian Church proclaims itself to be universal (catholic).

summary: Apollodorus of Damascus constructed the Forum of Trajan in Rome.
text: The Forum of Trajan is constructed in Rome, by the Syrian architect Apollodorus of Damascus.

summary: The Roman Empire maintained an extensive road network throughout its provinces.
text: The Roman Empire has more than of roads.

summary: Caravans departed Luoyang bearing Chinese goods to barter in Central Asia for Roman manufactured imports and bullion.
text: Caravans make regular departures from Luoyang with Chinese ginger, cassia (a type of cinnamon), and silk to be bartered in Central Asia for gold, silver, glassware, pottery, cloth, and intaglio gems from Rome.

summary: Roman historian Suetonius published his biographical work De viris illustribus.
text: Suetonius, Roman historian, publishes Viris Illustribus ("On Famous Men" – in the field of literature).

summary: Christian chronicler and writer Hegesippus was born.
text: Hegesippus of Nazarene, Christian chronicler and writer (d. 180)

summary: Pacorus II, King of Kings of the Parthian Empire, died.
text: Pacorus II, ruler (King of Kings ) of the Parthian Empire

summary: Emperor Trajan appointed Pliny the Younger as governor of Bithynia.
text: Emperor Trajan sends Pliny the Younger to be governor (legatus Augusti) of Bithynia.

summary: Antinous, the Bithynian Greek youth and lover of Emperor Hadrian, was born.
text: Antinous, Bithynian Greek lover of Emperor Hadrian (d. 130)

summary: Emperor Trajan and Titus Sextius Cornelius Africanus assumed office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Trajan and Titus Sextius Cornelius Africanus become Roman consuls.

summary: Salonia Matidia received the title of Augusta upon the death of Ulpia Marciana.
text: Salonia Matidia receives the title of Augusta upon the death of Marciana.

summary: Hadrian succeeded Gaius Julius Cassius Steirieus as eponymous archon of Athens.
text: Hadrian succeeds Gaius Julius Cassius Steirieus as archon of Athens.

summary: Tacitus was appointed proconsul of the Roman province of Asia.
text: Tacitus is named proconsul of the Roman province of Asia (112–113).

summary: Emperor Trajan inaugurated Trajan's Forum in Rome.
text: Trajan's Forum was inaugurated.

summary: Trajan's Column was completed in Rome to commemorate Emperor Trajan's victory over the Dacians.
text: Trajan's Column near the Colosseum in Rome is completed to commemorate the Emperor's victory over the Dacians in the Second Dacian War.

summary: Osroes I of Parthia violated the treaty with Rome by installing a puppet ruler in Armenia, prompting Emperor Trajan to march east.
text: Osroes I of Parthia violates the treaty with Rome by installing a puppet ruler in Armenia. Emperor Trajan marches east, without first attempting to use diplomacy to resolve the disagreement.

summary: Emperor Trajan sailed from Rome and arrived in Athens, where Parthian envoys met him with olive branches.
text: Emperor Trajan sails from Rome to begin his expedition against Parthia. He arrives in Athens where Parthian envoys greet him with olive branches, a sign of peace.

summary: The Basilica Ulpia was dedicated in Rome.
text: Basilica Ulpia is dedicated.

summary: Adrianus, a Greek sophist philosopher, was born.
text: Adrianus, Greek sophist philosopher (d. 193)

summary: Gnaeus Claudius Severus Arabianus, a Roman senator and philosopher, was born.
text: Gnaeus Claudius Severus Arabianus, Roman senator and philosopher (d. after 176)

summary: Pliny the Younger, the Roman lawyer and author, died.
text: Pliny the Younger, Roman lawyer and scientist (b. AD 61)

summary: Construction began on the Arch of Trajan in Benevento.
text: Construction begins on the Arch of Trajan in Benevento.

summary: The kingdom of Osroene became a vassal kingdom of the Roman Empire.
text: The kingdom of Osroene becomes a vassal kingdom of the Roman Empire.

summary: Emperor Trajan defeated the Parthians and overran Armenia and northern Mesopotamia.
text: Emperor Trajan defeats the Parthians and overruns Armenia and northern Mesopotamia.

summary: A monument to Philopappos, prince-in-exile of Commagene, was erected in Athens.
text: A monument to Philopappos, prince-in-exile of old Commagene (a buffer-state between Rome and Parthia) is erected in Athens.

summary: Diogenes succeeded Sedecion as bishop of Byzantium.
text: Change of Patriarch of Constantinople from Patriarch Sedecion to Patriarch Diogenes.

summary: Emperor Trajan deposed King Parthamasiris of Armenia and organized Armenia into a Roman province.
text: Trajan deposed the Armenian king Parthamasiris of Armenia, a Roman client, and organized the province of Armenia on his territory.

summary: Emperor Trajan was cut off in southern Mesopotamia during his invasion of the region.
text: Emperor Trajan is cut off in southern Mesopotamia after his invasion of that region.

summary: Emperor Trajan captured the Parthian capital of Ctesiphon.
text: Trajan captures the Parthian capital of Ctesiphon.

summary: The Diaspora Revolt erupted across Jewish communities in Egypt, Libya, and Cyprus against the Roman Empire.
text: The Diaspora Revolt erupts almost simultaneously across various Jewish Diaspora communities in the empire's east, including Egypt, Libya and Cyprus.

summary: Marcus Rutilius Lupus dispatched Legio XXII Deiotariana to protect Memphis after civil clashes damaged Alexandria.
text: Alexandria in Egypt is damaged during the Jewish-Greek civil wars. Marcus Rutilius Lupus, the Roman governor, sends Legio XXII Deiotariana to protect the inhabitants of Memphis.

summary: A revolt broke out in Britain and rebels massacred the Roman garrison at Eboracum.
text: A revolt breaks out in Britain; the garrison at Eboracum (York) is massacred.

summary: The Pantheon was reconstructed in Rome.
text: The Pantheon of Agrippa is reconstructed in Rome.

summary: An earthquake devastated Antioch and Apamea in Syria.
text: An earthquake destroys Apamea and Antioch in Syria. The local bishop is held responsible (he will be martyred and remembered as St. Ignatius).

summary: Pope Sixtus I succeeded Pope Alexander I as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Sixtus I succeeds Alexander I as the seventh pope of Rome (according to Catholic biographies).

summary: Pausanias, the Greek geographer and historian, was born.
text: Pausanias, Greek historian and geographer (d. 180)

summary: Pope Alexander I, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Alexander I, bishop of Rome

summary: Dio Chrysostom, the Greek philosopher and historian, died.
text: Dio Chrysostom, Greek philosopher and historian (b. AD 40)

summary: Emperor Trajan completed his invasion of Parthia by capturing Seleucia, Babylon, Ctesiphon, and Susa.
text: Emperor Trajan completes his invasion of Parthia by capturing the cities of Seleucia, Babylon, Ctesiphon and Susa, marking the high-water mark of the Roman Empire's eastern expansion.

summary: Emperor Trajan crossed the Tigris to annex Adiabene and advanced toward the Persian Gulf.
text: Trajan makes Syria a province of Rome and crosses the Tigris to annex Adiabene. He proceeds with his army to the Persian Gulf and conquers territory that becomes the province of Parthia.

summary: Emperor Trajan removed Osroes I and appointed Parthamaspates as king of Parthia.
text: Trajan removes Osroes I as king of Parthia, and appoints his son Parthamaspates in his place. Parthamaspates romanizes his name to Parthicus.

summary: Emperor Trajan dispatched Roman legions to suppress revolts in Judea and Cyprus.
text: Trajan sends two expeditionary forces. One, consisting of elements of Legio III Cyrenaica, to suppress the revolt in Judea and the other Legio VII Claudia to restore order on Cyprus.

summary: Lusius Quietus suppressed uprisings across Mesopotamia, recovering Nisibis and sacking Edessa.
text: In summer, rebellious movement emerges in Mesopotamia against Roman occupation. General Lusius Quietus is sent by Trajan to suppress the uprisings, recovering Nisibis, besieging and sacking Edessa, and waging war against local Jews

summary: Trajan sent laureatae to the Roman Senate to announce his conquest of Parthia.
text: Trajan sends laureatae to the Roman Senate on account of his victories and being conqueror of Parthia.

summary: Quintus Marcius Turbo sailed to Alexandria and defeated Jewish insurgents in several pitched battles.
text: Quintus Marcius Turbo sails to Alexandria and defeats Jewish insurgents in several pitched battles.

summary: Christian martyr Quirinus of Neuss died in Rome.
text: Quirinus of Neuss, Roman Christian martyr according to Roman Catholic tradition

summary: Abgar VII, ruler of Osroene, died.
text: Abgar VII, ruler of Osroene

summary: Prince Philopappos of Commagene died in Athens.
text: Philopappos, prince of Commagene (b. AD 65)

summary: Zacchaeus of Jerusalem, bishop of Jerusalem, died.
text: Zacchaeus of Jerusalem, bishop of Jerusalem

summary: The Roman Empire organized the provinces of Mesopotamia and Assyria on territory conquered from Parthia.
text: The provinces of Mesopotamia and Assyria were organized on territory conquered from Parthia.

summary: Jewish communities in Egypt revolted against Roman authority during the Diaspora Revolt.
text: Diaspora Revolt: The Jews of Egypt revolt

summary: Roman Emperor Trajan suffered a stroke and died at Selinus in Cilicia.
text: Emperor Trajan falls seriously ill and dies of a stroke at Selinus in Cilicia, age 63, while en route from Mesopotamia to Italy, leaving the Roman Empire at its maximal territorial extent.

summary: On his deathbed, Trajan adopted Hadrian and designated him as his imperial successor.
text: On his death bed, Trajan allegedly adopts Hadrian, a fellow Spaniard, and designates him as his successor. Hadrian will reign until 138.

summary: The Roman Empire suppressed the Jewish Diaspora Revolt, devastating Jewish populations in Cyrenaica, Cyprus, and Egypt.
text: The Jewish Diaspora Revolt is quelled, likely by autumn 117, though unrest may have persisted in Egypt until early 118. Its suppression results in the near-complete expulsion of Jews from Cyrenaica, Cyprus, and several regions of Egypt.

summary: Hadrian returned large parts of Mesopotamia to the Parthian Empire to pursue imperial retrenchment.
text: Hadrian returns large parts of Mesopotamia to the Parthians as part of a peace settlement. He inaugurates a policy of retrenchment and cultural integration, giving up the policy of conquest of his predecessor in order to consolidate the empire.

summary: Construction began on the Pantheon in Rome.
text: Construction begins on the Pantheon in Rome.

summary: Emperor Hadrian lowered the silver content of the Roman denarius from 93 percent to 87 percent.
text: The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 87 percent under emperor Hadrian, down from 93 percent in the reign of Trajan.

summary: John I became the seventh Bishop of Jerusalem.
text: John I becomes the 7th Bishop of Jerusalem.

summary: Greek orator Aelius Aristides was born.
text: Aelius Aristides, Greek orator (d. 181)

summary: Roman Emperor Trajan died at the age of sixty-three.
text: Trajan, Roman emperor (b. AD 53)

summary: Roman historian Tacitus died.
text: Gaius Cornelius Tacitus, Roman historian (b. AD 56)

summary: Roman general Gaius Julius Quadratus Bassus died.
text: Gaius Julius Quadratus Bassus, Roman general in Judea (b. AD 70)

summary: Hermione of Ephesus and other Christian martyrs died during persecution.
text: Hermione of Ephesus, Maurus, Pantalemon and Sergius, Astius and several other Christian martyrs in persecution by Trajan

summary: Roman forces captured the rebel stronghold of Lod and executed many inhabitants during the Kitos War.
text: Kitos War: Roman forces captured the rebel stronghold of Lod and executed many of its inhabitants.

summary: Osroes I deposed his son Parthamaspates and reclaimed the throne as shah of Parthia.
text: Osroes I deposed his son Parthamaspates of Parthia and replaced him as shah of Parthia.

summary: Trajan's Forum in Rome was completed with triumphal arches, market complexes, and the Basilica Ulpia.
text: Trajan's Forum (commissioned by the late Emperor Trajan) is completed with triumphal arches, columns, a market complex, and an enormous basilica, all of which replace hundreds of dwellings.

summary: Emperor Hadrian served as Roman consul.
text: Emperor Hadrian is also a Roman Consul.

summary: The population of Rome exceeded one million people, making it the largest city in the world.
text: Rome has a population exceeding 1 million, making it the largest city in the world.

summary: The Roman Empire restored Osroene to native rule.
text: Osroene is returned to native rule by the Roman Empire.

summary: Hadrian executed four consular senators accused of plotting against him, straining relations with the Senate.
text: Plot of the consuls: Hadrian executes four senators, all former consuls, who had been shown to have plotted against him. His relations with the Senate are strained.

summary: Construction began on the rebuilt Pantheon in Rome.
text: Pantheon, in Rome, starts to be built .

object: Battle of Centaurs and Wild Beasts
summary: The mosaic Battle of Centaurs and Wild Beasts was created for Hadrian's Villa in Tivoli.
text: 118–128 – Battle of Centaurs and Wild Beasts, from Hadrian's Villa, Tivoli, Italy, is made . It may be a copy of a painting done by the late 5th century BC Greek artist Zeuxis. It is now kept at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Preussischer Kulturbesitz, Antikensammlung.
names: Battle of Centaurs and Wild Beasts

summary: Primus, patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Primus, patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Roman politician and general Aulus Cornelius Palma Frontonianus was executed.
text: Aulus Cornelius Palma, Roman politician

summary: Bassus of Lucera, Roman bishop and martyr, died.
text: Bassus of Lucera, Roman bishop and martyr

summary: Roman politician Gaius Avidius Nigrinus was executed at Faventia.
text: Gaius Avidius Nigrinus, Roman politician

summary: Roman politician Lucius Publilius Celsus was executed at Baiae.
text: Lucius Publilius Celsus, Roman politician

summary: Roman general and former governor Lusius Quietus was executed.
text: Lusius Quietus, Roman general and governor

summary: Terentian, Roman bishop and martyr, died.
text: Terentian, Roman bishop and martyr

summary: Hadrian withdrew Roman forces from Armenia, Assyria, and Mesopotamia, returning them to client monarchies.
text: Hadrian withdrew from the territories of Armenia, Assyria and Mesopotamia, allowing the return of their respective client monarchies.

summary: Emperor Hadrian stationed Legio VI Victrix in Roman Britain to quell a local rebellion.
text: Emperor Hadrian stations Legio VI Victrix in Roman Britain, to assist in quelling the resistance of a local rebellion. The legion is key in securing the victory, and eventually replaces Legio IX Hispana at Eboracum.

summary: Hadrian visited Britain at the request of governor Quintus Pompeius Falco.
text: Hadrian also visits Britain in this year at the request of governor of Britain Quintus Pompeius Falco.

summary: Hadrian delivered a funeral oration for Salonia Matidia and granted her a temple in Rome.
text: Salonia Matidia (a niece of former Emperor Trajan) dies. Hadrian delivers her funeral oration, and grants her a temple in Rome.

summary: Roman politician Gaius Bruttius Praesens was born.
text: Gaius Bruttius Praesens, Roman politician

summary: Roman Christian martyr Marina of Aguas Santas was born.
text: Marina of Aguas Santas, Roman Christian martyr (d. 139)

summary: Salonia Matidia, niece of Trajan, died.
text: Salonia Matidia, niece of Trajan (b. AD 68)

summary: Greek historian and biographer Plutarch died.
text: Plutarch, Greek historian and biographer (b. AD 46)

summary: Roman bishop and martyr Secundus of Asti died.
text: San Secondo of Asti, Roman bishop and martyr

summary: Roman slave and martyr Serapia died.
text: Serapia, Roman slave and martyr

summary: Emperor Hadrian visited Britain.
text: Emperor Hadrian visits Britain.

summary: Foss Dyke was constructed in Roman Britain.
text: Foss Dyke is constructed in Britain.

summary: A Kushan ambassadorial contingent met with Emperor Hadrian.
text: A Kushan ambassadorial contingent visits with Hadrian.

summary: Suetonius became Hadrian's secretary ab epistolis.
text: Suetonius becomes Hadrian's secretary ab epistolis.

summary: Approximate date marker recorded for various Roman events.
text: Approximate date

summary: Legio IX Hispana was last known to be in active existence around this time.
text: Legio IX Hispana last known to be in existence.

summary: The Market Gate of Miletus was constructed at Miletus.
text: The Market Gate of Miletus is built at Miletos (moved in modern times to Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Antikensammlung).

summary: Greek astrologer Vettius Valens was born.
text: Vettius Valens, Greek astrologer (d. 175)

summary: Greek bishop and Christian theologian Irenaeus was born.
text: Irenaeus, Greek bishop and apologist

summary: Syrian rhetorician and satirist Lucian was born.
text: Lucian, Syrian rhetorician and satirist

summary: Syrian Christian writer and theologian Tatian was born.
text: Tatian, Syrian Christian writer and theologian (d. 180)

summary: Greek historian and philosopher Dio Chrysostom died.
text: Dio Chrysostom, Greek historian

summary: Roman Christian martyrs Faustinus and Jovita died.
text: Faustinus and Jovita, Roman Christian martyrs

summary: Roman officer and Christian martyr Getulius died.
text: Getulius, Roman officer and Christian martyr

summary: Christian martyr Saint Hermes died.
text: Hermes, Greek Christian martyr and saint

summary: Roman bishop Marcian of Tortona died.
text: Marcian of Tortona, Roman bishop (or 117)

summary: Matthias, bishop of Jerusalem, died.
text: Matthias of Jerusalem, bishop of Jerusalem

summary: Greek mathematician Nicomachus died.
text: Nicomachus, Greek mathematician (b. AD 60)

summary: Greek philosopher Plutarch died.
text: Plutarch, Greek philosopher

summary: Roman jurist Sextus Pedius died.
text: Sextus Pedius, Roman jurist (b. AD 50)

summary: Roman historian Tacitus died.
text: Tacitus, Roman historian

summary: A Roman settlement in present-day Wiesbaden was first mentioned.
text: Roman settlement in present-day Wiesbaden, Germany, is first mentioned.

summary: Emperor Hadrian fixed the border between Roman Britain and Caledonia from the River Tyne to the Solway Firth.
text: Emperor Hadrian fixes the border between Roman Britain and Caledonia, on a line running from the River Tyne to the Solway Firth.

summary: Construction of the Temple of Venus and Roma began in Rome.
text: Construction of the Temple of Venus and Roma begins in Rome.

summary: Marcus Aurelius, the future Roman emperor and philosopher, was born in Rome.
text: Marcus Annius Verus, later Emperor Marcus Aurelius (d. 180)

summary: Christian martyrs Eleutherius and Antia were executed during persecutions in the Roman Empire.
text: Eleutherius and Antia, Roman Christian martyrs and saints

summary: Emperor Hadrian ordered the construction of a 73-mile wall in northern Roman Britain to repel northern tribes.
text: Emperor Hadrian orders that a 73-mile (117-kilometer) wall be built to mark the northern Roman Empire while personally visiting the area. Hadrian's Wall, as it comes to be known, is intended to keep the Caledonians, Picts and other tribes at bay.

summary: The auxiliary Cohors VIII Batavorum garrisoned the Roman fort of Vindolanda in northern England.
text: Vindolanda, a Roman auxiliary fort (castrum) in northern England, is garrisoned by cohort VIII Batavorum.

summary: The Roman Empire began construction of Hadrian's Wall across northern Britain.
text: The building of Hadrian's Wall begins.

summary: Emperor Hadrian relinquished the Roman territories previously conquered in Scotland.
text: Hadrian gives up the territories conquered in Scotland.

summary: Emperor Hadrian averted war with Parthia by meeting King Osroes I.
text: Emperor Hadrian averts a war with Parthia by a personal meeting with Osroes I (according to the Historia Augusta, disputed).

summary: The Roman army constructed Housesteads Roman Fort on Hadrian's Wall north of Bardon Mill.

summary: Salvius Julianus completed the codification of the Praetor's Edict on the orders of Emperor Hadrian.
text: The Praetor's Edict is definitively codified by Salvius Julianus, on Hadrian's orders. This change means that senatorial decrees become a mere confirmation of the imperial speech (oratio principis) which initiated them.

summary: Hadrian reorganized the Imperial Council, centralizing administrative authority and excluding the Senate from state business.
text: Reorganization of the Imperial Council: Central administration is reinforced, and administrative positions are entrusted to knights, according to a very strict hierarchy. Under the reorganization, the Roman Senate is excluded from controlling the business of state.

summary: Hadrian granted the equestrian order full legal status as the second order of the Roman state.
text: Hadrian restores the monarchist policy of Claudius and Domitian. The equestrian order is given full legal status, and attains the second order of the state.

summary: Hadrian divided Italy into legal districts governed by consular magistrates.
text: Italy is divided into legal districts managed by consuls, a direct blow to the power and prestige of the Senate.

summary: Hadrian issued an edict banning circumcision and severely restricting Jewish religious observances.
text: The Edict of Hadrian prohibits the practice of circumcision. Additionally, Hadrian prohibits public reading of the Torah under penalty of death, as well as observance of festivals and the Sabbath, the teaching of Judaic Law, and the ordination of rabbis.

summary: Jewish rebels forced Legio X Fretensis to evacuate Jerusalem and re-established sacrificial worship.

They strike coins to celebrate their independence, which will last for only 30 months. Legio XXII Deiotariana, which advanced from Egypt, is completely destroyed.

Jewish rebels, led by Simon bar Kokhba and Eleazar, cut off the vital supply lines and Roman garrisons in Palestine. Despite Roman reinforcements from Syria and Egypt, they establish an independent state in Judea.

The suppression caused widespread devastation across Judaea, resulting in extensive destruction, significant loss of life, mass displacement, and enslavement, which substantially reduced the Jewish population. summary: Marcus Aurelius pursued policies favoring women and slaves while maintaining cooperative relations with the Roman Senate.
text: Marcus Aurelius, a Spaniard like Trajan and Hadrian, is a stoical disciple of Epictetus, and an energetic man of action. He pursues the policy of his predecessor and maintains good relations with the Senate. As a legislator, he endeavors to create new principles of morality and humanity, particularly favoring women and slaves.

text: Emperor Marcus Aurelius crosses the Danube with an expeditionary force. He subdues the Marcomanni and their allies and then, in a pact signed with the Germanic tribes, he imports them into the Roman Empire to occupy areas that have been depopulated by the plague.

summary: Commodus, son of Marcus Aurelius and Faustina the Younger, was named Caesar.
text: Commodus, son of Marcus Aurelius and his wife Faustina, is named Caesar.

summary: M. Sattonius Iucundus restored the Thermae of Coriovallum in modern Heerlen.
text: M. Sattonius Iucundus, decurio in Colonia Ulpia Traiana, restores the Thermae of Coriovallum (modern Heerlen). There are sources that state this happened in the 3rd century.

summary: The Bucolic War in Roman Egypt came to an end.
text: The end of the Bucolic War in Egypt.

summary: Ammonius Saccas, Egyptian philosopher, was born.
text: Ammonius Saccas, Egyptian philosopher (d. 242)

summary: Future Pope Pontian was born.
text: Pope Pontian of the Catholic Church (d. 235)

summary: Pontianus of Spoleto, Christian martyr, died.
text: Pontianus of Spoleto, Christian martyr (b. 156)

summary: Avidius Cassius, Roman general and usurper, was assassinated.
text: Avidius Cassius, Roman general, usurper (b. AD 130)

summary: Concordius of Spoleto, Christian martyr, died.
text: Concordius of Spoleto, Christian martyr

summary: Faustina the Younger, Roman empress and wife of Marcus Aurelius, died.
text: Faustina the Younger, Roman empress (b. AD 130)

summary: Vettius Valens, Greek astrologer and writer, died.
text: Vettius Valens, Greek astrologer, writer (b. AD 120)

summary: Rome and the Iazyges concluded a treaty to end their war, under which the Iazyges returned Roman prisoners and provided auxiliary troops.
text: Marcomannic Wars: Rome and the Iazyges signed a treaty under which the latter agreed to return Roman prisoners of war and supply troops to the Auxilia, ending the war.

summary: Marcus Aurelius granted Commodus the rank of Imperator and made him Supreme Commander of the Roman legions.
text: Emperor Marcus Aurelius grants his son Commodus the rank of Imperator, and makes him Supreme Commander of the Roman legions.

summary: Marcus Aurelius and Commodus entered Rome and celebrated a triumph for their victories over Germanic tribes.
text: Marcus Aurelius and Commodus enter Rome after a campaign north of the Alps, and receive a triumph for their victories over the Germanic tribes.

summary: The Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius was crafted in Rome.
text: The Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius is made. It is now kept at Museo Capitolini in Rome .

summary: Faustina the Younger, Roman empress, died.
text: Faustina the Younger, Roman empress (b. AD 130)

summary: Marcus Macrinius Avitus Catonius Vindex, Roman general and politician, died.
text: Marcus Macrinius Avitus Catonius Vindex, Roman politician

summary: Commodus and Marcus Peducaeus Plautius Quintillus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Lucius Aurelius Commodus Caesar (age 15) and Marcus Peducaeus Plautius Quintillus become Roman Consuls.

summary: Commodus was given the title Augustus and made co-emperor alongside Marcus Aurelius.
text: Commodus is given the title Augustus, and is made co-emperor, with the same status as his father, Marcus Aurelius.

summary: A systematic persecution of Christians began in Rome, forcing believers to seek refuge in the catacombs.
text: A systematic persecution of Christians begins in Rome; the followers take refuge in the catacombs.

summary: A crowd in southern Gaul destroyed local Christian churches after accusing believers of cannibalism.
text: The churches in southern Gaul are destroyed after a crowd accuses the local Christians of practicing cannibalism.

summary: Forty-eight Christians, including Blandina and Saint Pothinus, bishop of Lyon, were martyred in Lyon.
text: Forty-eight Christians are martyred in Lyon (Saint Blandina and Pothinus, bishop of Lyon, are among them).

summary: Marcus Aurelius and Commodus began the Second Marcomannic War against the Quadi and the Marcomanni.
text: Second Marcomannic War: Marcus Aurelius and Commodus begin war against the Quadi and the Marcomanni.

summary: Lucius Aurelius Commodus Pompeianus, a Roman politician and nobleman, was born.
text: Lucius Aurelius Commodus Pompeianus, Roman politician

summary: Saint Blandina was martyred during Christian persecutions in Lugdunum.
text: Blandina, Christian martyr and saint (b. 162)

summary: Greek politician, rhetorician, and Roman senator Herodes Atticus died.
text: Herodes Atticus, Greek politician (b. AD 101)

summary: Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, died.
text: Polycarpus, Greco-Roman bishop (b. AD 69)

summary: Saint Pothinus, the first bishop of Lyon, was martyred.
text: Pothinus, Roman bishop and martyr (b. AD 87)

summary: Bruttia Crispina married Commodus and received the title of Augusta.
text: Bruttia Crispina marries Commodus, and receives the title of Augusta.

summary: Marcus Aurelius and Commodus arrived at Carnuntum to conduct operations against the Marcomanni along the Danube.
text: Emperor Marcus Aurelius and his son Commodus arrive at Carnuntum in Pannonia, and travel to the Danube to fight against the Marcomanni.

summary: The Montanist movement was formally condemned as a heresy for the first time.
text: The Montanist heresy is condemned for the first time.

summary: Agrippinus, patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Agrippinus, patriarch of Alexandria

summary: The Roman fortress of Castra Regina was constructed on the Danube at modern Regensburg.
text: The Roman fort Castra Regina ("fortress by the Regen river") is built at Regensburg, on the right bank of the Danube in Germany.

summary: Soldiers of Legio II Adiutrix carved a Roman inscription commemorating Laugaritio on the rock face at Trenčín.
text: Roman legionaries of Legio II Adiutrix engrave on the rock of the Trenčín Castle (Slovakia) the name of the town Laugaritio, marking the northernmost point of Roman presence in that part of Europe.

summary: Marcus Aurelius repelled the Marcomanni across the Danube and settled the first Germanic colonists inside devastated Pannonia.
text: Marcus Aurelius drives the Marcomanni over the Danube and reinforces the border. To repopulate and rebuild a devastated Pannonia, Rome allows the first German colonists to enter territory controlled by the Roman Empire.

summary: Abgar IX the Great became King of Edessa.
text: Abgar IX the Great becomes King of Edessa.

summary: Praetorian prefect Tarutenius Paternus won a decisive victory over Germanic tribes, driving the Quadi deeper into Germania.
text: The Quadi are chased westwards, deeper into Germania. The Praetorian prefect, Tarutenius Paternus, achieves a decisive victory against the Germanic tribes.

summary: Emperor Marcus Aurelius died at Vindobona and was succeeded by his son Commodus.
text: Emperor Marcus Aurelius dies after a week's illness at his camp in Vindobona (modern Vienna). He is succeeded by his son Commodus (age 18).

summary: The Era of the Five Good Emperors ended with the death of Marcus Aurelius and the succession of Commodus.
text: The Era of the Five Good Emperors ends.

summary: Rome established a four-mile wide buffer strip along the northern bank of the Danube.
text: Rome creates a 4-mile wide buffer zone by the Danube.

summary: Construction began in Rome on the Column of Marcus Aurelius to commemorate his Danubian campaigns.
text: Work begins in Rome on the building of the Column of Marcus Aurelius.

summary: The Roman Empire entered the period known as the Late Empire.
text: 180–395 – Late Empire in Rome.

summary: Northern tribes from beyond Hadrian's Wall invaded northern Roman Britain, prompting Emperor Commodus to permit northern cities to construct walls.
text: Northern British from beyond Hadrian's Wall invade the North of modern-day England, causing Emperor Commodus to allow swathes of Northern cities to establish city walls.

summary: Cassius Dio arrived in Rome and became a Roman senator.
text: Cassius Dio arrives in Rome and becomes a Senator

summary: The Goths migrated to the shores of the Black Sea.
text: The Goths reach the banks of the Black Sea.

summary: Galen described the link between paralysis and the severing of the spinal cord in his Methodus Medendo.
text: In his Methodus Medendo, Greek physician Galen describes the connection between paralysis and the severing of the spinal cord.

summary: Galen published a popular medical treatise on hygiene.
text: Galen's popular work on hygiene is published.

summary: Twelve Christian inhabitants of Scillium were executed in Carthage for refusing to swear an oath to the Roman emperor.
text: Twelve Christian inhabitants of Scillium in Numidia are executed in Carthage (also in North Africa) (known as the Scillitan Martyrs) – they had refused to swear an oath to the Emperor.

summary: Emperor Commodus instituted an official Roman cult of the god Mithra.
text: Commodus creates an official cult of the Zoroastrian god Mithra.

summary: Johanan bar Nappaha, prominent Jewish rabbi, was born.
text: Johanan bar Nappaha, Jewish rabbi (d. 279)

summary: Julia Soaemias, Roman noblewoman and mother of Emperor Elagabalus, was born.
text: Julia Soaemias, mother of Elagabalus (d. 222)

summary: Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius died.
text: Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor (b. 121)

summary: Roman author and grammarian Aulus Gellius died.
text: Aulus Gellius, Roman author and grammarian (b. 125 AD)

summary: Roman jurist and legal scholar Gaius died.
text: Gaius, Roman jurist and writer

summary: Early Christian writer and chronicler Hegesippus died.
text: Hegesippus, Christian chronicler and writer (b. 110)

summary: Syrian-Greek satirist and rhetorician Lucian died.
text: Lucian of Samosata, Syrian rhetorician (b. 125 AD)

summary: Melito, bishop of Sardis and early Christian apologist, died.
text: Melito of Sardis, bishop of Sardis

summary: Pinytus, bishop of Knossos, died.
text: Pinytus, bishop of Knossos

summary: The Antonine Plague pandemic came to an end across the Roman Empire.
text: Antonine Plague: The pandemic ended.

summary: Commodus and Lucius Antistius Burrus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Imperator Lucius Aurelius Commodus and Lucius Antistius Burrus become Roman Consuls.

summary: The Picts overran the Antonine Wall in Britannia.
text: The Antonine Wall is overrun by the Picts in Britannia .

summary: Greek orator and writer Aelius Aristides died.
text: Aelius Aristides, Greek orator and writer (b. 117)

summary: Emperor Commodus survived an assassination attempt orchestrated by his sister Lucilla and senators, leading to widespread executions and Lucilla's exile to Capri.
text: Emperor Commodus escapes death at the hands of assassins, who have attacked him at the instigation of his sister Lucilla and a large group of senators. He puts many distinguished Romans to death on charges of being implicated in the conspiracy; Lucilla is exiled to Capri.

summary: Former Roman empress Lucilla was executed on Capri after plotting against her brother Emperor Commodus.
text: Lucilla, Roman empress and daughter of Marcus Aurelius

summary: Roman politician Marcus Ummidius Quadratus was executed for his role in the conspiracy against Commodus.
text: Marcus Ummidius Quadratus, Roman politician (b. 138)

summary: Saoterus, Bithynian freedman and chamberlain to Emperor Commodus, was assassinated.
text: Saoterus, Bithynian Greek freedman and chamberlain

summary: Roman noblewoman Ummidia Cornificia Faustina died.
text: Ummidia Cornificia Faustina, Roman noblewoman (b. 141)

summary: Christian scholar and theologian Origen was born in Alexandria.
text: Origen, Christian scholar and theologian

summary: Roman forces abandoned the Antonine Wall in Caledonia.
text: The Antonine Wall was abandoned by Roman forces.

summary: Roman nobles from Britain demanded that Emperor Commodus remove Tigidius Perennis from power.
text: Nobles of Britain demand that Emperor Commodus rescind all power given to Tigidius Perennis, who is eventually executed.

summary: Pertinax was appointed governor of Britain and quelled a mutiny of the British Roman legions.
text: Publius Helvius Pertinax is made governor of Britain and quells a mutiny of the British Roman legions who wanted him to become emperor. The disgruntled usurpers go on to attempt to assassinate the governor.

summary: Emperor Commodus had Tigidius Perennis and his family executed for conspiring against him.
text: Tigidius Perennis, his family and many others are executed for conspiring against Commodus.

summary: Emperor Commodus fought as a gladiator at the Circus Maximus while draining the treasury to stage spectacles.
text: Commodus drains Rome's treasury to put on gladiatorial spectacles and confiscates property to support his pleasures. He participates as a gladiator and boasts of victory in 1,000 matches in the Circus Maximus.

summary: Cleomedes discovered the refraction of light by the atmosphere of the Earth.
text: Cleomedes discovers the refraction of light by the Earth's atmosphere.

summary: Irenaeus asserted in his writings that there are only four canonical Gospels.
text: Irenaeus writes that there are only four Gospels .

summary: Christian theologian and scholar Origen was born in Alexandria.
text: Origen, Christian scholar and theologian

summary: Apollonius the Apologist, Christian apologist and martyr, was put to death in Rome.
text: Apollonius the Apologist, Christian apologist

summary: King Pharasmanes III of Iberia died.
text: Pharasmanes III (or P'arsman), Georgian king of Iberia

summary: Praetorian prefect Tigidius Perennis was executed in Rome.
text: Tigidius Perennis, Roman praetorian prefect (executed)

summary: Peasants in Gaul staged an anti-tax revolt under the leadership of Maternus.
text: Peasants in Gaul stage an anti-tax uprising under Maternus.

summary: Pertinax, governor of Britain, survived an assassination attempt by mutinous Roman legionaries.
text: Roman governor Pertinax escapes an assassination attempt, by British usurpers.

summary: Christian martyr Apollonius the Apologist died in Rome.
text: Apollonius the Apologist, Christian martyr

summary: Roman noblewoman Paccia Marciana died.
text: Paccia Marciana, Roman noblewoman

summary: Sohaemus, the Roman client king of Armenia, died.
text: Sohaemus, Roman client king of Armenia

summary: Septimius Severus married Julia Domna at Lugdunum.
text: Septimius Severus marries Julia Domna (age 17), a Syrian princess, at Lugdunum (modern-day Lyon). She is the youngest daughter of high-priest Julius Bassianus – a descendant of the Royal House of Emesa. Her elder sister is Julia Maesa.

summary: Clodius Albinus defeated the Chatti tribe.
text: Clodius Albinus defeats the Chatti, a highly organized German tribe that controlled the area that includes the Black Forest.

summary: Olympianus succeeded Pertinax as bishop of Byzantium.
text: Olympianus succeeds Pertinax as bishop of Byzantium (until 198).

summary: Maternus, a Gaulish rebel leader, died.
text: Maternus, Gaulish rebel leader

summary: Pertinax, bishop of Byzantium, died.
text: Pertinax, bishop of Byzantium

summary: Publius Helvius Pertinax became proconsul of Africa.
text: Publius Helvius Pertinax becomes pro-consul of Africa from 188 to 189.

summary: Caracalla, the future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Caracalla (or Antoninus), Roman emperor (d. 217)

summary: Julian, pope and patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Julian, pope and patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Lucius Antistius Burrus, a Roman politician, was executed.
text: Lucius Antistius Burrus, Roman politician (executed)

summary: Publius Atilius Aebutianus, the Roman praetorian prefect, was executed.
text: Publius Atilius Aebutianus, Roman prefect (executed)

summary: A deadly plague struck Rome, killing thousands per day and causing food shortages and riots.
text: Plague (possibly smallpox) kills as many as 2,000 people per day in Rome. Farmers are unable to harvest their crops, and food shortages bring riots in the city.

summary: Galen published his Treatise on the Various Temperaments.
text: Galen publishes his "Treatise on the various temperaments" (a.k.a. On the Elements According to Hippocrates).

summary: Victor I succeeded Eleutherius as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Victor I succeeds Pope Eleuterus as the fourteenth pope, the first from Africa.

summary: Demetrius became Patriarch of Alexandria.
text: Demetrius of Alexandria becomes Patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Publius Septimius Geta, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Publius Septimius Geta, Roman emperor (d. 211)

summary: Eleutherius, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Eleutherius, bishop of Rome (or Catholic Church)

summary: After a fire destroyed part of Rome, Emperor Commodus ordered it rebuilt under the name Colonia Commodiana.
