text: A part of Rome burns; Emperor Commodus orders the city to be rebuilt, under the name Colonia Commodiana.

summary: Marcus Aurelius Cleander appointed twenty-five men as Roman consuls, including Lucius Septimius Severus.
text: At the climax of his power, the freedman Marcus Aurelius Cleander appoints 25 men as Roman consuls. Amongst these is Lucius Septimius Severus, who later becomes emperor during the Year of the Five Emperors.

summary: A Roman road crossing the Alps by the Simplon Pass was opened.
text: A Roman road crosses the Alps, by the Simplon Pass.

summary: Cleomedes taught that the Moon does not glow on its own but reflects sunlight.
text: Cleomedes teaches that the moon does not glow on its own, but rather reflects sunlight.

summary: Roman Egypt suffered severe impoverishment due to runaway inflation over the preceding decade.
text: Egypt (under Roman rule) is impoverished due to an inflation rate of 100% during the previous decade.

summary: The Roman authorities debased the silver content of the Egyptian denarius from ninety percent to seventy percent.
text: The percentage of silver in the Egyptian denarius is lowered from 90% to 70%.

summary: Gaius Furius Sabinius Aquila Timesitheus, later Roman praetorian prefect, was born.
text: Gaius Furius Sabinius Aquila Timesitheus, Roman praetorian prefect (d. 243)

summary: Quintus Egnatius Proculus, later a Roman politician, was born.
text: Quintus Egnatius Proculus, Roman politician

summary: Marcus Aurelius Cleander, Roman praetorian prefect, died.
text: Marcus Aurelius Cleander, Roman praetorian prefect

summary: Athenagoras of Athens, Greek Christian apologist, died.
text: Athenagoras of Athens, Greek Christian apologist (b. 133)

summary: Emperor Commodus executed the Roman politician Julius of Rome.
text: Julius of Rome, Roman politician (executed by Commodus)

summary: The portrait bust of Commodus depicted as Hercules was sculpted on the Esquiline Hill in Rome.
text: c. 191–192 – The sculpture of Commodus as Hercules, from Esquiline Hill, Rome, is made (it is now kept at Palazzo dei Conservatori, Rome).

summary: Serapion became the Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Serapion becomes Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Empress Bruttia Crispina was executed in exile by order of Commodus.
text: Bruttia Crispina, Roman empress (executed) (b. 164)

summary: The wrestler Narcissus assassinated Emperor Commodus at the instigation of Commodus's mistress Marcia, ending the Nerva-Antonine dynasty.
text: Emperor Commodus alarms the Senate, by appearing dressed as a gladiator for his new consulship on January 1. His mistress Marcia finds her name on the imperial execution list, and hires champion wrestler Narcissus to assassinate Commodus; the Antonines Dynasty ends.

summary: A civil war broke out across the Roman Empire following the assassination of Commodus.
text: Civil war again strikes Ancient Rome (192–193).

summary: Barbarian attackers struck the city of Rome during civil unrest, killing forty-five people.
text: Barbarians strike the city of Rome during the Civil War on August 22. 45 die.

summary: A fire in Rome destroyed the library and personal writings of the physician Galen.
text: A fire destroys Galen's library.

summary: Gordian II, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Gordian II, Roman emperor (Year of the Six Emperors) (d. 238)

summary: Roman emperor Commodus was assassinated in Rome.
text: Commodus, Roman emperor (b. 161)

summary: Roman noblewoman Annia Fundania Faustina was executed.
text: Annia Fundania Faustina, Roman noblewoman

summary: The Roman Senate chose Pertinax to succeed Commodus as emperor.
text: Year of the Five Emperors: The Roman Senate chooses Publius Helvius Pertinax, against his will, to succeed the late Commodus as Emperor. Pertinax is forced to reorganize the handling of finances, which were wrecked under Commodus, to reestablish discipline in the Roman army, and to suspend the food programs established by Trajan, provoking the ire of the Praetorian Guard.

summary: Septimius Severus was proclaimed emperor by his troops at Carnuntum in Pannonia Superior.
text: Lucius Septimius Severus is proclaimed Emperor by his troops at Carnuntum, in Pannonia Superior (Balkans). He marches with his army to Rome.

summary: Septimius Severus entered Rome, had Didius Julianus put to death, and seized control of the Roman Empire.
text: Septimius Severus enters the capital, and has Julianus put to death. He replaces the Praetorian Guard with a 15,000-man force from the Danubian legions, and gains control of the Roman Empire, beginning the Severan dynasty.

summary: Septimius Severus defeated the forces of Pescennius Niger at Cyzicus and Nicaea in Asia Minor.
text: Battle of Cyzicus and Battle of Nicaea (Asia Minor): Septimius Severus defeats the army under Pescennius.

summary: British tribes took advantage of imperial disorder to damage Hadrian's Wall, prompting repairs by Roman legionaries.
text: In Britain, Clodius Albinus allies with Septimius Severus, and accepts the title of Caesar. British tribes take advantage of the disorder in the Empire, and damage Hadrian's Wall. Extensive repairs to the defence work is carried out by the legionaries.

summary: Counterfeiting workshops began appearing across the Roman Empire.
text: Counterfeiting workshops begin to appear throughout the Roman Empire.

summary: A pre-ecumenical church council was held in Rome.
text: The Council of Rome, the pre-ecumenical council

summary: Septimius Severus reduced the silver content of the Roman denarius to fifty percent.
text: The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 50 percent under emperor Septimius Severus, down from 68 percent under Marcus Aurelius.

summary: Roman emperor Pertinax was assassinated in Rome by the Praetorian Guard.
text: Pertinax, Roman emperor (assassinated) (b. 126)

summary: Roman emperor Didius Julianus was executed in Rome on the orders of the Senate.
text: Didius Julianus, Roman emperor (assassinated)

summary: Greek sophist and philosopher Adrianus died in Rome.
text: Adrianus (or Hadrian), Greek sophist, philosopher and writer

summary: Roman general and politician Tiberius Claudius Pompeianus died.
text: Tiberius Claudius Pompeianus, Roman general and politician

summary: Pescennius Niger, governor of Syria Palaestina, was proclaimed emperor by his legions.
text: Pescennius Niger, the legatus Augusti pro praetore of Syria Palaestina, was proclaimed ruler of Rome by his legions.

summary: Clodius Albinus assumed office as Roman consul.
text: Decimus Clodius Septimius Albinus Caesar becomes a Roman Consul.

summary: Septimius Severus defeated Pescennius Niger at the Battle of Issus, after which Pescennius was captured and executed near Antioch.
text: Battle of Issus: Septimius Severus marches with his army (12 legions) to Cilicia, and defeats Pescennius Niger, Roman governor of Syria. Pescennius retreats to Antioch, and is executed by Severus' troops.

summary: Septimius Severus began a siege of Byzantium, causing extensive damage to its city walls.
text: Septimius Severus besieges Byzantium (194–196); the city walls suffer extensive damage.

summary: Galen wrote his manual on pathology, The Art of Curing.
text: Galen writes his manual on pathology, The Art of Curing .

summary: Irenaeus declared Gnostic doctrines to be heretical.
text: Irenaeus declares Gnostic doctrines to be heretical .

summary: Roman usurper Pescennius Niger was killed after his defeat by Septimius Severus.
text: Pescennius Niger, Roman usurper (b. 140)

summary: Septimius Severus had the Roman Senate deify the late emperor Commodus to gain favor with Marcus Aurelius's family.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus has the Roman Senate deify the previous emperor Commodus, in an attempt to gain favor with the family of Marcus Aurelius.

summary: Septimius Severus marched into Mesopotamia to fight the Parthians after King Vologases V backed a provincial revolt.
text: King Vologases V and other eastern princes support the claims of Pescennius Niger. The Roman province of Mesopotamia rises in revolt with Parthian support. Severus marches to Mesopotamia to battle the Parthians.

summary: The Roman province of Syria was partitioned and Septimius Severus annexed Edessa and Nisibis as Roman colonies.
text: The Roman province of Syria is divided and the role of Antioch is diminished. The Romans annex the Syrian cities of Edessa and Nisibis. Severus re-establishes his headquarters and the colonies there.

summary: Lucius Septimius Bassianus changed his name to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and was appointed Caesar.
text: Lucius Septimius Bassianus (or Caracalla), age 7, changes his name to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, to solidify connections with the family of Marcus Aurelius, and is given the title Caesar.

summary: Clodius Albinus crossed from Britain into Gaul with his legions, prompting Septimius Severus to return from Mesopotamia toward Rome.
text: Clodius Albinus, who had been proclaimed emperor in Britain, crosses into Gaul with his legions, while at the same time recruiting new soldiers. He is soon the head of an army of 150,000 men, according to Cassius Dio. Severus, still in Mesopotamia, hastily returns to Rome.

summary: Septimius Severus devalued the denarius, reducing its precious metal content to fifty percent.
text: The denarius is devalued by Severus. The coin now contains only 50% precious metal.

summary: Septimius Severus attempted to assassinate Clodius Albinus, provoking open military retaliation.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus attempts to assassinate Clodius Albinus but fails, causing Albinus to retaliate militarily.

summary: Septimius Severus captured and sacked Byzantium after a long siege.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus captures and sacks Byzantium; the city is rebuilt and regains its previous prosperity.

summary: Clodius Albinus was declared Augustus by his army while crossing Gaul on his march toward Rome.
text: In order to assure the support of the Roman legion in Germany on his march to Rome, Clodius Albinus is declared Augustus by his army while crossing Gaul.

summary: Hadrian's Wall in northern Britain was partially destroyed.
text: Hadrian's Wall in Britain is partially destroyed.

summary: A church council was held in Caesarea to discuss the date of Easter.
text: A church council is held in Caesarea over the date of Easter.

summary: Septimius Severus defeated the usurper Clodius Albinus at the Battle of Lugdunum, after which Albinus committed suicide and the city was sacked.
text: Battle of Lugdunum: Emperor Septimius Severus defeats the self-proclaimed emperor Clodius Albinus at Lugdunum (modern Lyon). Albinus commits suicide; legionaries sack the town.

summary: Septimius Severus returned to Rome, executed thirty senators who supported Albinus, and proclaimed himself the adopted son of Marcus Aurelius.
text: Septimius Severus returns to Rome and has about 30 of Albinus's supporters in the Senate executed. After his victory he declares himself the adopted son of the late Marcus Aurelius.

summary: Septimius Severus formed new naval units in Italy and embarked his soldiers on a canal between the Tigris and Euphrates.
text: Septimius Severus forms new naval units, manning all the triremes in Italy with heavily armed troops for war in the East. His soldiers embark on an artificial canal between the Tigris and Euphrates.

summary: Septimius Severus levied Legio I, II, and III Parthica for his upcoming campaign against Parthia.
text: Legio I, II, and III Parthica are levied by Septimius Severus for his Parthian campaign.

summary: The Roman army looted the royal palace at Ctesiphon and enslaved many of its inhabitants.
text: The Roman army marches east to repel a Parthian invasion of Mesopotamia; they loot the royal palace at Ctesiphon and capture an enormous number of its inhabitants as slaves.

summary: Septimius Severus reconstituted the province of Mesopotamia under an equestrian governor commanding two legions.
text: Septimius Severus reconstitutes the Province of Mesopotamia under an equestrian governor commanding two legions.

summary: Septimius Severus excluded the Senate from governing the Roman Empire by declaring a military dictatorship.
text: Septimius Severus, who had spared the Senate at the beginning of his reign, now excludes it from controlling the Roman Empire by declaring a military dictatorship.

summary: Galen published his major medical work Pharmacologia.
text: Galen's major work on medicines, Pharmacologia, is published.

summary: A Christian council was held in Edessa.
text: A Christian council is held in Edessa.

summary: Roman general and usurper Clodius Albinus died.
text: Clodius Albinus, Roman general and usurper

summary: Roman politician Gaius Julius Erucius Clarus Vibianus died.
text: Gaius Julius Erucius Clarus Vibianus, Roman politician

summary: Roman statesman Titus Flavius Claudius Sulpicianus died.
text: Titus Flavius Claudius Sulpicianus, Roman statesman

summary: Publius Septimius Geta received the title of Caesar from his father Septimius Severus.
text: January 28: Publius Septimius Geta, son of Septimius Severus, receives the title of Caesar.

summary: Caracalla was elevated to the rank of Augustus by his father Septimius Severus.
text: January 28: Caracalla, son of Septimius Severus, is given the title of Augustus.

summary: Marcus I succeeded Olympianus as Bishop of Byzantium.
text: Marcus I succeeds Olympianus as Patriarch of Constantinople (until 211).

summary: Mesopotamia was partitioned into the two Roman provinces of Mesopotamia and Osroene.
text: Mesopotamia is partitioned into two Roman provinces divided by the Euphrates, Mesopotamia and Osroene.

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus besieged the city of Hatra but failed to capture it.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus lays siege to the city-state Hatra in Central-Mesopotamia, but fails to capture the city despite breaching the walls.

summary: Legio I Parthica and Legio III Parthica were formed as a permanent garrison.
text: Two new legions, I Parthica and III Parthica, are formed as a permanent garrison.

summary: Pope Zephyrinus succeeded Pope Victor I as the bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Zephyrinus succeeds Pope Victor I, as the 15th pope.

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus toured the provinces of Syria, Syria Palaestina, and Arabia Petraea.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus visits the provinces of Syria, Palestine, and Arabia.

summary: The Roman province of Numidia was separated from the proconsul of Africa and converted into an imperial province.
text: The province of Numidia is taken from the African proconsul, and made an Imperial province.

summary: The Severan Tondo panel painting of Emperor Septimius Severus and his family was produced in Fayum.
text: The Severan Tondo, depicting Septimius Severus, Julia Domna and their children Geta and Caracalla, from Fayum, Egypt, is made. It is now kept at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Antikensammlung.

summary: Clement of Alexandria denounced the use of musical instruments in Christian worship in favor of human voices.
text: Clement of Alexandria denounces the use of musical instruments instead of human voices in Christian music.

summary: Future Christian bishop and theologian Cyprian was born in North Africa.
text: Cyprian, Roman bishop and writer (d. 258)

summary: Greek mathematician Diophantus was born.
text: Diophantus, Greek mathematician and writer

summary: Future Roman emperor Marcus Claudius Tacitus was born.
text: Marcus Claudius Tacitus, Roman emperor (d. 276)

summary: Early Christian scholar and antipope Novatian was born.
text: Novatian, Roman antipope and theologian (d. 258)

summary: Future Roman emperor Valerian was born.
text: Valerian I, Roman emperor (d. 260/264)

summary: Praetorian prefect Quintus Aemilius Saturninus died.
text: Quintus Aemilius Saturninus, Roman prefect

summary: Lucius Annius Fabianus and Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus took office as Roman consuls.
text: Lucius Annius Fabianus and Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus become Roman Consuls.

states.value: Lucius Annius Fabianus and Marcus Nonius Arrius Mucianus

summary: A flood in Edessa destroyed a Christian church and killed over two thousand people.
text: November – A flood in Edessa destroys a Christian church, killing over 2,000 people.

summary: Future Roman emperor Decius was born in Pannonia Inferior.
text: Decius, Roman emperor (d. 251)

summary: Greek physician and philosopher Galen died.
text: Galen, Greek physician (see 210) (b. 129)

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus returned to Rome and reformed the administration and pay of the Roman legions.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus returns to Rome after a five-year absence. Festivals are held to celebrate his six-year reign. Severus undertakes changes in the imperial government, giving the Roman army a dominant role, raising pay in the legions and permitting legionaries to marry in order to secure their loyalty.

summary: Rome accommodated an estimated 1.5 million citizens primarily within multi-story insulae apartment blocks.
text: Rome is a city of about 1.5 million citizens, its people housed mostly in 46,600 insulae or apartment blocks, each three to eight stories high, flimsily made of wood, brick or rubble.

summary: An estimated 400,000 enslaved people performed the menial labor of Rome while free urban workers enjoyed daily leisure and public games.
text: Some 400,000 slaves perform the menial work of Rome, with middle-class citizens often owning eight; the rich from 500 to 1,000; an emperor as many as 20,000. Free urban workers enjoy 17 to 18 hours of leisure each day, with free admission to baths, sport events and gladiatorial games.

summary: Septimius Severus launched a campaign along the Limes Tripolitanus, capturing Garama and expanding the province of Numidia.
text: Severus launches a campaign in Africa; Legio III Augusta under Quintus Anicius Faustus fights a guerrilla war against the Garamantes along the Limes Tripolitanus. They capture several settlements such as Cydamus, Gholaia and their capital Garama, 600 km south of Lepcis Magna. The province of Numidia is enlarged: the Romans annex Castellum Dimmidi, Gemellae and Vescera.

summary: An imperial edict prohibited conversions to Christianity and banned all Christian propaganda.
text: An edict bans conversions to Christianity and all Christian propaganda.

summary: A Roman law banned women from participating as gladiators.
text: A Roman law bans female gladiators.

summary: The Roman authorities restored the Pantheon in Rome.
text: The Pantheon is restored.

summary: Clement of Alexandria sought refuge in Cappadocia to escape the anti-Christian persecutions ordered by Septimius Severus.
text: In order to avoid Septimus Severus' persecution of Christians, Clement of Alexandria seeks refuge with Alexander in Cappadocia.

summary: Irenaeus, bishop of Lugdunum and early Christian theologian, died.
text: Irenaeus, Greek bishop and theologian (b. 130)

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus rebuilt Byzantium, refortified Carthage, and expanded the southern frontier of Roman Africa.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus rebuilds Byzantium, and expands the southern frontier of Africa, with the metropolis Carthage re-fortified.

summary: Gaius Fulvius Plautianus and Publius Septimius Geta took office as Roman consuls.
text: Gaius Fulvius Plautianus and Publius Septimius Geta become Roman Consuls.
cast: Publius Septimius Geta (brother of Septimius Severus)
names: Publius Septimius Geta (brother of Septimius Severus)

states.value: Publius Septimius Geta (brother of Septimius Severus)

summary: A triumphal arch dedicated to Septimius Severus was erected near the Roman Forum.
text: An arch dedicated to Septimius Severus is erected near the Forum.

summary: The Portico of Octavia in Rome was reconstructed following fire damage.
text: The Portico of Octavia is reconstructed.

summary: Origen succeeded Clement of Alexandria as head of the Christian catechetical school in Alexandria.
text: Origen replaces Clement as the head of the Christian school in Alexandria.

summary: Christian martyrs Perpetua and Felicity were executed in Carthage.
text: Perpetua and Felicity, Christian martyrs

summary: Lucius Fabius Cilo and Marcus Annius Flavius Libo took office as Roman consuls.
text: Lucius Fabius Cilo and Marcus Annius Flavius Libo become Roman Consuls.

summary: The Daysan River overflowed and flooded the city of Edessa.
text: The Daysan River floods Edessa.

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus alleviated a trade recession in Leptis Magna by purchasing olive oil for free distribution in Rome.
text: A trade recession in the Leptis Magna region (Africa) is alleviated by Emperor Septimius Severus, who buys up the country's olive oil for free distribution in Rome.

summary: Future Roman emperor Elagabalus was born in Emesa.
text: Elagabalus, Roman emperor (d. 222)

summary: Future Roman emperor Philip the Arab was born in Shahba.
text: Philip the Arab, Roman emperor (d. 249)

summary: Caracalla and his brother Geta became Roman consuls.
text: Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and his brother Publius Septimius Geta Caesar become Roman Consuls.

summary: Hadrian's Wall was restored following heavy raids by Caledonian tribes across northern Britain.
text: Hadrian's Wall is restored, after heavy raids by Caledonian tribes had overrun much of northern Britain.

summary: Praetorian prefect Gaius Fulvius Plautianus was assassinated.
text: Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, a praetorian prefect and father-in-law of Caracalla, is assassinated.

summary: Papinian became praetorian prefect following the assassination of Gaius Fulvius Plautianus.
text: Aemilius Papinianus becomes praetorian prefect, after the death of Gaius Fulvius Plautianus.

summary: Plotinus, the Greek philosopher and founder of Neoplatonism, was born.
text: Plotinus, Greek philosopher and writer (d. 270)

summary: Roman consul and praetorian prefect Gaius Fulvius Plautianus died.
text: Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, Roman consul

summary: Former Roman consul Marcus Peducaeus Plautius Quintillus died.
text: Marcus Peducaeus Plautius Quintillus, Roman consul

summary: Roman politician Popilius Pedo Apronianus died.
text: Popilius Pedo Apronianus, Roman politician

summary: Roman forces retook Hadrian's Wall for the first time since the uprising of 180.
text: Hadrian's Wall is retaken for the first time, since the Pictish uprising of 180.

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus traveled to Britain accompanied by his sons Caracalla and Geta.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus goes to Britain, with his sons Caracalla and Geta.

summary: Future Roman emperor Trebonianus Gallus was born.
text: Trebonianus Gallus, Roman emperor (d. 253)

summary: Vologases VI succeeded his father Vologases V as ruler of the Parthian Empire as his brother Artabanus IV rebelled against him.
text: King Vologases VI succeeds his father Vologases V to the throne. His brother Artabanus V begins a rebellion against him in the Parthian Empire.

summary: Ardashir I revolted against his brother at Istakhr and founded the Sasanian Dynasty.
text: Ardashir I, ruler of Istakhr (Persia), revolts against his brother and founds the Sassanid Dynasty.

summary: Caracalla and his brother Geta became Roman consuls.
text: Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and his brother Publius Septimius Geta Caesar become Roman consuls.

summary: Septimius Severus led a military expedition into Scotland, pushed back the Caledonians to the River Tay, and repaired the Antonine Wall.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus leads an expedition (20,000 men) into Britannia, crosses Hadrian's Wall and moves through eastern Scotland. The Roman army pushes the Caledonians back to the River Tay and Severus signs a peace treaty. He repairs the Antonine Wall (his repairs are sometimes called the Severan Wall).

summary: Roman Britain was divided into the provinces of Britannia Inferior and Britannia Superior.
text: Britain is divided: in the north, Lower Britain (Britannia Inferior) is administered from the fortress at Eburacum (modern York), and in the south, Upper Britain (Britannia Superior) is controlled by the legions at Deva Victrix (Chester) and Isca Augusta (Caerleon) with its capital at Londinium (London).

summary: Future Roman emperor Diadumenian was born.
text: Diadumenian, Roman emperor (d. 218)

summary: Future Roman emperor Severus Alexander was born.
text: Severus Alexander, Roman emperor (d. 235)

summary: King Vologases V of the Parthian Empire died.
text: Vologases V, king of the Parthian Empire

summary: Septimius Severus granted the titles of Imperator and Augustus to his son Geta.
text: Publius Septimius Geta receives the titles of Imperator and Augustus from his father, Emperor Septimius Severus.

summary: Septimius Severus campaigned across northern Scotland while Scottish tribes engaged in guerrilla warfare.
text: Septimius Severus makes plans to subdue the land to the north of Scotland, ravaging it severely. Road-building and forest-clearing, the Roman army reaches Aber; Scottish tribes begin guerrilla warfare.

summary: Septimius Severus sent Caracalla to subdue the Scottish tribes through brutal campaigns.
text: Having suffered heavy losses since invading Scotland in 208, Emperor Septimius Severus sends his son - Caracalla - to systematically wipe out and torture the Scots into submission.

summary: Future Roman emperor Claudius Gothicus was born.
text: Claudius II, Roman emperor (d. 270)

summary: Greek historian and general Dexippus was born.
text: Dexippus, Greek historian and general (d. 273)

summary: Roman governor Egnatius Lucillianus was born.
text: Egnatius Lucillianus, Roman governor (d. 244)

summary: Greek philosopher Sextus Empiricus died.
text: Sextus Empiricus, Greek philosopher and writer

summary: Emperor Septimius Severus died at Eboracum, and Caracalla and Geta succeeded him as joint emperors.
text: Emperor Septimius Severus, having fallen ill, dies in Eboracum (modern-day York) while on campaign in Britain after an 18-year reign. He is later deified by the Senate. His sons Caracalla and Geta succeed him as joint Roman emperors.

summary: The Praetorian Guard murdered Emperor Geta in the arms of his mother Julia Domna.
text: Geta is lured to come without his bodyguards to meet Caracalla, to discuss a possible reconciliation. When he arrives the Praetorian Guard murders him, and he dies in the arms of his mother Julia Domna.

summary: Eboracum became the capital of the Roman province of Britannia Inferior.
text: Eboracum becomes the capital of Britannia Inferior, a northern province of the Roman Empire.

summary: Ardashir I became king of part of Persia.
text: Ardashir I becomes king of part of Persia.

summary: Construction began on the Baths of Caracalla in Rome.
text: Baths of Caracalla construction begins .

summary: Philadelphus succeeded Marcus I as bishop of Byzantium.
text: Marcus I is succeeded by Philadelphus, as Patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Roman Emperor Septimius Severus died at Eboracum.
text: Septimius Severus, Roman emperor (b. 145)

summary: Roman co-emperor Geta was assassinated on the orders of his brother Caracalla in Rome.
text: Publius Septimius Geta, Roman emperor (b. 189)

summary: Former Roman empress Fulvia Plautilla was executed while in exile.
text: Fulvia Plautilla, Roman empress and wife of Caracalla

summary: Serapion of Antioch, patriarch of Antioch, died.
text: Serapion of Antioch, patriarch of Antioch

summary: Caracalla ended the Roman military campaign in Caledonia.
text: Roman invasion of Caledonia 208–210: Caracalla ended the campaign.

summary: Emperor Caracalla issued the Constitutio Antoniniana, granting Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the Roman Empire.
text: The edict of Emperor Caracalla (Constitutio Antoniniana) extends Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the Roman Empire, with the exception of a limited group that may include Egyptians. The Jewish people are among those who receive citizenship. All free women in the Empire are given the same rights as Roman women.

summary: Caracalla had the jurist Papinian beheaded in Rome after he refused to defend the murder of Geta.
text: Roman jurist Papinian, one of the famous jurists who flourished during the reign of the late emperor Septimius Severus, refuses to write a legal defence for the murder of Caracalla's brother, Emperor Geta. He is beheaded in Rome, in Caracalla's presence.

summary: Caracalla quieted the Roman army's objections to Geta's murder with large donations.
text: Caracalla quiets the objections of the Roman army to Geta's murder, by huge donations.

summary: Construction began on the Baths of Caracalla in Rome.
text: Construction begins on the Baths of Caracalla in Rome.

summary: Edessa in Mesopotamia became a Roman province.
text: Edessa in Mesopotamia becomes a Roman province.

summary: Annia Cornificia Faustina Minor was executed on the orders of Emperor Caracalla.
text: Annia Cornificia Faustina Minor, daughter of Marcus Aurelius (b. 160)

summary: Papinian, Roman jurist and praetorian prefect, was executed in Rome.
text: Papinian, Roman jurist and praetorian prefect (b. 142)

summary: Roman poet and physician Serenus Sammonicus was put to death.
text: Serenus Sammonicus, Roman poet and physician

summary: Emperor Caracalla campaigned against the Alamanni and Chatti along the Rhine and Main frontiers.
text: Emperor Caracalla leaves Rome and expels some Germanic marauders from Gaul, while his mother, Julia Domna, rules the Empire. He defends the northern Rhine frontier against the Alamanni and the Chatti. Caracalla wins over the Germanic tribes on the banks of the River Main, and gives himself the title "Germanicus". It is probably while campaigning in Germania that he takes a liking to the caracalla, a Celtic or Germanic tunic from which he acquires the name by which he is known.

summary: Gregory Thaumaturgus, Christian bishop, was born in Neocaesarea.
text: Gregory Thaumaturgus, Christian bishop (d. 270)

summary: Roman politician Tiberius Claudius Cleobulus died.
text: Tiberius Claudius Cleobulus, Roman politician

summary: The kingdom of Osroene was annexed by the Roman Empire as a province.
text: The kingdom of Osroene becomes a province of the Roman Empire.

summary: Caracalla secured his popularity with the Roman army through victories in Germany.
text: Caracalla's victories in Germany ensure his popularity within the Roman army.

summary: The defenses of Raetia were reinforced with an uninterrupted stone wall.
text: The defences of Rhaetia are reinforced, in the form of an uninterrupted stone wall.

summary: Claudius Gothicus, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Claudius Gothicus, Roman emperor (d. 270)

summary: Aurelian, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Aurelian, Roman emperor (d. 275)

summary: Greek mathematician Diophantus was born.
text: Diophantus, Greek mathematician

summary: Emperor Caracalla introduced the Antoninianus coin into Roman currency.
text: A coin, the Antoninianus, is introduced. The weight of this coin is a mere 1/50 of a pound. Copper disappears gradually, and by the middle of the third century, with Rome's economy in crisis, the Antonianus will be the only official currency.

summary: Troops under Emperor Caracalla massacred the inhabitants of Alexandria following civic protests and satires mocking him.
text: Caracalla's troops massacre the population of Alexandria, Egypt, beginning with the leading citizens after the Alexandrian Revolts. The emperor was angry about a satire, produced in Alexandria, mocking his claim that he killed Geta in self-defense.

summary: Clement of Alexandria, Christian theologian and philosopher, died.
text: Clement of Alexandria, Greek scholar and philosopher

summary: The Baths of Caracalla were completed in Rome.
text: The Baths of Caracalla in Rome are completed with public baths (Thermae), reading rooms, auditoriums, running tracks, and public gardens that cover 20 acres.

summary: Emperor Caracalla accepted a Parthian marriage proposal as a ruse and slaughtered his bride and the wedding guests.
text: Emperor Caracalla tricks the Parthians by accepting a marriage proposal. He slaughters his bride and the wedding guests after the celebrations.

summary: Caracalla provoked a war with Artabanus IV of Parthia, crossed the Tigris, plundered Arbela, and annexed Armenia.
text: Caracalla provokes a war with Artabanus V (of Parthia) to imitate his idol Alexander the Great. He crosses the Tigris, destroys towns and spoils the tombs of Arbela. The Roman army annexes Armenia.

summary: The grand basilica of Leptis Magna, commissioned by Septimius Severus, was completed.
text: The basilica of Leptis Magna, ordered by Septimius Severus, is completed.

summary: Roman soldiers serving in Asia increasingly adopted the Persian religion of Mithraism.
text: Mithraism, which had begun in Persia, is on course to be adopted by many Roman soldiers serving in Asia.

summary: Mani, the prophet and founder of Manichaeism, was born near Ctesiphon.
text: Mani, prophet and founder of Manichaeism (d. 274)

summary: Clement of Alexandria, Greek Christian theologian, died.
text: Clement of Alexandria, Greek theologian

summary: Narcissus of Jerusalem, bishop of Jerusalem, died.
text: Narcissus of Jerusalem, patriarch of Jerusalem

summary: Greek Christian theologian Pantaenus died.
text: Pantaenus, Greek theologian

summary: Following the assassination of Caracalla near Edessa, Praetorian Prefect Macrinus proclaimed himself Roman emperor.
text: Caracalla is assassinated by his soldiers near Edessa. Marcus Opellius Macrinus, head of the Praetorian Guard, declares himself Roman emperor.

summary: Parthian forces defeated the Roman army commanded by Emperor Macrinus at the Battle of Nisibis.
text: Summer – Battle of Nisibis: A Roman army, under the command of Macrinus, is defeated in a three days' battle by the Parthians at Nisibis, in the province of Mesopotamia.

summary: King Artabanus IV of Parthia concluded a peace treaty with Rome after receiving two hundred million sesterces in reparations.
text: King Artabanus V signs a peace treaty with Rome after he receives 200 million sesterces, for the rebuilding of towns destroyed during the war in Parthia.

summary: Macrinus became the first equestrian Roman emperor.
text: Macrinus, of Mauretania, becomes the first equestrian Roman emperor.

summary: Empress Julia Domna committed suicide.
text: Empress Julia, wife of Septimius Severus and mother of Caracalla and Geta, commits suicide.

summary: A lightning strike caused a fire that badly damaged the upper levels of the Colosseum in Rome.
text: The Colosseum is badly damaged by fire (lightning) which destroys the wooden upper levels of the amphitheater.

summary: Pope Callixtus I was elected as the sixteenth pope following the end of Pope Zephyrinus's papacy.
text: The papacy of Zephyrinus ends. Callixtus I is elected as the sixteenth pope, but is opposed by the theologian Hippolytus who accuses him of laxity and of being a Modalist, one who denies any distinction between the three persons of the Trinity.

summary: Hippolytus of Rome began his tenure as antipope and established a breakaway Christian church.
text: Hippolytus begins his "pontificate" as antipope and sets up a breakaway church for Christian followers.

summary: Roman Emperor Caracalla was assassinated near Carrhae.
text: Caracalla, Roman emperor (b. 188)

summary: Pope Zephyrinus died in Rome.
text: Zephyrinus, pope of Rome

summary: Roman Empress Julia Domna died in Antioch.
text: Julia Domna, Roman empress (b. 160)

summary: Roman prefect Lucius Valerius Datus died.
text: Lucius Valerius Datus, Roman prefect

summary: Julia Maesa declared her grandson Elagabalus emperor of Rome while in Syria.
text: Julia Maesa, an aunt of the assassinated Emperor Caracalla, is banished to her home in Syria by the self-proclaimed emperor Macrinus, and declares her grandson Elagabalus, age 14, emperor of Rome.

summary: Elagabalus defeated Macrinus at the Battle of Antioch, securing his accession as emperor.
text: Battle of Antioch: Elagabalus defeats, with the support of the Syrian legions, the forces of Macrinus. Macrinus flees, but is captured near Chalcedon and later executed in Cappadocia.

summary: Diadumenian was captured at Zeugma while fleeing to Parthia and executed by forces loyal to Elagabalus.
text: Diadumenianus, son of Macrinus, escapes to the Parthian court, but is captured at Zeugma and also put to death.

summary: Elagabalus reduced the silver content of the Roman denarius to 43 percent.
text: The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 43 percent under the reign of Elagabalus, down from 50 percent under Septimius Severus, as he empties the treasury.

summary: Future Roman Emperor Gallienus was born.
text: Gallienus, Roman emperor (d. 268)

summary: Deposed Roman Emperor Macrinus was executed in Cappadocia.
text: Macrinus, Roman emperor (b. 165)

summary: Diadumenian, co-emperor and son of Macrinus, was executed at Zeugma.
text: Diadumenian, son of Macrinus (b. 208)

summary: Elagabalus and Quintus Tineius Sacerdos became Roman consuls.
text: Imperator Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus (Elagabalus) and Quintus Tineius Sacerdos become Roman Consuls.

summary: Julia Maesa arranged the lavish marriage of Elagabalus to Julia Paula, who was granted the title of Augusta.
text: Julia Maesa arranges, for her grandson Elagabalus, a marriage with Julia Paula. The wedding is a lavish ceremony and Paula is given the honorific title of Augusta.

summary: Elagabalus disbanded Legio III Gallica and Legio IV Scythica after their commanders rebelled.
text: Legions III Gallica and IV Scythica are disbanded by Elagabalus after their leaders, Verus and Gellius Maximus, rebel.

summary: Emperor Elagabalus was initiated into the cult of the Phrygian gods Cybele and Attis.
text: Emperor Elagabalus, age 15, is initiated into the worship of the Phrygian gods Cybele and Attis.

summary: Roman governor and politician Marcus Munatius Sulla Cerialis died.
text: Marcus Munatius Sulla Cerialis, Roman governor and politician

summary: The Goths invaded Roman territories in Asia Minor and the Balkans.
text: The Goths invade Asia Minor and the Balkans.

summary: An Indian delegation visited Roman emperor Elagabalus.
text: An Indian delegation visits the Roman emperor Elagabalus.

summary: A great frost reportedly lasted for five months in Roman Britain.
text: Great frost in Roman Britain is said to have lasted for five months.

summary: Emperor Elagabalus and Publius Valerius Comazon assumed office as Roman consuls.
text: Imperator Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus (Elagabalus) and Publius Valerius Comazon become Roman consuls.

summary: Emperor Elagabalus divorced Julia Paula and caused public outrage by marrying the Vestal Virgin Aquilia Severa.
text: Elagabalus divorces Julia Paula and marries Aquilia Severa, a Vestal Virgin. The wedding causes an enormous controversy – traditionally, the punishment for breaking celibacy is death by being buried alive.

summary: Ardashir I gathered support from Parthian sub-kings and revolted against King Vologases VI.
text: King Ardashir I, founder of the Sassanid dynasty, gains support from some Parthian sub-kings and revolts against the rule of Vologases VI. Ardashir, a grandson of Sasan, had ruled Persis since 208 and six years earlier gained control of the region surrounding Persepolis.

summary: Roman actress, dancer, and singer Bassilla died.
text: Bassilla, Roman actress, dancer and singer (approximate year)

summary: Early Christian author Tertullian died.
text: Tertullian, first Christian author to produce an extensive corpus of Latin Christian literature (b. 155)

summary: Emperor Elagabalus adopted his cousin Severus Alexander as heir and granted him the title of Caesar.
text: Emperor Elagabalus adopts his cousin Alexander Severus as his heir, and receives the title of Caesar.

summary: Emperor Elagabalus divorced Aquilia Severa to marry Annia Faustina, before returning to Severa later the same year.
text: July – Elagabalus is forced to divorce Aquilia Severa, and marries his third wife Annia Faustina. After five months he returns to Severa, and claims that the original divorce is invalid. The marriage is symbolic, because Elagabalus appears to be homosexual or bisexual. According to the historian Cassius Dio, he has a stable relationship with his chariot driver, the slave Hierocles.

summary: The Praetorian Guard assassinated Emperor Elagabalus and his mother Julia Soaemias during a revolt in Rome.
text: Emperor Elagabalus is assassinated, along with his mother, Julia Soaemias, by the Praetorian Guard during a revolt. Their mutilated bodies are dragged through the streets of Rome before being thrown into the Tiber.

summary: Severus Alexander succeeded Elagabalus as Roman emperor under the guidance of his mother Julia Avita Mamaea.
text: Alexander Severus succeeds Elagabalus. He is only 13 years old; his mother, Julia Avita Mamaea, governs the Roman Empire with the help of Domitius Ulpianus and a council composed of 16 senators.

summary: Severus Alexander reduced the silver content of the Roman denarius to thirty-five percent.
text: The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 35 percent under emperor Alexander Severus, down from 43 percent under Elagabalus.

summary: Pope Urban I succeeded Pope Callixtus I after Callixtus was killed by a mob in Trastevere.
text: Pope Callixtus I is killed by a mob in Rome's Trastevere after a 5-year reign in which he has stabilized the Saturday fast three times per year, with no food, oil, or wine to be consumed on those days. Callixtus is succeeded by Cardinal Urban I.

summary: Carus, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Marcus Aurelius Carus, Roman emperor (d. 283)

summary: Roman Emperor Elagabalus died after being assassinated in Rome.
text: Elagabalus, Roman emperor (b. 203)

summary: Julia Soaemias, mother of Elagabalus, died after being assassinated in Rome.
text: Julia Soaemias, mother of Elagabalus (b. 180)

summary: Annia Faustina, Roman noblewoman and empress, died.
text: Annia Faustina, Roman noblewoman and empress

summary: Bardaisan, Syriac scholar and philosopher, died.
text: Bardaisan, Syriac scholar and philosopher (b. 154)

summary: Pope Callixtus I was killed in Rome's Trastevere.
text: Callixtus I, pope of the Catholic Church

summary: Hierocles, favorite and lover of Elagabalus, was executed in Rome.
text: Hierocles, favourite and lover of Elagabalus

summary: Gaius Bellicius Torquatus and Appius Claudius Julianus II began their terms as Roman consuls.
text: Gaius Bellicius Torquatus and Appius Claudius Julianus II begin their one year terms as the new Roman consuls.

summary: Ardashir I defeated Artabanus V at the Battle of Hormozdgan, overthrowing the Parthian Empire and founding the Sasanian Empire.
text: Battle of Hormozdgan: King Ardashir I defeats Artabanus V, destroying the Parthian Empire, and establishing the Sassanid Dynasty. Artabanus V's brother Vologases VI will continue to rule, with Armenian and Kushan support, over outlying parts of Parthia.

summary: Marcus Aurelius Carus was born.
text: Marcus Aurelius Carus, Roman emperor (d. 283)

summary: Mercurius was born.
text: Mercurius, Christian saint and martyr (d. 250)

summary: King Artabanus IV of Parthia died in battle against Ardashir I.
text: Artabanus IV, king of Parthia

summary: Emperor Severus Alexander married Sallustia Orbiana.
text: Emperor Alexander Severus marries Sallustia Orbiana, and possibly raises her father Seius Sallustius to the rank of Caesar.

summary: The first Christian paintings appeared in the catacombs of Rome.
text: The first Christian paintings appear in Rome, decorating the Catacombs.

summary: Gordian III was born.
text: Gordian III, Roman emperor (d. 244)

summary: Lawrence was born.
text: Lawrence, Christian martyr (d. 258)

summary: Gaius Vettius Gratus Sabinianus died.
text: Gaius Vettius Gratus Sabinianus, Roman consul

summary: King Sun Quan of Eastern Wu received the Roman merchant Qin Lun after his arrival in Jiaozhi.
text: A merchant from the Roman Empire, called "Qin Lun" by the Chinese, arrives in Jiaozhi (modern Hanoi), and is taken to see King Sun Quan of Eastern Wu, who requests him to make a report on his native country and people. He is given an escort for the return trip, including a present of ten male and ten female "blackish-colored dwarfs." However, the officer in charge of the Chinese escort dies, and Qin Lun has to continue his journey home alone.

summary: The Sasanian Empire captured Ctesiphon and established it as their capital, ending the Parthian Empire.
text: Ctesiphon, until now capital of the Parthian Empire, falls into the hands of the Sasanian Empire, who also make it their capital, after putting an end to the Parthian Dynasty in Iran.

summary: Saint Valentine was born.
text: Saint Valentine, Roman patron saint (d. 269)

summary: Emperor Severus Alexander executed Seius Sallustius for treason and exiled Sallustia Orbiana to Libya.
text: Seius Sallustius is executed for the attempted murder of his son-in-law, Emperor Alexander Severus. Sallustius' daughter, as well as Alexander's wife, Sallustia Orbiana, is exiled to Libya.

summary: King Ardashir I annexed Chorasmia, Sistan, and Bahrain, and received submission from Turan and the Kushan Empire.
text: King Ardashir I annexes his new empire from the east to the northwest. He conquers, with his army, the provinces of Chorasmia, Sistan and the island Bahrain in the Persian Gulf. The kings of the Kushan Empire and Turan recognize Ardashir as their overlord.

summary: Herennius Etruscus was born.
text: Herennius Etruscus, Roman emperor (d. 251)

summary: Seius Sallustius died.
text: Seius Sallustius, Roman usurper (Caesar)

summary: The Praetorian Guard assassinated the prefect and jurist Ulpian during a riot in Rome.
text: Domitius Ulpianus, a Roman jurist and prefect, is assassinated by the Praetorian Guard, in the presence of Emperor Severus Alexander. His curtailment of the privileges of the palace guard becomes Ulpianus' downfall, who in the course of a riot at Rome is murdered, between the soldiers and the mob.

summary: Ardashir I completed his conquest of Parthia, consolidating the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Ardashir I, four years after establishing the Sassanid Persian Empire, completes his conquest of Parthia.

summary: Paul of Thebes, early Christian hermit, was born.
text: Paul of Thebes, Christian hermit

summary: Domitius Ulpianus, Roman jurist and praetorian prefect, died.
text: Domitius Ulpianus, Roman jurist and prefect (b. 170)

summary: Emperor Severus Alexander and historian Cassius Dio served as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Alexander Severus and Dio Cassius are joint Consuls.

summary: Ammonius Saccas renewed Greek philosophy by developing Neoplatonism in Alexandria.
text: Ammonius Saccas renews Greek philosophy by creating Neoplatonism.

summary: Emperor Severus Alexander made Thessaly a separate province from Macedonia and raised taxes for the Sasanian war.
text: Emperor Alexander Severus decides that Thessaly should be a separate province from Macedonia. He increases taxes, in order to maintain the war against the Sassanids, and strengthen the defenses of the Roman Empire.

summary: Ardashir I invaded Roman Mesopotamia and unsuccessfully besieged Nisibis.
text: King Ardashir I of the Persian Empire invades the Roman province of Mesopotamia, and unsuccessfully besieges the fortress town of Nisibis (Turkey). His army threatens the border outposts of Syria and Cappadocia.

summary: Severus Alexander established Roman military headquarters at Antioch after Persians rejected a diplomatic solution.
text: Alexander Severus assembles the Roman army, and establishes his headquarters at Antioch. He attempts a diplomatic solution, but the Persians decline and choose war.

summary: Pope Pontian succeeded Pope Urban I as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Pontian succeeds Pope Urban I, as the 18th pope of Rome.

summary: Castinus succeeded Ciriacus I as bishop of Byzantium.
text: Patriarch Castinus succeeds Ciriacus I as patriarch Constantinople.

summary: Seventy Christian bishops gathered in council in North Africa.
text: Seventy bishops hold the council of the Christian Church of Africa.

summary: Future Roman emperor Gaius Vibius Volusianus was born.
text: Gaius Vibius Volusianus, Roman emperor (d. 253)

summary: Future Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius Carus was born.
text: Marcus Aurelius Carus, Roman emperor (d. 283)

summary: Pope Urban I, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Urban I, bishop of Rome (b. 175)

summary: Marius Maximus, Roman consul and biographer, died.
text: Marius Maximus, Roman consul and biographer

summary: Emperor Severus Alexander accompanied Julia Mamaea to Syria and campaigned against the Sasanian Empire.
text: Emperor Alexander Severus accompanies his mother Julia Mamaea to Syria, and campaigns against the Persians. Military command rests in the hands of his generals, but his presence gives additional weight to the empire's policy.

summary: Origen was exiled to Caesarea Maritima.
text: Origen, disciple of Ammonius Saccas, founder of Neoplatonism, is exiled in Caesarea.

summary: Severus Alexander launched a counteroffensive against Ardashir I, but the Romans were defeated near Ctesiphon and agreed to a truce.
text: Roman–Persian Wars: Emperor Alexander Severus launches a three-pronged counterattack against the Persian forces of King Ardashir I, who have invaded Mesopotamia. However, the Roman army advancing through Armenia is halted. Alexander gives the order to march to the capital at Ctesiphon, but the Romans are defeated, and withdraw to Syria. The result is an acceptance of the status quo, and after heavy losses on both sides, a truce is signed.

summary: The relics of Thomas the Apostle were brought from India to Edessa.
text: Relics of St. Thomas are brought to Edessa from India.

summary: Origen founded a school of Christian theology in Caesarea Maritima.
text: Origen founds a school of Christian theology in Palestine.

summary: Pope Heraclas of Alexandria became the first Bishop of Alexandria to use the title of Pope.
text: Pope Heraclas of Alexandria is the first Bishop of Alexandria to use the appellation of "Pope".

summary: Future Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius Probus was born.
text: Marcus Aurelius Probus, Roman emperor (d. 282)

summary: Pope Demetrius I of Alexandria died.
text: Demetrius I, patriarch of Alexandria (b. 127)

summary: Bosporan client king Tiberius Julius Sauromates III died.
text: Tiberius Julius Sauromates III, Roman client king

summary: Severus Alexander celebrated a triumph in Rome over the Persians before departing for the Rhine frontier to face invading Alamanni.
text: Emperor Alexander Severus celebrates a triumph in Rome to observe his "victory" the previous year over the Persians (in reality, Severus Alexander advanced towards Ctesiphon in 233, but as corroborated by Herodian, his armies suffered a humiliating defeat against Ardashir I). He is soon summoned to the Rhine frontier, where the Alamanni invade what is now modern-day Swabia. German tribes destroy Roman forts, and plunder the countryside at the Limes Germanicus.

summary: Severus Alexander and Julia Mamaea moved to Moguntiacum, where his decision to negotiate peace with the Alemanni alienated his troops.
text: Emperor Alexander Severus and his mother Julia Mamaea move to Moguntiacum (modern Mainz), the capital of Germania Superior. His generals have planned a military offensive and built a bridge across the Rhine. Alexander prefers to negotiate for peace by buying off the Alemanni. This policy outrages the Roman legions and he loses the trust of the troops.

summary: Porphyry was born in Tyre.
text: Porphyry, Phoenician Neoplatonic philosopher (d. c. 305)

summary: Roman soldiers murdered Emperor Severus Alexander and his mother Julia Avita Mamaea near Mogontiacum and proclaimed Maximinus Thrax emperor.
text: Emperor Severus Alexander and his mother Iulia Mamaea are murdered by their own soldiers. The soldiers proclaim Maximinus Thrax as emperor. The Severan dynasty ends, marking the beginning of the Crisis of the Third Century.

summary: Pope Pontian abdicated after being exiled to the mines of Sardinia alongside Hippolytus of Rome.
text: Pope Pontian resigns, the first to abdicate, because he and Hippolytus, church leader of Rome, are exiled to the mines of Sardinia. Emperor Maximinus persecutes the Christians.

summary: Pope Anterus succeeded Pope Pontian as bishop of Rome.
text: Anterus succeeds Pontian as the nineteenth pope of Rome.

summary: Roman emperor Severus Alexander was murdered near Mogontiacum.
text: Severus Alexander, Roman emperor (b. 208)

summary: Roman historian Cassius Dio died in Bithynia.
text: Cassius Dio, Roman historian

summary: Roman usurper Gaius Petronius Magnus died.
text: Gaius Petronius Magnus, Roman consul and usurper

summary: Theologian Hippolytus died in exile in Sardinia.
text: Hippolytus, Christian theologian and writer (b. 170)

summary: Julia Avita Mamaea was murdered alongside her son Severus Alexander near Mogontiacum.
text: Julia Avita Mamaea, mother of Severus Alexander (b. 180)

summary: Roman client king Tiberius Julius Cotys III died.
text: Tiberius Julius Cotys III (or Kotys), Roman client king

summary: Roman client king Tiberius Julius Rhescuporis IV died.
text: Tiberius Julius Rhescuporis IV, Roman client king

summary: Roman usurper Titius Quartinus was killed.
text: Titius Quartinus, Roman governor and usurper

summary: Maximinus Thrax and Marcus Pupienus Africanus Maximus entered office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperor Maximinus Thrax and Marcus Pupienus Africanus Maximus become Roman consuls.

summary: Emperor Maximinus Thrax campaigned against the Dacians and Sarmatians from Sirmium.
text: Maximinus campaigns against Dacians and Sarmatians from his supply depot at Sirmium.

summary: Fabian succeeded Pope Anterus as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Fabian succeeds Pope Anterus as the twentieth pope.

summary: Pope Fabian divided the administration of Rome into seven deaconships.
text: Fabian separates Rome into seven deaconships.

summary: Pope Fabian dispatched seven missionary bishops to Gaul to evangelize its cities.
text: Fabian sends seven missionaries to Gaul to evangelize in the large cities.

summary: Pope Anterus died in Rome.
text: Anterus, bishop of Rome

summary: Emperor Maximinus Thrax defeated the Alemanni along the Rhine and Danube while facing growing hostility from the senatorial aristocracy in Rome.
text: Emperor Maximinus Thrax campaigns on the rivers Danube and Rhine in Germania, defeating the Alemanni, and never visits Rome. He is accepted by the Roman Senate, but taxes the rich aristocracy heavily, and engenders such hostility among them, that they plot against him. He had a road rebuilt in what is now the Golan Heights, between 236 and 237.

summary: King Ardashir I of Persia renewed his military attacks on the Roman province of Mesopotamia.
text: King Ardashir I of Persia renews his attacks on the Roman province of Mesopotamia.

summary: Eugenius I succeeded Castinus as Bishop of Byzantium.
text: Patriarch Eugenius I succeeds Patriarch Castinus as Patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Saint Babylas became the Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Saint Babylas becomes Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Future bishop Alexander of Constantinople was born.
text: Alexander of Constantinople, patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Future co-emperor Philip II was born.
text: Philip II (the Younger), Roman emperor (d. 249)

summary: Emperor Maximinus Thrax campaigned against the Carpi on the Danube in Moesia.
text: Emperor Maximinus Thrax campaigns against the Carpians on the Danube in Moesia (Balkans). In spite of the payment of a tribute, the Romans fail to persuade the Goths and the Germanic tribes.

summary: Gordian I and his son Gordian II were acclaimed joint Roman emperors in Africa in rebellion against Maximinus Thrax.
text: c. March – Roman subjects in Africa revolt against Maximinus. The elderly Gordian yields to public demand that he succeed Maximinus and rules jointly with his 46-year-old son Gordian II.

summary: Numidian forces and Legio III Augusta defeated Gordian II outside Carthage, prompting Gordian I to commit suicide.
text: c. April – Battle of Carthage: Numidian forces loyal to Maximinus invade Africa with support of Legio III Augusta. Gordian II is killed and after a siege, Gordian I commits suicide by hanging himself with his belt.

summary: The Roman Senate outlawed Maximinus Thrax and elected Pupienus and Balbinus as joint emperors.
text: c. May – The Senate outlaws Maximinus for his bloodthirsty proscriptions in Ancient Rome and nominates two of its members, Pupienus and Balbinus, to the throne.

summary: Soldiers of Legio II Parthica assassinated Emperor Maximinus Thrax and his son Gaius Julius Verus Maximus during the siege of Aquileia.
text: Maximinus advances to the town Aquileia in northern Italy; his army suffers from famine and disease, while the city is besieged. Soldiers of Legio II Parthica kill him in his tent, along with his son Maximus (who is appointed co-emperor). Their corpses are decapitated and their heads carried to Rome.

summary: The Praetorian Guard murdered Pupienus and Balbinus in Rome and acclaimed the young Gordian III as sole emperor.
text: c. August – The Praetorian Guard storms the palace and captures Pupienus and Balbinus. They are dragged naked through the streets of Rome and executed. On the same day Gordian III, age 13, is proclaimed the new emperor. Timesitheus becomes his tutor and advisor.

summary: Valerian was appointed princeps senatus of the Roman Senate.
text: Future Emperor Valerian becomes princeps senatus.

summary: The Colosseum in Rome was restored following fire and earthquake damage.
text: The Colosseum is restored after being damaged.

summary: The Goths crossed the Danube from the north and ravaged Roman territories toward Anatolia.
text: The Goths, coming from Ukraine, cross the Danube and devastate the Roman Empire up to the border with Anatolia.

summary: Legio III Augusta was disbanded in North Africa after its role in defeating Gordian I and Gordian II.
text: In North Africa, Legio III Augusta is dissolved. Until its reconstitution in 253, Africa is defended by auxiliary forces only.

summary: Emperor Gordian III reduced the silver content of the Roman denarius to twenty-eight percent.
text: The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 28 percent under Emperor Gordian III, down from 35 percent under Alexander Severus.

summary: Roman Emperor Gordian I committed suicide at Carthage upon hearing of his son's death in battle.
text: April 12: Gordian I, Roman emperor (b. 159)

summary: Roman Emperor Gordian II was killed fighting loyalist forces near Carthage.
text: April 12: Gordian II, Roman emperor (b. 192)

summary: Roman Emperor Pupienus was murdered in Rome by the Praetorian Guard.
text: July 29: Pupienus, Roman emperor (b. 165)

summary: Roman Emperor Balbinus was assassinated in Rome by the Praetorian Guard.
text: July 29: Balbinus, Roman emperor (b. 178)

summary: Roman Emperor Maximinus Thrax was murdered by his own troops during the siege of Aquileia.
text: Maximinus Thrax, Roman emperor (b. 173)

summary: Co-emperor Gaius Julius Verus Maximus was murdered alongside his father at Aquileia.
text: Maximinus the Younger, Roman emperor

summary: The Roman Senate officially acknowledged Gordian I and Gordian II as emperors of Rome.
text: The Senate accepted Gordian I and Gordian II as rulers of Rome.

summary: The Roman Senate appointed Gordian III as Caesar to placate civil unrest in Rome.
text: Facing popular opposition to Pupienus and Balbinus, the Senate gave Gordian I's young grandson Gordian III the title Caesar.

summary: Origen completed his Hexapla edition of the Old Testament in multiple languages.
text: Origen publishes the Old Testament in five languages .

summary: Franks raided the Roman Rhine frontier while rebellions broke out in Roman Africa.
text: The Roman Empire is threatened on several fronts at the same time. Africa revolts and tribes in northwest Germania, under the name of the Franks, are raiding the Rhine frontier.

summary: Shapur I was crowned co-ruler of the Sasanian Empire alongside his father Ardashir I.
text: Prince Shapur I becomes co-ruler of the Sasanian Empire with his father King Ardashir I.

summary: Sasanian forces laid siege to the allied Roman buffer city of Hatra.
text: Siege of Hatra: The Sasanians besiege the capital of the Kingdom of Hatra ruled by Sanatruq II.

summary: Mani proclaimed himself a prophet at the court of Ardashir I and began preaching Manichaeism across the Sasanian Empire.
text: Mani, a young mystic of Ctesiphon, proclaims himself a prophet at the court of Ardashir I. He preaches his doctrine, Manichaeism, throughout the Sassanid Empire.

summary: Christian theologian Lucian of Antioch was born.
text: Lucian of Antioch, Syrian theologian and martyr (d. 312)

summary: Sporus of Nicaea, the Greek mathematician, was born.
text: Sporus of Nicaea, Greek mathematician

summary: Zenobia, future queen of the Palmyrene Empire, was born.
text: Zenobia, queen of the Palmyrene Empire (d. 274)

summary: The Neoplatonic philosopher Ammonius Saccas died.
text: Ammonius Saccas, Neoplatonic philosopher

summary: The Roman historian and civil servant Herodian died.
text: Herodian of Antioch, Roman historian and writer (b. 170)

summary: Emperor Gordian III arrived in Antioch with his army to prepare an offensive against the Sasanian Empire.
text: Winter – Emperor Gordian III reaches Antioch and, with his army, prepares an offensive against the Sassanids.

summary: Gaius Furius Sabinius Aquila Timesitheus became praetorian prefect and the de facto ruler of the Roman Empire.
text: Gaius Furius Sabinius Aquila Timesitheus becomes praetorian prefect and de facto ruler of the Roman Empire.

summary: Shapur I succeeded his father Ardashir I as ruler of the Sasanian Empire.
text: Prince Shapur I succeeds his father Ardashir I as ruler of the Sassanid Empire. He begins his expansion in India.

summary: Shapur I captured and destroyed Hatra, ending the Kingdom of Hatra.
text: Fall of Hatra: Shapur I captures Hatra, the capital of the Kingdom of Hatra. The city is destroyed by the Sassanids.

summary: A domestic house in Dura-Europos was converted into a Christian house church.
text: The Dura-Europos church is converted from a house in Syria .

summary: Sanatruq II, the last king of Hatra, died during the fall of his kingdom.
text: Sanatruq II, king of Hatra (Ending of the Kingdom of Hatra)

summary: Emperor Gordian III launched a campaign against Shapur I, securing Roman victories at Antioch, Carrhae, Nisibis, and Resaina.
text: Emperor Gordian III begins a campaign against King Shapur I, and leads victories at Antioch, Carrhae, Nisibis, and Resaina.

summary: Gordian III evacuated Roman garrisons from the Cimmerian cities in the Bosporus as the region came under Gothic control.
text: Gordian III evacuates the Cimmerian cities in the Bosphorus (Crimea), as the territory is now controlled by the Goths.

summary: Timesitheus led a Roman army to defeat the Sasanians at Carrhae and Nisibis after Shapur I attacked Antioch.
text: Shapur I makes a pre-emptive attack on Antioch to drive out the Romans. Gordian's father-in-law, Timesitheus, leads a Roman army to defeat the Sassanids at Carrhae and Nisibis.

summary: Ardashir I, founder of the Sasanian Empire, died and was succeeded by his son Shapur I.
text: King Ardashir I, founder of the Sassanid Empire, dies after a 30-year reign. He is succeeded by his son and co-ruler Shapur I.

summary: Titus succeeded Eugenius I as bishop of Byzantium.
text: Patriarch Titus succeeds Eugenius I as Patriarch of Constantinople (until 272).

summary: Saloninus, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Saloninus, Roman emperor (d. 260)

summary: The philosopher Ammonius Saccas died in Alexandria.
text: Ammonius Saccas, Egyptian philosopher (b. 175)

summary: Ardashir I, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Ardashir I, king of the Sassanid Empire (b. 180)

summary: Timesitheus defeated the Sasanians at the Battle of Resaena, compelling Shapur I to retreat toward the Euphrates.
text: Battle of Resaena: A Roman army under Timesitheus defeats the Sassanids at Resaena (modern Syria); King Shapur I is forced to flee to the Euphrates.

summary: Timesitheus died of illness, prompting Shapur I to withdraw back into Sasanian territory.
text: Timesitheus becomes ill and dies under suspicious circumstances. Shapur I retreats to the Sassanid Empire, giving up all the territories he has conquered.

summary: Emperor Gordian III appointed Philip the Arab as praetorian prefect following the death of Timesitheus.
text: Emperor Gordian III appoints Philip the Arab as his new praetorian prefect (after the death of Timesitheus) and proceeds with his campaign in Mesopotamia.

summary: Cohors I Germanorum Civium Romanorum replaced Cohors I Ubiorum as the garrison at Capidava in Scythia Minor.
text: Cohors I Ubiorum, the garrison at Capidava in Scythia Minor, is replaced by Cohors I Germanorum Civium Romanorum, until the end of the 3rd century AD.

summary: Timesitheus, praetorian prefect of Rome, died during the campaign in the East.
text: Timesitheus, Roman advisor and praetorian prefect (b. 190)

summary: Emperor Gordian III was murdered by mutinous Roman soldiers at Zaitha in Mesopotamia.
text: Emperor Gordian III is murdered by mutinous soldiers in Zaitha (Mesopotamia). A mound is raised at Carchemish in his memory.

summary: Philip the Arab proclaimed himself emperor and concluded peace with the Sasanian Empire, ceding Armenia and paying 500,000 gold pieces.
text: Philip the Arab (Marcus Julius Philippus) declares himself co-emperor, and makes a controversial peace with the Sassanian Empire, withdrawing from their territory and giving Shapur 500,000 gold pieces. The Sassanians occupy Armenia.

summary: The Roman Senate recognized Philip the Arab as emperor, while he made his son Caesar, appointed his brother rector Orientis, and began building Shahba.
text: Philip the Arab is recognized by the Roman Senate as the new Roman Emperor with the honorific Augustus. He nominates his son Philippus, age 6, with the title of Caesar and makes him heir to the throne; gives his brother Priscus supreme power (rector Orientis) in the Eastern provinces; and begins construction of the city of Shahba (Syria) in the province of his birth.

summary: The Roman Empire absorbed the vassal kingdom of Osroene, ending the reign of Abgar XI Farhat Bar Manu.
text: The vassal Upper Mesopotamian kingdom of Osroene is absorbed into the Roman Empire, its last ruler being Abgar (XI) Farhat Bar Ma’nu.

summary: Plotinus escaped the bloodshed following the murder of Gordian III and fled to Antioch before returning to Rome.
text: Plotinus, Greek philosopher, escapes the bloodshed that accompanies the murder of Gordianus III and makes his way to Antioch. Back in Rome he founds his Neoplatonist school and attracts disciples like Porphyry, Castricius Firmus and Eustochius of Alexandria.

summary: A marble bust of Emperor Philip the Arab was sculpted.
text: 244–249 – Bust of Philip the Arab (in Braccio Nuovo, Vatican Museums, Rome).

summary: Emperor Philip the Arab debased the Roman denarius, reducing its silver content to 0.5 percent.
text: The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 0.5 percent under emperor Philippus I, down from 28 percent under Gordian III.

summary: The final phase of construction and wall-painting was carried out on the Dura-Europos synagogue.
text: 244–245 – Last phase of construction of the house-style Dura-Europos synagogue in Syria, one of the oldest to survive (wall-paintings in the National Museum of Damascus, Syria).

summary: Diocletian, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Diocletian, Roman emperor (d. 311)

summary: Alexander of Constantinople, future bishop of Byzantium, was born.
text: Alexander of Constantinople, bishop of Byzantium

summary: Roman Emperor Gordian III died during his campaign in Mesopotamia.
text: Gordian III, Roman emperor (b. 225)

summary: The Sasanian Empire defeated a Roman force at the Battle of Misiche, where Gordian III was killed and succeeded by Philip the Arab.
text: Battle of Misiche: The Sasanian Empire decisively defeated a Roman force at Misiche, near modern Fallujah. Gordian III was killed, probably by a fellow Roman. He was succeeded by Philip the Arab, the prefect of the Praetorian Guard, who was forced to cede Mesopotamia and Armenia to the Sasanian Empire.

summary: Emperor Philip the Arab entrusted Decius with a major military command on the Danube.
text: Emperor Philip the Arab entrusts Trajan Decius with an important command on the Danube.

summary: A massive flood inundated thousands of acres in Lincolnshire in Roman Britain.
text: In Britain, many thousands of acres of modern-day Lincolnshire are inundated by a great flood.

summary: The philosopher Plotinus took up residence in Rome.
text: The philosopher Plotinus goes to live in Rome.

summary: Iamblichus, Syrian Neoplatonist philosopher, was born.
text: Iamblichus, Syrian Neoplatonist philosopher

summary: Diocletian, future Roman emperor, was born.
text: Diocletian, Roman emperor

summary: Ammonius Saccas, Alexandrian philosopher, died.
text: Ammonius Saccas, Alexandrian-Greek philosopher

summary: Emperor Philip the Arab campaigned against Germanic tribes along the Danube River.
text: Emperor Philip the Arab fights the Germans along the Danube River.

summary: The first Council of Arabia in the Christian Church was convened in Bostra.
text: The first of two Councils of Arabia in the Roman Christian Church is held in Bostra, Arabia Petraea.

summary: Rome commemorated the 1,000th anniversary of its founding with the celebration of the Secular Games across the empire.
text: Rome becomes 1,000 years old. The 1,000th anniversary is commemorated with the Ludi Saeculares festivals, celebrated throughout the Roman Empire.

summary: Emperor Philip the Arab and his son Philip II served together as Roman consuls.
text: Marcus Julius Philippus Augustus and his 10-year-old son Marcus Julius Philippus Caesar become Roman Consuls.

summary: The Goths appeared along the lower Danube frontier and invaded Ukraine and Romania.
text: The Goths appear on the lower Danube frontier; they invade Ukraine and Romania.

summary: Emperor Philip the Arab marked Rome's millennium by staging the Secular Games.
text: Emperor Philip the Arab marks the millennium of Rome by holding the Ludi Saeculares.

summary: The second Council of Arabia was held in Bostra.
text: The last of the two Councils of Arabia in the Roman Christian Church is held in Bostra, Arabia Petraea.

summary: Prisca, future Roman empress and wife of Diocletian, was born.
text: Prisca, Roman empress and wife of Diocletian (d. 315)

summary: Trajan Decius put down the revolts of Pacatianus in Moesia and Jotapianus in Syria on orders from Emperor Philip the Arab.
text: The revolts of Pacatianus in Moesia and Iotapianus in Syria are put down by Senator Trajan Decius, by order of Emperor Philip the Arab.

summary: Philip the Arab organized the Secular Games in Rome to celebrate the city's 1,000th anniversary.
text: The Roman Empire continues the celebration of the 1,000th anniversary of Rome, with the ludi saeculares, organized by Philip the Arab.

summary: Origen wrote an eight-volume treatise criticizing the pagan philosopher Celsus.
text: Origen writes an eight-volume work, criticizing the pagan writer Celsus.

summary: Helena, future Roman empress and mother of Constantine the Great, was born.
text: Flavia Iulia Helena, Greco-Roman Augusta (empress), mother of Constantine I (d. 330)

summary: Trajan Decius put down revolts in Moesia and Pannonia, was proclaimed emperor by his legionaries, and marched into Italy.
text: Trajan Decius puts down a revolt in Moesia and Pannonia. Loyal legionaries proclaim him emperor, and he leads them into Italy.

summary: Decius initiated an empire-wide persecution targeting Christians and others who refused to sacrifice to the Roman gods.
text: Decian persecution: Decius begins persecuting Christians, and others refusing to sacrifice publicly to the Roman gods for the well-being of the emperor.

summary: Cyprian became bishop of Carthage.
text: Cyprian, Christian writer of Berber descent, becomes bishop of Carthage.

summary: The populace of Alexandria rioted and pillaged the homes of local Christians.
text: In Alexandria, the populace pillages the homes of Christians.

summary: Roman usurper Jotapianus was killed by his own soldiers.
text: Jotapianus (or Jotapian), Roman usurper

summary: Young Roman co-emperor Philip II was murdered by the Praetorian Guard.
text: Philip II (the Younger), Roman emperor (b. 237)

summary: Roman emperor Philip the Arab died in battle against Decius near Verona.
text: Philip the Arab, Roman general and emperor (b. 204)

summary: Decius defeated and killed Emperor Philip the Arab in battle at Verona.
text: Phillip was killed at Verona in battle with Decius, commander of Roman forces in Pannonia and Moesia.

summary: A raiding group of Franks penetrated as far as Tarragona in Roman Spain.
text: A group of Franks penetrate as far as Tarragona in Spain .

summary: King Cniva led the Goths across the Danube to invade Moesia and besiege Novae and Marcianopolis.
text: The Goths under King Cniva invade Moesia. They cross the Danube and lay siege to Novae and Marcianopolis.

summary: The Goths defeated the Roman army at the Battle of Augusta Traiana.
text: Battle of Augusta Traiana: The Romans lose the battle against the Goths.

summary: King Cniva besieged and conquered Philippopolis, slaughtering its inhabitants.
text: Cniva lays siege to Philippopolis (modern Plovdiv). After a long resistance, Cniva conquers the city and slays its one hundred thousand inhabitants.

summary: The Alamanni drove Roman forces from the region of Donau-Ries.
text: The Alamanni drive the Romans from the modern area of Donau-Ries.

summary: An epidemic known as the Plague of Cyprian originated in Ethiopia and spread across Egypt, North Africa, and the Roman Empire.
text: An epidemic begins in Ethiopia, moves into Egypt and the Roman colonies in North Africa, and spreads through the Roman Empire (named the Plague of Cyprian, after St. Cyprian, bishop of Carthage).

summary: Diophantus wrote Arithmetica, establishing the first systematic treatise on algebra.
text: Diophantus writes Arithmetica, the first systematic treatise on algebra.

summary: The gold-glass family portrait medallion known as the Family of Vunnerius Keramus was produced.
text: The family portrait medallion, traditionally called the Family of Vunnerius Keramus, is made (it is later placed in the Brescia Cross, and then in the Museo Civico dell'Etá Cristiana, Brescia).

summary: The Ludovisi Battle sarcophagus was sculpted depicting a battle between Romans and barbarians.
text: The Ludovisi Battle sarcophagus, depicting battle between the Romans and the Barbarians, is made for use in Rome (it is later moved to the collection of the National Roman Museum).

summary: The Igel Column monument was erected near Trier.
text: The Igel Column is erected at Trier in Germany.

summary: Emperor Decius initiated an empire-wide persecution of Christians, leading to the martyrdom of Pope Fabian.
text: Decian persecution of Christians is initiated when Emperor Decius orders everyone in the Roman Empire (except Jews) to perform a sacrifice to the gods of religion in ancient Rome. On January 20, Pope Fabian becomes one of the first martyrs of this persecution.

summary: Denis, bishop of Paris, was martyred by beheading.
text: Possible date – Denis, a bishop of Paris, is martyred by beheading.

summary: Future Roman emperor Constantius Chlorus was born.
text: Constantius Chlorus, Roman emperor (d. 306)

summary: Future Roman emperor Galerius was born in Moesia.
text: Gaius Galerius Valerius Maximianus, Roman emperor (d. 311)

summary: Future Roman emperor Maximian was born near Sirmium.
text: Maximian (Herculius), Roman consul and emperor (d. 310)

summary: Pope Fabian was martyred in Rome.
text: Fabian (or Fabianus), pope of Rome and martyr

actor: Faustus, Abibus and Dionysius of Alexandria
summary: Faustus, Abibus, and Dionysius suffered martyrdom in Alexandria.
text: Faustus, Abibus and Dionysius, Christian martyrs
cast: Faustus, Abibus and Dionysius of Alexandria
names: Faustus, Abibus and Dionysius of Alexandria

summary: Roman Christian apologist and writer Marcus Minucius Felix died.
text: Marcus Minucius Felix, Roman apologist and writer

summary: Christian martyrs Peter, Andrew, Paul, and Denise were executed for their faith.
text: Peter, Andrew, Paul and Denise, Christian martyrs

summary: Secundian, Marcellian, and Verian were martyred near Civitavecchia.
text: Secundian, Marcellian and Verian, Christian martyrs

summary: Christian martyrs Tryphon, Respicius, and Nympha died during the Decian persecution.
text: Tryphon, Respicius, and Nympha, Christian martyrs

summary: Saint Cyprian presided over the first Synod of Carthage.
text: May – The first Synod of Carthage, a pre-ecumenical council, is held under the presidency of Saint Cyprian.

summary: Franks and Saxons conducted raids against the southeastern coast of Roman Britain.
text: The prosperity of Roman Britain declines during this period, as the Germanic tribes of the Franks and Saxons, whose homelands are in Friesland and the Low Countries, make raids around the southeast coast.

summary: Emperor Trebonianus Gallus made peace with the Goths, allowing them to keep their plunder and offering them tributes.
text: Gallus makes peace with the Goths; he permits them to keep their plunder, and offers them a bribe not to return.

summary: The Plague of Cyprian began a fifteen-year outbreak across the Roman Empire.
text: A 15-year plague begins in the Roman Empire.

summary: Sasanian King Shapur I ordered an invasion of Roman Syria to capture Antioch.
text: Sassanid King Shapur I orders an invasion of Syria, with the intent of finally capturing the city of Antioch during the campaign of 251–254.

summary: Pope Cornelius succeeded Pope Fabian as Bishop of Rome.
text: March – Pope Cornelius succeeds Pope Fabian as the 21st pope.

summary: Christian monk and desert father Anthony the Great was born.
text: Anthony the Great, Christian monk and saint (d. 356)

summary: Roman Emperor Decius was killed in the aftermath of the Battle of Abritus.
text: Decius, Roman emperor (killed after the battle of Abritus)

summary: Roman Emperor Herennius Etruscus was killed at the Battle of Abritus.
text: Herennius Etruscus, Roman emperor and son of Decius

summary: Agatha of Sicily was martyred during the Decian persecution.
text: Agatha of Sicily, Christian martyr and saint

summary: Decius appointed his son Herennius Etruscus as co-emperor of Rome.
text: Decius appointed his natural son Herennius Etruscus co-ruler of Rome jointly with himself.

summary: The Goths defeated Roman forces at the Battle of Abritus, killing Decius and Herennius Etruscus.
text: Battle of Abritus: Roman forces were dealt a bloody defeat by the Goths near modern Razgrad. Decius and Herennius were killed.

summary: Roman legions along the Danube acclaimed Trebonianus Gallus as emperor of Rome.
