text: The armies of the Danube region acclaimed their commander Trebonianus Gallus ruler of Rome.

summary: Roman Emperor Hostilian died in Rome during the Plague of Cyprian.
text: Plague of Cyprian: Hostilian died, probably of plague.

summary: Trebonianus Gallus appointed his son Volusianus as co-emperor of Rome.
text: Gallus appointed his natural son Volusianus co-ruler jointly with himself.

summary: King Shapur I defeated the Roman army at the Battle of Barbalissos in Syria.
text: Battle of Barbalissos: King Shapur I defeats the Roman army (some 70,000 men) at Barbalissos in Syria .

summary: Shapur I invaded Armenia and installed Artavasdes V as king.
text: Shapur I invades Armenia, and appoints Artavazd VI as the new Armenian king.

summary: Emperor Trebonianus Gallus exiled Pope Cornelius to Centumcellae.
text: Pope Cornelius is exiled to Centumcellae, by Emperor Trebonianus Gallus.

summary: Roman general and martyr Eusignius of Antioch was born.
text: Eusignius of Antioch, Roman general and martyr (d. 362)

summary: Tiridates II, Roman client king of Armenia, died.
text: Tiridates II (or Khosrov), Roman client king of Armenia

summary: Roman legions on the Danube proclaimed Marcus Aemilius Aemilianus emperor, prompting his advance on Rome along the Via Flaminia.
text: The legions who have campaigned against the Goths on the Danube elect Marcus Aemilius Aemilianus as new emperor. He advances on Rome along the Flaminian Way, to meet his opponent emperor Trebonianus Gallus and his son Volusianus. For the most part, generals in the border regions are proclaimed emperor by their armies to halt the invasion of Germanic tribes.

summary: The Roman Senate proclaimed Aemilianus an enemy of the state, after which Trebonianus Gallus was defeated at Interamna Nahars and killed at Foligno.
text: Aemilianus is proclaimed "enemy of the State" by the Roman Senate. Trebonianus Gallus is defeated at Interamna Nahars (Umbria); he flees with Volusianus to the north, but at Foligno they are killed by their own troops.

summary: Aemilianus ruled the Roman Empire for three months and received the title Pontifex Maximus from the Senate.
text: Aemilianus rules the Roman Empire for three months; he promises to fight in Thrace and goes to war against Persia. The Senate gives him the rank of Pontifex Maximus.

summary: Following the murder of Aemilianus at Spoletium, Rhine legions proclaimed Valerian emperor, who then named Gallienus co-Augustus.
text: Aemilianus is murdered at Spoletium and Publius Valerianus, age 60, is recognised as the new emperor by the Rhine legions. He gives his son Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus the title Augustus. Valerianus I dispatches him to the Danube where the Goths have violated the treaty signed with Rome and invaded Moesia.

summary: Valerian divided rule of the Roman Empire, assigning Gallienus the West while taking control of the East.
text: Valerianus I splits the Roman Empire in two; Gallienus taking control of the West and his father ruling the East, where he faces the Persian threat.

summary: Shapur I defeated a Roman field army at the Battle of Barbalissos in Syria.
text: Battle of Barbalissos: King Shapur I, defeats a Roman field army at Barbalissos in Syria.

summary: Valerian reformed Legio III Augusta to combat a coalition of Berber tribes in Roman Africa.
text: Valerian reforms Legio III Augusta to fight the "five peoples", a dangerous coalition of Berber tribes in Africa.

summary: Pope Cornelius was sent into exile.
text: Pope Cornelius is sent into exile.

summary: Pope Lucius I succeeded Pope Cornelius as the bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Lucius I succeeds Pope Cornelius as the 22nd pope.

summary: Pope Lucius I was arrested shortly after his election and sent into exile.
text: Lucius is arrested almost immediately following his election and also exiled.

summary: Roman Emperor Aemilianus was assassinated at Spoletium.
text: Aemilianus, Roman emperor

summary: Pope Cornelius died in exile at Centumcellae.
text: Pope Cornelius

summary: Babylas, Patriarch of Antioch, died in prison during the Decian persecution.
text: Saint Babylas, Patriarch of Antioch

summary: Roman Emperor Trebonianus Gallus was killed by his own troops at Interamna.
text: Trebonianus Gallus, Roman emperor

summary: Roman co-emperor Volusianus was slain alongside his father at Interamna.
text: Volusianus, Roman emperor

summary: The Christian scholar Origen died at Tyre.
text: Origen, a Christian scholar from Alexandria (b. c. 184)

summary: Germanic confederations, Goths, and the Sasanian Empire threatened multiple frontiers of the Roman Empire.
text: The Roman Empire is threatened by several peoples on their borders: the Germanic confederations, such as the Franks on the Middle Rhine, the Alemanni on the upper Rhine and Danube, and the Marcomanni facing the provinces at Noricum and Raetia. On land the confederation of Goths threaten the lower Danube provinces, and on the sea they threaten the shores of Thracia, Bithynia et Pontus, and Cappadocia. In the eastern provinces, the Sassanid Persians had the previous year defeated a Roman field army at Barballisos, and afterwards plundered the defenseless provinces. This period of time is called today the Crisis of the Third Century.

summary: Pope Stephen I succeeded Pope Lucius I as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Stephen I succeeds Pope Lucius I.

summary: Pope Lucius I, bishop of Rome, died at Rome.
text: Lucius I, bishop of Rome

summary: Tiberius Julius Pharsanzes, Roman client king of the Bosporan Kingdom, died.
text: Tiberius Julius Pharsanzes, Roman client king

summary: Pope Marcellus I was born.
text: Marcellus I, bishop of Rome (d. 309)

summary: Dorotheus of Tyre, Syrian bishop and martyr, was born.
text: Dorotheus of Tyre, Syrian bishop and martyr (d. 362)

summary: Saint Helena, Roman empress and mother of Constantine the Great, was born at Drepanum.
text: Saint Helena, Roman empress who was the reputed discoverer of Christ’s cross and mother of Emperor Constantine (d. 318)

summary: Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 3035, an arrest warrant for a Christian, was written at Oxyrhynchus.
text: Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 3035, a warrant for the arrest of a Christian, is written.

summary: The Goths invaded Asia Minor, besieged Thessalonica, and drove Rome from Dacia.
text: The Goths invade Asia Minor. Dacia is lost for the Roman Empire, and the Goths appear at the walls of Thessalonica.

summary: The Alemanni reached Mediolanum after Franks crossed the Rhine.
text: The Franks cross the Rhine; the Alemanni reach Mediolanum (Milan) (disputed date).

summary: Berbers massacred Roman colonists in the province of Africa.
text: In Africa, the Berbers massacre Roman colonists.

summary: King Shapur I of the Sasanian Empire invaded Syria and Mesopotamia, sacking Antioch, Dura-Europos, and Zeugma.
text: King Shapur I of the Sasanian Empire invades Mesopotamia and Syria. He conquers and plunders Antioch, destroys Dura-Europos, and sacks the Anatolian city of Zeugma on the Euphrates. A devastating fire and an earthquake soon follow, causing Zeugma to be abandoned.

summary: Aurelian inspected defenses along the Rhine as Roman cities began constructing defensive walls.
text: Cities in the Roman Empire begin to build walls, as the defense of the frontiers begins to crumble; future emperor Aurelian inspects along the Rhine.

summary: A devastating pandemic struck Pontus and Alexandria, causing immense loss of life.
text: The great pandemic of the Roman world strikes violently in Pontus on the Black Sea, and causes enormous loss of life in Alexandria, encouraging thousands to embrace Christianity.

summary: Roman Emperor Valerian began persecuting Christians across the empire.
text: Emperor Valerian persecutes Christians.

summary: Pope Stephen I threatened Cyprian of Carthage with excommunication over the rebaptism of heretics.
text: Pope Stephen I threatens to excommunicate Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, and other bishops in Africa and Asia Minor, unless they stop rebaptizing heretics. Cyprian attacks the Pope in a treatise that gains support from the Council of Carthage. He sends envoys to Rome, raising the specter of a schism between the Roman and Carthaginian Churches.

summary: A synod was held in Carthage to address church matters.
text: A Synod of Carthage is held.

summary: The Christian priest and theologian Arius was born in Egypt.
text: Arius, Egyptian priest and founder of Arianism (d. 336)

summary: Emperor Gallienus campaigned to restore order along the Danube frontier.
text: Emperor Gallienus brings some order to the Danube area.

summary: Aurelian defeated the Goths and brought numerous captives back to Rome.
text: Future emperor Aurelian defeats the Goths and brings many prisoners back to Rome.

summary: The Romans abandoned the Upper Raetian Limes along the river Iller in Bavaria.
text: In Bavaria the Limes Germanicus (Upper Raetian Limes) along the river Iller is abandoned by the Romans.

summary: Valerian II was established at Sirmium under the guardianship of Ingenuus to represent the imperial authority in Illyricum.
text: Valerian, under guardianship of Ingenuus, is established at Sirmium (Pannonia) to represent the Roman government in the troubled Illyrian provinces.

summary: Emperor Valerian recovered Antioch from King Shapur I of Persia.
text: Emperor Valerian recovers Antioch, Syria from King Shapur I of Persia.

summary: The Goths constructed a naval fleet on the Black Sea.
text: The Goths build a fleet on the Black Sea.

summary: The Goths split into two distinct groups, the Ostrogoths and the Visigoths.
text: The Goths separate into the Ostrogoths and the Visigoths.

summary: Sixtus II succeeded Stephen I as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Sixtus II succeeds Pope Stephen I as the 24th pope.

summary: Emperor Valerian issued an edict compelling Christian clergy to perform pagan sacrifices and banning assemblies at cemeteries.
text: Valerian's persecution of Christians begins: his edict orders bishops and priests to sacrifice according to the pagan rituals, and prohibits Christians, under penalty of death, from meeting at the tombs of their deceased.

summary: Gregory the Illuminator, future patron saint and first head of the Armenian Church, was born.
text: Gregory the Illuminator, Armenian religious leader

summary: Pope Stephen I, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Stephen I, bishop of Rome

summary: The Goths raided Anatolia and sacked Trapezus.
text: The Goths ravage Asia Minor and Trapezus.

summary: The silver purity of the Roman denarius dropped below ten percent, worsening economic hardship across the empire.
text: The amount of silver in the Roman currency of the denarius falls below 10%. The crisis ruins craftsmen, tradesmen, and small farmers, who are forced into bartering; landowners grow richer by buying up cheap land.

summary: Following the death of Valerian II in Pannonia, Emperor Valerian elevated his grandson Saloninus to the rank of Caesar.
text: Valerian II, eldest son of Gallienus, dies, possibly murdered by Pannonia's governor Ingenuus; Emperor Valerian bestows on another one of Gallienus's sons, Saloninus, the title of Caesar.

summary: Emperor Valerian issued a severe second edict ordering the execution of Christian clergy and confiscation of property from Christian elites.
text: A second Imperial edict prohibits Christianity in the Roman Empire. This edict divides Christians into four categories: priests, who are to be put to death; senators and equestrians, who are to be stripped of their positions and their property confiscated; nuns, who are to be exiled; and imperial civil servants, who are condemned to forced labour.

summary: Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, was beheaded during the Valerian persecution.
text: Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, is martyred (decapitation).

summary: Pope Sixtus II was martyred in Rome under Emperor Valerian's persecution.
text: Pope Sixtus II, bishop of Rome, is martyred.

summary: Christian bishop and martyr Clement of Ancyra was born.
text: Clement of Ancyra, Christian bishop and martyr (d. 312)

summary: Pope Sixtus II died a martyr in Rome.
text: Sixtus II, bishop of Rome

summary: Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, died a martyr.
text: Cyprian, bishop of Carthage

summary: Parthian nobleman Anak the Parthian died.
text: Anak the Parthian, Parthian nobleman

summary: Theologian and antipope Novatian died.
text: Novatian, Italian antipope and theologian

summary: Valerian II, son of Gallienus and Caesar of the Roman Empire, died in Pannonia.
text: Valerian II, son of co-emperor Gallienus

summary: Emperor Valerian led an army to relieve Edessa from Persian siege, but an outbreak of plague weakened the Roman troops.
text: Emperor Valerian leads an army (70,000 men) to relieve Edessa, besieged by the forces of Persian King Shapur I. An outbreak of a plague kills many legionaries, weakening the Roman position in Syria.

summary: Roman legions under Gallienus defeated the Alamanni near Mediolanum.
text: Battle of Mediolanum: A Germanic confederation, the Alamanni (300,000 warriors), who crossed the Alps, are defeated by Roman legions under Gallienus, near Mediolanum (modern Milan).

summary: Postumus revolted against Gallienus in Gaul, establishing the Gallic Empire with the support of Britain and Spain.
text: Postumus revolts against Gallienus in Gaul. The western provinces of Britain and Spain join his independent realm–which is called in modern times the Gallic Empire.

summary: Postumus declared himself Emperor and began his rule over the Gallic Empire.
text: Postumus, governor of Gaul, declares himself Emperor, and continues to rule the Gallic Empire until 269, when he is killed by his soldiers.

summary: The Alamanni captured the Roman fort of Wiesbaden.
text: The Roman fort of Wiesbaden (Germany) is captured by the Alamanni (possibly 260).

summary: Franks raiding into the Roman Empire reached Tarraco in Hispania.
text: The Franks, who invaded the Roman Empire near Cologne in 257, reach Tarraco in Hispania.

summary: Odaenathus of Palmyra sacked the city of Nehardea, destroying its yeshiva.
text: Mesopotamia: Odaenathus, the ruler of the kingdom of Palmyra, sacks the city of Nehardea, destroying its great yeshiva.

summary: Pope Dionysius was elected as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Dionysius is elected as the pope.

summary: Polyeuctus, Roman soldier and Christian martyr, died.
text: Polyeuctus, Roman soldier and saint

summary: Augurius of Tarragona, Christian Hispano-Roman clergyman, was martyred.
text: Augurius of Tarragona, Christian Hispano-Roman clergyman

summary: Fructuosus of Tarragona, Christian bishop and martyr, was burned at the stake.
text: Fructuosus of Tarragona, Christian bishop, martyr and saint

summary: Shapur I defeated the Roman army at Edessa and captured Emperor Valerian.
text: Battle of Edessa: With a large army, said to number 70,000 men, Valerian attempts to drive the Persians back from Edessa. The Roman army is surrounded and most of its troops are killed or captured. Valerian is taken prisoner for the remainder of his life.

summary: Shapur I sent Valerian to Bishapur and used captured Roman soldiers to construct the Band-e Kaisar.
text: King Shapur I sends Valerian to Bishapur and uses the captured Roman army for engineering plans. They construct the Band-e Kaisar ("Bridge of Valerian").

summary: Gallienus became sole Roman Emperor after the capture of Valerian, as Ingenuus revolted on the Danube.
text: Gallienus becomes the sole emperor of Rome; during his reign the Pannonian governor Ingenuus revolts on the Danube.

summary: Gallienus evacuated the Roman fortifications in the Agri Decumates in the face of invading Alamanni.
text: Gallienus evacuates the fortifications (limes) in the Agri Decumates (Germania Superior), covering the Black Forest area in the face of invading Alamanni.

summary: Gallienus established his headquarters at Mediolanum and reorganized the Roman army with elite cavalry.
text: Gallienus establishes himself at Mediolanum (modern Milan); he reorganizes the army, supported by elite cavalry, and dispatches troops to the Rhine frontier.

summary: Postumus formed the Gallic Empire and defended the Rhine frontier against Germanic tribes.
text: Postumus, Roman usurper, forms the Gallic Empire and protects the Rhine against an invasion of Germanic tribes.

summary: Postumus besieged Cologne, where Saloninus was proclaimed Augustus alongside praetorian prefect Silvanus.
text: Saloninus, son of Gallienus, is proclaimed Augustus by his troops. Postumus besieges Cologne, where Silvanus is praetorian prefect and Roman ruler of Gaul.

summary: Postumus executed Saloninus and Silvanus after capturing Cologne and established his capital at Trier.
text: Postumus executes Saloninus and his adviser Silvanus after breaching the walls of Cologne. He is recognized as emperor and establishes his capital at Trier.

summary: Postumus won control of the Roman provinces west of the Alps, including Gaul, Britain, and Hispania.
text: Postumus wins over all the Roman provinces west of the Alps, including Gaul, Britain and Hispania.

summary: The Alamanni captured the Roman fort of Wiesbaden.
text: The Roman fort of Wiesbaden (Germany) is captured by the Alamanni.

summary: The Franks took control of the Scheldt estuary.
text: The Franks take control over the Scheldt estuary .

summary: King Shapur I destroyed Caesarea Mazaca in Cappadocia.
text: Persian king Shapur I destroys Caesarea Mazaca in Asia Minor.

summary: Pope Dionysius convened a synod at Rome concerning the theological views of bishop Dionysius of Alexandria.
text: Pope Dionysius convenes a synod at Rome to demand an explanation from bishop Dionysius of Alexandria, who has been charged with separating the members of the Trinity as three distinct deities.

summary: Paul of Samosata became Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Paul of Samosata becomes Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Eusebius of Caesarea, Greek Christian historian and bishop, was born.
text: Eusebius of Caesarea, Greek bishop and historian

summary: Saloninus, Roman emperor and son of Gallienus, was executed at Cologne.
text: Saloninus, Roman emperor and son of Gallienus (b.242)

summary: Shapur Meshanshah, Sasanian prince and governor of Meshan, died.
text: Shapur Meshanshah, Sasanian prince and governor

summary: Roman Emperor Valerian died while being held in Persian captivity.
text: Valerianus I, Roman consul and emperor

summary: Regalianus, a Roman usurper acclaimed emperor in Pannonia, was killed.
text: Death of Dacian king Regalianus that became Roman emperor for a brief period.
names: List of kings of Thrace and Dacia

summary: Emperor Gallienus defeated the Alemanni near Milan.
text: Emperor Gallienus crushes the Alemanni at Milan .

summary: Emperor Gallienus repealed the edict of persecution against Christians.
text: Gallienus repeals the edict of 258, which led to the persecution of the Christians.

summary: Aureolus defeated Macrianus Major and Macrianus Minor in Thrace, ending their rebellion.
text: Gallienus usurpers: The rebellion of Macrianus Major, Macrianus Minor, and Quietus against Gallienus comes to an end. They march from Asia to Europe but they are defeated in Thrace by Gallienus' general Aureolus, and both Macrianus Major and Macrianus Minor are killed. Quietus flees to Emesa, where he is killed by Odaenathus of Palmyra.

summary: Balista assembled Roman ships and defeated a Persian raiding force near Pompeiopolis.
text: Roman–Persian Wars: Balista, Roman usurper, collects ships from Cilician ports and defeats a Persian raiding force near Pompeiopolis.

summary: Lucius Mussius Aemilianus, a Roman usurper in Egypt, was captured and executed.
text: Lucius Mussius Aemilianus, Roman usurper

summary: Macrianus Major, a Roman general and usurper, was killed in battle in Thrace.
text: Macrianus Major, Roman general and usurper

summary: Macrianus Minor, a Roman consul and usurper, was killed in battle in Thrace.
text: Macrianus Minor, Roman consul and usurper

summary: Quietus, a Roman consul and usurper, was killed at Emesa by Odaenathus.
text: Quietus, Roman consul and usurper

summary: Valens Thessalonicus, a Roman usurper in Greece, was killed by his own soldiers.
text: Valens Thessalonicus, Roman usurper

summary: The Goths invaded Asia Minor and destroyed the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus.
text: The Goths invade Asia Minor and destroy the Temple of Artemis in Ephesus.

summary: A major earthquake struck Ephesus and Pergamon, and another hit Cyrene.
text: An earthquake strikes Ephesus and Pergamon and another strikes Cyrene.

summary: The Heruli accompanied the Goths in raiding the coasts of the Black Sea and the Aegean.
text: The Heruls accompany the Goths, ravaging the coasts of the Black Sea and the Aegean.

summary: Marinus of Caesarea, a Roman soldier, was beheaded as a Christian martyr.
text: Marinus of Caesarea, Roman soldier and Christian martyr

summary: Valerian, former Roman emperor, died while held captive in the Sasanian Empire.
text: Valerian, Roman consul and emperor

summary: Emperor Gallienus recognized Odaenathus of Palmyra and appointed him Dux Orientalis.
text: King Odenathus of Palmyra declares himself ruler of the area west of the River Euphrates and is declared Dux Orientalis by the Roman emperor Gallienus.

summary: Former Roman emperor Valerian died in Persian captivity.
text: Valerian died in captivity.

summary: Emperor Gallienus campaigned against Postumus in Gaul but broke off the siege after being wounded.
text: Emperor Gallienus tries twice to crush the usurper Postumus, but on the first occasion Aureolus, commander of the elite cavalry, carelessly lets him escape. The second time, Gallienus sustains an arrow wound and has to break off his siege of a Gallic town where Postumus has holed up. He makes no other serious attempt to overcome his rival, instead devoting his attention to the political and military problems in the Danube and eastern parts of the Roman Empire.

summary: Postumus made no attempt to march on Rome or expand his territory south of Gaul.
text: Postumus makes no move to march on Rome and claim his territory south of Gaul.

summary: Gallienus ordered the fortification of Milan and Verona.
text: Gallienus gives the order to fortify Milan and Verona.

summary: Gallienus repelled an invasion of the Goths in the Balkans.
text: Gallienus repels the invasion of the Goths in the Balkans.

summary: Roman general Victorinus defected from Gallienus to Postumus.
text: A general of Gallienus' army, Victorinus, defects to Postumus.

summary: Greek historian and theologian Eusebius of Caesarea was born.
text: Eusebius of Caesarea, Greek historian

summary: Dionysius the Great, patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Dionysius the Great, patriarch of Alexandria

summary: King Odaenathus of Palmyra invaded the Sasanian Empire, besieged Ctesiphon unsuccessfully, and took the title King of Kings.
text: King Odaenathus of Palmyra invades Persia to conquer the capital, Ctesiphon, and twice comes as far as the walls of the Persian capital, but fails to take it. After his victories in the East, he pronounces himself with the title "king of kings".

summary: A powerful tropical volcanic eruption caused below-average flooding of the Nile.
text: A powerful tropical volcanic eruption around this year brings a below-average flood of the Nile next year.

summary: Future Roman empress Galeria Valeria was born.
text: Galeria Valeria, Roman empress and wife of Galerius (d. 315)

summary: The Goths and Sarmatians invaded the Balkans and Greece, ravaging Moesia and Thrace.
text: First Gothic invasion: The Goths, originally from Scandinavia, with the Sarmatians (from modern Iran), invade the Balkans and Greece. They ravage Moesia and Thrace.

summary: The Heruli attacked Byzantium and Cyzicus before being defeated by the Roman fleet and escaping into the Aegean Sea.
text: The Heruli invade the Black Sea coast; they unsuccessfully attack Byzantium and Cyzicus. The Roman fleet defeats the Herulian fleet (500 ships) but allows them to escape into the Aegean Sea, where they raid the islands of Lemnos and Skyros.

summary: Gallienus defeated invading Goths near the Nestos River after they had sacked Athens, Corinth, Argos, and Sparta.
text: The Goths sack several cities of southern Greece including Athens, Corinth, Argos and Sparta. After the Sack of Athens, an Athenian militia force (2,000 men), under the historian Dexippus, pushes the invaders to the north where they are intercepted by the Roman army under emperor Gallienus. He wins an important victory near the Nestos River, on the boundary between Macedonia and Thrace.

summary: Aureolus defeated Victorinus in Italy, was proclaimed emperor by his troops, and began a march on Rome.
text: Aureolus, charged with defending Italy, defeats Victorinus (co-emperor of Gaul), is proclaimed emperor by his troops, and begins his march on Rome.

summary: King Odaenathus of Palmyra was assassinated, and Zenobia took power as regent for their young son Vaballathus.
text: King Septimius Odaenathus of Palmyra makes plans for a campaign in Cappadocia against the Goths. He is assassinated, along with his eldest son, most probably by his nephew due to a previous altercation between him and Odaenathus. His wife Zenobia succeeds him, and rules Vaballathus (the Palmyrene Empire) with her young son.

summary: Septimius Herodianus, co-king of Palmyra, was assassinated.
text: Septimius Herodianus, co-king of Palmyra (assassinated)

summary: King Septimius Odaenathus of Palmyra was assassinated.
text: Septimius Odaenathus, king of Palmyra (assassinated)

summary: Emperor Gallienus, assisted by Aurelian, defeated a Gothic army at the Battle of Naissus.
text: September – Battle of Naissus: Emperor Gallienus, aided by Aurelian, defeats a Gothic coalition (50,000 warriors) near Naissus (Niš, modern Serbia).

summary: Gallienus was assassinated outside Milan by his officers, and Aureolus was murdered by the Praetorian Guard.
text: Gallienus is killed by his senior officers at Mediolanum (Milan) while besieging his rival Aureolus. Aureolus is murdered in turn by the Praetorian guard.

summary: Claudius II became emperor of the Roman Empire following the death of Gallienus.
text: Marcus Aurelius Claudius, who may have murdered Gallienus, becomes the new emperor of Rome and will reign as Claudius II.

summary: Claudius II persuaded the Senate to spare Gallienus's supporters and deify the late emperor.
text: Claudius II asks the Senate to spare the lives of Gallienus's family and political supporters. Emperor Gallienus is deified and buried in a family tomb on the Appian Way.

summary: The Alamanni invaded northern Italy north of the Po River.
text: The Alamanni invade Italy north of the Po River.

summary: The Visigoths first appeared as a distinct people.
text: The Visigoths first appear as distinct people.

summary: A Roman army under Emperor Claudius II defeated the Alamanni at the Battle of Lake Benacus.
text: November – Battle of Lake Benacus: A Roman army (35,000 men) under emperor Claudius II defeats the Germanic tribes of the Alamanni along the banks of Lake Garda.

summary: Roman legions at Augusta Treverorum declared Victorinus emperor of the Gallic Empire.
text: Victorinus is declared emperor of the Gallic Empire by the legions at Augusta Treverorum (Trier), following the murders of his predecessors. He is recognized by the provinces of Gaul and Britain, but Hispania might have reunited with the Roman Empire.

summary: Pope Dionysius died in Rome after a nine-year pontificate and was succeeded by Felix I.
text: Pope Dionysius dies in Rome after a 9-year reign and is succeeded by Felix I.

summary: Pope Dionysius died in Rome.
text: Dionysius, bishop of Rome

summary: Roman usurper Aureolus died at Mediolanum.
text: Aureolus, Roman usurper

summary: Roman Emperor Gallienus died during the siege of Mediolanum.
text: Gallienus, Roman emperor (b. 218)

summary: Roman usurper Laelian died at Mogontiacum.
text: Laelianus, Roman usurper

summary: Gallic emperor Marcus Aurelius Marius died.
text: Marcus Aurelius Marius, Roman emperor (Gaul)

summary: Postumus, emperor of the Gallic Empire, died at Mogontiacum.
text: Postumus, Roman emperor of the Gallic Empire

summary: Emperor Claudius II defeated a large invasion of Goths along the Danube frontier, earning the title Gothicus.
text: Second Gothic invasion: The Goths and other German tribes attack Bosphorean towns on the coast of the Black Sea. Some 2,000 ships and 320,000 men from the Danube enter Roman territory. Emperor Claudius II defeats the invaders and receives the title Gothicus for his triumph. Many of the prisoners will serve in the Roman legions and settle in vacant lands in the Danubian provinces.

summary: Emperor Claudius II traveled to Sirmium to prepare for war against the Vandals raiding Pannonia.
text: Claudius II travels to Sirmium and prepares a war against the Vandals, who raid Pannonia.

summary: The Heruli captured Athens and raided Aegean islands across to Crete and Rhodes.
text: The Heruli capture Athens and raid the Aegean Islands as far as Crete and Rhodes.

summary: Postumus was killed by his own soldiers after forbidding them to sack Mogontiacum.
text: Marcus Cassianius Latinius Postumus is killed by his own troops, after not allowing them to sack the city of Mogontiacum.

summary: Queen Zenobia conquered Syria, Palestine, parts of Anatolia, and Egypt, taking control of Rome's grain supply.
text: Queen Zenobia conquers Syria, Palestine, Lebanon, parts of Mesopotamia and Anatolia and Egypt, giving her control of Rome's grain supply. The library at Alexandria is partly burned during a raid by Zabdas, general of Zenobia.

summary: Pope Felix I succeeded Dionysius as the Bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Felix I succeeds Dionysius as the 26th pope of Rome.

summary: A synod deposed Paul of Samosata as Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Paul of Samosata is deposed as Patriarch of Antioch (though he is not removed until 272).

summary: Christian priest and martyr Justin the Confessor died.
text: Justin the Confessor, Christian priest and martyr

summary: Gallic general and emperor Marcus Aurelius Marius died.
text: Marcus Aurelius Marius, Gallic general and emperor

summary: Gallic emperor Postumus died at Mogontiacum.
text: Marcus Cassianius Latinius Postumus, Gallic emperor

summary: Gallic usurper Laelian died at Mogontiacum.
text: Ulpius Cornelius Laelianus, Gallic emperor and usurper

summary: Victorinus murdered Marius and replaced him as emperor of the Gallic Empire.
text: Marius was murdered by Victorinus, formerly prefect of Postumus's Praetorian Guard, who replaced him as emperor of the Gallic Empire.

summary: Emperor Claudius II fought an extended campaign against Gothic raiders in the Balkans.
text: Emperor Claudius II Gothicus fights a drawn-out campaign against the Gothic raiders in the Balkans, with setbacks suffered on both sides. Eventually, many Goths die of plague and others are absorbed into the Roman legions.

summary: Queen Zenobia seized control of Roman Arabia and Egypt.
text: Zenobia seizes control of Roman Arabia and Egypt.

summary: Emperor Claudius II died of plague in Sirmium and was succeeded by his brother Quintillus.
text: Claudius dies of plague in Sirmium while preparing to fight the Vandals and Sarmatians, who have invaded Pannonia. He is succeeded by his brother Quintillus, who briefly holds power over the Roman Empire.

summary: Victorinus besieged and sacked Autun after the city declared loyalty to Emperor Claudius II.
text: Victorinus besieges and sacks the city of Autun, which had declared allegiance to Claudius.

summary: Aurelian seized power at Sirmium and marched against Quintillus, who committed suicide.
text: Lucius Domitius Aurelianus (or Aurelian), the cavalry commander who distinguished himself in the previous year at the Battle of Naissus (Serbia), usurps power in Sirmium and marches against Quintillus in Aquileia. Quintillus commits suicide.

summary: Aurelian defeated a Juthungi incursion into Raetia as they attempted to re-cross the Danube.
text: Aurelius defeats an incursion by the Iuthungi into Raetia, defeating them as they attempted to re-cross the Danube.

summary: The Kingdom of Aksum began minting gold coins modeled on Roman currency to facilitate trade.
text: The Kingdom of Aksum (modern Ethiopia) begins minting its own gold coins to facilitate international trade, following the model of Roman coinage.

summary: Anthony the Great retreated into the Egyptian wilderness to live as an ascetic.
text: Anthony the Great, a Christian saint from Egypt, regarded as "Father of All Monks", enters the wilderness to become ascetic.

summary: Saint Nicholas was born.
text: Saint Nicholas (Santa Claus) (d. 343)

summary: Saint Spyridon was born.
text: Saint Spyridon, bishop of Trimythous (d. 348)

summary: Roman emperor Claudius Gothicus died of plague.
text: Claudius II (Gothicus), Roman emperor (b. 214)

summary: Gregory Thaumaturgus died.
text: Gregory Thaumaturgus, Christian bishop and theologian

summary: Neoplatonist philosopher Plotinus died in Campania.
text: Plotinus, Greek philosopher and founder Neoplatonism

summary: Roman emperor Quintillus died at Aquileia.
text: Quintillus, Roman emperor and brother of Claudius II

summary: Shapur I, ruler of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Shapur I (the Great), ruler of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Emperor Aurelian defeated the Vandals and drove them out of Pannonia across the Danube.
text: After an indecisive battle, Emperor Aurelian defeats the Vandals, and forces them from Pannonia, and across the Danube.

summary: The Juthungi invaded Italy, sacked Piacenza, and ambushed and defeated a Roman army led by Emperor Aurelian.
text: Battle of Placentia: The Iuthungi invade Italy and sack the city of Piacenza. A Roman army under Emperor Aurelian is ambushed and defeated.

summary: Aurelian defeated the invading Juthungi at the Metauro River near Fano.
text: Battle of Fano: The Iuthungi move towards a defenseless Rome. Aurelian rallies his men and defeats the Germanic tribes on the Metauro River, just inland of Fano.

summary: Aurelian encircled and destroyed the invading Alamanni near Pavia.
text: Battle of Pavia: The Roman army pursues the Alamanni in Lombardy. Aurelian closes the passes in the Alps and encircles the invaders near Pavia. The Alamanni are destroyed and Aurelian receives the title Germanicus Maximus.

object: Revolt of the Rome mint workers
summary: Aurelian suppressed a revolt by mint workers and their senatorial supporters on the Caelian Hill in Rome.
text: Following Aurelian's execution of Felicissimus, the financial minister of the state treasury, on the charge of corruption, the mint workers of the city of Rome, with senatorial support, lead an uprising against Aurelian. In bitter street-fighting on the Caelian Hill the rebels are defeated. The revolt is followed by a purge of Aurelian's senatorial opponents, including Urbanus.
names: Revolt of the Rome mint workers

summary: Generals loyal to Aurelian defeated the usurpers Septimius in Dalmatia and Domitian II in southern Gaul.
text: Around this time, generals loyal to Aurelian defeat the usurpers Septimius in Dalmatia and Domitian II in southern Gaul. The Iuthungian invasion may have encouraged the spate of revolts.

summary: Aurelian began construction of the Aurelian Walls to protect the city of Rome.
text: Aurelian begins construction of a new defensive wall to protect Rome. The Aurelian Walls,, enclose the city with fortifications.

summary: Aurelian increased Rome's daily bread ration and added free pig fat distributions for the populace.
text: Perhaps around this time, Aurelian increases Rome's daily bread ration to nearly 1.5 pounds and adds pig fat to the list of foods distributed free to the populace.

summary: Aurelian repelled a Gothic raid in the Balkans and invaded their territory, killing their leader Cannabas.
text: Aurelian defeats a Gothic raid into the Balkans and then invades the Gothic homeland. Here he defeats the Goths again, killing one of their leaders, Cannabas, who may be Cniva, the Goth who had won the battle of Abritus, at which Emperor Decius was killed.

summary: Aurelian withdrew the Roman administration and military from Dacia to secure the Danube frontier.
text: Aurelian withdraws Rome's administrative and military presence from Dacia (modern Romania), thereby rationalizing the Danube frontier and freeing resources for the forthcoming campaign against Zenobia.

summary: Victorinus was assassinated by Attitianus, and Tetricus I succeeded him as Emperor of the Gallic Empire.
text: Victorinus, Emperor of the Gallic Empire, is assassinated by one of his officers, Attitianus, reportedly for reasons of personal revenge. He is succeeded by Tetricus I, who is elevated with the help of Victorinus' mother Victoria.

summary: Zenobia invaded Asia Minor and captured Cilicia and Galatia before halting in Bithynia.
text: Zenobia invades Asia Minor and seizes control of Cilicia and Galatia before being stalled in Bithynia.

summary: Hormizd I succeeded Shapur I as ruler of the Sasanian Empire and led an army against nomads in Sogdiana.
text: Shapur I of the Sasanian Empire dies, and his successor, his son Hormizd I, leads an army against nomads in Sogdiana, perhaps taking command of a war that had begun under his father. (Note: Some scholars date Shapur's death to 270 or 272)

summary: Shapur I established the Academy of Gondishapur as an intellectual centre of the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Shapur I builds the Academy of Gundishapur (Iran), which becomes the intellectual center of the Sassanid Empire.

summary: Gallic emperor Domitian II died.
text: Domitian II, emperor of the Gallic Empire

summary: Roman financial minister Felicissimus was executed for corruption.
text: Felicissimus, Roman financial minister (rationalis)

summary: Hormizd I, ruler of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Hormizd I (or Ohrmazd), ruler of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Victorinus, emperor of the Gallic Empire, died.
text: Victorinus, emperor of the Gallic Empire

summary: Aurelian launched an invasion of the Palmyrene Empire, marching into Asia Minor while sending Probus to retake Egypt.
text: Emperor Aurelian launches a two-pronged invasion of the Palmyrene Empire, sending his commander Marcus Aurelius Probus to restore Roman rule in Egypt while he marches into Asia Minor.

summary: Aurelian captured Tyana and spared its citizens, prompting Palmyrene forces to defect to him.
text: As part of a strategy of clemency, Aurelian spares Tyana after capturing the city. This strategy encourages units under Zenobia to defect to Aurelian.

summary: Aurelian defeated the Palmyrene army near Antioch, forcing Zenobia to flee to Emesa.
text: Battle of Immae: Aurelian defeats the Palmyrene heavy cavalry (clibanarii) near Antioch. Queen Zenobia flees under cover of darkness to Emesa (Syria).

summary: Aurelian supported the bishops of Italy in deposing Paul of Samosata as bishop of Antioch.
text: Aurelian supports the bishops of Italy in deposing the bishop of Antioch, Paul of Samosata, who had been a supporter of Zenobia. This is the first recorded instance of an imperial intervention in an ecclesiastical dispute.

summary: Aurelian decisively defeated the Palmyrene army at the Battle of Emesa.
text: Battle of Emesa: Aurelian decisively defeats the Palmyrene army.

summary: Aurelian besieged and captured Palmyra after capturing Queen Zenobia as she attempted to flee to Persia.
text: Aurelian besieges Palmyra. Zenobia attempts to escape to Persia but is captured on the Euphrates. Palmyra surrenders soon after.

summary: Cassius Longinus and other advisors of Zenobia were executed at Emesa for conspiring against Aurelian.
text: Following a series of trials held in Emesa, Cassius Longinus and other advisors of Zenobia are executed for conspiring against Aurelian.

summary: Dometius succeeded Titus as bishop of Byzantium.
text: Dometius succeeds Titus as Patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Denis of Paris and two of his disciples were beheaded near Lutetia.
text: Saint Denis, first Bishop of Paris, and two of his disciples are beheaded on the road to the Temple of Mercury that stands atop a hill outside of the city. The hill will later be called Montmartre (Mountain of Martyrs) in Lutetia (modern Paris).

summary: Paul of Samosata was deposed as Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Paul of Samosata is deposed as Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Future Roman emperor Constantine the Great was born in Naissus.
text: Constantine the Great, Roman emperor (d. 337)

summary: King Shapur I of the Sasanian Empire died.
text: Shapur I (the Great), king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Roman general and Christian martyr Sabbas Stratelates died.
text: Sabbas Stratelates, Roman general and martyr

summary: Marcus Claudius Tacitus served as Roman consul in Rome.
text: Marcus Claudius Tacitus, future Roman Emperor, is consul in Rome.

summary: Emperor Aurelian defeated an incursion by the Carpi into Moesia and Thrace.
text: Emperor Aurelian defeats an incursion by the Carpi into Moesia and Thrace.

summary: Aurelian sacked the city of Palmyra after suppressing a second rebellion.
text: Aurelian sacks the city of Palmyra, after putting down a second revolt.

summary: Aurelian crushed a rebellion in Alexandria led by Firmus, who was executed.
text: In bitter street-fighting, Aurelian crushes a rebellion in Alexandria by Firmus, a sympathizer of Palmyra. Firmus is strangled to death.

summary: Bahram I succeeded his brother Hormizd I as king of the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Hormizd I of Persia dies after a brief reign in which he has shown tolerance toward the ascetic, anti-materialist Manichean faith. He is succeeded by his brother Bahram I, who has been governing the province of Atropatene. Bahram proceeds to crush a rebellion by various vassal kings.

summary: Christian bishop Reverianus died.
text: Reverianus, Christian bishop

summary: Greek historian and sophist Callinicus died.
text: Callinicus, Greek historian and sophist

summary: Greek philosopher Cassius Longinus died.
text: Cassius Longinus, Greek philosopher

summary: Greek general and historian Dexippus died.
text: Dexippus, Greek general and historian

summary: King Hormizd I of the Sasanian Empire died.
text: Hormizd I, king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Roman usurper Septimius Antiochus died.
text: Septimius Antiochus, Roman usurper

summary: Aurelian defeated the Gallic Empire at the Battle of Châlons following the surrender of Tetricus I, reuniting the Roman Empire.
text: Battle of Châlons: The Emperor Aurelian invades Gaul to campaign against the Gallic Empire (Gaul and Britain). In the Catalaunian Plains, the Romano-Gallic Emperor Tetricus I surrenders to Aurelian and leaves his army without an emperor. The Gallic army is then crushed by Aurelian in a major battle. With the conquests of the Palmyrene Empire and the Gallic Empire, the Roman Empire is united again. However, the heavy losses incurred by the Gallic forces compromises the Rhine frontier.

summary: The people and Senate of Rome accorded Aurelian a magnificent triumph featuring captives Zenobia and Tetricus I.
text: Rome greets Aurelian as Restitutor Orbis ("Restorer of the World") and accords him a magnificent triumph (victory procession), which is graced by his captives Zenobia, Tetricus I, and his son Tetricus II.

summary: Aurelian reformed the Roman currency by replacing the denarius with an improved version of the antoninianus.
text: Aurelian reforms the Roman currency, replacing the denarius with a new version of the antoninianus that has a slightly improved silver-to-copper ratio. This overhaul of the currency system causes hyper-inflation.

summary: Germanic tribes took advantage of depleted Roman border defenses to raid Gaul.
text: Germanic tribes take advantage of the destroyed Roman forces of the Rhine to raid Gaul.

summary: Aurelian dedicated the Temple of the Sun to Sol Invictus in Rome, establishing the cult as a state religion.
text: Aurelian has the Temple of the Sun dedicated to Sol Invictus, on the third day after the solstice and day of rebirth of the sun. This religion, which is in essence monotheistic, becomes the state religion of Rome.

summary: Prophet Mani died in prison at Gundeshapur after preaching Manichaeism across Persia and Asia.
text: Mani, a sage of Persia, dies at Gundeshapur after 30 years of preaching his "heresy" at the court of the late Sassanian King Shapur I and on long journeys to Khorasan, India and China. He is executed or allowed to die in prison, and claims to be a prophet of God. Mani combines Zoroastrian dualism with Christian theology, and his disciples gain wide support for Manichaeism, despite opposition from Roman Emperors.

summary: Pope Felix I died in Rome after a five-year reign.
text: Pope Felix I dies in Rome after a 5-year reign.

summary: Mani, prophet and founder of Manichaeism, died in Gundeshapur.
text: Mani, prophet and founder of Manichaeism (b. 216)

summary: Bahram I, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: September – Bahram I, king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Felix I, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Felix I, bishop of Rome

summary: Zenobia, former queen of the Palmyrene Empire, died.
text: After 274 – Septimia Zenobia, queen of the Palmyrene Empire (b. 240)

summary: Emperor Aurelian suppressed unrest in Gaul and defeated Germanic incursions into Gaul and Raetia.
text: Emperor Aurelian puts down unrest in Gaul, and defeats Germanic incursions into Gaul and Raetia (these problems had been caused by Aurelian's defeat and overthrow of the Gallic Empire).

summary: Aurelian launched a campaign against the Goths raiding Thrace and Asia Minor.
text: The Goths begin to raid Thrace and Asia Minor. Aurelian begins a campaign against the Goths in Thrace.

summary: Emperor Aurelian was assassinated near Byzantium after his secretary Eros forged an execution list of military officers.
text: c. November – Aurelian is assassinated near Byzantium (Turkey). Aurelian had developed a reputation for punishing corruption with severity, and his secretary Eros was under suspicion. As a result, Eros, fearing for his life, forged a list of high-ranking officers marked for execution. In this way, the secretary tricked the officers into assassinating Aurelian. They then flee into Asia Minor to avoid the wrath of the soldiers.

summary: Marcus Claudius Tacitus was proclaimed Roman emperor, and his half-brother Florianus became praetorian prefect.
text: November/December – Marcus Claudius Tacitus is proclaimed Emperor by the imperial field army (other sources give him as proclaimed September 25 by the Senate). His half brother Marcus Annius Florianus becomes praetorian prefect.

summary: Emperor Tacitus marched into Asia Minor to fight the Goths and pursue the assassins of Aurelian.
text: Tacitus marches into Asia Minor to fight the Goths and track down the faction responsible for assassinating Aurelian.

summary: Eutychian succeeded Felix I as bishop of Rome.
text: Eutychian succeeds Felix I as the 27th pope of Rome.

summary: Saint George was born in Cappadocia.
text: Approximate date – Saint George of Lydda, Cappadocian Greek Roman soldier and Christian martyr (k. 303)

summary: Roman emperor Aurelian died near Byzantium.
text: c. November – Aurelian, Roman emperor (b. 214 or 215)

summary: Zenobia, former queen of the Palmyrene Empire, died.
text: Approximate date – Septimia Zenobia, queen of the Palmyrene Empire (b. c. 240)

summary: Emperor Tacitus reformed the Roman coinage by doubling the silver content of the aurelianianus and halving its tariff.
text: Emperor Tacitus doubles the silver content of the aurelianianus, and halves its tariffing to 2.5 d.c. They carry the value marks X.I.

summary: Emperor Tacitus and praetorian prefect Florianus campaigned successfully against the Goths invading Asia Minor.
text: Tacitus campaigns successfully against the Goths who have invaded Asia Minor, and his half-brother, the praetorian prefect Marcus Annius Florianus, continues the campaign.

summary: Conspirators, including Aurelian's assassins, assassinated Tacitus' cousin Maximinus in Syria.
text: Tacitus' cousin Maximinus administers Syria in a harsh manner, and is assassinated by local men of power, who are joined in the conspiracy by the faction responsible for having assassinated Aurelian in the previous year.

summary: Emperor Tacitus died at Tyana in Cappadocia, either from illness or assassination.
text: Tacitus dies in Tyana, Cappadocia. He either dies of illness, or is murdered by the faction responsible for having assassinated Aurelian and Maximinus.

summary: Florianus claimed the imperial throne with Senate support, while Marcus Aurelius Probus revolted against him in the east.
text: Florianus becomes Roman Emperor with the support of the Senate, but a general in the east, Marcus Aurelius Probus, usurps power against him. Florianus breaks off his campaign against the Goths and marches east from the Bosporus with support from the Roman legions in Britain, Gaul, Spain and Italy.

summary: Florianus was overthrown and assassinated by his own troops near Tarsus, and Probus was proclaimed the new Roman emperor.
text: Florianus holds power for some weeks and fights indecisively against Probus in Cilicia, but his soldiers, many of whom are from the colder Rhine and Danube frontiers, suffer from heat and disease. He is overthrown and then assassinated by his own troops near Tarsus (Turkey), in collusion with Probus. Probus, age 44, is proclaimed new Emperor of Rome.

summary: Emperor Probus restored the aurelianianus to the previous tariffing established by Aurelian.
text: Probus returns the aurelianianus to the tariffing of Aurelian.

summary: Emperor Probus lured the assassins of Aurelian and Tacitus to a banquet and had them massacred.
text: Probus invites the faction responsible for the murders of Aurelian and Tacitus to a banquet, only to massacre them. He then arrests a surviving conspirator and has him burned alive.

summary: King Bahram I died and was succeeded as ruler of the Sasanian Empire by his son Bahram II.
text: King Bahram I of Persia dies after a 3-year reign, in which the Zoroastrian priests at Ctesiphon (Iran) put pressure on him to persecute Buddhists, Christians, and Manichaeans. He is succeeded by his son Bahram II.

summary: Gregory of Nazianzus the Elder was born.
text: Gregory the Elder, bishop of Nazianzus

summary: Bahram I, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Bahram I, king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Roman emperor Florianus died near Tarsus.
text: Marcus Annius Florianus, Roman emperor

summary: Roman emperor Tacitus died in Tyana, Cappadocia.
text: Marcus Claudius Tacitus, Roman Emperor

summary: Tiberius Julius Synges, Roman client king of the Bosporan Kingdom, died.
text: Tiberius Julius Synges, Roman client king

summary: Emperor Probus marched across the Sea of Marmara through Thrace, Moesia, and Pannonia, defeating the Goths on the Danube and taking the title Gothicus.
text: Emperor Probus travels with his army west across the Sea of Marmara (Turkey), and through the provinces of Thrace, Moesia, and Pannonia to defeat the Goths along the lower Danube. He acquires from the troops the title of Gothicus.

summary: Probus entered Rome to have his position as emperor officially ratified by the Senate.
text: Probus enters Rome, to have his position as Emperor ratified by the Senate.

summary: Justus of Beauvais was born.
text: Justus of Beauvais, Gallo-Roman martyr

summary: Emperor Probus defeated the Alamanni along the Neckar Valley, expelled the Franks from Gaul, and reorganized Roman defenses on the Rhine.
text: Emperor Probus defeats the Alamanni, advancing through the Neckar Valley. He expels the Franks from Gaul, and reorganizes the Roman defenses on the Rhine.

summary: Emperor Probus resettled Germanic tribes in devastated Roman provinces and adopted the titles Gothicus Maximus and Germanicus Maximus.
text: Probus resettles the Germanic tribes in the devastated provinces of the Roman Empire. He adopts the titles of Gothicus Maximus and Germanicus Maximus.

summary: Roman forces besieged Cremna in Pisidia and killed the Isaurian bandit Lydius.
text: Piracy along the coast of Lycia et Pamphylia: The Romans besiege the city of Cremna (Pisidia) and kill the Isaurian robber Lydius.

summary: Rabbi Johanan bar Nappaha, compiler of the Jerusalem Talmud, died.
text: Johanan bar Nappaha, Jewish compiler of the Talmud

summary: Tiberius Julius Teiranes, client king of the Bosporan Kingdom, died.
text: Tiberius Julius Teiranes, Roman prince and client king

summary: Emperor Probus launched a military campaign against the Vandals in Illyricum.
text: Probus launched a campaign against the Vandals in Illyricum.

summary: Proculus initiated a rebellion at Lugdunum and proclaimed himself Roman emperor.
text: Roman usurper Proculus starts a rebellion at Lugdunum (Lyon, France), and proclaims himself emperor.

summary: Emperor Probus drove the Alans into Asia Minor, suppressed the revolt in Gaul, and executed the usurper Proculus.
text: Emperor Probus drives the Alans off to Asia Minor and suppresses the revolt in Gaul; Proculus is executed.

summary: Germanic tribes destroyed the Roman Rhine fleet, and Bonosus was proclaimed emperor at Colonia Agrippina.
text: The Germans destroy the Roman fleet on the Rhine; Bonosus is proclaimed emperor at Colonia Agrippina (Cologne).

summary: Emperor Probus defeated the army of Bonosus, who hanged himself.
text: Probus defeats the army under Bonosus. Bonosus sees no way out and hangs himself. His family is treated with honours.

summary: Julius Saturninus was proclaimed emperor in Alexandria and withdrew to Apamea, where Probus besieged the city and put him to death.
text: Julius Saturninus, governor of Syria, is in Alexandria, charged with the defense of the East. He is declared emperor and withdraws to Apamea. Probus besieges the city and puts him to death.

summary: Faced with persistent Frankish raids, Roman cities throughout Gaul were reinforced with defensive walls.
text: Roman territory is under constant threat of raids from Franks. The cities in Gaul are reinforced with defensive walls.

summary: King Bahram II of the Sasanian Empire sent envoys to Rome seeking peaceful relations.
text: King Bahram II of the Sassanid Empire (Persia) sends envoys to seek peaceful relations with Rome.

summary: Saint George, Roman soldier and Christian martyr, was born in Cappadocia.
text: Approximate date – Saint George, Cappadocian Greek-born Roman soldier and Christian martyr

summary: Roman usurper Bonosus died by suicide after his defeat by Emperor Probus.
text: Bonosus, Roman general and usurper, suicide

summary: Roman usurper Julius Saturninus was put to death at Apamea.
text: 280 or 281 – Julius Saturninus, Roman usurper

summary: Emperor Probus returned to Rome and celebrated a triumph over the Vandals and defeated usurpers.
text: Emperor Probus returns to Rome, where he celebrates his triumph over the Vandals and the usurpers (Bonosus, Julius Saturninus and Proculus).

summary: Tiberianus served his first term as Roman consul.
text: Tiberianus served his first of two terms as Consul.

summary: Theodore Stratelates, future Roman general and Christian martyr, was born.
text: Theodore Stratelates, Roman general and martyr (d. 319)

summary: The Roman usurper Proculus was executed.
text: Proculus, Roman general and usurper

summary: Emperor Probus marched toward Sirmium and employed his legions in draining the swamps of Pannonia.
text: Emperor Probus travels towards Sirmium (Serbia). He tries to employ his troops in peaceful projects, such as draining the swamps in Pannonia.

summary: Carus seized imperial power in Raetia while Emperor Probus was assassinated by his mutinous troops at Sirmium.
text: The praetorian prefect Marcus Aurelius Carus usurps power in Raetia. Probus attempts to organise a campaign against Carus but is murdered by his discontented troops in Sirmium.

summary: Carus defeated the Quadi and Sarmatians on the Danube frontier and assumed the title Germanicus Maximus.
text: Carus defeats the Quadi and Sarmatians on the Danube; for his victories he is given the title Germanicus Maximus.

summary: Emperor Carus elevated his sons Carinus and Numerian to the rank of Caesar.
text: Carus appoints his sons Carinus and Numerian as Caesar.

summary: Patriarch Theonas of Alexandria began using the title Pope.
text: The Patriarch Theonas of Alexandria becomes one of the first bishops to use the title Pope.

summary: Roman Emperor Probus was assassinated by his troops at Sirmium.
text: Marcus Aurelius Probus, Roman emperor (b. 232)

summary: Emperor Carus elevated his son Carinus to the rank of Augustus in the western Roman Empire.
text: Spring: Emperor Carus makes his son Carinus the Augustus in the west.

summary: Carus invaded the Sasanian Empire, sacked Seleucia and Ctesiphon, and advanced beyond the Tigris.
text: Exploiting the Persian civil war, Carus leaves Carinus in charge of much of the Roman Empire and, accompanied by his younger son Numerian, invades the Sassanid Empire. They sack Seleucia and Ctesiphon, the capital of the Persian kingdom, and they press on beyond the Tigris. For his victories, Carus receives the title of Persicus Maximus.

summary: Diocles distinguished himself during the Roman campaign against the Sasanian Empire.
text: The officer Diocles, the future Emperor Diocletian, distinguishes himself in the war against the Persians.

summary: Carinus conducted successful military campaigns in Britain and along the Rhine frontier.
text: Carinus campaigns with success in Britain and on the Rhine frontier.

summary: Emperor Carus died in mysterious circumstances while campaigning near the Tigris.
text: Summer: Carus dies in mysterious circumstances during the war against the Persians. Various sources claim he died of illness, was struck by lightning or was killed in combat.

summary: Carinus and Numerian succeeded Carus, and Numerian led the Roman army back from Persian territory.
text: Carinus and Numerian succeed their father Carus. Numerian, who had accompanied his father into the Persian Empire, leads the army back to Roman territory.

summary: Aurelius Julianus rebelled and claimed the imperial title in Pannonia but was suppressed by Carinus.
text: The corrector Aurelius Julianus usurps power in Pannonia but is defeated by Carinus.

summary: King of Kings Bahram II waged a civil war against his brother Hormizd of Sakastan.
text: The King of Kings Bahram II fights a civil war against his brother Hormizd, the king of Sakastan.

summary: Caius succeeded Eutychian as the bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Caius succeeds Eutychian as the 28th pope of Rome.

summary: Eusebius of Vercelli, future Christian bishop and opponent of Arianism, was born in Sardinia.
text: Eusebius of Vercelli, Christian bishop and saint (d. 371)

summary: Pope Eutychian died in Rome.
text: Etychian, bishop of Rome

summary: Roman Emperor Carus died near Ctesiphon.
text: Marcus Aurelius Carus, Roman emperor (b. 224)

summary: Emperor Numerian died while travelling in a closed carriage through Bithynia.
text: Emperor Numerian travels through Bithynia (Asia Minor) on his way home to Rome. Suffering from an inflammation of the eyes, he travels in a closed litter in which soldiers find his decaying corpse.

summary: Diocletian became emperor of Rome.
text: Diocletian becomes emperor of Rome

summary: Diocles was proclaimed emperor outside Nicomedia, changed his name to Diocletian, and killed praetorian prefect Arrius Aper.
text: The commander of Numerian's domestici (household troops), Diocles, is chosen to be the new emperor. In a military assembly outside Nicomedia (modern İzmit, Turkey), Diocles claims that the praetorian prefect (and rival for the throne) Arrius Aper murdered Numerian, and he personally stabs and kills the prefect on the spot. The new emperor changes his name to the Latinised 'Diocletian'. Building on existing trends, Diocletian presents his rule as that of a god-like dominus or autocrat.

summary: Sabinus Julianus revolted against Carinus and proclaimed himself emperor in northern Italy.
text: Sabinus Julianus, the praetorian prefect of Emperor Carinus, exploits the instability and usurps the throne in northern Italy.

summary: Sasanian monarch Bahram II installed Mirian III on the throne of the Kingdom of Iberia.
text: King of Kings Bahram II installs Mirian III, of the House of Mihran, on the throne of the Kingdom of Iberia. Mirian would rule the kingdom until his death in c. 361.

summary: Rufinus succeeded Dometius as Bishop of Byzantium.
text: Rufinus succeeds Dometius as Bishop of Byzantium.

summary: Roman Emperor Numerian was found dead in Bithynia.
text: Numerian, Roman emperor (b. 254)

summary: Praetorian prefect Lucius Flavius Aper was killed near Nicomedia.
text: Lucius Flavius Aper, Roman general and praetorian prefect

summary: Emperor Carinus marched from Britain to northern Italy and defeated the usurper Sabinus Julianus at Verona.
text: Spring – Emperor Carinus marches from Britain to northern Italy, and defeats the army of usurper Sabinus Julianus at Verona.

summary: Diocletian defeated Carinus at the Battle of the Margus, after which Carinus was killed by his own officers.
text: Summer – Battle of the Margus: Emperor Diocletian defeats the forces of Carinus in the valley of the Margus (Serbia). Numerous soldiers desert Carinus during the battle. Carinus then flees to the Pannonian fort of Cornacum, but he is soon slain by his officers.

summary: Diocletian appointed his fellow officer Maximian to the office of caesar.
text: July 21 or July 25 – Diocletian appoints his fellow-officer Maximian to the office of caesar, or junior co-emperor.

summary: The Roman Empire tasked naval commander Carausius with clearing the English Channel of Frankish and Saxon pirates.
text: Carausius, naval commander at Bononia (modern-day Boulogne), is given the task of clearing the English Channel of Frankish and Saxon pirates.

summary: Diocletian sent Maximian to Gaul to suppress the revolt of the Bagaudae.
text: Maximian is sent to pacify Gaul, where the Bagaudae, a band of peasants, are revolting against the Roman Empire.

summary: Roman emperor Carinus died near the Margus after being slain by his officers.
text: Marcus Aurelius Carinus, Roman consul and emperor

summary: Roman usurper Sabinus Julianus died following his defeat at Verona.
text: Sabinus Julianus, Roman usurper

summary: Maximian suppressed the Bagaudae rebellion in Gaul and repelled invasions by Burgundians, Alemanni, Chaibones, and Heruli.
text: Winter/Spring: The Caesar Maximian defeats the Bagaudae rebellion in Gaul. He then defeats a Germanic invasion into Gaul, defeating an army of Burgundians and Alemanni and another army of Chaibones and Heruli.

summary: Diocletian campaigned successfully against Sarmatian raiders along the Danube frontier.
text: Emperor Diocletian campaigns successfully against Sarmatian raids. The future emperor Constantius defeats the 'Bosporian Sarmatians'.

summary: Sentenced to death by Maximian, Carausius declared himself emperor and seized Roman Britain and northwestern Gaul.
text: Summer: Carausius, commander of the Classis Britannica, is accused of piracy by Maximian and is sentenced to death. He responds by declaring himself emperor of Britain and Northwestern Gaul. His forces consist of the newly built Roman fleet and three legions in Britain. The Carausian Revolt is supported by Gaulish merchant ships and Frankish mercenaries.

summary: Roman cobblers and Christian martyrs Crispin and Crispinian were martyred at Soissons.
text: Crispin and Crispinian, Roman cobblers and martyrs

summary: Christian martyr Domnina of Anazarbus died during persecution.
text: Domnina of Anazarbus, Christian martyr and saint

summary: Christian martyrs Mark and Marcellian were executed in Rome.
text: Mark and Marcellian, Christian martyrs

summary: Diocletian proclaimed Maximian augustus of the Western Roman Empire while continuing to rule as augustus of the East.
text: Diocletian proclaimed Maximian augustus of the west, ruling himself as augustus of the east.

summary: Maximian defeated an Alemannic invasion of Gaul and subsequently invaded Alemannic territory across the Upper Rhine.
text: On the same day that he is made consul, Maximian launches a campaign against an invasion of Gaul by the Alemanni. After defeating this invasion, he then invades Alemannia itself, entering across the Upper Rhine and returning to Roman territory via the Upper Danube.

summary: Constantius Chlorus defeated and captured a Germanic king who had prepared an ambush against Roman forces.
text: Around this time, the future emperor Constantius defeats and captures a Germanic king, the latter having prepared an ambush against the Romans.

summary: Diocletian signed a peace treaty with King Bahram II of Persia and installed Tiridates III as king over western Armenia.
text: Diocletian signs a peace treaty with King Bahram II of Persia, and installs the pro-Roman Arsacid Tiridates III as king over the western portion of Armenia.

summary: Diocletian reorganized the Mesopotamian frontier and fortified key locations along the Euphrates, including Circesium.
text: Diocletian re-organizes the Mesopotamian frontier, and fortifies various locations including the city of Circesium (modern Busayrah) on the Euphrates. Around this time, he begins the construction of the Strata Diocletiana. Throughout his reign, similar fortification efforts are conducted on the other frontiers as well, with fortifications constructed or restored behind, on and beyond the borders. Conscription and the number of legions increase, although the legions themselves are reformed into smaller and more flexible units. At some point in time, Diocletian may have also established the late Roman military system of Comitatenses (field army units) and Limitanei (border units), but some scholars date this development to the reign of Constantine I (r. 306–337).

summary: The Roman Empire instituted the first fifteen-year cycle of the Indiction taxation system.
text: September – The first Indiction begins.

summary: Christian martyrs Justa and Rufina were put to death in Hispalis.
text: Justa and Rufina, Christian martyrs

summary: Saint Maurice and the soldiers of the Theban Legion were martyred at Agaunum.
text: Maurice (or Mauritius), Christian martyr

summary: Christian missionary and martyr Saint Quentin was executed in Gaul.
text: Quentin, Christian missionary and martyr

summary: Christian martyrs Valerius and Rufinus were martyred near Soissons.
text: Valerius and Rufinus, Christian martyrs

summary: Christian martyrs Victoricus, Fuscian, and Gentian were martyred near Amiens.
text: Victoricus, Fuscian, and Gentian, Christian martyrs

summary: Diocletian launched a military campaign into Germanic territory from the province of Raetia.
text: Emperor Diocletian launches a campaign into Germanic territory from the province of Raetia (Switzerland).

summary: Constantius Chlorus defeated the usurper Carausius or his Frankish allies in northern Gaul, forcing Carausius to withdraw to Britain.
text: Around this time, an army loyal to Maximian, probably led by the future emperor Constantius, defeats the usurper Carausius or his Frankish allies in northern Gaul. In this or the following year, Carausius withdraws his military forces and administrative presence from Gaul, confining himself to Roman Britain.

summary: Maximian concluded an alliance with the Frankish king Gennobaudes.
text: Maximian makes an alliance with the Frankish king Gennobaudes.

summary: Maximian constructed a fleet in the rivers of Gaul to challenge Carausius in the North Sea and reconquer Britain.
text: Far from Carausius' fleet, in the rivers of Gaul, Maximian builds a fleet to contest control of the North Sea and re-take Britain.

summary: Constantius Chlorus married Maximian's stepdaughter Theodora to cement political ties.
text: Around this time, Constantius marries Maximian's stepdaughter, Theodora, and it may also be around this time that the general Galerius marries Diocletian's daughter Galeria Valeria.

summary: Christian missionary and bishop Maximilian of Lorch died as a martyr.
text: Maximilian of Lorch, Christian missionary and martyr

summary: Roman soldier and Christian martyr Saint Sebastian was martyred in Rome.
text: Sebastian, Roman soldier and Christian martyr

summary: Diocletian campaigned successfully against the Sarmatians along the Danube.
text: In this or the following year, Emperor Diocletian campaigns with success against the Sarmatians. The future emperor Galerius may have distinguished himself during this campaign.

summary: Carausius defeated Maximian's fleet at sea when Maximian attempted to reconquer Roman Britain.
text: In this or the following year, Maximian attempts to reconquer Britain from the usurper Carausius but is defeated at sea.

summary: Flavia Maxima Fausta, future Roman empress, was born.
text: Flavia Maxima Fausta, Roman empress (d. 326)

summary: Christian martyr Alexander of Rome died.
text: Alexander of Rome, Christian martyr

summary: Christian martyr Saint Kyriaki died.
text: Kyriaki the Great, Christian martyr

summary: Emperor Diocletian campaigned successfully against Arabic enemies.
text: Emperor Diocletian campaigns with success against Arabic enemies.

summary: Carausius invaded the European mainland and re-established his control in northern Gaul following his victory over Maximian's fleet.
text: Following his victory over Emperor Maximian's fleet, the usurper Carausius invades the European mainland and re-establishes his military and administrative presence in northern Gaul.

summary: Christian hermit and ascetic Abramios the Recluse was born.
text: Abramios the Recluse, Christian hermit and ascetic (d. 360)

summary: Greek mathematician Pappus of Alexandria was born.
text: Pappus of Alexandria, Greek mathematician (d. 350)

summary: Christian martyr Vitus was born in Sicily.
text: Vitus (or Guido), Roman hagiographer and martyr

summary: Emperors Diocletian and Maximian convened a conference in Milan.
text: Winter: The emperors Diocletian and Maximian convene in Milan.

summary: Emperors Diocletian and Maximian established an uneasy peace with Carausius.
text: An uneasy peace is established between the emperors Diocletian and Maximian on the one hand, and the rival emperor Carausius on the other.

summary: Carausius campaigned against Germanic raiders and began constructing the forts of the Saxon Shore.
text: Perhaps in cooperation with the forces of Maximian, Carausius campaigns successfully against Germanic raids in Gaul and Britain. Also during his reign, Carausius begins building the forts of the Saxon Shore.

summary: The Alemanni sought to regain territory they had previously lost to the Burgundians.
text: The Alemanni, having been expelled from part of their territory by the Burgundians, seek to regain their lost lands. These peoples had unsuccessfully invaded Gaul in tandem in 285/6, and the Alemanni had likely been weakened by the Roman counter-invasions of 287 and 288.

summary: A force of Goths defeated the Burgundians in battle.
text: A force of Goths defeat the Burgundians.

summary: The Tervingian Goths and Taifali fought a war against the Vandals and Gepids.
text: The Tervingian Goths and Taifali fight the Vandals and Gepids.

summary: King Bahram II fought a coalition led by his brother Hormizd of Sakastan alongside the Kushano-Sasanians and Gilans.
text: King Bahram II fights against a coalition consisting of his brother Hormizd of Sakastan, the Kushano-Sasanians, and the Gilans.

summary: Saint Agnes of Rome was born.
text: Saint Agnes, Christian martyress (d. c. 304)

summary: Saint Hilarion, Christian anchorite and saint, was born near Gaza.
text: Saint Hilarion, anchorite and saint (d. 371)

summary: Saint Philomena was born.
text: Saint Philomena, Christian martyress (d. c. 304)

summary: The jurist Gregorius produced the Gregorian Code, compiling imperial constitutions into a legal code.
text: The jurist Gregorius, at the court of Emperor Diocletian, produces the Gregorian Code, the first codification of Roman law .

summary: Revolts broke out in Upper Egypt centered at Thebes and involving Busiris and Coptos.
text: The Upper Egypt revolts of (292–293) outbreak in Egypt, centralized in the city of Thebes, primarily involving other Egyptian cities such as Busiris and Coptos. A precursor to the much larger national Egyptian rebellion that followed a few years later.

summary: Christian theologian and monastic founder Pachomius was born.
text: Pachomius, Christian theologian and writer (d. 348)

summary: Diocletian and Maximian appointed Constantius Chlorus and Galerius as Caesars, establishing the Tetrarchy.
text: Emperors Diocletian and Maximian appoint Constantius I and Galerius as Caesars. This is considered the beginning of the Tetrarchy, known as the Quattuor Principes Mundi ("Four Rulers of the World"). (Some sources and scholars date Galerius' elevation to May 21.)

summary: Constantius retook Gallic territories from the usurper Carausius and captured the port of Bononia.
text: Constantius retakes some of the Gallic territories from the usurper Carausius. He conquers the crucial port of Bononia (modern Boulogne).

summary: Allectus murdered Carausius and proclaimed himself emperor in Britain.
text: Towards the end of the year, Carausius is murdered by his finance minister Allectus, who proclaims himself the new emperor of Britain.

summary: Constantius defeated the Franks in Batavia.
text: In this or the following year, Constantius defeats the Franks in Batavia (Netherlands).

summary: Galerius began campaigns in Upper Egypt against rebel cities including Coptos and against the Blemmyes and Meroitic Nubians.
text: Galerius begins a series of two campaigns in Upper Egypt against the rebel cities of Coptos and Boresis as well as the Blemmyes and Meroitic Nubians.

summary: Diocletian reorganized the provinces of the Roman Empire into smaller units grouped into dioceses and separated civil and military authority.
text: Over the course of his reign, but especially from the time of the Tetrarchy's creation, Diocletian divides the large provinces of the early empire into smaller administrative units, and he groups these new smaller provinces into dioceses. He also accelerates the third-century trend whereby the administration and military of the provinces are increasingly divided between governors and generals (duces) respectively, whereas formerly governors had also been in charge of the legions. This expansion of imperial personnel increases Diocletian's control over the empire and weakens the power of individual officials and officers. Moreover, Diocletian expands the retinues of the individual emperors to have more ministers and secretaries, thus establishing what will become known as the late Roman Consistorium.

summary: Narseh marched on Ctesiphon and overthrew King Bahram III to become King of Kings of the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Bahram II of the Persian Empire dies after a 17-year reign; his son Bahram III ascends to the throne. After four months, Bahram III's great-uncle Narseh, the king of Persarmenia, marches on the Persian capital Ctesiphon with the support of a faction of the nobility and the eastern Satraps. Bahram is overthrown and Narseh is declared the new King of Kings.

summary: Probus succeeded Rufinus as Bishop of Byzantium.
text: Probus succeeds Rufinus, as Bishop of Byzantium.

summary: Bahram II, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Bahram II, king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Bahram III, king of the Sasanian Empire, died after being overthrown.
text: Bahram III, king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Carausius, Roman general and usurper, died.
text: Carausius, Roman general and usurper

summary: Emperor Diocletian defeated the Carpi.
text: Emperor Diocletian defeats the Carpi.

summary: Galerius concluded his military campaigns in Upper Egypt against Coptos, Boresis, the Blemmyes, and Meroitic Nubians.
text: Caesar Galerius completes a series of two campaigns in Upper Egypt, against the rebel cities of Coptos and Boresis, as well as the Blemmyes and Meroitic Nubians.

summary: The jurist Hermogenianus produced the Hermogenian Code at the court of Diocletian.
text: The jurist Hermogenianus, at the court of Diocletian, produces the Hermogenian Code. This new codification of Roman law complements the Gregorian Code of c. 292.

summary: Diocletian issued an edict banning incestuous marriages throughout the Roman Empire.
text: Diocletian, perhaps through Galerius, issues an edict against incest.

summary: Petra rejoined the province of Palestine and was converted to Christianity by the monk Barsauma.
text: Petra rejoins the province of Palestine, and is converted to Christianity by the Syrian monk Barsauma.

summary: Maximilian of Tebessa, Christian saint and martyr, died.
text: Maximilian of Tebessa, Berber Christian saint and martyr

summary: Constantius Chlorus and Asclepiodotus defeated and killed the usurper Allectus and re-incorporated Britain into the Roman Empire.
text: In this or the previous year, Caesar Constantius I assembles two invasion fleets with the intent of overthrowing the usurper Allectus, who is based in Britain. The first is under the command of Asclepiodotus, Maximian's long-serving Praetorian Prefect. Asclepiodotus sails from the mouth of the Seine, and lands near the Isle of Wight, where his forces defeat Allectus in Hampshire. Allectus is killed in the fighting. Constantius leaves Boulogne with his fleet, and occupies London, where he slaughters some of Allectus' Frankish mercenaries. With this victory, the Romano-British regime first established by Carausius is overthrown, and Britain is re-incorporated into the rest of the empire.

summary: Maximian fought Frankish pirates in Spain before crossing to North Africa to fight the Quinquegentiani.
text: Having supervised the Rhine frontier during Constantius' invasion of Britain, Maximian then marches into Spain, where he fights Frankish pirates. He then crosses into North Africa to contend with the rebellion of the Quinquegentiani.

summary: King Narseh invaded Roman Upper Mesopotamia and western Armenia, defeating Galerius between Carrhae and Callinicum.
text: The Persian king Narseh invades Roman-held Upper Mesopotamia and Arsacid western Armenia, the latter territory being under the leadership of the pro-Roman king Tiridates III. With only a small army, Caesar Galerius fights three holding actions against Narseh's army in Mesopotamia. Somewhere in the open plains between Carrhae and Callinicum, Galerius' army suffers a defeat against the Persian army, which is both more numerous and contains superior numbers of high-quality cavalry. Nevertheless, Galerius succeeds in blunting the Persian offensive.

summary: Marcellinus succeeded Pope Caius as the bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Caius dies after a 13-year reign and is succeeded by Marcellinus as the 29th pope of Rome.

summary: Pope Caius, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Caius, bishop of Rome

summary: Allectus, Roman usurper-emperor in Britain, was killed in battle.
text: Allectus, Roman treasurer and usurper-emperor

summary: Emperor Diocletian introduced a comprehensive new tax system and economic reforms.
text: Emperor Diocletian introduces a new tax system and other economic reforms.
