summary: Magnentius was proclaimed emperor by the Roman army at Augustodunum in Gaul.
text: Western Roman Emperor Constans I makes himself extremely unpopular; one of his generals, Magnentius, is proclaimed emperor at Augustodunum in the Diocese of Galliae, with the support of the army on the Rhine frontier.

summary: Western Roman Emperor Constans fled towards Spain and was assassinated at Castrum Helenae by agents of Magnentius.
text: January – Constans I flees towards Spain, where he is subsequently assassinated at Castrum Helenae. Magnentius rules the Western portion of the Roman Empire and is far more tolerant towards Christians and Pagans alike.

summary: Vetranio was persuaded by Constantina to proclaim himself Caesar in Illyricum and received funding from Constantius II.
text: Vetranio is asked by Constantina, sister of Constantius II, to proclaim himself Caesar. Constantius accepts the new emperor and sends him funds to raise an army.

summary: Marcellinus, a general sent by Magnentius, defeated and killed the usurper Nepotianus in Rome.
text: Nepotianus is defeated and killed by Marcellinus, a trusted general sent by Magnentius. His head is put on a spear and carried around the city.

summary: Constantius II met Vetranio at Naissus and forced him to abdicate his imperial title.
text: Vetranio meets Constantius II at Naissus (Serbia) and joins forces with him. Vetranio is forced to abdicate his title, and Constantius allows him to live as a private citizen on a state pension.

summary: The Huns began invading the Sasanian Empire.
text: About this time the Huns begin to invade the Sassanid Empire.

text: The city of Anbar (Iraq) is founded by king Shapur II.

text: Martin of Tongres, Roman Catholic bishop and saint;

summary: Nepotianus, Roman usurper, was killed in Rome.
text: Nepotianus, Roman usurper;

summary: Cassian of Autun, bishop of Autun, died.
text: Cassian of Autun Roman Catholic bishop and saint;

summary: Paul I of Constantinople, exiled bishop of Constantinople, was murdered in Cucusus.
text: Paul I of Constantinople, Byzantine Orthodox bishop and saint.

summary: Nepotianus entered Rome with a band of gladiators and declared himself imperator.
text: Constantius Chlorus's grandson Nepotianus entered Rome with a band of gladiators and there declared himself imperator.

summary: Constantius II elevated Constantius Gallus to Caesar at Sirmium and put him in charge of the eastern provinces.
text: Emperor Constantius II elevates his 25-year-old cousin Constantius Gallus to Caesar at Sirmium (Pannonia). He arranges a marriage with his sister Constantina, and puts him in charge of the Eastern portion of the Roman Empire.

summary: Constantius II marched west with a large army to confront the usurper Magnentius in Pannonia.
text: Constantius II marches West with a large field army (around 60,000 men) to topple Magnus Magnentius in Pannonia.

summary: The Jewish revolt against Constantius Gallus broke out in Palestine, destroying the Roman garrison at Sepphoris.
text: The Jewish revolt against Constantius Gallus breaks out. After his arrival at Antioch, the Jews begin a rebellion in Palestine. The Roman garrison in the town of Diocesarea is wiped out.

summary: Constantius II defeated Magnentius at the Battle of Mursa Major along the Drava.
text: Battle of Mursa Major: Constantius II defeats the usurper Magnentius along the valley of the Drava. The battle is one of the bloodiest in Roman military history. During the fighting Marcellinus, a general of Magnentius is killed; Magnentius himself survives.

summary: Magnentius fled to Aquileia and fortified the Alpine passes.
text: Winter – Magnentius flees to Aquileia in northern Italy and fortifies the mountain passes in the Alps.

summary: Macedonius I was restored as Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Macedonius is restored as Patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Flavius Romulus, Roman consul, died.
text: Flavius Romulus, Roman consul

summary: Marcellinus, Roman general and official under Magnentius, died during the Battle of Mursa Major.
text: Marcellinus, Roman general (magister officiorum)

summary: Constantius II invaded northern Italy in pursuit of Magnentius, who withdrew to Gaul.
text: Emperor Constantius II invades northern Italy in pursuit of the usurper Magnus Magnentius, who withdraws with his army to Gaul. He declares an amnesty for Magnentius' soldiers, many of whom desert to him.

summary: Constantius II entered Milan by the end of the year.
text: By the end of the year Constantius enters Milan.

summary: The Alamanni and Franks crossed the Rhine, defeating Roman frontier units and capturing dozens of settlements.
text: The Alamanni and the Franks cross the Rhine and defeat the depleted Roman units left at the frontier. The Germans take control of around 40 towns and cities between the Moselle and the Rhine.

summary: Ursicinus brutally suppressed the Jewish revolt in Palestine and stationed a permanent Roman garrison in Galilee.
text: Constantius Gallus sends his general (magister equitum) Ursicinus to forcefully put down the Jewish revolt in Palestine. The rebels destroy the cities Diopolis and Tiberias, while Diocesarea is razed to the ground. Ursicinus gives the order to kill thousands of Jews, even children. After the revolt, a permanent garrison is stationed in Galilee.

summary: Pope Liberius succeeded Pope Julius I as Bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Julius I dies after a 15-year reign in which he has made himself the chief opponent of Arianism. He is succeeded by Pope Liberius as the 36th pope, who immediately writes to Constantius II requesting a council at Aquileia to discuss the former Alexandrian patriarch Athanasius, who opposes the Arian belief to which the emperor subscribes.

summary: Arsenius the Great was born.
text: Arsenius the Great, anchorite and Desert Father

summary: Pope Julius I, bishop of Rome, died.
text: Julius I, bishop of Rome

summary: Constantius II defeated Magnentius at the Battle of Mons Seleucus, reunifying the Roman Empire after Magnentius committed suicide.
text: Battle of Mons Seleucus: Emperor Constantius II defeats the usurper Magnentius, who commits suicide in Gaul in order to avoid capture. Constantius becomes sole emperor, and reunifies the Roman Empire.

summary: Flavius Martinus, vicarius of Roman Britain, committed suicide after failing to kill the imperial inquisitor Paulus Catena.
text: Constantius II sends his official Paulus Catena to Britain, to hunt down the opponents supporting Magnentius. Flavius Martinus, vicarius of Britain and supporter of Constantius, opposes the persecutions; he is then accused by Catena of being a traitor. In response, Martinus tries to kill Catena with a sword; he fails and then commits suicide.

summary: Constantius II convened a synod at Arles that condemned Patriarch Athanasius of Alexandria.
text: Constantius II assembles a conciliabulum at Arles, and condemns Athanasius as Patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Vigilius of Trent was born.
text: Saint Vigilius, Bishop of Trent (d. 405)

summary: The Roman usurper Magnentius committed suicide in Gaul.
text: Magnentius, Roman usurper (b. 303)

summary: Decentius, brother and Caesar of Magnentius, committed suicide in Sens.
text: Magnus Decentius, brother and Caesar of Magnentius

summary: Flavius Martinus, vicarius of Roman Britain, died.
text: Flavius Martinus, vicarius of Roman Britain

summary: Emperor Constantius II recalled his Caesar Constantius Gallus to Constantinople, stripped him of his powers, and had him executed at Pola.
text: Emperor Constantius II recalls his Caesar (and cousin) Constantius Gallus to Constantinople after hearing unfavorable reports about him. Gallus, Caesar of the East, has suppressed revolts in Syria Palaestina and central Anatolia. Constantius strips him of his powers and later has him executed in Pola (Croatia).

summary: The Roman Calendar of 354 was drawn up as an illuminated manuscript codex.
text: The Roman Calendar of 354, an illuminated manuscript, is drawn up and becomes the earliest dated codex.

summary: Franks and Alemanni crossed the upper Rhine into Gaul and invaded the territory of the Helvetii after Western Roman forces were withdrawn.
text: As a result of the armies of the West having been largely withdrawn by the usurper Magnus Magnentius, to fight Constantius II, hordes of barbarians (Franks and Alemanni) cross the upper Rhine into Gaul and invade the lands of the Helvetians.

summary: The Bulgars were first mentioned in surviving European chronicles.
text: The Bulgars are first mentioned in extant European chronicles.

summary: Libanius became a teacher of rhetoric in Antioch, instructing John Chrysostom and Theodore of Mopsuestia.
text: Libanius becomes a teacher of rhetoric in Antioch; his students include John Chrysostom and Theodore of Mopsuestia.

summary: Augustine of Hippo was born in Thagaste.
text: Augustine of Hippo, North African bishop (d. 430)

summary: Christian hermit and saint Apa Bane was born.
text: Apa Bane, Christian hermit and saint

summary: Paulinus of Nola was born near Burdigala.
text: Paulinus of Nola, French bishop and writer (d. 431)

summary: Pelagius, the monk and theologian, was born in Roman Britain.
text: Pelagius, English monk and theologian (d. 418)

summary: Constantina, daughter of Emperor Constantine the Great, died in Bithynia.
text: Constantina, daughter of Constantine the Great (b. c. 320)

summary: Constantius Gallus was executed at Pola on the orders of Constantius II.
text: Constantius Gallus, Roman consul and statesman (b. 326)

summary: Arbitio and Lollianus Mavortius entered office as Roman consuls.
text: Arbitio and Lollianus Mavortius begin their term as Roman consuls.
cast: Quintus Flavius Maesius Egnatius Lollianus Mavortius
names: Quintus Flavius Maesius Egnatius Lollianus Mavortius

summary: Ursicinus arrived in Colonia Agrippinensium and had the usurper Claudius Silvanus murdered.
text: Claudius Silvanus, accused of treason, proclaims himself Roman Emperor. After 28 days, Ursicinus arrives from Rome and has Silvanus murdered.

summary: Emperor Constantius II raised his cousin Julian to the rank of Caesar at Mediolanum and gave him command of the western provinces.
text: In Mediolanum (Italy), Emperor Constantius II raises his cousin Julian the Apostate to the rank of Caesar. He takes command of the western provinces and marries Constantius' sister, Helena.

summary: The Roman commander Arbitio fined the Germanic Lentienses tribe after their incursions into the Roman Empire.
text: The Lentienses, a Germanic tribe, are fined by the Roman commander Arbetio under Constantius II for several incursions against the Roman Empire.

summary: The Franks besieged Colonia Agrippinensium for ten months.
text: The Franks besiege Colonia Agrippinensium for ten months.

summary: Emperor Constantius II exiled Pope Liberius to Beroea after he refused to condemn Athanasius, replacing him with Felix II.
text: Pope Liberius refuses to sign a condemnation of Athanasius, Patriarch of Alexandria, imposed at Milan by Constantius II. Liberius is exiled to Beroea (Greece) and replaced by Felix II. He becomes an antipope and bishop of Rome.

summary: Claudius Silvanus, Roman general and short-lived usurper, was murdered in Colonia Agrippinensium.
text: Claudius Silvanus, Roman usurper

summary: Aedesius, Roman Neoplatonist philosopher, died in Pergamum.
text: Aedesius, Roman Neoplatonist philosopher and mystic

summary: Emperor Constantius II ordered the closure of all pagan temples and banished Patriarch Athanasius of Alexandria, who fled into the desert.
text: Emperor Constantius II issues a decree closing all pagan temples in the Roman Empire, and ordering the banishment once again of the anti-Arian patriarch of Alexandria, Athanasius. He tries to have him arrested during a vigil service, but Athanasius flees to the Nitrian desert in Upper Egypt.

summary: The veneration of non-Christian images was banned across the Roman Empire.
text: The veneration of non-Christian images is banned in the Roman Empire.

summary: The Alemanni besieged Augustodunum whose walls were in disrepair.
text: Siege of Autun: Julian receives a report that Augustodunum (Autun) is under attack by the Alemanni. The city walls are in poor state and in danger of falling.

summary: The Alemanni defeated Caesar Julian at the Battle of Reims in Gaul.
text: Battle of Reims: Julian is defeated by the Alemanni at Reims (Gaul).

summary: Julian defeated Germanic warbands at the Battle of Brumath in Alsace.
text: Battle of Brumath: Roman forces pursue Germanic warbands through the Gallic countryside. Julian wins an open battle near Brumath (Alsace).

summary: The Alemanni invaded the Roman province of Rhaetia.
text: Rhaetia (Switzerland) is invaded by the Alemanni.

summary: Hostile Germanic warbands besieged Julian at Senonae after Roman foederati deserted.
text: Winter – Siege of Senonae: Julian over-winters at Senonae (Bourgogne). German federated troops (foederati) desert and hostile warbands besiege the town.

summary: Anthony the Great died at his hermitage near the Red Sea at approximately 105 years of age.
text: Anthony the Great (pictured) dies at his hermitage near the Red Sea in mid-January at age 105 (approximate), having preached against Arianism, and having tried to codify guidelines for monastic life. His followers subsequently establish the Monastery of Saint Anthony, beginning the tradition of Coptic monasticism.

summary: Construction began on the first basilica of Saint Peter in Rome.
text: Construction begins on the first basilica of Saint Peter in Rome.

summary: Aelia Flaccilla, future Roman empress and wife of Theodosius I, was born.
text: 31 March – Aelia Flaccilla, Roman empress and wife of Theodosius I (d. 386)

summary: John II, future bishop of Jerusalem and Christian theologian, was born.
text: John II, Byzantine bishop, theologian and writer (d. 417)

summary: Bishop Amasius of Teano died.
text: Amasius of Teano, bishop Teano (also known as St. Paris)

summary: Egyptian monk and Desert Father Anthony the Great died.
text: Anthony the Great, Egyptian monk and Desert Father

summary: Bishop and missionary Sanctinus of Meaux died.
text: Sanctinus of Meaux, French bishop and missionary (b. 270)

summary: Former Roman statesman, usurper, and co-emperor Vetranio died in retirement.
text: Vetranio, Roman statesman, usurper and co-emperor

summary: Constantius II entered Rome for the first time to celebrate his victory over Magnentius and addressed the Senate and the Roman people.
text: Emperor Constantius II enters Rome for the first time to celebrate his victory over Magnentius. He address the Senate and the Roman people.

summary: Julian defeated the Alemanni at the Battle of Strasbourg, driving them back behind the Rhine.
text: Summer – Battle of Strasbourg: Julian, Caesar (deputy emperor) and supreme commander of the Roman army in Gaul, wins an important victory against the Alemanni at Strasbourg (Argentoratum), driving the barbarians back behind the Rhine.

summary: The Imperial Library of Constantinople was founded by Constantius II.
text: The Imperial Library of Constantinople is founded.

summary: Ammianus Marcellinus described the Pantheon in Rome as rounded like the boundary of the horizon and vaulted with loftiness.
text: Ammianus Marcellinus describes the Pantheon as being "rounded like the boundary of the horizon and vaulted with a beautiful loftiness".

summary: Constantius II received Persian ambassadors who demanded that Rome restore lands surrendered under King Narseh.
text: Winter – Constantius II receives ambassadors from the Persian Empire. They demand that Rome restore the lands surrendered by King Narseh.

summary: Pope Liberius visited Sirmium and signed documents weakening the Nicene Creed, leading to George of Cappadocia replacing Athanasius as patriarch of Alexandria.
text: Late in the year Pope Liberius travels to Sirmium (Pannonia) and agrees to sign documents that effectively undo the Nicene Creed (which implicitly disavows Arianism) and to sever his relationship with the former Alexandrian patriarch Athanasius, who is replaced as patriarch of Alexandria by his Arian opponent George of Cappadocia.

summary: Constantius II ordered the relics of Saint Andrew the Apostle transferred from Patras to the Church of the Holy Apostles in Constantinople.
text: At about this date, the relics of St Andrew the Apostle are taken from Patras to Constantinople by order of the Emperor Constantius II, and deposited in the Church of the Holy Apostles.

summary: Basil of Caesarea visited the monastic communities of Egypt.
text: At about this date, Basil of Caesarea visits Egypt.

summary: Constantius II fortified upper Mesopotamia and rejected territorial demands brought by an emissary of King Shapur II of Persia.
text: Emperor Constantius II builds new forts to secure upper Mesopotamia. Persia's king Shapur II sends an emissary to Constantinople with gifts and a letter wrapped in white silk. He requests that Constantius return the lands of his ancestors from the Euphrates to the frontier of Macedonia. Constantius tactfully refuses to cede any territories.

summary: The Salian Franks surrendered to Julian in Gaul and were settled as Roman foederati in Toxandria.
text: The Salian Franks capitulate to Julian the Apostate in Gaul. He allows them to form a Roman foederati in Toxandria. Frankish settlers are established in areas in the north and the east to help with the defense of the Rhine frontier.

summary: Constantius II repulsed an invasion of Pannonia by the Quadi and the Sarmatians.
text: An invasion of Pannonia by the Quadi and the Sarmates is repulsed by Constantius II.

summary: A major earthquake destroyed Nicomedia and damaged cities across Macedonia, Asia, and Pontus.
text: An earthquake destroys Nicomedia, and damages 150 cities in Macedonia, Asia and Pontus.

summary: Constantius II recalled Pope Liberius to Rome, prompting Antipope Felix II to retire to his estate.
text: Constantius II recalls Pope Liberius to Rome, where he receives a joyous welcome from the Christians. Antipope Felix II prudently retires to his estate near Porto (Portugal).

summary: Eudoxius became Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Eudoxius becomes Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: The Great Sanhedrin issued its last universally binding decision to establish a fixed Hebrew calendar.
text: The last universally binding decision, of the Great Sanhedrin, establishes a fixed Hebrew calendar.

summary: Christian bishop Aignan of Orleans was born.
text: Aignan of Orleans, Christian bishop (d. 453)

summary: Paulinus of Trier, Christian bishop and saint, died in exile in Phrygia.
text: Paulinus of Trier, Christian bishop and saint

summary: Shapur II invaded southern Armenia, leading the Romans to initiate a scorched-earth defense along the Euphrates crossings.
text: King Shapur II the Great of the Persian Empire invades southern Armenia. The Romans implement a scorched earth policy and place strong guards at the Euphrates crossings.

summary: Shapur II captured the Roman fortress of Amida after a seventy-three-day siege and massacred its inhabitants.
text: Siege of Amida: Shapur II besieges the Roman fortress of Amida (modern Diyarbakir). After seventy-three days the city is conquered and the population is massacred by the Persians. Ammianus Marcellinus is a fortunate survivor and flees to Singara (Iraq).

summary: Honoratus took office as the first known Urban Prefect of Constantinople.
text: The first known Prefect of the city of Constantinople, Honoratus, takes office.

summary: A Roman fleet shipped grain from Britain across the Rhine to relieve a famine in the Upper Rhineland.
text: Famine in Upper Rhineland: A fleet of 800 river boats, built for the Rhine, cross to the British east coast, and carry back enough corn to raise the famine.

summary: Shapur II halted his invasion of the Roman Empire due to heavy casualties.
text: Winter – Shapur II halts his campaign, due to heavy casualties during the Persian invasion.

summary: The Sarcophagus of Junius Bassus was carved for his burial in Old Saint Peter's Basilica.
text: The Sarcophagus of Junius Bassus, in the Old St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican, is made .

summary: Emperor Constantius II convened the Council of Rimini to address the Arian crisis in the Western church.
text: July – Emperor Constantius II convenes the Council of Rimini, to resolve the crisis over Arianism in the Church. Some 400 bishops of the Western portion of the Roman Empire attend, while the Eastern bishops simultaneously hold a meeting at Seleucia. Given Saint Jerome's comment that, "The whole world groaned in astonishment to find itself Arian", it appears to have failed. Pope Liberius rejects the new creed at Rimini.

summary: Godigisel, future king of the Vandals, was born.
text: Godigisel, king of the Vandals (d. 406)

summary: Future Roman emperor Gratian was born in Sirmium.
text: Gratian, Roman emperor (d. 383)

summary: Stilicho, future Roman general and patrician, was born.
text: Stilicho, Roman general (d. 408)

summary: Roman magister militum Barbatio was executed for treason.
text: Barbatio, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Hosius of Corduba, longtime bishop and theological advisor, died.
text: Hosius of Corduba, Christian bishop (b. 256)

summary: Junius Bassus Theotecnius, urban prefect of Rome, died in office.
text: Junius Bassus Theotecnius, Roman politician

summary: Julian repelled an Alemannic raid into Raetia, driving them across the Rhine into the Black Forest.
text: The Alamanni raid Raetia (Switzerland), but are pushed back behind the Rhine by Julian, into the Black Forest.

summary: King Shapur II captured the Roman fortresses of Singara and Bezabde.
text: King Shapur II continues his campaign against the Roman fortresses, capturing Singara, Bezabde and Nisibis.

summary: Emperor Constantius II and Julian exchanged letters in an attempt to avert civil war.
text: Emperor Constantius II and Julian exchange several letters, both hoping to avoid a civil war.

summary: The Huns invaded the Pontic steppes, displacing the Alans, Heruli, Ostrogoths, and Visigoths.
text: The Huns invade the Pontic steppes by the thousands, spreading terror as they take over territories held for generations by Alans, Heruls, Ostrogoths and Visigoths.

summary: Roman Britain exported grain to supply the legions stationed along the Rhine.
text: Roman authorities in Britain export wheat to supply the legions on the Rhine; they have encouraged production of wheat for that purpose.

summary: The first Hagia Sophia church was consecrated in Constantinople.
text: 14 February – The first Hagia Sophia church is consecrated in Constantinople.

summary: Emperor Constantius II convened the Council of Constantinople, which enforced an Arian creed and deposed rival bishops.
text: Council of Constantinople (360): Emperor Constantius II requests a church council, at Constantinople; both the eastern and western bishops attend the meeting. Ulfilas also attends the council and endorses the resulting creed. After the council several homoiousian bishops are deposed or banished, including Macedonius I of Constantinople and Cyril of Jerusalem.

summary: Martin of Tours founded Ligugé Abbey under the direction of Bishop Hilary of Poitiers.
text: At about this date, Ligugé Abbey in France is founded for the monastic Order of Saint Benedict by Martin of Tours, under dispensation from Bishop Hilary of Poitiers.

summary: John Cassian, Christian monk and theologian, was born.
text: John Cassian, Desert Father and Christian saint

summary: Mesrop Mashtots, Armenian scholar and theologian who invented the Armenian alphabet, was born.
text: Saint Mesrob, Armenian monk and theologian

summary: Saint Ninian, Christian missionary to Scotland, was born.
text: Saint Ninian, missionary to Scotland

summary: Bishop and Christian martyr Judas Cyriacus died.
text: Judas Cyriacus, Roman Catholic priest and saint

summary: Bishop Gaudentius of Rimini died after being martyred by Arians.
text: Gaudentius of Rimini, Roman Catholic priest and saint

summary: Christian hermit Abramios the Recluse died near Edessa.
text: Abramios the Recluse, Byzantine Orthodox priest and saint

summary: Auxentius of Mopsuestia, bishop and Christian saint, died.
text: Auxentius of Mopsuestia, Byzantine Orthodox priest and saint

summary: Eusebius of Emesa, bishop and theologian, died in Antioch.
text: Eusebius of Emesa, Byzantine Orthodox bishop and saint (b. 290)

summary: The Petulantes mutinied in Paris and proclaimed Julian augustus.
text: The Petulantes, ordered east from Paris in preparation for a war with the Sasanian Empire, instead mutinied and proclaimed Julian augustus.

summary: Julian led his army eastward from Gaul to confront Emperor Constantius II.
text: July – Julian begins leading his troops eastwards against Constantius II.

summary: Emperor Constantius II died of a fever at Mopsuestia after naming Julian his rightful successor.
text: Emperor Constantius II dies of a fever at Mopsuestia in Cilicia, age 44; on his deathbed he is baptised, and declares his cousin Julian rightful successor.

summary: Julian became sole emperor of the Roman Empire and entered Constantinople to promote paganism.
text: Julian becomes sole emperor of the Roman Empire; he rules from Constantinople, and tries to restore paganism. Constantius II is buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles.

summary: The Chalcedon tribunal prosecuted and condemned ministers of the late Constantius II.
text: Ministers and followers of Constantius II are put on trial, at the Chalcedon Tribunal.

summary: A coin depicting Emperor Julian the Apostate was minted.
text: 361–363 – A Julian the Apostate coin is issued. It is now kept at the British Museum, London.

summary: Authorities in Constantinople instituted a strict licensing system for practicing physicians.
text: Constantinople enforces a strict licensing system for physicians.

summary: Julian attempted to organize an official pagan church to rival and replace Christianity.
text: Emperor Julian tries to organize a pagan church and substitute it for Christianity. Pope Liberius repudiates the Arian creed, and declares that the Council of Ariminum has no authority to issue decrees.

summary: Gregory of Nazianzus returned to Nazianzus and was ordained a priest by his father.
text: Gregory Nazianzus (Saint Gregory the Theologian) returns to Nazianzus and is appointed a priest by his father, who wants him to assist local Christians.

summary: Construction began on the Monastery of Saint Anthony in the Eastern Desert of Egypt.
text: Construction of the Monastery of Saint Anthony in the Eastern Desert of Egypt begins.

summary: Athanasius of Alexandria returned to Alexandria after the murder of the rival bishop George of Cappadocia.
text: George of Cappadocia, the Arian intruding bishop of Alexandria, is murdered in his see and Athanasius of Alexandria returns to his native city in triumph.

summary: Emperor Constantius II died of a fever in Cilicia.
text: November – Constantius II, Roman Emperor (b. 317)

summary: George of Cappadocia was murdered by a mob in Alexandria.
text: December 24: George of Cappadocia, Byzantine Orthodox archbishop and saint

summary: Bishop George of Laodicea died.
text: December 24: George of Laodicea, Byzantine Orthodox archbishop and saint

summary: The Roman secret agent Apodemius was executed at Chalcedon.
text: Apodemius, Roman officer and secret agent

summary: The Roman grand chamberlain Eusebius was condemned and executed at Chalcedon.
text: Eusebius, Roman officer

summary: Maximus, Bishop of Naples, died in exile.
text: Maximus of Naples, Roman Catholic archbishop and saint

summary: Emperor Julian arrived at Antioch with an expeditionary force to prepare a major campaign against the Sasanian Empire.
text: Emperor Julian arrives at Antioch with an expeditionary force (60,000 men), and stays there for nine months, to launch a campaign against the Persian Empire. He secures the co-operation of King Arsaces of Armenia, who fights a bloody guerrilla war against the Persians.

summary: Emperor Julian constructed a large fleet of warships and transport boats at Samosata for his campaign against Persia.
text: Julian builds a fleet of 50 warships, and more than 1,000 transport boats at Samosata, for his expedition in Persia against King Shapur II the Great.

summary: An earthquake struck the city of Nicaea.
text: An earthquake strikes Nicaea (Turkey).

summary: An earthquake struck the city of Al-Karak.
text: An earthquake strikes Al-Karak (Jordan).

summary: Emperor Julian ordered Athanasius of Alexandria into exile after Athanasius convened a church council in the city.
text: Athanasius returns to Alexandria and convenes a council, at which he appeals for unity among Christians who differ in terminology, but Emperor Julian orders Athanasius to leave Alexandria. He will remain in exile in Upper Egypt, until after Julian's death the next year.

summary: The temple of Apollo at Daphne outside Antioch was destroyed by fire.
text: The temple of Apollo at Daphne, outside Antioch, is destroyed in a mysterious fire.

summary: Flavia Maxima Constantia, posthumous daughter of Constantius II, was born.
text: Flavia Maxima Constantia, daughter of Constantius II

summary: The Armenian linguist and scholar Mesrop Mashtots was born.
text: Mesrop Mashtots, Armenian linguist (d. 440)

summary: The Roman imperial notary Paulus Catena was executed at Chalcedon.
text: Paulus Catena, Roman politician

summary: Bishop Reginos of Skopelos died.
text: Reginos, Greek Orthodox bishop and saint

summary: The Christian martyrs Gordianus and Epimachus were put to death at Rome.
text: Gordianus and Epimachus, Roman Catholic priests, martyrs and saints

summary: Bishop Dorotheus of Tyre was martyred at Odessos.
text: Dorotheus of Tyre, Roman Catholic bishop and martyr (b. 255)

summary: Crispus, Crispinianus, and Benedicta were martyred at Rome.
text: Crispus, Crispinianus, and Benedicta, Roman Catholic, priests, martyrs and saints

summary: Basil of Ancyra was martyred during the persecutions under Julian.
text: Basil of Ancyra, Byzantine Orthodox bishop and saint

summary: Eusignius of Antioch was martyred at Antioch under Julian.
text: Eusignius of Antioch, Byzantine Orthodox bishop and martyr (b. 252)

summary: Bishop Donatus of Arezzo was martyred.
text: Donatus of Arezzo, Roman Catholic bishop and saint

summary: The Christian martyr Eliphius was put to death in Gaul.
text: Eliphius, Roman Catholic priest and saint

summary: The Roman military commander and martyr Artemius was executed at Antioch.
text: October 20: Artemius, Egyptian Orthodox martyr and saint

summary: The Christian priest Theodoret of Antioch was martyred.
text: October 20: Theodoret of Antioch, Syrian Christian priest and martyr

summary: Gemellus of Ancyra was martyred during the reign of Julian.
text: Gemellus of Ancyra, Byzantine Orthodox bishop and saint

summary: Emperor Julian departed Antioch with his invasion army and sent Procopius on a diversionary march toward Armenia.
text: Emperor Julian departs from Antioch with his army (90,000 men) and heads north towards the Euphrates. En route he creates a diversion and sends a force of 30,000 soldiers under his cousin Procopius to Armenia.

summary: Emperor Julian bridged the Euphrates near Hierapolis, advanced to Carrhae, and destroyed the Persian fortress of Perisapora.
text: April – Julian crosses the Euphrates near Hierapolis, using 50 pontoon ships, and moves eastwards to Carrhae. He destroys Perisapora and overruns Persian forts along the desert frontier (Limes Arabicus).

summary: Emperor Julian defeated a Persian force outside Ctesiphon but found the capital heavily fortified while King Shapur II adopted a scorched-earth policy.
text: Battle of Ctesiphon: Julian reaches the vicinity of the strongly fortified capital Ctesiphon. King Shapur II in charge of a large Persian army adopts a scorched earth policy, leaving the Romans desperately short of supplies.

summary: Emperor Julian burned his fleet of supply boats on the Tigris and began retreating northward under repeated Persian attacks.
text: The Roman army starts its retreat northward to Corduene (Armenia). Julian marches back up the Tigris and burns his fleet of supply ships. During the withdrawal Julian's forces suffer several attacks from the Persians.

summary: Jovian was proclaimed Roman emperor by the army after Julian died of battle wounds near Samarra.
text: Battle of Samarra: Julian is mortally wounded in a skirmish and dies from a wound received during the fighting near Samarra (Iraq). Jovian, general of the Guard, succeeds him and is proclaimed Emperor by the troops.. The project to rebuild the Jewish Temple is permanently abandoned.

summary: Jovian negotiated a peace treaty with Persia, ceding several Roman provinces along with the frontier cities Nisibis and Singara.
text: Emperor Jovian negotiates a disastrous peace with Persia, surrendering four of the five Roman provinces gained by Caesar Galerius in 298, and the cities Nisibis and Singara (Mesopotamia).

summary: Egyptians revolted against Roman rule, resulting in armed clashes.
text: Egyptian rose in revolt against Roman occupation, armed clashes occur.

summary: The Galilee earthquake caused severe damage to the city of Petra.
text: 19 – Galilee earthquake of 363. Petra, capital of the Nabataeans (in modern-day Jordan), is seriously damaged.

summary: An earthquake damaged the cities of Arsakawan and Salat in Armenia.
text: 363 Arsakawan earthquake: It affects the cities of Arsakawan (modern Doğubayazıt) and Salat (modern Sisian).

summary: The Council of Laodicea was held and prohibited resting on the Saturday Sabbath, designating Sunday as the Christian day of worship.
text: The Council of Laodicea, which deals with constricting the conduct of church members, is held. The major canon approved by this council is Canon 29, which prohibits resting on the Sabbath (Saturday), restricting Christians to honoring the Lord on Sunday.
names: Canon law of the Catholic Church

summary: Christian writer Sulpicius Severus was born.
text: Sulpicius Severus, Christian writer

summary: Roman Emperor Julian died from wounds received during the Battle of Samarra.
text: Julian the Apostate, Roman emperor (b. 331)

summary: Gallo-Roman physician and writer Aemilia Hilaria died.
text: Aemilia Hilaria, Galo-Roman physician and writer (b. 300)

summary: Roman commander Lucillianus died.
text: Lucillianus, Roman commander (magister equitum)

summary: Emperor Jovian died under suspicious circumstances in his tent at Tyana after an eight-month reign.
text: Emperor Jovian dies after a reign of eight months. He is found dead in his tent at Tyana (Asia Minor) en route back to Constantinople, in suspicious circumstances.

summary: Roman army officers at Nicaea proclaimed Valentinian I emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Valentinian I is proclaimed Emperor by officers of the Roman army at Nicaea in Bithynia. He addresses the soldiers (who threaten to riot) in a speech. He founds the Valentinianic dynasty and rules the Western portion of the Roman Empire, from Caledonia (Scotland) to the Rhine frontier, ensuring it a few years of relative security. He settles in Lutetia (Paris) and establishes a militia to defend the region.

summary: Valentinian I appointed his brother Valens as co-emperor at the Hebdomon palace to govern the eastern provinces.
text: Valens, brother of Valentinian I, is appointed co-emperor (Augustus) in the palace of Hebdomon (Turkey). He rules the Eastern portion of the Roman Empire, from the Danube to the Persian border, and begins the first anti-pagan persecutions.

summary: Roman Britain endured fierce raids launched by barbarians.
text: Britain is forced to endure fierce barbarian raids.

summary: The Council of Laodicea settled disciplinary questions and attempted to define the Biblical canon.
text: The Council of Laodicea decides some disciplinary questions of the church and attempts to establish the Biblical canon, but fails.

summary: Theon of Alexandria observed both a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse.
text: Theon of Alexandria, Greek mathematician, observes a solar eclipse (June 16) and a lunar eclipse (November 25).

summary: Roman noblewoman Blaesilla was born.
text: Blaesilla, Roman noblewoman (d. 384)

summary: Roman Emperor Jovian died at Tyana.
text: Jovian, Roman emperor (b. 331)

summary: Christian bishop Theophilos the Indian died.
text: Theophilos the Indian, Christian bishop

summary: An undersea earthquake and tsunami devastated Crete and Alexandria, causing extensive damage across the eastern Mediterranean.
text: An earthquake and tsunami devastate Crete and Alexandria and affects Italy, Greece, and Palestine.

summary: Procopius revolted against Valens, bribed two passing legions, proclaimed himself emperor, and seized Thrace and Bithynia.
text: Procopius revolts and bribes two legions passing by Constantinople. He proclaims himself Emperor, and takes control of Thrace and Bithynia.

summary: The Alamanni crossed the Rhine and invaded Gaul, prompting Valentinian I to relocate his headquarters to Paris.
text: The Alamanni cross the Rhine and invade Gaul. Emperor Valentinian I moves to Paris to command the army and defend the Gallic cities.

summary: Basil of Caesarea was appointed presbyter of Caesarea in Cappadocia.
text: Basil of Caesarea becomes presbyter of Caesarea.

summary: Emperor Valens ordered the expulsion of Bishop Athanasius from Alexandria, prompting him to withdraw to the city outskirts.
text: Emperor Valens orders the expulsion of the Alexandrian bishop Athanasius from his see, but instead of going into exile Athanasius, now about 67, moves to the outskirts of Alexandria.

summary: Antipope Felix II died, ending the schism over the papacy in Rome.
text: Antipope Felix II dies after a 9-year reign, ending the double occupancy of the papacy.

summary: Future Roman consul and praetorian prefect Julius Agricola was born.
text: Julius Agricola, Roman consul and praetorian prefect

summary: Antipope Felix II died.
text: Felix II, antipope of Rome (b. 287)

summary: The Alamanni crossed the frozen Rhine and invaded Roman Gaul, capturing Alsace and much of the Swiss Plateau.
text: The Alamanni cross the frozen Rhine in large numbers, and invade the Gallic provinces. They capture Alsace and a large part of the Swiss Plateau.

summary: Valens crushed the revolt of Procopius at the Battle of Thyatira and had the usurper executed.
text: April – Battle of Thyatira: Emperor Valens defeats the troops of Procopius, bringing an end to his revolt; Serenianus and Marcellus are killed. Procopius flees the battlefield, but is executed by Valens.

summary: Valens built a pontoon bridge across the Danube and drove the Visigoths north.
text: Valens builds a pontoon bridge across the Danube, and drives the Visigoths further north, where they will come under pressure from the advancing Huns.

summary: Jovinus defeated the Alamanni in three successive battles and pushed them out of Gaul.
text: Winter – Emperor Valentinian I appoints Jovinus, his Master of the Horse (Magister Equitum), general of the army. He defeats the Alamanni in three successive battles, and pushes them out of Gaul.

summary: The Tabula Peutingeriana, an illustrated road map of the Roman world, was created.
text: The Tabula Peutingeriana, a map showing Roman possessions and roads, is created about this time.

summary: Athanasius of Alexandria returned from his fifth exile after four months in his ancestral tomb.
text: Athanasius of Alexandria returns from his fifth exile. He has spent four months in his ancestral tomb outside Alexandria.

summary: Pope Liberius died and Damasus I succeeded him as pope, while rival factions elected Ursicinus as antipope.
text: Pope Liberius dies after a 14-year reign and is succeeded by Damasus I as 37th pope. Romans unhappy with this choice elect the antipope Ursicinus.

summary: Valentinianus Galates, son of Emperor Valens, was born.
text: Valentinianus Galates, Roman emperor (d. 370)

summary: Christian priest and martyr Ajabel died during the persecutions in the Sasanian Empire.
text: Ajabel, Christian priest and martyr

summary: Roman usurper Procopius was captured and executed following the Battle of Thyatira.
text: Procopius, Roman general and usurper

summary: Christian bishop and saint Leo of Montefeltro died.
text: Leo of Montefeltro, Christian bishop and saint

summary: Pope Liberius died in Rome.
text: Liberius, pope of the Catholic Church (b. 310)

summary: Acacius, Bishop of Caesarea, died.
text: Acacius of Caesarea, Christian bishop

summary: Roman usurper Marcellus was captured and executed.
text: Marcellus, Roman general and usurper

summary: Saint Marinus, Christian hermit and traditional founder of San Marino, died.
text: Marinus, Christian hermit and saint (b. 275)

summary: Roman general Serenianus was killed during the suppression of Procopius's revolt.
text: Serenianus, Roman general of the Imperial Guard

summary: The Alamanni crossed the Rhine and plundered Moguntiacum, prompting Emperor Valentinian I to launch a punitive campaign.
text: Battle of Solicinium: Emperor Valentinian I launches a punitive expedition against the Alamanni, due to the crises in Britannia and Gaul. The Alamanni re-cross the Rhine and plunder Moguntiacum (modern Mainz).

summary: Valentinian I decreed that Christians could not be forced into gladiator training schools.
text: Valentinian I declares that Christians will not be forced into gladiator training schools.

summary: The Roman garrison on Hadrian's Wall mutinied, enabling Picts, Scotti, Attacotti, and Saxons to invade and devastate Roman Britain.
text: Great Conspiracy: The Roman garrison on Hadrian's Wall revolts and allows Picts from Caledonia to devastate Britain. Simultaneously Attacotti, the Scotti from Hibernia (Ireland), and the Saxons from Germania invade the island's mid-western and south-eastern borders. They sack the cities and murder, rape or enslave Romano-British civilians.

summary: Eunomius of Cyzicus was banished to Mauretania for harbouring the usurper Procopius.
text: Eunomius of Cyzicus is banished to Mauretania for harbouring the usurper Procopius.

summary: Valentinian I elevated his son Gratian to the rank of Augustus.
text: Gratian receives the title of Augustus under his father, Valentinian I.

summary: Valentinian I mobilized Italian and Illyrian legions for a planned offensive against the Alamanni and Franks.
text: Winter – Valentinian I mobilises a massive army for his campaign against the Alamanni and the Franks. He summons the Italian and Illyrian legions for a spring offensive.

summary: Athanasius of Alexandria listed the twenty-seven books of the New Testament in his festal letter.
text: The first Listing of the New Testament (Bible) is made by St. Athanasius of Alexandria.

summary: The urban prefects banished Antipope Ursicinus from Rome to Gaul.
text: Antipope Ursicinus is banished by the praefecti to Gaul.

summary: Epiphanius became bishop of Salamis in Cyprus.
text: Epiphanius of Salamis becomes bishop of Salamis, Cyprus.

summary: Eudoxius of Antioch baptized Emperor Valens into Arian Christianity.
text: Emperor Valens is baptized by Eudoxius of Antioch.

summary: Hilary of Poitiers, bishop and Doctor of the Church, died.
text: Hilary of Poitiers, Byzantine bishop, Doctor of the Church and saint (b. c. 315)

summary: Emperor Valentinian I crossed the Rhine with Gratian, defeated the Alemanni, and concluded a temporary peace with King Macrian.
text: Spring – Emperor Valentinian I and his 8-year-old son, Gratian, cross the Rhine with an army into Alamannic territory. He defeats the Alemanni and burns food stores along the border. A temporary peace is signed with Macrian, king of the Bucinobantes, and Valentinian returns to his capital Augusta Treverorum (modern Trier).

summary: Theodosius the Elder arrived in Britain with a relief army to liberate Londinium from invading Picts, Scotti, and Saxons.
text: Great Conspiracy: Picts, Scotti and Saxons reach Roman London and plunder the city. Theodosius, a general (Comes Britanniarum), is sent with a relief force to Britannia. He marches from Richborough, Kent, to deal with the invaders.

summary: Theodosius the Elder recovered Hadrian's Wall, restored order in Roman Britain, and mounted punitive expeditions into Ireland.
text: Winter – The barbarians are driven back to their homelands, Hadrian's Wall is retaken and order returns to the Roman diocese. Theodosius reorganises the abandoned forts and mounts punitive expeditions in Hibernia (Ireland).

summary: An earthquake struck the Roman city of Nicaea.
text: 11 October – An earthquake strikes Nicaea (modern Turkey).

summary: Eustochium, an early Christian Desert Mother and saint, was born in Rome.
text: Eustochium, Christian Desert Mother and saint

summary: Philostorgius, Anomoean Christian church historian, was born in Cappadocia.
text: Philostorgius, Anomoean church historian and writer (d. 439)

summary: Maternien, bishop of Reims, died.
text: Maternien, Christian bishop and saint

summary: Caesarius of Nazianzus, Roman physician and imperial official, died.
text: Caesarius of Nazianzus, Roman physician and politician

summary: Vulcacius Rufinus, Roman politician and praetorian prefect, died.
text: Vulcacius Rufinus, Roman prefect, consul and politician

summary: Emperor Valens crossed the Danube to attack Gothic tribes and concluded a peace treaty with Athanaric.
text: Spring – Emperor Valens crosses the Danube, and attacks the Gothic tribes (Greuthungi and Tervingi). Valens and Athanaric, the Gothic king, eventually sign a treaty.

summary: Fritigern became leader of the Thervingian Goths with Roman military assistance and converted to Christianity.
text: Fritigern becomes king of the Visigoths; amidst hostilities with his rival Athanaric, he asks Valens and the Thracian field army to intervene. They end the civil war, and Fritigern converts to Christianity.

summary: Theodosius the Elder brought Britain fully back under Roman imperial rule following the Great Conspiracy.
text: Theodosius the Elder brings Britain fully back to the Empire after the Great Conspiracy of 367.

summary: King Shapur II invaded Armenia and besieged Prince Pap at the fortress of Artogerassa.
text: King Shapur II occupies the pro-Roman kingdom of Armenia. He besieges Artogerassa in modern Georgia, where Papas (Pap), son of King Arsaces II (Arshak II), defends the fortress and the royal treasure against Persian forces.

summary: Ulfilas devised the Gothic alphabet and converted the Goths to Arian Christianity.
text: Wulfila creates a Gothic alphabet composed of letters based on Greek and Roman letters, as well as some Germanic runes. He converts the Goths to Arian Christianity.

summary: Juvenal of Narni, the first bishop of Narni, died.
text: Juvenal of Narni, Roman Catholic bishop, confessor and saint

summary: Caesarius of Nazianzus, Roman physician and politician, died.
text: Caesarius of Nazianzus, Byzantine physician and politician (b. 331)

summary: Parandzem, queen and regent of Armenia, was captured and killed by Persian forces.
text: Pharantzem, Armenian queen and regent

summary: Valentinus, an exiled Roman rebel leader executed in Britain, died.
text: Valentinus, Roman criminal and rebel leader

summary: The westward advance of the Huns pushed numerous Germanic tribes against the northern frontier of the Roman Empire.
text: Germanic Invasions: Various Germanic tribes are forced against the northern borders of the Roman Empire as they flee the invading Huns.

summary: Emperors Valentinian I and Valens outlawed marriages between Romans and barbarians on penalty of death.
text: A law of Valentinian I and Valens bans marriages between Romans and barbarians under penalty of death.

object: importation of wine and olive oil
summary: Emperors Valentinian I and Valens issued an edict banning the importation of wine and olive oil from barbarian territories.
text: An edict issued by Valentinian I and Valens bans the importation of wine and olive oil from areas controlled by the barbarians.
names: importation of wine and olive oil

summary: Athanaric established defensive positions along the Dniester to protect the Tervingi against the approaching Huns.
text: Athanaric, Gothic leader of the Tervingi, advances eastwards and takes up a defensive position along the banks of the Dniester (Romania).

summary: Basil of Caesarea became bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia.
text: Basil the Great becomes bishop of Caesarea (Cappadocia).

summary: Demophilus became Patriarch of Constantinople despite his appointment being contested by Evagrius.
text: Demophilus of Constantinople becomes Patriarch of Constantinople, although his position is disputed by Evagrius of Constantinople.

summary: John Chrysostom received baptism at Antioch.
text: John Chrysostom is baptized.

summary: Alaric I, future king of the Visigoths, was born on Peuce Island in the Danube Delta.
text: Alaric I (or Alaricus), king of the Visigoths (d. 410)

summary: Brice of Tours, future bishop of Tours, was born.
text: Brice of Tours, Catholic bishop of Tours (d. 444)

summary: Claudian, Roman poet at the court of Emperor Honorius, was born in Alexandria.
text: Claudian, Roman poet and writer (d. 404)

summary: Decimus Rusticus, Roman praetorian prefect of Gaul, was born.
text: Decimus Rusticus, Roman praetorian prefect

summary: Hypatia, Greek philosopher, astronomer, and mathematician, was born in Alexandria.
text: Hypatia, Greek female philosopher (d. 415)

summary: Eudoxius of Antioch, Patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Eudoxius of Antioch, Syrian patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Lucifer of Cagliari, bishop and founder of the Luciferians, died in Sardinia.
text: Lucifer Calaritanus, founder of the Luciferian sect

summary: Parandzem, queen and regent of Armenia, died.
text: Pharantzem, Armenian queen and regent

summary: Roman politician Strategius Musonianus died.
text: Strategius Musonianus, Roman politician

summary: Valentinianus Galates, son of Roman emperor Valens, died.
text: Valentinianus Galates, Roman emperor

summary: Fortified cities along the Danube, led by Sirmium, helped repel an invasion by the Quadi.
text: The fortified cities of the Danube, with Sirmium (Pannonia) at the forefront, contribute to stop an invasion of the Quadi.

summary: The Romans renewed their war against the Sasanian Empire under King Shapur II.
text: The Persian Empire attains the zenith of its power under King Shapur II as the Romans renew their war against Persia. Hostilities will continue for the next 5 years.

summary: Roman poet Ausonius wrote about a voyage along the Rhine and Moselle in his poem Mosella.
text: Roman poet Ausonius writes of a voyage on the Rhine and the Moselle in his work 'Mosella'.

summary: Augustine of Hippo travelled to Carthage to continue his education in rhetoric.
text: Augustine of Hippo, age 17, travels to Carthage to continue his education in rhetoric.

summary: Martin of Tours became bishop of Tours.
text: Martin of Tours becomes bishop of Tours .

summary: Future Roman emperor Valentinian II was born.
text: Valentinian II, Roman consul and emperor (d. 392)

summary: Christian bishop Zeno of Verona died.
text: Zeno of Verona, Christian bishop and martyr

summary: Eusebius of Vercelli, Christian bishop, died.
text: Eusebius of Vercelli, Christian bishop (b. 283)

summary: Syrian anchorite and saint Hilarion died in Cyprus.
text: Hilarion, Syrian anchorite and saint (b. 291)

summary: Lucifer of Cagliari, Christian bishop and founder of the Luciferians, died.
text: Lucifer Calaritanus, Christian bishop

summary: Emperor Valentinian I campaigned against the Alamanni, Quadi, and Sarmatians while his subordinates engaged Firmus in Africa and the Picts in Britain.
text: Emperor Valentinian I is engaged in operations against the Alamanni, Quadi and Sarmatians, while his subordinates are dealing with the Roman usurper Firmus in Africa and the Picts in Britain.

summary: The Huns attacked and overwhelmed the Tervingi along the Dniester River, forcing King Athanaric to flee into the Carpathian Mountains.
text: The Huns attack the Tervingi on the Dniester, overwhelming them with light cavalry (horse archers), and devastating the settlements of the Goths. King Athanaric is defeated and seeks refuge in Caucaland in the Carpathian Mountains.

summary: Athanaric began constructing defensive fortifications to protect his people from the Alans and Huns.
text: Athanaric starts building new defensive works to protect his people against the Alans and the Huns.

summary: Basil the Great founded the Basileias hospital near Caesarea Mazaca on land granted by Emperor Valens.
text: Basil the Great establishes the Basileias, possibly the first hospital, near Caesarea Mazaca on land granted by emperor Valens.

summary: Gregory of Nyssa was consecrated bishop of Nyssa.
text: Gregory of Nyssa becomes bishop of Nyssa.

summary: Augustine of Hippo converted to Manichaeism while living in Carthage.
text: Saint Augustine adopts Manichaeism.

summary: Emperor Valentinian I issued an edict banning Manichaean meetings throughout the Western Empire.
text: Valentinian I bans Manichaean meetings.

summary: Greek Neoplatonist philosopher Maximus of Ephesus was executed.
text: Maximus of Ephesus, Greek Neoplatonist philosopher

summary: Christian reader and martyr Sabbas the Goth was drowned in the Buzău River.
text: Sabbas the Goth, Christian reader and saint (b. 334)

summary: Emperor Valens converted to Arianism and ordered the persecution of Nicene Christians in the Roman East.
text: Emperor Valens is converted to Arianism, and orders the persecution of Trinitarian Christians in the Roman East.

summary: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus became proconsul of Africa and joined the pontifical college.
text: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus becomes proconsul of Africa, and is made a member of the pontifical college.

summary: Count Theodosius the Elder was appointed to command an expedition to suppress the rebellion of Firmus in Mauretania.
text: Count Theodosius the Elder is appointed commander of an expedition to suppress the rebellion of Firmus in Mauretania.

summary: The Aqueduct of Valens was inaugurated in Constantinople.
text: The Aqueduct of Valens is inaugurated near Constantinople (modern Istanbul); the aqueduct has a length of 971 meters.

summary: King Shapur II declared war on the Roman Empire over Roman involvement in Armenia, prompting Emperor Valens to make Antioch his military base.
text: King Shapur II declares war as a result of Valens' support of Armenia. Emperor Valens makes Antioch his military base for the campaign against Persia.

summary: Saint Martin of Tours undertook the Christianization of the countryside of Gaul.
text: Saint Martin of Tours undertakes the Christianization of Gaul.

summary: Christian philosopher and future bishop Synesius was born in Cyrene.
text: Synesius of Cyrene, Christian bishop

summary: Athanasius of Alexandria, influential Christian theologian and bishop, died in Alexandria.
text: Athanasius of Alexandria, Egyptian bishop and saint (b. 296)

summary: Syrian Christian hymnographer and theologian Ephrem the Syrian died in Edessa.
text: Ephrem the Syrian, Syrian Orthodox priest and saint (b. 306)

summary: Nerses I the Great, catholicos of the Armenian Church, died.
text: Nerses I (the Great), Armenian catholicos (or patriarch)

summary: The Quadi crossed the Danube and plundered the unprotected countryside of Pannonia.
text: The Quadi cross the Danube and begin ravaging Pannonia. They avoid the fortified cities and plunder the unprotected countryside.

summary: The citizens of Milan acclaimed regional governor Ambrose as their new bishop.
text: The people of Milan astonish Ambrosius, governor of Aemilia-Liguria, by acclaiming him bishop. He is the second son of the former praetorian prefect of Gaul, and becomes a creative thinker whose ideas will provide the paradigm for medieval church-state relations.

summary: Gregory of Nazianzus the Elder, bishop of Nazianzus, died.
text: Gregory the Elder, Christian bishop and saint (b. 276)

summary: Marcellinus of Gaul, bishop of Embrun, died.
text: Marcellinus of Gaul (or Marcellin), Christian bishop

summary: King Pap of Armenia was assassinated by Roman officers.
text: Pap of Armenia (or Papas), king of Armenia

summary: Auxentius of Milan, Arian bishop of Milan, died.
text: Auxentius of Milan, Christian bishop and theologian

summary: Marcellus of Ancyra, bishop of Ancyra, died.
text: Marcellus of Ancyra, Christian bishop and saint

summary: Emperor Valentinian I died of a stroke during negotiations with the Quadi at Brigetio.
text: Emperor Valentinian I concludes an enduring peace with the Alamanni in Germany, then marches into Illyricum to repel an invasion of the Quadi and the Sarmatians on the Danube frontier. While negotiating with the Quadi, Valentinian, age 54, becomes so enraged that he dies in a fit of apoplexy at Brigetio (Hungary). Extreme cruelty has marked his 11-year reign, but he has also founded schools and provided physicians to serve the poor of Constantinople.

summary: The Quadi concluded a peace treaty with magister militum Merobaudes and received settlement lands along the Danube.
text: The Quadi accept an uneasy peace from Merobaudes (Magister militum), which gives them land to settle on the Danube.

summary: Gratian took control of the Western Empire from Trier while his half-brother Valentinian II was proclaimed co-emperor under Justina's regency at Milan.
text: Gratian, age 16, takes over the government at Augusta Treverorum (modern Trier), but ministers wishing to retain the loyalty of the Illyrian army fear a usurper. They proclaim Valentinian's 4-year-old son Valentinian II co-emperor with his mother, Justina, as regent. Gratian reserves for himself the administration of the Gallic provinces, and hands over Italy, Illyrium, Hispania and Africa to his stepmother, who makes Mediolanum (Milan) her residence.

summary: Emperor Gratian began a systematic persecution of pagans, confiscated temple wealth for the imperial treasury, and proscribed heresy.
text: Gratian, advised by his chief advisor Ambrosius, begins a systematic persecution of the pagans. He confiscates the fortunes of the temples and adds the money to the Imperial Treasury. He proscribes Arianism and Donatism.

summary: The rebel Berber prince Firmus was captured and handed over to the Romans by his brother Gildo in Africa.
text: In Africa, the dissident Berber prince Firmus is delivered to the Romans by his brother Gildon.

summary: The earliest surviving wooden leaf-bound books were deposited and preserved in the desert sands of Dakhla Oasis.
text: The earliest extant books – a school textbook and an account book – with bound wooden leaves, are lost at the Dakhla Oasis in western Egypt. The desert sands preserve them for modern archaeologists.

summary: Saint Jerome retired as an ascetic to the desert of Chalcis near Antioch.
text: Saint Jerome retires to the desert of Chalcis (Syria).

summary: Saint Maron laid the monastic foundations that gave rise to the Maronite Church in Lebanon.
text: The Maronite Church is founded by Saint Maron in Lebanon.

summary: Christian historian and theologian Paulus Orosius was born.
text: Orosius, Christian historian and theologian

summary: Saint Gorgonia, daughter of Gregory of Nazianzus the Elder, died.
text: Saint Gorgonia, daughter of Gregory the Elder

summary: Emmelia of Caesarea, mother of several prominent Christian saints, died.
text: Emmelia of Caesarea, Byzantine Eastern Orthodox priest

summary: Saint Mansuetus, the first bishop of Toul, died.
text: Mansuetus, Christian bishop and saint

summary: Roman emperor Valentinian I died at the fortress of Brigetio.
text: Valentinian I, Roman emperor (b. 321)

summary: Pambo, a Coptic Desert Father, died in Egypt.
text: Pambo (or Pemwah), Coptic Desert Father (b. 305)

summary: Emperor Valens permitted Fritigern and the Visigoths to cross the Danube and settle in Lower Moesia.
text: Gothic War: Emperor Valens permits the Visigothic chieftain Fritigern and his people to cross the Danube from Thrace (later Romania), and settle on Roman soil in Lower Moesia, on the condition that they provide soldiers to the legions. The Visigoths embark by troops on boats and rafts, and canoes made from hollowed tree trunks. The river is swollen by frequent rains; a large number try to swim and are drowned in their struggle against the force of the stream.

summary: The Greuthungi, led by Alatheus and Saphrax, crossed the Danube and joined Fritigern after being refused asylum by Rome.
text: The Greuthungi, led by Alatheus and Saphrax, displaced by the predations of the Huns and Alans, request asylum within the Roman Empire. They are refused. The Roman frontier forces stretched to the breaking point, they slip across the Danube and unite with Fritigern. With their situation critical and desperately short of food, discontent is rising amongst the Goths.

summary: The Goths broke out of their containment area along the Danube and marched south toward Marcianopolis after mistreatment by Roman authorities.
text: The Romans fail to disarm the Visigoths, bungle administration of the refugees, and mistreat them, taking some of their children as slaves. The Goths break out of their containment area along the Danube and strike south towards the low-lying fertile region near Marcianople (Bulgaria). Although defying the local Roman officials, they are not in open revolt.

summary: Lupicinus attempted to assassinate Fritigern at a banquet near Marcianopolis, inciting the Goths to plunder the countryside.
text: Lupicinus, count (Comes) of Thrace, tries to bring the Visigoths back under control. He invites Fritigern and the Gothic leaders to a banquet, letting them believe that in addition to food and drink, they can discuss provisions for their people. During the feast, Lupicinus tries to assassinate the Gothic delegation. Fritigern escapes and the Goths begin looting and burning the farms and Roman villas near Marcianople.

summary: The Visigoths annihilated a Roman force under Lupicinus outside Marcianopolis and equipped themselves with captured Roman weapons.
text: Lupicinus attacks the Visigoths 9 miles outside Marcianople with hastily gathered local troops. His force (5,000 men) is annihilated and the Goths equip themselves with Roman armour and weapons. Fritigern marches south towards Adrianople (Turkey).

summary: Roman troops of Gothic origin rebelled at Adrianople and joined forces with Fritigern.
text: Fearing they will join Fritigern, Roman troops of Gothic origin stationed in Adrianople are ordered by Valens to move east. The soldiers request a two-day delay to prepare and ask for food and money for the journey. However, the chief magistrate of Adrianople refuses and the Goths break out in open rebellion. They inflict heavy casualties among the citizens. Arming themselves with Roman equipment, they join forces with Fritigern.

summary: Fritigern unsuccessfully besieged Adrianople before dispersing his troops into foraging bands across the countryside.
text: Winter – Fritigern attempts an unsuccessful siege of Adrianople. His troops try to storm the city walls, but abandon the attacks and break into small bands, better able to forage and feed themselves. Roman prisoners switch sides and give the Goths a valuable source of local intelligence.

summary: Cyril of Alexandria, future Patriarch of Alexandria, was born.
text: Cyril of Alexandria, Egyptian patriarch (d. 444)

summary: Ermanaric, king of the Greuthungi, died.
text: Ermanaric, king of the Goths (Greuthungi) (b. 291)

summary: Roman general Theodosius the Elder was executed at Carthage.
text: Theodosius the Elder, Roman general

summary: Famine devastated Lower Moesia as Roman governors refused adequate aid to starving Goths.
text: Gothic War: Famine in Lower Moesia (occupied by the Goths) takes a fearsome toll. Fritigern and his followers appeal for help, but the governors Lupicinus and Maximus regard them as second-class citizens. Little help is forthcoming, and thousands starve to death. The pressure on the Roman frontier is still severe, with the Taifali and other hostile bands of Goths on the Danube. In addition, groups of Huns and Alans have also moved up to the river.

summary: Emperor Gratian sent reinforcements under Frigeridus and Richomeres to assist Emperor Valens against the Goths.
text: Emperor Valens requests his nephew Gratian to send Roman troops against the Goths. He responds by sending the ageing General Frigeridus with elite reinforcements that Ammianus calls ‘Pannonian and Transalpine auxiliaries (Pannonicis et Transalpinis auxiliis).’ Gratian also sends Richomeres, his Frankish commander of household troops (comes domesticorum), at the head of a number of troops drawn from the Gallic field army.

summary: The Goths and Romans fought an indecisive and bloody battle at the Willows.
text: Battle of the Willows: The Romans abandon the guerrilla strategy and are attacked by the Goths. The battle is indecisive but both sides suffer heavy casualties. The only Roman army available to face the Goths is no longer a fighting force. Richomeres withdraws his troops south of Marcianople (Bulgaria).

summary: Emperor Valens dispatched Saturninus to block the passes of the Balkan Mountains against the Goths.
text: Valens sends Saturninus to the Balkan Mountains to block the passes. These efforts are possibly supported by units of limitanei (light infantry) withdrawn from areas under Goth control. Split into small bands and unable to join the Tervingi in sufficient strength to overcome the Roman cordon, the Goths grow increasingly desperate.

summary: The Goths allied with Huns and Alans along the Danube, compelling Saturninus to withdraw and opening the Balkan passes.
text: The Goths (possibly Greuthungi) make an alliance with some of the Huns and Alans along the Danube, and entice them across the river. With the balance of power now shifted Saturninus concentrates his forces to avoid his outposts being overrun. This opens the passes, allowing the Goths, Huns and Alans to break out into the lowlands of southern Thrace.

summary: Gothic forces destroyed a Roman heavy cavalry unit outside Dibaltum.
text: Autumn – Bands of predatory "barbarians" spread throughout the province in search of food, supplies and booty. Most Roman troops are bottled up in the towns. Some elite units remain in the field and skirmish with the Goths. One such action takes place outside the town of Dibaltum. The Scutarii heavy cavalry is destroyed in a mad charge against the Goths.

summary: Frigeridus withdrew his army from Beroea over the Succi Pass to Illyricum to avoid the advancing Goths.
text: The Goths, now seeking a military victory to force the Empire to make terms, aim to dislodge the army of Frigeridus from Beroea. He withdraws over the Succi (Ihtiman) Pass back to Illyrium, and reports to Gratian that an expedition by the main imperial armies is required to repulse the Goths in Thrace.

summary: Emperor Valens concluded peace with the Sasanian Empire and quelled a revolt led by Queen Mavia.
text: Valens concludes a peace with the Persian Empire and leaves enough troops to defend the eastern frontier. The Saracens under Queen Mavia revolt and devastate a swath of territory stretching from Phoenicia and Palestine as far as the Sinai (Egypt). Valens successfully brings the uprising under control.

summary: King Shapur II drove the Huns back across the Caucasus.
text: Persian king Shapur II pushes the Huns back across the Caucasus.

summary: Arcadius, future Eastern Roman Emperor, was born in Hispania.
text: Arcadius, Roman consul and emperor

summary: Euthymius the Great, Armenian abbot and monastic leader, was born in Melitene.
text: Euthymius the Great, Armenian abbot and bishop (d. 473)

summary: Valerian of Abbenza, Christian bishop and saint, was born.
text: Valerian of Abbenza, Christian bishop and saint (d. 457)

summary: Julian Sabas, a Christian hermit, died in the Syrian desert.
text: Julian Sabas (the Ascetic), Byzantine hermit

summary: Sahak I, Catholicos of Armenia, died.
text: Sahak I, Armenian archbishop and catholicos

summary: Emperor Valens returned to Constantinople, raised an army, and appointed Sebastianus as magister militum in Thrace.
text: Spring – Emperor Valens returns to Constantinople and mobilises an army (40,000 men). He appoints Sebastianus, newly arrived from Italy, as magister militum to reorganize the Roman armies in Thrace.

summary: The Lentienses crossed the frozen Rhine to raid Roman territory but were repelled by Roman auxilia palatina.
text: February – The Lentienses (part of the Alemanni) cross the frozen Rhine and raid the countryside. They are driven back by Roman auxilia palatina (Celtae and Petulantes), who defend the western frontier.

summary: Mallobaudes defeated the Lentienses near Colmar at the Battle of Argentovaria.
text: May – Battle of Argentovaria: Emperor Gratian is forced to recall the army he has sent East. The Lentienses are defeated by Mallobaudes near Colmar (France). Gratian gains the title Alemannicus Maximus.

summary: Emperor Valens sent Sebastianus with two thousand picked troops to Thrace to conduct guerrilla warfare against the Goths around Adrianople.
text: Gothic War: Valens sends Sebastian with a body of picked troops (2,000 men) to Thrace and renews the guerrilla war against the Goths. He chases down small groups of Gothic raiders around Adrianople.

summary: Fritigern concentrated his Gothic forces at Cabyle.
text: Fritigern concentrates his army at Cabyle (Bulgaria). The Goths are mainly centred in the river valleys south of the Balkan Mountains, around the towns of Beroea, Cabyle and Dibaltum.

summary: General Frigeridus fortified the Succi Pass to prevent barbarian forces from breaking out into Pannonia.
text: July – Frigeridus, Roman general, fortifies the Succi (Ihtiman) Pass to prevent the "barbarians" from breaking out to the north-west (Pannonia).

summary: Emperor Gratian traveled down the Danube from Lauriacum with light troops and halted at Sirmium due to a fever.
text: Gratian sets out from Lauriacum (Austria) with a body of light armed troops. His force is small enough to travel by boat down the Danube. He halts for four days at Sirmium (Serbia) suffering from fever.

summary: A band of Alans ambushed Gratian's troops near modern Niš, inflicting casualties.
text: August – Gratian continues down the Danube to the "Camp of Mars" (frontier fortress near modern Niš), where he loses several men in an ambush by a band of Alans.

summary: Fritigern advanced south along the Tundzha River toward Adrianople to sever Roman supply lines to Constantinople.
text: Fritigern strikes south from Cabyle, following the Tundzha River towards Adrianople, and tries to get behind the supply lines to Constantinople.

summary: After Roman scouts detected the Goths, Emperor Valens turned back and set up a fortified camp outside Adrianople.
text: Roman reconnaissance detects the Goths. Valens, already west of Adrianople, turns back and establishes a fortified camp outside the city.

summary: The Goths withdrew northwards with their wagons while their cavalry foraged undetected in the Tundzha valley.
text: The Goths, with their wagons and families vulnerable to attack, withdraw back to the north. Roman scouts fail to detect the Greuthungi cavalry foraging further up the Tundzha valley.

summary: Emperor Valens rejected peace overtures brought to the Roman camp by a Christian priest on behalf of Fritigern.
text: Fritigern sends a Christian priest to the Roman camp with an offer of terms and a letter for Valens. The peace overtures are rejected.

summary: The Goths attempted to scale the walls of Adrianople but were driven back by the garrison.
text: The Goths attack Adrianople; they attempt to scale the city walls with ladders but are repelled by the defenders, who drop lumps of masonry.

summary: Arab federate troops checked the advance of the Goths and Huns toward Constantinople.
text: The Goths, supported by the Huns, move on to Constantinople. Their progress is checked by the Saracens, recruited from Arab tribes who control the eastern fringes of the empire.

summary: Suffering from food shortages, the Greuthungi moved west into Pannonia and raided settlements.
text: October – The Greuthungi, faced with food shortages, split off and move west into Pannonia. Followed by their families, they raid villages and farmland.

summary: Emperor Valens completed the aqueduct of Constantinople originally begun by Constantine the Great.
text: Valens completes the aqueduct of Constantinople begun by Constantine I.

summary: Gregory of Nazianzus was ordained bishop of Constantinople.
text: Gregory of Nazianzus is ordained bishop of Constantinople.

summary: Emperor Gratian exonerated Pope Damasus I of charges of adultery.
text: Pope Damasus I is accused of adultery but is exonerated by Gratian.

summary: Germanus of Auxerre was born.
text: Germanus of Auxerre, Christian bishop

summary: Roman general Sebastianus died at the Battle of Adrianople.
text: August 9: Sebastianus, Roman general (magister peditum)

summary: Roman general Traianus died at the Battle of Adrianople.
text: August 9: Traianus, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Emperor Valens was killed at the Battle of Adrianople.
text: August 9: Valens, Roman consul and emperor (b. 328)

summary: Roman general and politician Flavius Arintheus died.
text: Flavius Arintheus, Roman politician and general

summary: Christian theologian and bishop Titus of Bostra died.
text: Titus of Bostra, Christian bishop and theologian

summary: A Gothic and Alan coalition decisively defeated the Eastern Roman army near Adrianople and killed Emperor Valens.
text: Battle of Adrianople: A combined Gothic-Alanic force decisively defeated the Roman army near Edirne. Valens was killed.

summary: Emperor Gratian elevated Theodosius I to Augustus at Sirmium, granting him control of the eastern provinces.
text: Emperor Gratian elevates Flavius Theodosius at Sirmium, giving him the title Augustus with power over all the eastern provinces. Theodosius comes to terms with the Visigoths and settles them in the Balkans as military allies (foederati).

summary: Emperor Gratian refused the title of Eastern Emperor.
text: Gratian refuses the title of Eastern Emperor.

summary: Emperor Gratian renounced the traditional pagan imperial title of Pontifex Maximus.
text: Gratian renounces the title Pontifex Maximus.

summary: Roman Britain endured heavy raids by barbarian invaders.
text: Britain is forced to endure fierce Barbarian raids.

summary: King Shapur II died after a sixty-nine-year reign and was succeeded on the Persian throne by his brother Ardashir II.
text: King Shapur II, ruler of the Persian Empire, age 70, dies after a 69-year reign in which he conquered Armenia and transferred multitudes of people from the western lands to Susiana (Khuzistan). The great town Nishapur in Khorasan (eastern Parthia) is also founded by him. His brother Ardashir II, governor-king of Adiabene, is placed by the nobles on the throne.

summary: Gregory of Nazianzus became Patriarch of Constantinople and was injured in an attack by a mob.
text: Gregory Nazianzus becomes Patriarch of Constantinople, and is wounded when he is attacked by a mob of heretics.

summary: John Chrysostom wrote a treatise on the Christian education of children.
text: John Chrysostom writes a book on the Christian education of children.

summary: Gunderic, future king of the Vandals and Alans, was born.
text: Gunderic, king of the Vandals and Alans (d. 428)

summary: Basil of Caesarea, bishop of Caesarea Mazaca and church father, died.
text: Basil ("the Great"), bishop of Caesarea Mazaca (b. 330)

summary: Macrina the Younger died.
text: Macrina the Younger, Christian nun and saint (b. 327)

summary: Shapur II, ruler of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Shapur II ("the Great"), ruler of the Sasanian Empire (b. 309)

summary: Theodosius I, Gratian, and Valentinian II issued the Edict of Thessalonica, ordering all Roman citizens to adhere to Nicene trinitarian Christianity.
text: Edict of Thessalonica: Theodosius I, with co-emperors Gratian and Valentinian II, declare their wish that all Roman citizens convert to trinitarian Christianity, in accordance with the patriarchs of Rome and Alexandria, implicitly rejecting the Arianism of the patriarch of Constantinople as heretical.

summary: Goths led by Fritigern defeated a Roman army in Macedonia during the Battle of Thessalonica.
text: Battle of Thessalonica: The Goths under Fritigern defeat a Roman army in Macedonia. Theodosius I retreats to Thessalonica and leaves Gratian in control of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: The Roman Empire enlisted Germans, Sarmatians, and Huns into imperial military service.
text: Rome's enemies (the Germans, Sarmatians and Huns) are taken into Imperial service; as a consequence, barbarian leaders begin to play an increasingly active role in the Roman Empire.

summary: Theodosius I made his formal adventus entry into Constantinople.
text: Theodosius I makes his adventus, or formal entry, into Constantinople.

summary: Queen Mavia and her Saracen forces defeated a Roman army in southern Syria.
text: Queen Mavia, with her Saracen forces, defeats the Roman army in southern Syria.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I was baptized as a Christian.
text: Emperor Theodosius I is baptized.

summary: Following the death of Fritigern, Athanaric became king of the entire Gothic people.
text: The Visigothic chieftain Fritigern dies after ravaging the Balkans; his rival Athanaric becomes king of the entire Gothic nation.

summary: Ticonius wrote an influential commentary on the Book of Revelation.
text: Ticonius writes a commentary on the Bible's Book of Revelation.

summary: A Christian cathedral was constructed at Augusta Treverorum.
text: A cathedral is built in Augusta Treverorum.

summary: The Council of Saragossa met and condemned the teachings of Priscillianism.
text: The Council of Saragossa is held; Spanish and Aquitanian bishops condemn the teachings of Priscillianism.

summary: Aelia Eudoxia, future Roman empress, was born.
text: Aelia Eudoxia, empress and wife of Arcadius

summary: Alexius of Rome was born.
text: Alexius, Eastern saint

summary: Eucherius, future bishop of Lyon, was born.
text: Eucherius, bishop of Lyon

summary: Eutyches, presbyter and archimandrite, was born.
text: Eutyches, presbyter and archimandrite

summary: Egyptian astrologer Hephaestion of Thebes was born.
text: Hephaestion of Thebes, Egyptian astrologer

summary: Historical writer Olympiodorus of Thebes was born.
text: Olympiodorus of Thebes, historical writer

summary: Peter Chrysologus, future bishop of Ravenna, was born.
text: Peter Chrysologus, bishop of Ravenna

summary: Christian church historian Philip of Side was born.
text: Philip of Side, Christian church historian

summary: Church historian Socrates of Constantinople was born.
text: Socrates of Constantinople, church historian

summary: Priests James, Azadanus, and Abdicius were martyred.
text: James, Azadanus and Abdicius, Roman Catholic priests, martyrs and saints

summary: Fritigern, chieftain of the Visigoths, died.
text: Fritigern, king of the Visigoths
