summary: Gratian moved the western imperial capital to Mediolanum, renounced the title Pontifex Maximus, and refused the traditional robe of office.
text: Emperor Gratian moves the capital to Mediolanum (modern-day Milan). Because of his Christian beliefs, he eliminates Pontifex Maximus as Imperial title. Gratian also refuses the robe of office, insulting the pagan aristocrats of Rome.

summary: The Gallic city of Cularo was renamed Gratianopolis in honor of Gratian.
text: The Gallic city of Cularo is renamed Gratianopolis (later Grenoble), in honor of Gratian having created a bishopric.

summary: Athanaric visited Constantinople and concluded a peace treaty with Theodosius I that made the Goths Roman foederati, dying two weeks later.
text: The Visigothic chieftain Athanaric becomes the first foreign king to visit the Eastern Roman capital of Constantinople. He negotiates a peace treaty with emperor Theodosius I that makes his people foederati as "one body within the imperial soldiery". Athanaric dies 2 weeks later after an 18-year reign in which he has been undisputed king of all the Goths for just 1 year. The peace will continue until Theodosius's death in 395.

summary: The Sciri and Huns launched joint attacks along the Roman frontier on the lower Danube.
text: The Sciri together with the Huns attack along Rome's lower Danubian frontier.

summary: Theodosius I summoned the First Council of Constantinople, which reaffirmed the Nicene Creed and condemned Arianism and Apollinarism.
text: First Council of Constantinople (some authorities date this council to 383): Theodosius I calls a general council to affirm and extend the Nicene Creed, and denounce Arianism and Apollinarism. Most trinitarian churches consider this an Ecumenical council.

summary: Ambrose and the Council of Aquileia deposed the Arian bishops Palladius of Ratiaria and Secundianus of Singidunum.
text: Council of Aquileia: Ambrose and the council depose the Arian bishops Palladius of Ratiaria and Secundianus of Singidunum.

summary: Flavian succeeded Meletius as Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Flavian succeeds Meletius as Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Timothy succeeded Peter II as Patriarch of Alexandria.
text: Timothy succeeds Peter II as Patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Nectarius succeeded Gregory of Nazianzus as Archbishop of Constantinople.
text: Nectarius succeeds Gregory Nazianzus as Archbishop of Constantinople.

summary: John Chrysostom was ordained as a deacon.
text: John Chrysostom becomes a deacon.

summary: Faustinus of Brescia, bishop and saint, died.
text: Faustinus of Brescia, Roman Catholic bishop and saint

summary: Peter II, Patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Peter II, Patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Saint Syrus, Bishop of Genoa, died.
text: Saint Syrus, Bishop of Genoa

summary: Athanaric, king of the Visigoths, died at Constantinople.
text: Athanaric, king of the Visigoths

summary: Saint Meletius, Patriarch of Antioch, died while presiding over the council at Constantinople.
text: Saint Meletius, Patriarch of Antioch

summary: Emperor Theodosius I concluded a peace treaty settling the Visigoths as foederati in Moesia and Thrace.
text: Emperor Theodosius I commands his general Saturninus to conclude a peace treaty with the Visigoths, allowing them to settle south of the Danube. They are installed as foederati in Moesia and Thrace with the title of "Allies of the Roman People", in exchange for furnishing a contingent of auxiliary troops to defend the borders.

summary: Emperor Gratian refused the divine attributes of the imperial cult and removed the Altar of Victory from the Senate.
text: Emperor Gratian refuses the divine attributes of the Imperial cult and removes the Altar of Victory from the Senate.

summary: The Council of Rome established the Biblical canon, and Pope Damasus I commissioned Jerome to revise the Latin scriptures.
text: The Council of Rome establishes Biblical canon in the Catholic Church. Pope Damasus I commissions a revision of the Vetus Latina, eventually resulting in the Vulgate of Jerome.

summary: The Council of Rome adopted Trinitarianism, condemned Apollinarism, and Emperor Theodosius I condemned Manichaean monks to death.
text: The same council adopts Trinitarianism as doctrine, condemning Apollinarism. Theodosius I orders the death of members of the Manichaean monks.

summary: John Chrysostom delivered sermons declaring the perpetual virginity of Mary.
text: The first sermons declaring the virginity of Mary are given by John Chrysostom.

summary: Apollinaris of Laodicea, bishop of Syrian Laodicea, died.
text: Apollinaris the Younger, bishop of Laodicea in Syria.

summary: Magnus Maximus withdrew Roman troops from Wales, effectively ending Roman rule in the region.
text: Magnus Maximus withdraws Roman troops from the region of Wales, marking the effective end of Roman rule in Wales.
names: End of Roman rule in Britain

summary: Arcadius was elevated to the rank of Augustus.
text: Arcadius is elevated to Emperor.

summary: Magnus Maximus was proclaimed emperor by troops in Britannia and established his capital at Trier.
text: Roman troops in Britannia proclaim Magnus Maximus as their Emperor. He crosses over to the continent and makes Trier his capital. Gaul, the Italian provinces and Hispania proclaim loyalty to him.

summary: Emperor Gratian was assassinated at Lugdunum, leaving Valentinian II under the regency of Justina.
text: Emperor Gratian, age 24, is assassinated at Lugdunum (modern-day Lyon), leaving a young widow Laeta. Pannonia and Africa maintain their allegiance to co-emperor Valentinian II, now 12, whose mother, Justina, rules in his name.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I ceded Dacia and Macedonia to Valentinian II and recognized Magnus Maximus as Augustus.
text: Emperor Theodosius I cedes Dacia and Macedonia to Valentinian II. They recognize Magnus Maximus as Augustus.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I sent Stilicho to Ctesiphon to negotiate the partition of Armenia with Shapur III.
text: Theodosius I sends Flavius Stilicho as an envoy to the Persian court of King Shapur III at Ctesiphon, to negotiate a peace settlement relating to the partition of Armenia.

summary: Shapur III succeeded his father Ardashir II as king of the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Ardashir II dies after a 4-year reign. He is succeeded by his son Shapur III.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I convened a general council at Constantinople to affirm the Nicene Creed and condemn Arianism and Apollinarism.
text: First Council of Constantinople (some authorities date this council to 381): Theodosius I calls a general council to affirm and extend the Nicene Creed, and denounce Arianism and Apollinarism. Most trinitarian Christian churches consider this an Ecumenical council.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I banished Eunomius of Cyzicus to Moesia.
text: By the order of Theodosius I, Eunomius of Cyzicus is banished to Moesia.

summary: Lupus of Troyes, later bishop and saint, was born.
text: Lupus of Troyes, French bishop and saint

summary: Isaac of Dalmatia, Orthodox priest and saint, died.
text: Isaac of Dalmatia, Byzantine Orthodox priest and saint

summary: Emperor Gratian was assassinated at Lugdunum.
text: Gratian, Roman Emperor (assassinated) (b. 359)

summary: Saint Ursula, Roman Christian martyr, died.
text: Ursula, Roman Christian martyr and saint

summary: Ardashir II, Sasanian King of Kings, died.
text: Ardashir II, Sassanid king (shah) ("King of Kings")

summary: Constantia, daughter of Constantius II and wife of Gratian, died.
text: Flavia Maxima Constantia, daughter of Constantius II

summary: Frumentius, missionary and bishop of Axum, died.
text: Frumentius, Phoenician missionary and bishop

summary: Ulfilas, Gothic bishop and translator of the Bible, died.
text: Ulfilas (or Wulfila), Gothic missionary and bishop

summary: Magnus Maximus elevated his son Flavius Victor to the rank of Augustus.
text: Magnus Maximus elevates his son Flavius Victor to the rank of Augustus.

summary: Magnus Maximus returned to Britain to assist the Roman army against barbarian raids.
text: Magnus Maximus returns to Britain to aid the Roman army with the barbarian raids triggered by Maximus' withdrawal of troops to the continent.

summary: The Forum of Theodosius was constructed in Constantinople.
text: The Forum of Theodosius ("Forum of the Bull") is built in Constantinople.

summary: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus became urban prefect of Rome.
text: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus becomes urban prefect of Rome.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I issued an edict closing pagan temples in the Nile Valley.
text: An edict of Theodosius I closes pagan temples in the Nile Valley (Egypt).

summary: Stilicho married Serena, the adopted niece of Emperor Theodosius I.
text: Stilicho marries Serena, adopted niece of Theodosius I.

summary: King Shapur III and Emperor Theodosius I signed the Peace of Acilisene, partitioning Armenia between Rome and Persia.
text: King Shapur III signs the Peace of Acilisene with Theodosius I. Armenia is divided in two kingdoms and becomes a vassal state of the Roman Empire and Persia. The friendly relations survive for 36 years.

summary: Pope Siricius succeeded Pope Damasus I as bishop of Rome and adopted the title Pontifex Maximus.
text: Pope Siricius succeeds Damasus I as the 38th pope. He takes the title Pontifex Maximus, after it is relinquished by the late emperor Gratian.

summary: Jerome wrote his letter on the vow of virginity to Eustochium after completing his Vulgate translation of the Gospels.
text: Jerome, Christian prophet, writes his celebrated letter "De custodia virginitatis" (vow of virginity) to Eustochium, daughter of the ascetic Paula. He has by this time completed his Vulgate translation of the Gospels.

summary: Ambrose refused Empress Justina's request for a church in Milan for Arian worship.
text: Ambrosius refuses the request of Empress Justina for a church in Milan, where she can worship according to her Arian belief.

summary: A Christian synod was held in Bordeaux.
text: A synod is held in Bordeaux (France).

summary: Egeria concluded her pilgrimage to the Holy Land and recorded her travels in the Itinerarium Egeriae.
text: The Gallaeci or Gallic woman Egeria concludes her Christian pilgrimage to the Holy Land at about this date; her narrative of it, the Itinerarium Egeriae, may be the earliest surviving formal writing by a woman in western European culture.

summary: Future Western Roman Emperor Honorius was born.
text: Honorius, Roman Emperor (d. 423)

summary: Maria, future Roman empress and daughter of Stilicho, was born.
text: Maria, empress and daughter of Stilicho

summary: Servatius of Tongeren, bishop and saint, died.
text: Servatius of Tongeren, Roman Catholic bishop and saint

summary: Pope Timothy I of Alexandria died.
text: Pope Timothy I of Alexandria

summary: Pope Damasus I died in Rome.
text: Pope Damasus I

summary: Praetorian prefect Vettius Agorius Praetextatus died.
text: Vettius Agorius Praetextatus, praetorian prefect

summary: A Roman synod exiled Jerome, who then departed for Egypt and the Holy Land accompanied by Paula.
text: The Roman synod exiles the prophet Jerome, who has incorporated ideas first propounded by the Roman statesman Cicero. He departs for Egypt, Bethlehem, and Jerusalem, accompanied by the Christian ascetic Paula, who will edit Jerome's translation of the Bible, which becomes the Latin Vulgate.

summary: Ammianus Marcellinus began writing his history covering the Roman Empire from the year ninety-six to three hundred seventy-eight.
text: Ammianus Marcellinus begins writing a history, in the style of Tacitus, covering the years AD 96–378.

summary: A Christian mob destroyed the Serapeum of Alexandria in Egypt.
text: The Serapeum of Alexandria, one of the largest Greek temples in Egypt, is destroyed by a Christian mob. The precise date is disputed, with 391 sometimes given as the moment of final destruction.

summary: Theophilus became Patriarch of Alexandria.
text: Theophilus becomes Patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Pope Siricius issued the Directa Decretal proclaiming Roman primacy and priestly celibacy.
text: Pope Siricius issues the Directa Decretal, proclaiming the primacy of Rome and the priestly obligation of celibacy.

summary: Priscillian was beheaded at Trier after being accused of Manichaeism and magic, becoming the first person executed for heresy in Christianity.
text: Priscillian, Spanish bishop, is accused of Manichaeism and magic, and beheaded at Trier. He becomes the first person in the history of Christianity to be executed for heresy.

summary: Aurelios Zopyros won the junior pankration, becoming the last recorded athlete at the Ancient Olympic Games.
text: Aurelios Zopyros becomes the last reported athlete at the Ancient Olympic Games. He is a victor in "junior boxing" (pankration).

summary: Future Western Roman Emperor Avitus was born.
text: Avitus, Western Roman Emperor

summary: Pulcheria, daughter of Roman Emperor Theodosius I, was born.
text: Pulcheria, daughter of Theodosius I who died in infancy (d. 386)

summary: Saint Patrick, future missionary to Ireland, was born in Roman Britain.
text: Saint Patrick, missionary in Ireland

summary: Historian and theologian Paulus Orosius was born.
text: Paulus Orosius, historian and theologian

summary: Roman Empress Aelia Flaccilla, wife of Theodosius I, died.
text: Aelia Flaccilla, Roman empress and wife of Theodosius I (or possibly 386)

summary: Priscillian, a Spanish bishop and theologian, was executed for heresy.
text: Priscillian, Spanish bishop and theologian

summary: Theodosius I signed a peace treaty with Shapur III dividing Armenia into Roman and Persian vassal kingdoms.
text: Emperor Theodosius I signs a peace treaty with King Shapur III; they divide Armenia into two kingdoms (vassal states). The treaty establishes friendly relations between the Roman Empire and Persia for the next 36 years.

summary: A Roman fleet ambushed and destroyed the Greuthungi as they attempted to cross the Danube.
text: The Greuthungi cross the Danube to raid the Roman garrisons on the northern frontier. They are met midstream by a well-armed fleet, and their rafts and dugouts sink. Those not drowned are slaughtered.

summary: Magnus Maximus invaded Italy and destroyed Novara for supporting Valentinian II.
text: Magnus Maximus invades Italy; he destroys Novara for supporting his rival Valentinian II.

object: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
summary: Theodosius I began rebuilding the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls.
text: Theodosius I begins to rebuild the present-day Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls.

place.title: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls

names: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls

summary: A victory column was erected at Constantinople honoring Theodosius I for his victories in the Balkans.
text: A column is constructed at Constantinople in honour of Theodosius I. Reliefs depict the emperor's victory over the barbarians in the Balkan.

summary: Saint Ambrose defended the independence of the Church against the authority of the imperial court.
text: Saint Ambrose defends the rights of the Catholic Church with respect to those of the State.

summary: John Chrysostom was ordained as a presbyter and delivered his homilies against the Jews.
text: John Chrysostom becomes a presbyter; he also writes eight Homilies entitled "Adversus Iudaeos" ("Against the Jews").

summary: Augustine converted to Christianity in Milan after hearing a sermon on Anthony the Great.
text: Augustine converts to Christianity. He ends his marriage plans after hearing a sermon on the life of Saint Anthony.

summary: Pagan resistance against increasingly strict anti-pagan laws in the Roman Empire grew futile.
text: The fight in the Roman Empire against anti-pagan laws becomes increasingly futile.

summary: Sumela Monastery was founded in the Pontic Mountains of Asia Minor.
text: Sumela Monastery is established in Asia Minor.

summary: Nestorius, future theologian and founder of Nestorianism, was born.
text: Nestorius, founder of Nestorianism

summary: Cyril of Jerusalem, bishop and theologian, died.
text: Cyril of Jerusalem, theologian and saint

summary: Demophilus, former patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Demophilus, Patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Pulcheria, daughter of Emperor Theodosius I, died in childhood.
text: Pulcheria, daughter of Theodosius I (b. 385)

summary: Theodosius I sent troops to suppress a riot in Antioch caused by tax increases and closed public facilities.
text: Spring – Emperor Theodosius I increases the taxes in Antioch. A peasant uprising leads to a riot, and public buildings are set afire. Theodosius sends imperial troops to quell the disturbance, and closes the public baths and theatres.

summary: Magnus Maximus invaded Italy, forcing Valentinian II and his family to flee Rome for Thessaloniki.
text: Magnus Maximus, usurping emperor of the West, invades Italy. Emperor Valentinian II, age 16, is forced out of Rome. He flees with his mother Justina and sisters to Thessaloniki (Thrace).

summary: Theodosius I took Valentinian II under his protection and married his sister Galla.
text: Winter – The widowed emperor Theodosius I takes Valentinian II under his protection, and marries his sister Flavia Galla.

summary: Theodosius I and Shapur III finalized the Peace of Acilisene, dividing Armenia between Rome and Persia.
text: Peace of Acilisene: King Shapur III signs a treaty with Theodosius I. Armenia is divided in two kingdoms, and becomes a vassal state of the Roman Empire and Persia.

summary: Greek physician Oribasius published a treatise on paralysis and bleedings.
text: Oribase, Greek doctor, publishes a treatise on paralysis and bleedings.

summary: Ambrose baptized Augustine of Hippo on the Easter Vigil in Milan.
text: Augustine is baptized on Easter Vigil by Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan.

summary: Armenian military leader Vardan Mamikonian was born.
text: Vardan Mamikonian, Armenian military leader (d. 451)

summary: Roman empress Aelia Flaccilla, wife of Theodosius I, died.
text: Aelia Flaccilla, Roman Empress and wife of Theodosius I
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Ostrogothic chieftain Alatheus was killed during combat on the Danube frontier.
text: Alatheus, chieftain of the Ostrogoths

summary: Saint Monica, mother of Augustine of Hippo, died at Ostia.
text: Saint Monica, mother of Augustine of Hippo

summary: Emperor Theodosius I defeated Magnus Maximus at the Battle of the Save near Emona, restoring Valentinian II as Western Roman emperor.
text: Battle of the Save: Emperor Theodosius I defeats Magnus Maximus near Emona (modern Slovenia). Theodosius is in command of an army including Goths, Huns and Alans. Valentinian II, now 17, is restored as Roman Emperor.

summary: Franks led by Marcomer, Sunno, and Genobaud invaded the Roman Empire, threatened Cologne, and ambushed and defeated a Roman army under Quintines.
text: Frankish invasion of 388: Rebellious Franks led by Marcomer, Sunno and Genobaud invade the Roman Empire with plunder and threaten Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium (Cologne). A part of the invaders are destroyed by the Romans in the charcoal forest (present-day Belgium). The Roman general Quintines pursues the invaders on Frankish soil and is ambushed. His army is surrounded and defeated by the Franks.

summary: Magnus Maximus surrendered at Aquileia and was executed, while his son Flavius Victor was executed at Trier by Arbogast.
text: Magnus Maximus surrenders at Aquileia, and is executed. Theodosius I devotes himself to gluttony and voluptuous living. Maximus' son Flavius Victor is executed at Trier, by Valentinian's magister militum Arbogast.

summary: Bahram IV succeeded his father Shapur III as king of the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Shapur III dies after a reign in which he has partitioned Armenia with the Roman Empire. He is succeeded by his son Bahram IV, who becomes the twelfth Sassanid king of Persia.

summary: Paternus became bishop of the episcopal see of Braga.
text: Paternus becomes bishop of the Episcopal see of Braga (Portugal).

summary: Isaac was named Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church.
text: Isaac, age 50, is named Catholicos (spiritual head) of the Armenian Apostolic Church.

summary: Jerome moved to Palestine to spend the remainder of his life as a hermit near Bethlehem.
text: Jerome moves to Palestine, where he spends the rest of his life as a hermit near Bethlehem.

summary: A group of Christians stormed the synagogue in the city of Callinicum on the Euphrates.
text: A group of Christians storms the synagogue of the city Callinicum (Syria), at the Euphrates.

summary: Christian bishop Elpidius of Atella was born.
text: Elpidius of Atella (or Elpidio), Christian bishop (d. 452)

summary: Roman usurper emperor Magnus Maximus died.
text: Magnus Maximus, Roman emperor

summary: Roman co-emperor Flavius Victor was executed at Trier.
text: Flavius Victor, Roman co-emperor (Augustus)

summary: Roman praetorian prefect Maternus Cynegius died.
text: Maternus Cynegius, Roman praetorian prefect

summary: Shapur III, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Shapur III, king of the Sassanid Empire (Persia)

summary: Roman statesman and philosopher Themistius died.
text: Themistius, Byzantine statesman and rhetorician

summary: Pagan buildings in Alexandria, including the Serapeum and its library collection, were destroyed by fire.
text: All pagan buildings in Alexandria, including the library, are destroyed by fire.

summary: Geiseric, future king of the Vandals and Alans, was born.
text: Geiseric, king of the Vandals and Alans

summary: Donatian, bishop of Reims, died.
text: Donatian of Reims (or Donat), Christian bishop and saint

summary: Florus of Lodève, Christian bishop and martyr, died.
text: Florus of Lodève, Christian bishop and martyr

summary: The Roman army massacred more than seven thousand citizens of Thessalonica on the orders of Emperor Theodosius I following the murder of general Butheric.
text: April – Massacre of Thessalonica: Resentment among the citizens of Thessalonica (Macedonia) breaks out into violence after the arrest of a popular charioteer. Butheric, military commander of Illyricum, is murdered. Emperor Theodosius I orders vengeance, despite the pleas for mercy by Ambrose, bishop of Milan; more than 7,000 inhabitants are massacred by the Roman army.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I performed public penance before Bishop Ambrose in the cathedral of Milan for the massacre at Thessalonica.
text: Ambrose retires to Milan (residence of Theodosius I) and refuses to celebrate a mass in the emperor's presence, until he repents for ordering the massacre in Thessalonica. Theodosius, filled with remorse, kneels in humility and strips off his royal purple, before the altar of the cathedral in Milan, humbling himself before the church.

summary: Visigoths and Huns led by Alaric invaded Thrace, prompting Stilicho to raise an army and campaign against them.
text: The Visigoths and Huns, led by Alaric, invade Thrace. Stilicho, high-ranking general (magister militum) of Vandal origin, raises an army and begins a campaign against the Goths.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I transported an Egyptian obelisk and re-erected it in the Hippodrome of Constantinople.
text: Theodosius I brings an obelisk from Egypt to the Hippodrome of Constantinople.

summary: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus and Virius Nicomachus Flavianus commemorated the alliance of their senatorial families by producing an ivory diptych.
text: C. 390–401 – Priestess of Bacchus: Late Antiquity ivory diptych; documents the relationship of the senators Quintus Aurelius Symmachus and Virius Nicomachus Flavianus. It commemorates the marriage of the two families. The right panel is inscribed "Symmachorum", with an elaborately dressed priestess who makes an offer on an altar. It is now kept at the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.

summary: Jerome began translating the Old Testament into Latin after completing his translation of the New Testament.
text: Jerome, having finished the Latin translation of the New Testament, begins translating the Old Testament.

summary: Bleda, future king of the Huns, was born.
text: Bleda, king of the Huns

summary: Christian writer Prosper of Aquitaine was born.
text: Prosper of Aquitaine, disciple and Christian writer

summary: Hermit and saint Romanus of Condat was born.
text: Romanus of Condat, hermit and saint

summary: Christian stylite Simeon Stylites was born.
text: Simeon Stylites, Christian Stylite

summary: Tonantius Ferreolus, future praetorian prefect of Gaul, was born.
text: Tonantius Ferreolus, prefect of Gaul

summary: Gregory of Nazianzus, theologian and former Patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Gregory Nazianzus, theologian and Patriarch of Constantinople (b. 329)

summary: Apollinaris of Laodicea, bishop and theologian, died.
text: Apollinaris of Laodicea, bishop and theologian

summary: Roman historian and politician Aurelius Victor died.
text: Aurelius Victor, Roman historian and politician

summary: Diodorus of Tarsus, bishop and monastic reformer, died.
text: Diodorus of Tarsus, bishop and monastic reformer

summary: Emperor Theodosius I established Christianity as the Roman state religion, closed pagan temples, extinguished the eternal fire of Vesta, and disbanded the Vestal Virgins.
text: Emperor Theodosius I establishes Christianity as the official state religion. All non-Christian temples in the Roman Empire are closed. The eternal fire in the Temple of Vesta at the Roman Forum is extinguished, and the Vestal Virgins are disbanded.

summary: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus petitioned Emperor Theodosius I to reopen pagan temples, but was opposed by Ambrose.
text: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus, urban prefect of Rome, pleads for traditional cult practices. He petitions Theodosius I to re-open the pagan temples, but is opposed by Ambrose.

summary: Saint Telemachus died after being stoned to death by a crowd in Rome.
text: Saint Telemachus dies after being stoned to death. His date of death is also given to the year 404.

summary: A fire destroyed the Library of Alexandria, consuming numerous ancient scientific and literary works.
text: Flames destroy the great Library of Alexandria, established in the Mouseion in the fourth century BC. Among the items lost in the fire are works of science, including parchments by the Greek astronomer Aristarchus of Samos asserting that the Earth orbits the Sun, and dozens of dramatic works by Euripides and Sophocles.

summary: Patriarch Theophilus ordered the destruction of pagan temples in Alexandria, including the Serapeum, under imperial decree.
text: Patriarch Theophilus destroys all pagan temples in Alexandria under orders from Theodosius I. Christians go on an iconoclastic rampage, smashing religious symbols or monuments through the city and destroying the Temple of Serapis. The "Order of Monks" known as the Parabalani take charge of patrolling the streets.

summary: Roman general Flavius Aetius was born in Durostorum.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (Magister militum) of part Gothic heritage. (d.454)

summary: Roman empress Justina died.
text: Justina, Roman empress

summary: Christian monk and hermit Macarius of Egypt died.
text: Macarius of Egypt, Christian monk and hermit

summary: Bishop Peter of Sebaste died.
text: Peter of Sebaste, bishop of Armenia

summary: Stilicho defeated the Visigoths and Huns in Thrace, after which Emperor Theodosius I recruited Alaric as a Roman federate.
text: Stilicho, Roman general (magister militum), defeats the Visigoths and Huns in Thrace. Emperor Theodosius I permits Alaric to go free on condition he provides, as foederati, military services to the Roman Empire.

summary: Western Roman Emperor Valentinian II died under mysterious circumstances, found hanging at his residence in Vienne.
text: Emperor Valentinian II, age 21, dies while advancing into Gaul against the Frankish usurper Arbogast. He is found hanging in his residence at Vienne under unknown circumstances.

summary: Arbogast nominated Eugenius as emperor of the Western Roman Empire and sought recognition from Emperor Theodosius I.
text: Arbogast nominates Eugenius, Roman teacher of rhetoric, as the next emperor of the Western Roman Empire. He sends ambassadors to Theodosius's court asking for his recognition.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I issued an edict banning all pagan sacrifices, domestic rituals, and the Eleusinian Mysteries.
text: Theodosius I issues an edict reinforcing the prohibition of prayers or sacrifices at non-Christian temples, leading to the persecution of pagans and the end of the almost 2,000-year-old Eleusinian Mysteries. He also bans items of pagan spiritual significance that could be used in the home, such as incense or spiritual figures.
names: Persecution of pagans under Theodosius I

summary: Future Roman emperor Marcian was born.
text: Flavius Marcian, Roman Emperor (d. 457)

summary: Galla Placidia, Roman empress and daughter of Emperor Theodosius I, was born in Constantinople.
text: Galla Placidia, Roman Empress and daughter of Theodosius I (d. 450)
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Western Roman Emperor Valentinian II died at Vienne.
text: Valentinian II, Roman Emperor (b. 371)

summary: Bishop Gregory of Elvira died in Spain.
text: Gregory Bæticus, bishop of Elvira (Spain)

summary: Emperor Theodosius I proclaimed his eight-year-old son Honorius co-Augustus of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Emperor Theodosius I proclaims his son Honorius, age 8, co-ruler (Augustus) of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I ordered the destruction of pagan temples, holy sites, and religious objects throughout the Roman Empire.
text: Theodosius I demands the destruction of pagan temples, holy sites, and ancient objects throughout the Roman Empire.

summary: Emperor Theodosius I abolished the Ancient Olympic Games as part of his policy promoting universal Christian worship.
text: Theodosius I abolishes the Greek Olympic Games, ending a thousand years of festivals, as part of the general Christian policy to establish universal Christian worship in accordance with the doctrines set forth in the Nicene Creed (the next Olympic Games will not be held until 1896).

summary: The Synod of Hippo approved a biblical canon corresponding to that of the Roman Catholic Church.
text: Synod of Hippo: A council at Hippo Regius (Algeria) is hosted by the Church. The bishops approve a canon of Sacred Scripture that correspond to the Roman Catholic Church.

summary: Theologian and bishop Theodoret of Cyrrhus was born in Antioch.
text: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, bishop and theologian

summary: Arian bishop and theologian Eunomius of Cyzicus died.
text: Eunomius of Cyzicus, Arian bishop and theologian

summary: Emperor Theodosius I defeated and killed the usurper Eugenius at the Battle of the Frigidus, leading Arbogast to commit suicide.
text: Battle of the Frigidus: Emperor Theodosius I defeats and kills the usurper Eugenius. The forces of Theodosius are bolstered by numerous auxiliaries, including 20,000 Visigoth federates under Alaric. The Frankish general Arbogast (magister militum) escapes into the Alps and commits suicide.

summary: The Late Roman army maintained 200,000 frontier troops and a 50,000-man mobile reserve, relying extensively on Germanic recruits.
text: Late Roman army: The Notitia Dignitatum shows the development of forces in the Roman Empire. By now 200,000 soldiers guard the borders, and a reserve force of 50,000 is available for deployment. Many non-Roman soldiers are from Germanic tribes: Alamanni, Franks, Goths, Saxons and Vandals.

summary: The Huns crossed the frozen Danube and destroyed Gothic settlements while Emperor Theodosius I withheld Roman reinforcements.
text: Winter – The Huns cross the frozen Danube and destroy the villages built by the Goths. Theodosius I, six hundred miles away in Italy, sends no reinforcements to defend the northern frontier.

summary: The sacred fire of Vesta stopped burning in Rome following anti-pagan decrees.
text: In Rome, the sacred fire stops burning (see Vesta and Vestal Virgins).

summary: The Graffito of Esmet-Akhom, the last known Egyptian hieroglyphic inscription, was carved at Philae in Roman Egypt.
text: The last known hieroglyphic inscription, known as the Graffito of Esmet-Akhom, is written in Philae, Egypt.

summary: Epiphanius of Salamis attacked the followers of Origen and urged John II, Bishop of Jerusalem, to condemn Origen's writings.
text: Epiphanius of Salamis attacks Origen's followers and urges John II, Bishop of Jerusalem, to condemn his writings.

summary: A council of 310 Donatist bishops was held at Bagai in Roman Africa.
text: The Council of Bagaï in Africa brings 310 Donatist bishops together.

summary: The Roman usurper Eugenius died after his defeat at the Battle of the Frigidus.
text: Eugenius, Roman usurper

summary: Arbogast, Frankish general and Roman magister militum, died by suicide following the Battle of the Frigidus.
text: Arbogast, Frankish general

summary: Virius Nicomachus Flavianus, Roman historian and politician, died by suicide after the defeat of Eugenius at the Frigidus.
text: Virius Nicomachus Flavianus, Roman historian and politician (b. 334)

summary: Emperor Theodosius I died in Milan, resulting in the permanent division of the Roman Empire between Arcadius and Honorius.
text: Emperor Theodosius I, age 48, dies of a disease involving severe edema in Milan. The Roman Empire is divided for the final time into an eastern and a western half. The Eastern Roman Empire is centered in Constantinople under Arcadius, son of Theodosius, and the Western Roman Empire in Mediolanum under his brother Honorius.

summary: Arcadius married Aelia Eudoxia in Constantinople, while Galla Placidia was sent to Rome to live with Stilicho and Serena.
text: Arcadius marries Aelia Eudoxia, daughter of the Frankish general Flavius Bauto (without the knowledge or consent of Rufinus, Praetorian prefect of the East). His seven-year-old half-sister, Galla Placidia, is sent to Rome, where she spends her childhood in the household of Stilicho and his wife Serena.

summary: Alaric renounced Roman fealty, was acclaimed king by the Visigoths, and launched a war against both halves of the Roman Empire.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: Alaric, Visigothic leader of the foederati, renounces Roman fealty and is declared king, waging war against both parts of the Roman Empire, and ending a 16-year period of peace.

summary: Alaric besieged Constantinople before moving westward after receiving concessions from Rufinus.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: Alaric besieges Constantinople. After commitments from Rufinus, the Pretorian prefect of the East, and chief adviser to Arcadius, the Goths move further west.

summary: Arcadius, influenced by Rufinus, ordered Stilicho to stop his campaign against Alaric and leave the Eastern Roman Empire.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: Stilicho arrives in the fall with his army to fight the Goths. Rufinus, the strong man of the east, persuades the emperor to cancel Stilicho's campaign. Emperor Arcadius forbade Stilicho to attack Alaric and demandes that his army leave the territory of the East Roman Empire.

summary: Visigothic forces under Alaric invaded Thrace and Macedonia and exacted tribute from Athens.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: The Goths, led by Alaric, invade and devastate Thrace and Macedonia and impose a tribute on Athens.

summary: Rufinus, Praetorian prefect of the East, was assassinated outside Constantinople by Gothic troops under Gainas.
text: Rufinus, Praetorian prefect of the East, is murdered by Gothic mercenaries under Gainas.

summary: The Huns launched a major invasion of the Eastern Roman Empire, ravaging Armenia, Cappadocia, and Syria and threatening Antioch.
text: The Huns begin their large-scale attack on the Eastern Roman Empire. They invade Armenia, Cappadocia, and enter parts of Syria, threatening Antioch.

summary: An estimated 330,000 acres of farmland lay abandoned in Campania because of malaria and soil depletion.
text: An estimated 330,000 acres of farmland lie abandoned in Campania (southern Italy), partly as a consequence of malaria from mosquitoes bred in swampy areas, but mostly because imprudent agriculture has ruined the land.

summary: Augustine became bishop of Hippo Regius, focusing on reconciling Donatists with the Catholic Church in Roman Africa.
text: Augustine, age 40, becomes bishop of Hippo Regius (modern Algeria). His assignment is the reunification of the Roman Catholic Church in Africa, primarily focusing on the Donatist movement led by Primianus of Carthage.
names: Christianity in the Roman Africa province

summary: Theodosius I, Roman emperor, died at Milan.
text: Theodosius I, Roman emperor (b. 347)

summary: Rufinus, Roman consul and Praetorian prefect of the East, died when he was assassinated by Gothic troops.
text: Rufinus, Roman consul and politician

summary: Apa Bane, Christian hermit and saint, died in Egypt.
text: Apa Bane, Christian hermit and saint

summary: Ausonius, Roman poet and rhetorician, died.
text: Ausonius, Roman poet and rhetorician

summary: Gelasius of Caesarea, Christian bishop of Caesarea Maritima, died.
text: Gelasius of Caesarea, Christian bishop

summary: Macarius of Alexandria, Christian monk and desert father, died in Egypt.
text: Macarius of Alexandria, Christian monk

summary: Stilicho became regent for Honorius and de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire, securing the Rhine with Frankish and Alamannic federates.
text: Stilicho, Roman general (magister militum), controls the young emperor Honorius as his regent, and becomes the de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire. He enlists the Alemanni and the Franks, to defend the Rhine frontier.

summary: Alaric plundered Corinth, Argos, and Sparta, destroyed the Eleusinian sanctuary, and later settled the Visigoths in Epirus under a truce with Stilicho.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: The Visigoths, led by Alaric I, rampage through Greece and plunder Corinth, Argos and Sparta. They destroy the Temple of Eleusis, and harry the Peloponnese. Stilicho makes peace with the Goths, and allows them to settle in Epirus (Balkans).

summary: Petronius Maximus, future Western Roman Emperor, was born.
text: Petronius Maximus, Western Roman Emperor

summary: Stilicho trapped Alaric I in the Peloponnese but abandoned the campaign, allowing the Visigoths to escape north into Epirus.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: Stilicho traps the Visigoths under King Alaric in the Peloponnese, but decides to abandon the campaign against the Visigoths in Greece, thus allowing King Alaric to escape north to Epirus with his loot. Presumably, Stilicho has left Greece in order to prepare for military action in northern Africa, where a rebellion (see Gildonic Revolt in 398) seems imminent.

summary: Emperor Honorius enacted a law forbidding barbarian styles of dress, including trousers, boots, and long hair, in Rome.
text: Emperor Honorius passes a law making barbarian styles of dress illegal in the city of Rome. As a result of this law, everybody in Rome is forbidden from wearing boots, trousers, animal skins, and long hair. This law is passed in response to the increasing popularity of barbarian fashions among the people of Rome.

summary: Ambrose, bishop of Milan and major political figure of the Roman Empire, died.
text: Ambrose, Archbishop of Milan, dies in his diocese after 23 years in office, during which he dominated the political life of the Roman Empire.

summary: The Council of Carthage formally confirmed the biblical canon.
text: Council of Carthage: The biblical canon is definitely declared.

summary: Hispanic bishops convening at the First Council of Toledo condemned Priscillianism.
text: First Council of Toledo: Hispanic bishops, including Lampius, condemn Priscillianism.

summary: John Chrysostom was appointed Archbishop of Constantinople.
text: John Chrysostom is appointed Archbishop of Constantinople.

summary: Mor Gabriel Monastery was founded on the Tur Abdin plateau near Midyat.
text: Mor Gabriel Monastery is founded and located on the Tur Abdin plateau near Midyat (Turkey).

summary: Sulpicius Severus wrote the earliest known life of a saint, documenting Martin of Tours.
text: Sulpicius Severus writes the earliest biography of Martin of Tours, the first known "life of a saint" ever written.

summary: Augustine of Hippo began writing his autobiographical Confessions.
text: Augustine of Hippo begins his Confessions, an autobiography that recounts his intellectual and spiritual development.

summary: Ninian established the Candida Casa church at Whithorn and began missionary work among the Picts.
text: Scottish missionary Ninian establishes a church (Candida Casa) at Whithorn, and begins his work among the Picts.

summary: Ambrose, bishop of Milan, died.
text: Aurelius Ambrosius, bishop of Milan

summary: Martin of Tours, bishop and saint, died.
text: Martin of Tours, bishop and saint

summary: The Eastern Roman Empire made peace with Alaric, granting the Visigoths land in Illyricum and appointing Alaric magister militum per Illyricum.
text: Revolt of Alaric I: After Stilicho returns to Italy, the Eastern Roman Empire concludes a peace treaty with Alaric. The Visigoths are given a settlement area in Illyricum and their king is appointed magister militum per Illyricum.

summary: Flavius Stilicho defeated the rebel Gildo in North Africa, restoring the grain supply to Rome and driving Gildo to suicide.
text: Gildonic Revolt: Gildo, a Berber serving as a high-ranking official (comes) in Mauretania, rebels against the Western Roman Empire. The Gildonic Revolt is instigated by a powerful official in the Eastern Roman Empire named Eutropius, who wishes to undermine his enemies in the Western Roman Empire by cutting off the grain supply to Rome. After Gildo takes much of North Africa and cuts off the grain supply to Rome, Flavius Stilicho returns to Italy to raise troops against the rebels. After a short campaign in the desert, he defeats Gildo. Gildo flees and commits suicide by hanging himself.

summary: Eutropius celebrated his victory over the Huns with a Roman triumph in Constantinople.
text: Eutropius, Roman general (magister militum), celebrates his victory over the Huns ("the wolves of the North") in a parade through Constantinople (see 395).

summary: An imperial edict required Roman landowners to relinquish one third of their estates to settled barbarians.
text: An imperial edict obliges Roman landowners with plantations to yield 1/3 of their fields to the "barbarians" who have been settled in the Roman Empire.

summary: Emperor Honorius married Stilicho's daughter Maria.
text: Emperor Honorius marries Stilicho's daughter Maria.

summary: The Second Pictish War was fought between the Picts and Roman forces in northern Britain.
text: Possible date for the Second Pictish War.

summary: Emperor Arcadius, influenced by John Chrysostom and Eutropius, ordered the closure of pagan temples in Gaza.
text: John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople, receives a delegation of clergy who want to close the pagan temples at Gaza (Palestine) where worshippers are openly defying the law. John works through the eunuch Eutropius, who has great power over emperor Arcadius, and within a week an imperial Constitution is issued closing the Roman temples, but the official appointed to execute this order is bribed.

summary: Augustine of Hippo completed his autobiographical work, Confessions.
text: Augustine of Hippo completes his Confessions, an autobiography that recounts his intellectual and spiritual development.

summary: Didymus the Blind, Christian theologian of Alexandria, died.
text: Didymus the Blind, Alexandrian theologian

summary: Gildo, Moorish prince and Roman comes Africae, committed suicide following the defeat of his rebellion.
text: Gildo, Moorish prince and comes Africae (governor)

summary: Nectarius, archbishop of Constantinople, died.
text: Nectarius, archbishop of Constantinople

summary: Emperor Honorius closed the gladiatorial schools in Rome and ended gladiatorial games.
text: The Emperor Honorius of the Western Roman Empire, who is only 15 years old, closes the gladiatorial schools in Rome, and legally ends munera (gladiator games).

summary: Flavius Mallius Theodorus took office as Roman consul.
text: Flavius Mallius Theodorus becomes Roman consul and official at the imperial court of emperor Arcadius.

summary: Gainas seized power in Constantinople, deposed rival officials, and had Eutropius executed.
text: Gainas, a Gothic leader, is made magister militum and forms an alliance with deserters of Tribigild along the Bosphorus. He proclaims himself co-regent (usurper), and installs his forces in Constantinople. Gainas deposes anti-Gothic officials and has Eutropius, imperial advisor (cubicularius), executed.
names: List of political groups by country

summary: Yazdegerd I succeeded the deceased Bahram IV as ruler of the Sasanian Empire.
text: King Bahram IV dies after an 11-year reign. He is succeeded by Yazdegerd I, who becomes the thirteenth Sassanid Emperor of Persia.

summary: Pope Siricius died at Rome after commanding clerical celibacy and asserting western papal authority during a fifteen-year reign.
text: Pope Siricius dies at Rome after a 15-year reign in which he has commanded celibacy for priests, asserted papal authority over the entire Western Church, and threatened to impose sanctions on those who do not follow his dictates.

summary: Pope Anastasius I succeeded Pope Siricius as bishop of Rome.
text: Anastasius I succeeds Siricius as the 39th pope. He seeks to reconcile the churches of Rome and Antioch. Anastasius also condemns the doctrine of Origen.

summary: The Church of Rome acknowledged Flavian I as the legitimate bishop of Antioch.
text: Flavian I is acknowledged as legitimate bishop of Antioch by the Church of Rome.

summary: Pope Siricius died.
text: Pope Siricius

summary: Bahram IV, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Bahram IV, king of the Sassanid Empire (Persia)

summary: Roman consul and eunuch Eutropius died.
text: Eutropius, Roman consul and eunuch

summary: Christian monk and ascetic Evagrius Ponticus died.
text: Evagrius Ponticus, Christian monk and ascetic (b. 345)

summary: Christian saint Fabiola died.
text: Fabiola, Christian saint

summary: Ostrogothic general Tribigild died.
text: Tribigild, Ostrogothic general

summary: Emperor Arcadius granted his wife Aelia Eudoxia the official title of Augusta.
text: Emperor Arcadius gives his wife Aelia Eudoxia the official title of Augusta. She is able to wear the purple paludamentum and is depicted in Roman currency.

summary: Anthemius was sent on an embassy to Ctesiphon to congratulate King Yazdegerd I on his accession.
text: Anthemius, praetorian prefect of the East, is sent on an embassy to the Persian capital, Ctesiphon, to congratulate King Yazdegerd I on his accession the year before.

summary: A riot in Constantinople led to the burning of the Great Palace and the massacre of seven thousand Goths under Gainas, whose fleeing fleet was then destroyed at the Hellespont by Fravitta.
text: A riot breaks out in Constantinople; the Great Palace is burned to the ground. Gainas, a Gothic leader, attempts to evacuate his soldiers out of the city, but 7,000 armed Goths are trapped and killed by order of Arcadius. After the massacre, Gainas tries to escape across the Hellespont, but his rag-tag ad hoc fleet is destroyed by Fravitta, a Gothic chieftain in imperial service.

summary: Hunnic chieftain Uldin defeated Gainas across the Danube and sent his severed head to Arcadius in Constantinople.
text: Winter – Gainas leads the remaining Goths back to their homeland across the Danube. They meet the Huns and are defeated; the Hunnic chieftain Uldin sends the head of Gainas to Constantinople, where Arcadius receives it as a diplomatic gift.

summary: The Paeonians in Illyricum lost their distinct ethnic identity.
text: The Paeonians (Illyricum) lose their identity .

object: Two Marys with Angel near the Empty Tomb
summary: An ivory diptych panel depicting the Resurrection and the holy women at the empty tomb was produced in Rome.
text: Resurrection and "Two Marys with Angel near the Empty Tomb", panel of a diptych, found in Rome, is made. It is now kept at Castello Sforzesco, Milan .
names: Two Marys with Angel near the Empty Tomb

summary: The Vergilius Vaticanus, an illuminated manuscript of Virgil's poetry, was created in Rome.
text: The Vergilius Vaticanus, an illuminated manuscript containing fragments of Virgil's Aeneid and Georgics, is made in Rome.

summary: Roman physician Caelius Aurelianus practiced and worked on his medical treatise on acute and chronic diseases.
text: Caelius Aurelianus, Roman physician, is practising his work "De morbis acutis et chronicis" (Concerning Acute and Chronic Illness), a guide to acute and chronic diseases.

summary: Hypatia became the head of the Neoplatonist school in Alexandria.
text: Hypatia, Greek philosopher, distinguishes herself as one of the first female scientists and becomes head of the Neo-Platonist school at Alexandria.

summary: The mausoleum of Galerius in Thessalonica was converted into a Christian church.
text: The mausoleum of Galerius in Salonica (Greece) is converted into a church.

summary: Bishops from Gaza arrived in Constantinople to petition Arcadius to shut down the pagan temple of Marnas.
text: Bishops from Gaza (Palaestina Prima) arrive at Constantinople to ask Arcadius that he close the pagan temple of Marnas.

summary: Alan patrician and general Aspar was born.
text: Aspar, Alan patrician and general (magister militum)

summary: Sasanian king Bahram V was born.
text: Bahram V, Sasanian King of Kings (shahanshah)

summary: Hydatius, chronicler and bishop of Aquae Flaviae, was born.
text: Hydatius, bishop of Aquae Flaviae (modern Chaves, Portugal)

summary: Future pope Leo I was born.
text: Pope Leo I, Bishop of Rome

summary: Christian writer Salvian was born.
text: Salvian, Christian writer

summary: Christian church historian Sozomen was born.
text: Sozomen, Christian Church historian

summary: Christian priest and hermit Castor of Karden died.
text: Castor of Karden, Christian priest and hermit

summary: Gothic chieftain and Roman general Gainas was killed.
text: Gainas, Gothic chieftain and general (magister militum)

summary: Greek physician and medical writer Oribasius died.
text: Oribasius, Greek medical writer and physician

summary: Emperor Arcadius sent gifts to the Hunnic chieftain Uldin and formed an alliance with the Huns.
text: Emperor Arcadius sends many gifts to the Hunnic chieftain Uldin, in appreciation of his victory over the Goths and Gainas. Arcadius then allies himself with the Huns.

summary: Galatian slave-traders engaged in piracy along the coast of Roman Africa.
text: Piracy is committed by slave-traders from Galatia (Anatolia), along the coasts of Africa.

summary: Legio II Adiutrix was divided into two comitatenses units at Aquincum and shipped to Britannia.
text: The old Legio II Adiutrix, part of which had always been stationed at Aquincum (modern Budapest), is divided into two comitatenses, and shipped to Britannia.

summary: Roman general Stilicho led an extensive military campaign against the Vandals in Raetia.
text: Stilicho, Roman general (magister militum), leads his army in an extensive campaign against the Vandals in Rhaetia (Switzerland).

summary: The Temple of Artemis near Ephesus was dismantled.
text: The Temple of Artemis near Selçuk in Ephesus is dismantled.

summary: The Visigoths under King Alaric I crossed the Alps and invaded northern Italy.
text: The Visigoths, led by king Alaric I, cross the Alps and invade northern Italy.

summary: Emperor Honorius began using Ravenna as an administrative and military center.
text: Emperor Honorius begins to use the city of Ravenna as a temporary center for certain administrative and military functions. The city is chosen because of its proximity to the bulk of the Western Roman army and due to the fact that its relative poverty makes it a less tempting target for barbarian invaders than cities such as Rome or Milan. This event is often misinterpreted as the establishment of Ravenna as a capital. In reality, the capital of the Western Roman Empire was not truly established at Ravenna until 408.

summary: The Black Sea froze over completely.
text: The Chronicon Pachale (Paschal Chronicle) reports that the Black Sea is completely frozen.

summary: Innocent I succeeded Anastasius I as Bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Anastasius I dies at Rome after a 2-year reign, and is succeeded by Innocent I as the 40th pope proclaiming his universal power over the whole of Christendom.

summary: Future Roman emperor Theodosius II was born.
text: Theodosius II, Roman emperor (d. 450)

summary: Future Roman empress Aelia Eudocia was born in Athens.
text: Aelia Eudocia, Roman empress and wife of Theodosius II
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Future Roman emperor Leo I was born.
text: Leo I, Byzantine Emperor (d. 474)

summary: Pope Anastasius I died in Rome.
text: Pope Anastasius I

summary: The Visigoths advanced toward Mediolanum and besieged Asti in Liguria.
text: The Visigoths advance on Mediolanum (modern Milan) and besiege Asti in Liguria. King Alaric I sends envoys to negotiate a peace, but the Roman government refuses to make deals with "barbarians."

summary: Stilicho attacked the Visigoths at the Battle of Pollentia and captured the family of Alaric I.
text: Battle of Pollentia: Stilicho recalls troops from Britain and the Rhine frontier to defend Italy. He decides to attack the Goths on Easter Sunday, and manages to capture Alaric's wife and children.

summary: Emperors Arcadius and Honorius took office as Roman consuls.
text: Emperors Arcadius and his younger brother Honorius become Roman consuls.

summary: Jerome wrote treatises defending his positions against Rufinus.
text: Jerome writes "Apologiae contra Rufinum" and "Liber tertius seu ultima responsio adversus scripta Rufini".

summary: Acting on imperial authority, Cynegius oversaw the destruction of pagan temples in Gaza.
text: Cynegius, acting for Emperor Arcadius at the insistence of Bishop Porphyry, orders the destruction of pagan temples in Gaza.

summary: Roman orator and consul Quintus Aurelius Symmachus died.
text: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus, Roman consul and intellectual

summary: The capital of the Western Roman Empire was moved to Ravenna.
text: The capital of the Western Roman Empire was moved to Ravenna.

summary: Stilicho defeated the Visigoths under Alaric I north of Verona, prompting a withdrawal to Illyricum.
text: June – Battle of Verona: The Visigoths, under command of King Alaric I, invade Italy again, and advance through the Brenner Pass. Stilicho, with an army of 30,000 men, defeats the Goths north of Verona. Alaric makes a truce, and withdraws eastward to Illyricum.

summary: Emperor Honorius and Stilicho celebrated a triumph in Rome for victories against the Goths and Vandals.
text: Emperor Honorius and Stilicho are honored with a triumphal march, for the victories against the Goths and Vandals. This becomes the last victory celebrated in Rome.

summary: The two-year-old Theodosius II assumed the consulship in the Eastern Roman Empire.
text: Theodosius II, age 2, becomes consul of the Eastern Roman Empire.

summary: The Synod of the Oak deposed and banished John Chrysostom, bishop of Constantinople.
text: The Synod of the Oak deposes and banishes John Chrysostom, bishop of Constantinople, but shortly afterward he is recalled only to be banished again.

summary: Hilary, later bishop of Arles, was born.
text: Hilary, bishop of Arles (d. 449)

summary: Epiphanius of Salamis, bishop and Church Father, died at sea while returning to Cyprus.
text: Epiphanius of Salamis, Church Father

summary: Saint Telemachus was martyred by a crowd in Rome while attempting to halt a gladiatorial fight.
text: Last known gladiator fight in Rome: This date is usually given as the date of the martyrdom of Saint Telemachus, a Christian monk who was stoned by the crowd for trying to stop a gladiators' fight in a Roman amphitheatre.

summary: Empress Aelia Eudoxia died of an infection in Constantinople following a miscarriage.
text: Empress Eudoxia has her seventh and last pregnancy, which ends in a miscarriage. She is left bleeding and dies of an infection shortly after.

summary: The Gothic general Fravitta was executed in Constantinople at the behest of Joannes.
text: Fravitta, a Goth serving the Eastern Roman Empire as a high-ranking general, is executed on the behest of a powerful official named Ioannes. Fravitta is executed because he accused Ioannes of pitting Emperor Arcadius and Emperor Honorius (of the Eastern and Western Roman Empires, respectively) against each other. The execution of Fravitta results in the Eastern Roman Empire losing one of their most loyal and competent generals. (404 or 405)

summary: Empress Aelia Eudoxia exiled John Chrysostom, bishop of Constantinople, to Armenia.
text: Eudoxia exiles John Chrysostom, bishop of Constantinople, for criticizing her sumptuous lifestyle. He is banished to the Caucasus in Armenia. Pope Innocent I at Rome orders a synod to reinstate the bishop, but his envoys are imprisoned. Atticus becomes the new bishop of Constantinople.

summary: Saint Telemachus, Christian monk and martyr, died in Rome.
text: Telemachus, Christian monk and martyr

summary: Flavian I, patriarch of Antioch, died.
text: February – Flavian I, Patriarch of Antioch

summary: Aelia Eudoxia, Roman empress and wife of Emperor Arcadius, died.
text: Aelia Eudoxia, Roman Empress and wife of Arcadius
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: The Roman poet Claudian died.
text: Claudian, Roman poet

summary: Saint Paula of Rome, Desert Mother and associate of Jerome, died in Bethlehem.
text: Paula, Desert Mother and saint (b. 347)

summary: Emperor Honorius closed the Colosseum in Rome to abolish gladiator combats and public amusements.
text: Emperor Honorius closes the Flavian Amphitheatre (Colosseum), in an austerity move that abolishes amusements.

summary: Stilicho ordered the Sibylline Books to be burned in Rome.
text: Stilicho, Roman general (magister militum), orders the Sibylline Books to be burned, according to the Roman poet Rutilius Claudius Namatianus.

summary: Stilicho crushed a coalition of Vandals, Ostrogoths, and Quadi using troops withdrawn from the Rhine frontier.
text: Stilicho crushes a coalition of Asding Vandals, Ostrogoths and Quadi with an army raised from forces of the Rhine frontier, leaving this sector dangerously weakened.

summary: King Radagaisus led a large invasion force across the Alps into northern Italy and wintered in the Po Valley.
text: War of Radagaisus: King Radagaisus leads an invasion with a force of 20,000 men and crosses the Alps. He spends the winter in the Po Valley and is observed by Stilicho, who lacks sufficient strength to prepare an offensive against the invading German tribes. The exact numbers of the migration are unknown, probably nearly 100,000, including Alans, Burgundians, Goths, Vandals, and other smaller tribes.

summary: Flavius Aetius was sent as a child hostage to the court of Alaric I, king of the Visigoths.
text: Flavius Aetius is sent as a child hostage at the court of Alaric I, king of the Visigoths.

summary: Mesrop Mashtots devised the Armenian alphabet.
text: The Armenian alphabet is devised by Mesrop Mashtots.

summary: Theon of Alexandria, Greek mathematician and father of Hypatia, died.
text: Theon of Alexandria, Greek mathematician, dies at age 70 (approximate), having been helped in his work by his daughter Hypatia.

summary: Jerome completed his Vulgate Latin translation of the Bible by translating the Hebrew scriptures.
text: Jerome's Vulgate translation of the Bible into Latin is completed by his translations of the Tanakh from the Hebrew language.

summary: Augustine of Hippo opposed Donatism as a heresy in Roman Africa.
text: In the Roman province of Africa, Augustine of Hippo opposes Donatism as a heresy.

summary: Ricimer, later general and de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire, was born.
text: Ricimer, de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Salvian, Christian writer and presbyter, was born in Roman Gaul.
text: Salvian, Christian writer

summary: Saint Vigilius, bishop of Trent, died.
text: Saint Vigilius, bishop of Trent (b. 353)

summary: Arsacius of Tarsus, archbishop of Constantinople, died.
text: Arsacius of Tarsus, archbishop of Constantinople
names: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

summary: Saint Moses the Black, Christian monk and Desert Father, was killed by raiders in Egypt.
text: Moses the Black, Christian monk and priest (b. 330)

summary: Theon of Alexandria, the last recorded director of the Library of Alexandria, died.
text: Theon of Alexandria, last director of the Library of Alexandria

summary: Radagaisus retreated into the hills of Fiesole and was captured by the Romans.
text: Radagaisus is forced to retreat into the hills of Fiesole. There he tries to escape, but is captured by the Romans.

summary: The Romans executed Radagaisus and incorporated twelve thousand barbarian captives into the army or sold them into slavery.
text: Radagaisus is executed; 12,000 "barbarians" are incorporated into the Roman army, or sold as slaves.

summary: Roman legions in Britain mutinied and proclaimed Marcus emperor.
text: Autumn – The remaining Roman legions in Britain decide to mutiny. The usurper Marcus is proclaimed emperor.

summary: The Franks under Marcomer defeated the Vandals and killed King Godigisel, who was succeeded by his son Gunderic.
text: Vandal-Frankish war: The Vandals, led by Godigisel, are intercepted and defeated by the Franks under Marcomir. Godigisel is killed in battle and succeeded by his son Gunderic.

summary: A coalition of Vandals, Alans, and Suebi crossed the Rhine at Mogontiacum to invade Gaul.
text: Vandals, Alans and Suebians cross the Rhine at Mogontiacum (modern Mainz), beginning an invasion of Gaul (traditional date, this may have occurred in 405).

summary: Vandals, Alans, and Sciri introduced new crops such as rye, oats, and hops along with the wheeled plow to Europe.
text: Cultivation of rye, oats, hops, and spelt (a wheat used for livestock feed) is introduced in Europe by the native Vandals, Alans, and Sciri, who also introduce a heavy wheeled plow to be used for farming.

summary: Stained glass was used for the first time in Roman churches.
text: Stained glass is used for the first time in churches in Rome.

summary: Attila the Hun, future ruler of the Hunnic Empire, was born.
text: Attila the Hun, ruler of the Hunnic Empire (d. 453)

summary: Gothic king Radagaisus died.
text: Radagaisus, Gothic king

summary: Christian priest and martyr Alban of Mainz died.
text: Alban of Mainz, priest and martyr

summary: Godigisel, king of the Vandals, died in battle against the Franks.
text: Godigisel, king of the Vandals

summary: Gratian was installed as emperor in Britain following the death of Marcus.
text: Gratian, Roman usurper, is installed as emperor after the death of Marcus. According to Orosius, he is a native Briton of the urban aristocracy.

summary: The Roman usurper Gratian was assassinated.
text: Gratian is assassinated.

summary: Constantine III declared himself Roman emperor, took the legions from Britain to Gaul, and established his base at Arles.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415:Constantine III, a general (magister militum), declares himself Roman emperor. To extend his dominion over Gaul and Spain, he takes practically all the Roman garrisons from Britain and crosses the English Channel. Constantine occupies Arles and establishes tenuous authority over Gaul, sharing control with marauding "barbarians". This is generally seen as the beginning of Rome's withdrawal from Britain.

summary: Constans clashed with Honorius's relatives Didymus and Verinianus in Hispania.
text: Autumn - Resistance of Honorius cousins: In Spain comes Constans II into conflict with Didymus and Verinianus, nephews and followers of Honorius.

summary: Local leaders in Britain raised their own forces against Saxon raiders as Roman imperial administration ended.
text: End of Roman rule in Britain: After 360 years of occupation, the local regional British-Roman leaders raise their own levies for defence against Saxon sea rovers. They cultivate oysters, having learned the technique from the Romans.
names: End of Roman rule in Britain

summary: Roman usurper Gratian died.
text: Gratian, Roman usurper

summary: John Chrysostom, former archbishop of Constantinople, died in exile.
text: John Chrysostom, archbishop of Constantinople

summary: Roman usurper Marcus died in Britain.
text: Marcus, Roman usurper

summary: Maria, empress consort and wife of Emperor Honorius, died.
text: Maria, empress consort and wife of Honorius

summary: Victricius, bishop of Rouen and missionary, died.
text: Victricius, missionary and bishop of Rouen

summary: Arcadius died in Constantinople and was succeeded as Eastern Roman Emperor by his young son Theodosius II under the regency of Anthemius.
text: Emperor Arcadius dies in his palace at Constantinople, after a weak 13-year reign. He is succeeded by his 7-year-old son, Theodosius II, who rules under the domination of his devout Christian sister Pulcheria and Anthemius, who acts as regent.

summary: Emperor Honorius married Thermantia, the second daughter of Stilicho.
text: Summer – Emperor Honorius marries Thermantia, second daughter of Stilicho, his famous general (magister militum).

summary: Constantine III made Arles his headquarters, elevated his son Constans to Caesar, and sent him with Gerontius to Hispania.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: The Roman usurper Constantine III establishes his headquarters at Arles (Southern Gaul) and elevates his eldest son, Constans, to the rank of Caesar. He sends him with an expeditionary force under Gerontius to Hispania, in order to suppress the revolt of some members of the Theodosian dynasty, who are loyal to Honorius.

summary: Troops reviewing in Pavia mutinied, killed imperial dignitaries, and massacred suspected supporters of Stilicho.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: August 13 – During a review of troops at Pavia, the soldiers stationed at this city murder the dignitaries present, then rage through the city, slaying anyone they suspected of being a supporter of Stilicho.

summary: Stilicho was accused of treason and executed at Ravenna, followed by massacres of barbarian soldiers and their families.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: August 22 – Stilicho is accused of treason against Honorius and is decapitated at Ravenna. His Hun bodyguard is killed; mass murders of Vandal soldiers follow.

summary: Alaric I led the Visigoths into Italy, besieged Rome, and extracted a massive ransom in gold, silver, and goods from the Senate.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: September – Rex Alaric I of the Visigoths crosses the Julian Alps with an army of 30,000 men, and marches into the Roman heartland. He lays siege to Rome, and Gothic auxiliaries desert to join Alaric's forces. After much bargaining, the Senate agrees to pay him a ransom of 5,000 pounds of gold, 30,000 pounds of silver, 4,000 silken tunics, and 3,000 hides dyed scarlet.

summary: Alaric I secured the release of thirty thousand enslaved individuals in Rome.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Alaric also demands, and obtains, the freedom of 30,000 people who had been enslaved in Rome.

summary: The Hexamilion wall was constructed across the Isthmus of Corinth to fortify access to the Peloponnese.
text: The Hexamilion wall is constructed. Fortifications are built across the Isthmus of Corinth, guarding the only land route into the Peloponnese peninsula from Greece.

summary: Anthemius repelled an invasion of the Eastern Roman Empire across the Danube by the Huns under Uldin.
text: The Huns under Uldin cross the lower Danube and attack the Eastern Roman Empire, setting fire to frontier forts and taking control of the Castra Martis (modern Bulgaria). The Romans negotiate for peace, but Uldin demands an exorbitant gold tribute in return for his withdrawal. This demand is rejected and Anthemius forces the Huns back across the Danube.

summary: The Romans and the Huns exchanged hostages, sending Flavius Aetius to the Huns and receiving the young Attila at the court in Rome.
text: Attila, age 2, is sent as a child hostage to the court at Rome and in return, the Romans send Flavius Aetius to the Huns.

summary: King Yazdegerd I of Persia agreed to execute Arcadius' will and protect the young Theodosius II.
text: King Yazdegerd I of Persia maintains cordial relations with the Roman Empire. He becomes an executor of Arcadius' will and is entrusted with the care of the young Theodosius II until he comes of age.

summary: Alaric I exacted a heavy tribute from Rome, including three thousand pounds of pepper.
text: Alaric I exacts a tribute from Rome that includes 3,000 pounds of pepper. The spice is valued for alleged medicinal virtues and for disguising spoilage in meat that is past its prime.

summary: Eastern Roman Emperor Arcadius died at Constantinople.
text: Arcadius, Roman emperor

summary: Venerius, bishop of Milan, died.
text: Venerius, bishop of Milan and Saint

summary: Roman general Stilicho was executed at Ravenna.
text: Stilicho, Roman general

summary: Gerontius revolted against Constantine III in Hispania and proclaimed Maximus emperor.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Spring – Gerontius, Roman general (magister militum), who had been a partisan of Constantine III, revolts in Hispania. He elevates Maximus, his domesticus, as emperor.

summary: The Vandals crossed the Pyrenees into the Iberian Peninsula, while Alans and Suebi occupied other regions of Hispania.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: October 13 – The Vandals, led by King Gunderic, cross the Pyrenees into the Iberian Peninsula. They receive land from the Romans, as foederati, in Baetica (Southern Spain). The Alans occupy lands in Lusitania and the Suebi control parts of Gallaecia.

summary: Alaric I besieged Rome a second time and installed Priscus Attalus as rival emperor after Honorius refused peace talks.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: The Visigothic king Alaric I lays siege to Rome a second time, bringing the inhabitants close to starvation. Emperor Honorius, safe in inaccessible Ravenna, refuses to negotiate for peace, despite repeated offers from Alaric, who then comes to terms with the Senate and sets up a rival emperor, Priscus Attalus, prefect (praefectus urbi) of the city.

summary: Honorius agreed to send Roman noble hostages across the Danube in exchange for ten thousand Hun mercenaries.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Honorius agrees that sons of prominent families at court in Ravenna be sent beyond the Danube as hostages; in return, later he calls up ten thousand Hun mercenaries.

summary: Famine struck Hispania following the disruptive invasions of the Vandals, Alans, and Suebi.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Following the invasions by the Vandals, Alans, and Suebi in 409, chroniclers report severe disruption to food supplies in Hispania and nearby regions, leading to famine and hardship.

summary: Peasants in Armorica launched the Bagaudic rebellion against Roman authority.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Bacaudic Rebellion: Peasants in Armorica, northwestern Gallia launch a revolt. The unrest continues until 417.

summary: Daniel the Stylite, Christian monk and saint, was born.
text: Daniel the Stylite, Christian saint

summary: Didymus and Verinianus, cousins of Emperor Honorius, were executed by Constantine III.
text: Didymus and Verinianus, cousins of emperor Honorius.

summary: Roman consul Flavius Mallius Theodorus died.
text: Mallius Theodorus, Roman consul

summary: Serena, Roman noblewoman and widow of Stilicho, was executed at Rome.
text: Serena, noblewoman and wife of Stilicho

summary: Constantine III invaded Liguria across the Alps but retreated back to Gaul after Gerontius revolted in Hispania.
text: Spring – Constantine III crosses the Alps into Liguria (Northern Italy), but retreats to Gaul after Gerontius revolts in Spain against his son Constans II.

summary: Irish raiders, including the Uí Liatháin and Laigin, raided Wales and settled parts of Gwynedd.
text: Raiders from Ireland, such as the Uí Liatháin and Laigin, harry the coasts of Wales. They plunder towns and capture slaves but later colonise large areas of what is called Gwynedd, in particular Llŷn, the coasts of Arllechwedd, Arfon and the Isle of Mona .

summary: Honorius promoted Flavius Constantius to magister militum, making him the effective ruler of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Flavius Constantius, Roman general and politician, is promoted to the rank of magister militum. He becomes the imperial adviser of Honorius, and the power behind the throne in the Western Roman Empire.

summary: The Eastern Roman Empire sent six legions to Ravenna to assist Honorius, prompting Alaric I to depose Priscus Attalus.
text: The Eastern Roman Empire sends six legions (6,000 men) to aid Honorius at Ravenna. He negotiates with King Alaric I, who ceremonially deposes Priscus Attalus as co-emperor.

summary: The Visigoths under Alaric I entered through the Salarian Gate and sacked Rome for three days.
text: The Visigoths under Alaric I sack Rome after a third siege. Slaves open the Salarian Gate and Goths loot the city for three days; according to Augustine in The City of God and others, comparatively few Roman men are killed and women raped. Only two churches are burned, and people who took refuge in churches are usually spared. Many Romans who survived the Sack flee to Africa, or to the Eastern Empire (see Saint Jerome). It is the first time since 390 BC that Rome has fallen to an enemy. This marks the decline of the Roman Empire. Only 45 years later, in 455 AD, Rome will again be sacked, this time by the Vandals who will kill, burn, and loot much more ferociously than the Visigoths in 410 AD.
names: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

summary: The Visigoths captured Galla Placidia as a hostage following the sack of Rome.
text: Galla Placidia, daughter of Theodosius I, is captured by the Visigoths and becomes a hostage during their move from the Italian Peninsula to Gaul.

summary: Alaric I died at Cosenza while preparing to invade Africa, and was succeeded as king of the Visigoths by Athaulf.
text: Alaric I marches southwards into Calabria and makes plans to invade Africa. But a storm destroys his Gothic fleet and many of his soldiers drown. Alaric dies in Cosenza, probably of fever, and his body is buried along with his treasure under the riverbed of the Busento. He is succeeded by his brother-in-law Ataulf, who becomes king of the Visigoths.

summary: Emperor Honorius sent a rescript telling British cities to look to their own defense, effectively ending Roman administration in Britain.
text: According to Zosimus, this is the year when Emperor Honorius sends his Rescript (diplomatic letters) to the Romano-British magistrates, ending Roman rule in Great Britain. However this is likely an example of scribal error. Most recently, David Woods has argued that the account refers instead to Raetia, a Roman province north of Italy.

summary: Early Anglo-Saxons established a settlement at Mucking near the mouth of the River Thames.
text: At around this time, one of the first Anglo-Saxon settlements in Britain, Mucking, is established by the mouth of the Thames River.

summary: A massive fire devastated the port city of Aléria on the island of Corsica.
text: The city of Aléria on the island of Corsica is devastated by a huge fire, destroying its port and most of its inhabitants.

summary: The Council of Seleucia organized the Church of the East in Persia and adopted the Nicene Creed.
text: Council of Seleucia: Persian Christians create a national church and adopt the Nicene Creed.

summary: Honoratus founded Lérins Abbey on the Île Saint-Honorat.
text: Honoratus founds the Monastery of Lérins on the île Saint-Honorat (France), and forms a monastic community.

summary: Pope Gelasius I was born.
text: Pope Gelasius I, Pope in Catholic church (d. 496)

summary: Severinus of Noricum was born.
text: Severinus of Noricum, monk and saint

summary: Alaric I, king of the Visigoths, died at Cosenza.
text: Alaric I, king of the Visigoths

summary: Maron, a Syriac Christian monk and hermit, died near Cyrrhus.
text: Maron, Syriac Christian monk

summary: Gerontius defeated and killed Constans II at the Battle of Vienne.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Battle of Vienne: Emperor Constantine III sends his son Constans II to stop the advance of Gerontius. Constans is defeated and killed.

summary: Roman generals sent by Emperor Honorius defeated the usurper Constantine III at Arles and executed him at Ravenna.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Battle or siege of Arles: Emperor Honorius sends two Roman generals to deal with the usurper Constantine III in Gaul. They take over the army of Gerontius, Constantine's rebellious general (magister militum) who flees to Spain, then defeat Edobichus near Arles and defeat Constantine III. He is taken prisoner and put to death at Ravenna.

summary: The Burgundians and Gallic nobility proclaimed Jovinus emperor of the Western Roman Empire at Mogontiacum.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Following the defeat of Constantine III, the Burgundians and the Gallic nobility proclaim Jovinus, Gallo-Roman senator, emperor of the Western Roman Empire at Mogontiacum (modern Mainz).

summary: Athaulf led the Visigoths into Gaul under an agreement with Emperor Honorius to defeat usurpers.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: King Ataulf leads the Goths into Gaul at the instigation of Honorius, who promises to recognise a Visigothic Kingdom if he defeats the several usurpers who threaten the Roman Empire.

summary: The Alans established rule over the Roman province of Lusitania.
text: The Alans establish their rule in the Roman province of Lusitania (Portugal south of the Duero River and Spain).

summary: Germanic tribes in Hispania joined the Roman Empire as foederati.
text: The Teutonic tribes in Spain join the Roman Empire as foederati (allies with military commitments).

summary: Rabbula became bishop of Edessa.
text: Rabbula becomes bishop of Edessa.

summary: A council was held at Carthage to address the Donatist controversy.
text: The Councils of Carthage are held, on the issue of Donatism.

summary: Merovech, founder of the Merovingian dynasty, was born.
text: Merovech, Founder of the Merovingian dynasty and grandfather of Clovis I

summary: Constantine III, Roman usurper, was executed at Ravenna.
text: Constantine III, Roman usurper

summary: Constans II, son and co-ruler of the usurper Constantine III, was killed at Vienne.
text: Constans II, usurper and son of Constantine III

summary: Gerontius, rebellious Roman general, died in Hispania.
text: Gerontius, Roman general

summary: Gundomar I, king of Burgundy, died.
text: Gundomar I, king of Burgundy

summary: Athaulf led the Visigoths into southern Gaul, made his residence at Narbonne, and allied with Emperor Honorius against Jovinus.
