text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: The Visigoths, led by King Ataulf, move into the south of Gaul. He establishes his residence at Narbonne, and makes an alliance with Emperor Honorius, against the usurper Jovinus.

summary: The usurper Jovinus elevated his brother Sebastianus as co-emperor in Gaul.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Emperor Jovinus elevates his brother Sebastianus as co-emperor (Augustus) and takes control of Gaul.

summary: Heraclianus revolted against Emperor Honorius, halted grain shipments to Rome, and was condemned to death.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Heraclianus, governor (Comes Africae), revolts against Honorius and proclaims himself Augustus. He interrupts the grain supply to Rome. Honorius condemns him and his supporters to death with an edict at Ravenna.

summary: Anthemius supervised the construction of the Theodosian Walls at Constantinople during the reign of Theodosius II.
text: The Theodosian Walls are constructed at Constantinople during the reign of emperor Theodosius II. The work is carried out under supervision of Anthemius, notable praetorian prefect of the East.

summary: Emperor Honorius sent the historian Olympiodorus on a diplomatic mission across the Black Sea to the Huns.
text: Winter – Olympiodorus, historical writer, is sent on an embassy by Honorius, and sails in stormy weather around Greece up the Black Sea, to meet the Huns who are located on the middle Danube (modern Bulgaria).

summary: Roman forts along the west bank of the Danube were rebuilt and a new fleet was launched.
text: The forts on the west bank of the Danube, which were destroyed by the Huns, are rebuilt, and a new Danubian fleet is launched.

summary: Emperor Honorius issued an edict formally outlawing Donatism.
text: An edict of Honorius outlaws Donatism.

summary: Cyril became Patriarch of Alexandria.
text: Cyril of Alexandria becomes Patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Lazarus of Aix and Heros of Arles were expelled from their bishoprics on accusations of Manichaeism.
text: Lazarus, bishop of Aix-en-Provence, and Heros, bishop of Arles, are expelled from their sees on a charge of Manichaeism.

summary: Proclus, Greek Neoplatonist philosopher, was born in Constantinople.
text: Proclus, Greek Neoplatonist philosopher (d. 485)

summary: Theophilus, Patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Theophilus, Patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Sarus the Goth, a Gothic chieftain, was killed in Gaul by Athaulf.
text: Sarus, Gothic chieftain

summary: Uldin, chieftain of the Huns, died.
text: Uldin, chieftain of the Huns

summary: The Roman usurper Heraclianus was defeated in Italy and put to death in Carthage.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Heraclianus, Roman usurper

summary: Emperor Honorius issued an edict granting tax relief to Italian provinces devastated by the Visigoths.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: May 8 – Honorius signs an edict providing tax relief for the Italian provinces Tuscia, Campania, Picenum, Samnium, Apulia, Lucania and Calabria, which were plundered by the Visigoths.

summary: Athaulf conquered Toulouse and Bordeaux, captured Jovinus and Sebastianus at Valence, and executed them at Narbonne.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: The Visigoths, led by King Ataulf, conquer the towns of Toulouse and Bordeaux by force of arms. After a successful siege of Valence, he captures the usurper Jovinus and his brother Sebastianus. In Narbonne they are executed and their heads are sent to Honorius' court at Ravenna.

summary: Augustine of Hippo began writing De Civitate Dei to respond to claims that Christianity caused the decline of the Roman Empire.
text: Augustine of Hippo, age 59, begins to write his spiritual book De Civitate Dei (City of God), as a reply to the charge that Christianity was responsible for the decline of the Roman Empire.

summary: The Roman usurper Heraclianus died in Carthage.
text: Heraclianus, Roman usurper

summary: Marcellinus of Carthage was martyred.
text: Marcellinus of Carthage, martyr and saint

summary: The Roman usurper Jovinus was executed in Narbonne.
text: Jovinus, Roman usurper of Gaul

summary: Roman Christian poet Prudentius died.
text: Prudentius, Roman Christian poet (b. 348)

summary: Roman usurper Sebastianus was executed.
text: Sebastianus, Roman usurper and brother of Jovinus

summary: Visigothic king Athaulf married Galla Placidia, half-sister of Emperor Honorius, at Narbonne.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: January 1 – Galla Placidia, half-sister of emperor Honorius, is married to the Visigothic king Ataulf at Narbonne. The wedding is celebrated with Roman festivities and magnificent gifts from the Gothic booty.

summary: Pulcheria was proclaimed Augusta and assumed the regency of the Eastern Roman Empire for her younger brother Theodosius II.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: July 4 – Emperor Theodosius II, age 13, yields power to his older sister Aelia Pulcheria, who reigns as regent and proclaims herself empress (Augusta) of the Eastern Roman Empire.

summary: Constantius III campaigned against the Visigoths in Gaul, blockading ports and besieging Marseille.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Constantius III, Roman general (magister militum), begins a military campaign against the Visigoths in Gaul. He blockades the Gallic ports and besieges Marseille.

summary: The Visigoths proclaimed Priscus Attalus rival Roman emperor for a second time at Bordeaux.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Priscus Attalus is proclaimed rival emperor by the Visigoths for a second time at Bordeaux, in order to impose their terms on Honorius, who has his residence in Ravenna.

summary: Synesius, bishop of Ptolemais, died.
text: Synesius, bishop of Ptolemais

summary: Constantius drove the Visigoths from Gaul and captured the usurper Priscus Attalus.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Constantius, Roman general (magister militum), drives the Visigoths out of Gaul. He captures the usurper Priscus Attalus, and sends him under military escort to Ravenna.

summary: The Visigoths invaded the Iberian Peninsula, where King Athaulf was assassinated in Barcelona and Sigeric succeeded him briefly before being murdered.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: The Visigoths invade the Iberian Peninsula and begin to conquer territory taken previously by the Vandals. King Athaulf and his pregnant wife Galla Placidia leave Gallia Narbonensis; they relocate at Barcelona. Their infant son, Theodosius, dies in infancy, eliminating an opportunity for a Roman-Visigothic line. Athaulf is assassinated in the palace while taking a bath. Sigeric succeeds him, but after a reign of seven days he is also murdered.

summary: Wallia became king of the Visigoths and concluded a peace treaty with Emperor Honorius.
text: Roman Civil war of 407–415: Autumn – Wallia, brother of Athaulf, becomes king of the Visigoths. He accepts a peace treaty with emperor Honorius, in return for a supply of 600,000 measures of grain. After the negotiations he sends Placidia to Rome with hostages.

summary: The Daysan River flooded Edessa in Mesopotamia.
text: The Daysan River floods Edessa, Mesopotamia.

summary: Hypatia of Alexandria was murdered at the Caesareum by a Christian mob instigated by Patriarch Cyril.
text: March – Hypatia of Alexandria, Neoplatonist philosopher, is murdered by a Christian mob of Nitrian monks at the church (former temple conceived by Cleopatra VII) called Caesareum. Having driven out the Jews, Alexandria's new patriarch, Cyril, has instigated the mob after taking offense at Hypatia's scientific rationalism .

summary: John Cassian settled at a monastery in Marseille and organised monastic communities after an eastern model.
text: John Cassian, Christian theologian, settles at a monastery in Marseille (Gaul); he organizes monastic communities after an eastern model.

summary: The Eustathian schism in Antioch was resolved.
text: The Eustathian schism in Antioch is healed .

summary: Neoplatonist philosopher and mathematician Hypatia was murdered in Alexandria.
text: March – Hypatia of Alexandria, female Neoplatonist philosopher and mathematician, murdered in Egypt

summary: Athaulf, king of the Visigoths, was assassinated in Barcelona.
text: Athaulf, king of the Visigoths, assassinated

summary: Sigeric, king of the Visigoths, was assassinated after reigning for seven days.
text: Sigeric, king of the Visigoths, assassinated

summary: Former Roman empress consort Thermantia died.
text: Thermantia, Roman empress consort

summary: Emperor Honorius displayed the captured usurper Priscus Attalus in a triumph at Rome and exiled him to the Aeolian Islands.
text: Priscus Attalus, Roman usurper, is forced to participate in a triumph celebrated by Emperor Honorius, in the streets of Rome. After the festivities, he is exiled to the Lipari Islands (north of Sicily).

summary: King Wallia led the Visigoths in conquering Tarraconensis, occupying the gold mines at Las Médulas and forcing Jewish residents to convert.
text: The Visigoths continue their invasion of Hispania, and take control of Tarraconensis. King Wallia occupies the gold mines at Las Médulas, and forces Jewish citizens to convert to Christianity.

summary: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus began his journey from Rome to Gaul, later chronicled in De Reditu Suo.
text: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus begins his journey home from Rome to Gaul. This becomes the subject of his unfinished poem, De Reditu Suo.

summary: Emperor Honorius compelled his half-sister Galla Placidia to marry his general Constantius III and appointed him patricius.
text: Emperor Honorius forces his half-sister Galla Placidia into marriage to Constantius, his general (magister militum). He is appointed patricius and becomes a prominent member of the House of Theodosius.

summary: Exuperantius suppressed the Bagaudae Revolt in Armorica.
text: Exuperantius suppresses the Bagaudae Revolt in Armorica.

summary: The Western Roman Empire granted Aquitaine to the Visigoths, who established their capital at Toulouse.
text: The Visigoths are granted Aquitaine, and become allies (foederati) of the Western Roman Empire. King Wallia establishes his capital at Toulouse.

summary: Pope Innocent I condemned Pelagianism and excommunicated Pelagius.
text: January – Pope Innocent I condemns Pelagianism, and excommunicates the ascetic Pelagius.

summary: Pope Innocent I died and was succeeded by Pope Zosimus as bishop of Rome.
text: Innocent I dies after a 16-year reign in which he has restored relations between the sees of Rome and Antioch, enforced celibacy of the clergy, and maintained the right of the bishop of Rome to judge appeals from other churches. Innocent is succeeded by Zosimus as the 41st pope.

summary: Peter the Iberian, Georgian theologian and saint, was born.
text: Peter the Iberian, Georgian theologian and Saint

summary: Justa Grata Honoria, daughter of Constantius III, was born.
text: Justa Grata Honoria, daughter of Constantius III

summary: Pope Innocent I died in Rome.
text: Pope Innocent I

summary: Emperor Honorius persuaded Wallia, king of the Visigoths, to campaign against barbarian tribes in Hispania on behalf of the Roman Empire.
text: Emperor Honorius bribes Wallia, king of the Visigoths, into regaining Hispania for the Roman Empire. His victory over the Vandals in 416 forces them to retire to Baetica. The Visigothic territory in Gaul now extends from the Garonne to the Loire, and becomes known as the Visigothic Kingdom.

summary: Theodoric I became king of the Visigoths.
text: Theodoric I becomes king of the Visigoths. He completes the settlements in Gallia Aquitania and expands his military power to the south.

summary: Pope Boniface I succeeded Zosimus as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Boniface I succeeds Zosimus as the 42nd pope.

summary: Eulalius was elected antipope in Rome and appealed to Emperor Honorius for recognition.
text: Eulalius is elected antipope of Rome. He claims in a letter to Honorius his recognition as pope.

summary: Ricimer, future general and de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire, was born.
text: Ricimer, Germanic Roman general

summary: Pope Zosimus died in Rome.
text: Pope Zosimus

summary: Attaces, king of the Alans, died.
text: Attaces, king of the Alans

summary: Wallia, king of the Visigoths, died.
text: Wallia, king of the Visigoths

summary: The Roman Empire enacted a law prohibiting Roman subjects from teaching barbarians how to build ships.
text: A law is passed, prohibiting the act of instructing barbarians on shipbuilding in the Western and Eastern Roman Empires.

summary: Valentinian III, future Western Roman emperor, was born.
text: Valentinian III, emperor of the Western Roman Empire (d. 455)

summary: The Franks crossed the Rhine and invaded northern Gaul, prompting Castinus to assemble an army in Italy.
text: The Franks cross the Rhine and invade Northern Gaul. In Italia an army is prepared to campaign with Castinus as chief.

summary: Asterius campaigned in Gallaecia and ended the usurpation of Maximus.
text: Comes Asterius conducts campaign in Gallaecia and ends the usurpation of Maximus.

summary: A Roman army under vicar Maurocellus suffered a defeat at Braga in Gallaecia.
text: A Roman army under command of vicar Maurocellus suffers a defeat at Braga in Gallaecia.

summary: Yazdegerd I died and was succeeded by his son Bahram V as monarch of the Sasanian Empire.
text: Yazdegerd I dies after a 21-year reign, and is succeeded by his son Bahram V, who becomes head of the Persian Empire.

summary: Yazdegerd I ordered the execution of Abdas, bishop of Susa, for destroying a Zoroastrian fire temple.
text: Abdas, bishop of Susa, is accused of burning down one of the fire temples of Ahura Mazda, and after refusing to rebuild it, he is executed, under orders of Shah Yazdegerd I.

summary: Anthemius, future Western Roman emperor, was born.
text: Anthemius, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Ecdicius, Roman general and patrician, was born.
text: Ecdicius, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Euric, future king of the Visigoths, was born.
text: Euric, king of the Visigoths (d. 484)

summary: Libius Severus, future Western Roman emperor, was born.
text: Libius Severus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Majorian, future Western Roman emperor, was born.
text: Majorian, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Palladius, future Western Roman Caesar, was born.
text: Palladius, caesar and son of Petronius Maximus

summary: Valamir, future king of the Ostrogoths, was born.
text: Valamir, king of the Ostrogoths (he is also thought to have been born in 425 AD)

summary: Yazdegerd I, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Yazdegerd I, king of the Sassanid Empire

summary: Saint Porphyrius, bishop of Gaza, died.
text: Saint Porphyry, bishop of Gaza (Palestine)

summary: Jerome, Christian priest and translator of the Latin Vulgate Bible, died near Bethlehem.
text: Saint Jerome, priest and translator of the Bible

summary: Saint Abdas, bishop of Susa, died.
text: Saint Abdas, bishop of Susa (Iran)

summary: Orosius, Christian historian and theologian, died.
text: Orosius, Christian historian and theologian

summary: Pelagius, British monk and theologian, died in the East.
text: Pelagius, British monk

summary: Honorius appointed Constantius III as co-emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Constantius III is appointed co-emperor (Augustus) with his ineffectual brother-in-law, Honorius, and becomes the real ruler of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Venice was traditionally founded on the islet of Rialto with the dedication of the church of San Giacomo.
text: Venice is founded at twelve o'clock noon (according to legend) with the dedication of the first church, San Giacomo, at the islet of Rialto (Italy).

summary: Emperor Theodosius II married Aelia Eudocia in Constantinople.
text: Emperor Theodosius II marries Aelia Eudocia, a woman of Greek origin. The wedding is celebrated at Constantinople with chariot racing in the Hippodrome.

summary: Constantius III died suddenly of an illness in Ravenna.
text: Constantius III dies suddenly of an illness; his wife Galla Placidia becomes, for the second time, a widow.

summary: Castinus led a Roman army on a military campaign against the Franks in northern Gaul.
text: Castinus campaign against the Franks: A Roman army under command of Castinus fights against the Franks in Northern Gaul.

summary: Rugila, chieftain of the Huns, attacked the Roman dioceses of Dacia and Thrace.
text: Rugila, chieftain of the Huns, attacks the dioceses of Dacia and Thrace (Balkans). Theodosius II allows Pannonian Ostrogoths to settle in Thrace, to defend the Danube frontier.

summary: The Franks expanded their territory and sacked the Roman city of Augusta Treverorum.
text: The Franks conquer new territories in their kingdom and sack the old Roman capital Augusta Treverorum (modern Trier).

summary: Theodosius II declared war on the Sasanian Empire and sent Ardaburius to invade Mesopotamia.
text: Roman–Sassanid War: Theodosius II starts a war against the Sassanids, sending an expeditionary force under command of Ardaburius, and invades Mesopotamia.

summary: Ardaburius devastated Arzanene and forced Persian forces to retreat to Nisibis.
text: Autumn – Ardaburius devastates Arzanene (Armenia) and forces the Persians to retreat to Nisibis (Syria). King Bahram V allies himself with the Lakhmid Arabs of Hirah.

summary: Constantius III, co-emperor of the Western Roman Empire, died.
text: Constantius III, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Mary of Egypt, ascetic and hermit in the desert, died.
text: Mary of Egypt, patron saint

summary: Theodosius II signed a hundred-year peace treaty with the Sasanian Empire, establishing the status quo ante bellum.
text: End of the Roman–Sassanid War: Emperor Theodosius II signs a 100-year peace treaty with Persia after 2 years of war. He agrees to a status quo ante bellum ("the state in which things were before the war"), and both parties guarantee liberty of religion in their territories.

summary: Theodosius II required tower tenants in the Theodosian Walls to store provisions and agreed to pay annual tribute to the Huns.
text: Theodosius II issues a law to form provisions in peacetime. He instructs landowners leasing towers in the Theodosian Walls to assist with the build-up of emergency goods. Theodosius pays an annual tribute of 350 pounds of gold to the Huns in order to buy peace.

summary: A statue dedicated to Emperor Theodosius II was erected at the Hebdomon near Constantinople.
text: Theodosius II receives a statue at Hebdomon, military parade ground on the shores of the Propontis, just outside Constantinople. On its base (fragments are now in the Istanbul Archaeology Museum), an inscription praises him as “everywhere and forever victorious.”

summary: An earthquake cracked the walls of the Colosseum in Rome.
text: The walls of Rome's Flavian Amphitheater (Colosseum) crack during an earthquake.

summary: The Vandals defeated a Roman army under Castinus in Hispania Baetica.
text: Vandal war: The Roman commander-in-chief Castinus leads a defeat against the Vandals at Baetica.

summary: A Roman army invaded Frankish territory in Gaul and executed King Theudemeres and his family.
text: The Roman army invades Gaul; they capture and execute the Frankish king Theudemeres with his family.

summary: Peter of Illyria began construction of the basilica of Santa Sabina in Rome.
text: Petrus, bishop of Illyria, starts construction of the Church of Santa Sabina .

summary: Pope Celestine I succeeded Pope Boniface I as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Boniface I dies after a 4-year reign that was interrupted for 15 weeks, by the faction of the antipope Eulalius. He is succeeded by Celestine I as the 43rd pope.

summary: Saint Genevieve, patron saint of Paris, was born in Nanterre.
text: Genevieve, patron saint of Paris

summary: Licinia Eudoxia, future Roman empress, was born in Constantinople.
text: Licinia Eudoxia, Roman empress (d. 493)
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Pope Boniface I died in Rome.
text: Pope Boniface I

summary: Abraham of Cyrrhus, Syrian hermit and bishop of Carrhae, died in Constantinople.
text: Abraham of Cyrrhus, Syrian hermit and bishop

summary: Theudemeres, king of the Franks, was executed by the Romans in Gaul.
text: Theudemeres, king of the Franks

summary: Galla Placidia departed Ravenna with her children Justa Grata Honoria and Valentinian III for the court of Constantinople.
text: Early spring – Roman empress Galla Placidia departs with her children Grata Honoria and Valentinian to the court of Constantinople.

summary: Following the death of Emperor Honorius at Ravenna, Joannes seized the throne of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Emperor Honorius, age 38, dies at Ravenna of dropsy, perhaps pulmonary edema. With no children to claim the throne, Joannes, primicerius notariorum ("chief notary", head of the civil service), seizes the throne of the Western Roman Empire, and is declared emperor. Among his supporters are Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum). Joannes' rule is accepted in the dioceses of Gaul, Hispania and Italia, but not in Africa.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II refused to recognize Joannes as Western emperor and mobilized an expeditionary army under Ardabur and Aspar.
text: Winter – Emperor Theodosius II refuses to recognize Joannes as emperor, and prepares for war. He mobilizes an expeditionary force under command of Ardaburius, and his son Flavius Aspar.

summary: Theodoret became bishop of Cyrrhus and converted over a thousand Marcionites in his diocese.
text: Theodoret becomes bishop of Cyrrhus (Syria). He converts more than 1,000 Marcionites in his diocese.

summary: Theodosius the Cenobiarch, monk and monastery founder, was born in Cappadocia.
text: Theodosius the Cenobiarch, monk and founder of the Monastery of St. Theodosius

summary: Western Roman Emperor Honorius died of dropsy at Ravenna.
text: Honorius, Roman Emperor (b. 384)

summary: Former antipope Eulalius died in Campania.
text: Eulalius, antipope of Rome

summary: Flavius Anthemius Isidorus took office as Praetorian prefect of Illyricum at Sirmium.
text: Flavius Anthemius Isidorus becomes the new Praetorian prefect of Illyricum, comprising most of Greece and Serbia, taking office at the capital, Sirmium (now Sremska Mitrovica in Serbia).

summary: Emperor Theodosius II nominated his young cousin Valentinian III as Caesar of the Western Roman Empire and betrothed him to Licinia Eudoxia.
text: Emperor Theodosius II nominates his cousin Valentinian, age 5, the imperial title nobilissimus Caesar ("most noble") of the Western Roman Empire. Valentinian is betrothed to Theodosius's own daughter Licinia Eudoxia, who is only 2 years old.

summary: Joannes dispatched Flavius Aetius to negotiate military assistance from the Huns.
text: Roman usurper Joannes sends Flavius Aetius, governor of the Palace (cura palatii), to the Huns to ask for their assistance. After negotiating, he returns to Italy with a large force.

summary: A Roman army led by Ardabur departed Thessalonica and established a base at Aquileia in northern Italy.
text: Winter – A Roman army under the command of Ardaburius leaves Thessalonica (modern Central Macedonia) and marches for Northern Italy, where they make their base at Aquileia.

summary: The Church of the East declared its independence under Catholicos Dadisho.
text: Church of the East declares itself independent, under Catholicos of the East Dadisho.

summary: The usurper Joannes was captured at Ravenna, paraded on a donkey, and executed at Aquileia.
text: Roman civil war: Summer – Joannes, Roman usurper, is defeated at the fortified city of Ravenna and brought to Aquileia. After a humiliating parade on a donkey and the insults of the populace, he is executed.

summary: Six-year-old Valentinian III was installed as emperor of the Western Roman Empire under the regency of Galla Placidia.
text: Valentinian III, six-year-old son of Galla Placidia, is installed as emperor (Augustus) of the Western Roman Empire. Real power is in the hands of his mother who becomes a regent.

summary: Flavius Aetius entered northern Italy with a large Hunnic army and negotiated an appointment as commander-in-chief in Gaul.
text: Flavius Aetius leads a force of Huns (60,000 men) into Northern Italy. He reaches a compromise with Placidia, in return for obtaining the rank commander-in-chief (magister militum) in Gaul.

summary: The Huns advanced unopposed toward Constantinople but were halted by an outbreak of plague.
text: The Huns advance unopposed on Constantinople, but are halted by a plague that decimates their hordes (see 433).

summary: The Roman Empire disbanded the Sanhedrin following the death of Gamaliel VI.
text: After death of Gamaliel VI, the Sanhedrin is disbanded by the Roman Empire.

summary: The Mausoleum of Galla Placidia was constructed at Ravenna.
text: c. 425–426 – Mausoleum of Galla Placidia is built.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II founded the University of Constantinople at the urging of Empress Aelia Eudocia.
text: The University of Constantinople is founded by emperor Theodosius II at the urging of his wife Aelia Eudocia.

summary: The Syrian philosopher Iamblichus was born.
text: Iamblichus, Syrian philosopher

summary: Future Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno was born in Isauria.
text: Zeno, Byzantine Emperor

summary: Atticus, archbishop of Constantinople, died.
text: Atticus, archbishop of Constantinople

summary: Gamaliel VI, the last Nasi of the Sanhedrin, died.
text: Gamaliel VI, last Nasi (head of the Sanhedrin)

summary: The Western Roman usurper Joannes was executed at Aquileia.
text: Joannes, Roman usurper

summary: The Arab queen Mawiyya died.
text: Mavia, Arab warrior-queen

summary: Christian writer Sulpicius Severus died in Gaul.
text: Sulpicius Severus, Christian writer

summary: Flavius Aetius suppressed the Visigothic revolt of Theodoric I in southern Gaul.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), ends the Gothic revolt of Theodoric I in southern Gaul.

summary: King Gunderic of the Vandals accepted the request of the Alans in Hispania to become their king.
text: Rex Flavius Gundericus of the Vandals accepts the request of the Alans in Hispania to become their ruler .

summary: Augustine of Hippo published his theological work The City of God.
text: Augustine of Hippo publishes the De Civitate Dei, City of God.

summary: Sisinnius became Archbishop of Constantinople.
text: Sisinnius becomes Archbishop of Constantinople.

summary: Bonifatius revolted in Africa against Emperor Valentinian III and was convicted of treason by Galla Placidia.
text: Bonifacius, Roman governor (Last of the Romans), revolts in Africa against Emperor Valentinian III. Under the influence of Aetius, he is convicted of treason by empress-mother Galla Placidia.

summary: The Huns assimilated the Roman province of Pannonia Prima into the Hunnic Empire.
text: The Roman province of Pannonia Prima is finally assimilated into the Hunnic Empire.

summary: The Hephthalites invaded Western Asia, prompting Bahram V to send an expeditionary force into Khorasan.
text: The Ephthalites (White Huns) invade Western Asia and reduce the Sasanian Empire threat to the Eastern Roman Empire. King Bahram V sends an expeditionary force into Khorasan.

summary: Sisinnius I, archbishop of Constantinople, died.
text: Sisinnius I, archbishop of Constantinople

summary: Flavius Felix was elected consul for the Western Roman Empire.
text: Flavius Felix is elected consul for the Western Empire and issues consular diptychs during his political office.

summary: Flavius Aetius was appointed magister militum praesentalis after victories over Visigothic and Frankish forces in Gaul.
text: Flavius Aetius gains appointment as master of both services (magister militum praesentalis), after gaining victories in Gaul over Visigoth and Frankish forces.

summary: Gaiseric succeeded his half-brother Gunderic as king of the Vandals and Alans in Hispania Baetica.
text: King Gunderic, age 49, dies after a reign of 21 years, and is succeeded by his half-brother Genseric. He is styled with the title Rex Wandalorum et Alanorum ("King of the Vandals and Alans"). Genseric increases his power and wealth in the residence of the province of Hispania Baetica (Southern Spain).

summary: Flavius Aetius put an end to the invasion of northern Gaul by King Chlodio of the Salian Franks.
text: Frankish War (428): Commander-in-chief of the Roman army Aetius put an end to the invasion of Chlodio, king of the Salian Franks in Northern Gaul.

summary: Bahram V deposed Artaxias IV, ending the Arsacid dynasty and making Armenia a province of the Sasanian Empire.
text: Artaxias IV, last king of Greater Armenia, is deposed by Bahram V. The Arshakuni Dynasty ends and the kingdom becomes a province of the Persian Empire.

summary: Nestorius became Patriarch of Constantinople and began preaching the doctrine later termed Nestorianism.
text: Nestorius is made patriarch of Constantinople. He preaches a new doctrine, that will be called Nestorianism. It makes a distinction between the divine and human natures of Jesus, but comes under immediate attack from Pope Celestine I, and Cyril of Alexandria.

summary: Hydatius became bishop of Aquae Flaviae in Gallaecia.
text: Hydatius becomes bishop of Aquae Flaviae in Gallaecia (modern Chaves) in Portugal.

summary: John succeeded Theodotus as Patriarch of Antioch and supported Nestorius.
text: John succeeds Theodotus as patriarch of Antioch, and gives his support to Nestorius.

summary: Euthymius the Great founded a monastery near the Dead Sea in Palestine.
text: Euthymius the Great builds a monastery in Palestine, near the Dead Sea.

summary: Gunderic, king of the Vandals and Alans, died.
text: Gunderic, king of the Vandals and Alans (b. 379)

summary: Theodore of Mopsuestia, bishop and theologian, died.
text: Theodore of Mopsuestia, bishop and theologian

summary: Genseric led the Vandals and Alans across the Strait of Gibraltar into North Africa and blockaded supplies to Italy.
text: Spring – The Vandals, led by Genseric ("Caesar King"), invade North Africa. They land with a force of 80,000 men including Alans, and Germanic tribesmen with their families from the Iberian Peninsula, across the narrow Strait of Gibraltar. The Vandal fleet raids the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea, and blockades the grain and oil supply to Italy.

summary: Genseric ravaged Mauretania, forcing the Roman governor Bonifatius to retreat to Hippo Regius.
text: Genseric seizes lands from the Berbers and destroys church buildings all over Mauretania. He goes on a rampage forcing Bonifacius, Roman governor, to retreat to the fortified coastal town of Hippo Regius (modern Annaba).

summary: Bonifatius sued for peace with Galla Placidia and was elevated to magister militum of Africa.
text: Bonifacius, weakened by the civil war against empress Galla Placidia, sues for peace and is elevated to the rank of supreme commander (magister militum) of Africa.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II formed a commission in Constantinople to compile the Codex Theodosianus.
text: Emperor Theodosius II starts to reform the Codex Theodosianus in Constantinople. He establishes a committee to codify all Roman laws. All funds raised by Jews to support schools have to be turned over to the state treasury.

summary: The Temple of Athena on the Acropolis of Athens was sacked, and Athenian pagans were persecuted.
text: The Temple of Goddess Athena on the Acropolis of Athens is sacked. Athenian Pagans are persecuted.

summary: Pope Celestine I dispatched bishops Germanus of Auxerre and Lupus of Troyes to Britain to combat Pelagianism.
text: Pope Celestine I dispatches two bishops from Gaul, Germanus of Auxerre and Lupus of Troyes to Britain combat the Pelagian heresy.

summary: Hilary succeeded his kinsman Honoratus as archbishop of Arles.
text: Hilary succeeds his kinsman Honoratus and becomes archbishop of Arles.

summary: Domnus II, future patriarch of Antioch, was ordained as a deacon.
text: Domnus II, future patriarch of Antioch, is ordained as a deacon.

summary: Honoratus, archbishop of Arles, died.
text: Honoratus, archbishop of Arles

summary: Heremigar, a military leader of the Suebi, drowned in the Guadiana River while retreating from the Vandals.
text: Heremigarius, military leader of the Suebi

summary: The Vandals, led by King Gaiseric, advanced through North Africa and laid siege to Hippo Regius.
text: Spring – The Vandals under King Genseric extend their power in North Africa along the Mediterranean Sea, and lay siege to Hippo Regius (where Augustine has recently been bishop).

summary: Flavius Aetius suppressed a Gothic rebellion near Arles and captured the rebel leader Anaolsus.
text: Aetius puts an end to the Gothic revolt of Anaolsus, not far from Arles; Anaolsus is taken prisoner.

summary: Flavius Aetius defeated the Juthungi during his military campaign in the Alps.
text: April - Aetius defeats the Juthungi during his campaign in the Alps.

summary: Flavius Felix and his wife were executed in Ravenna on accusations of plotting against Flavius Aetius, who was promoted to patrician.
text: May - Flavius Felix, his wife and a deacon are accused of plotting against Aetius. They are arrested in Ravenna and executed. Aetius is granted the title of patricius (Roman nobility).

summary: The Burgundians destroyed an attacking Hunnic army near Worms, resulting in the death of the Hunnic leader Octar.
text: The Huns led by Octar attack the Burgundians, who occupied territory on the Rhine near the city of Worms (Germany). During the fighting Octar dies, and his army is destroyed.

summary: Augustine of Hippo died at the age of seventy-five during the Vandal siege of Hippo Regius.
text: Augustine dies during the siege of Hippo Regius at age 75, leaving behind his monumental work The City of God and other works that will have influence on Christianity.

summary: Peter the Iberian founded a Georgian monastery near Bethlehem.
text: Peter the Iberian founds a Georgian monastery near Bethlehem.

summary: Asclepigenia, an Athenian Neoplatonist philosopher and mystic, was born.
text: Asclepigenia, Athenian philosopher and mystic (d. 485)

summary: Future Western Roman Emperor Julius Nepos was born.
text: Julius Nepos, Western Roman Emperor (d. 480)

summary: Future Western Roman empress Marcia Euphemia was born.
text: Marcia Euphemia, Roman Empress

summary: Sidonius Apollinaris, Gallo-Roman poet, diplomat, and bishop, was born.
text: Sidonius Apollinaris, bishop and diplomat

summary: Syagrius, Roman official and future ruler of the Domain of Soissons, was born.
text: Syagrius, Roman official and son of Aegidius

summary: Victor Vitensis, African Catholic bishop and chronicler, was born.
text: Victor Vitensis, African bishop

summary: Flavius Felix, former Roman consul and patrician, was executed in Ravenna.
text: May – Flavius Felix, Roman consul

summary: Augustine of Hippo, Christian theologian and bishop, died in Hippo Regius.
text: Augustine of Hippo, bishop and theologian (b. 354)

summary: Saint Aurelius, bishop of Carthage, died.
text: Saint Aurelius, bishop of Carthage

summary: Nilus of Sinai, Christian bishop and ascetic author, died.
text: Nilus of Sinai, bishop and saint

summary: Octar, a Hunnic ruler, died during a campaign against the Burgundians near the Rhine.
text: Octar, Hunnic ruler

summary: Plutarch of Athens, Greek philosopher and head of the Neoplatonic Academy, died.
text: Plutarch of Athens, Greek philosopher

summary: Flavius Aetius put down rebellions in Raetia and Noricum and re-established Roman control on the Danube frontier at Augsburg.
text: Aetius campaign in the Alps: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), fights the rebellion in Rhaetia (Switzerland) and Noricum (Austria). He is attested in the city of Vindelicia (modern Augsburg), reestablishing Roman rule on the Danube frontier.

summary: Flavius Aetius pushed the Salian Franks across the Somme and made King Chlodio a Roman foederatus by treaty.
text: Aetius pushes the Salian Franks back across the River Somme. King Chlodio signs a peace treaty and becomes a foederatus of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: The Vandals captured Hippo Regius after a long siege and established it as their capital while a Roman expedition under Aspar landed at Carthage.
text: Hippo Regius becomes the capital of the Vandal Kingdom. After 14 months of hunger and disease, the Vandals ravage the city. Emperor Theodosius II sends an imperial fleet with an army under command of Aspar, and lands at Carthage.

summary: The Vandals routed Aspar's Roman forces and captured Marcian, who negotiated peace with King Gaiseric.
text: Aspar is routed by the Vandals and Flavius Marcian, future Byzantine emperor, is captured during the fighting. He negotiates a peace with King Genseric and maintains imperial authority in Carthage.

summary: Greek Neoplatonist philosopher Proclus began studying at the Platonic Academy in Athens.
text: Greek Neoplatonist philosopher Proclus begins studying at the Academy in Athens.

summary: The Council of Ephesus rejected Nestorianism, confirmed the Nicene Creed, and deposed Nestorius as Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: June – First Council of Ephesus: Nestorianism is rejected; the Nicene Creed is declared to be complete. Nestorius is deposed from his see.

summary: Maximianus was consecrated and enthroned as Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Maximianus is enthroned as Patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Pope Celestine I dispatched Palladius to Ireland to serve as the first bishop to the Irish Christians.
text: Pope Celestine I dispatches Palladius to serve as bishop to the Irish.

summary: Future Eastern Roman Emperor Anastasius I was born in Dyrrhachium.
text: Anastasius I, emperor of the Byzantine Empire

summary: Odoacer, future barbarian king of Italy, was born.
text: Odoacer, first "barbarian" king of Italy (d. 493)

summary: Paulinus of Nola, Christian bishop and poet, died.
text: Paulinus of Nola, Christian bishop and poet (b. 354)

summary: Forces under Bonifatius defeated Flavius Aetius near Rimini, though Bonifatius was mortally wounded, after which Aetius fled to the Huns.
text: Roman civil war: Roman forces under command of Flavius Aetius are defeated near Rimini (Italy) in battle. His rival comes Bonifacius is mortally wounded and dies several days later. Aetius flees to Dalmatia and seeks refuge with the Huns.

summary: Empress Galla Placidia appointed Sebastianus as magister militum of the Western Roman army.
text: Sebastianus, son-in-law of Bonifacius, becomes supreme commander (magister militum) of the Western Roman army. Empress Galla Placidia gives him considerable influence over imperial policy.

summary: King Rugila united the Huns on the Hungarian Plain and exacted annual tribute from the Eastern Roman Empire.
text: The Huns are united by King Rugila (also called Rua) on the Hungarian Plain. He exacts annual peace payments from the Eastern Roman Empire.

summary: Priest Petrus of Illyria completed construction of the Basilica of Saint Sabina on the Aventine Hill in Rome.
text: The Basilica of Saint Sabina at the Aventine (Rome) is finished by Priest Petrus of Illyria.

object: The Parting of Lot and Abraham
summary: Assembly began on the mosaic of The Parting of Lot and Abraham in the nave of the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome.
text: Assembly begins on The Parting of Lot and Abraham, a mosaic in the nave arcade of the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore.
names: The Parting of Lot and Abraham

summary: Pope Celestine I died and was succeeded by Sixtus III as bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Celestine I dies after a 10-year reign in which he led a vigorous policy against Nestorianism. He is succeeded by Sixtus III as the 44th pope.

summary: Saint Patrick was consecrated as a bishop and began his mission to convert the Irish to Christianity.
text: Saint Patrick, Roman Britain-born missionary, is consecrated a bishop and converts the Irish to Christianity until his death around 460.

summary: Christmas was celebrated for the first time in Alexandria.
text: Christmas is celebrated for the first time in Alexandria .

summary: Pope Celestine I died in Rome.
text: Pope Celestine I

summary: Roman noblewoman Anicia Faltonia Proba died.
text: Anicia Faltonia Proba, Roman noblewoman

summary: Roman general and African governor Bonifatius died from wounds received at the Battle of Rimini.
text: Bonifacius, Roman general and governor in Africa (born 354 BC).

summary: Saint Ninian, early Christian missionary in Scotland, died.
text: Saint Ninian, missionary in Scotland

summary: Flavius Aetius returned to Italy with Hunnic backing and established dominance over Emperor Valentinian III.
text: Flavius Aetius returns to Italy with the support of the Huns. He gains control over the young emperor Valentinian III, and becomes his "protector".

summary: Petronius Maximus was appointed consul of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Petronius Maximus is appointed consul of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Cyril of Alexandria and John of Antioch reconciled their Christological dispute over Nestorianism by signing the Formula of Reunion.
text: Pope Sixtus III helps to settle a Christological dispute between the patriarchs Cyril of Alexandria and John of Antioch, that has continued since the First Council of Ephesus, two years ago. They sign the "Formula of Reunion", thus ending their conflict over Nestorianism.

summary: Flavius Aetius took effective power in the Western Empire and settled the Huns in Pannonia along the Sava River.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum) in the service of Emperor Valentinian III, begins to hold power in Rome (this will continue for 20 years). He allows the Huns to settle in Pannonia, along the Sava River.

summary: Valentinian III executed his sister Justa Grata Honoria's lover after she became pregnant.
text: Justa Grata Honoria, older sister of Valentinian, becomes pregnant from an officer in her household. Circles in the court at Ravenna assume inevitably that Honoria is planning to raise her paramour to imperial rank and challenge her brother. Valentinian then has him executed.

summary: Rugila led the Huns in devastating Thrace and advanced toward the walls of Constantinople.
text: Summer – The Huns under Rugila devastate Thrace and move steadily towards Constantinople. The citizens prepare themselves for a long siege, depending on the strength of the Theodosian Walls.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II paid subsidies to the Huns to preserve peace for the Eastern Roman Empire.
text: Emperor Theodosius II bribes the Huns (after the death of Rugila) to keep the peace in the Eastern Roman Empire.

summary: The Vandals defeated Roman general Aspar in North Africa, forcing him to withdraw.
text: The Vandals in North Africa defeat the Roman general Aspar and force him to withdraw. He serves as consul at Constantinople.

summary: Attila consolidated power in Hungary and began joint rule over the Huns with his brother Bleda.
text: Attila, king of the Huns, consolidates his power in the Hungarian capital, probably on the site of Buda (modern Budapest). He jointly rules the kingdom with his brother Bleda.

summary: Following the death of Maximianus, Proclus was appointed archbishop of Constantinople.
text: Maximianus dies on Great and Holy Thursday. He is succeeded by Proclus, who becomes archbishop of Constantinople.

summary: Maximianus, archbishop of Constantinople, died.
text: Maximianus, archbishop of Constantinople

summary: Rugila, king of the Huns, died.
text: Rugila, king of the Huns

summary: Tibatto led the Bagaudae in a second major revolt in Armorica.
text: Second revolt of Bagaudae in Armorica under leading of Tibatto.

summary: Flavius Aetius began a military campaign in Gaul against the Burgundians following King Gunther's raids into Gallia Belgica.
text: Roman general (magister militum) Flavius Aetius begins a campaign in Gaul against the Burgundians, following their raids into neighbouring Gallia Belgica by King Gunther.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II issued an edict mandating the death penalty for heretics and pagans while confirming Judaism as legal.
text: Emperor Theodosius II orders a new edict for the death penalty of all heretics and pagans in the Empire. Judaism is considered a legal non-Christian religion.

summary: King Genseric made peace with the Western Roman Empire, retaining Mauretania and part of Numidia as foederati.
text: King Genseric concludes a peace treaty with the Romans, under which the Vandals retain Mauretania and a part of Numidia as foederati (allies under a special treaty) of Rome.

summary: Genseric made Hippo Regius a Vandal base and established a merchant fleet linking Africa and Italy.
text: The Vandals use Hippo Regius (modern Annaba) as a port for their expeditions. Genseric establishes a merchant fleet to transport goods between Africa and the Italian mainland.

summary: Huneric was sent as a child hostage to the Western Roman court at Ravenna to secure an alliance.
text: Huneric, eldest son of Genseric, is sent as a child hostage to the court at Ravenna to secure the alliance with the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Theodosius II exiled Nestorius, archbishop of Constantinople, to a monastery in the Libyan desert.
text: Theodosius II exiles Nestorius, archbishop of Constantinople, to a monastery in the Libyan desert at the behest of his sister Pulcheria.

summary: Ibas was elected bishop of Edessa.
text: Ibas is elected bishop of Edessa. He becomes associated with the growth of Nestorianism and openly preaching heretical doctrines in public.

summary: The Desert Father and theologian John Cassian died.
text: John Cassian, Desert Father and theologian

summary: The British monk Pelagius died.
text: Pelagius, British monk

summary: The Christian church historian Philip of Side died.
text: Philip of Side, Christian church historian

summary: Rabbula, bishop of Edessa, died.
text: Rabbula, bishop of Edessa

summary: Flavius Aetius, with Hun mercenaries under Attila and Bleda, crushed the Burgundians at Augusta Vangionum and killed King Gunther.
text: End of the Burgundian Revolt of Gunther: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), attempts to put an end to Burgundian raids in Gaul. He calls in Hun mercenaries under the command of Attila and his brother Bleda, which plunder Augusta Vangionum, killing some 20,000 Burgundians. The Kingdom of the Burgundians is destroyed; King Gunther and his family are killed (this epic disaster will later provide the source for the Nibelungenlied).

summary: King Theodoric I of the Visigoths besieged the Roman city of Narbonne.
text: In the Gothic War (436-439) besieges king Theodoric I the city of Narbonne; the Visigoths obtain access to the Mediterranean Sea and the roads to the Pyrenees.

summary: Gunther, king of the Burgundians, died.
text: Gunther, king of the Burgundians

summary: Flavius Aetius defeated Tibatto to quell the Bagaudae revolt, relieved Narbonne, and concluded a peace treaty with the Visigoths.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum) beats Tibatto and ends temporary the uprising of the Baguads. Then he secures the besieged city of Narbonne (Southern Gaul) against King Theodoric I. He concludes a peace treaty with the Visigoths, and becomes consul for the second time.

summary: Galla Placidia ended her regency as Valentinian III reached age 18 and assumed direct rule of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Valentinian III, age 18, rules as emperor over the Western Roman Empire. His mother Galla Placidia ends her regency, but continues to exercise political influence until her death in 450.

summary: Western Roman Emperor Valentinian III married Licinia Eudoxia in Constantinople, reuniting the branches of the Theodosian dynasty.
text: Valentinian III cements an alliance with the eastern emperor, Theodosius II, by marrying his daughter Licinia Eudoxia in Constantinople. This marks the reunion of the two branches of the House of Theodosius.
names: List of political groups by country

summary: Pope Sixtus III reminded Illyrian bishops of their obligations to his vicar in Thessaloniki after a synod at Constantinople challenged papal authority.
text: A synod at Constantinople attempts to impinge on the Pope's rights in Illyria. Proclus tries to implement the synod's decisions, and Pope Sixtus III reminds the Illyrian bishops of their obligations to his vicar at Thessaloniki.

summary: Childeric I, future king of the Salian Franks, was born.
text: Childeric I, king of the Salian Franks

summary: Remigius, future bishop of Reims, was born.
text: Remigius, bishop of Reims

summary: Theodosius II forbade divulging secrets of naval carpentry to prevent them reaching the Vandals.
text: Emperor Theodosius II forbids the divulging of secrets of naval carpentry, probably to avoid its spread to the rising Vandal power in North Africa.

summary: The Codex Theodosianus, a collection of Roman imperial edicts, was published.
text: The Codex Theodosianus, a collection of edicts of Roman law, is published.

summary: Empress Aelia Eudocia went on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem and brought back holy relics.
text: Aelia Eudocia, wife of Theodosius II, goes on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem, bringing back with her holy relics to prove her faith.

summary: The last recorded gladiatorial fights were held in the Colosseum at Rome.
text: The last gladiatorial fights are held in the Colosseum in Rome.

summary: King Hermeric of the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia retired due to illness and handed power to his son Rechila.
text: King Hermeric of the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia is forced to retire after a seven-year illness. He hands the government over to his son Rechila.

summary: Flavius Aetius defeated the Visigoths at the Battle of Mons Colubrarius.
text: In the Gothic War (436-439) besieges Flavius Aetius over the Visigoths in the Battle of Mons Colubrarius.

summary: Yazdegerd II succeeded his father Bahram V as king of the Sasanian Empire.
text: Bahram V dies after an 18-year reign as Sassanid king of the Persian Empire. He is succeeded by his son Yazdegerd II.

summary: The relics of John Chrysostom were translated to Constantinople.
text: Relics of John Chrysostom are transported to Constantinople.

summary: Epiphanius, future bishop of Pavia, was born.
text: Epiphanius, bishop of Pavia (d. 496)

summary: Bahram V, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Bahram V, king of the Persian Empire

summary: Visigoths under King Theodoric I defeated and killed Roman general Litorius before the walls of Toulouse.
text: Gothic War (436-439): Litorius, Roman general (Magister militum per Gallias), lays siege to Toulouse. During the decisive battle before the walls he suffers a severe defeat and is killed, and only the heavy loss of Visigoths makes King Theodoric I decide to agree to a provisional restoration of the status quo.

summary: Licinia Eudoxia was granted the title of Augusta following the birth of her daughter Eudocia.
text: Licinia Eudoxia, wife of emperor Valentinian III, is granted the title of Augusta following the birth of their daughter Eudocia.

summary: Attila and his brother Bleda accepted a four-point peace plan with Eastern Roman envoys at Margum.
text: Winter – Hun and Roman envoys meet at Margum (modern Bosnia and Herzegovina), an important market town on the Sava River. After negotiations, Attila and his brother Bleda, who are present, accept a four-point peace plan. Trading rights between the two states are confirmed and emperor Theodosius II pays an annual tribute of 700 pounds of gold.

summary: King Gaiseric broke his treaty with the Western Roman Empire and invaded Africa Proconsularis.
text: Vandal War (439-442): King Genseric breaks his treaty with the Western Roman Empire and invades Africa Proconsularis.

summary: Carthage fell to the Vandals, who made it the capital of the Vandal Kingdom.
text: Carthage falls to the Vandals. Genseric makes it his capital and establishes the Vandal Kingdom.

summary: The Vandals established control over North African grain supplies to exert influence over dependent Mediterranean powers.
text: The Vandals establish a North African granary that enables them to enforce their will on other nations, who are dependent on North Africa for grain and other food staples.

summary: The Ecclesiastical History of Socrates of Constantinople was concluded.
text: The Historia Ecclesiastica of Socrates of Constantinople is concluded, perhaps due to the author's death.

summary: The monastery of Mar Saba was founded near Bethlehem in Palestine.
text: The monastery of Mar Saba is founded near Bethlehem (Palestine).

summary: Eudocia, daughter of Emperor Valentinian III, was born.
text: Eudocia, Vandal queen and daughter of Valentinian III

summary: Christian monk and saint Sabbas the Sanctified was born in Cappadocia.
text: Sabbas the Sanctified, Christian monk and saint (d. 532)

summary: Western Roman general Litorius died after being captured by the Visigoths.
text: Litorius, general of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Roman general Flavius Aetius celebrated a triumph in Rome after campaigning against the Burgundians and Visigoths.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), returns as triumphator back to Rome, after several years' fighting the Burgundians and Visigoths in Gaul. He is honoured by a statue erected by the Senate, and by order of Emperor Valentinian III.

summary: Attila led the Huns in raids across the Danube, attacking merchants and sacking Viminacium.
text: The Huns under Attila reappear in force, along the frontier of the Western Roman Empire. They attack merchants on the north bank of the Danube and cities in Illyricum, including (according to Priscus) Viminacium, city of Moesia.

summary: A Vandal fleet sailed from Carthage to Sicily, raiding coastal settlements and besieging Palermo.
text: A Vandal fleet and their allies (Alans, Goths and Moors) set out from Carthage for Sicily, the principal supplier of oil and grain to Italy after the loss of North Africa. They loot all the coastal towns and besiege Palermo. Heavily laden ships return to the court of King Genseric.

actor: The Parting of Lot and Abraham
summary: The nave arcade mosaic depicting the Parting of Lot and Abraham was created in the basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome.
text: The Parting of Lot and Abraham, mosaic in the nave arcade, Church of Santa Maria Maggiore (Rome), is made.
cast: The Parting of Lot and Abraham
names: The Parting of Lot and Abraham

summary: Pope Leo I succeeded Sixtus III as the bishop of Rome.
text: Pope Sixtus III dies after an 8-year reign in which he has resisted heresy and sponsored major construction programs in Rome. He is succeeded by Leo I as the 45th pope.

summary: Pope Leo I began defining orthodox doctrine and condemned the monophysite teachings of Eutychianism.
text: Leo I begins to formulate Orthodoxy and condemns Eutychianism, an extreme form of monophysitism which holds that the human nature of Christ is absorbed by His divine nature.

summary: Pope Leo I sent a theological letter to Emperor Valentinian III regarding divine imperial inspiration.
text: Winter – Leo I sends a letter to Valentinian III stating, "by the Holy Spirit's inspiration the emperor needs no human instruction and is incapable of doctrinal error".

summary: Future Visigothic king Euric was born.
text: Euric, Visigothic king and son of Theodoric I (d. 484)

summary: Gaudentius, son of Roman general Flavius Aetius, was born.
text: Gaudentius, son of Flavius Aetius

summary: Gallo-Roman senator and praetorian prefect Tonantius Ferreolus was born.
text: Tonantius Ferreolus, Gallo-Roman senator and prefect of Gaul

summary: Future king Vakhtang I of Iberia was born.
text: Vakhtang I, king of Iberia (modern Georgia)

summary: Pope Sixtus III died in Rome.
text: Pope Sixtus III (b. 390)

summary: Emperor Theodosius II dismissed his sister Pulcheria at Constantinople at the urging of Chrysaphius.
text: Chrysaphius, chief minister, persuades Emperor Theodosius II at Constantinople to dismiss his sister Pulcheria, for her policy of exiling the Jews, and destroying their synagogues.

summary: Theodosius II sent the Eastern Roman fleet under Areobindus to Sicilian waters against the Vandals.
text: Theodosius II sends the Eastern imperial fleet, under the command of the Romano-Goth Areobindus, into Sicilian waters, taking the Vandals by surprise.

summary: Pulcheria left Constantinople for the Hebdomon and became a nun.
text: Pulcheria leaves for the seaport Hebdomon (Turkey), and becomes a nun to support Nestorianism in the Holy Land (Palestine).

summary: Attila led the Huns in a surprise attack on Constanța, capturing the Roman fort and slaughtering its garrison.
text: The Huns, led by Attila, attack Constanţa (modern Romania), one of the few remaining Roman forts on the northern bank of the Danube, and designated as a secure trading post. On a crowded market day, the Huns take the town by surprise and slaughter the garrison.

summary: The Alans suppressed the second Bagaudae revolt in Armorica, forcing its leader Eudoxius to flee to the Huns.
text: The second Revolt of Bagaudae in Armorica under leading of Eudoxius is knocked down by the Alans. Eudoxius fled to the Huns.

summary: Rechila succeeded his father Hermeric as sole ruler of the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia.
text: King Hermeric dies after a two-year illness; he is succeeded by his son Rechila, who becomes sole ruler over the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia.

summary: Rechila invaded Baetica and captured Seville, largely expelling Roman authority from the Iberian Peninsula.
text: Rechila invades Baetica and conquers the capital Seville. The Romans are driven from the Iberian Peninsula with the exception of the Levante.

summary: Hilary of Arles presided over the convening of the first Council of Orange.
text: The first Council of Orange is convened under the guidance of Hilary of Arles in Orange (France).

summary: King Yazdegerd II of Persia signed a peace treaty with Eastern Roman envoy Anatolius, agreeing not to fortify the frontier.
text: King Yazdegerd II of Persia signs a peace treaty after a short war with the Eastern Roman Empire. Theodosius II sends his commander, Anatolius, to conclude his terms and promise not to build any new fortifications along the border territories.

summary: Domnus II succeeded his uncle John as Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Domnus II succeeds his uncle John as Patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Hermeric, king of the Suebi, died after an illness.
text: Hermeric, king of the Suebi

summary: John I, Patriarch of Antioch, died.
text: John, Patriarch of Antioch

summary: Gaiseric mutilated the Visigothic wife of Huneric and expelled her to Toulouse to arrange a marriage with Valentinian III's daughter Eudocia.
text: Valentinian III forms a marriage proposal for his eldest daughter Eudocia and Genseric's son Huneric. He is already married to a Visigoth princess, and Genseric decides to free him of his obligations by accusing her of trying to poison him. He leaves her mutilated - her ears and nose are cut off - and sends her back to her father Theodoric I, in Toulouse (Gaul).

summary: The Huns destroyed the Roman fortress of Naissus and compelled the Roman Senate to pay an annual tribute of 700 pounds of gold.
text: The Huns, on a military campaign along the Danube and the Great Morava, destroy the city of Naissus (modern Serbia). They have mastered siege technology and are able to capture fortified cities. The Roman Senate agrees to pay Attila a tribute of 700 pounds of gold per year.

summary: Emperor Valentinian III signed a peace treaty with Gaiseric, recognising the Vandal Kingdom in Africa while recovering Sicily and Mauretania.
text: End of the Vandal War (439-442): Emperor Valentinian III signs a peace treaty with King Genseric, and recognises the Vandal Kingdom. He grants him sovereignty over most of Africa. Genseric gives back Sicily and Mauretania (Algeria and Morocco). This marks the end of the Vandal migrations; they settle in North Africa, with Carthage as their capital.

summary: The White Monastery was built near Sohag in Egypt.
text: The Monastery of St. Shenouda the Archimandrite (White Monastery) near Sohag (Egypt) is built.

summary: Byzantine architect and mathematician Isidore of Miletus was born.
text: Isidore of Miletus, Byzantine architect and mathematician (d. 537)

summary: Placidia, daughter of Roman Emperor Valentinian III, was born.
text: Placidia, Roman empress and daughter of Valentinian III

summary: Veh Mihr Shapur, Sasanian military commander and Marzban of Armenia, died.
text: Veh Mihr Shapur, Sasanian military officer and Marzban of Armenia

summary: Flavius Aetius settled the Burgundians around Geneva as Roman foederati following a peace treaty.
text: The Burgundians sign a peace treaty with Rome, agreeing to serve as foederati in the Roman army. They begin to move from the Upper Rhine and Flavius Aetius, commander-in-chief (magister militum), gives them land in the Geneva area (Maxima Sequanorum).

summary: Civil war, famine, and Pictish invasions struck Britain, prompting pro-Roman citizens to migrate to Gaul.
text: Period of civil war and famine in Britain, caused by rival kingdoms and Pictish invasions; the situation aggravates tensions between Pelagian and Roman factions. Pro-Roman citizens migrate towards Gaul.

summary: Flavius Aetius settled groups of Alans around Valence and Orléans to suppress regional unrest in Brittany.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), settles the Alans around Valence and Orléans, to contain unrest in Brittany.

summary: Emperor Valentinian III betrothed his eldest daughter Eudocia to Huneric, son of Vandal king Gaiseric.
text: Eudocia, eldest daughter of Emperor Valentinian III, is betrothed to Huneric, son of Vandal King Genseric (hostage in Italy).

summary: Attila established his royal residence along the Tisza River to prepare campaigns into the Balkans.
text: Attila the Hun establishes his residence along the Tisza River (modern Hungary), and plans the coming campaign in the Balkans.

summary: Pope Leo I suppressed the Gallican vicariate centered at Arles.
text: Pope Leo I extinguishes the Gallican vicariate.

summary: Dioscorus I became Patriarch of Alexandria following the death of Cyril.
text: Dioscorus I becomes Patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Brice, bishop of Tours, died.
text: Bricius, bishop of Tours

summary: Cyril of Alexandria, patriarch and theologian, died.
text: Cyril of Alexandria, patriarch and theologian

summary: Emperor Valentinian III issued Novel 18, imposing severe legal penalties against Manichaeans.
text: Roman emperor Valentinian III issues Novel 18 (Novella XVIII) on June 19, an imperial edict against Manichaeism. Heavy penalties are decreed against those who do not denounce the religion, and retain Manichaean books.

summary: Petronius Maximus was appointed to the rank of Patrician, becoming a principal political rival of Flavius Aetius.
text: Petronius Maximus, prominent aristocrat, is given the title of Patrician. He becomes the most honored of all non-imperial Romans, and political rival of Flavius Aetius.

summary: Attila became sole ruler of the Hunnic Empire following the death of his brother Bleda.
text: Bleda, co-ruler of the Huns, dies in a hunting accident. He is possibly murdered at the instigation of his younger brother Attila, with whom he has ruled since 434. Now about 39, Attila takes the throne for himself, and becomes king of the Hunnic Empire.

summary: Domnus II of Antioch convened a synod of Syrian bishops to confirm the deposition of Athanasius of Perrha.
text: Domnus II, Patriarch of Antioch, summons a synod of Syrian bishops to confirm the deposition of Athanasius of Perrha.

summary: Emperor Valentinian III issued Novel 17, formally recognising papal authority throughout the Western Roman Empire.
text: Valentinian III issued Novel 17 (Novella XVII) on July 8. It was an imperial edict recognizing papal authority in the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Desert Father Arsenius the Great died in Egypt.
text: Arsenius the Great, Desert Father

summary: Bleda, co-ruler of the Huns, died.
text: King Bleda of the Huns

summary: Bishop Germanus of Auxerre visited Ravenna to seek imperial leniency for the Bagaudae of Armorica.
text: Bishop Germanus of Auxerre visits Ravenna, seeking to soften imperial hostility towards the Bagaudae. On his arrival at the capital, empress-mother Galla Placidia sends him a silver dish with a choice selection of prepared dainties—all vegetarian, out of respect for the bishop's strict diet. Germanus petitions the Senate for leniency for the citizens of Armorica (Brittany).

summary: Vortigern appealed to Flavius Aetius for Roman military assistance against the Picts and Irish.
text: The Britons and Anglo-Saxon mercenaries, under King Vortigern, appeal to Flavius Aetius (magister militum of Gaul) for military assistance in their struggle against the Picts and Irish. Aetius has enough problems with Attila the Hun and is unable to send any help (according to Groans of the Britons).

summary: Turibius of Astorga held a local church synod.
text: A local synod is held by Turibius of Astorga.

summary: Flavian became patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Flavian becomes patriarch of Constantinople.
names: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

summary: Leontius, bishop of Trier, died.
text: Leontius of Trier, Bishop of Trier

summary: Proclus, patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Proclus, patriarch of Constantinople
names: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

summary: An earthquake severely damaged the Walls of Constantinople, which were subsequently rebuilt under praetorian prefect Constantine.
text: The Walls of Constantinople are severely damaged by an earthquake, which destroys large parts of the structure, including 57 towers. The population is threatened by a plague. Emperor Theodosius II orders Constantine, praetorian prefect of the East, to supervise the repairs. He employs the city's demoi ("Circus factions") in the work, and rebuilds the walls within 60 days.

summary: Attila led the Huns across the Danube into the Balkans, destroying Serdica and advancing as far as Thermopylae.
text: The Huns, led by Attila, cross the Danube, and invade the Balkans as far as Thermopylae (Greece). During the invasion, Serdica (modern Sofia) is destroyed. For disobeying the terms of the treaty made in 442, Attila triples his demand for tribute to 2,100 pounds (ca. 700 kg) of gold per year; and the ransom for each Roman prisoner to 12 solidi.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II dispatched an embassy including Priscus of Panium to the court of Attila.
text: Theodosius II sends an embassy to Attila; Priscus of Panium, envoy for the Eastern Roman Empire. Priscus records one of the few eyewitness accounts of the Hun kingdom.

summary: Attila defeated a Roman army at the Battle of the Utus and pillaged the Balkan provinces.
text: Battle of the Utus: Attila defeats the Roman army near the river Utus (Vit, Bulgaria). The Huns are forced to abandon the siege of Constantinople. They march north and plunder the defenseless Balkan provinces (including Thrace, Scythia, Moesia, Dacia and Illyricum).

summary: Emperor Theodosius II removed Aspar and Areobindus from their military commands to safeguard Constantinople.
text: Winter – Theodosius II chooses a policy to protect Constantinople against the Huns. He removes Aspar and Areobindus (magister militum) from their military commands.

summary: Bishop Germanus of Auxerre made his second journey to Britain.
text: Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, makes his second visit to Britain.

summary: The Synod of Toledo attempted to add the filioque clause to the Nicene Creed.
text: The Synod of Toledo (Spain) tries to add the filioque clause to the Nicene Creed. The Eastern Orthodox Church refuses to go along with this idea.

summary: The Roman general and former consul Areobindus died.
text: Areobindus, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Emperor Theodosius II sent an embassy led by Anatolius to Attila, concluding a peace treaty in exchange for tribute.
text: Emperor Theodosius II sends an embassy to Attila the Hun; Anatolius, an Eastern Roman general (magister militum) responsible for the security of the Eastern frontier, achieves a peace treaty with the Huns, in exchange for an annual tribute of of gold per year.

summary: Attila demanded the evacuation of Roman territory along the Danube from Singidunum to Novae to create a buffer zone.
text: Attila demands in the treaty the evacuation of the territory running from Singidunum (Belgrade, in Serbia) east along the Danube to Novae (Svishtov, in Bulgaria). This depopulated buffer zone deprives the Romans of their natural defensive advantages.

summary: Emperor Theodosius II ordered all non-Christian books to be burned.
text: Theodosius II orders all non-Christian books burned.

summary: Flavius Aetius suppressed the Bagaudae in Armorica and defeated the Salian Franks under Chlodio near Arras.
text: Flavius Aetius suppresses the Bagaudae in Armorica (Gaul), and defeats the Salian Franks under King Chlodio near Arras (Belgica Secunda); the invaders are stopped around a river-crossing near Vicus Helena.

summary: Rechiar succeeded his father Rechila as king of the Suebi in Galicia and married a daughter of Theodoric I.
text: Rechiar succeeds his father Rechila as king of the Suebi in Galicia (Northern Spain). He marries a daughter of the Visigoth king Theodoric I and converts to Catholicism.

summary: Eutyches was accused of heresy at a synod held in Constantinople.
text: Eutyches is accused of heresy at a synod held in Constantinople.

summary: Saint Cyriacus the Anchorite was born in Corinth.
text: Cyriacus of Athens, Greek anchorite and saint (d. 557)

summary: Rechila, king of the Suebi, died.
text: Rechila, king of the Suebi

summary: Saint Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, died in Ravenna.
text: Saint Germanus, bishop of Auxerre

summary: Emperor Valentinian III sent an emissary to Attila and rejected his demands regarding Danube spoils of war.
text: Emperor Valentinian III sends an emissary to Attila the Hun. The purpose of the meeting is a long-running dispute over spoils of war during the Danube offensive (441–442). Attila claims his lost property, but Valentinian and Flavius Aetius (magister militum) refuse this request.

summary: Flavius Orestes was sent to Attila's court and served as his chief secretary.
text: Flavius Orestes, Roman aristocrat, is sent to Attila's court and becomes a high-ranking secretary (notarius). He is the father of the future emperor Romulus Augustulus.

summary: The Second Council of Ephesus, chaired by Dioscorus of Alexandria, deposed Patriarchs Flavian and Domnus II.
text: The Second Council of Ephesus opens, chaired by Dioscorus, patriarch of Alexandria. Flavian, patriarch of Constantinople, and Domnus II, patriarch of Antioch, are deposed on August 8.

summary: A Roman synod under Pope Leo I repudiated the decisions of the Second Council of Ephesus.
text: October – A Roman synod repudiates all the decisions of the Second Council of Ephesus.

summary: Anatolius became patriarch of Constantinople following the deposition of Flavian.
text: Anatolius becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Maximus II became patriarch of Antioch.
text: Maximus II becomes patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Eugendus, future abbot of Condat Abbey, was born.
text: Eugendus, abbot of Condat Abbey

summary: Kavad I, future king of the Sasanian Empire, was born.
text: Kavadh I, king of the Persian Empire (d. 531)

summary: Flavian, patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Flavian, patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Eucherius, bishop of Lyon, died.
text: Eucherius, bishop of Lyon

summary: Hilary, bishop of Arles, died.
text: Hilary, bishop of Arles (b. 403)

summary: Emperor Theodosius II died after falling from his horse while hunting near Constantinople.
text: Emperor Theodosius II, age 49, falls from his horse while hunting at Constantinople and dies soon afterward. He has reigned since 408, mostly under the domination of his Christian sister Pulcheria, who has been allowed to return to court (see 441).

summary: Pulcheria married Marcian and crowned him emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire in the Hippodrome of Constantinople.
text: Pulcheria is forced to marry and co-rule the Eastern Roman Empire. She gives the imperial diadem to the Illyrian (or Thracian) officer and senator Marcian, age 58, and is crowned as empress in the Hippodrome at Constantinople, in the first religious coronation ceremony.

summary: Emperor Marcian ordered the execution of the court eunuch Chrysaphius and ended tribute payments to Attila.
text: Marcian orders the execution (or assassination) of the unpopular court eunuch Chrysaphius. He discontinues the tribute payments to Attila.

summary: The temples of Aphrodisias were demolished, its libraries burned down, and the city was renamed Stauroupolis.
text: All the Temples of Aphrodisias (City of Goddess Aphrodite) are demolished and its libraries burned down. The city is renamed Stauroupolis (City of the Cross).

summary: Justa Grata Honoria sent her ring to Attila asking for his aid, prompting him to claim half of the Western Roman Empire as her dowry.
text: Spring – Justa Grata Honoria, eldest sister of emperor Valentinian III, sends her ring to Attila the Hun in an effort to escape a marriage being forced upon her by her brother. Now about 34, she has had an affair with an officer in her household and has allegedly plotted to overthrow Valentinian, who has sent her to a convent at Constantinople. Attila announces his intention to marry her, says he expects to be given half the Western Roman Empire as her dowry, and gathers a large Hun invasion force. Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), musters an army in Gaul of Burgundians, Celts, Ripuarians, Salian Franks and Visigoths under the command of the Visigoth king Theodoric I.

summary: Remodeling of the dome of the Baptistery of Neon began in Ravenna.
text: Remodelling of the Dome of Baptistry of Neon, Ravenna (Italy) begins .

summary: King Yazdegerd II summoned Armenian nobles to Ctesiphon to pressure them to sever ties with the Western Church.
text: King Yazdegerd II summons the leading Armenian nobles to the Persian capital Ctesiphon, pressuring them to cut their ties with the Western Church.

summary: Metal horseshoes came into widespread use across Europe and the Near East.
text: Metal horseshoes come into more common use in the Near East and in Europe, increasing the efficiency of horsepower in agriculture and transportation.

summary: Justin I, future Byzantine emperor, was born.
text: Justin I, Byzantine Emperor (d. 527)

summary: Ariadne, daughter of Leo I and future Byzantine empress, was born.
text: Ariadne, Byzantine Empress
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Avitus, future archbishop of Vienne, was born.
text: Avitus, archbishop of Vienne (d. 518)

summary: Chilperic II, future king of Burgundy, was born.
text: Chilperic II, king of Burgundy

summary: Gunthamund, future king of the Vandals, was born.
text: Gunthamund, king of the Vandals (d. 496)

summary: Isidore of Alexandria, Neoplatonist philosopher, was born.
text: Isidore, Neoplatonist philosopher

summary: Hormisdas, future pope, was born.
text: Pope Hormisdas (d. 523)

summary: Thrasamund, future king of the Vandals, was born.
text: Thrasamund, king of the Vandals (d. 523)

summary: Eastern Roman Emperor Theodosius II died.
text: Theodosius II, Roman Emperor (b. 401)

summary: Peter Chrysologus, bishop of Ravenna, died.
text: Peter Chrysologus, bishop of Ravenna

summary: Former Roman empress Galla Placidia died.
text: Galla Placidia, Roman Empress (b. 392)
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Chrysaphius, eunuch and chief minister of the Eastern Roman Empire, was executed.
text: Chrysaphius, eunuch and chief minister

summary: Chlodio, king of the Salian Franks, died.
text: Chlodio, semi legendary Frankish king and supposed great-grandfather of Clovis I (b.390)

summary: Quodvultdeus, exiled bishop of Carthage, died.
text: Quodvultdeus, bishop of Carthage

summary: Socrates of Constantinople, church historian, died.
text: Socrates Scholasticus, church historian

summary: Sozomen, Byzantine church historian, died.
text: Sozomen, church historian

summary: Attila led an army of Huns and Germanic vassals across the Rhine into Gallia Belgica.
text: Spring – Attila gathers his vassals—Bastarnae, Gepids, Heruls, Ostrogoths, Rugians, Scirians and Thuringians (among others), and smashes through Germany, causing widespread panic and destruction. He arrives in Belgica with an army (50,000 men) and crosses the Rhine.

summary: The Huns invaded Gaul, sacking Metz and destroying numerous major cities.
text: Attila's forces invade Gaul and sack Metz. The major cities of Strasbourg, Worms, Mainz, Trier, Cologne, Reims, Tournai, Cambrai, Amiens and Beauvais are destroyed by the Huns.

summary: Huneric married Eudocia in Ravenna to strengthen the alliance between the Western Roman Empire and the Vandal Kingdom.
text: Eudocia, daughter of Emperor Valentinian III, marries Huneric in Ravenna. The engagement serves to strengthen the alliance between the Western Roman Empire and the Vandal Kingdom.

summary: Attila laid siege to Orléans while Flavius Aetius advanced into Gaul to combine forces with King Theodoric I.
text: June – Attila approaches Aurelianum (modern Orléans) and the city's inhabitants close the gates, forcing him to lay siege. After learning of the Hun invasion, Flavius Aetius (magister militum) moves quickly from Italy into Gaul, and joins forces with Visigoth king Theodoric I.

summary: A Roman coalition defeated the Huns at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains, during which King Theodoric I was killed.
text: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains (Châlons): Attila avoids a pitched battle near Orléans, and withdraws to the Catalaunian Plains (Champagne-Ardenne). The Roman coalition defeats the Huns, but Theodoric I is killed in the encounter. This is one of the last military victories of the Western Roman Empire, before the victories of Emperor Majorian against the Alemanni, Visigoths, Suebi and Burgundians, between 457 and 461.

summary: Thorismund succeeded his father Theodoric I as king of the Visigoths and was crowned at Toulouse.
text: Thorismund succeeds his father Theodoric I as king of the Visigoths. He is crowned in the capital at Toulouse, and extends the Visigothic Kingdom in Hispania.

summary: Egyptians in Alexandria rebelled against the Byzantine garrison and rejected Patriarch Proterius before being suppressed by imperial reinforcements.
text: The Egyptian people clash with Byzantine soldiers in Alexandria rejecting Proterius of Alexandria as the new Chalcedonian Patriarch. The Egyptian rebels besieged the imperial garrison in the ancient temple of Serapis, and burned them alive. The Byzantine military eventually suppressed the uprising with heavy reinforcements.

summary: The Council of Chalcedon repudiated Monophysitism, issued the Chalcedonian Definition, and deposed Dioscorus of Alexandria.
text: November 1 – Council of Chalcedon, an ecumenical council of the Church: The monophysitism of Eutyches is repudiated, and the Chalcedonian Definition set forth.
