As a result of this council, the Oriental Orthodox Churches eventually become a separate communion. More immediately, Jerusalem becomes a Patriarchate, and Dioscorus of Alexandria is deposed as Patriarch of Alexandria by the Council.
names: List of Armenian patriarchs of Jerusalem

summary: Syrian poet and theologian Jacob of Serugh was born.
text: Jacob of Serugh, Syrian poet and theologian

summary: King Theodoric I of the Visigoths died at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains.
text: Theodoric I, king of the Visigoths

summary: Egyptian abbot and saint Zeno the Prophet died.
text: Zeno the Prophet, Egyptian abbot and saint

summary: Attila led the Huns in an invasion of Northern Italy, destroying Aquileia, Padua, and Verona while sparing Milan.
text: The Huns under Attila invade Northern Italy. Emperor Valentinian III flees from Ravenna to Rome, and sends Pope Leo I to persuade Attila to return to the Hungarian Plain. The cities of Aquileia, Padua and Verona are destroyed by the Huns. Milan is saved because Attila is offered a huge amount of gold. Flavius Aetius (magister militum) is unable to raise a new army against him.

summary: Attila was persuaded to withdraw from Italy following an embassy led by Pope Leo I.
text: Rome is threatened by Attila but not attacked, due to a last-minute effort by Leo I. Threatened by news of reinforcements from the Eastern Roman Empire and the plague breaking out among the Huns, Attila is persuaded to withdraw.

summary: Fugitives fleeing the Hunnic invasion founded the city of Venice in the Venetian Lagoon.
text: The city of Venice is founded by fugitives from Attila's army who flee to small islands in the Venetian Lagoon.

summary: The Demotic script was inscribed for the last recorded time in Egypt.
text: Last known usage of Demotic script in Egypt.

summary: Future king of the Burgundians Gundobad was born.
text: Gundobad, king of the Burgundians

summary: Bishop and saint John the Silent was born.
text: John the Silent, bishop and Saint (died 558)

summary: Empress Pulcheria died of natural causes in Constantinople.
text: July – Empress Pulcheria dies of natural causes at Constantinople. She has commissioned many new churches in the city during her reign. Her death leaves Flavius Aspar (magister militum) as the dominant influence on her husband, Marcian.

summary: Anthemius married Marcia Euphemia, became comes, and was dispatched to fortify the Danubian frontier.
text: Anthemius marries Marcia Euphemia, daughter of Marcian, and is elevated to the rank of comes. He is sent to the Danubian frontier to rebuild the border defences.

summary: Attila died in Hungary following his marriage to Ildico, leaving his sons to fracture the Hunnic Empire.
text: c. March – Attila the Hun is found dead in bed, after a wedding feast with the Goth princess Ildico. He dies of a nosebleed at his Hungarian stronghold, drowning in his own blood, aged about 47. The Huns celebrate a strava (lamentation) over his burial place with great feasting. Attila's son Ellac is appointed successor, but his brothers Dengizich and Ernakh divide the Hunnic Empire by establishing their own kingdoms north of the Black Sea (Ukraine), supported by vassal states.

summary: Theodoric II succeeded his murdered brother Thorismund as king of the Visigoths.
text: Theodoric II succeeds his brother Thorismund as king of the Visigoths, Thorismund having been murdered after he violated the alliance with the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Frankish bishop Vedast was born in western Gaul.
text: Vedast, Frankish bishop

summary: Attila, ruler of the Huns, died.
text: c. March – Attila, ruler of the Huns (b. 406)

summary: Byzantine Empress Pulcheria died.
text: July – Pulcheria, Byzantine Empress

summary: Thorismund, king of the Visigoths, was assassinated.
text: Thorismund, king of the Visigoths, assassinated

summary: Emperor Valentinian III murdered his commander-in-chief Flavius Aetius during an imperial council meeting at Ravenna.
text: Emperor Valentinian III stabs his commander-in-chief Flavius Aetius to death, during a meeting of the imperial council at Ravenna. He has accused Aetius of plotting against him to seize power. After his assassination, the Western Roman Empire has no effective defender against its hostile barbarian neighbors (Alans, Franks, Ostrogoths, Vandals and Visigoths).

summary: Allied Germanic peoples led by King Ardaric defeated the Huns at the Battle of Nedao in Pannonia, killing King Ellac.
text: Battle of Nedao: Allied forces of subjected peoples (Gepids, Heruli, Ostrogoths, Rugii, Sciri and Suebi), under the leadership of King Ardaric, defeat the Huns under Ellac, eldest son of Attila the Hun, in Pannonia. Ellac is killed during the battle and succeeded by his brother Dengizich.

summary: Ardaric united the Gepids with other Germanic tribes and founded the Kingdom of the Gepids in the Pannonian Basin.
text: Ardaric unites the Gepids with other Germanic tribes, and founds the Kingdom of the Gepids in the Pannonian Basin.

summary: The Vandals conquered Malta.
text: The Vandals conquer Malta.

summary: Theodoric the Great, future king of the Ostrogoths, was born.
text: Theodoric the Great, king of the Ostrogoths (d. 526)

summary: Roman general Flavius Aetius died at Ravenna.
text: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Ellac, king of the Huns, died at the Battle of Nedao.
text: Ellac, king of the Huns

summary: Justa Grata Honoria, sister of Emperor Valentinian III, died.
text: Justa Grata Honoria, sister of Valentinian III

summary: Dioscorus the Great, deposed patriarch of Alexandria, died in exile at Gangra.
text: Dioscorus the Great, patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Hunnic retainers of Flavius Aetius assassinated Emperor Valentinian III and Heraclius on the Campus Martius in Rome.
text: Emperor Valentinian III, age 35, is assassinated by two Hunnic retainers of the late Flavius Aetius, while training with the bow on the Campus Martius (Rome), ending the Theodosian dynasty. His primicerius sacri cubiculi, Heraclius, is also murdered.

summary: Petronius Maximus became emperor of the Western Roman Empire and forced Licinia Eudoxia to marry him.
text: Petronius Maximus, former domesticus ("elite bodyguard") of Aetius, becomes (with support of the Roman Senate) emperor of the Western Roman Empire. He secures the throne by bribing officials of the imperial palace. Maximus consolidates his power by a forced marriage with Licinia Eudoxia, widow of Valentinian III.

summary: Emperor Petronius Maximus appointed Avitus as magister militum and elevated his son Palladius to Caesar.
text: Maximus appoints Avitus, most trusted general, to the rank of magister militum and sends him on an embassy to Toulouse, to gain the support of the Visigoths. He elevates his son Palladius to Caesar and has him marry Eudocia, eldest daughter of Valentinian III.

summary: An angry mob stoned Emperor Petronius Maximus to death as he attempted to flee Rome.
text: Maximus is stoned to death by an angry mob while fleeing Rome. A widespread panic occurs when many citizens hear the news that the Vandals are plundering the Italian mainland.

summary: King Genseric led the Vandals in sacking Rome for two weeks and took Empress Eudoxia hostage.
text: Sack of Rome: King Genseric leads the Vandals into Rome, after he has promised Pope Leo I not to burn and plunder the city. Genseric sacks the city for a period of two weeks. Eudoxia and her daughters, Eudocia and Placidia, are taken hostage. The loot is sent to the harbour of Ostia and loaded into ships, from whence the Vandals depart and return to Carthage.

summary: Avitus was proclaimed Roman emperor at Toulouse and recognized by Gallic chiefs near Arles.
text: Avitus is proclaimed Roman emperor at Toulouse, and later recognised by the Gallic chiefs in Viernum (near Arles).

summary: Emperor Avitus entered Rome with a Gallic army and restored imperial authority in Noricum.
text: Avitus enters Rome with a Gallic army. He restores the imperial authority in Noricum (modern Austria) and leaves a Gothic force under Remistus, Visigoth general (magister militum), at Ravenna.

summary: The Ostrogoths conquered the Roman provinces of Pannonia and Dalmatia.
text: The Ostrogoths conquer Pannonia and Dalmatia.

summary: A barter economy replaced organized trade as Roman citizens deserted their towns for the countryside.
text: Barter economy replaces organized trade as Romans and other citizens desert their towns for the countryside, where they will be less vulnerable to barbarian raids .

summary: An epidemic struck Vindobona and spread across Roman provinces.
text: The city of Vindobona (Vienna) is struck by an epidemic that spreads through the Roman provinces. The disease is probably streptococcus or a form of scarlet fever with streptococcus pneumoniae .

summary: Rusticus, future archbishop of Lyon, was born.
text: Rusticus, archbishop of Lyon

summary: Valentinian III, emperor of the Western Roman Empire, died in Rome.
text: March 16: Valentinian III, emperor of the Western Roman Empire (b. 419)

summary: Heraclius, primicerius sacri cubiculi of the Western Roman Empire, was murdered in Rome.
text: March 16: Heraclius, Roman courtier (primicerius sacri cubiculi )

summary: Petronius Maximus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire, died in Rome.
text: Petronius Maximus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Palladius, son of Emperor Petronius Maximus, died.
text: Palladius, son of Petronius Maximus

summary: Prosper of Aquitaine, Christian writer and disciple of Augustine, died.
text: Prosper of Aquitaine, disciple and Christian writer

summary: Emperor Marcian sent an embassy to Carthage to halt Vandal raids and quelled unrest on the Armenian frontier.
text: March – Emperor Marcian sends an embassy to Carthage, to end the Vandal raids in the Mediterranean from their strongholds in North Africa, and quells disturbances on the Armenian frontier.

summary: Ricimer defeated the Vandals on land at Agrigentum and in a naval battle off Corsica.
text: Emperor Avitus sends a Germanic naval expedition under command of Ricimer, to defend Sicily. They defeat the Vandals twice: on land at the Battle of Agrigentum, and in a sea battle off Corsica.

summary: The Vandals destroyed Capua, prompting Ricimer to secure Senate support for an expedition against Emperor Avitus.
text: Summer – Capua is destroyed by the Vandals. Ricimer is unable to end piracy in the western Mediterranean. Backed by his popularity, he gains the consent of the Senate for an expedition against Avitus.

summary: Ricimer besieged the Roman general Remistus at Ravenna and had him executed at Classis.
text: Remistus, Roman general (magister militum), is besieged with a Gothic force at Ravenna and later executed in the Palace in Classis, outside the city.

summary: King Theodoric II of the Visigoths invaded Spain on behalf of Emperor Avitus and shattered the Suebi near Astorga.
text: The Visigoths under King Theodoric II, acting on orders of Avitus, invade Spain with an army of Burgundians, Franks and Goths, led by their kings Chilperic I and Gondioc. They defeat the Suebi under King Rechiar on the Urbicus River, near Astorga (Gallaecia); this shatters the power of the Suebi.

summary: Ricimer and Majorian defeated Emperor Avitus near Piacenza and forced him to abdicate.
text: Battle of Placentia: Ricimer, supported by Majorian (comes domesticorum), defeats the usurper Avitus near Piacenza (northern Italy). They compel him to renounce the purple, and Avitus is obliged to become bishop of Piacenza.

summary: The Visigoths brutally sacked the Suebian capital of Braga and burned its churches.
text: The Visigoths brutally sack the Suebi's capital of Braga (modern Portugal); churches are burnt to the ground. Rechiar flees wounded from the battlefield.

summary: King Rechiar of the Suebi was captured at Porto and executed by the Visigoths.
text: December - Rechiar, first Germanic king to convert to Nicene Christianity, is captured at Oporto and executed.

summary: Remistus, Roman general and magister militum, died.
text: Remistus, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Eutyches, presbyter and archimandrite, died.
text: Eutyches, presbyter and archimandrite

summary: Rechiar, King of the Suebi, was captured and executed.
text: Rechiar, King of the Suebi (captured and executed)

summary: Emperor Marcian died at Constantinople and was buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles.
text: Emperor Marcian dies at Constantinople, possibly of foot gangrene, an infection contracted during a long religious journey. He is buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles, together with his late wife Pulcheria.

summary: Leo I became emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire, crowned by the Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Leo I, a Thraco-Roman (or Dacian) high-ranking officer, becomes the new emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire, reigning for nearly 20 years. He is first to accept the Byzantine crown from the hands of the patriarch of Constantinople.{{cite book|last= Bury|first= John Bagnell|author-link = John Bagnell Bury|title= History of the Later Roman Empire: from the death of Theodosius I to the death of Justinian|volume = 1|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=HqA9NA7MQ6kC|publisher = Dover Publications|year=2016 |orig-year = 1958|series = Dover books|isbn = 978-0-486-20398-0

summary: The Roman army acclaimed Majorian emperor after he defeated an Alemannic raid near Lake Maggiore.
text: Majorian is acclaimed emperor by the Roman army, after defeating 900 Alemanni near Lake Maggiore (Italy).

summary: Majorian was crowned emperor of the Western Roman Empire and recognized by Pope Leo I.
text: Majorian is crowned emperor of the Western Roman Empire and recognized by Pope Leo I. His rule is accepted in Italy, Dalmatia and some territories in Northern Gaul.

summary: Rebellious Alexandrians assassinated Patriarch Proterius of Alexandria and elected Timothy II Aelurus in his place.
text: Egyptian people rose in revolt and assassinate Proterius of Alexandria, and dragged his body through the streets of Alexandria and burned it. Timothy II Aelurus anti-Chalcedonian pope becomes elected by Egyptians.

summary: Victorius of Aquitaine computed new tables for calculating the date of Easter.
text: Victorius of Aquitaine computes new tables for celebrating Easter.

summary: Leontia, Roman empress and daughter of Emperor Leo I, was born.
text: Leontia, Roman empress and wife of Anthemius (d. 479)

summary: Medardus, future bishop of Vermandois, was born.
text: Medardus, bishop of Vermandois

summary: Eastern Roman Emperor Marcian died.
text: Flavius Marcian, Roman emperor (b. 392)

summary: Ibas, bishop of Edessa, died.
text: Ibas, bishop of Edessa (modern Turkey)

summary: Avitus, former emperor of the Western Roman Empire, died.
text: Avitus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Framta, king of the Suebi, died.
text: Framta, king of the Sueves

summary: Merovech, king of the Salian Franks, died.
text: Merovech, king of the Salian Franks

summary: Palladius, the first bishop of Ireland, died.
text: Palladius, first bishop of Ireland

summary: Proterius, Patriarch of Alexandria, was murdered.
text: Saint Proterius, Patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, bishop and Christian theologian, died.
text: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, bishop and theologian

summary: Valerian of Abbenza, bishop and saint, died in North Africa during the Vandal persecution.
text: Valerian of Abbenza, bishop and saint (b. 377)

summary: Yazdegerd II, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Yazdegerd II, king of the Persian Empire

summary: Eastern Roman Emperor Leo I appointed Majorian as magister militum in the west.
text: The Byzantine augustus Leo I the Thracian appointed Majorian Magister militum in the west.

summary: Emperor Majorian built a Roman fleet at Miseno and Ravenna and recruited numerous barbarian mercenaries.
text: Emperor Majorian builds a Roman fleet at Miseno and Ravenna. He strengthens the army, by recruiting a large number of barbarian mercenaries (Bastarnae, Burgundians, Huns, Ostrogoths, Rugii, Scythians and Suebi).

summary: Majorian defeated Vandal invaders near Sinuessa after they landed in Campania and raided the region.
text: Summer – The Vandals land in Campania, at the mouth of the Liri or the Garigliano River, and devastate the region. Majorian personally leads the Roman army and defeats the invaders near Sinuessa, destroying their ships on the seashore, loaded with booty.

summary: Majorian defeated the Visigoths under King Theodoric II at Arles, forcing him to sign a peace treaty and become a Roman foederatus.
text: Battle of Arelate: Majorian defeats the Visigoths under King Theodoric II at Arles (Southern Gaul), near the Rhone River. Theodoric is forced to sign a peace treaty and becomes a foederatus (pl. foederati) of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Majorian defeated the Burgundians under King Gondioc at Lugdunum and forced the Bagaudae into an alliance against the Suebi.
text: Winter – Majorian enters the Rhone Valley, and defeats the Burgundians under King Gondioc at Lugdunum. He forces the Bagaudae to join the western coalition against the Suebi in Spain.

summary: Childeric I succeeded Merovech as king of the Salian Franks, established his capital at Tournai, and became a foederatus of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Childeric I succeeds his father Merovech as king of the Salian Franks. He establishes his capital at Tournai (modern Belgium) and becomes a foederatus (pl. foederati) of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Gennadius I became patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Gennadius I becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Damascius, Syrian Neoplatonist philosopher, was born.
text: Damascius, Syrian neoplatonist

summary: Anatolius, patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Anatolius, patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Emperor Leo I signed a peace treaty with the Ostrogoths, and King Theodemir sent Theodoric the Great as a hostage to Constantinople.
text: Emperor Leo I signs a peace treaty with the Ostrogoths. King Theodemir sends his son, the future Theodoric the Great, age 5, as a child hostage to Constantinople. He learns at court about Latin, military tactics and religion (until 469).

summary: King Vortigern was besieged and burnt to death at Ganarew by a Romano-British force under Ambrosius Aurelianus.
text: King Vortigern is burnt to death, while being besieged by a Romano-British force under Ambrosius Aurelianus at Ganarew (Herefordshire).

summary: The Franks conquered Trier, entering Roman politics as a growing military power.
text: The Franks conquer the city of Trier. The Frankish Kingdom becomes a military power and gets involved in Roman politics.

summary: Remigius was elected bishop of Reims at the age of twenty-two.
text: Remigius, age 22, is elected bishop of Reims .

summary: Simeon Stylites, Christian ascetic and pillar-saint, died.
text: Simeon Stylites, Christian pillar-saint.

summary: Hormizd III, king of the Sasanian Empire, died.
text: Hormizd III, king of the Sasanian Empire

summary: Vortigern, king of the Britons, died.
text: Vortigern, king of the Britons

summary: Emperor Majorian gathered an army in Liguria, marched into Aquitaine, and visited King Theodoric II at Toulouse.
text: Emperor Majorian gathers an expeditionary force (Alans and other barbarians) in Liguria, and enters Aquitaine after a long march, where he visits King Theodoric II at Toulouse.

summary: Majorian invaded Hispania, leading Roman and Visigothic forces to defeat the Suebi and conquer Lusitania.
text: Majorian invades Hispania; his generals Nepotianus and Sunieric lead a Visigoth army into Gallaecia. The Suebi are defeated and Lusitania (modern Portugal) is conquered.

summary: After Majorian refused peace terms, King Genseric and the Vandals devastated Mauretania and poisoned the wells.
text: King Genseric, fearing a Roman invasion, tries to negotiate peace with Majorian, who refuses. The Vandals devastate Mauretania and Moorish warriors poison the wells.

summary: King Genseric destroyed Majorian's fleet at Nova Carthago, forcing the abandonment of the invasion of the Vandal Kingdom.
text: Majorian assembles a large fleet in Nova Carthago (Cartagena) in preparation for an invasion of the Vandal Kingdom in Africa. However, King Genseric organizes an attack on the fleet, using individuals sympathetic to the Vandals to conduct the raid. The fleet is destroyed and the expedition is abandoned.

summary: Emperor Leo I founded the Excubitors imperial guard at Constantinople, recruiting soldiers from the Isaurians.
text: Emperor Leo I founds the Excubitors (imperial guard) at Constantinople; this elite tagmatic unit (300 men) is recruited from among the warlike Isaurians .

summary: Suebi invaders captured the city of Lugo and killed the Roman governor.
text: March 27 (night) – Swabians invade the Gallic city of Lugo. The governor is killed.

summary: A multi-year famine began in the Sasanian Empire.
text: A famine that will last for several years begins in the Persian Empire .

summary: The remodeling of the dome of the Baptistery of Neon at Ravenna was finished.
text: The remodeling of the dome of Baptistry of Neon at Ravenna (Italy) is finished.

summary: The Coptic Orthodox Church in Egypt split from the Chalcedonian Orthodox Church of Alexandria.
text: The Coptic Orthodox Church (Egypt) splits from the Chalcedonian Orthodox Church of Alexandria.

summary: Gennadius I, patriarch of Constantinople, banished Patriarch Timothy II of Alexandria.
text: Gennadius I, patriarch of Constantinople, banishes Timothy II, patriarch of Alexandria.

summary: Budic II, future king of Brittany, was born.
text: Budic II, king of Brittany

summary: Hilderic, future king of the Vandals and Alans, was born.
text: Hilderic, king of the Vandals and Alans

summary: Romulus Augustulus, the future last Western Roman emperor, was born.
text: Romulus Augustulus, last emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Aelia Eudocia, Roman empress and wife of Theodosius II, died in Jerusalem.
text: Aelia Eudocia, Roman empress and wife of Theodosius II
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Ardaric, king of the Gepids, died.
text: Ardaric, king of the Gepids

summary: Maldras, king of the Suebi, died.
text: Maldras, king of the Sueves

summary: Isaac of Antioch, a Syriac theologian, died.
text: Isaac of Antioch, Syriac theologian

summary: Ricimer arrested and deposed Emperor Majorian near Tortona.
text: Majorian is arrested near Tortona (Northern Italy), and deposed by Ricimer (magister militum) as puppet emperor.

summary: Majorian was beheaded near the Iria River after enduring five days of torture.
text: Majorian, having been beaten and tortured for five days, is beheaded near the Iria River (Lombardy).

summary: Olybrius emerged as a candidate for the Western Roman throne.
text: Olybrius becomes the second candidate for the western throne. He is the husband of Placidia, who is being held in Vandal captivity.

summary: Libius Severus was proclaimed emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Libius Severus, Roman senator from Lucania, is declared emperor of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Gaiseric raided the coasts of Sicily and Italy, prompting Ricimer to send an embassy to Carthage.
text: Vandal War (461-468): King Genseric continues the Vandal raids on the coast of Sicily and Italy. Ricimer sends an embassy to Carthage.

summary: Theodoric II and the Visigoths recaptured Septimania and launched a renewed invasion of Hispania.
text: Roman civil war of 461: The Visigoths under king Theodoric II recapture Septimania (Southern Gaul) after the assassination of Majorian, and invade Hispania again.

summary: Aegidius established rule over the Domain of Soissons in northern Gaul.
text: Roman civil war of 461: Aegidius becomes ruler over the Domain of Soissons (Gaul). He has friendly relations with the Romano-British (in Brittany).

summary: An earthquake struck the province of Apahunik' north of Lake Van in Anatolia.
text: 461 Apahunik' earthquake. It affected the province of Apahunik', located to the north of Lake Van, in Anatolia.

summary: Pope Leo I died at Rome and was succeeded as pope by Hilarius.
text: Pope Leo I dies at Rome, age 61 (approximate), after a 21-year reign in which he has resisted Manichaeism and defended the Church against Nestorianism. He is succeeded by Hilarius as the 46th pope.

summary: Mamertus was elected bishop of Vienne in Gaul.
text: Mamertus is elected bishop of Vienne (Gaul).

summary: Hilderic, future king of the Vandals, was born.
text: Hilderic, king of the Vandals

summary: Romulus Augustulus, later emperor of the Western Roman Empire, was born.
text: Romulus Augustulus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Majorian, emperor of the Western Roman Empire, died after being executed near Tortona.
text: Majorian, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Pope Leo I died.
text: Pope Leo I

summary: The Byzantine Empire possibly began its first indiction cycle.
text: Possible start of the first Byzantine indiction cycle.

summary: Emperor Leo I paid a substantial ransom to secure the release of Licinia Eudoxia and Placidia from Vandal captivity.
text: Vandal War (461-468): After negotiations, Emperor Leo I pays a large ransom for Licinia Eudoxia and Placidia. They return after seven years of captivity in Carthage.

summary: The Monastery of Stoudios was founded in Constantinople.
text: The Monastery of Stoudios is founded in Constantinople.

summary: Anicia Juliana, daughter of Olybrius, was born.
text: Anicia Juliana, daughter of Olybrius

summary: Childeric I and Aegidius defeated the Visigoths under Theodoric II near Orléans.
text: In the Gothic war against Aegidius, Childeric I, king of the Salian Franks, allies with the Roman general Aegidius. This war is ended by the battle near Orléans, where the Visigoths under King Theodoric II are defeated by the Franks, while crossing the Loire River.

summary: The Suebi fought a civil war over the kingship under a diarchy in Galicia.
text: The Suebi live under a diarchy, and fight a civil war over the kingship in Galicia (Northern Spain).

summary: Frumar, Suevic king of Galicia, died.
text: Frumar, Suevic king of Galicia

summary: Richimund, Suevic king of Galicia, died.
text: Richimund, Suevic king of Galicia

summary: Romanus of Condat, a hermit and saint, died.
text: Romanus of Condat, hermit and saint

summary: The Eastern Roman court in Constantinople elected Olybrius as Roman consul.
text: Olybrius is elected Roman consul by the Eastern court in Constantinople.

summary: Remismund unified the Suevi in Galicia under his rule.
text: The Suevic nation in Galicia (Northern Spain) is unified under King Remismund.

summary: Theodoric II sent weapons and a Gothic bride to Remismund in recognition of his kingship.
text: King Theodoric II sends Remismund gifts (for recognizing his kingship), including weapons, and a Gothic princess for a wife.

summary: Syagrius succeeded his father Aegidius as ruler of the Domain of Soissons.
text: Aegidius dies (possibly poisoned) and is succeeded by his son Syagrius, who becomes ruler of the Domain of Soissons (Gaul).

summary: Roman general Aegidius died.
text: Aegidius, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Basiliscus became consul in the Eastern Roman Empire through the influence of his sister Verina.
text: Basiliscus, with the help of his sister Verina (wife of emperor Leo I), becomes a consul in the Eastern Roman Empire.

summary: Western Roman emperor Libius Severus died after a four-year reign.
text: Libius Severus, puppet emperor of the Western Roman Empire, dies after a 4-year reign.

summary: A massive fire in Constantinople destroyed eight of the imperial capital's fourteen districts over six days.
text: A fire begins in Constantinople and, over the next six days, destroys the buildings in eight of the 14 sections into which the Eastern Roman Imperial capital had been divided.

summary: Ricimer established direct political control over the Western Roman Empire from his residence in Rome.
text: Ricimer, de facto ruler, establishes political control for 2 years from his residence in Rome.

summary: King Remismund aligned the Suebi with the Visigoths and promoted Suebic conversion to Arianism in Galicia.
text: King Remismund establishes a policy of friendship with the Visigoths, and promotes the conversion of the Suebi into Arianism in Galicia (Northern Spain).

summary: Pope Hilarius convoked a church synod at the Church of Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome.
text: Pope Hilarius convokes a synod at Rome's Church of Santa Maria Maggiore.

summary: Peter the Fuller became patriarch of Antioch.
text: Peter the Fuller becomes patriarch of Antioch .

summary: Roman aristocrat Liberius was born.
text: Liberius, Roman aristocrat

summary: Procopius of Gaza, Christian rhetorician and sophist, was born.
text: Procopius of Gaza, Christian sophist and rhetorician

summary: Severus of Antioch, future patriarch of Antioch, was born.
text: Severus, patriarch of Antioch

summary: Zacharias Rhetor, bishop and ecclesiastical historian, was born.
text: Zacharias Rhetor, bishop and ecclesiastic historian

summary: Gerontius, archbishop of Milan, died.
text: Gerontius, Archbishop of Milan

summary: Libius Severus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire, died.
text: Libius Severus, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Emperor Leo I repelled a Hun invasion in Dacia, and Constantinople's reinforced walls protected the city from assault.
text: Emperor Leo I repels the Hun invasion of Dacia (modern Romania). They ravage the Balkans but are unable to take Constantinople thanks to the city walls, which are rebuilt and reinforced.

summary: Tarasicodissa exposed a conspiracy by magister militum Ardabur against Leo I, resulting in Ardabur's arrest for treason.
text: Tarasicodissa, an Isaurian officer, comes with evidence that Ardabur (magister militum) is forming a conspiracy against Leo I. Ardabur is arrested for treason.

summary: Tarasicodissa adopted the Greek name Zeno and married Ariadne, the eldest daughter of Emperor Leo I.
text: Tarasicodissa adopts the Greek name of Zeno and marries Ariadne, eldest daughter of Leo I .

summary: Euric killed his brother Theodoric II, claimed the Visigothic throne, and conquered Hispania and Marseille.
text: King Theodoric II is killed by his younger brother Euric, who succeeds him on the throne. He conquers Hispania and the harbor city of Marseille (Southern Gaul), adding them to the existing Visigothic Kingdom.

summary: Euric sent an embassy to Constantinople seeking recognition of Visigothic sovereignty and allied with the Suebi and Vandals.
text: Euric sends an embassy to the Eastern Roman Empire for recognition of the Visigoth sovereignty. He forms an alliance with the Suebi and the Vandals.

summary: A council of twelve townships formed in the Venetian lagoon to establish a system of local governance.
text: A council of twelve townships emerges on the islands in the Venetian lagoon, to form a basic system of governance .

summary: Julian was elected patriarch of Antioch following the deposition of Peter the Fuller.
text: Peter the Fuller is deposed as patriarch of Antioch; Julian is elected as his successor.

summary: Clovis I, founder of the Frankish Kingdom, was born.
text: Clovis I, first king of the Franks

summary: Theodoret, theologian and bishop of Cyrrhus, died.
text: Theodoret of Cyprus, theologian

summary: Theodoric II, king of the Visigoths, died.
text: Theodoric II, king of the Visigoths

summary: Emperor Leo I had Anthemius made Western Roman Emperor and allied with Ricimer by marrying Anthemius's daughter Alypia to him.
text: Emperor Leo I has his general Anthemius elected emperor of the Western Roman Empire. He allies himself with Ricimer, de facto ruler of Rome, and marries Anthemius's daughter Alypia to him, to strengthen the relationship and end the hostilities between the Eastern and Western Empire.

summary: King Genseric expanded Vandal raids across the Mediterranean, sacking settlements in Illyricum and Greece.
text: Summer – Vandal War (461-468): King Genseric extends his pirate raids in the Mediterranean Sea; the Vandals sack and enslave the people living in Illyricum, the Peloponnese and other parts of Greece. Leo I joins forces with the Western Empire.

summary: Future Byzantine Emperor Leo II was born.
text: Leo II, Byzantine emperor (d. 474)

summary: Emperor Leo I assembled a massive naval expedition at Constantinople to fight against the Vandals.
text: Emperor Leo I assembles a massive naval expedition at Constantinople, which costs 64,000 pounds of gold (more than a year's revenue) and consists of over 1,100 ships carrying 100,000 men. It is the greatest fleet ever sent against the Vandals and brings Leo near to bankruptcy.

summary: Marcellinus expelled the Vandals from Sicily and retook Sardinia for the Roman Empire, while Heraclius of Edessa invaded Tripolitania.
text: Emperor Anthemius sends a Roman expedition under command of Marcellinus. He expels the Vandals from Sicily and retakes Sardinia. The Eastern general Heraclius of Edessa lands with a force on the Libyan coast, east of Carthage, and advances from Tripolitania.

summary: Genseric destroyed the Roman invasion fleet under Basiliscus using fire ships at the Battle of Cape Bon.
text: Battle of Cape Bon: The Vandals defeat the Roman navy under Basiliscus, anchored at Promontorium Mercurii, 45 miles from Carthage (Tunisia). During peace negotiations Genseric uses fire ships, filling them with brushwood and pots of oil, destroying 700 imperial galleys. Basiliscus escapes with his surviving fleet to Sicily, harassed all the way by Moorish pirates.

summary: Marcellinus was murdered in Sicily, likely on the orders of his rival Ricimer.
text: August – Marcellinus is murdered in Sicily, probably at the instigation of his political rival, Ricimer. Heraclius is left to fight alone against the Vandals; after a 2-year campaign in the desert he returns to Constantinople.

summary: Emperor Leo I pardoned Basiliscus for the defeat against the Vandals but banished him to Heraclea Sintica.
text: Basiliscus returns to Constantinople after a disastrous expedition against the Vandals. He is forced to seek sanctuary in the church of Hagia Sophia to escape the wrath of the people. Leo I gives him imperial pardon, but banishes him for 3 years to Heraclea Sintica (Thrace).

summary: Dengizich refused Emperor Leo I's terms and crossed the Danube to invade Roman territory.
text: Dengizich, son of Attila the Hun, sends an embassy to Constantinople to demand money. Leo I offers the Huns settlement in Thrace in exchange for recognition of his authority. Dengizich refuses and crosses the Danube.

summary: King Euric led a Gothic revolt in Aquitania and occupied southern Gaul.
text: Revolt of Euric: The Goths in Aquitania revolts. Their king Euric occupies the south of Gaul.

summary: Roman forces under Anagast defeated the Huns at the river Utus, killing Dengizich.
text: Roman forces under Anagast defeat the Huns at the river Utus (Vit, Bulgaria). Dengizich is killed and his head is paraded through the streets of Constantinople. Stuck on the end of a wooden pole, it is displayed above the Xylokerkos Gate.

summary: The Vandals decisively defeated Western Roman forces and reconquered Sicily.
text: The Vandals reconquer Sicily, administering a decisive defeat to the Western forces.

summary: Pope Hilarius died at Rome and was succeeded by Simplicius.
text: Pope Hilarius dies at Rome after a 6½-year reign, and is succeeded by Simplicius as the 47th pope.

summary: Pope Hilarius died.
text: February 29, – Pope Hilarius

summary: Roman general Marcellinus was killed in Sicily.
text: Marcellinus, Roman general (magister militum)

summary: Ostrogothic prince Theodoric returned to Pannonia after living as a hostage in Constantinople.
text: Ostrogoth prince Theodoric, age 15, returns to Pannonia, after living as a child hostage at the court of Emperor Leo I in Constantinople (see 459).

summary: King Euric defeated the Romano-Breton army led by Riothamus at Déols.
text: Revolt of Euric: King Euric defeated the Romano-Breton army of Riothamus at Déols (modern Châteauroux).

summary: Adovacrius defeated the Roman commander Paulus in the Battle of Angers.
text: Revolt of Euric: Adovacrius defeats Paulus in the Battle of Angers

summary: Roman commander Lusidius surrendered Lisbon to the Suevi.
text: Roman lord Lusidius surrenders Lisbon to the Suevi.

summary: The Vandals raided Epirus, were expelled from the Peloponnese, and slaughtered 500 hostages from Zakynthos.
text: The Vandals invade Epirus (modern Greece). They are expelled from the Peloponnese (Greece) and in retaliation, the Vandals take 500 hostages at Zakynthos. On the way back to Carthage they are slaughtered.

summary: The Papacy made a pact with Salian Frankish king Childeric I, offering to call him the new Constantine if he converted to Christianity.
text: The Vatican makes a pact with the Salian Frankish king Childeric I, agreeing to call him "the new Constantine" on condition that he accept conversion to Christianity.

summary: Dengizich, king of the Huns, died in battle against the Romans.
text: Dengizich, king of the Huns

summary: Hydatius, bishop of Aquae Flaviae and chronicler, died.
text: Hydatius, bishop of Aquae Flaviae

summary: Remismund, king of the Suevi in Gallaecia, died.
text: Remismund, king of the Sueves

summary: Roman and Frankish forces under Paulus and Childeric I halted the Visigoths at Bourges and temporarily recaptured Tours.
text: Revolt of Euric: Roman forces under Paulus and Childeric I stop the Aquitanian Goths at Bourges and briefly recaptured Tours in 470. All the loot they had stolen fell into the hands of Paul.

summary: Roman general Paulus was killed in battle at Angers.
text: The Roman general Paulus is killed shortly afterwards at Angers.

summary: The church of Santo Stefano Rotondo was consecrated in Rome.
text: The church of Santo Stefano Rotondo at Rome is consecrated .

summary: Odoacer became the leader of Germanic foederati in northern Italy.
text: Odoacer becomes the leader of the Germanic tribes (Herulic – Scirian foederati) in Northern Italy .

summary: Mamertus, bishop of Vienne, introduced the Rogation days processions.
text: Mamertus, bishop of Vienne, introduces the Rogation days (a three days' procession involving prayer to invoke God's mercy).

summary: Caesarius, future bishop of Arles, was born at Chalon-sur-Saône.
text: Caesarius, bishop of Arles (or 469; d. 542)

summary: Dionysius Exiguus, who devised the Anno Domini dating system, was born in Scythia Minor.
text: Dionysius Exiguus, inventor of the Anno Domini era

summary: Gallo-Roman senator Ferreolus of Rodez was born.
text: Ferreolus of Rodez, Roman senator

summary: The future Pope John I was born in Tuscany.
text: approximate date – Pope John I

summary: Western Roman usurper Romanus was executed in Rome.
text: Romanus, Roman usurper in the West Roman Empire (executed)

summary: Basiliscus returned from exile and helped Emperor Leo I assassinate Aspar in Constantinople.
text: Basiliscus, brother-in-law of Emperor Leo I, returns from exile (see 468) and leads an imperial conspiracy against Aspar (magister militum), helping in his murder at Constantinople.

summary: Visigothic forces under Euric defeated an imperial Roman army near Arles, seized Provence, and besieged Clermont-Ferrand.
text: Revolt of Euric: The Aquitanian Goths under Euric defeat a Roman army that was sent by Emperor Anthemius near Arles and conquer a large part of the Provence (Southern Gaul). The city of Clermont-Ferrand in Auvergne is besieged.

summary: Theodoric Strabo led a Gothic rebellion in Thrace after the assassination of Aspar.
text: The Goths, led by Theodoric Strabo, revolt in Thrace after the assassination of Aspar. Leo I sends Basiliscus to suppress the uprising.

summary: Theodoric the Great succeeded his father Theodemir as king of the Ostrogoths and settled his people in lower Moesia.
text: Theodoric the Great, age 17, succeeds his father Theodemir as king of the Ostrogoths, settling his people in lower Moesia (Balkans).

summary: Acacius became patriarch of Constantinople following the death of Gennadius I.
text: Acacius becomes patriarch of Constantinople, succeeding Gennadius I.

summary: Gennadius I, patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Gennadius I, patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Roman general Ardabur was assassinated alongside his father Aspar in Constantinople.
text: Ardabur, Roman general and son of Aspar

summary: The powerful magister militum Aspar was assassinated in the imperial palace in Constantinople.
text: Aspar, Alan patrician and general (magister militum)

summary: Eudocia, Vandal queen and daughter of Valentinian III, died in Jerusalem.
text: Eudocia, Vandal queen and daughter of Valentinian III

summary: Julius Patricius, Roman Caesar and son of Aspar, was attacked and killed or mortally wounded in Constantinople.
text: Julius Patricius, Roman general and son of Aspar

summary: Epiphanius, bishop of Pavia, negotiated a temporary reconciliation between Emperor Anthemius and Ricimer.
text: The Western Roman Empire enters a period of unrest. Relations between Ricimer, de facto ruler, and Emperor Anthemius deteriorate completely. Epiphanius, bishop of Pavia, negotiates a peace agreement.

summary: Ricimer captured Rome, executed Emperor Anthemius, proclaimed Olybrius emperor, and installed Gundobad in command of the Western Roman army.
text: Anthemius, besieged in the part of Rome he controls until his troops are defeated, is caught while fleeing the city disguised as a supplicant in the Old St. Peter's Basilica (or at the church of Santa Maria in Trastevere), and later beheaded by Gundobad or Ricimer. Ricimer proclaims Olybrius emperor. Ricimer's nephew, the Burgundian general Gundobad, assumes command of the Western army and holds de facto power in the Empire.

summary: Ricimer died of malignant fever at his palace in Rome.
text: Ricimer dies at his palace of malignant fever, vomiting blood.

summary: Western Roman Emperor Olybrius died of dropsy in Rome after reigning for four months.
text: Olybrius dies of dropsy. During his four months' rule he has been mainly interested in religion.

summary: Mount Vesuvius erupted and blanketed southern Europe with volcanic ash.
text: Mount Vesuvius erupts. During the volcanic eruption the whole of southern Europe is blanketed by ash.

summary: Iberian hermit and saint Emilian of Cogolla was born.
text: Emilian of Cogolla, Iberic abbot and saint

summary: Western Roman Emperor Anthemius was captured and beheaded in Rome.
text: Anthemius, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Ricimer, de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire, died in Rome.
text: Ricimer, de facto ruler of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Western Roman Emperor Olybrius died in Rome.
text: Olybrius, emperor of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Gundobad nominated Glycerius as emperor of the Western Roman Empire, though Eastern Roman Emperor Leo I rejected him in favor of Julius Nepos.
text: Gundobad (nephew of Ricimer) nominates Glycerius as emperor of the Western Roman Empire. Emperor Leo I refuses to recognize him, and chooses Julius Nepos as candidate to the Western throne.

summary: Emperor Leo I appointed his young grandson Leo II to the rank of Caesar.
text: Leo I grants his grandson Leo II, age 6, the title of Caesar .

summary: Theodoric Strabo signed a peace treaty with Emperor Leo I, receiving an annual tribute, territory in Thrace, and the rank of magister militum.
text: Theodoric Strabo signs a peace treaty with Leo I, and according to the terms the Goths are paid with an annual tribute of 2,000 pounds of gold. Leo gives him an independent state in Thrace and he obtains the rank of magister militum.

summary: The Ostrogoths departed Pannonia and migrated to Macedonia and Moesia, where they ravaged the Balkans.
text: The Ostrogoths leave Pannonia, and migrate to Macedonia and Moesia, from whence they ravage the Balkans.

summary: King Euric ordered an invasion of Italy but was defeated by Glycerius, after which the Visigoths withdrew to Gaul and seized Arles and Marseille.
text: King Euric orders the invasion of Italy, but is defeated by Glycerius. The Visigoths withdraw to Gaul, and conquer the cities of Arles and Marseille.

summary: Gundobad returned to Burgundy after the death of his father Gondioc and became king of the Burgundians.
text: Gundobad returns to Burgundy, where his father Gondioc has died, and becomes king of the Burgundians.

summary: Future Sasanian king Kavad I was born.
text: Kavad I, king (shah) of the Sasanian Empire from 488 to 531, with an interruption of two years

summary: Christian abbot and bishop Euthymius the Great died.
text: Euthymius the Great, abbot and bishop (b. 377)

summary: King Gondioc of Burgundy died.
text: Gondioc, king of Burgundy

summary: Emperor Leo I died of dysentery at Constantinople and was succeeded by his grandson Leo II.
text: Emperor Leo I dies of dysentery at Constantinople, after a 17-year reign. He is succeeded by his 7-year-old grandson Leo II, who briefly becomes ruler of the Byzantine Empire.

summary: Zeno was crowned co-emperor alongside his son Leo II.
text: Zeno, father of Leo II, is crowned as co-emperor (Augustus). He rules the empire together with his son, and stabilises the Eastern frontier.

summary: Julius Nepos landed at Portus, marched on Ravenna, forced Glycerius to abdicate, and proclaimed himself emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
text: Julius Nepos arrives at Portus, and marches on Ravenna. He forces Glycerius to abdicate the throne, and proclaims himself emperor of the Western Roman Empire.

summary: Glycerius was exiled to Dalmatia to become bishop of Salona as Julius Nepos assumed the Western Roman imperial throne uncontested.
text: Glycerius is exiled to Dalmatia (Balkans) and becomes bishop of Salona. Neither the Senate nor the Gallo-Roman aristocracy decide to resist, and Nepos accepts the imperial purple.

summary: Leo II died after a ten-month reign, leaving his father Zeno as the sole Eastern Roman emperor.
text: Leo II dies of an unknown disease (possibly poisoned by his mother Ariadne), after a reign of 10 months. Zeno becomes sole Eastern Emperor.

summary: Emperor Zeno concluded a peace treaty with King Genseric of the Vandals to secure Mediterranean trade routes.
text: Winter – Zeno sends an embassy, to conclude a peace with King Genseric. He succeeds in an agreement with the Vandals, to secure the commercial routes in the Mediterranean.

summary: Christian monk and saint Abraham of Cratia was born.
text: Abraham of Kratia, Christian monk, saint

summary: Greek architect and mathematician Anthemius of Tralles was born.
text: Anthemius of Tralles, Greek architect, mathematician

summary: Clotilde, future queen of Clovis I, was born into the Burgundian royal family.
text: Clotilde, Christian wife of Clovis I, ancestress of the succeeding Merovingian kings (d.545)

summary: Bishop and Latin poet Magnus Felix Ennodius was born.
text: Magnus Felix Ennodius, bishop, Latin poet

summary: Byzantine Emperor Leo I died at the age of seventy-three.
text: Leo I, Byzantine emperor (b. 401)

summary: Byzantine Emperor Leo II died after a brief reign.
text: Leo II, Byzantine emperor (b. 467)

summary: Emperor Leo I appointed Julius Nepos ruler of the Western Roman Empire in opposition to Glycerius.
text: Leo the Thracian appointed Julius Nepos, his nephew and governor of Dalmatia, ruler of the Western Roman Empire in opposition to Glycerius.

summary: King Euric forced the Roman commander Vincentius to capitulate and completed the Visigothic conquest of Spain.
text: Spring - Spanish War of Euric: The comes Hispaniarum Vincentius capitulates against the Aquitanian Goths; Euric completes his conquest of Spain.

summary: Basiliscus staged a coup in Constantinople, forcing Emperor Zeno to flee to Isauria, and seized the Eastern Roman imperial throne.
text: Emperor Zeno abdicates under pressure, as his wife's uncle Basiliscus stages a coup d'état at Constantinople, with support from Zeno's trusted adviser and fellow Isaurian Illus. Basiliscus usurps the throne and is proclaimed new emperor (Augustus) of the Eastern Roman Empire. He begins a 20-month reign; Zeno and his supporters flee to Isauria.

summary: Emperor Basiliscus issued a circular letter to the empire's bishops promoting Miaphysitism.
text: Basiliscus issues a circular letter (Enkyklikon) to the bishops of his empire, promoting the Miaphysite christological position. These religious views will make him highly unpopular.

summary: Emperor Julius Nepos granted King Euric legal tenure over Visigothic conquests including Provence in exchange for independence.
text: Summer – Emperor Julius Nepos grants the Visigoth King Euric legal tenure of his conquests, which include Provence (region of Gaul), in exchange for full independence.

summary: Magister militum Orestes took control of the imperial government in Ravenna, forcing Julius Nepos to flee to Dalmatia.
text: Magister Militum Orestes takes control of the government in Ravenna, and forces Julius Nepos to flee to Dalmatia.

summary: Orestes installed his son Romulus Augustus as emperor of the Western Roman Empire, ruling as regent.
text: Romulus Augustus is installed as emperor by his father Orestes, who becomes regent in effect of the Western Roman Empire. Augustus will ultimately rule for 10 months, as the last Western Emperor.

summary: A great fire devastated Constantinople, destroying the Palace of Lausus and the Statue of Zeus from Olympia.
text: Great fire in Constantinople with loss of Palace of Lausus and - along with it - the famous Zeus from Olympia.

summary: The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites was consecrated in Syria.
text: The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites is consecrated in Syria.

summary: Roman senator Ferreolus of Rodez was born.
text: Ferreolus of Rodez, Roman senator

summary: Bishop Eutropius of Orange died.
text: Eutropius, bishop of Orange

summary: Former Roman consul Flavius Magnus died.
text: Flavius Magnus, Roman consul

summary: Mamertus, bishop of Vienne, died.
text: Mamertus, bishop of Vienne

summary: Theodemir, king of the Ostrogoths, died.
text: Theodemir, king of the Ostrogoths

summary: Tonantius Ferreolus, former praetorian prefect of Gaul, died.
text: Tonantius Ferreolus, praetorian prefect

summary: Vincentius, comes Hispaniarum, died.
text: Vincentius, comes Hispaniarum

summary: Julius Nepos appointed Orestes as Magister militum and commander-in-chief of the Western Roman military.
text: Nepos appointed Orestes (father of Romulus Augustulus) Magister militum and commander-in-chief of the Western Roman military.

summary: Odoacer led his Germanic mercenaries in revolt after Orestes refused to grant them lands in Italy.
text: Summer – Odoacer, chieftain of the Germanic tribes (Herulic/Scirian foederati), visits the imperial palace at Ravenna. He petitions Orestes (magister militum) to reward his mercenaries for their services and their support of his rebellion a year earlier, by making good on his promise to grant them lands to settle permanently in Italy. Orestes refuses this proposal and Odoacer leads his tribesmen in a revolt.

summary: Zeno besieged Constantinople, deposed the usurper Basiliscus, and was restored as Eastern Roman emperor.
text: August – Basiliscus, Roman usurper, is deposed and Zeno is restored as emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire. With the support of his adviser Illus, he besieges Constantinople, but the Senate opens the gates, allowing him to resume the throne. Basiliscus flees to sanctuary in a church, but surrenders himself and his family after extracting a solemn promise from Zeno not to shed their blood. Basiliscus is sent to a fortress in Cappadocia, where he later dies from starvation.

summary: Odoacer was proclaimed King of Italy by his troops and advanced through the Po Valley toward Ravenna.
text: Odoacer, age 43, is proclaimed rex Italiae ("king of Italy") by his troops. He leads his Ostrogoth army into the Po Valley, and advances to Ravenna while plundering the countryside.

summary: Odoacer captured and executed Orestes near Piacenza.
text: Orestes is arrested by Odoacer near Piacenza, and swiftly executed.

summary: Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna and exiled him to the Castel dell'Ovo near Naples.
text: Romulus Augustulus, Roman usurper of the Western Roman Empire, is deposed by Odoacer at Ravenna. Odoacer spares the boy's life and gives him a pension of 6,000 solidi, but exiles him to the "Castellum Lucullanum" (Castel dell'Ovo), on the island of Megaride in the Gulf of Naples. This event will later be romanticized in Western literature and history as the Fall of Western Rome, and is traditionally used by historians to mark the beginning of the European Middle Ages.
names: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

summary: Julius Nepos remained the de jure last Western Roman Emperor, ruling Dalmatia and other territories without effective authority in Italy.
text: Julius Nepos, de jure ruler, becomes legally the last "Western Roman Emperor". He governs Dalmatia (Balkans), Morocco, and Northwest Gaul until his death in 480, but has no effective power on the Italian Peninsula.

summary: Odoacer crossed the Maritime Alps and conquered Arles and Marseille after defeating the Burgundians.
text: Odoacer crosses the Maritime Alps with a Gothic army and invades Provence (Southern Gaul). He conquers the cities of Arles and Marseille, after a victorious battle against the Burgundians.

summary: Emperor Zeno brokered a peace treaty under which Odoacer surrendered newly conquered territory in Gaul to Euric's Visigoths.
text: The Visigoths under King Euric march into Italy, and suffer defeat against the forces of Odoacer. Emperor Zeno concludes a peace treaty between the Goths and Odoacer surrenders the newly conquered territory in Gaul. Euric pledges himself to undertake no further hostilities.

summary: Zeno granted Odoacer the title of Patricius, declining the Roman Senate's request to take sole rule over the unified empire.
text: The Roman Senate petitions Zeno to recognize Nepos as deposed and take the sole emperorship himself, abolishing the 81-year-long east/west division of the empire and recognizing Odoacer's authority in Italy. Zeno declines the first request, but names Odoacer Patricius, investing his rule with Imperial legitimacy.

summary: Gaiseric ceded most of Sicily to Odoacer in return for tribute, as Zeno recognized the Vandal Kingdom's territories.
text: Winter – Zeno recognizes the full extent of the Vandal Kingdom, including all of western Africa, the Balearic Islands, Corsica, Sardinia and Sicily. King Gaiseric gives Sicily, with the exception of the city of Lilybaeum, to Odoacer in return for tribute.

summary: Peter the Fuller was restored as Patriarch of Antioch.
text: Peter the Fuller is restored as patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Hilary of Galeata, Christian monk and saint, was born.
text: Hilary of Galeata, Christian monk and saint (d. 558)

summary: Basiliscus, deposed Eastern Roman Emperor, died in Cappadocia.
text: Basiliscus, Emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire

summary: Marcus, co-emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire, died in Cappadocia.
text: Marcus, co-Emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire

summary: Orestes, Roman politician and regent, was executed near Piacenza.
text: Orestes, Roman politician and regent

summary: Byzantine general Armatus was murdered by Onoulphus on the orders of Emperor Zeno.
text: Armatus, Byzantine military commander (magister militum), is killed by order of emperor Zeno, being murdered by his own friend Onoulphus after supporting the rebellion of his uncle Basiliscus in 475.

summary: Byzantine magister militum Armatus was killed in Constantinople.
text: Armatus, Byzantine general (magister militum)

summary: Timothy II, Coptic Orthodox patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Timothy II, Coptic Orthodox patriarch of Alexandria
names: List of popes of the Coptic Orthodox Church

summary: Verina attempted to kill the Isaurian general Illus, prompting a revolt led by Marcian and Theodoric Strabo.
text: Verina, mother-in-law of Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno, attempts to kill Isaurian general Illus for turning against her brother Basiliscus. A major revolt is led by her son-in-law Marcian and the Ostrogoth warlord Theodoric Strabo, but Illus again proves his loyalty to Zeno by quashing the revolt in 479.

summary: Narses, later a Byzantine general, was born.
text: Narses, Byzantine general (d. 573)

summary: Theodoric the Great led the Ostrogoths in a campaign against the Byzantine Empire, ravaging Moesia and Thrace.
text: King Theodoric the Great starts a 4-year campaign against the Byzantine Empire. The Ostrogoths ravage the Roman provinces (Moesia and Thrace), and threaten the capital of Constantinople itself.

summary: Emperor Zeno dissolved the division of the Roman imperial office, becoming the sole Roman emperor.
text: Emperor Zeno officially dissolves the east/west co-emperorship, ruling as the first sole emperor of Rome in 85 years. The position of emperor is never again divided.

summary: Theodoric Strabo died after falling from a horse onto a spear near Philippi during an aborted march against Constantinople.
text: Theodoric Strabo defeats the Bulgars in Thrace, and moves with an army (13,000 men) towards Constantinople. After logistical problems, he is forced to return to Greece. In an encampment at Stabulum Diomedis, near Philippi, he falls from an unruly horse onto a spear and dies.

summary: Roman general Sabinianus Magnus died.
text: Sabinianus Magnus, Roman general

summary: Ostrogothic chieftain Theodoric Strabo died near Philippi.
text: Theodoric Strabo, Ostrogothic chieftain

summary: Timothy Salophakiolos, patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Timothy III, patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Emperor Zeno promulgated the Henotikon in an attempt to reconcile theological divisions between the Eastern and Western Churches.
text: Emperor Zeno promulgates an Edict of Union (Henotikon), in an unsuccessful effort to soften the decision made at the Council of Chalcedon (451), and resolve differences between the Eastern and Western Churches. Zeno wishes to placate the Monophysite churches of Egypt, Palestine and Syria for political reasons.

summary: Justinian I, future Byzantine emperor, was born in Tauresium.
text: Justinian I, emperor of the Byzantine Empire (d. 565)

summary: Illus and dowager empress Verina attempted to overthrow Emperor Zeno and crown Leontius.
text: Byzantine general Illus (magister officiorum), and Verina (widow of the late emperor Leo I), attempt to overthrow Emperor Zeno and place another general named Leontius on the throne.

summary: The Byzantine Empire granted foederati status to the Ostrogoths in Macedonia and Thrace.
text: The Ostrogoths are given status as foederati; they control a large part of Macedonia and Thrace (Balkans).

summary: Leontius was crowned emperor at Tarsus and set up his capital at Antioch.
text: Leontius, Roman usurper, is crowned emperor at Tarsus (modern Turkey). Empress dowager Verina sends a letter to the governors of the Diocese of the East and the Diocese of Egypt for support. He is recognized in Antioch and makes it his capital.

summary: Leontius rebelled against Emperor Zeno, who sent forces to Syria that were defeated by Illus.
text: Leontius raises a rebellion against emperor Zeno, who also faces a revolt from the Ostrogoth king Theodoric the Great. He sends an army to Syria, but is defeated by the Byzantine general Illus.

summary: Emperor Zeno concluded a peace treaty with Theodoric the Great, naming him magister militum and consul.
text: Zeno signs a peace treaty with Theodoric the Great. He appoints him to magister militum and becomes a consul. The Eastern Empire is saved by diplomatic negotiations, and the imperial army is strengthened behind the walls of Constantinople.

summary: Pope Felix III excommunicated Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople and Peter III of Alexandria over the Henotikon, beginning the Acacian Schism.
text: Pope Felix III excommunicates Acacius of Constantinople and Peter III of Alexandria, for their role in having Zeno issue his Edict of Union (Henotikon) 2 years ago. He considers the edict to be heretical and the schism between the Church of Rome and the Church of Constantinople widens. The Acacian Schism will not be resolved until 519.

summary: Antonina, future Byzantine patrikia and wife of the general Belisarius, was born.
text: Antonina, Byzantine patrikia and wife of Belisarius

summary: Verina, former Byzantine empress and widow of Emperor Leo I, died while besieged at the fortress of Papurius.
text: Verina, wife of former emperor Leo I

summary: A Western synod at Rome condemned and excommunicated Patriarch Peter the Fuller of Antioch.
text: Peter the Fuller, patriarch of Antioch, is condemned and excommunicated by a synod of Western bishops at Rome.

summary: Proclus, the prominent Greek Neoplatonist philosopher and head of the Platonic Academy, died in Athens.
text: Proclus, Greek Neoplatonist philosopher (b. 412)

summary: Asclepigenia, the Athenian Neoplatonist philosopher and theurgist, died in Athens.
text: Asclepigenia, Athenian philosopher and mystic (b. 430)

summary: Emperor Zeno crushed the rebellion of Leontius and Illus, executing both rebels after capturing the fortress of Papurius.
text: Emperor Zeno regains power from the usurper Leontius and the Isaurian patrician Illus, who are captured and executed, ending a 4-year rebellion (see 484).

summary: Emperor Zeno ordered Theodoric the Great to invade Italy and overthrow Odoacer.
text: Zeno orders Theodoric the Great to overthrow his rival Odoacer, who has established himself as king of Italy (see 476). He marches with an Ostrogoth army to the West.

summary: Hunulf evacuated Roman provincial populations and the relics of Severinus from Noricum to Italy as the Danubian frontier collapsed.
text: Among the peoples who live on the south bank of the Danube in Noricum ripense and who are de facto ruled by the Rugii, whose empire has its centre near Krems on the north bank, are Romii who had been evacuated earlier from Danube settlements above the River Enns. They include members of the Severin convent. Because some of the Rugii want to fight for East Rome against Odoacer, they destroy the Rugian Empire and allow the Romii to be evacuated to Italy by his brother, Hunulf, in order to prevent the re-establishment of the Rugian Empire by a surviving prince. The northern Danubian Limes of the Roman Empire are effectively abandoned. Even the relics of Severinus of Noricum are carried with them.

summary: The Gepids captured the Roman fortress city of Singidunum.
text: The Gepids capture Belgrade.

summary: Palladius succeeded Peter the Fuller as patriarch of Antioch.
text: Peter the Fuller is succeeded by Palladius as patriarch of Antioch.

summary: Fravitta became patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Fravitta becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: Illus, Byzantine general and rebel against Zeno, died.
text: Illus, Byzantine general

summary: Leontius, Byzantine usurper, was executed.
text: Leontius, Byzantine usurper

summary: Peter the Fuller, patriarch of Antioch, died.
text: Peter the Fuller, patriarch of Antioch

summary: Emperor Zeno closed the School of Edessa for teaching Nestorian doctrine.
text: Emperor Zeno closes the School of Edessa (modern Turkey) for their teaching of Nestorian doctrine, whereupon the scholars seek refuge at the Syriac Church of the East.

summary: The Ostrogoths under Theodoric defeated the Gepids at the Battle of Sirmium.
text: August Battle of Sirmium in Pannonia: The Ostrogoths under Theodoric the Great, moving to invade Northern Italy at the behest of Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno, defeat the Gepids attempting to stop their advance.

summary: Acacius, patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Acacius, patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Euphemius became patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Euphemius becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

summary: John Philoponus, philosopher and commentator on Aristotle, was born.
text: John Philoponus, Aristotelian commentator and philosopher (d. 570)

summary: Romanos the Melodist, Syrian Christian poet and hymnographer, was born.
text: Romanos the Melodist, Syrian poet

summary: Vigilantia, Byzantine princess and sister of Justinian I, was born.
text: Vigilantia, Byzantine princess

summary: Peter III Mongus, patriarch of Alexandria, died.
text: Peter III Mongus, patriarch of Alexandria

summary: Theodora of Alexandria, a Christian Desert Mother, died.
text: Theodora of Alexandria, Desert Mother

summary: Emperor Zeno died, and palace official Anastasius was elevated to the imperial throne.
text: Emperor Zeno, age 66, dies of dysentery (or of epilepsy) after a 17-year reign. He has no sons to succeed him and Anastasius, palace official (silentiarius) and favoured friend of empress Ariadne, is elevated to the throne.

summary: Anastasius I married Empress Ariadne shortly after his accession.
text: Anastasius I marries Ariadne shortly after his accession. His reign is disturbed by religious distractions and a civil war started by Longinus, brother of late emperor Zeno.

summary: Anti-Isaurian riots erupted in the Hippodrome at Constantinople, prompting the exile of Longinus and other Isaurians to Egypt.
text: Anti-Isaurian riots break out in the Hippodrome at Constantinople. Longinus and several other Isaurians, including general Longinus of Cardala, are exiled to Thebaid (Egypt).

summary: Byzantine chronicler John Malalas was born around this year.
text: Approximate date – John Malalas, Byzantine chronicler (d. c. 578)

summary: Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno died in Constantinople.
text: Zeno, Byzantine Emperor

summary: Georgian theologian and bishop Peter the Iberian died in Palestine.
text: Peter the Iberian, Georgian theologian and saint

summary: The Isaurians revolted against Eastern Roman Emperor Anastasius I in southern Central Anatolia.
text: Isaurian War: The Isaurians begin a revolt against Emperor Anastasius I in southern Central Anatolia.

summary: The Eastern Roman army defeated Isaurian rebels at the Battle of Cotyaeum.
text: Battle of Cotyaeum: The Isaurian rebels are defeated by the Eastern Roman army, under John the Scythian and John the Hunchback (subordinate commanders include the future Justin I). They retreat to their mountain fortresses, and continue guerrilla warfare against the Roman forces until 497.

summary: Pope Felix III died in Rome and was succeeded by Gelasius I.
text: Pope Felix III dies after a 9-year reign in which he has excommunicated Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople, thus dividing the Western Church and Eastern Church (Acacian schism). He is succeeded by Gelasius I as the 49th pope.

summary: Eastern Roman general John the Hunchback captured Claudiopolis and defeated Isaurian rebel forces.
text: Isaurian War: Claudiopolis, ancient city of Cappadocia, is besieged and captured by the Romans. The Isaurians blockade the mountain passes, but John the Hunchback (John Gibbo) wins an overwhelming victory against the rebels.

summary: Mor Shlemon converted a former Roman fortress into Mor Hananyo Monastery in Tur Abdin.
text: Mor Hananyo Monastery is established by Mor Shlemon, converting a former Roman fortress (ex temple) in the Tur Abdin region on the Turkish/Syrian border.

summary: Christian ascetic Daniel the Stylite died near Constantinople.
text: Daniel the Stylite, Christian saint

summary: An earthquake devastated the port city of Latakia.
text: An earthquake devastates the port town of Latakia (modern Syria).

summary: Pope Gelasius I formulated the doctrine of the two swords on spiritual and temporal power in a letter to Emperor Anastasius I.
text: Gelasius I delineates the relationship between church and state (Doctrine of the two swords, formulated in his letter Famuli vestrae pietatis to the East Roman Emperor Anastasius I.)

summary: Pope Gelasius I gained the support of Italian bishops in asserting the spiritual superiority of the papacy over temporal imperial authority.
text: Pope Gelasius I gains support from Italian bishops, in his assertion that the spiritual power of the papacy is superior to the emperor's temporal authority. Like his predecessors, the pope opposes the Byzantine emperor Anastasius I's efforts to establish Miaphysite doctrine.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I had Patriarch Euphemius of Constantinople deposed, excommunicated, and exiled, appointing Macedonius II as his successor.
text: Emperor Anastasius I has Euphemius, patriarch of Constantinople, deposed and excommunicated. He appoints Macedonius II as his successor. Euphemius is sent into exile.

summary: Patriarch Athanasius II of Alexandria died.
text: Athanasius, Coptic Orthodox patriarch of Alexandria
names: List of popes of the Coptic Orthodox Church

summary: Emperor Anastasius I formally recognized Ostrogothic king Theodoric the Great as his viceroy in Italy, sending the imperial standard to Ravenna.
text: Emperor Anastasius I gives formal recognition to the Ostrogoth king Theodoric the Great, as his representative (viceroy) in Italy. He sends the imperial standard to Ravenna. Theodoric respects the agreement and allows Roman citizens within the Ostrogothic Kingdom to be subject to Roman law.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I regained control of Isauria and executed the rebel leaders, ending the six-year Isaurian War.
text: Isaurian War: Anastasius I regains control of the Isauria region (Asia Minor) and has the rebel leaders executed. Anastasius I pacifies the mountain strongholds of the Isaurians, ending the revolt that they began upon his ascension to the throne 6 years ago.

summary: The illuminated manuscript known as the Ambrosian Iliad was produced in Constantinople.
text: The Ambrosian Iliad, an Illuminated manuscript on vellum, of the Iliad of Homer, is produced in Constantinople .

summary: Isaurian rebel leader Longinus of Cardala was executed following the suppression of his revolt.
text: Longinus of Cardala, Isaurian official, rebel leader

summary: Emperor Anastasius I abolished the chrysargyron tax throughout the Eastern Roman Empire and reformed the monetary system.
text: Emperor Anastasius I abolishes the chrysargyron tax throughout the Eastern Roman Empire, before reforming the monetary system, using Greek numerals instead of Roman.

summary: Pope Anastasius II died after a two-year pontificate during which he sought reconciliation over the Acacian schism.
text: Pope Anastasius II dies after a 2-year reign in which he has tried to conciliate followers of Acacius, late patriarch of Constantinople, who was excommunicated by Felix III.

summary: Flavian II succeeded Palladius as patriarch of Antioch.
text: Flavian II succeeds Palladius as patriarch of Antioch.

summary: The 499 Nicopolis earthquake struck the border region of Mesopotamia, Pontus, and Roman Armenia, devastating Nicopolis, Neocaesarea, and Arsamosata.
text: September – The 499 Nicopolis earthquake takes place in the borders between the regions of Mesopotamia, Pontus, and Roman Armenia. It affects the cities of Nicopolis, Neocaesarea (modern Niksar), Arsamosata, and Abarne, as well as the cultural areas of Anatolia (Asia Minor) and Mesopotamia.

summary: Maximianus, future bishop of Ravenna, was born in Pola.
text: Maximianus, bishop of Ravenna (d. 556)

summary: Emperor Anastasius I concluded treaties with nomadic Arab tribes, permitting them to settle frontier agricultural lands in exchange for tribute and military defense.
text: Emperor Anastasius I concludes treaties with a number of nomad tribes in northern Arabia. In return for tribute to the Byzantine Empire and military defense of these eastern territories, such tribes are permitted to settle and farm agricultural lands in Arabia .

summary: Belisarius, the Byzantine general, was born.
text: Belisarius, Byzantine general

summary: Procopius, the Byzantine historian, was born.
text: Procopius, Byzantine historian

summary: Paul the Black, future Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch, was born.
text: Paul the Black, Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch

summary: Theodora, future Byzantine empress, was born.
text: Theodora, Byzantine Empress
names: List of Roman and Byzantine empresses

summary: Tribonian, the Byzantine jurist, was born.
text: Tribonian, Byzantine jurist

summary: King Kavadh I invaded Armenia and captured Theodosiopolis after Emperor Anastasius I refused to fund the defense of the Caucasian Gates.
text: War with Sassanid Persia: Emperor Anastasius I refuses to pay a share of the cost of defending the Caucasian Gates, through which nomadic tribes have come for raids on Persia and the Byzantine Empire. King Kavadh I invades Armenia and captures Theodosiopolis.

summary: Sasanian king Kavadh I besieged and eventually captured the fortress-city of Amida after three months of resistance.
text: Winter – Kavadh I besieges the fortress-city of Amida (modern Turkey). The defenders, although unsupported by Byzantine troops, repel the Persian assaults for three months before they are finally beaten.

summary: The Bulgars invaded and ravaged Thrace without meeting opposition from Byzantine forces.
text: The Bulgars ravage Thrace. A semi-nomadic people, they have absorbed the surviving Huns and meet no opposition from Byzantine forces.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I sent a Roman army to Armenia that was defeated by Persian forces.
text: War with Sassanid Persia: Emperor Anastasius I sends a Byzantine army (52,000 men) to Armenia, but is defeated. The Romans attempt an unsuccessful siege of the Persian-held city Amida, on the Tigris. King Kavadh I invades Osroene, and lays siege to the city of Edessa (Northern Mesopotamia).

summary: Byzantine general Areobindus was stationed at Dara to monitor the Persian fortress of Nisibis.
text: May – Areobindus, Byzantine general (magister militum), is stationed as commander at Dara, with an army of 12,000 men to keep watch at the Persian stronghold of Nisibis (modern Turkey).

summary: Lakhmid king Mundhir III raided Palaestina Salutaris and Arabia Petraea, capturing numerous Romans.
text: Mundhir III, king of the Lakhmids (Arab Christians), raids Palaestina Salutaris and Arabia Petraea. He captures a large number of Romans.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I renewed the siege of Amida and gained the upper hand in Armenia.
text: War with Sassanid Persia: Emperor Anastasius I gains the upper hand in Armenia, with the renewed investment of Amida.

summary: King Kavadh I agreed to an armistice with the Byzantine Empire and handed over Amida.
text: King Kavadh I hands over the fortress-city of Amida, and agrees to an armistice with the Byzantine Empire.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I agreed to contribute to the defense costs of the Caucasian Gates against nomadic invasions.
text: Emperor Anastasius I agrees to pay his share of the cost of defending the Caucasian Gates, against nomadic invasions from East Asia.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I rebuilt Dara into a major frontier fortress.
text: Anastasius I decides to rebuild the village of Dara (Northern Mesopotamia). He constructs a new strategic fortress to guard the frontier.

summary: Byzantine general Belisarius was born.
text: Belisarius, Byzantine general (d. 565)

summary: Christian monk and abbot Dorotheus of Gaza was born.
text: Dorotheus of Gaza, Christian monk and abbot

summary: Pope John I of Alexandria died.
text: John I, Coptic Orthodox patriarch of Alexandria
names: List of popes of the Coptic Orthodox Church

summary: Emperor Anastasius I concluded a peace agreement with the Sasanian Empire and upgraded fortifications across northern Mesopotamia.
text: November – Emperor Anastasius I accepts a peace agreement with the Sasanian Empire (Persia), based on the status quo. He upgrades the fortifications at Batnae, Edessa and Amida (Northern Mesopotamia).

summary: Emperor Anastasius I completed the fortress at Dara and constructed the Anastasian Wall near Constantinople.
text: Emperor Anastasius I completes the strategic fortress at Dara (Northern Mesopotamia). He raises the city walls to 30 feet (10 m), disregarding Persian protests. Alarmed by the depredations of Slavs and Bulgars in Thrace, he builds the Anastasian Wall from the Black Sea to Propontis, across the narrow peninsula near Constantinople (modern Turkey).

summary: Armenian bishop and historian John of Ephesus was born.
text: John of Ephesus, Armenian bishop

summary: Emperor Anastasius I recognized Clovis I as ruler of Gaul and dispatched a Byzantine fleet to raid the coasts of Italy.
text: Emperor Anastasius I formally recognizes Clovis I of the Salian Franks as ruler of Gaul. He sends a Byzantine fleet of 100 warships to raid the coasts of Italy.

summary: Riots erupted in Antioch between supporters of Patriarch Flavian II and Emperor Anastasius I over Non-Chalcedonianism.
text: Riots erupt in the streets of Antioch, between supporters of Patriarch Flavian II and Emperor Anastasius I, in sympathy with Non-Chalcedonianism.

summary: Macedonius II was deposed as patriarch of Constantinople and replaced by Timothy I.
text: Macedonius II is deposed as patriarch of Constantinople, and replaced by Timothy I.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I abandoned religious compromise and began openly favoring Miaphysite beliefs.
text: Emperor Anastasius I ends a period of moderate eclectic policy, and starts strongly favoring his own monophysitist beliefs.

summary: Areobindus was proclaimed emperor by rioters in Constantinople but refused to usurp the throne.
text: Areobindus, Byzantine general, is proclaimed emperor during a riot at Constantinople but refuses to take part in the usurpation.

summary: Anastasius I constructed a defensive wall from the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara to protect Constantinople.
text: Anastasius I constructs a wall from the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, to protect Constantinople from raiding Bulgars and Slavs.

summary: Eutychius, future patriarch of Constantinople, was born.
text: Eutychius, patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Byzantine general and politician Areobindus died.
text: Areobindus, Byzantine general and politician

summary: Vitalian revolted against Emperor Anastasius I and conquered much of the Diocese of Thrace.
text: Revolt of Vitalian: Byzantine general Vitalian revolts against Emperor Anastasius I, and conquers a large part of the Diocese of Thrace. He gains the support of the local people, and assembles an army of 50,000–60,000 men.

summary: Vitalian marched to Constantinople and encamped at Hebdomon after Anastasius I reduced taxes in Bithynia and Asia.
text: Anastasius I reduces taxes in the provinces of Bithynia and Asia, to prevent them from joining the rebellion. Vitalian marches to Constantinople and encamps at the suburb of Hebdomon (modern Turkey).

summary: Emperor Anastasius I sent an embassy under Patricius to open negotiations with the rebel Vitalian.
text: Anastasius I sends an embassy under the former consul Patricius to start negotiations. Vitalian declares his aims: restoration of Chalcedonian Orthodoxy and the settling of the Thracian foederati.

summary: Emperor Anastasius I dispatched an imperial army under his nephew Hypatius against Vitalian in Lower Moesia.
