text: The Knights Hospitaller, led by Grand Master Foulques de Villaret, land with 600 men on the island of Rhodes, one of the Dodecanese Islands off of the coast of Byzantium, and begin a four-year long war to capture the fortified city of Rhodes (which will not fall until August 15, 1310).

summary: The Knights Hospitaller captured Feraklos Castle during their siege of Rhodes.
text: The Knights Hospitaller, besieging on the island of Rhodes, capture the Feraklos Castle.

summary: Byzantine prince and general Constantine Palaiologos died.
text: Constantine Palaiologos, Byzantine prince and general (b. 1261)

summary: The Knights Hospitaller completed their four-year conquest of the Byzantine island of Rhodes.
text: The Knights Hospitaller complete the conquest of the Greek island of Rhodes after four years.

summary: The Byzantine garrison of Rhodes surrendered to the Knights Hospitaller under Foulques de Villaret.
text: Conquest of Rhodes: The Byzantine garrison of the city of Rhodes surrenders to the Crusader forces of the Knights Hospitaller under Grand Master Foulques de Villaret – completing their conquest of Rhodes. The knights establish their headquarters on the island and rename themselves as the Knights of Rhodes.

summary: Nephon I became Patriarch of Constantinople following the forced retirement of Athanasius I.
text: Nephon I of Constantinople becomes the new Patriarch of the Eastern Orthodox Church in Byzantium, now at Turkey. He is elected after his predecessor, the 80-year-old Athanasius I, is forced to retire.

summary: Athanasius I, former Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, died.
text: Athanasius I, Byzantine patriarch (b. 1230)

summary: George Pachymeres, Byzantine historian and theologian, died.
text: George Pachymeres, Byzantine historian and theologian

summary: A combined Byzantine and Serbian force supported by Genoese ships annihilated the Turcopoles at Gallipoli.
text: Winter – Battle of Gallipoli: A combined Byzantine-Serbian force (supported by a Genoese fleet) defeats the Turcopoles (some 2,000 men) at Gallipoli.

summary: The Mamluk Sultanate army invaded and looted the Byzantine Christian outpost of Malatya.
text: The Mamluk Sultanate army invades the Christian outpost of Malatya in Byzantium, then loots the city.

summary: Louis of Burgundy, supported by Byzantine troops, defeated and killed Ferdinand of Majorca at the Battle of Manolada.
text: Battle of Manolada: Latin forces under Louis of Burgundy, supported by Byzantine troops sent by governor Michael Kantakouzenos, defeat the Catalan army under Ferdinand of Majorca. During the battle, Ferdinand is killed and John II of Nivelet, who claims the Principality of Achaea is executed on the field as a traitor. His lands are given to Louis' Burgundian followers. Louis of Burgundy and his wife, Matilda of Hainaut, become the joint rulers of Achaea.

summary: Niphon Kausokalybites was born in Lukovitsa in the Byzantine Empire.
text: Niphon of Kafsokalyvia, Greek monk, mystic and writer (d. 1411)

summary: The Battle of Manolada was fought in Elis, resulting in heavy casualties.
text: (Battle of Manolada)

summary: Michael Kantakouzenos, the first Byzantine governor of the Despotate of the Morea, died.
text: Michael Kantakouzenos, Byzantine general and governor

summary: Byzantine empress consort Irene of Montferrat died in Drama.
text: Irene Violante of Montferrat, Byzantine empress consort (b. 1274)

summary: John II Doukas of Thessaly, ruler of Thessaly, died.
text: John II Doukas of Thessaly, Byzantine nobleman and ruler (sebastokrator)

summary: Despot of Epirus Thomas I Komnenos Doukas was assassinated by Nicholas Orsini.
text: Thomas I Komnenos Doukas, Byzantine nobleman (assassinated) (b. 1288)

summary: Byzantine forces commanded by Andronikos Asen defeated the army of the Principality of Achaea at the Battle of Saint George and secured Arcadia.
text: Battle of Saint George: Byzantine forces under Andronikos Asen defeat the army of the Principality of Achaea, securing the possession of Arcadia. During the battle, Latin commander Bartholomew II Ghisi is taken prisoner, along with several high-ranking nobles of the principality, and is sent to Constantinople.

summary: Byzantine co-emperor Michael IX Palaiologos died, leaving his father Andronikos II Palaiologos as sole emperor.
text: Andronikos II Palaiologos, who was co-ruler of Byzantium, becomes the sole ruler upon the death of his son Michael IX Palaiologos. Michael's son Andronikos begins a rebellion against his grandfather emperor six months later.

summary: Byzantine forces under Andronikos Asen captured the castles of Akova and Karytaina, securing control over Arcadia and Cynuria.
text: Autumn – Byzantine forces under Andronikos Asen capture the Latin castles of Akova and Karytaina. They secure control over Arcadia and Cynuria in the Peloponnese.

summary: Byzantine jurist and judge Constantine Harmenopoulos was born.
text: Constantine Harmenopoulos, Byzantine judge (d. 1385)

summary: Michael Panaretos, Byzantine chronicler and historian of Trebizond, was born.
text: Michael Panaretos, Byzantine historian and writer (d. 1390)

summary: Nicodemus of Tismana, Byzantine-born monk and writer, was born in Prilep.
text: Nicodemus of Tismana, Byzantine monk and writer (d. 1406)

summary: Byzantine co-emperor Michael IX Palaiologos died in Thessaloniki.
text: Michael IX Palaiologos, Byzantine emperor (b. 1277)

summary: Anna Palaiologina, Byzantine princess and queen consort of Epirus, died.
text: Anna Palaiologina, Byzantine princess and queen consort

summary: Co-Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos fled Constantinople to Adrianople and revolted against Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos, starting a civil war.
text: At Easter, the Byzantine civil war of 1321–1328 breaks out in the Byzantine Empire as Co-Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos flees Constantinople to Adrianople, where he sets up his court and initiates an uprising against his grandfather, the Byzantine Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos. The 24-year-old Andronikos is joined by Theodore Synadenos and John Kantakouzenos in the rebellion. Syrgiannes Palaiologos leads an expeditionary army towards the capital, forcing the emperor to negotiate.

summary: Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos made peace by granting Thrace and Macedonia to Co-Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos.
text: Andronikos II Palaiologos concludes a peace agreement and divides the Byzantine Empire in two. Andronikos III is recognized as co-emperor and receives Thrace and Macedonia. He rewards his followers and gives them towns and regions to administer. Adrianople becomes the new capital.

summary: Syrgiannes Palaiologos defected to Emperor Andronikos II in Constantinople and persuaded him to renew the war against Andronikos III.
text: Winter – Byzantine civil war of 1321–1328: Syrgiannes Palaiologos switches support to Andronikos II Palaiologos, fleeing to Constantinople. Rewarded with the title of megas doux, he convinces the emperor to resume the war against Andronikos III.

summary: Future Emperor of Trebizond John III of Trebizond was born.
text: John III of Trebizond ("Megas Komnenos"), Emperor of Trebizond (d. 1362)

summary: Emperor Andronikos II and Andronikos III Palaiologos signed an agreement at Epibates to rule Byzantium jointly as co-emperors.
text: An agreement is reached in the Byzantine civil war between Emperor Andronikos II and his rebellious grandson, Andronikos III Palaiologos, signed outside the Byzantine fortress of Epibates (modern Selimpaşa in Turkey). The two men agree that they will jointly rule Byzantium as co-Emperors.

summary: Theoleptos of Philadelphia, a Byzantine mystic and metropolitan bishop of Philadelphia, died.
text: Theoleptos of Philadelphia, Byzantine mystic and bishop

summary: The Byzantine Empire concluded a treaty with the Republic of Venice led by Doge Giovanni Soranzo.
text: The Byzantine Empire, represented by diplomatic envoy Stephen Syropoulos, signs a treaty with the Republic of Venice, led by the Doge Giovanni Soranzo.

summary: Irene of Brunswick, Byzantine empress consort, died at Rhaedestus.
text: Irene of Brunswick, Byzantine empress consort (b. 1293)

summary: Ottoman forces led by Sultan Orhan captured the Byzantine city of Bursa and made it the new Ottoman capital.
text: Siege of Bursa: Ottoman forces (some 10,000 men) led by Sultan Orhan I capture the Byzantine city of Bursa. Orhan makes Bursa the first official Ottoman capital.

summary: Byzantine nobleman Manuel Kantakouzenos was born.
text: Manuel Kantakouzenos, Byzantine nobleman (d. 1380)

summary: Byzantine nobleman and governor John Palaiologos died in Skopje.
text: John Palaiologos, Byzantine nobleman and governor (b. 1288)

summary: Byzantine scholar and statesman Nikephoros Choumnos died in Constantinople.
text: Nikephoros Choumnos, Byzantine scholar and statesman (b. 1250 or 1255)

summary: Byzantine nobleman and governor Andronikos Angelos Palaiologos died.
text: Andronikos Angelos Palaiologos, Byzantine nobleman and governor (b. ca. 1282)

summary: Ottoman forces defeated the Byzantine Empire at the Battle of Pelekanon.
text: Battle of Maltepe (Pelekanon): Ottoman Turks defeat the Byzantine Empire.

summary: Byzantine grammarian and theologian Maximus Planudes died.
text: Maximus Planudes, Byzantine grammarian and theologian

summary: Michael Palaiologos, Byzantine prince and son of Emperor Andronikos III, was born.
text: Michael Palaiologos, Byzantine prince

summary: The Ottoman Empire captured the Byzantine city of Nicaea after a prolonged siege.
text: Byzantine–Ottoman Wars: The Ottoman Empire captured Nicaea.

summary: John V Palaiologos, future Byzantine Emperor, was born in Didymoteicho.
text: John V Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (d. 1391)

summary: Andronikos II Palaiologos, former Byzantine Emperor who had abdicated to become a monk, died in Constantinople.
text: Andronikos II Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (b. 1259)

summary: Theodore Metochites, Byzantine statesman, author, and patron of the arts, died in Constantinople.
text: Theodore Metochites, Byzantine Empire statesman, author, man of learning, and patron of the arts (b. 1270)

summary: Future Byzantine empress Helena Kantakouzene was born.
text: Helena Kantakouzene, empress consort of Byzantium (d. 1396)

summary: The Byzantine Empire conquered the Despotate of Epirus.
text: The Despotate of Epirus is conquered by the Byzantine Empire.

summary: The Ottoman Empire besieged Nicomedia as part of its expansion across Bithynia at the expense of the Byzantine Empire.
text: Siege of Nicomedia: After its foundation by Osman I in about 1299, the Ottoman Empire expanded across Bithynia in north-west Anatolia by capturing territory from the Byzantine Empire.

summary: The Ottoman Empire captured Nicomedia from the Byzantine Empire.
text: Nicomedia is captured by the Ottoman Empire.

summary: Simonida, Byzantine princess and queen consort of Serbia, died in Constantinople.
text: date unknown – Simonida, queen consort of Serbia (b. 1294)

summary: A civil war broke out between John VI Kantakouzenos and the regency for John V Palaiologos in the Byzantine Empire.
text: September–October – The Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 (between John VI Kantakouzenos and the regency for the infant John V Palaiologos) breaks out.

summary: Byzantine Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos died.
text: Andronikos III Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (b. 1297)

summary: The Zealots seized control of Thessalonica, driving out the aristocracy during the Byzantine civil war.
text: Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 – The Zealots seize power in Thessalonica, expelling its aristocrats and declaring themselves in favour of the regency.

summary: Tsar Stefan Dušan conquered Byzantine Albania.
text: Tsar Dušan conquers Albania.

summary: The Turkish allies of John VI Kantakouzenos defeated Momchil at the Battle of Peritheorion.
text: Battle of Peritheorion: the forces of Momchil, autonomous ruler of the Rhodope, are defeated by the Turkish allies of John VI Kantakouzenos.

summary: Alexios Apokaukos, chief minister of the Byzantine Empire, was lynched by political prisoners.
text: Alexios Apokaukos, chief minister of the Byzantine Empire (lynched by political prisoners)

summary: Momchil was killed in battle at Peritheorion.
text: Momchil, semi-independent brigand ruler in the Rhodope Mountains (killed in battle)

summary: Byzantine general John Vatatzes was murdered.
text: John Vatatzes, Byzantine general (murdered)

summary: John Apokaukos, the governor of Thessalonica, was executed during an uprising in Thessalonica.
text: John Apokaukos, governor of Thessalonica (executed)

summary: Stefan Dušan proclaimed the Serbian Empire in Skopje and was crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks.
text: The Serbian Empire is proclaimed in Skopje by Dusan Silni, occupying much of Southeast Europe.

summary: Genoese forces led by Simone Vignoso landed on Chios and captured the island from local Byzantine Greek control.
text: Genoese forces led by Simone Vignoso land on the Mediterranean island of Chios and capture it from local Greek control within a week, apart from the Castle of Chios, which resists until 12 September.

summary: Repairs were undertaken on the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople following earthquake damage.
text: Repairs are made in the Hagia Sophia.

summary: Gregory of Sinai died.
text: Saint Gregory of Sinai (b. c. 1260)

summary: John VI Kantakouzenos entered Constantinople, concluding the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347.
text: The Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 between John VI Kantakouzenos and the regency for John V Palaiologos ends with Kantakouzenos entering Constantinople.

summary: John V Palaiologos married Helena Kantakouzene to finalize the political settlement in the Byzantine Empire.
text: May: The agreement reorganizing the Byzantine Empire's affairs is finalized, as Anna of Savoy's son John V Palaiologos marries Kantakouzenos' 15-year-old daughter Helena.

summary: Genoese ships fleeing the Black Death plague in Feodosia arrived in Constantinople and contaminated the city.
text: May: Genoese ships fleeing the 1331 Black Death plague in Theodosia stop in Constantinople, contaminating the city.

summary: Emperor Stefan Dušan of Serbia conquered Byzantine Thessaly and Epirus.
text: Stefan the Mighty, Emperor of Serbia, conquers Thessaly and Epirus.

summary: Future Byzantine Emperor Andronikos IV Palaiologos was born in Constantinople.
text: Andronikos IV Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (d. 1385)

summary: Future Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos was born in Constantinople.
text: Manuel II Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (d. 1425)

summary: The Genoese fleet defeated allied Venetian, Aragonese, and Byzantine fleets in the Battle of the Bosporus.
text: War of the Straits – The Battle of the Bosporus is fought in a stormy sea into the night between the Genoese, Venetian, Aragonese, and Byzantine fleets. The Genoese emerge victorious, as the other fleets withdraw.

summary: Ottoman forces allied with John VI Kantakouzenos defeated the Serbs at the Battle of Demotika, scoring their first victory on European soil.
text: October – Byzantine civil war of 1352–1357 – Battle of Demotika: Fighting as allies of John VI Kantakouzenos, the Ottoman beylik scores its first victory on European soil, against the Serbs.

summary: Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos granted control of Çimpe Castle to Süleyman Pasha, establishing the first Ottoman territory in Europe.
text: Süleyman Pasha (son of Orhan) is probably granted control of Çimpe Castle on the Gallipoli peninsula by Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos, the first territory west of the Bosporus held by the Ottoman Empire.

summary: A strong earthquake destroyed the city and walls of Gallipoli and neighboring settlements.
text: During the night between 1 and 2 March, a strong earthquake destroyed the city of Gallipoli and its city walls, weakening its defenses, along with destroying the neighboring villages and towns in the area.

summary: The Ottoman Empire besieged and captured Gallipoli following the earthquake, establishing its first stronghold in Europe.
text: March - Within a month after the devastating earthquake the Ottomans besieged and captured the town of Gallipoli, making it the first Ottoman stronghold in Europe and the staging area for Ottoman expansion across the Balkans.

summary: John V Palaiologos retook Constantinople and ended the reign of John VI Kantakouzenos, restoring himself as sole Byzantine emperor.
text: The reign of John VI Kantakouzenos as Byzantine Emperor is ended, after John V Palaiologos retakes Constantinople and is restored as sole emperor.

summary: Byzantine scholar and humanist Manuel Chrysoloras was born.
text: Manuel Chrysoloras, Byzantine humanist (d. 1415)

summary: Greek Neoplatonist philosopher and scholar Gemistus Pletho was born.
text: Gemistus Pletho, Greek scholar

summary: Bayezid I, future Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, was born.
text: Bayezid I, sultan of the Ottoman Empire (d. 1403)

summary: Byzantine historian Nicephorus Gregoras died.
text: Nicephorus Gregoras, Byzantine historian (b. 1295)

summary: Emir Ahi Ayna invaded the Empire of Trebizond and besieged Lazica, Golacha, and Koukos.
text: The Emir Ahi Ayna guides his army into the Empire of Trebizond and besieges the cities of Lazica, Golacha and Koukos.

summary: The Ottoman Emirate conquered the Byzantine city of Didymoteicho.
text: Ottoman Emirate conquered Didymoteicho

summary: Ottoman Sultan Orhan died in Bursa.
text: Orhan Ghazi, Ottoman Sultan (b. 1274)

summary: Murad I succeeded his father Orhan as sultan of the Ottoman Empire.
text: Murad I succeeds his father Orhan as sultan of the Ottoman Empire.

summary: The Ottoman Turks captured Philippopolis and Adrianople from the Byzantine Empire.
text: The Ottomans capture Philippopolis (or in 1364, 1371) and Adrianopole (the modern-day city of Edirne, or in 1369) from the Byzantine Empire, reducing its territory to the city of Constantinople, part of the Peloponessus, and some islands.

summary: Ottoman forces seized Philippopolis from Byzantine control in Thrace.
text: Ottoman Turks seize Filibe (Philippopolis) in Thrace in the Byzantine–Ottoman wars.

summary: Philip of Anjou succeeded his late brother as Prince of Taranto and titular Latin Emperor of Constantinople.
text: Philip of Anjou becomes Titular Emperor of Constantinople and Prince of Taranto.

summary: Byzantine Emperor John V Palaiologos appointed Philotheos Kokkinos as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for the second time.
text: Philotheos Kokkinos is appointed by the Byantine Emperor John V Palaiologos to the position of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for the second time in his life, as leader of the Eastern Orthodox Christians. He had previously been the Patriarch from 1353 to 1354.

summary: Future Emperor Manuel III of Trebizond was born in Trebizond.
text: Emperor Manuel III of Trebizond (d. 1417)

summary: Adrianople became the new capital city of the Ottoman Sultanate.
text: Adrianopole (modern-day Edirne) becomes the capital city of the Ottoman Sultanate.

summary: Pope Urban V appointed Paul of Thebes as the Latin Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Paul of Thebes is appointed by Pope Urban V as the new Latin Patriarch of Constantinople

summary: Pope Urban V suspended aid to the Greek Orthodox Church, prompting Byzantine Emperor John V Palaiologos to refuse assistance to the Savoyard Crusade.
text: Pope Urban V suspends aid to the Greek Orthodox Church for a year, and conditions further aid to the return of the Orthodox clergy to Roman Catholicism. In response, the Emperor of Byzantium, John V Palaiologos declines to assist the Savoyard Crusade.

summary: Crusaders under Francesco I Gattilusio captured Gelibolu from the Turks.
text: Savoyard crusade: The crusaders under Amadeus launch a naval attack and invasion, led by Francesco I Gattilusio, Prince of Lesbos, against the Turkish-held city of Gelibolu (Gallipoli). The Turks abandon the city and Gelibolu falls to the Crusaders on August 26.

summary: The fleet of the Savoyard crusade arrived off the coast of Constantinople.
text: Savoyard crusade: The crusaders' ships arrive off of the coast of Constantinople.

summary: Amadeus of Savoy and his crusaders crossed the Black Sea and captured Nesebar.
text: Savoyard crusade: After leaving a contingent of troops to protect Constantinople and the Chrisitan community, Amadeus and his fleet arrive at the coast of Turkish-held Bulgaria, after crossing the Black Sea. By October 20, the crusaders capture Nesebar.

summary: Maria of Calabria, titular Latin Empress of Constantinople, died.
text: Maria of Calabria, Empress of Constantinople (b. 1329)

summary: Emperor John V Palaiologos met Pope Urban V in Rome and made a personal submission recognizing papal primacy.
text: John V Palaiologos, partiarch of Constantinople and leader of the Eastern Orthodox Christian faith, meets in Rome with the Roman Catholic Pope Urban V and agrees to recognize the Pope as the leader of all Christendom, after negotiation between Rome and Constantinople had been made by Demetrios Chrysoloras.

summary: The Ottoman Empire invaded Bulgaria.
text: The Ottoman Empire invades Bulgaria.

summary: Philip of Anjou, titular Latin Emperor of Constantinople, married Elizabeth of Slavonia.
text: Philip of Anjou, Titular Emperor of Constantinople, marries his second wife Elizabeth of Slavonia (daughter of Stephen of Anjou and Margaret of Bavaria).

summary: Future Byzantine Emperor John VII Palaiologos was born.
text: John VII Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (d. 1408)

summary: Simeon Uroš, ruler of Epirus and Thessaly, died.
text: Simeon Uroš, Emperor of Serbs and Greeks and half-brother of Stefan Dušan (b. 1326)

summary: Ivan Sratsimir and Ivan Shishman became rival co-emperors of Bulgaria following the death of their father Ivan Alexander.
text: Rival brothers Ivan Sratsimir and Ivan Shishman become co-Emperors of Bulgaria after the death of their father, Ivan Alexander. Bulgaria is weakened by the split.

summary: Byzantine Emperor John V Palaiologos became a vassal of the Ottoman Empire to prevent an invasion of Constantinople.
text: Byzantine co-emperor John V Palaiologos pledges loyalty to the Ottoman Empire, to prevent the Turks from invading Constantinople.

summary: Helena Dragaš, future empress consort of the Byzantine Empire, was born.
text: Helena Dragaš, empress consort of Byzantium (d. 1450)

summary: Andronikos IV Palaiologos allied with Ottoman prince Savcı Bey and rebelled against Emperor John V Palaiologos.
text: Byzantine co-emperor Andronikos IV Palaiologos allies with Savcı Bey, the son of the Ottoman Sultan Murad I, rebels against his father, John V Palaiologos, for agreeing to let Constantinople become a vassal of the Ottoman Empire, but the rebellion fails.

summary: Emperor John V Palaiologos had his son Andronikos IV imprisoned and partially blinded following his failed rebellion.
text: Andronikos IV is arrested, imprisoned, and blinded in one eye on orders of his father, the Emperor John V Palaiologos, who was directed by Sultan Murad to carry out the punishment.Savci, who was completely blinded, is executed on orders of Murad, his father. After the rebellion fails, Ottoman Emperor Murad I commands to blind his son.

summary: Emperor John V Palaiologos proclaimed Manuel II Palaiologos co-emperor at Constantinople.
text: At Constantinople, Manuel II Palaiologos is proclaimed as co-Emperor of Byzantium by his father, the Emperor John V Palaiologos.

summary: Ecumenical Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos created the Orthodox metropolis of Lithuania and consecrated Cyprian as its first metropolitan at Constantinople.
text: With the threat of the Russian Orthodox believers of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania being converted to the Roman Catholic Church, the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, Philotheos Kokkinos, creates the Orthodox metropolis of Lithuania with the approval of the other bishops at the Council of Constantinople. Philotheos consecrates Cyprian as the first Orthodox Metropolitan of Lithuania and designates Cyprian will be the successor to Alexius II, Metropolitan of Kiev and all Russia.

summary: The Principality of Achaea defeated the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea at the Battle of Gardiki.
text: Approximate date – Battle of Gardiki: The Principality of Achaea defeats the Despotate of the Morea.

summary: Andronikos IV Palaiologos invaded Constantinople with Genoese assistance and dethroned his father John V Palaiologos.
text: With the help of the Genoese, Byzantine co-emperor Andronicus IV Palaeologus invades Constantinople and dethrones his father, John V Palaeologus, as co-emperor. John V Palaeologus is taken prisoner.

summary: Venetian and Ottoman forces entered Constantinople and restored John V Palaiologos as Byzantine co-emperor, exiling Andronikos IV Palaiologos to Silivri.
text: Forces of the Republic of Venice and Ottoman Turks, having invaded Constantinople, restore John V Palaiologos as Byzantine co-emperor. Andronikos IV Palaiologos is allowed to remain as co-emperor, but is confined to the city of Silivri for the remainder of his life.

summary: The Ottoman Empire captured and occupied the city of Serres in Macedonia.
text: In Macedonia in Greece, the city of Serres is conquered and occupied by forces of the Ottoman Empire and renamed Siroz. Under the terms of surrender, the Greek population keeps control of the churches and most homes inside the walled city, while the Ottoman Turks settle outside the walls, which are eventually torn down.

summary: Former Byzantine Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos died in Mystras.
text: John VI Kantakouzenos, Byzantine Emperor (b. 1292)

summary: Andronikos IV Palaiologos, co-ruler of the Byzantine Empire, died.
text: Andronikos IV Palaiologos, co-ruler of the Byzantine Empire

summary: The Ottoman Empire and Serbian forces fought the Battle of Kosovo, in which both Sultan Murad I and Prince Lazar were killed.
text: At the Battle of Kosovo, The Ottoman Empire and the Serbs fight an inconclusive clash, with both sides suffering heavy losses. Both Sultan Murad I and Serbian Prince Lazar Hrebeljanovic are killed in the battle.

summary: Bayezid I succeeded his father Murad I as Ottoman Sultan, while Stefan Lazarević succeeded Prince Lazar in Serbia.
text: The day after the Battle of Kosovo, Bayezid I succeeds his father Murad I as Ottoman Sultan, and Stefan Lazarević succeeds his father Lazar as ruler of Serbia.
names: List of sultans of the Ottoman Empire

summary: Casualties were sustained during the Battle of Kosovo.
text: June 15 (in the Battle of Kosovo)

summary: Ottoman Sultan Murad I died during the Battle of Kosovo.
text: Murad I, Ottoman Sultan (b. 1326)

summary: Manuel III succeeded his father Alexios III as Emperor of Trebizond.
text: Manuel III succeeds his father, Alexios III, as Emperor of Trebizond (modern north eastern Turkey).

summary: John VII Palaiologos overthrew his grandfather John V Palaiologos as Byzantine Emperor.
text: John VII Palaiologos overthrows his grandfather, John V Palaiologos, as Byzantine Emperor.

summary: John VII Palaiologos fled to Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I after John V Palaiologos was restored to the Byzantine throne.
text: John VII Palaiologos seeks refuge with the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, after John V Palaiologos is restored by his son, Manuel, and the Republic of Venice.

summary: Pope Boniface IX appointed Angelo Corraro as the Latin Patriarch of Constantinople.
text: Angelo Corraro is named as the Latin Patriarch of Constantinople, the Roman Catholic envoy to Byzantium and the Eastern Orthodox Church, by Pope Boniface IX. Corraro is chosen in 1406 as Pope Gregory XII.

summary: The Ottoman Empire captured Philadelphia, the last significant Byzantine enclave in Anatolia.
text: Fall of Philadelphia – The Ottomans take Philadelphia, the last Byzantine enclave of any significance in Anatolia.

summary: Alexios III Megas Komnenos, Emperor of Trebizond, died.
text: Alexios III Megas Komnenos, Emperor of Trebizond (b. 1338)

summary: Keratsa of Bulgaria, former Byzantine empress consort, died.
text: Keratsa of Bulgaria, Byzantine empress consort (b. 1348)

summary: Manuel II Palaiologos became Byzantine emperor following the death of John V Palaiologos.
text: Manuel II Palaiologos becomes Byzantine emperor after his father, John V Palaiologos, dies from a nervous breakdown, due to his continued humiliation by the Ottoman Empire.

summary: Byzantine Emperor John V Palaiologos died in Constantinople.
text: John V Palaiologos, Byzantine emperor (b. 1332)

summary: Helena Dragaš married Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos and was crowned Empress Consort in Constantinople.
text: Helena Dragaš, a descendant of King Stefan III Dečanski of Serbia, marries the Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos, and is crowned the next day as the Empress Consort of the Byzantine Empire.

summary: Future Byzantine emperor John VIII Palaiologos was born.
text: John VIII Palaiologos, penultimate Byzantine emperor (d. 1448)

summary: The Venetian Senate directed Paolo Foscari to negotiate an alliance with Nerio I Acciaioli and Theodore I Palaiologos against the Navarrese Company.
text: The Senate of the Republic of Venice secretly directs Paolo Foscari to seek an alliance with Nerio I Acciaioli, Duke of Athens and Theodore I Palaiologos, Despot of the Morea, against the mercenary Navarrese Company.

summary: Süleyman Çelebi led Ottoman forces in capturing Tarnovo after a three-month siege, ending the Second Bulgarian Empire.
text: Troops of the Ottoman Empire, led by General Süleyman Çelebi, capture the Bulgarian capital, Tarnovo, after a three-month siege, bringing an end to the Second Bulgarian Empire.

summary: Ottoman forces captured Turnovgrad, reducing Emperor Ivan Shishman to a puppet ruler.
text: The Ottoman Turks capture Turnovgrad (now Veliko Tarnovo), the capital city of east Bulgaria. Emperor Ivan Shishman is allowed to remain as puppet ruler of east Bulgaria.

summary: The Byzantine Empire lost Thessaly to conquest by the Ottoman Empire.
text: Byzantium loses Thessaly to the growing Ottoman Empire.

summary: Anna of Moscow, future Byzantine empress consort, was born.
text: Anna of Moscow, Byzantine empress consort (d. 1417)

summary: Venice took possession of Argos in the Peloponnese from Despot Theodore I Palaiologos.
text: The Venetians take over possession of Argos in the Peloponnese from Despot Theodore I Palaiologos.

summary: The Ottoman Empire conquered Thessaly and began an eight-year siege of Constantinople while constructing the Anadoluhisarı fortress.
text: The Ottomans conquer Thessaly (modern eastern Greece) and begin an eight-year siege of Constantinople, in the Byzantine Empire. In the same year, they begin building the Anadoluhisarı fortress to defend themselves during the siege.

summary: Maria Angelina Doukaina Palaiologina, basilissa of Epirus, died.
text: Maria Angelina Doukaina Palaiologina, basilissa of Epirus (b. 1350)

summary: George of Trebizond, Greek philosopher and scholar, was born.
text: George of Trebizond, Greek philosopher and scholar (d. 1484)

summary: Isidore Glabas, Metropolitan bishop of Thessalonica, died.
text: Isidore Glabas, Metropolitan bishop of Thessalonica (b. 1341/2)

summary: Callistus II Xanthopoulos became Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople following the death of Antony IV.
text: Callistus II Xanthopoulos becomes the new Patriarch to lead the Eastern Orthodox Church after the death of the previous Patriarch Antony IV.

summary: Matthew I of Constantinople became Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople following the death of Callistus II Xanthopoulos.
text: Matthew I of Constantinople becomes the new Patriarch to lead the Eastern Orthodox Church to replace the previous Patriarch, Callistus II Xanthopoulos.

summary: Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos departed Constantinople on a diplomatic mission to Western Europe to seek military aid against the Ottomans.
text: Manuel II Palaiologos, The Emperor of Byzantium, departs from Constantinople along with French General Jean II Le Maingre (known as Boucicaut) and a ships of the Venetian navy on a diplomatic mission to obtain military aid, traveling first to the Republic of Venice to negotiate with the Doge Antonio Venier.
names: Journey of Manuel II to Western Europe

summary: Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos visited England, meeting King Henry IV at Blackheath and staying at Eltham Palace for Christmas.
text: Manuel II Palaiologos becomes the only Byzantine Emperor ever to visit England, and is greeted at Blackheath by King Henry IV, who hosts the Emperor at Eltham Palace during the Christmas holiday.

summary: Byzantine philosopher and theologian Gennadius Scholarius was born in Constantinople.
text: Gennadius Scholarius, Byzantine Greek philosopher and theologian, and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople (d. 1473)

summary: Byzantine painter Manuel Fokas was born.
text: Manuel Fokas, Greek Byzantine painter (d. after 1454)

summary: Byzantine co-emperor Andronikos V Palaiologos was born.
text: Andronikos V Palaiologos, Byzantine ruler of Thessalonica and surrounding territories alongside his father John VII Palaiologos (d. 1407)

summary: Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos accepted three thousand gold marks from King Henry IV before planning his departure from England to France.
text: The Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos, who has spent almost two months in England as the guest of King Henry IV, accepts a payment of 3,000 English gold marks in support of an alliance between the two nations, then makes plans to depart England for France.

summary: Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos departed France after a stay of nearly two years seeking military assistance.
text: The Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos leaves France after a stay of almost two years.

summary: Süleyman Çelebi concluded the Treaty of Gallipoli, granting extensive territorial concessions to the Byzantine Empire and other Christian powers.
text: Signing of the Treaty of Gallipoli is completed as Süleyman Çelebi makes wide-ranging concessions to the Byzantine Empire and other Christian powers, in the southern Balkans.

summary: Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos returned to Constantinople after spending more than two years seeking aid across Western Europe.
text: The Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos returns to Constantinople after an absence for more than two years in Western Europe.

summary: Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos restored Matthew I to the throne of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople.
text: The Emperor Manuel II restores Matthew I as the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, leader of the Eastern Orthodox Christians. Matthew had been deposed the previous autumn during the Emperor's absence from Byzantium.

summary: Basilios Bessarion, later Latin Patriarch of Constantinople and prominent humanist cardinal, was born in Trebizond.
text: Basilios Bessarion, Latin Patriarch of Constantinople (d. 1472)

summary: Constantine XI Palaiologos, the last Byzantine Emperor, was born in Constantinople.
text: Constantine XI, last Byzantine Emperor (d. 1453)

summary: Byzantine prince Demetrios Palaiologos was born in Constantinople.
text: Demetrios Palaiologos, Byzantine prince (d. 1470)

summary: Andronikos Palaiologos became the ruler of Thessalonica following the death of John VII Palaiologos.
text: Andronikos Palaiologos becomes the new Byzantine Emperor of Thessalonica after the death of his brother, John VIII Palaiologos.

summary: Byzantine Emperor John VII Palaiologos died in Thessalonica.
text: John VII Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (b. 1370)

summary: Süleyman Çelebi defeated his brother Musa Çelebi at the Battle of Kosmidion outside Constantinople during the Ottoman Interregnum.
text: Ottoman Interregnum: Süleyman Çelebi, the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, defeats his brother Musa Çelebi, at the Battle of Kosmidion outside of the Byzantine capital, Constantinople.

summary: Euthymius II was installed as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople following the death of Patriarch Matthew I.
text: Euthymius II becomes the new Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, leader of the Eastern Orthodox Church among Christians, after the death in August of the Patriarch Matthew I.
names: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

summary: Patriarch Matthew I of Constantinople died in Constantinople.
text: August – Matthew I of Constantinople

summary: Musa Çelebi briefly laid siege to Constantinople after Byzantium supported his brother Süleyman Çelebi.
text: Constantinople is briefly besieged by the Ottoman pretender Musa Çelebi, due to Byzantine support for Süleyman Çelebi during the Ottoman Interregnum.

summary: Byzantine scholar and diplomat Manuel Chrysoloras died.
text: Manuel Chrysoloras, Greek humanist

summary: Manuel III Megas Komnenos, Emperor of Trebizond, died.
text: Manuel III Megas Komnenos, Emperor of Trebizond (b. 1364)

summary: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Venice signed a commercial treaty.
text: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Venice sign a treaty of commerce.

summary: John VIII Palaiologos was crowned Byzantine co-emperor in Constantinople.
text: The coronation of John VIII Palaiologos as the Emperor of Byzantium, the "Eastern Roman Empire", takes place in Constantinople.

summary: Ottoman Sultan Murad II besieged Constantinople until forced to abandon the siege by the rebellion of Küçük Mustafa.
text: September – The Ottoman sultan Murad II besieges Constantinople; the siege is broken off as a result of the rebellion of Küçük Mustafa.

summary: Turahan Bey broke through the Hexamilion wall and ravaged the Peloponnese.
text: Byzantine–Ottoman Wars: After a two-day battle, Turakhan Beg, Ottoman governor of Thessaly, breaks through the Hexamilion wall, and ravages the Peloponnese Peninsula in Greece.

summary: Giovanni Aurispa arrived in Venice from Byzantium with 238 ancient Greek manuscripts.
text: After a two-year expedition to Byzantium, Giovanni Aurispa arrives in Venice with largest and finest collection of Greek language texts up to that time, including 238 ancient manuscripts.

summary: Byzantine diplomat Nicholas Eudaimonoioannes died.
text: Nicholas Eudaimonoioannes, Byzantine diplomat

summary: John VIII Palaiologos became Byzantine Emperor upon the death of his father Manuel II Palaiologos.
text: John VIII Palaiologos becomes the Emperor of Byzantium upon the death of the Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos.

summary: Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos died in Constantinople.
text: Manuel II Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor (b. 1350)

summary: A Byzantine fleet defeated the naval forces of Carlo I Tocco at the Battle of the Echinades.
text: Battle of the Echinades: A Byzantine fleet defeats the fleet of Carlo I Tocco.

summary: Helena Palaiologina, future Queen of Cyprus, was born in the Morea.
text: Helena Palaiologina, Queen of Cyprus (d. 1458)

summary: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania hosted the Congress of Lutsk to deliberate on the coronation of Vytautas and anti-Ottoman alliances.
text: The Congress of Lutsk opens in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania at the castle of Liubartas in Lutsk. In addition to the Lithuanian nobles gathered there with the Supreme Duke of Lithuania Władysław II Jagiełło and the Grand Duke Vytautas, the Congress is attended by Sigismund, King of Germany, Bohemia, Hungary and Croatia; Erik VII, King of Denmark; a Komtur of the Teutonic Knights; Vasily II, Grand Prince of Moscow; Boris, Duke of Tver; Ivan III, Duke of Ryazan; the Voivode Dan II of Wallachia; and representatives of the Pope, the Byzantine Empire and Moldavia, to discuss the coronation of Vytautas as the King of Lithuania, as well as the siege of Moldavia, entering a against the Ottoman Empire, the ongoing war between Denmark and the Hanseatic League, religious unions and divisions, and assorted economic, trade, and tax-related issues.

summary: Constantine Palaiologos besieged and captured the Venetian-controlled port of Patras.
text: Constantine XI Palaiologos, Emperor of Byzantium, begins the siege of the Greek port of Patras, which is controlled by the Venetian Republic. The city surrenders to the Byzantines on June 1.

summary: Carlo I Tocco, Despot of Epirus, died in Ioannina.
text: Carlo I Tocco, ruler of Epirus (b. 1372)

summary: Emperor Alexios IV Megas Komnenos of Trebizond died.
text: October – Alexios IV Megas Komnenos, Empire of Trebizond (b. 1382)

summary: Ottoman forces under Sultan Murad II took Thessalonica after an eight-year siege.
text: The Ottoman Empire, led by the Sultan Murad II, captures Thessalonica in Greece after an eight-year siege.

summary: The Republic of Venice signed a peace treaty with the Ottoman Empire concluding their eight-year war.
text: the Republic of Venice signs a treaty with the Ottoman Empire to end the eight-year war between the two nations after the Ottoman capture of Thessalonica, replacing the previous agreement of 1419.

summary: The Byzantine Despotate of the Morea annexed Patras and Chalandritsa, ending the Principality of Achaea.
text: With the surrender of Chalandritsa and the citadel of Patras to the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea, the Principality of Achaea comes to an end.

summary: Ottoman governor Turahan Bey breached the Hexamilion wall and ravaged the Peloponnese.
text: Byzantine–Ottoman Wars: The Ottoman governor of Thessaly Turahan Bey breaks through the Hexamilion wall for the second time, and ravages the Peloponnese Peninsula.

summary: Helena Palaiologina, member of the Byzantine imperial dynasty and future Despotess of Serbia, was born in the Despotate of the Morea.
text: Helena Palaiologina, Despotess of Serbia (d. 1473)

summary: Byzantine military commander and statesman Demetrios Laskaris Leontares died.
text: Demetrios Laskaris Leontares, Byzantine soldier and statesman

summary: Mehmed II was born in Edirne.
text: Mehmed II, the Conqueror, Ottoman Sultan (d. 1481)
names: List of sultans of the Ottoman Empire

summary: Centurione II Zaccaria, the last Prince of Achaea, died.
text: Centurione II Zaccaria, last Prince of Achaea, Baron of Arcadia

summary: The Republic of Venice and the Byzantine Empire renewed their treaty for five years at Constantinople.
text: The treaty between the Republic of Venice and the Byzantine Empire is renewed for five years in a signing at Constantinople.

summary: Following the death of Ecumenical Patriarch Joseph II, Pope Eugene IV declared the union of the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
text: Joseph II, the leader of the Eastern Orthodox Church as the 155th Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, dies after a reign of 23 years, leaving a vacancy that is used by the Roman Catholic Pope Eugene IV to declare a unification of the two churches to end the East–West Schism of 1054.
names: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

object: Bull of Union with the Greeks
summary: Pope Eugene IV issued the Bull of Union with the Greeks, proclaiming the union of the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
text: Pope Eugene IV issues the Bull of Union with the Greeks (Laetentur Caeli), signed by the Byzantine Emperor John VIII Palaiologos, proclaiming the end of the East–West Schism between Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy and the union of the two divisions of the Christian faith. The bull is repudiated by most Eastern bishops shortly thereafter.
names: Bull of Union with the Greeks

summary: Byzantine Emperor John VIII Palaiologos appointed Metrophanes II as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople to succeed Joseph II.
text: Metrophanes II, Bishop of Cyzicus, is appointed by the Byzantine Emperor John VIII Palaiologos as the new Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, leader of the Eastern Orthodox Church, to succeed Joseph II, who had died in 1439.
cast: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople
names: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

states.entity: List of bishops and Ecumenical Patriarchs of Constantinople

summary: Constantine XI Palaiologos invaded the Duchy of Athens, compelling it to pay tribute and return Thebes to the Byzantine Empire.
text: Constantine XI Palaiologos, as ruler of the Despotate of the Morea, invades the Duchy of Athens (at this time under Florentine control), and forces it to pay tribute and return Thebes to the Byzantine Empire.

summary: Ottoman Sultan Murad II invaded Attica, forcing Constantine XI Palaiologos to restore Thebes to the Duchy of Athens and submit to Ottoman tribute.
text: October – Murad II, who recently became the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire after his son Mehmed II was forced by the Janissaries to abdicate, invades Attica, forcing Constantine XI to return Thebes to the duchy of Athens, and remove the tribute imposed in 1444. Murad II imposes his own tribute.

summary: Ottoman Sultan Murad II destroyed the Hexamilion wall, ravaged the Peloponnese, and reduced the Despotate of the Morea to an Ottoman vassal state.
text: After hesitating for several weeks, Sultan Murad II, of the Ottoman Empire, destroys the Hexamilion wall, in an assault that includes cannons. Murad and the Ottoman governor of Thessaly, Turakhan Beg, ravage the Peloponnese Peninsula at will, with the Sultan devastating the northern shore, while Glarentza and Turakhan raid in the interior. The Despotate of the Morea is turned into an Ottoman vassal state.

summary: Future Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II was born in Didymoteicho.
text: Bayezid II, Ottoman Sultan (d. 1512)
names: List of sultans of the Ottoman Empire

summary: The Council of Russian Bishops installed Jonah as Metropolitan of Kiev and All Rus without Constantinople's consent, establishing de facto autocephaly for the Russian church.
text: Jonas, a Russian bishop, is installed by the Council of Russian Bishops in Moscow, as Metropolitan of Kiev and All Rus. The event marks the independence of the Russian Orthodox Church because the election of Jonas is made without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople as this is without the consent of the Patriarch of Constantinople, it signifies the beginning of an effectively independent church structure in the Grand Duchy of Moscow.
names: Metropolis of Kiev and all Rus'

summary: John VIII Palaiologos, Byzantine Emperor, died in Constantinople.
text: John VIII Palaeologus, Byzantine Emperor (b. 1390)

summary: Constantine XI Palaiologos was crowned Byzantine Emperor at Mystras.
text: Constantine XI Palaiologos is crowned Byzantine Emperor at Mistra; he will be the last in a line of rulers that can be traced to the founding of Rome.

summary: Turahan Bey breached the Hexamilion wall and ravaged the Peloponnese to prevent the Despotate of the Morea from aiding Constantinople.
text: October – Byzantine–Ottoman Wars: The Ottoman governor of Thessaly, Turakhan Beg, breaks through the Hexamilion wall for the fourth time, and ravages the Peloponnese Peninsula to prevent the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea from assisting Constantinople, during the final Ottoman siege of the imperial capital.

summary: Isidore of Kiev proclaimed the union of the Greek and Latin churches at Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
text: Isidore of Kiev, the Latin Patriarch of Constantinople, proclaims the union of the Greek and Latin churches at the Hagia Sophia in hopes of an alliance with Western Christians to prevent the loss of Constantinople to the Ottoman Turks.

summary: Byzantine philosopher Gemistos Plethon died in Mystras.
